entries.zh: 興祖後執錄，奐仍令蠻領仗身於獄守視。
entries.en: After Xingzu was arrested, Huan still had that barbarian lead armed attendants to guard him in prison.
entries.literal: After Xingzu was arrested, Huan still had the barbarian lead armed attendants to guard and watch him in prison.

entries.zh: 興祖未死之前，於獄以物畫漆柈子中出密報家，道無罪，令啓乞出都一辨，萬死無恨」。
entries.en: Before he died, Xingzu scratched a secret message on a lacquered tray in prison and sent it to his family, declaring his innocence and asking them to petition that he be brought to the capital for a hearing—he would accept any punishment without regret."
entries.literal: Before Xingzu died, in prison he used an object to draw on a lacquered tray and sent a secret message to his family, saying he was innocent and asking them to petition that he be brought to the capital for a hearing—he would die without regret.

entries.zh: 又云：「奐駐興祖嚴禁信使，欲作方便，殺以除口舌。」
entries.en: He also said, "Huan placed Xingzu under strict guard and cut off messengers, intending to seize an opportunity to kill him and silence him."
entries.literal: He also said: "Huan stationed strict guards on Xingzu and cut off messengers, intending to find an opportunity to kill him and silence his mouth."

entries.zh: 又云：「奐意乃可。
entries.en: He also said, "That was indeed Huan's intent.
entries.literal: He also said: "Huan's intent was indeed so.

entries.zh: 奐第三息彪隨奐在州，凡事是非皆干豫，扇構密除興祖。」
entries.en: Huan's third son Biao was with him in the province and meddled in every decision, inciting plots to have Xingzu secretly eliminated."
entries.literal: Huan's third son Biao accompanied Huan in the province; in every matter of right and wrong he intervened, inciting plots to have Xingzu secretly removed."

entries.zh: 又云：「興祖家餉糜，中下藥，食兩口便覺，回乞獄子，食者皆大利。
entries.en: He also said, "Xingzu's family sent gruel in which poison had been placed; after two mouthfuls he fell ill and begged the jailer—everyone who ate of it was violently purged.
entries.literal: He also said: "Xingzu's family sent gruel; poison was placed in it—after two mouthfuls he felt ill and begged the jailer; all who ate it suffered severely.

entries.zh: 興祖大呌道『糜中有藥』。
entries.en: Xingzu cried out, 'There is poison in the gruel!'
entries.literal: Xingzu cried out loudly: 'There is poison in the gruel.'

entries.zh: 近獄之家，無人不聞。」
entries.en: Every household near the prison heard it."
entries.literal: Among families near the prison, there was none who did not hear."

entries.zh: 又云：「奐治著興祖日急，判無濟理。
entries.en: He also said, "Huan pressed Xingzu harder day by day; plainly there was no hope of survival.
entries.literal: He also said: "Huan's handling of Xingzu grew more pressing day by day; plainly there was no hope of deliverance.

entries.zh: 十一月二十一日，奐使獄吏來報興祖家，道興祖於獄自經死。
entries.en: On the twenty-first day of the eleventh month, Huan sent prison clerks to tell Xingzu's family that he had hanged himself in prison.
entries.literal: On the twenty-first day of the eleventh month, Huan sent prison clerks to report to Xingzu's family that Xingzu had hanged himself in prison.

entries.zh: 尸出，家人共洗浴之，見興祖頸下有傷，肩胛烏，陰下破碎，實非興祖自經死。
entries.en: When the body was brought out, the family washed it together and found wounds on the neck, blackened shoulders, and shattered private parts—clearly he had not died by hanging.
entries.literal: When the corpse was brought out, the family together washed the body and saw wounds beneath Xingzu's neck, blackened shoulders, and shattered private parts—truly he had not hanged himself.

entries.zh: 家人及門義共見，非是一人。」
entries.en: Family and retainers alike witnessed it—many people, not one alone."
entries.literal: Family and retainers all saw it; it was not a single person."

entries.zh: 重攝檢雍州都留田文喜，列與倪符同狀。
entries.en: Tian Wenxi, who had remained in Yong Province, was examined again; his testimony matched Ni's in every detail.
entries.literal: Tian Wenxi, who had remained in Yong Province, was again taken for examination; his statements matched Ni's in every particular.

entries.zh: :　　興祖在獄，嗛苦望下，旣蒙降旨，欣願始遂，豈容於此，方復自經？
entries.en: Xingzu in prison had suffered bitterly while awaiting the court's mercy; having received the gracious decree, his long hope was at last fulfilled—how could he at that moment take his own life?
entries.literal: Xingzu in prison endured bitter hardship while looking to the court; having received the gracious decree, his glad hope was just fulfilled—how could he at this moment hang himself again?

entries.zh: 敕以十九日至，興祖以二十一日死，推理檢迹，灼然矯假。
entries.en: The decree arrived on the nineteenth and Xingzu died on the twenty-first; weighed by reason and evidence, the fraud is glaringly clear.
entries.literal: The decree arrived on the nineteenth; Xingzu died on the twenty-first—reasoning through the evidence, the forgery is glaringly clear.

entries.zh: 尋敕使送下，奐輙拒詔，所謗諸條，悉出奐意。
entries.en: An imperial messenger was shortly to escort him to the capital, yet Huan defied the decree. Every charge of slander came entirely from Huan's own design.
entries.literal: Shortly thereafter an imperial messenger was to escort him down; Huan abruptly defied the decree. Every item of slander issued entirely from Huan's intent.

entries.zh: 毀故丞相若陳顯達，誹訕朝事，莫此之深。
entries.en: He slandered the late Chancellor Chen Xianda and reviled the court—nothing could be more grave.
entries.literal: He slandered the late Chancellor Chen Xianda and reviled court affairs—nothing goes deeper.

entries.zh: 彪私隨父之鎮，敢亂王法，罪竝合窮戮。
entries.en: Biao had followed his father to the province without authorization and dared to violate the law—his crimes together warrant the utmost penalty.
entries.literal: Biao privately followed his father to the province and dared to disturb royal law; his crime together warrants the utmost punishment.

entries.zh: 奐子彪素凶剽，奐不能制。
entries.en: Huan's son Biao had always been fierce and violent, and Huan could not control him.
entries.literal: Huan's son Biao was by nature fierce and violent; Huan could not control him.

entries.zh: 女婿殷叡懼禍，謂奐曰：「曹、呂今來，旣不見真敕，恐爲姦變，政宜錄取，馳啓聞耳。」
entries.en: His son-in-law Yin Rui, fearing disaster, said to Huan, "Cao and Lu have come without showing the true decree—I fear treachery; you should arrest them at once and send an urgent report to the throne."
entries.literal: His son-in-law Yin Rui, fearing disaster, said to Huan: "Cao and Lu have come now without showing the true decree—I fear a treacherous turn; you should just arrest them and send a swift report."

entries.zh: 奐納之。
entries.en: Huan accepted the advice.
entries.literal: Huan accepted this.

entries.zh: 彪輙令率州內得千餘人，開鎮庫，取仗，配衣甲，出南堂陳兵，閉門拒守。
entries.en: Biao at once mustered more than a thousand men in the province, opened the headquarters arsenal, issued arms and armor, drew up troops in the southern hall, closed the gates, and prepared to resist.
entries.literal: Biao on his own authority mustered more than a thousand men within the province, opened the headquarters arsenal, took weapons, issued armor, deployed troops in the southern hall, closed the gates, and resisted.

entries.zh: 奐門生鄭羽叩頭啓奐，乞出城迎臺使。
entries.en: Huan's student Zheng Yu kowtowed and begged Huan to go out and welcome the envoys from the capital.
entries.literal: Huan's student Zheng Yu kowtowed and petitioned Huan, begging to go out of the city to welcome the capital envoys.

entries.zh: 奐曰：「我不作賊，欲先遣啓自申。
entries.en: Huan said, "I am no rebel; I wish first to send a memorial in my own defense.
entries.literal: Huan said: "I am not becoming a rebel; I wish first to send a report to explain myself.

entries.zh: 政恐曹、呂輩小人相陵藉，故且閉門自守耳。」
entries.en: I only fear that petty men like Cao and Lu will abuse us—so for the moment I close the gates and hold my ground."
entries.literal: I only fear that Cao, Lu, and such petty men will bully and trample us—therefore for the moment I close the gates and hold my own."

entries.zh: 彪遂出與虎軍戰，其黨范虎領二百人降臺軍，彪敗走歸。
entries.en: Biao then went out to fight Hu's army; his follower Fan Hu led two hundred men over to the capital forces, and Biao was beaten and fled back inside.
entries.literal: Biao then went out to fight Hu's army; his follower Fan Hu led two hundred men in surrender to the capital forces, and Biao was defeated and fled back.

entries.zh: 土人起義攻州西門，彪登門拒戰，却之。
entries.en: Local men rose and attacked the western gate of the headquarters; Biao mounted the gate to fight them off and repulsed them.
entries.literal: Local men rose in arms and attacked the western gate of the province; Biao mounted the gate to resist and drove them back.

entries.zh: 奐司馬黃瑤起、寧蠻長史裴叔業於城內起兵攻奐。
entries.en: Huan's chief administrator Huang Yaoqi and Pei Shuye, chief administrator of the Pacification of the Barbarians, raised troops inside the city to attack him.
entries.literal: Huan's chief administrator Huang Yaoqi and the chief administrator of the Pacification of the Barbarians Pei Shuye raised troops within the city to attack Huan.

entries.zh: 奐聞兵入，還內禮佛，未及起，軍人遂斬之。
entries.en: Hearing that troops had entered, Huan went inside to worship the Buddha; before he could rise, the soldiers cut him down.
entries.literal: Huan, hearing troops enter, returned inside to worship the Buddha; before he could rise, the soldiers cut him down.

entries.zh: 年五十九。
entries.en: He was fifty-nine years old.
entries.literal: He was fifty-nine.

entries.zh: 執彪及弟爽、弼、殷叡，皆伏誅。
entries.en: Biao, his brothers Shuang and Bi, and Yin Rui were seized and all put to death.
entries.literal: Biao and his brothers Shuang and Bi were seized, together with Yin Rui; all were executed.

entries.zh: 奐長子太子中庶子融，融弟司徒從事中郎琛，於都棄市。
entries.en: Huan's eldest son Rong, Attendant in the Heir Apparent's Household, and Rong's younger brother Chen, Attendant Gentleman of the Minister of Works, were executed in the market at the capital.
entries.literal: Huan's eldest son Rong, Attendant in the Heir Apparent's Household, and Rong's younger brother Chen, Attendant in the Secretariat, were exposed in the market at the capital.

entries.zh: 餘孫皆原宥。
entries.en: The remaining grandsons were all granted pardon.
entries.literal: The remaining grandsons were all pardoned.

entries.zh: 叡族父恒，字昭度，與叡同承融後。
entries.en: Rui's clansman uncle Heng, whose style name was Zhaodu, like Rui succeeded to Rong's line.
entries.literal: Rui's clansman uncle Heng, style name Zhaodu, with Rui alike succeeded to Rong's line.

entries.zh: 宋司空景仁孫也。
entries.en: He was the grandson of Jingren, Minister of Works in the Song.
entries.literal: He was grandson of Jingren, Minister of Works in Song.

entries.zh: 恒及父道矜，竝有古風，以是見蚩於世，其事非一。
entries.en: Heng and his father Daojin both affected an antique manner, for which they were ridiculed in their day on more than one occasion.
entries.literal: Heng and his father Daojin both had an antique manner; for this they were mocked by the world—not a single instance alone.

entries.zh: 恒，宋泰始初，爲度支尚書，坐屬父疾及身疾多，爲有司所奏。
entries.en: At the beginning of the Taishi era in Song, Heng served as Minister of Revenue but was impeached because his father's illness and his own frequent illnesses violated regulations on mourning and attendance.
entries.literal: Heng, at the beginning of Taishi in Song, was Minister of Revenue; he was impeached because his father's illness and his own frequent illnesses fell under the statute.

entries.zh: 明帝詔曰：「殷道矜有生便病，比更無橫病。
entries.en: Emperor Ming's edict read, "Yin Daojin has been ill from birth; recently he has suffered no sudden illness.
entries.literal: Emperor Ming's edict said: "Yin Daojin has been ill from birth; recently there has been no sudden illness.

entries.zh: 恒因愚習惰，久妨清敘。
entries.en: Heng, through foolish habit and sloth, has long obstructed proper advancement in office.
entries.literal: Heng, through foolish habit and sloth, has long obstructed clear advancement.

entries.zh: 左遷散騎常侍，領校尉。」
entries.en: He is demoted to Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and concurrently Colonel."
entries.literal: He is demoted to Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and concurrently Colonel."

entries.zh: 恒歷官清顯，至金紫光祿大夫。
entries.en: Heng nevertheless served through a series of eminent posts and rose to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal.
entries.literal: Heng passed through clear and eminent offices and reached Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal.

entries.zh: 建武中，卒。
entries.en: He died during the Jianwu era.
entries.literal: During Jianwu he died.

entries.zh: 奐弟女爲長沙王晃妃，世祖詔曰：「奐自陷逆節，長沙王妃男女竝長，且奐又出繼，前代或當有准，可特不離絕。」
entries.en: The daughter of Huan's younger brother was consort to Prince Huang of Changsha. Emperor Shizu decreed, "Huan brought treason upon himself, but the Princess of Changsha's children are grown, and Huan himself was given in adoption—precedents exist from earlier ages; their ties shall not be severed."
entries.literal: Huan's younger brother's daughter was consort to Prince Huang of Changsha. Emperor Shizu's edict said: "Huan brought himself into treason; the Princess of Changsha's sons and daughters are both grown, and moreover Huan was given in adoption—former ages perhaps had precedents; they may specially not be severed."

entries.zh: 奐從弟繢。
entries.en: Huan's cousin was Wang Hui.
entries.literal: Huan's cousin Hui.

entries.zh: =繢字叔素，宋車騎將軍景文子也。
entries.en: Wang Hui, whose style name was Shusu, was the son of Jingwen, General of Chariots and Cavalry in the Song.
entries.literal: Hui, style name Shusu, was son of Jingwen, General of Chariots and Cavalry in Song.

entries.zh: 弱冠，爲祕書郎，太子舍人，轉中書舍人。
entries.en: Upon reaching manhood he served as Secretariat Gentleman and Attendant in the Heir Apparent's Household, then was transferred to Palace Gentleman of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: At capped age he became Secretariat Gentleman, Attendant in the Heir Apparent's Household, then transferred to Palace Gentleman of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 景文以此授超階，令繢經年乃受。
entries.en: Jingwen would have granted him a leap in rank on this account, but made Hui wait a full year before accepting the appointment.
entries.literal: Jingwen on this account granted him a leap in rank, but had Hui wait a full year before accepting.

entries.zh: 景文封江安侯，繢襲其本爵，爲始平縣五等男。
entries.en: Jingwen had been enfeoffed as Marquis of Jiang'an; Hui inherited his original noble rank and became a fifth-grade baron of Shiping County.
entries.literal: Jingwen was enfeoffed as Marquis of Jiang'an; Hui inherited his original rank and became a fifth-grade baron of Shiping County.

entries.zh: 遷祕書丞，司徒右長史。
entries.en: He was promoted to Secretariat Assistant and Right Chief Administrator of the Minister of Works.
entries.literal: He was moved to Secretariat Assistant and Right Chief Administrator of the Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 元徽末，除寧朔將軍、建平王征北長史、南東海太守，黃門郎，寧朔將軍、東陽太守。
entries.en: At the end of the Yuanhui era he was appointed General of Pacifying the North, chief administrator to the General Who Campaigns North for the Prince of Jianping, and Grand Administrator of Southern Donghai, then Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, General of Pacifying the North, and Grand Administrator of Dongyang.
entries.literal: At the end of Yuanhui he was appointed General of Pacifying the North, chief administrator to the General Who Campaigns North for Prince of Jianping, Grand Administrator of Southern Donghai, Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, General of Pacifying the North, and Grand Administrator of Dongyang.

entries.zh: 世祖爲撫軍，吏部尚書張岱選繢爲長史，呈選牒。
entries.en: When Shizu was General Who Consoles the Army, Minister of Personnel Zhang Dai selected Hui as his chief administrator and presented the nomination.
entries.literal: When Shizu was General Who Pacifies the Army, Minister of Personnel Zhang Dai selected Hui as chief administrator and presented the selection document.

entries.zh: 太祖笑謂岱曰：「此可謂素望。」
entries.en: Emperor Gao smiled and said to Dai, "This is what one calls a man of established reputation."
entries.literal: Emperor Gao laughed and said to Dai: "This may be called long-standing repute."

entries.zh: 遷散騎常侍，驍騎將軍。
entries.en: He was promoted to Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and General of Valiant Cavalry.
entries.literal: He was moved to Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and General of Valiant Cavalry.

entries.zh: 出補義興太守。
entries.en: He was sent out as Grand Administrator of Yixing.
entries.literal: He went out to fill the post of Grand Administrator of Yixing.

entries.zh: 輙錄郡吏陳伯喜付陽羨獄，欲殺之，縣令孔逭不知何罪，不受繢教，爲有司所奏，繢坐白衣領職。
entries.en: He on his own authority arrested commandery clerk Chen Boxi and sent him to prison in Yangxian intending to kill him; County Magistrate Kong Huan, not knowing the charge, refused to obey Hui's order; the matter was reported to the authorities, and Hui was reduced to serving in plain clothes.
entries.literal: He on his own authority arrested the commandery clerk Chen Boxi and sent him to prison in Yangxian, intending to kill him; the magistrate of the county Kong Huan did not know what the crime was and would not accept Hui's order; he was reported by the responsible offices, and Hui was punished by serving in office in plain clothes.

entries.zh: 遷太子中庶子，領驍騎，轉長兼侍中。
entries.en: He was appointed Attendant in the Heir Apparent's Household and concurrently General of Valiant Cavalry, then Chief Concurrent Palace Attendant.
entries.literal: He was moved to Attendant in the Heir Apparent's Household, concurrently General of Valiant Cavalry, then transferred to Chief Concurrent Palace Attendant.

entries.zh: 世祖出射雉，繢信佛法，稱疾不從駕。
entries.en: When Shizu went out pheasant hunting, Hui, a devout Buddhist, pleaded illness and did not accompany the imperial procession.
entries.literal: When Shizu went out to shoot pheasants, Hui, believing in Buddhism, claimed illness and did not follow the imperial carriage.

entries.zh: 轉左民尚書，以母老乞解職，改授寧朔將軍、大司馬長史、淮陵太守。
entries.en: He was transferred to Minister of the Left for the People; citing his mother's age, he asked to resign and was reassigned as General of Pacifying the North, chief administrator to the Grand Marshal, and Grand Administrator of Huailing.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Minister of the Left for the People; because his mother was old he begged to resign office and was reassigned as General of Pacifying the North, chief administrator to the Grand Marshal, and Grand Administrator of Huailing.

entries.zh: 出爲宣城太守，秩中二千石，
entries.en: He was sent out as Grand Administrator of Xuancheng at the middle two-thousand-picul rank.
entries.literal: He went out as Grand Administrator of Xuancheng, with salary of two thousand piculs at the middle grade.

entries.zh: 隆昌元年，遷輔國將軍、太傅長史，不拜。
entries.en: In the first year of Longchang, he was appointed General Who Assists the State and chief administrator to the Grand Tutor but declined the post.
entries.literal: In the first year of Longchang, he was moved to General Who Assists the State and chief administrator to the Grand Tutor but did not accept.

entries.zh: 仍爲冠軍將軍、豫章內史。
entries.en: He was then made General Who Establishes Valor and Interior Administrator of Yuzhang.
entries.literal: He was then made General Who Establishes Valor and Interior Administrator of Yuzhang.

entries.zh: 進號征虜。
entries.en: His designation was raised to General Who Subdues the Barbarians.
entries.literal: His designation was advanced to General Who Subdues the Barbarians.

entries.zh: 又坐事免官。
entries.en: He was again dismissed from office for an offense.
entries.literal: He again was dismissed from office because of an affair.

entries.zh: 除冠軍將軍，司徒左長史，散騎常侍，隨王師。
entries.en: He was appointed General Who Establishes Valor, Left Chief Administrator of the Minister of Works, Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, and tutor to the Prince of Sui.
entries.literal: He was appointed General Who Establishes Valor, Left Chief Administrator of the Minister of Works, Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, and tutor to the Prince of Sui.

entries.zh: 除征虜將軍，驃騎長史，遷散騎常侍，太常。
entries.en: He was appointed General Who Subdues the Barbarians and chief administrator to the General of Agile Cavalry, then promoted to Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Minister of Ceremonies.
entries.literal: He was appointed General Who Subdues the Barbarians and chief administrator to the General of Agile Cavalry, then moved to Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Minister of Ceremonies.

entries.zh: 永元元年，卒。
entries.en: He died in the first year of Yongyuan.
entries.literal: In Yongyuan 1, he died.

entries.zh: 年五十三。
entries.en: He was fifty-three years old.
entries.literal: He was fifty-three.

entries.zh: 諡靖子。
entries.en: He was given the posthumous title Jingzi.
entries.literal: His posthumous title was Jingzi.

entries.zh: 繢女適安陸王子敬，世祖寵子，
entries.en: Hui's daughter married Zijing, Prince of Anlu, a favorite son of Emperor Shizu.
entries.literal: Hui's daughter was married to Zijing, Prince of Anlu, a favored son of Shizu.

entries.zh: 永明三年，納妃，脩外舅姑之敬。
entries.en: In the third year of Yongming, when the prince took her as consort, he showed the full respect due to his wife's parents.
entries.literal: In the third year of Yongming, when he took a consort, he showed the respect due to his wife's parents.

entries.zh: 世祖遣文惠太子相隨往繢家置酒設樂，公卿皆冠冕而至，當世榮之。
entries.en: Emperor Shizu sent Crown Prince Wenhui to accompany the prince to Hui's house for a feast with music; dukes and ministers all came in full court dress—the age regarded it as the highest honor.
entries.literal: Shizu sent the Crown Prince Wen Hui to accompany him in going to Hui's house to set out wine and music; dukes and ministers all came in caps and regalia—his age counted it an honor.

entries.zh: 時新蔡太守席謙，永明中爲中書郎王融所薦。
entries.en: At that time Xi Qian, Grand Administrator of Xincai, had been recommended in the Yongming era by Secretariat Gentleman Wang Rong.
entries.literal: At that time Xi Qian, Grand Administrator of Xincai, had in the Yongming era been recommended by the Secretariat Gentleman Wang Rong.

entries.zh: 父恭穆，鎮西司馬，爲魚復侯所害。
entries.en: His father Gongmu, chief administrator to the General Who Guards the West, had been killed by the Marquis of Yufu.
entries.literal: His father Gongmu, chief administrator to the General Who Guards the West, was killed by the Marquis of Yufu.

entries.zh: 至是謙鎮盆城，聞義師東下，曰：「我家世忠貞，殞死不二。」
entries.en: By then Qian was holding Pencheng; when he heard that the righteous army was marching east, he said, "Our house has been loyal for generations—I will die rather than turn."
entries.literal: At this time Qian held Pencheng; hearing that the righteous army was coming east, he said: "Our house for generations has been loyal and steadfast—death without a second thought."

entries.zh: 爲陳伯之所殺。
entries.en: He was killed by Chen Bozhi.
entries.literal: He was killed by Chen Bozhi.

entries.zh: 王奐
entries.en: Wang Huan
entries.literal: Wang Huan

entries.zh: 巴陵王昭秀字懷尚，太子第三子也。
entries.en: Zhaoxiu, Prince of Baling, whose style name was Huaishang, was Crown Prince Wen Hui's third son.
entries.literal: The Prince of Baling, Zhaoxiu, style name Huaishang, was the crown prince's third son.

entries.zh: 永明中，封曲江公，千五百戶。
entries.en: During the Yongming era he was enfeoffed as Duke of Qujiang with a fief of fifteen hundred households.
entries.literal: During the Yongming era he was enfeoffed as Duke of Qujiang with fifteen hundred households.

entries.zh: 十年，爲寧朔將軍、濟陽太守。
entries.en: In the tenth year he was appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Jiyang.
entries.literal: In the tenth year he was made General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Jiyang.

entries.zh: 鬱林卽位，封臨海郡王，二千戶。
entries.en: When the Prince of Yulin took the throne, Zhaoxiu was enfeoffed as Prince of Linhai with a fief of two thousand households.
entries.literal: When the Prince of Yulin acceded, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Linhai Commandery with two thousand households.

entries.zh: 隆昌元年，爲使持節、都督荊雍益寧梁南北秦七州軍事、西中郎將、荊州刺史。
entries.en: In the first year of Longchang (494) he was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Area Commander of Jing, Yong, Yi, Ning, Liang, and Northern and Southern Qin, General of the West, and Governor of Jing.
entries.literal: In the first year of Longchang he was made Bearer of the Staff, Supervisor of Military Affairs for the seven provinces of Jing, Yong, Yi, Ning, Liang, and Northern and Southern Qin, General of the West, and Governor of Jing.

entries.zh: 延興元年，徵爲車騎將軍，衞京師，以永嘉王昭粲代之。
entries.en: In the first year of Yanxing (494) he was recalled as General of the Chariots and Cavalry to guard the capital, and Zhaocan, Prince of Yongjia, replaced him.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yanxing he was summoned as General of the Chariots and Cavalry to guard the capital, and the Prince of Yongjia, Zhaocan, was sent to replace him.

entries.zh: 明帝建武二年，通直常侍庾曇隆啓曰：「周定雒邑，天子置畿內之民；
entries.en: In the second year of Jianwu (495), Regular Attendant Yu Tanlong memorialized: "When the Zhou fixed their capital at Luoyi, the Son of Heaven settled the people of the capital domain;
entries.literal: In the second year of Jianwu under Emperor Ming, Regular Attendant Yu Tanlong submitted: "When the Zhou fixed their capital at Luoyi, the Son of Heaven placed the people of the capital domain;

entries.zh: 漢都咸陽，三輔爲社稷之衞。
entries.en: when Han made its capital at Xianyang, the Three Metropolitans guarded the altars of state.
entries.literal: when Han made its capital at Xianyang, the Three Metropolises were the guard of the altars of state.

entries.zh: 中晉南遷，事移威弛，近郡名邦，多有國食。
entries.en: After the Jin moved south, authority slackened over time, and famous nearby commanderies often drew state stipends.
entries.literal: When mid-Jin moved south, affairs shifted and authority slackened; famous commanderies near the capital often received state stipends.

entries.zh: 宋武創業，依擬古典，神州部內，不復別封。
entries.en: When Emperor Wu of Song founded the dynasty on ancient models, he ceased granting separate fiefs within the imperial domain.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu of Song founded the dynasty, following ancient models, within the imperial domain he no longer enfeoffed separately.

entries.zh: 而孝武末年，分樹寵子，苟申私愛，有乖訓准。
entries.en: But in Emperor Xiaowu's later years, favored sons were enfeoffed separately to indulge private affection, contrary to proper norms.
entries.literal: But in the late years of Emperor Xiaowu, enfeoffments were divided to favor beloved sons, indulging private affection against proper norms.

entries.zh: 隆昌之元，特開母弟之貴，竊謂非古。
entries.en: In the first year of Longchang, special rank was granted to younger uterine brothers; I submit that this is uncanonical.
entries.literal: In the first year of Longchang, special honor was opened to younger brothers of the same mother; I privately consider this uncanonical.

entries.zh: 聖明御宇，禮舊爲先，畿內限斷，宜遵昔制，賜茅授土，一出外州。」
entries.en: The sage ruler governs the realm with ancient rites foremost; the limits of the capital domain should follow former institutions, and grants of fief and land should all lie outside the inner provinces."
entries.literal: The sage and enlightened ruler governs the realm; ancient rites come first. The limits of the capital domain should follow former institutions—bestowal of estates and grant of land should all go to outer provinces."

entries.zh: 詔付尚書詳議。
entries.en: An edict referred the matter to the Masters of Writing for detailed deliberation.
entries.literal: An edict referred the memorial to the Masters of Writing for detailed deliberation.

entries.zh: 其冬，改封昭秀爲巴陵王。
entries.en: That winter Zhaoxiu was reassigned as Prince of Baling.
entries.literal: That winter Zhaoxiu's enfeoffment was changed to Prince of Baling.

entries.zh: 永泰元年見殺，年十六。
entries.en: In the first year of Yongtai (498) he was put to death at the age of sixteen.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongtai he was killed. He was sixteen.

entries.zh: 桂陽王昭粲，太子第四子也。
entries.en: Zhaocan, Prince of Guiyang, was Crown Prince Wen Hui's fourth son.
entries.literal: Zhaocan, Prince of Guiyang, was the crown prince's fourth son.

entries.zh: 鬱林立，以皇弟封永嘉郡王，南徐州刺史。
entries.en: When the Prince of Yulin was installed as emperor, Zhaocan was enfeoffed as Prince of Yongjia as the emperor's younger brother and appointed Governor of Southern Xu.
entries.literal: When Yulin was established, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yongjia Commandery as the emperor's younger brother and made Governor of Southern Xu.

entries.zh: 延興元年，出爲使持節、都督荊雍益寧梁南北秦七州軍事、西中郎將、荊州刺史。
entries.en: In the first year of Yanxing (494) he was sent out as Bearer of the Staff, Area Commander of Jing, Yong, Yi, Ning, Liang, and Northern and Southern Qin, General of the West, and Governor of Jing.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yanxing he went out as Bearer of the Staff, Supervisor of Military Affairs for the seven provinces of Jing, Yong, Yi, Ning, Liang, and Northern and Southern Qin, General of the West, and Governor of Jing.

entries.zh: 明帝立，欲以聞喜公遙欣爲荊州，轉昭粲爲右將軍，中書令。
entries.en: When Emperor Ming took the throne, intending to appoint Yaoxin, Duke of Wenxi, to Jing Province, he reassigned Zhaocan as General of the Right and Director of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: When Emperor Ming was established, wishing to make the Duke of Wenxi, Yaoxin, Governor of Jing, he transferred Zhaocan to General of the Right and Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 建武二年，改封桂陽王。
entries.en: In the second year of Jianwu (495) he was reassigned as Prince of Guiyang.
entries.literal: In the second year of Jianwu his enfeoffment was changed to Prince of Guiyang.

entries.zh: 四年，遷太常，將軍如故。
entries.en: In the fourth year (497) he was promoted to Grand Minister of Ceremonies, retaining his rank as general.
entries.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to Grand Minister of Ceremonies; his generalship remained as before.

entries.zh: 永泰元年見殺，年八歲。
entries.en: In the first year of Yongtai (498) he was put to death at the age of eight.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongtai he was killed. He was eight.

entries.zh: 南齊書卷五十‧列傳第三十一
entries.en: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 50 · Biographies 31
entries.literal: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 50 · Biographies 31

entries.zh: 太祖承宋氏奢縱，風移百城，輔立幼主，思振民瘼。
entries.en: The Founding Emperor inherited the Song dynasty's extravagance and lax rule, which had spread decadent habits through cities everywhere. Supporting a young sovereign on the throne, he sought to relieve the people's distress.
entries.literal: The Founder inherited the Song clan's luxury and laxity; custom shifted through a hundred cities. He assisted in establishing a young lord and thought to revive the people's afflictions.

entries.zh: 爲政未朞，擢山陰令傅琰爲益州刺史。
entries.en: Early in his reign he promoted Fu Yan, the magistrate of Shanyin, to regional inspector of Yizhou.
entries.literal: His governance had not yet reached its term when he promoted Fu Yan, magistrate of Shanyin, to Inspector of Yizhou.

entries.zh: 乃捐華反樸，恭己南面，導民以躬，意存勿擾。
entries.en: He renounced ornament for plain living, held himself with humble dignity on the throne, led the people by personal example, and kept administration as unobtrusive as possible.
entries.literal: Thereupon he cast aside splendor and returned to simplicity, held himself reverently facing south, guided the people by his own person, and his intent was to leave them undisturbed.

entries.zh: 以山陰大邑，獄訟繁滋，建元三年，別置獄丞，與建康爲比。
entries.en: Because Shanyin was a large district with a heavy caseload, in the third year of Jianyuan a separate prison deputy was appointed, matching the arrangement at the capital.
entries.literal: Because Shanyin was a great district and prison lawsuits proliferated, in the third year of Jianyuan a separate prison assistant was appointed, on a par with Jiankang.

entries.zh: 永明繼運，垂心治術。
entries.en: Under the Yongming reign the court devoted itself earnestly to the art of government.
entries.literal: When Yongming succeeded to the mandate, he bent his mind to the art of governance.

entries.zh: 杖威善斷，猶多漏網，長吏犯法，封刃行誅。
entries.en: The court wielded stern authority and judged cases decisively, yet many offenders still slipped through; when senior officials broke the law, swords were drawn and punishment was enforced without delay.
entries.literal: Relying on authority and skilled in judgment, yet many still escaped the net; when senior officials violated the law, the blade was sealed and execution carried out.

entries.zh: 郡縣居職，以三周爲小滿。
entries.en: Officials serving in the commanderies and districts were expected to complete three annual cycles before their term was considered minimally fulfilled.
entries.literal: For those serving in commanderies and districts, three cycles were taken as a minor fulfillment of term.

entries.zh: 水旱之災，輙加賑卹。
entries.en: Whenever floods or droughts struck, the government promptly provided relief.
entries.literal: When flood or drought disasters occurred, relief and succor were always added.

entries.zh: 明帝自在布衣，曉達吏事，君臨億兆，專務刀筆，未嘗枉法申恩，守宰以之肅震。
entries.en: Emperor Ming had understood official business since his days as a commoner. Once he ruled the realm, he devoted himself entirely to legal paperwork, never bending the law to show favor, and prefects and magistrates were awed into strict compliance.
entries.literal: Emperor Ming, from the time he was in common cloth, understood administrative affairs. When he ruled over the hundred millions, he devoted himself solely to legal documents and the brush; he never bent the law to show favor, and prefects and magistrates were thereby awed into reverence.

entries.zh: 復除邵陵王南中郎參軍，廣德令，尚書駕部郎。
entries.en: He was later appointed adjutant to the southern gentlemen of the interior under the Prince of Shaoling, magistrate of Guangde, and director in the imperial carriages office of the Masters of Writing.
entries.literal: He was again appointed Adjutant of the Southern Gentlemen of the Interior under the Prince of Shaoling, magistrate of Guangde, and Master of Writing in the Department of Imperial Carriages.

entries.zh: 懷慰宗從善明等，太祖心腹，懷慰亦豫焉。
entries.en: Huaiwei's kinsmen Shanming and others were trusted confidants of the Founding Emperor, and Huaiwei was counted among them.
entries.literal: Huaiwei's clansmen Shanming and others were the Founder's intimate confidants; Huaiwei also participated therein.

entries.zh: 沈攸之有舊，令爲書戒喻攸之，太祖省之稱善。
entries.en: He had old ties with Shen Youzhi and was ordered to write a letter warning him; the Founding Emperor read it and praised it highly.
entries.literal: He had old ties with Shen Youzhi and was ordered to write a letter admonishing and instructing Youzhi; the Founder read it and praised it as good.

entries.zh: 除步兵校尉。
entries.en: He was appointed colonel of foot soldiers.
entries.literal: He was appointed Colonel of Foot Soldiers.

entries.zh: 齊國建，上欲置齊郡於京邑，議者以江右土沃，流民所歸，乃治瓜步，以懷慰爲輔國將軍、齊郡太守。
entries.en: When the Qi state was founded, the emperor wished to establish Qi commandery in the capital region, but advisers argued that the fertile lands south of the Yangtze attracted displaced populations, so the seat was placed at Guabu instead, with Huaiwei appointed general who supports the state and grand administrator of Qi commandery.
entries.literal: When the State of Qi was established, the sovereign wished to place Qi commandery in the capital region. Discussants said that the lands south of the Yangtze were fertile soil to which floating population returned, so they governed Guabu instead, and Huaiwei was made General Who Supports the State and Grand Administrator of Qi commandery.

entries.zh: 上謂懷慰曰：「齊邦是王業所基，吾方以爲顯任。
entries.en: The emperor said to Huaiwei, "The Qi state is the foundation of our royal enterprise, and I intend this as a weighty appointment.
entries.literal: The sovereign said to Huaiwei: "The Qi state is the foundation of our royal enterprise; I intend this as a prominent appointment.

entries.zh: 經理之事，一以委卿。」
entries.en: All matters of administration I entrust entirely to you."
entries.literal: All matters of administration I entirely entrust to you."

entries.zh: 又手勑曰：「有文事者，必有武備。
entries.en: He also wrote a personal edict: "Where there are civil affairs, there must also be military preparedness.
entries.literal: He also wrote a personal edict saying: "Where there are civil affairs, there must also be military preparation.

entries.zh: 今賜卿玉環刀一口。」
entries.en: I now bestow upon you a jade ring-hilted sword."
entries.literal: Now I bestow upon you one jade ring-hilted sword."

entries.zh: 懷慰至郡，修治城郭，安集居民，墾廢田二百頃，決沈湖灌溉。
entries.en: When Huaiwei arrived at the commandery, he repaired the walls and moats, settled the people, reclaimed two hundred qing of abandoned fields, and opened Shen Lake for irrigation.
entries.literal: When Huaiwei reached the commandery, he repaired the walls and moats, settled and gathered the inhabitants, reclaimed two hundred qing of abandoned fields, and opened Shen Lake for irrigation.

entries.zh: 不受禮謁，民有餉其新米一斛者，懷慰出所食麥飯示之，曰：「旦食有餘，幸不煩此。」
entries.en: He accepted no gifts or courtesy calls. When a commoner brought him one hu of new rice, Huaiwei showed him the barley meal he was eating and said, "My morning meal still leaves me with plenty; please do not trouble yourself."
entries.literal: He accepted no gifts or visits. When a commoner brought him one hu of new rice as tribute, Huaiwei brought out the barley meal he was eating and showed it to him, saying: "My morning meal still has surplus; kindly do not trouble yourself with this."

entries.zh: 因著《廉吏論》以達其意。
entries.en: He then wrote An Essay on Incorrupt Officials to make his meaning clear.
entries.literal: He therefore wrote An Essay on Incorrupt Officials to express his intent.

entries.zh: 太祖聞之，手勑褒賞。
entries.en: The Founding Emperor heard of it and sent a personal edict commending and rewarding him.
entries.literal: The Founding Emperor heard of it and wrote a personal edict commending and rewarding him.

entries.zh: 進督秦、沛二郡。
entries.en: He was promoted to oversee the commanderies of Qin and Pei.
entries.literal: He was promoted to oversee the two commanderies of Qin and Pei.

entries.zh: 妻子在都，賜米三百斛。
entries.en: His wife and children remained in the capital, and he was granted three hundred hu of rice.
entries.literal: His wife and children were in the capital; he was granted three hundred hu of rice.

entries.zh: 兖州刺史柳世隆與懷慰書曰：「膠東淵化，潁川致美，以今方古，曾何足云。」
entries.en: Yanzhou inspector Liu Shilong wrote to Huaiwei, "Jiaodong's deep transformation and Yingchuan's bringing of beauty—set against your work today, what are those old examples even worth mentioning?"
entries.literal: Yanzhou Inspector Liu Shilong wrote to Huaiwei: "Jiaodong's deep transformation and Yingchuan's bringing of beauty—compared with the present, what are those worth mentioning?"

entries.zh: 在郡二年，遷正員郎，領青冀二州中正。
entries.en: After two years in the commandery, he was promoted to regular staff gentleman and concurrently served as chief arbiter for Qing and Ji provinces.
entries.literal: After two years in the commandery, he was transferred to regular staff gentleman and concurrently served as chief arbiter for Qing and Ji provinces.

entries.zh: 武陵王曄爲會稽，以憲爲左軍司馬。
entries.en: When the Prince of Wuling Ye was posted to Kuaiji, Xian was made left army aide-de-camp.
entries.literal: When the Prince of Wuling Ye was at Kuaiji, Xian was made Left Army aide-de-camp.

entries.zh: 太祖以山陰戶衆難治，欲分爲兩縣。
entries.en: The Founding Emperor, because Shanyin's population was large and difficult to govern, wished to divide the county in two.
entries.literal: The Founding Emperor, because Shanyin's population was large and difficult to govern, wished to divide it into two counties.

entries.zh: 世祖啓曰：「縣豈不可治，但用不得其人耳。」
entries.en: Emperor Wu submitted a memorial saying, "The county is not untamable—it is only that the wrong man has been put in charge."
entries.literal: Emperor Wu submitted a memorial saying: "The county is not untamable—only the wrong man has been put in charge."

entries.zh: 乃以憲帶山陰令，政聲大著。
entries.en: Thereupon Xian was appointed concurrently magistrate of Shanyin, and his reputation for good governance spread widely.
entries.literal: Thereupon Xian was appointed concurrently magistrate of Shanyin, and his reputation for good governance became widely noted.

entries.zh: 孔稚珪請假東歸，謂人曰：「沈令料事特有天才。」
entries.en: Kong Zhigui took leave to return east and said to people, "Magistrate Shen's handling of affairs shows a special genius for judgment."
entries.literal: Kong Zhigui took leave to return east and said to people: "Magistrate Shen's handling of affairs shows a special genius for judgment."

entries.zh: 加寧朔將軍。
entries.en: He was given the additional title general who pacifies the north.
entries.literal: He was given the additional title General Who Pacifies the North.

entries.zh: 王敬則爲會稽，憲仍留爲鎮軍長史，令如故。
entries.en: When Wang Jingze was posted to Kuaiji, Xian remained chief secretary to the pacification army, with his magistracy unchanged.
entries.literal: When Wang Jingze was at Kuaiji, Xian remained as chief secretary to the Pacification Army, with his magistracy unchanged.

entries.zh: 太祖輔政，以山陰獄訟煩積，復以琰爲山陰令。
entries.en: When the Founding Emperor served as regent, lawsuits in Shanyin had again piled up, so he reappointed Yan as magistrate of Shanyin.
entries.literal: When the Founder assisted in government, because prison lawsuits in Shanyin piled up in annoyance, he again appointed Yan magistrate of Shanyin.

entries.zh: 賣針賣糖老姥爭團絲，來詣琰，琰不辨覈，縳團絲於柱鞭之，密視有鐵屑，乃罰賣糖者。
entries.en: An old woman who sold needles and one who sold sugar disputed a ball of silk and brought the case to Yan. Without questioning either party, he tied the silk to a pillar and whipped it; watching closely, he saw iron filings and then punished the sugar-seller.
entries.literal: An old woman who sold needles and an old woman who sold sugar disputed a ball of silk thread and came before Yan. Yan did not distinguish and verify; he bound the silk ball to a pillar and flogged it, secretly watched and saw iron filings, and then punished the sugar-seller.

entries.zh: 二野父爭雞，琰各問「何以食雞」，一人云「粟」，一人云「豆」，乃破雞得粟，罪言豆者。
entries.en: Two peasants disputed ownership of a chicken. Yan asked each, "With what do you feed the chicken?" One said, "Millet"; the other said, "Beans." He slaughtered the bird, found millet in its crop, and punished the man who had claimed beans.
entries.literal: Two countrymen disputed a chicken. Yan asked each, 'With what do you feed the chicken?' One said 'millet,' one said 'beans.' He then broke open the chicken and found millet, and punished the one who had said beans.

entries.zh: 縣內稱神明，無敢復爲偷盜。
entries.en: The district hailed him as uncannily wise, and no one dared steal again.
entries.literal: Within the district he was called divine and perspicacious; none dared again to be thieves.

entries.zh: 琰父子竝著奇績，江左鮮有。
entries.en: Father and son Yan together achieved extraordinary records, rarely matched in the lands south of the Yangtze.
entries.literal: Father and son Yan together achieved extraordinary records; east of the Yangtze there were few such cases.

entries.zh: 世云「諸傅有《治縣譜》，子孫相傳，不以示人」。
entries.en: People said, "The various Fu have a Register of Governing Districts, handed down among descendants and not shown to others."
entries.literal: The age says, 'The various Fu have a Register of Governing Districts, handed down among descendants and not shown to others.'

entries.zh: 昇明二年，太祖擢爲假節、督益寧二州軍事、建威將軍、益州刺史、宋寧太守。
entries.en: In the second year of Shengming the Founding Emperor promoted him to provisional bearer of the staff, commander of Yi and Ning, general who establishes might, governor of Yi, and grand administrator of Songning.
entries.literal: In the second year of Shengming the Founding Emperor promoted him to bearer of the provisional staff, commander of military affairs in Yi and Ning, General Who Establishes Might, governor of Yi, and grand administrator of Songning.

entries.zh: 建元元年，進號寧朔將軍。
entries.en: In the first year of Jianyuan his title was advanced to general who pacifies the north.
entries.literal: In the first year of Jianyuan his title was advanced to General Who Pacifies the North.

entries.zh: 四年，徵驍騎將軍，黃門郎。
entries.en: In the fourth year he was recalled as general of valiant cavalry and gentleman at the Yellow Gate.
entries.literal: In the fourth year he was summoned as General of Valiant Cavalry and Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.

entries.zh: 永明二年，遷建威將軍、安陸王北中郎長史，改寧朔將軍。
entries.en: In the second year of Yongming he was transferred to general who establishes might and chief clerk to the northern gentlemen of the interior under the Prince of Anlu, with his title changed to general who pacifies the north.
entries.literal: In the second year of Yongming he was transferred to General Who Establishes Might and chief clerk to the Northern Gentlemen of the Interior under the Prince of Anlu; his title was changed to General Who Pacifies the North.

entries.zh: 明年，徙廬陵王安西長史、南郡內史，行荊州事。
entries.en: The next year he was moved to chief clerk to the pacify-the-west army under the Prince of Luling and interior minister of Nan commandery, acting governor of Jingzhou.
entries.literal: The next year he was moved to chief clerk to the Pacify-the-West army under the Prince of Luling and interior minister of Nan commandery, acting in Jingzhou affairs.

entries.zh: 五年，卒。
entries.en: In the fifth year he died.
entries.literal: In the fifth year he died.

entries.zh: 琰喪西還，有詔出臨。
entries.en: As Yan's coffin was borne westward, an edict ordered the emperor to attend in person.
entries.literal: As Yan's coffin returned westward, an edict ordered the sovereign to come out and attend.

entries.zh: 從祖弟顗，字彥齊。
entries.en: His younger clansman cousin Yi, courtesy name Yanqi.
entries.literal: His younger clansman cousin Yi, courtesy name Yanqi.

entries.zh: 少有異操。
entries.en: From youth he held unusual principles.
entries.literal: From youth he had unusual principles.

entries.zh: 泰始中，於總明觀聽講，不讓劉秉席，秉用爲參軍。
entries.en: During the Taishi reign, while listening to lectures at Zongming Observatory, he would not yield his seat to Liu Bing, who then employed him as adjutant.
entries.literal: During Taishi, while listening to lectures at Zongming Observatory, he would not yield his seat to Liu Bing; Bing employed him as adjutant.

entries.zh: 昇明末，爲奉朝請。
entries.en: Late in the Shengming era he served as attendant at court.
entries.literal: Late in the Shengming era he served as attendant at court.

entries.zh: 齊臺建，世子裴妃須外戚譜，顗不與，遂分籍。
entries.en: When the Qi regime was established, the crown prince's Pei consort needed a genealogy of maternal relatives; Yi refused to provide it, and they therefore split the family registry.
entries.literal: When the Qi regime was established, the crown prince's Pei consort needed a maternal relatives' genealogy; Yi refused to provide it, and they therefore split the registry.

entries.zh: 太祖受禪，上表誹謗，掛冠去，伏誅。
entries.en: When the Founding Emperor accepted the abdication, Yi submitted a memorial slandering the court, resigned his office, and fled; he was executed.
entries.literal: When the Founding Emperor accepted the abdication, Yi submitted a memorial slandering the court, hung up his cap and departed; he was executed.

entries.zh: 昇明二年，西中郎將晃爲豫州，太祖擢憲爲晃長史，南梁太守，行州事。
entries.en: In the second year of Shengming, when General of the Western Gentlemen of the Interior Huang was posted to Yuzhou, the Founding Emperor promoted Xian to Huang's chief secretary, grand administrator of Nanliang, and acting provincial governor.
entries.literal: In the second year of Shengming, when General of the Western Gentlemen of the Interior Huang was at Yuzhou, the Founding Emperor promoted Xian to Huang's chief secretary, Grand Administrator of Nanliang, acting in provincial affairs.

entries.zh: 遷豫章王諮議，未拜，坐事免官。
entries.en: He was transferred to advisory counselor under the Prince of Yuzhang, but before he could assume the post he was dismissed from office for an offense.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Advisory Counselor under the Prince of Yuzhang; before assuming the post he was dismissed from office for an offense.

entries.zh: 復除安成王冠軍、武陵王征虜參軍，遷少府卿。
entries.en: He was again appointed adjutant to the champion under the Prince of Ancheng and adjutant to the barbarian subduer under the Prince of Wuling, then promoted to director of the palace treasury.
entries.literal: He was again appointed adjutant to the Champion under the Prince of Ancheng and adjutant to the Barbarian Subduer under the Prince of Wuling, then promoted to Director of the Palace Treasury.

entries.zh: 少府管掌市易，與民交關，有吏能者，皆更此職。
entries.en: The palace treasury managed market transactions and dealt directly with the people, so officials with real administrative talent were usually rotated through this post.
entries.literal: The Palace Treasury managed market transactions and had dealings with the people; those with administrative talent were usually rotated through this post.

entries.zh: 遷王儉鎮軍長史。
entries.en: He was transferred to chief secretary to the pacification army under Wang Jian.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Chief Secretary to the Pacification Army under Wang Jian.

entries.zh: 遷尚書左丞，又以職事知名。
entries.en: He was promoted to left assistant director in the Masters of Writing and again won renown for his competence in office.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Left Assistant of the Masters of Writing and again became known for his official duties.

entries.zh: 轉前軍將軍，兼少府。
entries.en: He was transferred to general of the forward army and concurrently minister of the palace supplies.
entries.literal: He was transferred to General of the Forward Army and concurrently Minister of the Palace Supplies.

entries.zh: 遷驍騎將軍，少府如故。
entries.en: He was promoted to general of valiant cavalry while retaining his post at the ministry of palace supplies.
entries.literal: He was transferred to General of Valiant Cavalry, with the Ministry of Palace Supplies as before.

entries.zh: 出爲寧朔將軍、高宗冠軍征虜長史、江夏內史。
entries.en: He was sent out as general who pacifies the north, chief clerk to the champion who conquers the barbarians under the High Ancestor, and interior minister of Jiangxia.
entries.literal: He went out as General Who Pacifies the North, Chief Clerk to the Champion Who Conquers the Barbarians under the High Ancestor, and Interior Minister of Jiangxia.

entries.zh: 還爲正員常侍，兼左民尚書、廷尉卿。
entries.en: On returning to court he was appointed regular attendant-in-ordinary and concurrently director for the left people in the Masters of Writing and minister of justice.
entries.literal: On return he became Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and concurrently Master of Writing for the Left People and Minister of Justice.

entries.zh: 出爲臨海太守，在任清約，罷郡還，獻乾薑二十斤，世祖嫌少，及知琇之清，乃歎息。
entries.en: He was sent out as grand administrator of Linhai and governed with austere integrity. When his term ended he presented twenty jin of dried ginger as a gift. Emperor Wu at first thought the offering too meager, but on learning how incorrupt Xiuzhi was, he sighed in admiration.
entries.literal: He went out as Grand Administrator of Linhai; in office he was pure and abstemious. When he finished his commandery and returned, he presented twenty jin of dried ginger. Emperor Wu thought it too little, but when he learned of Xiuzhi's purity he sighed.

entries.zh: 除武陵王前軍長史，未拜，仍出爲輔國將軍，監吳興郡，尋拜太守，治稱清嚴。
entries.en: He was appointed chief clerk to the forward army of the Prince of Wuling but never took up the post; instead he was sent out as general who supports the state to oversee Wuxing commandery, soon confirmed as grand administrator, where his rule was praised as pure and stern.
entries.literal: He was appointed Chief Clerk of the Forward Army under the Prince of Wuling but did not receive the appointment; he was still sent out as General Who Supports the State, overseer of Wuxing commandery, and soon appointed Grand Administrator, with governance praised as pure and stern.

entries.zh: 懷慰本名聞慰，世祖卽位，以與舅氏名同，勑改之。
entries.en: Huaiwei's original name was Wenwei; when Emperor Wu took the throne, an edict changed it because it matched his maternal uncle's name.
entries.literal: Huaiwei's original name was Wenwei; when Emperor Wu ascended the throne, because it was the same as his maternal uncle's name, an edict changed it.

entries.zh: 出監東陽郡，爲吏民所安。
entries.en: He went out as overseer of Dongyang commandery, where officials and commoners alike found security under his rule.
entries.literal: He went out as overseer of Dongyang commandery and was trusted by officials and people.

entries.zh: 還兼安陸王北中郎司馬。
entries.en: On his return he also served as northern gentlemen of the interior aide-de-camp to the Prince of Anlu.
entries.literal: Upon return he also served as Northern Gentlemen of the Interior aide-de-camp to the Prince of Anlu.

entries.zh: 永明九年，卒。
entries.en: He died in the ninth year of Yongming.
entries.literal: In the ninth year of Yongming he died.

entries.zh: 年四十五。
entries.en: He was forty-five years old.
entries.literal: He was forty-five.

entries.zh: 明帝卽位，謂僕射徐孝嗣曰：「劉懷慰若在，朝廷不憂無清吏也。」
entries.en: When Emperor Ming took the throne, he said to chief minister Xu Xiaosi, "If Liu Huaiwei were still alive, the court would never worry about lacking incorrupt officials."
entries.literal: When Emperor Ming ascended the throne, he said to Chief Minister Xu Xiaosi: "If Liu Huaiwei were still alive, the court would not worry about lacking incorrupt officials."

entries.zh: 懷慰與濟陽江淹、陳郡袁彖善，亦著文翰。
entries.en: Huaiwei was on good terms with Jiang Yan of Jiyang and Yuan Luan of Chen commandery, and he also wrote literary works.
entries.literal: Huaiwei was on good terms with Jiang Yan of Jiyang and Yuan Luan of Chen commandery; he also wrote literary works.

entries.zh: 永明初，獻《皇德論》云。
entries.en: At the beginning of the Yongming reign he submitted An Essay on Imperial Virtue, which reads:
entries.literal: At the beginning of Yongming he presented An Essay on Imperial Virtue, which says:

entries.zh: 建武初，爲王玄邈安北長史、廣陵太守。
entries.en: At the beginning of the Jianwu reign he served as chief secretary for pacification of the north under Wang Xuanyao and grand administrator of Guangling.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Jianwu he served as Chief Secretary for Pacification of the North under Wang Xuanyao and Grand Administrator of Guangling.

entries.zh: 明帝以其在事無所啓奏，代還，責之。
entries.en: Emperor Ming, because during his tenure he had submitted no memorials, replaced and recalled him and reproached him.
entries.literal: Emperor Ming, because during his tenure he had submitted no memorials, replaced and recalled him and reproached him.

entries.zh: 昭明曰：「臣不欲競執關楗故耳。」
entries.en: Zhaoming said, "Your servant did not wish to compete over holding the gate bars, that is all."
entries.literal: Zhaoming said: "Your servant did not wish to compete over holding the gate bars, that is all."

entries.zh: 昭明歷郡皆有勤績，常謂人曰：「人生何事須聚蓄，一身之外，亦復何須？
entries.en: Zhaoming achieved diligent results in every commandery he served and often told people, "What in life requires hoarding? Beyond one's own person, what else is needed?
entries.literal: Zhaoming in every commandery he served had diligent achievements; he often told people: "What in life requires hoarding? Beyond one's own person, what else is needed?

entries.zh: 子孫若不才，我聚彼散；
entries.en: If one's descendants lack talent, what one gathers they will squander;
entries.literal: If descendants lack talent, what I gather they will squander;

entries.zh: 若能自立，則不如一經。」
entries.en: If they can stand on their own, one classic is worth more than a fortune."
entries.literal: If they can stand on their own, one classic is better than wealth."

entries.zh: 故終身不治產業。
entries.en: Therefore he never managed property or estates throughout his life.
entries.literal: Therefore throughout his life he did not manage property or estates.

entries.zh: 中興二年，卒。
entries.en: He died in the second year of Zhongxing.
entries.literal: In the second year of Zhongxing he died.

entries.zh: 高宗輔政，防制諸蕃，致密旨於上佐。
entries.en: When the High Ancestor held the regency, he checked the various princes and conveyed confidential instructions to his chief subordinates.
entries.literal: When the High Ancestor assisted in government, he checked and controlled the various princes, conveying confidential instructions to chief subordinates.

entries.zh: 隆昌元年，遷琇之爲寧朔將軍、晉熙王冠軍長史，行郢州事，江夏內史。
entries.en: In the first year of Longchang, Xiuzhi was transferred to general who pacifies the north, chief clerk to the champion under the Prince of Jinxi, acting governor of Yingzhou, and interior minister of Jiangxia.
entries.literal: In the first year of Longchang, Xiuzhi was transferred to General Who Pacifies the North, chief clerk to the Champion under the Prince of Jinxi, acting in Yingzhou affairs, and interior minister of Jiangxia.

entries.zh: 琇之辭，不許。
entries.en: Xiuzhi declined, but the appointment was not allowed.
entries.literal: Xiuzhi declined; he was not permitted.

entries.zh: 未拜，卒。
entries.en: Before he could take up the post he died.
entries.literal: Before receiving the appointment he died.

entries.zh: 帝以故宅起湘宮寺，費極奢侈。
entries.en: The emperor built the Xiang Palace Temple on the site of his former residence at enormous expense.
entries.literal: The Emperor raised the Xiang Palace Temple on his former residence; the expense was extremely luxurious.

entries.zh: 以孝武莊嚴剎七層，帝欲起十層，不可立，分爲兩剎，各五層。
entries.en: Emperor Xiaowu's Zhuangyan Monastery had stood seven stories high; the emperor wanted ten but the structure would not bear it, so he split it into two pagodas of five stories each.
entries.literal: Because Emperor Xiaowu's Zhuangyan Monastery had seven stories, the Emperor wished to build ten; it could not stand, so it was divided into two monasteries of five stories each.

entries.zh: 新安太守巢尚之罷郡還，見帝，曰：「卿至湘宮寺未？
entries.en: Chao Shangzhi, who had finished his term as grand administrator of Xin'an, came to court and asked the emperor, 'Have you visited the Xiang Palace Temple yet?
entries.literal: Chao Shangzhi, Grand Administrator of Xin'an, finished his commandery and returned; seeing the Emperor he said, 'Have you been to the Xiang Palace Temple yet?

entries.zh: 我起此寺，是大功德。」
entries.en: I built this temple—it is a great act of merit.'
entries.literal: I raised this temple—it is great merit.'

entries.zh: 愿在側曰：「陛下起此寺，皆是百姓賣兒貼婦錢，佛若有知，當悲哭哀愍，罪高佛圖，有何功德？」
entries.en: Yuan, standing beside them, said, 'Your Majesty, this temple was paid for with money from common folk who sold their sons and pawned their wives. If the Buddha knew, he would weep in pity; the sin towers higher than any pagoda—where is the merit in that?'
entries.literal: Yuan at his side said, 'Your Majesty raised this temple—all of it is money from the common people selling sons and pawning wives. If Buddha had knowledge, he would weep in grief and pity; the guilt exceeds Buddha's stupa—what merit is there?'

entries.zh: 尚書令袁粲在坐，爲之失色。
entries.en: Minister-in-Chief Yuan Can, who was present, turned pale at this.
entries.literal: Minister-in-Chief Yuan Can was seated and lost color on his account.

entries.zh: 帝乃怒，使人驅下殿，愿徐去無異容。
entries.en: The emperor flew into a rage and had him driven from the hall. Yuan withdrew slowly, his expression unchanged.
entries.literal: The Emperor then grew angry and had men drive him down from the hall. Yuan departed slowly without change of countenance.

entries.zh: 以舊恩，少日中，已復召入。
entries.en: Thanks to their old bond, he was summoned back before noon the same day.
entries.literal: Because of old favor, before midday he was again summoned in.

entries.zh: 永明三年，使虜，世祖謂之曰：「以卿有將命之才，使還，當以一郡相賞。」
entries.en: In the third year of Yongming he was sent as envoy to the northern barbarians; Emperor Wu said to him, "Because you have talent for bearing imperial orders, when you return I shall reward you with a commandery."
entries.literal: In the third year of Yongming he was sent as envoy to the northern barbarians; Emperor Wu said to him: "Because you have talent for bearing imperial orders, when you return I shall reward you with a commandery."

entries.zh: 還爲始安內史。
entries.en: On his return he was appointed interior steward of Shian.
entries.literal: Upon return he became interior steward of Shian.

entries.zh: 郡民龔玄宣，云神人與其玉印玉板書，不須筆，吹紙便成字。
entries.en: A district resident named Gong Xuanxuan claimed that a spirit had given him a jade seal and jade tablet for writing; without a brush, he need only blow on paper and characters would appear.
entries.literal: A district resident, Gong Xuanxuan, claimed that a spirit man gave him a jade seal and jade tablet writing; without a brush, he need only blow on paper and characters would form.

entries.zh: 自稱「龔聖人」，以此惑衆。
entries.en: He called himself "the Sage Gong" and used this to mislead the people.
entries.literal: He called himself "the Sage Gong" and used this to delude the masses.

entries.zh: 前後郡守敬事之，昭明付獄治罪。
entries.en: Previous grand administrators had treated him with reverence, but Zhaoming handed him over to prison for punishment.
entries.literal: Previous grand administrators had treated him with reverence; Zhaoming handed him over to prison for punishment.

entries.zh: 及還，甚貧罄。
entries.en: When he returned from office he was utterly destitute.
entries.literal: When he returned he was utterly destitute.

entries.zh: 世祖曰：「裴昭明罷郡還，遂無宅。
entries.en: Emperor Wu said, "Pei Zhaoming returned from leaving a commandery and has no house at all.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu said: "Pei Zhaoming returned from leaving a commandery and has no house at all.

entries.zh: 我不諳書，不知古人中誰比？」
entries.en: I am not versed in books—who among the ancients compares with him?"
entries.literal: I am not versed in books—who among the ancients compares with him?"

entries.zh: 遷射聲校尉。
entries.en: He was transferred to colonel of the archers who shoot at sound.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Colonel of the Archers Who Shoot at Sound.

entries.zh: 九年，復遣北使。
entries.en: In the ninth year he was again sent as envoy to the north.
entries.literal: In the ninth year he was again sent as envoy to the north.

entries.zh: 遷爲冠軍長史，行南豫州事，晉安王後軍長史、廣陵太守。
entries.en: He was transferred to chief secretary under the champion and acting governor of Southern Yuzhou, then chief secretary to the rear army under the Prince of Jin'an and grand administrator of Guangling.
entries.literal: He was transferred to chief secretary under the Champion, acting in Southern Yuzhou affairs, then chief secretary to the Rear Army under the Prince of Jin'an and Grand Administrator of Guangling.

entries.zh: 西陽王子明代爲南兖州，憲仍留爲冠軍長史，太守如故，頻行州府事。
entries.en: When Ziming, Prince of Xiyang, was posted to Southern Yanzhou, Xian remained chief secretary under the champion with his grand administrator post unchanged, repeatedly acting in provincial and prefectural affairs.
entries.literal: When Ziming, Prince of Xiyang, was at Southern Yanzhou, Xian remained chief secretary under the Champion with his grand administrator post unchanged, repeatedly acting in provincial and prefectural affairs.

entries.zh: 永明八年，子明典籤劉道濟取府州五十人役自給，又役子明左右，及船仗贓私百萬，爲有司所奏，世祖怒，賜道濟死。
entries.en: In the eighth year of Yongming, Ziming's chief clerk Liu Daoji conscripted fifty men from the prefecture and province for his own use, also used labor from Ziming's personal attendants, and embezzled a million in ships, arms, and private goods; when the responsible officials memorialized the case, Emperor Wu was furious and ordered Daoji to death.
entries.literal: In the eighth year of Yongming, Ziming's chief clerk Liu Daoji conscripted fifty men from the prefecture and province for his own use, also used labor from Ziming's personal attendants, and embezzled a million in ships, arms, and private goods; memorialized by the responsible officials, Emperor Wu was furious and ordered Daoji to death.

entries.zh: 憲坐不糾，免官。
entries.en: Xian was punished for failing to investigate and was dismissed from office.
entries.literal: Xian was punished for failing to investigate and was dismissed from office.

entries.zh: 尋復爲長史、輔國將軍，以疾去官。
entries.en: Soon after he was again appointed chief secretary and general who supports the state, then left office due to illness.
entries.literal: Soon after he was again appointed chief secretary and General Who Supports the State, then left office due to illness.

entries.zh: 除散騎常侍，未拜，卒。
entries.en: He was appointed cavalier attendant-in-ordinary but died before assuming the post.
entries.literal: He was appointed Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary but died before assuming the post.

entries.zh: 當世稱爲良吏。
entries.en: His contemporaries acclaimed him as a good official.
entries.literal: His contemporaries acclaimed him as a good official.

entries.zh: 先是，四年，滎陽毛惠素爲少府卿，吏才強而治事清刻。
entries.en: Earlier, in the fourth year, Mao Huisu of Xingyang served as minister of the palace supplies; he was a forceful administrator who ran affairs with austere precision.
entries.literal: Earlier, in the fourth year, Mao Huisu of Xingyang was Minister of the Palace Supplies—a man of strong administrative talent who governed affairs with austere clarity.

entries.zh: 勑市銅官碧青一千二百斤供御畫，用錢六十萬。
entries.en: An edict ordered the purchase of twelve hundred jin of malachite pigment from the copper office for imperial painting, at a cost of six hundred thousand cash.
entries.literal: An edict ordered the purchase from the copper office of twelve hundred jin of malachite blue-green for imperial painting, at a cost of six hundred thousand cash.

entries.zh: 有讒惠素納利者，世祖怒，勑尚書評賈，貴二十八萬餘，有司奏之，伏誅。
entries.en: Someone accused Huisu of taking a kickback. Emperor Wu was furious and ordered the Masters of Writing to reassess the price at just over two hundred eighty thousand cash; the authorities memorialized the case, and Huisu was executed.
entries.literal: Someone slandered Huisu for taking profit. Emperor Wu grew angry and ordered the Masters of Writing to assess the price; it was valued at a little over two hundred eighty thousand, the relevant offices memorialized, and he was executed.

entries.zh: 死後家徒四壁，上甚悔恨。
entries.en: After his death his home was utterly bare, and the emperor deeply regretted what had been done.
entries.literal: After his death his house held only bare walls; the sovereign deeply regretted it.

entries.zh: 南齊書卷五十三‧列傳第三十四 良政
entries.en: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 53, Biographies 34: Virtuous Officials
entries.literal: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 53, Biographies 34: Good Governance

entries.zh: 公孫僧遠，會稽剡人也。
entries.en: Gongsun Sengyuan was from Shan county in Kuaiji.
entries.literal: Gongsun Sengyuan was a native of Shan in Kuaiji.

entries.zh: 治父喪至孝，事母及伯父甚謹，年饑穀貴，僧遠省餐減食，以供母、伯。
entries.en: He was deeply filial in mourning his father and scrupulous in caring for his mother and uncle. In famine years, when grain was costly, he ate less himself so that they might have enough.
entries.literal: In observing mourning for his father he was supremely filial; in serving his mother and his father's elder brother he was most careful. In years of famine when grain was dear, Sengyuan reduced his own meals to supply his mother and uncle.

entries.zh: 弟亡，無以葬，身販貼與隣里，供斂送之費。
entries.en: When his younger brother died and he had no money for the funeral, he indentured himself to neighbors to pay for the burial.
entries.literal: When his younger brother died and there was no means to bury him, he sold himself on bond to his neighbors to provide the expenses of encoffining and burial.

entries.zh: 躬負土，手種松柏。
entries.en: He carried the earth for the grave himself and planted pine and cypress trees with his own hands.
entries.literal: He personally carried earth on his back and planted pine and cypress with his own hands.

entries.zh: 兄姊未婚嫁，乃自賣為之成禮。
entries.en: His elder brother and sister were still unmarried, so he sold himself once more to provide for their weddings.
entries.literal: His elder brother and sister were still unmarried, so he sold himself again to provide for their weddings.

entries.zh: 名聞郡縣。
entries.en: His reputation spread throughout the region.
entries.literal: His fame spread through the commandery and county.

entries.zh: 太祖即位，遣兼散騎常侍虞炎等十二部使行天下，建元三年，表列僧遠等二十三人，詔竝表門閭，蠲租稅。
entries.en: When Emperor Gao took the throne he sent twelve missions, led by Yu Yan, Acting Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, to tour the empire. In the third year of Jianyuan, memorials named Sengyuan and twenty-two others; an edict ordered commemorative placards erected at their gates and their rents and taxes remitted.
entries.literal: When the Founding Emperor took the throne, he dispatched twelve groups of envoys led by Acting Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry Yu Yan and others to travel throughout the realm; in the third year of Jianyuan, memorials listed Sengyuan and twenty-two others, and an edict ordered that their household gates all be honored with commemorative placards and that their rents and taxes be remitted.

entries.zh: 朱謙之字處光，吳郡錢唐人也。
entries.en: Zhu Qianzhi, courtesy name Chuguang, was from Qiantang in Wu commandery.
entries.literal: Zhu Qianzhi, courtesy name Chuguang, was a native of Qiantang in Wu commandery.

entries.zh: 父昭之，以學解稱於鄉里。
entries.en: His father Zhaozhi was renowned in the district for learning.
entries.literal: His father Zhaozhi was famed in the village for learning and understanding.

entries.zh: 謙之年數歲，所生母亡，昭之假葬田側，為族人朱幼方燎火所焚。
entries.en: When Qianzhi was still a child his birth mother died. Zhaozhi had her buried provisionally by the fields, but kinsman Zhu Youfang's brush fire burned the grave.
entries.literal: When Qianzhi was only a few years old, his birth mother died; Zhaozhi had her provisionally buried beside the fields, and the grave was burned by a brush fire set by his clansman Zhu Youfang.

entries.zh: 同產姉密語之，謙之雖小，便哀戚如持喪。
entries.en: His elder sister told him in secret. Though he was still small, he grieved as though in full mourning.
entries.literal: His elder sister by the same mother told him in secret; though Qianzhi was small, he grieved as though in mourning.

entries.zh: 年長不婚娶。
entries.en: When he grew up he never married.
entries.literal: When he grew older he did not marry.

entries.zh: 永明中，手刃殺幼方，詣獄自繫。
entries.en: During Yongming he slew Youfang with his own hand and surrendered himself to prison.
entries.literal: During Yongming he killed Youfang with his own hand and went to prison to surrender himself.

entries.zh: 縣令申靈勗表上，別駕孔稚珪、兼記室劉璡、司徒左西掾張融牋與刺史豫章王曰：「禮開報仇之典，以申孝義之情；
entries.en: Magistrate Shen Lingxu reported the case. Kong Zhigui, Liu Lin, and Zhang Rong wrote to the Prince of Yuzhang, governor of the region: "Ritual law permits vengeance to express filial duty;
entries.literal: The Magistrate Shen Lingxu reported upward; the Attendant Counselor Kong Zhigui, Acting Recorder Liu Lin, and Western Section Clerk of the Minister of Works Zhang Rong wrote a memorial to the Governor, the Prince of Yuzhang, saying: "Rites open the statute of vengeance to express filial and righteous feeling;

entries.zh: 法斷相殺之條，以表權時之制。
entries.en: statutory law forbids killing to uphold the order of the age.
entries.literal: law sets the statute against mutual killing to display the expedient regulation of the age.

entries.zh: 謙之揮刃斬冤，旣申私禮；
entries.en: Qianzhi struck down his enemy and fulfilled his private duty;
entries.literal: Qianzhi swung his blade and cut down his enemy, already fulfilling private obligation;

entries.zh: 繫頸就死，又明公法。
entries.en: he bound himself and submitted to death, thereby honoring public law as well.
entries.literal: he bound his neck and submitted to death, thereby also clarifying public law.

entries.zh: 今仍殺之，則成當世罪人；
entries.en: If he is executed now, the court makes a criminal of him;
entries.literal: If he is now still put to death, he becomes a criminal of the age;

entries.zh: 宥而活之，即為盛朝孝子。
entries.en: if he is pardoned, he becomes a filial son of this flourishing age.
entries.literal: if he is pardoned and allowed to live, he becomes a filial son of this flourishing dynasty.

entries.zh: 殺一罪人，未足弘憲；
entries.en: Executing one man does little to magnify the law;
entries.literal: To kill one criminal is not enough to magnify the constitution;

entries.zh: 活一孝子，實廣風德。
entries.en: sparing one filial son truly broadens moral influence.
entries.literal: to spare one filial son truly broadens custom and virtue.

entries.zh: 張緒陸澄，是其鄉舊，應具來由。
entries.en: Zhang Xu and Lu Cheng, men of his district, should report the full circumstances.
entries.literal: Zhang Xu and Lu Cheng are old acquaintances of his village and should set forth the full circumstances.

entries.zh: 融等與謙之竝不相識，區區短見，深有恨然。」
entries.en: We do not know Qianzhi at all, yet in our limited view we feel deep regret at the case."
entries.literal: Rong and the others did not know Qianzhi at all; in our narrow view we deeply regret this."

entries.zh: 豫章王言之世祖，時吳郡太守王慈、太常張緒、尚書陸澄竝表論其事，世祖嘉其義，慮相復報，乃遣謙之隨曹虎西行。
entries.en: The Prince of Yuzhang reported to Emperor Wu. Administrator Wang Ci, Zhang Xu of the Ministry of Rites, and Lu Cheng of the Ministry of the Interior all memorialized on the case. The emperor admired Qianzhi's conduct but feared further blood feuds, and sent him west with Cao Hu.
entries.literal: The Prince of Yuzhang reported this to Emperor Wu; at the time the Administrator of Wu commandery Wang Ci, the Minister of Ceremonies Zhang Xu, and the Minister of the Interior Lu Cheng all memorialized on the matter. Emperor Wu admired his righteousness but feared mutual reprisals, and therefore sent Qianzhi west with Cao Hu.

entries.zh: 將發，幼方子惲於津陽門伺殺謙之，謙之之兄選之又刺殺惲，有司以聞。
entries.en: As he was about to leave, Youfang's son Yun ambushed and killed Qianzhi at Jinyang Gate. Qianzhi's brother Xuanzhi then stabbed Yun to death. Officials reported the matter.
entries.literal: As he was about to depart, Youfang's son Yun lay in wait at Jinyang Gate and killed Qianzhi; Qianzhi's elder brother Xuanzhi in turn stabbed and killed Yun. The authorities reported this.

entries.zh: 世祖曰：「此皆是義事，不可問。」
entries.en: Emperor Wu said: "These are all acts of righteousness and must not be prosecuted."
entries.literal: Emperor Wu said: "These are all matters of righteousness and must not be prosecuted."

entries.zh: 悉赦之。
entries.en: He pardoned them all.
entries.literal: He pardoned them all.

entries.zh: 吳興沈顗聞而歎曰：「弟死於孝，兄殉於義。
entries.en: Shen Yan of Wuxing sighed and said: "The younger brother died for filial piety; the elder brother gave his life for righteousness.
entries.literal: Shen Yan of Wuxing, hearing of it, sighed and said: "The younger brother died for filial piety; the elder brother gave his life for righteousness.

entries.zh: 孝友之節，萃此一門。」
entries.en: Filial piety and brotherly devotion are gathered in this one family."
entries.literal: The virtues of filial piety and brotherly devotion are gathered in this one household."

entries.zh: 選之字處林，有志節，著辯相論。
entries.en: Xuanzhi, courtesy name Chulin, was a man of resolve and wrote a treatise on physiognomy.
entries.literal: Xuanzhi, courtesy name Chulin, had resolve and integrity and wrote Discourse on Distinguishing Physiognomy.

entries.zh: 幼時顧歡見而異之，以女妻焉。
entries.en: As a youth Gu Huan was impressed by him and gave him his daughter in marriage.
entries.literal: In his youth Gu Huan saw him and was struck by him, giving him his daughter in marriage.

entries.zh: 官至江夏王參軍。
entries.en: He rose to serve as aide to the Prince of Jiangxia.
entries.literal: He reached office as Aide to the Prince of Jiangxia.

entries.zh: 封延伯字仲璉，渤海人也。
entries.en: Feng Yanbo, courtesy name Zhonglian, was from Bohai.
entries.literal: Feng Yanbo, courtesy name Zhonglian, was a native of Bohai.

entries.zh: 有學行，不與世人交，事寡嫂甚謹。
entries.en: A scholar of learning and integrity, he kept apart from worldly society and served his widowed sister-in-law with scrupulous care.
entries.literal: He had learning and conduct, did not associate with the world, and served his widowed sister-in-law with great care.

entries.zh: 州辟主簿，舉秀才，不就。
entries.en: The province summoned him as Registrar and recommended him as Cultivated Talent, but he declined both.
entries.literal: The province summoned him as Registrar; he was recommended as a Cultivated Talent but did not accept.

entries.zh: 後乃仕。
entries.en: Only later did he enter office.
entries.literal: Only later did he take office.

entries.zh: 垣崇祖為豫州，啟太祖用為長史，帶梁郡太守。
entries.en: When Yuan Chongzu governed Yuzhou he recommended Yanbo to Emperor Gao as Chief Clerk, with concurrent appointment as Administrator of Liang commandery.
entries.literal: When Yuan Chongzu was Governor of Yuzhou, he memorialized the Founding Emperor to appoint Yanbo Chief Clerk, concurrently serving as Administrator of Liang commandery.

entries.zh: 以疾自免，僑居東海，遂不至京師。
entries.en: He resigned citing illness, settled in Donghai, and never went to the capital again.
entries.literal: He resigned on grounds of illness and lived as a sojourner in Donghai, and thereafter never went to the capital.

entries.zh: 三世同財，為北州所宗附。
entries.en: Three generations held their wealth in common, and families throughout the north looked up to them.
entries.literal: Three generations held property in common and were looked to and attached to by the northern commanderies.

entries.zh: 豫章王辟中兵，不就，卒。
entries.en: The Prince of Yuzhang summoned him as a central army officer; he declined and died.
entries.literal: The Prince of Yuzhang summoned him as Central Army officer; he did not accept, and died.

entries.zh: 杜栖字孟山，吳郡錢唐人，徵士京產子也。
entries.en: Du Qi, courtesy name Mengshan, was from Qiantang in Wu commandery, son of the recluse Jingchan.
entries.literal: Du Qi, courtesy name Mengshan, was a native of Qiantang in Wu commandery, son of the Recluse Jingchan.

entries.zh: 同郡張融與京產相友，每相造言論，栖常在側。
entries.en: Zhang Rong of the same commandery was a friend of Jingchan. Whenever they met to discuss learning, Qi was always present.
entries.literal: Zhang Rong of the same commandery was friends with Jingchan; whenever they visited each other to discuss learning, Qi was always at their side.

entries.zh: 融指栖曰：「昔陳太丘之召元方，方之為劣。
entries.en: Rong pointed to Qi and said: "When Chen Taqiu summoned Yuanfang, Yuanfang was the lesser son.
entries.literal: Rong pointed to Qi and said: "When Chen Taqiu summoned Yuanfang, Yuanfang was the lesser.

entries.zh: 以今方古，古人何貴。」
entries.en: Compared with today, why should the ancients be prized?"
entries.literal: Comparing the present with antiquity, why should the ancients be esteemed?"

entries.zh: 栖出京師，從儒士劉瓛受學。
entries.en: Qi left the capital to study under the scholar Liu Huan.
entries.literal: Qi left the capital and studied under the scholar Liu Huan.

entries.zh: 善清言，能彈琴飲酒，名儒貴遊多敬待之。
entries.en: He excelled at pure conversation, played the zither, and drank wine; eminent scholars and noble travelers treated him with respect.
entries.literal: He was skilled in pure conversation, could play the zither and drink wine, and eminent scholars and noble travelers treated him with respect.

entries.zh: 中書郎周顒與京產書曰：「賢子學業清標，後來之秀。
entries.en: Zhou Yong of the Secretariat wrote to Jingchan: "Your worthy son's learning is clear and distinguished—a rising talent.
entries.literal: Zhou Yong, Attendant of the Secretariat, wrote to Jingchan: "Your worthy son's learning is clear and distinguished—a talent of the rising generation.

entries.zh: 嗟愛之懷，豈知云已。
entries.en: My affection for him—how can I say it has an end?
entries.literal: My sighing affection—how can I say it is ended?

entries.zh: 所謂人之英彥，若己有之也。」
entries.en: He is the sort of brilliant man one feels one already possesses."
entries.literal: What is called a brilliant man among people—I feel as though I already possess him."

entries.zh: 刺史豫章王聞其名，辟議曹從事，仍轉西曹佐。
entries.en: The Prince of Yuzhang, governor of the region, summoned him as an aide in the Deliberation Bureau and later made him western section assistant.
