entries.literal: The Governor, the Prince of Yuzhang, hearing his fame, summoned him as an aide in the Deliberation Bureau, and he was later transferred to Western Section Assistant.

entries.zh: 竟陵王子良數致禮接。
entries.en: Prince Ziliang of Jingling repeatedly honored him with invitations.
entries.literal: The Prince of Jingling, Ziliang, repeatedly sent him courteous invitations.

entries.zh: 國子祭酒何胤治禮，又重栖，以為學士，掌婚冠儀。
entries.en: He Yin, chancellor of the Imperial University and expert in ritual, also valued Qi, made him a university scholar, and put him in charge of marriage and capping ceremonies.
entries.literal: He Yin, Chancellor of the Imperial University, versed in ritual, also valued Qi and made him a University Scholar in charge of marriage and capping ceremonies.

entries.zh: 蕭叡明，南蘭陵人。
entries.en: Xiao Ruiming was from southern Lanling.
entries.literal: Xiao Ruiming was a native of Nan Lanling.

entries.zh: 領軍將軍諶從祖兄弟也。
entries.en: He was a cousin of General-in-Chief Zhen.
entries.literal: He was a paternal cousin of the General-in-Chief Zhen.

entries.zh: 父孝孫，左軍。
entries.en: His father Xiaosun commanded the Left Army.
entries.literal: His father Xiaosun was a commander of the Left Army.

entries.zh: 叡明初仕員外殿中將軍。
entries.en: Ruiming first served as acting general of the palace attendants.
entries.literal: Ruiming first served as Acting General of the Palace Attendants.

entries.zh: 少有至性，奉親謹篤。
entries.en: From youth he was deeply devoted and served his parents with scrupulous care.
entries.literal: From youth he had utmost sincerity and served his parents with careful devotion.

entries.zh: 母病躬禱，夕不假寐，及亡，不勝哀而卒。
entries.en: When his mother fell ill he prayed in person and did not sleep at night. When she died his grief overwhelmed him and he died.
entries.literal: When his mother fell ill he prayed in person, and at night did not sleep; when she died, he could not bear his grief and died.

entries.zh: 永明五年，世祖詔曰：「龍驤將軍、安西中兵參軍、松滋令蕭叡明，愛敬淳深，色養盡禮，喪過乎哀，遂致毀滅。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Yongming Emperor Wu decreed: "Xiao Ruiming, Flying Dragon General, central army aide of the Anxi army, and magistrate of Songzi, loved his parents with pure devotion, served them with joyful ritual care, and mourned so deeply that he destroyed himself.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Yongming, Emperor Wu issued an edict: "The Flying Dragon General, Central Army Aide of the Anxi Army, and Magistrate of Songzi, Xiao Ruiming, loved and revered with pure depth, nourished his parents with cheerful countenance and full ritual, and in mourning exceeded proper grief until he destroyed himself.

entries.zh: 雖未達聖教，而一至可愍。
entries.en: Though he did not attain the sage's teaching, his utmost devotion is deeply moving.
entries.literal: Though he did not attain the sage's teaching, his utmost sincerity is pitiable.

entries.zh: 宜加榮命，以矜善人。
entries.en: Let posthumous honors be granted to commend his goodness.
entries.literal: He should be granted posthumous honor to commend a good man.

entries.zh: 可贈中書郎。」
entries.en: Let him be posthumously appointed Attendant of the Secretariat."
entries.literal: Let him be posthumously appointed Attendant of the Secretariat."

entries.zh: 世祖以為南康王子琳侍讀。
entries.en: Emperor Wu appointed him reader to Prince Zilin of Nankang.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu appointed him Reader to the Prince of Nankang, Zilin.

entries.zh: 建武中，明帝害諸王後，泌憂念子琳，詣誌公道人問其禍福。
entries.en: During Jianwu, after Emperor Ming killed the princes, Bi worried for Zilin and asked the Daoist master Zhigong what fate held for him.
entries.literal: During Jianwu, after Emperor Ming had killed the princes, Bi worried for Zilin and went to the Daoist master Zhigong to ask his fortune.

entries.zh: 誌公覆香鑪灰示之，曰：「都盡。
entries.en: Zhigong tipped over the incense burner and showed him the ashes. "All is gone," he said.
entries.literal: Zhigong overturned the incense burner and showed him the ashes, saying: "All is gone.

entries.zh: 無所餘。」
entries.en: Nothing remains."
entries.literal: Nothing remains."

entries.zh: 及子琳被害，泌往哭之，淚盡，繼之以血。
entries.en: When Zilin was killed, Bi went to mourn him until his tears gave out and blood followed.
entries.literal: When Zilin was killed, Bi went to mourn him; his tears ran dry and were followed by blood.

entries.zh: 親視殯葬，乃去。
entries.en: He personally oversaw the burial, then left.
entries.literal: He personally oversaw the encoffining and burial, and only then departed.

entries.zh: 時廣漢王侍讀嚴桓之亦哭王盡哀。
entries.en: Yan Huanzhi, reader to the Prince of Guanghan, also mourned the prince with full grief.
entries.literal: At the time Yan Huanzhi, Reader to the Prince of Guanghan, also mourned the prince with full grief.

entries.zh: 弟預亦孝，父臨亡，執其手以託郢州行事王奐，預悲感悶絕，吐血數升，遂發病。
entries.en: His younger brother Yu was also filial. As their father lay dying he took Yu's hand and entrusted him to Wang Huan, acting governor of Yingzhou. Yu fainted from grief, vomited blood, and fell ill.
entries.literal: His younger brother Yu was also filial; as their father lay dying he took Yu's hand and entrusted him to Wang Huan, Acting Governor of Yingzhou. Yu was overcome with grief, fainted, vomited several sheng of blood, and thereafter fell ill.

entries.zh: 官至驃騎錄事。
entries.en: He rose to recorder under the Rapid Tiger General.
entries.literal: He reached office as Recorder under the Rapid Tiger General.

entries.zh: 隆昌末，預謂丹陽尹徐孝嗣曰：「外傳藉藉，似有伊周之事，君蒙武帝殊常之恩，荷託付之重，恐不得同人此舉。
entries.en: Late in Longchang Yu told Xu Xiaosi, governor of Danyang: "Rumors are rife, as though men plot like Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou. You received extraordinary favor from Emperor Wu and bear a heavy trust—I fear you cannot join them.
entries.literal: At the end of Longchang, Yu said to Xu Xiaosi, Governor of Danyang: "Rumors are widespread, as though there were a matter like Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou; you have received Emperor Wu's extraordinary grace and bear the weight of his entrustment—I fear you cannot join in this undertaking.

entries.zh: 人笑褚公，至今齒冷。」
entries.en: People still mock Lord Chu, and the shame has not faded."
entries.literal: People still laugh at Lord Chu, and teeth are cold to this day."

entries.zh: 孝嗣心甚納之。
entries.en: Xiaosi took the warning deeply to heart.
entries.literal: Xiaosi took this deeply to heart.

entries.zh: 建武中，為永世令，民懷其德。
entries.en: During Jianwu he served as magistrate of Yongshi, and the people cherished his virtue.
entries.literal: During Jianwu he served as Magistrate of Yongshi, and the people cherished his virtue.

entries.zh: 卒官。
entries.en: He died in office.
entries.literal: He died in office.

entries.zh: 有一老嫗行擔斛蔌葉將詣市，聞預死，弃擔號泣。
entries.en: An old woman carrying vegetable leaves to market heard of Yu's death, dropped her pole, and wept aloud.
entries.literal: An old woman was walking with a carrying-pole of vegetable leaves bound for market; hearing that Yu had died, she cast down her pole and wailed.

entries.zh: 南齊書卷第五十五‧列傳第三十六 孝義
entries.en: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 55, Biography 36: Filial Piety and Righteous Conduct
entries.literal: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 55, Biographies 36: Filial Piety and Righteous Conduct

entries.zh: 有天象，必有人事焉。
entries.en: Where there are signs in the heavens, there are corresponding events among men.
entries.literal: When there are celestial signs, there must be human affairs.

entries.zh: 倖臣一星，列于帝座。
entries.en: The Star of Court Favorites stands arrayed beside the imperial throne.
entries.literal: The Star of Favored Officials is arrayed beside the imperial throne.

entries.zh: 經禮立教，亦著近臣之服。
entries.en: The classics that establish ritual and instruction also prescribe the dress of those who serve close at hand.
entries.literal: In establishing ritual and teaching through the classics, the attire of close ministers is also set forth.

entries.zh: 親倖之義，其來已久。
entries.en: The practice of granting intimate favor has a history stretching far back.
entries.literal: The meaning of personal favor and trust has been longstanding.

entries.zh: 爰自衰周，侯伯專命，桓、文霸主，至于戰國，寵用近習，不乏於時矣。
entries.en: From the waning Zhou dynasty on, regional lords held independent power; Duke Huan and Duke Wen rose as hegemons; and by the Warring States period, rulers who pampered and relied on those nearest them were never in short supply.
entries.literal: From the declining Zhou onward, marquises and earls held sole command; Duke Huan and Duke Wen became hegemons; down to the Warring States, favoring and employing close intimates was never lacking in those times.

entries.zh: 漢文幸鄧通，雖錢徧天下，位止郎中。
entries.en: Emperor Wen of Han favored Deng Tong; though his wealth reached every corner of the empire, his office never rose above Gentleman of the Palace.
entries.literal: Emperor Wen of Han favored Deng Tong; although money spread throughout the realm, his rank stopped at Gentleman of the Palace.

entries.zh: 孝武韓嫣、霍去病，遂至侍中大司馬。
entries.en: Under Emperor Wu, favorites such as Han Yan and Huo Qubing advanced as high as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand Marshal.
entries.literal: Under Emperor Wu, Han Yan and Huo Qubing rose as far as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand Marshal.

entries.zh: 迄于魏、晉，世任權重，才位稍爽，而信倖唯均。
entries.en: By Wei and Jin times, such men held heavy power generation after generation; talent and office no longer matched as neatly, yet imperial trust and favor were lavished on them all alike.
entries.literal: Down to Wei and Jin, generation after generation they held heavy power; talent and rank grew somewhat misaligned, yet trust and favor remained evenly granted.

entries.zh: 中書之職，舊掌機務。
entries.en: The Secretariat had long handled the most confidential affairs of state.
entries.literal: The office of the Secretariat had formerly managed state secrets.

entries.zh: 漢元以令僕用事，魏明以監令專權，及在中朝，猶爲重寄。
entries.en: Under Emperor Yuan of Han the Masters of Writing ran affairs; under Emperor Ming of Wei the Supervisor and Director held sole sway; and even in the central dynasties the office remained a post of the deepest trust.
entries.literal: Emperor Yuan of Han had the Masters of Writing wield power; Emperor Ming of Wei had the Supervisor and Director monopolize authority; even in the central court, the post still carried heavy trust.

entries.zh: 陳准歸任上司，荀勗恨於失職。
entries.en: Chen Zhun yielded his duties back to his superiors, while Xun Xu brooded over the loss of his position.
entries.literal: Chen Zhun returned responsibility to his superior; Xun Xu resented the loss of his post.

entries.zh: 晉令舍人位居九品，江左置通事郎，管司詔誥。
entries.en: Under Jin, secretarial attendants held ninth-rank status; in the Eastern Jin court they created Communications Officers to handle imperial edicts and proclamations.
entries.literal: In Jin, secretarial attendants ranked in the ninth grade; east of the Yangzi they established Communications Officers to manage imperial edicts and proclamations.

entries.zh: 其後郎還爲侍郎，而舍人亦稱通事。
entries.en: Later the officers were again styled Gentlemen Attendants, and secretarial attendants likewise came to be called communications officers.
entries.literal: Thereafter the officers were restored as Gentlemen Attendants, while attendants were also called communications officers.

entries.zh: 元帝用琅邪劉超，以謹慎居職。
entries.en: Emperor Yuan employed Liu Chao of Langye, who kept his post through scrupulous care.
entries.literal: Emperor Yuan employed Liu Chao of Langye, who held his post through careful diligence.

entries.zh: 宋文世，秋當、周糾竝出寒門。
entries.en: In the reign of Emperor Wen of Song, Qiu Dang and Zhou Jiu both rose from humble households.
entries.literal: In the era of Emperor Wen of Song, Qiu Dang and Zhou Jiu both came from humble families.

entries.zh: 孝武以來，士庶雜選，如東海鮑照，以才學知名。
entries.en: From Emperor Xiaowu on, men of gentry and common birth were chosen side by side, as with Bao Zhao of Donghai, famed for his talent and scholarship.
entries.literal: From Emperor Xiaowu onward, gentlemen and commoners were mixed in selection; such as Bao Zhao of Donghai, who was renowned for talent and learning.

entries.zh: 又用魯郡巢尚之，江夏王義恭以爲非選。
entries.en: He also appointed Chao Shangzhi of Lu commandery, though Prince Yigong of Jiangxia judged the choice improper.
entries.literal: He also employed Chao Shangzhi of Lu commandery; Prince Yigong of Jiangxia considered this an improper selection.

entries.zh: 帝遣尚書二十餘牒，宣敕論辯，義恭乃歎曰：「人主誠知人。」
entries.en: The emperor sent more than twenty dispatches from the Masters of Writing, issuing edicts to argue the point back and forth, until Yigong sighed and said, "The ruler truly knows how to judge men."
entries.literal: The emperor sent more than twenty memorials from the Masters of Writing, proclaiming edicts to debate the matter; Yigong then sighed and said, "The sovereign truly knows men."

entries.zh: 及明帝世，胡母顥、阮佃夫之徒，專爲佞倖矣。
entries.en: By Emperor Ming's reign, men such as Humu Hao and Ruan Tianfu had turned the post wholly to sycophancy and private favor.
entries.literal: By the era of Emperor Ming, men such as Humu Hao and Ruan Tianfu devoted themselves solely to flattery and favor.

entries.zh: 建元初，帶東燕令，封新陽縣男，三百戶。
entries.en: At the start of Jianyuan he concurrently served as magistrate of Dongyan and was enfeoffed as Baron of Xinyang county with three hundred households.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Jianyuan he concurrently served as magistrate of Dongyan and was enfeoffed as Baron of Xinyang county with three hundred households.

entries.zh: 轉羽林監，加建威將軍，遷尚書主客郎，太尉中兵參軍，令如故。
entries.en: He was transferred to supervisor of the Feathered Forest Guard, given the additional rank of General Who Establishes Might, and promoted to gentleman of the Ministry of Receptions and central army staff officer to the Grand Commandant, retaining his magistracy.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Supervisor of the Feathered Forest Guard, given the additional rank of General Who Establishes Might, and promoted to Gentleman of the Ministry of Receptions and central army staff officer to the Grand Commandant, retaining his magistracy.

entries.zh: 復以本官兼中書舍人。
entries.en: Again, while retaining his original office, he concurrently served as secretariat attendant.
entries.literal: Again, on the basis of his original office he concurrently served as Secretariat Attendant.

entries.zh: 太祖疾甚，令僧真典遺詔。
entries.en: When the Founding Emperor was gravely ill, he ordered Sengzhen to draft the death testament.
entries.literal: When the Founding Emperor was gravely ill, he ordered Sengzhen to draft the death testament.

entries.zh: 永明元年，寧喪，起爲建威將軍，尋除南泰山太守，又爲舍人，本官如故。
entries.en: In the first year of Yongming, after completing mourning, he was recalled as General Who Establishes Might; soon he was appointed governor of Nantaishan, again served as attendant, and retained his former offices.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongming, after completing mourning, he was recalled as General Who Establishes Might; soon he was appointed governor of Nantaishan, and again served as attendant, retaining his former offices.

entries.zh: 領諸王第事。
entries.en: He oversaw affairs of the princes' mansions.
entries.literal: He oversaw affairs of the princes' mansions.

entries.zh: 僧真容貌言吐，雅有士風。
entries.en: Sengzhen's appearance and speech were refined, with a true scholar's bearing.
entries.literal: Sengzhen's features and speech were elegant, with a true scholar's bearing.

entries.zh: 世祖嘗目送之，笑曰：「人何必計門戶，紀僧真常貴人所不及。」
entries.en: Emperor Wu once watched him depart and said with a laugh, "Why must one count family standing? Ji Sengzhen is often what the highly born cannot match."
entries.literal: Emperor Wu once followed him with his eyes and said with a laugh, "Why must one count family standing? Ji Sengzhen is often what the highly born cannot match."

entries.zh: 諸權要中，最被盻遇。
entries.en: Among the powerful he was the most favored with attentive regard.
entries.literal: Among the powerful he was most favored with attentive regard.

entries.zh: 除越騎校尉，餘官如故。
entries.en: He was appointed colonel of the Yue Cavalry; his other offices remained as before.
entries.literal: He was appointed Colonel of the Yue Cavalry; his other offices remained as before.

entries.zh: 出爲建武將軍，建康令。
entries.en: He went out as General Establishing Might and magistrate of Jiankang.
entries.literal: He went out as General Establishing Might and magistrate of Jiankang.

entries.zh: 還除左右郎將，泰山太守。
entries.en: On returning he was appointed left and right commander of the palace guards and governor of Taishan.
entries.literal: On returning he was appointed Left and Right Commander of the Palace Guards and governor of Taishan.

entries.zh: 加先驅使。
entries.en: He was given the additional post of vanguard commissioner.
entries.literal: He was given the additional post of vanguard commissioner.

entries.zh: 尋除前軍將軍。
entries.en: Soon he was appointed General of the Vanguard.
entries.literal: Soon he was appointed General of the Vanguard.

entries.zh: 遭母喪，開冢得五色兩頭蛇。
entries.en: When his mother died, opening the tomb revealed a five-colored two-headed snake.
entries.literal: When his mother died, in opening the tomb they found a five-colored two-headed snake.

entries.zh: 世祖崩，僧真號泣思慕。
entries.en: When Emperor Wu died, Sengzhen wailed and mourned in longing.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu died, Sengzhen wailed and mourned in longing.

entries.zh: 明帝以僧真歷朝驅使，建武元年，除游擊將軍，兼司農，待之如舊。
entries.en: Because Sengzhen had served as a dispatch runner through successive reigns, in the first year of Jianwu Emperor Ming appointed him General Who Scatters the Enemy with concurrent charge as Minister of Grand Food and treated him as before.
entries.literal: Because Sengzhen had served through successive reigns as a dispatch runner, in the first year of Jianwu Emperor Ming appointed him General Who Scatters the Enemy with concurrent charge as Minister of Grand Food, treating him as before.

entries.zh: 欲令僧真治郡，僧真啓進其弟僧猛爲鎮蠻護軍、晉熙太守。
entries.en: When the emperor wished to have Sengzhen govern a commandery, Sengzhen memorialized to advance his younger brother Sengmeng as protector-general for pacifying the barbarians and governor of Jinxi.
entries.literal: When the emperor wished to have Sengzhen govern a commandery, Sengzhen memorialized to advance his younger brother Sengmeng as protector-general who pacifies the barbarians and governor of Jinxi.

entries.zh: 永泰元年，除司農卿。
entries.en: In the first year of Yongtai he was appointed Minister of Grand Food.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongtai he was appointed Minister of Grand Food.

entries.zh: 明帝崩，掌山陵事。
entries.en: When Emperor Ming died, he oversaw matters of the imperial tomb.
entries.literal: When Emperor Ming died, he oversaw matters of the imperial mound-tomb.

entries.zh: 出爲廬陵內史，年五十五，卒。
entries.en: He was sent out as interior scribe of Luling and died at the age of fifty-five.
entries.literal: He went out as interior scribe of Luling; at the age of fifty-five he died.

entries.zh: 茹法亮，吳興武康人也。
entries.en: Ru Faliang was a native of Wukang in Wuxing commandery.
entries.literal: Ru Faliang was a native of Wukang in Wuxing.

entries.zh: 宋大明世，出身爲小史，歷齋幹扶。
entries.en: In the Daming era of Song he began as a petty clerk and rose through posts as orderly and attendant.
entries.literal: In the Daming era of Song he first served as a petty clerk and passed through posts as orderly and attendant.

entries.zh: 孝武末年，作酒法，鞭罰過度，校獵江右，選白衣左右百八十人，皆面首富室，從至南州，得鞭者過半。
entries.en: In Emperor Xiaowu's last years he instituted drinking regulations with excessive flogging. On a hunting expedition south of the Yangzi he selected one hundred eighty attendants in plain dress, all men of wealthy households, and took them to the southern regions; more than half were flogged.
entries.literal: In the last years of Emperor Xiaowu he instituted drinking regulations with excessive flogging; on a hunting expedition to the lands south of the Yangzi he selected one hundred eighty attendants in plain dress, all handsome men from wealthy households, and took them to the southern regions; more than half received the lash.

entries.zh: 法亮憂懼，因緣啓出家得爲道人。
entries.en: Faliang, anxious and afraid, seized the opportunity to petition to leave the world and become a Daoist priest.
entries.literal: Faliang, anxious and afraid, seized the opportunity to report that he wished to leave the world and become a Daoist priest.

entries.zh: 明帝初，罷道，結事阮佃夫，用爲兖州刺史孟次陽典籤。
entries.en: At the start of Emperor Ming's reign he left the religious life, attached himself to Ruan Tianfu, and was appointed chief clerk to Meng Ciyang, governor of Yanzhou.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Ming's reign he left the religious life, attached himself to Ruan Tianfu, and was employed as chief clerk to Meng Ciyang, governor of Yanzhou.

entries.zh: 累至太祖冠軍府行參軍。
entries.en: He rose step by step to acting staff officer in the Founding Emperor's Champion General's headquarters.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Acting Staff Officer in the Founding Emperor's Champion General's headquarters.

entries.zh: 元徽初，除殿中將軍，爲晉熙王郢州典籤，除長兼殿中御史。
entries.en: At the start of the Yuanhui era he was made General of the Palace, chief clerk to the Prince of Jinxi in Yingzhou, and chief censor of the palace with extended authority.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhui he was appointed General of the Palace, made chief clerk to the Prince of Jinxi in Yingzhou, and appointed Chief Censor of the Palace with extended authority.

entries.zh: 世祖鎮盆城，須舊驅使人，法亮求留爲上江州典籤，除南臺御史，帶松滋令。
entries.en: When Emperor Wu was stationed at Pencheng and needed experienced dispatch runners, Faliang asked to stay on as chief clerk of Upper Jiangzhou, was appointed censor of the Southern Terrace, and concurrently served as magistrate of Songzi.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu was stationed at Pencheng and needed old dispatch runners, Faliang asked to remain as chief clerk of Upper Jiangzhou, was appointed censor of the Southern Terrace, and concurrently served as magistrate of Songzi.

entries.zh: 法亮便辟解事，善於承奉，稍見委信。
entries.en: Faliang was quick and capable, skilled at attendance and service, and gradually won trust and responsibility.
entries.literal: Faliang was clever and capable in affairs, skilled at attending and serving, and gradually won trust and appointment.

entries.zh: 從還石頭。
entries.en: He followed the emperor back to Stone City.
entries.literal: He followed back to Stone City.

entries.zh: 建元初，度東宮主書。
entries.en: At the start of Jianyuan he was transferred to chief clerk of the Eastern Palace.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Jianyuan he was transferred to Eastern Palace chief clerk.

entries.zh: 除奉朝請，補東宮通事舍人。
entries.en: He was appointed court gentleman for attendance and made Eastern Palace communications attendant.
entries.literal: He was appointed Court Gentleman for Attendance and supplemented as Eastern Palace Communications Attendant.

entries.zh: 世祖卽位，仍爲中書通事舍人。
entries.en: When Emperor Wu took the throne, he continued as secretariat communications attendant.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu took the throne, he remained Secretariat Communications Attendant.

entries.zh: 除員外郎，帶南濟陰太守。
entries.en: He was appointed supplementary gentleman and concurrently served as governor of Nanjiyin.
entries.literal: He was appointed Supplementary Gentleman and concurrently served as governor of Nanjiyin.

entries.zh: 永明元年，除龍驤將軍。
entries.en: In the first year of Yongming he was appointed General of the Dragon Cavalry.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongming he was appointed General of the Dragon Cavalry.

entries.zh: 明年，詔曰：「茹法亮近在盆城，頻使銜命，內宣朝旨，外慰三軍。
entries.en: The next year an edict said: "Ru Faliang was recently at Pencheng, repeatedly bearing imperial commands, proclaiming the court's will within and comforting the armies without.
entries.literal: The next year an edict said: "Ru Faliang was recently at Pencheng, repeatedly bearing imperial commands, proclaiming court directives within and comforting the three armies without.

entries.zh: 義勇齊奮，人百其氣。
entries.en: With righteous courage all strove as one; each man fought with redoubled spirit.
entries.literal: With righteous courage all strove together; each man gave a hundredfold of his spirit.

entries.zh: 險阻艱難，心力俱盡。
entries.en: Through peril and hardship he gave his utmost in heart and strength.
entries.literal: Through peril and hardship he exhausted heart and strength alike.

entries.zh: 宜沾茅土，以甄忠績。」
entries.en: He should receive a fief to reward his loyal service."
entries.literal: He should be granted a fief of soil to distinguish his loyal achievement."

entries.zh: 封望蔡縣男，食邑三百戶。
entries.en: He was enfeoffed as Baron of Wangcai county with a fief of three hundred households.
entries.literal: He was enfeoffed as Baron of Wangcai county with a fief of three hundred households.

entries.zh: 轉給事中，羽林監。
entries.en: He was transferred to gentleman attendant and supervisor of the Feathered Forest Guard.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Gentleman Attendant and Supervisor of the Feathered Forest Guard.

entries.zh: 七年，除臨淮太守，轉竟陵王司徒中兵參軍。
entries.en: In the seventh year he was appointed governor of Linhuai and transferred to central army staff officer to the Minister of State on the Prince of Jingling's staff.
entries.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed governor of Linhuai and transferred to central army staff officer to the Minister of State for the Prince of Jingling.

entries.zh: 鬱林卽位，除步兵校尉。
entries.en: When Emperor Yulin took the throne, Faliang was appointed colonel of footsoldiers.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yulin took the throne, Faliang was appointed Colonel of Footsoldiers.

entries.zh: 延興元年，爲前軍將軍。
entries.en: In the first year of Yanxing he was made General of the Vanguard.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yanxing he was made General of the Vanguard.

entries.zh: 延昌殿爲世祖陰室，藏諸御服。
entries.en: Yanchang Hall was Emperor Wu's private chamber, where the imperial wardrobe was kept.
entries.literal: Yanchang Hall was Emperor Wu's private chamber, where all imperial garments were stored.

entries.zh: 二少帝竝居西殿，高宗卽位住東齋，開陰室出世祖白紗帽防身刀，法亮歔欷流涕。
entries.en: The two young emperors both lived in the western hall. When Emperor Gao took the throne he lodged in the eastern studio, opened the private chamber, and brought out Emperor Wu's white gauze cap and self-defense knife. Faliang sobbed and wept.
entries.literal: The two young emperors both dwelt in the western hall; when Emperor Gao took the throne he lodged in the eastern studio, opened the private chamber, and brought out Emperor Wu's white gauze cap and self-defense knife; Faliang sobbed and wept.

entries.zh: 除游擊將軍。
entries.en: He was appointed General Who Scatters the Enemy.
entries.literal: He was appointed General Who Scatters the Enemy.

entries.zh: 高武舊人鮮有存者，法亮以主署文事，故不見疑，位任如故。
entries.en: Few of Emperor Gao Wu's old associates still survived. Because Faliang handled documentary affairs at the secretariat, he was not suspected, and his rank and duties remained unchanged.
entries.literal: Few of Emperor Gao Wu's old associates still survived; because Faliang was in charge of documentary affairs at the secretariat, he was not suspected, and his rank and duties remained as before.

entries.zh: 永泰元年，王敬則事平，法亮復受敕宣慰。
entries.en: In the first year of Yongtai, when Wang Jingze's revolt was put down, Faliang again received orders to proclaim imperial comfort.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongtai, when Wang Jingze's affair was settled, Faliang again received orders to proclaim comfort.

entries.zh: 出法亮爲大司農，中書勢利之職，法亮不樂去，固辭不受，旣而代人已致，法亮垂涕而出。
entries.en: Faliang was transferred out to serve as Minister of Grand Food. The Secretariat was a post of power and profit, and he was unwilling to leave; he firmly declined the transfer, but soon his replacement had arrived, and Faliang left in tears.
entries.literal: Faliang was sent out as Minister of Grand Food; the Secretariat was a post of power and profit, and Faliang was unwilling to leave; he firmly declined and would not accept, but soon his replacement had arrived, and Faliang went out in tears.

entries.zh: 年六十四，卒官。
entries.en: He died in office at the age of sixty-four.
entries.literal: At the age of sixty-four he died in office.

entries.zh: 呂文顯，臨海人也。
entries.en: Lü Wenxian was a native of Linhai.
entries.literal: Lü Wenxian was a native of Linhai.

entries.zh: 初爲宋孝武齋幹直長。
entries.en: He first served as chief orderly of the fasting guard under Emperor Xiaowu of Song.
entries.literal: Initially he served as chief orderly of the fasting guard under Emperor Xiaowu of Song.

entries.zh: 昇明初，爲太祖錄尚書省事，累位至殿中侍御史，羽林監，帶蘭陵丞、令，龍驤將軍，秣陵令。
entries.en: At the start of Shengming he served in the Founding Emperor's secretariat for recording master-of-writing affairs and rose through posts as attendant censor of the palace, supervisor of the Feathered Forest Guard, concurrently assistant magistrate and magistrate of Lanling, General of the Dragon Cavalry, and magistrate of Moling.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Shengming he served in the Founding Emperor's Secretariat for Recording Master of Writing affairs, and was repeatedly promoted to attendant censor of the palace, supervisor of the Feathered Forest Guard, concurrently assistant magistrate and magistrate of Lanling, General of the Dragon Cavalry, and magistrate of Moling.

entries.zh: 封劉陽縣男。
entries.en: He was enfeoffed as Baron of Liuyang county.
entries.literal: He was enfeoffed as Baron of Liuyang county.

entries.zh: 永明元年，除寧朔將軍，中書通事舍人，本官如故。
entries.en: In the first year of Yongming he was appointed General Who Pacifies the North and secretariat communications attendant, retaining his former offices.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongming he was appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Secretariat Communications Attendant, retaining his former offices.

entries.zh: 呂文度，會稽人。
entries.en: Lü Wendu was a native of Kuaiji.
entries.literal: Lü Wendu was a native of Kuaiji.

entries.zh: 宋世爲細作金銀庫吏，竹局匠。
entries.en: During Song he served as clerk in the fine-work gold and silver treasury and as a bamboo-frame craftsman.
entries.literal: In Song times he served as clerk in the fine-work gold and silver treasury and as a bamboo-frame craftsman.

entries.zh: 元徽中，爲射雉典事，隨監莫脩宗上郢。
entries.en: During the Yuanhui era he was officer in charge of pheasant shooting and followed Supervisor Mo Xiuzong to Ying.
entries.literal: During Yuanhui he was officer in charge of pheasant shooting and followed Supervisor Mo Xiuzong to Ying.

entries.zh: 世祖鎮盆城拒沈攸之，文度仍留伏事，知軍隊雜役，以此見親。
entries.en: When Emperor Wu was stationed at Pencheng resisting Shen Youzhi, Wendu remained behind to serve in secret and knew the army's miscellaneous duties; for this he won the emperor's favor.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu was stationed at Pencheng resisting Shen Youzhi, Wendu remained behind to serve in secret, knowing the miscellaneous duties of the army; for this he was treated with favor.

entries.zh: 從還都，爲石頭城監，仍度東宮。
entries.en: On returning to the capital he was made supervisor of Stone City and then transferred to the Eastern Palace.
entries.literal: On returning to the capital he was made supervisor of Stone City and then transferred to the Eastern Palace.

entries.zh: 世祖卽位，爲制局監，位至員外郎，帶南濮陽太守。
entries.en: When Emperor Wu took the throne, Wendu was made supervisor of the Equipment Bureau, rose to supplementary gentleman, and concurrently served as governor of Nanpuyang.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu took the throne, Wendu was made Supervisor of the Equipment Bureau, rose to Supplementary Gentleman, and concurrently served as governor of Nanpuyang.

entries.zh: 殿內軍隊及發遣外鎮人，悉關之，甚有要勢。
entries.en: Palace troops and personnel dispatched to outer garrisons all passed through his hands, and he wielded great strategic power.
entries.literal: Palace troops within the hall and personnel dispatched to outer garrisons all depended on him; he held great strategic power.

entries.zh: 故世傳越州嘗缺，上覔一直事人往越州，文度啓其所知費延宗合旨，上卽以爲刺史。
entries.en: Hence the story that when Yuezhou once lacked a governor, the emperor sought a direct attendant to send there. Wendu reported that Fei Yanzong, a man he knew, suited the emperor's wishes, and the emperor at once appointed him governor.
entries.literal: Hence it was said in the world that when Yuezhou once lacked an appointee, the emperor sought a direct attendant to go to Yuezhou; Wendu reported that Fei Yanzong, whom he knew, suited the emperor's wish, and the emperor at once made him governor.

entries.zh: 永明中，敕親近不得輙有申薦，人士免官，寒人鞭一百。
entries.en: During Yongming an edict forbade intimates from making recommendations at will: gentlemen were dismissed from office, humble men were flogged one hundred strokes.
entries.literal: During Yongming an edict forbade intimates from making recommendations at will; gentlemen were dismissed from office, humble men were flogged one hundred strokes.

entries.zh: 紀僧真，丹陽建康人也。
entries.en: Ji Sengzhen was a native of Jiankang in Danyang commandery.
entries.literal: Ji Sengzhen was a native of Jianye in Danyang.

entries.zh: 僧真少隨逐征西將軍蕭思話及子惠開，皆被賞遇。
entries.en: As a youth Sengzhen followed General Who Conquers the West Xiao Sihua and his son Hui Kai, and both men treated him with favor.
entries.literal: In youth Sengzhen followed and served General Who Conquers the West Xiao Sihua and his son Hui Kai; both rewarded and favored him.

entries.zh: 惠開性苛，僧真以微過見罰，旣而委任如舊。
entries.en: Hui Kai was harsh by nature. Sengzhen was once punished for a trifling fault, but was soon entrusted again as before.
entries.literal: Hui Kai was harsh by nature; Sengzhen was punished for a minor fault, yet afterward was entrusted as before.

entries.zh: 及罷益州還都，不得志，僧真事之愈謹。
entries.en: When Hui Kai left Yizhou and returned to the capital, bitter at his thwarted ambitions, Sengzhen served him with still greater care.
entries.literal: When he left his post in Yizhou and returned to the capital, frustrated in his ambitions, Sengzhen served him all the more carefully.

entries.zh: 惠開臨終歎曰：「紀僧真方當富貴，我不見也。」
entries.en: On his deathbed Hui Kai sighed and said, "Ji Sengzhen is on the verge of wealth and rank — and I shall not live to see it."
entries.literal: On his deathbed Hui Kai sighed and said, "Ji Sengzhen is about to attain wealth and honor; I shall not live to see it."

entries.zh: 乃以僧真託劉秉、周顒。
entries.en: He then commended Sengzhen to the care of Liu Bing and Zhou Yong.
entries.literal: He then entrusted Sengzhen to Liu Bing and Zhou Yong.

entries.zh: 初，惠開在益州，土反，被圍危急，有道人謂之曰：「城圍尋解。
entries.en: Earlier, while Hui Kai held Yizhou, the local tribes rebelled and he was besieged in grave danger. A Daoist told him, "The siege will soon be lifted.
entries.literal: Earlier, when Hui Kai was in Yizhou, the natives rebelled and he was besieged in dire peril; a Daoist told him, "The siege will soon be lifted.

entries.zh: 檀越貴門後方大興，無憂外賊也。」
entries.en: Your patron's noble house will rise to great glory hereafter. You need not fear outside enemies."
entries.literal: The patron's noble house will flourish greatly hereafter; do not worry about outside enemies."

entries.zh: 惠開密謂僧真曰：「我子弟見在者，竝無異才。
entries.en: Hui Kai told Sengzhen in confidence, "None of my sons and brothers now living has any unusual talent.
entries.literal: Hui Kai secretly said to Sengzhen, "Among my sons and younger brothers now living, none has unusual talent.

entries.zh: 政是道成耳。」
entries.en: It is Daocheng alone who matters."
entries.literal: It is truly Daocheng alone."

entries.zh: 僧真憶其言，乃請事太祖。
entries.en: Sengzhen kept these words in mind and therefore sought service under the Founding Emperor.
entries.literal: Sengzhen remembered these words and therefore asked to serve the Founding Emperor.

entries.zh: 隨從在淮陰，以閑書題，令荅遠近書疏。
entries.en: Following the emperor at Huaiyin, he was set to answering correspondence from near and far because of his skill at informal writing.
entries.literal: Following him at Huaiyin, because he was skilled at casual writing, he was ordered to reply to correspondence from near and far.

entries.zh: 自寒官歷至太祖冠軍府參軍、主簿。
entries.en: From humble posts he rose to serve as staff officer and chief clerk in the Founding Emperor's Champion General's headquarters.
entries.literal: From a humble office he rose through posts to Staff Officer and Chief Clerk in the Founding Emperor's Champion General's headquarters.

entries.zh: 僧真夢蒿艾生滿江，驚而白之。
entries.en: Sengzhen dreamed that mugwort and wormwood filled the river. Alarmed, he reported the dream.
entries.literal: Sengzhen dreamed that mugwort and wormwood grew covering the river; startled, he reported it.

entries.zh: 太祖曰：「詩人採蕭，蕭卽艾也。
entries.en: The Founding Emperor said, "The poets gather artemisia — and artemisia is wormwood.
entries.literal: The Founding Emperor said, "The poets gather artemisia; artemisia is wormwood.

entries.zh: 蕭生斷流，卿勿廣言。」
entries.en: Artemisia growing cuts the river's flow. Do not speak of this abroad."
entries.literal: Artemisia growing cuts the flow of the river; do not speak widely of this."

entries.zh: 其見親如此。
entries.en: Such was the degree of intimacy he enjoyed.
entries.literal: Such was the intimacy with which he was regarded.

entries.zh: 太祖坐東府高樓，望石頭城，僧真在側。
entries.en: The Founding Emperor sat in the high tower of the Eastern Headquarters, gazing toward Stone City, with Sengzhen at his side.
entries.literal: The Founding Emperor sat in the high tower of the Eastern Headquarters, gazing at Stone City; Sengzhen was at his side.

entries.zh: 上曰：「諸將勸我誅袁、劉，我意不欲便爾。」
entries.en: The emperor said, "My generals urge me to execute Yuan and Liu, but I am not inclined to act so hastily."
entries.literal: The emperor said, "The generals urge me to execute Yuan and Liu; my mind is not inclined to do so immediately."

entries.zh: 及沈攸之事起，從太祖入朝堂。
entries.en: When Shen Youzhi's revolt broke out, he followed the Founding Emperor into the court hall.
entries.literal: When Shen Youzhi's affair arose, he followed the Founding Emperor into the court hall.

entries.zh: 石頭反夜，太祖遣衆軍掩討。
entries.en: Stone City rose in revolt that night, and the Founding Emperor sent his armies to strike by surprise.
entries.literal: Stone City rebelled by night; the Founding Emperor sent the armies to strike in surprise.

entries.zh: 宮城中望石頭火光及呌聲甚盛，人懷不測。
entries.en: From within the palace city they could see the blaze at Stone City and hear the clamor of battle. No one knew what to expect.
entries.literal: Within the palace city they watched the fires and shouting at Stone City, which were very loud; people harbored uncertainty.

entries.zh: 僧真謂衆曰：「呌聲不絕，是必官軍所攻。
entries.en: Sengzhen told those around him, "The shouting never stops — that can only mean our own armies are attacking.
entries.literal: Sengzhen said to the crowd, "The shouting does not cease; this must be the government armies attacking.

entries.zh: 火光起者，賊不容自燒其城，此必官軍勝也。」
entries.en: As for the flames, the rebels would never burn their own city. This can only mean our armies have won."
entries.literal: Where fires rise, the rebels would not burn their own city; this must mean the government armies have won."

entries.zh: 尋而啓石頭平。
entries.en: Before long a report arrived that Stone City had been pacified.
entries.literal: Soon a report came that Stone City was pacified.

entries.zh: 上出頓新亭，使僧真領千人在帳內。
entries.en: The emperor went out to encamp at Xinting and placed a thousand men under Sengzhen's command within the camp enclosure.
entries.literal: The emperor went out to encamp at Xinting and ordered Sengzhen to lead a thousand men within the camp enclosure.

entries.zh: 初，上在領軍府，令僧真學上手迹下名，至是報荅書疏，皆付僧真，上觀之，笑曰：「我亦不復能別也。」
entries.en: Earlier, while still at the commander-in-chief's headquarters, the emperor had Sengzhen learn to imitate his hand in signing his name. Now all replies to letters and memorials were entrusted to Sengzhen. The emperor looked them over and laughed. "Even I can no longer tell the difference," he said.
entries.literal: Earlier, when the emperor was at the headquarters of the Commander-in-Chief, he had Sengzhen learn his own hand in signing his name; now replies to letters and memorials were all entrusted to Sengzhen; the emperor looked at them and laughed, saying, "I too can no longer tell the difference."

entries.zh: 初，上在淮陰治城，得一錫趺，大數尺，下有篆文，莫能識者。
entries.en: Earlier, while building the city at Huaiyin, the emperor unearthed a tin pedestal several feet across. Seal script was inscribed beneath it, but no one could read it.
entries.literal: Earlier, when the emperor was building the city at Huaiyin, he obtained a tin pedestal several feet in size; beneath it was seal script that no one could read.

entries.zh: 僧真曰：「何須辨此文字，此自久遠之物，九錫之徵也。」
entries.en: Sengzhen said, "Why trouble to read these characters? The object itself is ancient — a sign of the Nine Bestowals."
entries.literal: Sengzhen said, "Why need we decipher these characters? This is itself an object of great antiquity — a sign of the Nine Bestowals."

entries.zh: 太祖曰：「卿勿妄言。」
entries.en: The Founding Emperor said, "Do not speak rashly."
entries.literal: The Founding Emperor said, "Do not speak rashly."

entries.zh: 及上將拜齊公，已剋日，有楊袓之謀於臨軒作難。
entries.en: When the emperor was about to receive investiture as Duke of Qi, with the day already set, Yang Zuzhi plotted an attack at the audience hall.
entries.literal: When the emperor was about to receive investiture as Duke of Qi, the day already fixed, Yang Zuzhi plotted to make trouble at the audience hall.

entries.zh: 僧真更請上選吉辰，尋而祖之事覺。
entries.en: Sengzhen again asked the emperor to choose a more auspicious day. Before long Zuzhi's plot was discovered.
entries.literal: Sengzhen again asked the emperor to choose an auspicious day; soon Zuzhi's plot was discovered.

entries.zh: 上曰：「無卿言，亦當致小狼狽，此亦何異呼遝之冰。」
entries.en: The emperor said, "Even without your warning I would have been put to some embarrassment. This is no different from the ice at Hulao."
entries.literal: The emperor said, "Without your words, I would still have met with some embarrassment; this is no different from the ice of Hulao."

entries.zh: 轉齊國中書舍人。
entries.en: He was transferred to the post of secretariat attendant of the State of Qi.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Secretariat Attendant of the State of Qi.

entries.zh: 太祖廢蒼梧，明旦，呼正直舍人虞整，醉不能起，係宗歡喜奉命。
entries.en: When the Founding Emperor deposed Emperor Cangwu, the next morning he summoned the upright attendant Yu Zheng, who was too drunk to rise. Xizong gladly took the order in his place.
entries.literal: When the Founding Emperor deposed Cangwu, the next morning he summoned the upright attendant Yu Zheng, who was drunk and could not rise; Xizong gladly accepted the command.

entries.zh: 太祖曰：「今天地重開，是卿盡力之日。」
entries.en: The Founding Emperor said, "Heaven and earth open anew today. This is the day for you to give your utmost."
entries.literal: The Founding Emperor said, "Today heaven and earth open anew; this is the day for you to exert yourself to the utmost."

entries.zh: 使寫諸處分敕令，及四方書疏。
entries.en: He had him draft all disposition orders and edicts, as well as correspondence to every quarter of the realm.
entries.literal: He had him write all disposition orders and edicts, as well as correspondence to the four directions.

entries.zh: 使主書十人書吏二十人配之，事皆稱旨。
entries.en: He assigned him ten chief clerks and twenty writing clerks. In every matter Xizong met the emperor's wishes.
entries.literal: He assigned him ten chief clerks and twenty writing clerks; in every matter he met with approval.

entries.zh: 除羽林監，轉步兵校尉。
entries.en: He was appointed supervisor of the Feathered Forest Guard and then transferred to colonel of footsoldiers.
entries.literal: He was appointed Supervisor of the Feathered Forest Guard and transferred to Colonel of Footsoldiers.

entries.zh: 仍除龍驤將軍，出爲海鹽令。
entries.en: He was then appointed General of the Dragon Cavalry and sent out to serve as magistrate of Haiyan.
entries.literal: He was then appointed General of the Dragon Cavalry and sent out as magistrate of Haiyan.

entries.zh: 太祖卽位，除龍驤將軍、建康令。
entries.en: When the Founding Emperor took the throne, Xizong was appointed General of the Dragon Cavalry and magistrate of Jiankang.
entries.literal: When the Founding Emperor took the throne, Xizong was appointed General of the Dragon Cavalry and magistrate of Jiankang.

entries.zh: 永明元年，除寧朔將軍，令如故。
entries.en: In the first year of Yongming he was made General Who Pacifies the North while keeping his post as magistrate.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongming he was appointed General Who Pacifies the North, retaining his magistracy as before.

entries.zh: 尋轉右軍將軍、淮陵太守，兼中書通事舍人。
entries.en: Soon afterward he became General of the Right Army and governor of Huailing, with concurrent duty as secretariat communications attendant.
entries.literal: Soon he was transferred to General of the Right Army and governor of Huailing, concurrently Secretariat Communications Attendant.

entries.zh: 母喪自解，起爲寧朔將軍，復本職。
entries.en: He resigned on his mother's death, then on returning from mourning was restored as General Who Pacifies the North and resumed his former posts.
entries.literal: On his mother's death he resigned of his own accord; on mourning's end he was restored as General Who Pacifies the North and resumed his former duties.

entries.zh: 太祖欲度廣陵起兵，僧真又啓曰：「主上雖復狂釁，虐加萬民，而累世皇基，猶固盤石。
entries.en: When the Founding Emperor planned to cross to Guangling and raise troops, Sengzhen urged him again: "Though the sovereign is violent and cruel and brings suffering on the people, the imperial foundation built over generations still stands firm as bedrock.
entries.literal: The Founding Emperor wished to cross to Guangling and raise troops; Sengzhen again reported, saying, "Although the sovereign is again violent and cruel, inflicting suffering on the myriad people, the imperial foundation built over generations remains firm as bedrock.

entries.zh: 今百口北度，何必得俱。
entries.en: If your whole household crosses north now, why must every soul go together?
entries.literal: Now if a hundred mouths cross north, why must all go together?

entries.zh: 縱得廣陵城，天子居深宮施號令，目明公爲逆，何以避此？
entries.en: Even if you take Guangling, the Son of Heaven will remain in the deep palace issuing orders and will mark you as a rebel. How will you escape that charge?
entries.literal: Even if you take Guangling city, the Son of Heaven dwells in the deep palace issuing commands, and will regard my lord as a rebel — how will you escape this?

entries.zh: 如其不勝，則應北走胡中，竊謂此非萬全策也。」
entries.en: And if you fail, you would have to flee north among the barbarians. I do not believe this is a plan that can truly secure your safety."
entries.literal: If you do not prevail, you would have to flee north among the barbarians; I venture to say this is not a plan of complete security."

entries.zh: 上曰：「卿顧家，豈能逐我行耶。」
entries.en: The emperor said, "You are thinking of your family. How could you follow me in this?"
entries.literal: The emperor said, "You are thinking of your family; how could you follow me in this?"

entries.zh: 僧真頓首稱無貳。
entries.en: Sengzhen kowtowed and swore he would not waver.
entries.literal: Sengzhen bowed his head to the ground and declared he would not waver.

entries.zh: 昇明元年，除員外郎，帶東武城令。
entries.en: In the first year of Shengming he was appointed supplementary gentleman, with concurrent duty as magistrate of Dongwucheng.
entries.literal: In the first year of Shengming he was appointed Supplementary Gentleman, concurrently serving as magistrate of Dongwucheng.

entries.zh: 尋除給事中、邵陵王參軍。
entries.en: Soon afterward he was made gentleman attendant and staff officer to the Prince of Shaoling.
entries.literal: Soon he was appointed Gentleman Attendant and staff officer to the Prince of Shaoling.

entries.zh: 元徽初，從太祖頓新亭，拒桂陽賊。
entries.en: At the start of the Yuanhui era he followed the Founding Emperor in encamping at Xinting to resist the Guiyang rebels.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Yuanhui era, he followed the Founding Emperor in encamping at Xinting to resist the rebels of Guiyang.

entries.zh: 蕭惠朗突入東門，僧真與左右共拒戰。
entries.en: Xiao Huilang broke through the eastern gate, and Sengzhen fought him off together with the men at hand.
entries.literal: Xiao Huilang burst through the eastern gate; Sengzhen and the attendants resisted together in battle.

entries.zh: 賊退，太祖命僧真領親兵，遊邏城中。
entries.en: When the rebels withdrew, the Founding Emperor ordered Sengzhen to lead his personal troops in patrolling the city.
entries.literal: When the rebels withdrew, the Founding Emperor ordered Sengzhen to lead personal troops and patrol the city.

entries.zh: 事寧，除南臺御史、太祖領軍功曹。
entries.en: When the crisis passed, he was appointed censor of the Southern Bureau and merit officer on the Founding Emperor's staff as commander-in-chief.
entries.literal: When affairs were settled, he was appointed Censor of the Southern Bureau and Merit Officer in the Founding Emperor's headquarters as Commander-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 上將廢立，謀之袁粲、褚淵，僧真啓上曰：「今朝廷猖狂，人不自保，天下之望，不在袁、褚。
entries.en: As the emperor prepared to depose the ruler and set another on the throne, he took counsel with Yuan Can and Chu Yuan. Sengzhen urged him, saying, "The court is now running wild and no one can feel safe. The hopes of the realm do not rest on Yuan and Chu.
entries.literal: As the emperor was about to depose and enthrone, he consulted Yuan Can and Chu Yuan; Sengzhen reported to him, saying, "Now the court is reckless; no one can protect himself; the hopes of the realm do not rest on Yuan and Chu.

entries.zh: 明公豈得默己，坐受夷滅。
entries.en: How can you remain silent and sit by while you and yours are destroyed?
entries.literal: How can my lord remain silent and sit by while destruction overtakes you?

entries.zh: 存亡之機，仰希熟慮。」
entries.en: The question of survival or ruin hangs on this. I beg you to weigh it with care."
entries.literal: The moment of survival or destruction hangs on this; I beg you to consider it carefully."

entries.zh: 太祖納之。
entries.en: The Founding Emperor took his advice.
entries.literal: The Founding Emperor accepted this.

entries.zh: 宋世道人楊法持，與太祖有舊。
entries.en: During Song times the Daoist Yang Fachi had long-standing ties with the Founding Emperor.
entries.literal: In Song times the Daoist Yang Fachi had old ties with the Founding Emperor.

entries.zh: 元徽末，宣傳密謀。
entries.en: At the end of the Yuanhui era he helped spread secret plots.
entries.literal: At the end of Yuanhui he spread secret plots.

entries.zh: 昇明中，以爲僧正。
entries.en: During the Shengming era he was made superintendent of monks.
entries.literal: During Shengming he was made Superintendent of Monks.

entries.zh: 建元初，罷道，爲寧朔將軍，封州陵縣男，三百戶。
entries.en: At the start of Jianyuan he left the religious life, was appointed General Who Pacifies the North, and enfeoffed as Baron of Zhouling county with three hundred households.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Jianyuan he left the religious life, was made General Who Pacifies the North, and enfeoffed as Baron of Zhouling county with three hundred households.

entries.zh: 二年，虜圍朐山，遣法持爲軍主，領支軍救援。
entries.en: In the second year, when the barbarians besieged Qushan, Fachi was sent as army commander to lead a relief detachment.
entries.literal: In the second year, when the barbarians besieged Qushan, Fachi was sent as army commander to lead a supporting force in relief.

entries.zh: 永明四年，坐役使將客，奪其鮭稟，削封。
entries.en: In the fourth year of Yongming he was stripped of his enfeoffment for forcing a traveling guest into service and seizing his salmon ration.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Yongming, for employing and mistreating a traveling guest and seizing his salmon ration, his enfeoffment was revoked.

entries.zh: 卒。
entries.en: He died.
entries.literal: He died.

entries.zh: 四年，白賊唐宇之起，宿衞兵東討，遣係宗隨軍慰勞，徧至遭賊郡縣。
entries.en: In the fourth year the White-bandit rebel Tang Yuzhi rose. The palace guard marched east to suppress him, and Xizong was sent with the army to offer comfort and rewards, visiting every commandery and county the rebels had ravaged.
entries.literal: In the fourth year the White-bandit rebel Tang Yuzhi rose; the palace guard marched east to suppress him, and Xizong was sent with the army to offer comfort and rewards, reaching every commandery and county that had suffered the rebels.

entries.zh: 百姓被驅逼者，悉無所問，還復民伍。
entries.en: Commoners who had been driven into service were not punished and were restored to civilian life.
entries.literal: Common people who had been driven and compelled were all left unpunished and restored to civilian status.

entries.zh: 係宗還，上曰：「此段有征無戰，以時平蕩，百姓安怗，甚快也。」
entries.en: When Xizong returned, the emperor said, "This campaign brought expedition without battle. The disturbance was pacified in good time and the people are at peace — I am most pleased."
entries.literal: When Xizong returned, the emperor said, "In this campaign there was expedition without battle; the disturbance was pacified in good time and the people are settled in peace — most gratifying."

entries.zh: 賜係宗錢帛。
entries.en: He rewarded Xizong with money and silks.
entries.literal: He bestowed money and silks on Xizong.

entries.zh: 上欲脩治白下城，難於動役。
entries.en: The emperor wished to repair Baixia city but hesitated to mobilize labor for the project.
entries.literal: The emperor wished to repair and improve Baixia city but found it difficult to mobilize labor.

entries.zh: 係宗啓謫役東民丁隨宇之爲逆者，上從之。
entries.en: Xizong proposed assigning corvée labor from eastern households that had followed Yuzhi in rebellion, and the emperor agreed.
entries.literal: Xizong reported that corvée labor from eastern households that had followed Yuzhi in rebellion should be assigned to the work; the emperor agreed.

entries.zh: 後車駕講武，上履行白下城，曰：「劉係宗爲國家得此一城。」
entries.en: Later, during an imperial martial review, the emperor walked along Baixia city and said, "Liu Xizong won this city for the state."
entries.literal: Later, when the imperial carriage reviewed the troops in martial display, the emperor walked along Baixia city and said, "Liu Xizong won this city for the state."

entries.zh: 永明中，虜使書常令係宗題答，祕書書局皆隷之。
entries.en: During Yongming, replies to letters from barbarian envoys were often entrusted to Xizong for drafting, and the secretariat's writing offices were all placed under his supervision.
entries.literal: During Yongming, when barbarian envoys sent letters, Xizong was often made to inscribe the replies; the secretariat's writing offices were all placed under him.

entries.zh: 再爲少府，遷游擊將軍、魯郡太守。
entries.en: He twice served as Minister of the Palace Parks, then was promoted to General Who Scatters the Enemy and governor of Lu commandery.
entries.literal: He twice served as Minister of the Palace Parks, then was transferred to General Who Scatters the Enemy and governor of Lu commandery.

entries.zh: 鬱林卽位，除驍騎將軍，仍除寧朔將軍、宣城太守。
entries.en: When Emperor Yulin took the throne, Xizong was made General of Valiant Cavalry and then concurrently General Who Pacifies the North and governor of Xuancheng.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yulin took the throne, Xizong was appointed General of Valiant Cavalry, then concurrently General Who Pacifies the North and governor of Xuancheng.

entries.zh: 係宗久在朝省，閑於職事。
entries.en: Xizong had long served in the court offices and was thoroughly skilled in official business.
entries.literal: Xizong had long served in the court offices and was skilled in official business.

entries.zh: 明帝曰：「學士不堪治國，唯大讀書耳。
entries.en: Emperor Ming said, "Scholars cannot govern a state — they only read vast numbers of books.
entries.literal: Emperor Ming said, "Scholars are unfit to govern the state; they only read many books.

entries.zh: 一劉係宗足持如此輩五百人。」
entries.en: A single Liu Xizong is worth five hundred of them."
entries.literal: One Liu Xizong is enough to manage five hundred such men."

entries.zh: 其重吏事如此。
entries.en: Such was the weight he placed on practical administration.
entries.literal: Such was the weight he placed on practical administration.

entries.zh: 建武二年，卒官，年七十七。
entries.en: In the second year of Jianwu he died in office at the age of seventy-seven.
entries.literal: In the second year of Jianwu he died in office at the age of seventy-seven.

entries.zh: 文顯治事以刻覈被知。
entries.en: Wenxian became known for administering affairs with harsh rigor.
entries.literal: Wenxian became known for handling affairs with harsh rigor.

entries.zh: 三年，帶南清河太守。
entries.en: In the third year he concurrently served as governor of Nanqinghe.
entries.literal: In the third year he concurrently served as governor of Nanqinghe.

entries.zh: 與茹法亮等迭出入爲舍人，竝見親倖。
entries.en: He and Ru Faliang and others took turns serving as secretariat attendants, and all enjoyed the emperor's intimate favor.
entries.literal: He and Ru Faliang and others took turns entering and leaving as attendants, and all were personally favored.

entries.zh: 四方餉遺，歲各數百萬，竝造大宅，聚山開池。
entries.en: Gifts from every quarter brought them several million a year apiece. They all built great mansions, heaped up artificial hills, and opened ornamental pools.
entries.literal: Gifts from the four directions amounted to several million each year; they all built great mansions, heaped up hills, and opened pools.

entries.zh: 五年，爲建康令，轉長水校尉，歷帶南泰山、南譙太守，尋爲司徒中兵參軍，淮南太守，直舍人省。
entries.en: In the fifth year he became magistrate of Jiankang, then colonel of the Long River, and successively held concurrent governorships of Nantaishan and Nanqiao. Soon afterward he was made central army staff officer to the Minister of State, governor of Huainan, and attached to the attendants' bureau.
entries.literal: In the fifth year he was magistrate of Jiankang, then transferred to Colonel of the Long River, successively concurrently governor of Nantaishan and Nanqiao, soon made Central Army Staff Officer to the Minister of State, governor of Huainan, and attached to the Attendants' Bureau.

entries.zh: 累遷左中郎將，南東莞太守，右軍將軍。
entries.en: He rose through the posts of left commander of the palace guards, governor of Nandongguan, and General of the Right Army.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Left Commander of the Palace Guards, governor of Nandongguan, and General of the Right Army.

entries.zh: 高宗輔政，以文顯守少府，見任使。
entries.en: When Emperor Gao held the regency, Wenxian was made acting Minister of the Palace Parks and was trusted with important duties.
entries.literal: When Emperor Gao held regency, Wenxian was made acting Minister of the Palace Parks and was trusted and employed.

entries.zh: 歷建武、永元之世，尚書右丞，少府卿。
entries.en: Through the Jianwu and Yongyuan eras he served as right assistant master of writing and Minister of the Palace Parks.
entries.literal: Through the Jianwu and Yongyuan eras he served as Right Assistant Master of Writing and Minister of the Palace Parks.

entries.zh: 卒。
entries.en: He died.
entries.literal: He died.

entries.zh: 南齊書卷第五十六 列傳第三十七
entries.en: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 56, Biographies 37
entries.literal: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 56, Biographies 37

entries.zh: 高麗俗服窮袴，冠折風一梁，謂之幘。
entries.en: Goguryeo custom favored narrow trousers and a cap with a single crosswise rib, called a ze.
entries.literal: Gaoli custom: dress of narrow trousers, a cap with one crossbeam of folded wind, called a ze.

entries.zh: 知讀五經。
entries.en: They could read the Five Classics.
entries.literal: They know how to read the Five Classics.

entries.zh: 使人在京師，中書郎王融戯之曰：「服之不衷，身之災也。
entries.en: When a Goguryeo envoy was in the capital, Secretariat Gentleman Wang Rong teased him, quoting, 'Dress that is not centered brings bodily disaster.
entries.literal: When an envoy was in the capital, Secretariat Gentleman Wang Rong jested with him, saying: 'Dress not at the center is a bodily calamity.

entries.zh: 頭上定是何物？」
entries.en: What in the world is that on your head?'
entries.literal: What exactly is that on your head?'

entries.zh: 答曰：「此即古弁之遺像也。」
entries.en: The envoy replied, 'This is the ancient ceremonial cap preserved from antiquity.'
entries.literal: He answered: 'This is the surviving image of the ancient bian cap.'

entries.zh: 蠻
entries.en: The Man.
entries.literal: The Man.

entries.zh: 宋世其國相希利垔解星筭數術，通胡、漢語，常言南方當有姓名齊者，其人當興。
entries.en: During Song times their state chancellor Xili'an mastered astrology and mathematics, spoke both Hu and Chinese, and often said that in the south there would be a man surnamed Qi who would rise to power.
entries.literal: In the Song era their state chancellor Xili'an understood star calculation and number arts, knew both Hu and Han speech, and often said that in the south there would be one whose surname and given name were Qi, and that man would rise.

entries.zh: 昇明二年，太祖輔政，遣驍騎將軍王洪範使芮芮，剋期共伐魏虜。
entries.en: In the second year of Shengming, while the Founding Emperor held the regency, he sent General of Valiant Cavalry Wang Hongfan to Rouran to arrange a joint campaign against the Northern Wei.
entries.literal: In the second year of Shengming, while the Founding Emperor assisted in government, he sent General of Valiant Cavalry Wang Hongfan as envoy to Rouran to fix a date for a joint attack on the Wei barbarians.

entries.zh: 建元元年八月，芮芮主發三十萬騎南侵，去平城七百里，魏虜拒守不敢戰，芮芮主於燕然山下縱獵而歸。
entries.en: In the eighth month of the first year of Jianyuan, the Rouran ruler sent three hundred thousand horsemen south as far as seven hundred li from Pingcheng; the Northern Wei held their defenses and would not give battle, and the Rouran ruler hunted below Mount Yanran and withdrew.
entries.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Jianyuan, the Rouran lord sent three hundred thousand horsemen south in invasion, coming within seven hundred li of Pingcheng; the Wei barbarians defended and dared not fight, and the Rouran lord hunted beneath Mount Yanran and returned.

entries.zh: 上初踐阼，不遑出師。
entries.en: When the emperor first took the throne, he had no time to march out in person.
entries.literal: When the emperor first ascended the throne, he had no leisure to take the field.

entries.zh: 永明元年，王洪範還京師，經途三萬餘里。
entries.en: In the first year of Yongming, Wang Hongfan returned to the capital after a journey of more than thirty thousand li.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongming, Wang Hongfan returned to the capital, having traveled more than thirty thousand li.

entries.zh: 洪範，齊郡臨淄人，為太祖所親信。
entries.en: Hongfan was from Linzi in Qi commandery and enjoyed the Founding Emperor's personal trust.
entries.literal: Hongfan was a man of Linzi in Qi commandery and was personally trusted by the Founding Emperor.

entries.zh: 建武中，為青冀二州刺史。
entries.en: During the Jianwu era he served as inspector of Qing and Ji.
entries.literal: During Jianwu he was made inspector of the two provinces Qing and Ji.

entries.zh: 私占丁侵虜堺，奔敗結氣卒。
entries.en: He privately seized households and encroached on the Wei frontier; after fleeing in defeat he died of choking rage.
entries.literal: He privately registered households and encroached on the barbarian frontier; fleeing in defeat, he died of pent-up rage.

entries.zh: 二年、三年，芮芮主頻遣使貢獻貂皮雜物。
entries.en: In the second and third years of the dynasty, the Rouran ruler repeatedly sent envoys bearing sable pelts and other gifts.
entries.literal: In the second and third years, the Rouran lord frequently sent envoys to present tribute of sable furs and miscellaneous goods.

entries.zh: 與上書欲伐魏虜，謂上「足下」，自稱「吾」。
entries.en: In his memorial to the throne he proposed attacking the Northern Wei, addressed the emperor as "Your Foot," and referred to himself as "I."
entries.literal: In his letter to the emperor he wished to attack the Wei barbarians; he addressed the emperor as "Your Foot" and called himself "I."

entries.zh: 獻師子皮袴褶，皮如虎皮，色白毛短。
entries.en: He presented a jacket-and-trousers set of supposed lion skin; the hide resembled tiger skin, pale in color with short fur.
entries.literal: He presented a lion-skin jacket and trousers; the hide was like tiger skin, white in color with short hair.

entries.zh: 時有賈胡在蜀見之，云此非師子皮，乃扶拔皮也。
entries.en: A foreign merchant then in Shu saw it and said it was not lion skin at all but baboon hide.
entries.literal: At the time a merchant from abroad in Shu saw it and said this was not lion skin but baboon skin.

entries.zh: 國相邢基祇羅迴奉表曰：
entries.en: The Rouran chancellor Xingjizhiluo Hui submitted a memorial that read:
entries.literal: The state chancellor Xingjizhiluo Hui presented a memorial, saying:

entries.zh: 夫四象稟政，二儀改度，而萬物生焉。
entries.en: The four emblems take up the mandate of rule, the two cosmic principles shift their measure, and the ten thousand things come into being.
entries.literal: The four images receive governance; the two principles change their measure, and the ten thousand things are thereby born.

entries.zh: 斯蓋虧盈迭襲，歷數自然也。
entries.en: This is nothing but the alternation of decline and fullness, the natural rhythm of dynastic fortune.
entries.literal: This is surely the succession of waning and waxing in turn—the natural course of dynastic numbers.

entries.zh: 昔晉室將終，楚桓竊命，寔賴宋武匡濟之功，故能扶衰定傾，休否以泰。
entries.en: When the Jin house neared its end, Huan Wen of Chu seized power; it was Song Wu Di's work of rescue that propped up a failing dynasty, steadied a tottering state, and turned misfortune into prosperity.
entries.literal: Formerly when the Jin house was about to end, Chu Huan usurped the mandate; it truly relied on Song Wu's merit in righting the age, and therefore was able to support the declining and settle the tipping, turning adversity into peace.

entries.zh: 祚流九葉，而國嗣不繼。
entries.en: The throne passed through nine generations, yet the line of succession broke off.
entries.literal: The throne passed through nine generations, yet the succession of the state did not continue.

entries.zh: 今皇天降禍於上，宋室猜亂于下。
entries.en: Now Heaven has sent down calamity from above, while the Song house below is riven by suspicion and turmoil.
entries.literal: Now Heaven above sends calamity, and the Song house below is suspicious and in disorder.

entries.zh: 臣雖荒遠，粗闚圖書，數難以來，星文改度，房心受變，虛危納祉，宋滅齊昌，此其驗也。
entries.en: Though I dwell in a distant land, I have gleaned something from the charts and classics: as disasters have piled up one after another, the stars have shifted their stations—Fang and Xin have changed, Xu and Wei have taken in good fortune—Song is destroyed and Qi rises: this is the proof.
entries.literal: Your servant, though remote and barbarous, has roughly glimpsed the charts and books; since calamities have come in succession, the star writings have changed their degrees—Fang and Xin received transformation, Xu and Wei received blessing—Song perished and Qi flourished: this is the proof.

entries.zh: 水運遘屯，木德應運，子年垂刈，劉穆之記，崏嶺有不衽之山，京房讖云「卯金十六，草肅應王」。
entries.en: The fortune of Water meets obstruction; the virtue of Wood answers the times; the zi year is ripe for the reaping; so runs Liu Muzhi's record; on Mount Min stands the Mountain of Unlapped Robes; and Jing Fang's prophecy reads, "Mao-metal at sixteen—grass and su shall answer as king."
entries.literal: The Water Phase's fortune meets obstruction; the Wood Virtue responds to the mandate; the zi year approaches harvest; Liu Muzhi's record; on Mount Min there is a mountain of unlapped robes; Jing Fang's prophecy says, "Mao-metal sixteen, grass-su responds as king."

entries.zh: 歷觀圖緯，休徵非一，皆云慶鍾蕭氏，代宋者齊。
entries.en: Surveying the prognostic charts and weft-texts, the auspicious omens are many, and all declare that fortune will settle on the house of Xiao—that Qi is destined to replace Song.
entries.literal: Reviewing the charts and weft-texts throughout, auspicious signs are not one alone; all say blessing concentrates on the Xiao clan—he who replaces Song is Qi.

entries.zh: 會有使力法度及△此國使反，採訪聖德，彌驗天縱之姿。
entries.en: By chance the envoy Li Fadu and other envoys of your state returned from their missions; in seeking out your sagely virtue they confirmed all the more your heaven-endowed excellence.
entries.literal: It happened that the envoy Li Fadu and [lacuna] envoys of this state returned, inquiring into sagely virtue and confirming all the more a heaven-endowed bearing.

entries.zh: 故能挾隆皇祚，光權定之業，翼亮天功，濟悖主之難。
entries.en: Thus you could uphold the exalted imperial succession, bring glory to the work of securing the realm, aid Heaven's achievement, and deliver the realm from a wayward ruler's peril.
entries.literal: Therefore you were able to embrace the exalted imperial succession, glorify the enterprise of settling authority, assist and brighten Heaven's achievement, and rescue the difficulty of a perverse lord.

entries.zh: 樹勳京師，威振海外。
entries.en: You built up merit in the capital, and your prestige shook the lands beyond the seas.
entries.literal: You planted merit in the capital; your awe shook lands beyond the seas.

entries.zh: 杖義之功，侔縱湯、武。
entries.en: Your righteous achievement matched that of Tang and Wu.
entries.literal: The achievement of upholding righteousness was equal to Tang and Wu of old.

entries.zh: 冥績旣著，寶命因歸，受終之曆，歸于有道。
entries.en: Once your hidden merit had shone forth, the precious mandate returned to you; the calendar of succession passed to the one who holds the Way.
entries.literal: Hidden merit having been displayed, the precious mandate thereby returned; the calendar of receiving the end belonged to the Way.

entries.zh: 況夫帝無常族，有德必昌，時來之數，唯靈是與。
entries.en: Moreover, the throne has no fixed house: those with virtue must prosper, and the fortune of the age belongs only to the worthy spirit.
entries.literal: Moreover, emperorship has no fixed clan; those with virtue must flourish—the number of the time come shares only with the numinous.

entries.zh: 陛下承乾啓之機，因乘龍之運，計應符革祚，久已踐極，荒裔傾戴，莫不引領。
entries.en: Your Majesty seized the opening granted by Heaven and rode the dragon's fortune; by every reckoning you matched the omens to change the dynasty and have long since ascended the throne, while distant lands bow in allegiance and all stretch their necks in hope.
entries.literal: Your Majesty inherited the opportunity of Qian's opening and rode the fortune of the dragon's ascent; by reckoning you matched the omen to change the throne and long since trod the ultimate—barbarian lands lean in allegiance, none not stretching their necks.

entries.zh: 設未龍飛，不宜沖挹，上違天人之心，下乖黎庶之望。
entries.en: If the dragon has not yet taken flight, it is wrong to hold yourself back: above, you would defy the hearts of Heaven and men; below, you would betray the people's hopes.
entries.literal: If you have not yet flown as the dragon, it is not fitting to hold back in humility—above you would violate the hearts of Heaven and man, below you would go against the hopes of the common people.

entries.zh: 芮芮王求醫工等物，世祖詔報曰：「知須醫及織成錦工、指南車、漏刻，竝非所愛。
entries.en: The Rouran king asked for physicians and other items. Emperor Wu replied by edict: "We know you need physicians, brocade weavers, a south-pointing carriage, and a clepsydra—none of these are things we are willing to provide.
entries.literal: The Rouran king requested physicians and other things; Emperor Shizu replied by edict: "We know you need physicians and brocade-weaving craftsmen, the south-pointing carriage, and the clepsydra—all are not what we favor sending.

entries.zh: 南方治疾，與北土不同。
entries.en: Medicine in the south differs from practice in the north.
entries.literal: In the south, treating illness differs from the northern soil.

entries.zh: 織成錦工，竝女人，不堪涉遠。
entries.en: Brocade weavers are all women and cannot endure a long journey.
entries.literal: Brocade-weaving craftsmen are all women and cannot bear to travel far.

entries.zh: 指南車、漏刻，此雖有其器，工匠久不復存，不副爲誤。」
entries.en: As for the south-pointing carriage and clepsydra, although the devices exist, the craftsmen who made them have long since vanished; it would be a mistake to send them."
entries.literal: As for the south-pointing carriage and clepsydra, although these devices exist, the craftsmen have long ceased to exist—it would not suit to send them in error."

entries.zh: 建元元年，太祖即本官進號驃騎大將軍。
entries.en: In the first year of Jianyuan, the Founding Emperor advanced him, in his existing offices, to General of Agile Cavalry.
entries.literal: In the first year of Jianyuan, the Founding Emperor advanced him, in his existing offices, to General of Agile Cavalry.

entries.zh: 宋世遣武衞將軍王世武使河南，是歲隨拾寅使來獻。
entries.en: During Song, General of the Martial Guard Wang Shiwu was sent to Henan; that year he came with Shiyin's envoy bearing tribute.
entries.literal: In the Song era they sent General of the Martial Guard Wang Shiwu as envoy to Henan; that year he came with Shiyin's envoy to present tribute.

entries.zh: 詔答曰：「皇帝敬問使持節、散騎常侍、都督西秦河沙三州諸軍事、車騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、領護羌校尉、西秦河二州刺史、新除驃騎大將軍、河南王：寶命革授，爰集朕躬，猥當大業，祗惕兼懷。
entries.en: An edict replied: "The emperor respectfully greets the Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Commander of Military Affairs in Western Qin, He, and Sha, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Grand Master with an office equal to the Three Excellencies, Colonel Protector of the Qiang, Inspector of Western Qin and He, and newly appointed General of Agile Cavalry, King of Henan: the sacred mandate has passed to Us, and unworthily We bear the great task with reverence and fear.
entries.literal: An edict replied: "The emperor respectfully inquires of the Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Commander of all military affairs of the three provinces Xi-Qin-He-Sha, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Grand Master opening an office equal to the Three Excellencies, Colonel Protector of the Qiang, Inspector of the two provinces Xi-Qin-He, and newly appointed General of Agile Cavalry, King of Henan: the precious mandate has been changed and conferred and has gathered upon Our person; unworthily We bear the great enterprise, reverent and fearful together.

entries.zh: 夏中增感。
entries.en: In midsummer Our feelings deepened.
entries.literal: In midsummer Our feeling increased.

entries.zh: 王世武至，得元徽五年五月二十一日表，聞之濕熱，想比平安。
entries.en: Wang Shiwu arrived with your memorial dated the twenty-first day of the fifth month of Yuanhui 5; hearing of the damp heat there, We trust you remain safe.
entries.literal: Wang Shiwu arrived and We received the memorial of the twenty-first day of the fifth month of the fifth year of Yuanhui; hearing of the damp heat, We trust you are comparatively safe.

entries.zh: 又卿乃誠遙著，保寧遐壃。
entries.en: Your loyalty shines from afar, guarding and pacifying the distant frontier.
entries.literal: Moreover your loyalty shines from afar, guarding and pacifying the distant frontier.

entries.zh: 今詔升徽號，以酬忠款。
entries.en: We now decree the advancement of your title in reward for your loyalty.
entries.literal: Now We decree advancement of your honored title to repay loyal sincerity.

entries.zh: 遣王世武銜命拜授。
entries.en: We send Wang Shiwu with the commission to invest you.
entries.literal: We send Wang Shiwu bearing the mandate to invest you.

entries.zh: 又仍使王世武等往芮芮，想即資遣，使得時達。
entries.en: We also send Wang Shiwu and others on to Rouran; please supply and dispatch them promptly so they may arrive in time.
entries.literal: We also again send Wang Shiwu and others to Rouran; We trust you will promptly supply and dispatch them so they may arrive in time.

entries.zh: 又奏所上馬等物悉至，今往別牒錦絳紫碧綠黃青等紋各十匹。」
entries.en: We note your report that the horses and other tribute have all arrived; by separate dispatch We send brocades in crimson, purple, blue-green, green, yellow, and blue, ten bolts of each."
entries.literal: Your memorial that the horses and other goods presented have all arrived is noted; by separate dispatch We now send brocades in crimson, purple, blue-green, green, yellow, and blue patterns, ten bolts each."

entries.zh: 易度侯卒，八年，立其世子休留茂爲使持節、督西秦河沙三州諸軍事、鎮西將軍、領護羌校尉、西秦河二州刺史。
entries.en: When Yiduhou died, in the eighth year his heir Xiulumao was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Supervisor of Military Affairs in the Three Provinces of Western Qin, He, and Sha, General Who Pacifies the West, Colonel Protector of the Qiang, and Inspector of Western Qin and He.
entries.literal: When Yiduhou died, in the eighth year they established his heir Xiulumao as Bearer of the Staff, Supervisor of all military affairs of the three provinces Xi-Qin-He-Sha, General Who Pacifies the West, Colonel Protector of the Qiang, and Inspector of the two provinces Xi-Qin-He.

entries.zh: 復遣振武將軍丘冠先拜授，幷行弔禮。
entries.en: The court again sent General Who Quells Martial Qiu Guanxian to invest him and offer condolences.
entries.literal: They again sent General Who Quells Martial Qiu Guanxian to confer the appointment and also perform mourning rites.

entries.zh: 冠先至河南，休留茂逼令先拜，冠先厲色不肯，休留茂恥其國人，執冠先於絕巖上推墮深谷而死。
entries.en: When Guanxian reached Henan, Xiulumao tried to force him to bow first; Guanxian sternly refused. Ashamed before his people, Xiulumao seized him on a sheer cliff, pushed him into a deep ravine, and killed him.
entries.literal: When Guanxian reached Henan, Xiulumao forced him to bow first; Guanxian sternly refused. Xiulumao, shamed before his countrymen, seized Guanxian on a sheer cliff, pushed him off, and he fell into a deep ravine and died.

entries.zh: 冠先字道玄，吳興人，晉吏部郎傑六世孫也。
entries.en: Guanxian, styled Daoxuan, was from Wuxing and a sixth-generation descendant of Jie, Minister of the Civil Service under the Jin.
entries.literal: Guanxian's style was Daoxuan; he was a man of Wuxing, sixth-generation descendant of the Jin Minister of the Civil Service Jie.

entries.zh: 上初遣冠先，示尚書令王儉，儉答上曰：「此人不啻堪行。」
entries.en: When the emperor first chose Guanxian, he showed him to Director Wang Jian, who told the throne: "This man is more than fit for the mission."
entries.literal: When the emperor first sent Guanxian, he showed him to the Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Jian; Jian answered the emperor: "This man is not merely fit for the mission."

entries.zh: 乃再銜命。
entries.en: So he was sent out again.
entries.literal: Therefore he received the command a second time.

entries.zh: 及死，世祖敕其子雄曰：「卿父受使河南，秉忠守死，不辱王命，我甚賞惜，喪屍絕域，不可復尋，於卿後宦塗無妨，甚有高比。」
entries.en: After his death, Emperor Wu instructed his son Xiong: "Your father took the mission to Henan, kept faith unto death, and did not dishonor the imperial command. I prize and mourn him deeply. His body lies in a far land and cannot be recovered, but your official career will not suffer—you have a father to be proud of."
entries.literal: When he died, Emperor Shizu instructed his son Xiong: "Your father received the mission to Henan, held loyalty and kept death, and did not disgrace the royal command—we greatly prize and mourn him. His corpse lies in a distant land and cannot be sought again; your later official career will not be hindered—you have a very high comparison."

entries.zh: 賜錢十萬，布三十匹。
entries.en: He was granted one hundred thousand cash and thirty bolts of cloth.
entries.literal: He granted one hundred thousand cash and thirty bolts of cloth.

entries.zh: 拾寅子易度侯好星文，嘗求星書，朝議不給。
entries.en: Shiyin's son Yiduhou was fond of astronomy and once asked for star charts; the court refused to supply them.
entries.literal: Shiyin's son Yiduhou loved astral writings and once requested star books; court deliberation did not grant them.

entries.zh: 寅卒，三年，以河南王世子吐谷渾易度侯爲使持節、都督西秦河沙三州諸軍事、鎮西將軍、領護羌校尉、西秦河二州刺史、河南王。
entries.en: When Shiyin died, in the third year the heir of the King of Henan, Tuyuhun Yiduhou, was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Commander of Military Affairs in the Three Provinces of Western Qin, He, and Sha, General Who Guards the West, Colonel Protector of the Qiang, Inspector of Western Qin and He, and King of Henan.
entries.literal: When Shiyin died, in the third year they made the Heir of the King of Henan Tuyuhun Yiduhou Bearer of the Staff, Commander of all military affairs of the three provinces Xi-Qin-He-Sha, General Who Guards the West, Colonel Protector of the Qiang, Inspector of the two provinces Xi-Qin-He, and King of Henan.

entries.zh: 永明三年，詔曰：「易度侯守職西蕃，綏懷允緝，忠績兼舉，朕有嘉焉。
