entries.en: In the third year of Yongming, an edict read: "Yiduhou has kept his post on the western frontier, ruled with true harmony, and shown both loyalty and merit—we commend him.
entries.literal: In the third year of Yongming, an edict said: "Yiduhou guards his post in the western borderlands, pacifies and cherishes with true harmony, and loyalty and achievement are both displayed—we are pleased.

entries.zh: 可進號車騎大將軍。」
entries.en: He is promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry."
entries.literal: He may advance in title to General of Chariots and Cavalry."

entries.zh: 遣給事中丘冠先使河南道，幷送芮芮使。
entries.en: The court sent Attendant Within Qiu Guanxian on the Henan route and also to escort the Rouran envoy.
entries.literal: They sent the Attendant Within the Yellow Gate Qiu Guanxian as envoy on the Henan route, and also to escort the Rouran envoy.

entries.zh: 至六年乃還。
entries.en: He did not return until the sixth year.
entries.literal: He returned only in the sixth year.

entries.zh: 得玉長三尺二寸，厚一尺一寸。
entries.en: He brought back a jade slab three chi two cun long and one chi one cun thick.
entries.literal: He obtained jade three chi two cun long and one chi one cun thick.

entries.zh: 太祖即位，欲綏懷異俗。
entries.en: When the Founding Emperor took the throne, he sought to win over foreign peoples.
entries.literal: When the Founding Emperor took the throne, he wished to soothe and cherish foreign peoples.

entries.zh: 建元元年，詔曰：「昔絕國入贄，美稱前冊，殊俗內款，聲流往記。
entries.en: In the first year of Jianyuan, an edict read: "In former times distant states brought tribute and won praise in earlier annals; foreign peoples submitted and their fame filled past records.
entries.literal: In the first year of Jianyuan, an edict said: "In former times distant states entered with tribute, praised in earlier annals; foreign peoples submitted inwardly, their fame flowing in past records.

entries.zh: 偽虜茄蘆鎮主、陰平郡公楊廣香，怨結同族，舋起親黨，當宋之世，遂舉地降敵。
entries.en: Yang Guangxiang, the Northern Wei commander of Jialu and Duke of Yinping, bound by clan grievances and stirred up by kin, surrendered his territory to the enemy during Song.
entries.literal: The false barbarians' Jialu garrison chief and Duke of Yinping commandery Yang Guangxiang, with grievances binding his clan and trouble rising among kin, in the Song era then raised his lands and surrendered to the enemy.

entries.zh: 茄蘆失守，華陽暫驚。
entries.en: Jialu fell and Huayang was briefly thrown into alarm.
entries.literal: Jialu was lost and Huayang was briefly alarmed.

entries.zh: 近單使先馳，宣揚皇威，廣香等追其遠世之誠，仰我惟新之化，肉袒請附，復地千里，氐羌雜種，咸同歸從。
entries.en: Recently a lone envoy went ahead to proclaim imperial majesty; Guangxiang and others recalled their ancient loyalty, looked to Our renewing rule, came bare-chested to submit, restored a thousand li of territory, and Di and Qiang tribes alike returned to allegiance.
entries.literal: Recently a lone envoy went ahead, proclaiming imperial majesty; Guangxiang and others recalled the loyalty of distant ages, looked up to Our renewing transformation, bared their torsos to request attachment, restored a thousand li of territory, and Di and Qiang mixed stocks all alike returned in submission.

entries.zh: 宜時領納，厚加優卹。
entries.en: They should be received at once and generously favored.
entries.literal: They should promptly be received and generously favored with relief.

entries.zh: 廣香翻迷反正，可特量所授。
entries.en: Guangxiang, having turned from error back to loyalty, should receive a specially measured grant of office.
entries.literal: Guangxiang, turning from delusion back to the right, may be specially measured in what is granted.

entries.zh: 部曲酋豪，隨名酬賞。」
entries.en: Chieftains and leaders of his following are to be rewarded by name."
entries.literal: Chieftains and magnates of his following are to be rewarded according to their names."

entries.zh: 以廣香為督沙州諸軍事、平羌校尉、沙州刺史。
entries.en: Guangxiang was appointed Commander of Military Affairs in Shazhou, Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang, and Inspector of Shazhou.
entries.literal: Guangxiang was made Commander of all military affairs of Shazhou, Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang, and Inspector of Shazhou.

entries.zh: 尋進號征虜將軍。
entries.en: Soon he was promoted to general who punishes the barbarians.
entries.literal: Soon his title was advanced to General Who Punishes the Barbarians.

entries.zh: 文弘容納叛戾，專爲淵藪，外侮皇威，內凌國族。
entries.en: Wenhong sheltered rebels and outlaws, turning his domain into a rebel nest; he affronted imperial authority abroad and bullied the imperial clan at home.
entries.literal: Wenhong harbored rebels and outlaws, making himself a deep lair; outwardly he insulted imperial majesty, inwardly he bullied the imperial clan.

entries.zh: 君弈世忠款，深識理順，想卽起義，應接大軍，共爲掎角，討滅烏奴，剋建忠勤，茂立誠節。
entries.en: You have been loyal for generations and understand where duty lies; we expect you to rise at once, join our main army in a pincer movement, destroy Wunu, win merit through loyalty, and stand as a model of integrity.
entries.literal: My lord, your house for generations has been loyal and sincere, deeply knowing what reason and compliance require; we expect you at once to rise in righteous action, meet our great army, together form pincers, destroy Wunu, achieve merit in loyalty and diligence, and abundantly establish sincere integrity.

entries.zh: 沈攸之資十年之積，權百旅之衆，師出境而城潰，兵未戰而自屠，朝廷無遺鏃之費，士民靡傷痍之弊。
entries.en: Shen Youzhi had ten years of buildup and commanded armies a hundred brigades strong—yet his forces barely crossed the border before cities fell, and his men destroyed themselves without a battle; the court spent scarcely an arrow, and the people suffered hardly a wound.
entries.literal: Shen Youzhi relied on ten years' accumulation and commanded the hosts of a hundred brigades—his army left the borders and cities collapsed, troops had not fought and they slaughtered themselves; the court spent not a leftover arrow's cost, officers and people suffered no wound of harm.

entries.zh: 況蕞爾小豎，方之篾如，其取殲殄，豈延漏刻。
entries.en: As for this petty rebel, he is not even a splinter beside Shen Youzhi—his destruction cannot take more than a moment.
entries.literal: How much more this tiny villain, compared to whom he is like a splinter—his capture and extinction could not delay even a quarter-hour.

entries.zh: 忝以寡昧，分陝司蕃，清氛蕩穢，諒惟任職。
entries.en: Though I am unworthy in my limited wisdom, I oversee the frontier and must clear away this corruption—that is my duty.
entries.literal: I am unworthy in my slight dullness, dividing Shaan and overseeing the frontier; to clear the air and sweep away filth is surely my charge.

entries.zh: 此府器械山積，戈旗林聳，士卒剽勁，蓄銳權威，除難剿寇，豈俟徵習！
entries.en: This commandery's arms are heaped like mountains, its banners stand like a forest, its troops are fierce and ready—when cutting down rebels, why wait for drill!
entries.literal: This prefecture's weapons pile like mountains, spears and banners stand like forests, soldiers are fierce and sharp, stored edge and stored authority—destroying difficulty and cutting down bandits, how wait for mobilization and drill!

entries.zh: 但以剪伐萌菌，弗勞洪斧，撲彼蚊蚋，無假多力。
entries.en: This is only clearing away sprouts—no need for the great axe; swatting gnats requires no great effort.
entries.literal: It is only that cutting down sprouting fungus does not weary the great axe; swatting those mosquitoes needs no extra force.

entries.zh: 皇上聖哲應期，恩澤廣被，罪止首惡，餘無所問。
entries.en: Our sage emperor answers the times, and his grace is wide; guilt rests on the ringleader alone, and the rest will not be punished.
entries.literal: The emperor is sagely and wise, responding to the age; grace spreads widely; guilt stops at the chief villain, the rest are not questioned.

entries.zh: 賞罰之科，具寫如別。
entries.en: Rewards and punishments are set forth in the attached schedule.
entries.literal: The categories of reward and punishment are fully written as attached.

entries.zh: 使道寶步出魏興，分軍泝墊江，俱會晉壽。
entries.en: They sent Daobao out from Weixing, divided the army to go up the Dian River, and all converged on Jinshou.
entries.literal: They sent Daobao to march out from Weixing, divided the army to ascend the Dian River, and all met at Jinshou.

entries.zh: 太祖以文弘背叛，進廣香爲持節、都督西秦州刺史。
entries.en: Because Wenhong had rebelled, the Founding Emperor promoted Guangxiang to Bearer of the Staff and Commander of Western Qin.
entries.literal: The Founding Emperor, because Wenhong rebelled, advanced Guangxiang to Bearer of the Staff and Commander of Western Qinzhou.

entries.zh: 廣香子北部鎮將軍郡事炅爲征虜將軍、武都太守。
entries.en: Guangxiang's son Jiong, who handled commandery affairs at the northern garrison, was appointed General Who Punishes the Barbarians and administrator of Wudu.
entries.literal: Guangxiang's son, the northern garrison general in charge of commandery affairs Jiong, was made General Who Punishes the Barbarians and Administrator of Wudu.

entries.zh: 以難當正胤楊後起爲持節、寧朔將軍、平羌校尉、北秦州刺史、武都王，鎮武興，卽文弘從兄子也。
entries.en: Nandang's legitimate heir Yang Houqi was appointed Bearer of the Staff, General Who Pacifies the North, Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang, Inspector of Northern Qin, and King of Wudu, with his seat at Wuxing—Wenhong's cousin's son.
entries.literal: They made Nandang's legitimate heir Yang Houqi Bearer of the Staff, General Who Pacifies the North, Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang, Inspector of Northern Qinzhou, and King of Wudu, stationed at Wuxing—he was Wenhong's cousin's son.

entries.zh: 三年，文弘歸降，復以爲征西將軍、北秦州刺史。
entries.en: In the third year Wenhong submitted again and was reappointed General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Northern Qin.
entries.literal: In the third year, Wenhong returned in submission and was again made General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Northern Qinzhou.

entries.zh: 先是廣香病死，氐衆半奔文弘，半詣梁州刺史崔慧景。
entries.en: Earlier Guangxiang had died; half the Di people went to Wenhong and half to Cui Huijing, inspector of Liangzhou.
entries.literal: Earlier Guangxiang had died of illness; half the Di host fled to Wenhong, half went to the Inspector of Liangzhou Cui Huijing.

entries.zh: 文弘遣從子後起進據白水。
entries.en: Wenhong sent his cousin's son Houqi to advance and occupy Baishui.
entries.literal: Wenhong sent his cousin's son Houqi forward to seize Baishui.

entries.zh: 白水居晉壽上流，西接涪界，東帶益路，北連陰平、茄蘆，爲形勝之地。
entries.en: Baishui lay upstream from Jinshou, bordered Fu to the west and the Yi road to the east, and linked Yinping and Jialu to the north—a strategic strongpoint.
entries.literal: Baishui lay upstream of Jinshou, west connecting to Fu territory, east bordering the road to Yi, north linking Yinping and Jialu—a place of strategic advantage.

entries.zh: 晉壽太守楊公則啓經略之宜，上答曰：「文弘罪不可恕，事中政應且加恩耳。
entries.en: Jinshou administrator Yang Gongze submitted a plan of campaign; the emperor replied: "Wenhong's crime cannot be forgiven, yet for now the court should show him some grace.
entries.literal: The Administrator of Jinshou Yang Gongze memorialized on the proper strategy; the emperor answered: "Wenhong's crime cannot be forgiven, yet in the affair the government should for the moment add grace.

entries.zh: 卿若能襲破白水，必加厚賞。」
entries.en: If you can storm and take Baishui, your reward will be greatly increased."
entries.literal: If you can surprise and take Baishui, rewards will surely be greatly increased."

entries.zh: 世祖即位，進後起號冠軍將軍。
entries.en: When Emperor Wu took the throne, Houqi was promoted to general of the champion.
entries.literal: When Emperor Shizu took the throne, Houqi's title was advanced to General of the Champion.

entries.zh: 永明元年，以征虜將軍炅為沙州刺史、陰平王，將軍如故。
entries.en: In the first year of Yongming, General Who Punishes the Barbarians Jiong was appointed Inspector of Shazhou and King of Yinping, retaining his general's rank.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongming, General Who Punishes the Barbarians Jiong was made Inspector of Shazhou and King of Yinping, his general's rank unchanged.

entries.zh: 二年，八座奏，後起勤彰款塞，忠著邊城。
entries.en: In the second year the Eight Seats reported that Houqi's diligence had shown frontier loyalty and won renown on the border.
entries.literal: In the second year the Eight Seats memorialized that Houqi's diligence showed sincerity at the frontier and loyalty was manifest on the border walls.

entries.zh: 進號征虜將軍。
entries.en: He was promoted to general who punishes the barbarians.
entries.literal: His title was advanced to General Who Punishes the Barbarians.

entries.zh: 四年，後起卒，詔曰：「後起奄至殞逝，惻愴于懷。
entries.en: In the fourth year Houqi died; an edict read: "Houqi has died suddenly, and We are deeply grieved.
entries.literal: In the fourth year Houqi died; an edict said: "Houqi has suddenly reached death and fallen away; We are deeply grieved at heart.

entries.zh: 綏禦邊服，宜詳其選。
entries.en: To guard the frontier, the appointment must be carefully chosen.
entries.literal: To soothe and guard the frontier regions, the choice should be carefully considered.

entries.zh: 行輔國將軍、北秦州刺史、武都王楊集始，幹局沈亮，乃心忠款，必能緝境寧民、宣揚聲教。
entries.en: Acting General Who Assists the State, Inspector of Northern Qin, and King of Wudu Yang Jishi is capable and steadfastly loyal, and will surely pacify the frontier, settle the people, and spread imperial instruction.
entries.literal: Acting General Who Assists the State, Inspector of Northern Qinzhou, and King of Wudu Yang Jishi is deep and bright in capacity, loyal and sincere at heart, and can surely bring the borders to order, settle the people, and spread civilizing instruction.

entries.zh: 可持節、輔國將軍、北秦州刺史、平羌校尉、武都王。」
entries.en: He is appointed Bearer of the Staff, General Who Assists the State, Inspector of Northern Qin, Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang, and King of Wudu."
entries.literal: He may be Bearer of the Staff, General Who Assists the State, Inspector of Northern Qinzhou, Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang, and King of Wudu."

entries.zh: 後起弟後明為龍驤將軍、白水太守。
entries.en: Houqi's younger brother Houming was appointed general of the flying dragon and administrator of Baishui.
entries.literal: Houqi's younger brother Houming was made General of the Flying Dragon and Administrator of Baishui.

entries.zh: 集始弟集朗為寧朔將軍。
entries.en: Jishi's younger brother Jilang was appointed general who pacifies the north.
entries.literal: Jishi's younger brother Jilang was made General Who Pacifies the North.

entries.zh: 五年，有司奏集始驅狐剪棘，仰化邊服。
entries.en: In the fifth year the responsible offices reported that Jishi had cleared the frontier and won the border peoples' allegiance.
entries.literal: In the fifth year the responsible offices memorialized that Jishi had driven off foxes and cut brambles, looking up to transformation on the frontier.

entries.zh: 母以子貴，宜加榮寵。
entries.en: As the mother is ennobled through her son, added honors are fitting.
entries.literal: Because the mother is ennobled through the son, added honor and favor are fitting.

entries.zh: 除集始母姜氏為太夫人，假銀印。
entries.en: Jishi's mother, Lady Jiang, was made Grand Lady and granted a provisional silver seal.
entries.literal: Jishi's mother, Lady Jiang, was appointed Grand Lady and given a provisional silver seal.

entries.zh: 九年，八座奏，楊炅嗣勤西牧，馳款內昭，宜增戎章，用輝遐外。
entries.en: In the ninth year the Eight Seats reported that Yang Jiong had continued his loyal service on the western frontier and that his military honors should be increased to shine abroad.
entries.literal: In the ninth year the Eight Seats memorialized that Yang Jiong succeeded in diligence on the western pastures, hastening sincerity inward to make it manifest, and that military honors should be increased to shine on the distant marches.

entries.zh: 進號前將軍。
entries.en: He was promoted to general of the vanguard.
entries.literal: His title was advanced to General of the Vanguard.

entries.zh: 宕昌，羌種也。
entries.en: Dangchang was a Qiang people.
entries.literal: Dangchang was a Qiang stock.

entries.zh: 各有酋豪，領部眾汧、隴閒。
entries.en: Each tribe had chieftains leading their followers between the Qian and Long region.
entries.literal: Each had chieftains and magnates leading their hosts between Qian and Long.

entries.zh: 宋末，宕昌王梁彌機為使持節、督河涼二州、安西將軍、東羌校尉、河涼二州刺史、隴西公。
entries.en: At the end of Song, King of Dangchang Liang Miji held the posts of Bearer of the Staff, Commander of He and Liang, General Who Pacifies the West, Colonel of the Eastern Qiang, Inspector of He and Liang, and Duke of Longxi.
entries.literal: At the end of Song, King of Dangchang Liang Miji was Bearer of the Staff, Commander of the two provinces He and Liang, General Who Pacifies the West, Colonel of the Eastern Qiang, Inspector of the two provinces He and Liang, and Duke of Longxi.

entries.zh: 建元元年，太祖進號鎮西將軍。
entries.en: In the first year of Jianyuan, the Founding Emperor promoted him to general who guards the west.
entries.literal: In the first year of Jianyuan, the Founding Emperor advanced his title to General Who Guards the West.

entries.zh: 又征虜將軍、西涼州刺史羌王像舒彭亦進為持節、平西將軍。
entries.en: The Qiang king Xiang Shupeng, general who punishes the barbarians and inspector of Xiliang, was likewise promoted to bearer of the staff and general who pacifies the west.
entries.literal: Also General Who Punishes the Barbarians and Inspector of Xiliangzhou, the Qiang king Xiang Shupeng, was likewise advanced to Bearer of the Staff and General Who Pacifies the West.

entries.zh: 後叛降虜。
entries.en: Later he rebelled and surrendered to the Wei.
entries.literal: Later he rebelled and surrendered to the barbarians.

entries.zh: 永明元年，八座奏，前使持節、都督河涼二州軍事、鎮西將軍，東羌校尉、河涼二州刺史、隴西公、宕昌王梁彌機，前使持節、平北將軍、西涼州刺史、羌王像舒彭，竝著勤西垂，寧安邊境，可復先官爵。
entries.en: In the first year of Yongming the Eight Seats reported that the former King of Dangchang Liang Miji and the former Qiang king Xiang Shupeng had both served faithfully on the western frontier and secured the border, and that their former offices and titles should be restored.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongming the Eight Seats memorialized that the former Bearer of the Staff, Commander of military affairs of the two provinces He and Liang, General Who Guards the West, Colonel of the Eastern Qiang, Inspector of the two provinces He and Liang, Duke of Longxi, and King of Dangchang Liang Miji, and the former Bearer of the Staff, General Who Pacifies the North, Inspector of Xiliangzhou, and Qiang king Xiang Shupeng, had both shown diligence on the western marches and secured and pacified the frontier, and their former offices and titles might be restored.

entries.zh: 詔又可以隴右都帥羌王劉洛羊為輔國將軍。
entries.en: An edict also appointed Longyou commander Liu Luoyang, king of the Qiang, general who assists the state.
entries.literal: An edict also made the Longyou commander-in-chief and Qiang king Liu Luoyang General Who Assists the State.

entries.zh: 南齊書卷第五十九 列傳第四十
entries.en: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 59, Biographies 40
entries.literal: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 59, Biographies 40

entries.zh: 《南齊書》，八紀，十一志，四十列傳，合五十九篇，梁蕭子顯撰。
entries.en: The 《Book of Southern Qi》 comprises eight annals, eleven treatises, and forty biographies—fifty-nine fascicles in all—written by Xiao Zixian of the Liang dynasty.
entries.literal: The 《Book of Southern Qi》: eight annals, eleven treatises, forty biographies, fifty-nine fascicles in all, compiled by Xiao Zixian of Liang.

entries.zh: 始江淹已爲十志，沈約又爲《齊紀》，而子顯自表武帝，別爲此書。
entries.en: Jiang Yan had already drafted ten treatises, and Shen Yue had also written the 《Qi Chronicle》; but Zixian, having presented himself to Emperor Wu of Liang, undertook this work as a separate history.
entries.literal: At first Jiang Yan had already composed ten treatises, and Shen Yue had also written the 《Qi Chronicle》, but Zixian, having himself petitioned Emperor Wu, separately produced this book.

entries.zh: 臣等因校正其訛謬，而敘其篇目，曰：
entries.en: We, your subjects, have corrected its errors and set forth the table of contents, saying:
entries.literal: We, your subjects, therefore corrected its errors and blunders, and set forth its table of contents, saying:

entries.zh: 帝好讀書，愛文義，在藩時撰江左以來文章志，又續衛瓘所注論語二卷。
entries.en: The emperor loved reading and valued literary culture. While still a prince he compiled a record of writings from the lands east of the Yangzi since the Jin, and continued Wei Guan's annotated Lunyu in two scrolls.
entries.literal: The emperor loved reading and cherished literary principles; while still in his princedom he compiled a record of writings from the lands east of the Yangzi since the Jin, and also continued Wei Guan's annotated Lunyu in two scrolls.

entries.zh: 及即大位，舊臣才學之士多蒙引進。
entries.en: Once enthroned, he favored and promoted many veteran ministers and learned men.
entries.literal: When he reached the great throne, many old ministers and men of learning were favored and promoted.

entries.zh: 末年好鬼神，多忌諱，言語文書有禍敗凶喪疑似之言應回避者，犯即加戮。
entries.en: In his later years he grew obsessed with spirits and taboos. Any word in speech or documents suggesting disaster, defeat, or death that ought to be avoided would, if uttered, bring immediate execution.
entries.literal: In his later years he favored spirits and ghosts and was full of taboos; in speech and documents, any word suggesting disaster, defeat, mourning, or death that ought to be avoided—if violated, execution followed at once.

entries.zh: 改「騧」馬字為「馬」邊「瓜」，以「騧」字似「禍」故也。
entries.en: He changed the character for "piebald horse" to "horse" beside "melon," because the original character resembled the character for "disaster."
entries.literal: He changed the character for "piebald horse" to "horse" beside "melon," because the character for "piebald horse" resembled the character for "disaster."

entries.zh: 嘗以南苑借張永，云：「且給三百年，期盡更請。」
entries.en: He once lent the Southern Park to Zhang Yong, saying, "I shall lend it for three hundred years; when the term expires you may ask again."
entries.literal: He once lent the Southern Park to Zhang Yong, saying: "I shall lend it for three hundred years; when the term expires you may ask again."

entries.zh: 宣陽門謂之白門，上以白門不祥，諱之。
entries.en: The Xuanyang Gate was called the White Gate; the emperor considered "white gate" inauspicious and forbade the name.
entries.literal: The Xuanyang Gate was called the White Gate; the sovereign considered "white gate" inauspicious and tabooed it.

entries.zh: 尚書右丞江謐嘗誤犯，上變色曰：「白汝家門！」
entries.en: Jiang Mi, Right Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing, once accidentally violated the taboo. The emperor flushed and said, "May whiteness fall upon your family's gate!"
entries.literal: Jiang Mi, Right Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing, once accidentally violated the taboo; the sovereign changed color and said: "White upon your family's gate!"

entries.zh: 路太后停屍漆床移出東宮，上幸宮見之，怒，免中庶子，以之坐死者數十人。
entries.en: When Empress Dowager Lu's corpse was moved out of the Eastern Palace on a lacquered couch, the emperor visited the palace, saw it, flew into a rage, dismissed the Palace Mentor, and several dozen men were put to death on that account.
entries.literal: When Empress Dowager Lu's corpse was moved out of the Eastern Palace on a lacquered couch, the sovereign visited the palace, saw it, grew angry, dismissed the Palace Mentor, and several dozen men were put to death on that account.

entries.zh: 內外常慮犯觸，人不自保。
entries.en: Within and without the court, everyone lived in constant fear of giving offense and could not protect themselves.
entries.literal: Within and without, people constantly feared giving offense and could not protect themselves.

entries.zh: 移床修壁，先祭土神，使文士為祝策，如大祭饗。
entries.en: Before moving beds or repairing walls, they first sacrificed to the earth god and had literary men compose prayer texts as at a great sacrificial feast.
entries.literal: When moving beds or repairing walls, they first sacrificed to the earth god and had literary men compose prayer texts, as at a great sacrificial feast.

entries.zh: 宋本紀下第三
entries.en: Liu Song Annals, Part Three.
entries.literal: Liu Song Annals, lower scroll, third.

entries.zh: 穆之字思靜，晉司空華六世孫也。
entries.en: Zhang Muzhi, courtesy name Sijing, was a sixth-generation descendant of Zhang Hua, Grand Marshal of Jin.
entries.literal: Muzhi, whose courtesy name was Sijing, was a sixth-generation descendant of Zhang Hua, Grand Marshal of Jin.

entries.zh: 少方雅，有識鑒。
entries.en: In youth he was cultivated and discerning.
entries.literal: As a youth he was refined and elegant, with discernment and judgment.

entries.zh: 初為員外散騎侍郎，深被始興王浚引納。
entries.en: He began as a supernumerary attendant in the outer retinue of cavalries and was warmly taken up by Liu Jun, Prince of Shixing.
entries.literal: He first served as Supernumerary Attendant in the Outer Retinue of Cavalries and was deeply drawn in by Prince Jun of Shixing.

entries.zh: 穆之鑒其禍萌，求為交址太守，政有異績。
entries.en: Muzhi saw the disaster Liu Jun would bring and asked to be sent away as administrator of Jiaozhi, where his rule won unusual praise.
entries.literal: Muzhi perceived the budding of disaster in him and requested appointment as Administrator of Jiaozhi; his administration won unusual achievements.

entries.zh: 宋文帝將以為交州刺史，會病卒。
entries.en: Emperor Wen of Song was on the point of making him inspector of Jiaozhou when Muzhi died of illness.
entries.literal: Emperor Wen of Song was about to appoint him Inspector of Jiaozhou when Muzhi died of illness.

entries.zh: 子弘籍字真藝，齊初為鎮西參軍，卒於官。
entries.en: His son Zhang Hongji, courtesy name Zhenyi, served in early Qi as staff officer to the army pacifying the west and died in that post.
entries.literal: His son Hongji, courtesy name Zhenyi, in the early Qi served as Staff Officer for the Army of Pacifying the West and died in office.

entries.zh: 梁武踐阼，追贈穆之光祿大夫，加金章紫綬。
entries.en: When Emperor Wu of Liang took the throne, he posthumously granted Muzhi the office of grand master of the palace with the golden seal and purple cord.
entries.literal: When Liang Wu took the throne, he posthumously granted Muzhi the office of Grand Master of the Palace with the Golden Seal and Purple Cord.

entries.zh: 贈弘籍廷尉卿。
entries.en: He also posthumously granted Hongji the office of minister of justice.
entries.literal: He posthumously granted Hongji the office of Minister of Justice.

entries.zh: 弘籍無子，從父弟弘策以子纘嗣，別有傳。
entries.en: Hongji had no sons; his younger cousin Zhang Hongce had his own son Zuan continue the line — a separate biography treats them.
entries.literal: Hongji had no sons; his collateral younger cousin Hongce had his son Zuan succeed to the line — treated separately in another biography.

entries.zh: 隋煬帝每巡幸，恒令從駕。
entries.en: On every tour of Emperor Yang of Sui she was ordered to accompany the imperial train.
entries.literal: Whenever Emperor Yang of Sui went on tour he always ordered her to follow the imperial carriage.

entries.zh: 及煬帝被殺，后自廣陵過江，於毗陵天靜寺為尼，名觀音。
entries.en: After Yang's death she crossed the Yangzi from Guangling and took the tonsure at Tianjing Temple in Piling under the name Guanyin.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yang was killed the empress crossed the Yangzi from Guangling and at Tianjing Temple in Piling became a nun, taking the name Guanyin.

entries.zh: 貞觀初卒。
entries.en: She died early in the Zhenguan era.
entries.literal: In the early Zhenguan era she died.

entries.zh: 時後主怠於政事，百司啟奏，並因宦者蔡臨兒、李善度進請，後主倚隱囊，置張貴妃于膝上共決之。
entries.en: Neglecting government, he let memorials pass through eunuchs Cai Lin'er and Li Shandu while he lay back with Zhang Guifei on his knee deciding them.
entries.literal: At that time the last ruler was slack in government affairs; memorials from the hundred offices all entered through the eunuchs Cai Lin'er and Li Shandu; the last ruler leaned on a bolster with Honored Consort Zhang on his knees jointly deciding them.

entries.zh: 李、蔡所不能記者，貴妃並為疏條，無所遺脫。
entries.en: What the eunuchs forgot she summarized without omission.
entries.literal: What Li and Cai could not remember, the honored consort would set out in summary with nothing omitted.

entries.zh: 因參訪外事，人間有一言一事，貴妃必先知白之，由是益加寵異，冠絕後庭。
entries.en: She spied on the world outside as well; whatever was said in the streets she reported first, and her favor surpassed every rival.
entries.literal: Because she also investigated external affairs, whenever there was a word or affair among the people the honored consort would first know and report it; thereby favor increased still more, surpassing all the rear palace.

entries.zh: 而後宮之家，不遵法度，有絓於理者，但求恩于貴妃，貴妃則令李、蔡先啟其事，而后從容為言之。
entries.en: Kin of consorts who broke the law sought her favor; she had Li and Cai bring the case up, then spoke for them at leisure.
entries.literal: When families of the rear palace did not observe the law and were entangled in reason, they need only seek favor from the honored consort; the honored consort would have Li and Cai first raise the matter, then calmly speak of it for them.

entries.zh: 大臣有不從者，因而譖之，言無不聽。
entries.en: Ministers who resisted were slandered, and the emperor never refused her.
entries.literal: When great ministers did not comply, she thereupon slandered them, and her words were never not heeded.

entries.zh: 於是張、孔之權，熏灼四方，內外宗族，多被引用，大臣執政，亦從風而靡。
entries.en: The Zhang and Kong clans blazed with power east and west; ministers bent to their wind.
entries.literal: Thereupon the power of Zhang and Kong scorched the four quarters; inside and outside their clans were widely employed, and great ministers holding government also bent with the wind.

entries.zh: 閹宦便佞之徒，內外交結，轉相引進。
entries.en: Eunuchs and flatterers wove a web of mutual promotion.
entries.literal: Eunuchs and fawning men, inside and outside interlinked, introduced one another in turn.

entries.zh: 賄賂公行，賞罰無常，綱紀瞀亂矣。
entries.en: Bribes flowed freely, rewards and punishments lost all rule, and government collapsed into chaos.
entries.literal: Bribery ran openly; rewards and punishments had no constancy; the bonds of discipline were confused and chaotic.

entries.zh: 及隋軍克台城，貴妃與後主俱入井，隋軍出之，晉王廣命斬之於青溪中橋。
entries.en: When Sui took Taicheng she and the last ruler hid in a well; pulled out, Yang Guang had her beheaded at Zhongqiao on Qing Stream.
entries.literal: When the Sui army captured Taicheng, the honored consort and the last ruler both entered a well; the Sui army drew them out, and Prince of Jin Guang ordered her beheaded at the Zhongqiao on Qing Stream.

entries.zh: 梁文獻張皇后 武德郗皇后 武丁貴嬪 武阮修容 簡文王皇后 元徐妃 敬夏太后 敬王皇后 陳武宣章皇后 文沈皇后 廢帝王皇后 宣柳皇后 後主沈皇后
entries.en: This chapter treats Empress Zhang Wenxian of Liang, Empress Chi Wude of Liang, Honored Consort Ding, Lady of Cultivated Elegance Ruan, Empress Wang of Emperor Jianwen of Liang, Consort Xu of Emperor Yuan of Liang, Empress Dowager Xia the Reverent, Empress Wang the Reverent, Empress Zhang Xuan of Emperor Wu of Chen, Empress Shen of Emperor Wen of Chen, Empress Wang of the deposed emperor, Empress Liu Xuan of Emperor Xuan of Chen, and Empress Shen of the Chen last ruler.
entries.literal: Empress Zhang the Dedicated of Liang, Empress Chi the Martial Virtue of Liang, Honored Consort Ding the Martial of Liang, Lady of Cultivated Elegance Ruan the Martial of Liang, Empress Wang of Emperor Jianwen, Consort Xu of Emperor Yuan, Empress Dowager Xia the Reverent, Empress Wang the Reverent, Empress Zhang the Proclaiming Virtue of Chen Wu, Empress Shen of Emperor Wen, Empress Wang of the Deposed Emperor, Empress Liu the Proclaiming of Emperor Xuan, Empress Shen of the Last Ruler.

entries.zh: 五年，武帝伐慕容超，除中軍諮議參軍，與兗州刺史劉藩大破超軍，進圍廣固，屢獻規略。
entries.en: the fifth year of In, campaigning against Murong Chao, Jingxuan became an advising aide in the central army; with Liu Fan of Yanzhou he routed Chao and besieged Guanggu, offering strategy at every turn.
entries.literal: In the fifth year Emperor Wu attacked Murong Chao; Jingxuan was made advising aide in the central army and with Yanzhou Inspector Liu Fan greatly defeated Chao's army, advanced to besiege Guanggu, and repeatedly offered plans.

entries.zh: 盧循逼建鄴，敬宣分領鮮卑獸斑突騎，置陣甚整。
entries.en: When Lu Xun threatened Jiankang, Jingxuan led Xianbei cavalry with spotted mounts and drew up an impeccable line.
entries.literal: When Lu Xun pressed Jiankang Jingxuan separately commanded Xianbei beast-spotted shock cavalry and set the formation very orderly.

entries.zh: 循走，仍從南討，為左衛將軍。
entries.en: After Xun fled he continued south and was made General of the Left Guard.
entries.literal: Xun fled; he still followed the southern campaign and became General of the Left Guard.

entries.zh: 敬宣寬厚，善待士，多伎藝，弓馬音律，無事不善。
entries.en: Generous and gracious to men of talent, he mastered archery, horsemanship, music—there was scarcely an art he could not handle.
entries.literal: Jingxuan was generous, treated scholars well, and had many skills—in archery, horsemanship, and music there was nothing he did not excel at.

entries.zh: 尚書僕射謝混美才地，少所交納，與敬宣遇便盡禮。
entries.en: Xie Hun, vice director of the secretariat, seldom befriended anyone, yet with Jingxuan he was immediately cordial.
entries.literal: Secretary Deputy Director Xie Hun had fine talent and standing and rarely made new acquaintances; with Jingxuan he at once showed full courtesy.

entries.zh: 或問混：「卿未嘗輕交，而傾蓋劉壽，何也？」
entries.en: Someone asked Hun, "You rarely open up to people—why this instant bond with Liu Shou?"
entries.literal: Someone asked Hun, "You have never lightly befriended anyone, yet you treat Liu Shou with open arms—why?"

entries.zh: 混曰：「孔文舉禮太史子義，天下豈有非之邪。」
entries.en: Hun replied, "When Kong Wenju honored Taishi Ziyi, who in the realm criticized him?"
entries.literal: Hun said, "Kong Wenju honored Taishi Ziyi—did anyone under heaven fault him for it?"

entries.zh: 時帝西討劉毅，豫州刺史諸葛長人監太尉軍事，貽敬宣書曰：「盤龍狼戾專恣，自取夷滅。
entries.en: While the emperor marched west against Liu Yi, Zhuge Changren of Yuzhou, overseeing the grand marshal's armies, wrote Jingxuan: "Panlong's arrogance destroyed him.
entries.literal: When the Emperor campaigned west against Liu Yi, Yuzhou Inspector Zhuge Changren supervised the Grand Marshal's military affairs and wrote Jingxuan, "Panlong was wolfish, wilful, and brought ruin on himself.

entries.zh: 異端將盡，世路方夷，富貴之事，相與共之。」
entries.en: The rebel faction is almost finished and better days lie ahead—let us share the rewards together."
entries.literal: The strange branch is nearly gone and the world's path is clearing; matters of wealth and honor let us share them."

entries.zh: 敬宣報曰：「下官常懼福過災生，實思避盈居損。
entries.en: Jingxuan answered, "I have always feared that good luck invites disaster and sought to stay modest rather than grasp for more.
entries.literal: Jingxuan replied, "This humble officer has always feared fortune outrunning merit and truly wishes to avoid fullness and dwell in modesty.

entries.zh: 富貴之旨，非所敢當。」
entries.en: I dare not accept such an offer of rank and riches."
entries.literal: The intent of wealth and honor is not what I dare accept."

entries.zh: 便以長人書呈，帝謂王誕曰：「阿壽故為不負我。」
entries.en: He forwarded Changren's letter at once; the emperor told Wang Dan, "A Shou has not let me down."
entries.literal: He at once presented Changren's letter; the Emperor said to Wang Dan, "A Shou truly does not fail me."

entries.zh: 懷肅次弟懷敬，澀訥無才能。
entries.en: Huaisu's younger brother Huaijing was slow of speech and lacked ability.
entries.literal: Huaisu's next younger brother Huaijing was dull-spoken and without talent.

entries.zh: 初，武帝產而皇妣殂，孝皇帝貧薄，無由得乳人，議欲不舉，帝從母生懷敬，未期，乃斷懷敬乳而自養帝。
entries.en: When the future emperor was born his mother died; the household was too poor for a wet nurse and nearly abandoned the infant until his aunt, still nursing Huaijing, weaned her own son to feed him.
entries.literal: At first when the Emperor was born the imperial mother died; Emperor Xiao was poor and had no wet nurse; they debated not raising the child; the Emperor's maternal aunt bore Huaijing, not yet weaned, so she stopped Huaijing's milk and nursed the Emperor herself.

entries.zh: 帝以舊恩，懷敬累見寵授，至會稽太守。
entries.en: Out of gratitude for that old debt the emperor kept advancing Huaijing until he became administrator of Kuaiji.
entries.literal: Because of the old kindness the Emperor repeatedly favored Huaijing, reaching Administrator of Kuaiji.

entries.zh: 時以為速，武帝曰：「亡姨于我恩重，此何可忘？」
entries.en: Critics called the promotions too swift; the emperor said, "My aunt's kindness was profound—how could I forget it?"
entries.literal: People then thought it too fast; the Emperor said, "My late aunt's kindness to me was heavy—how could this be forgotten?"

entries.zh: 曆尚書，金紫光祿大夫。
entries.en: He went on to serve as minister of the masters of writing and as grand master with the gold seal and purple ribbon.
entries.literal: He served as Minister of the Masters of Writing and as Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.

entries.zh: 劉懷肅，彭城人，宋武帝從母兄也。
entries.en: Liu Huaisu of Pengcheng was the emperor's cousin on his mother's side.
entries.literal: Liu Huaisu was a man of Pengcheng, maternal elder cousin to Song Emperor Wu.

entries.zh: 家世貧窶，而躬耕好學。
entries.en: Though his family was poor he farmed himself and loved study.
entries.literal: The family had long been poor, yet he personally plowed and loved learning.

entries.zh: 仕晉為費令。
entries.en: Under Jin he served as magistrate of Fei county.
entries.literal: He served Jin as magistrate of Fei.

entries.zh: 及聞武帝起義，棄縣來奔。
entries.en: Hearing the emperor had risen in arms, he abandoned his post and rushed to join him.
entries.literal: When he heard the Emperor had raised the banner of revolt he abandoned his county and came to join.

entries.zh: 初，敬宣蜀還，劉毅欲以重法繩之。
entries.en: When Jingxuan came back from Shu, Liu Yi wanted him punished severely.
entries.literal: At first, when Jingxuan returned from Shu, Liu Yi wanted to punish him by heavy law.

entries.zh: 武帝既相任待，又何無忌謂不宜以私憾傷至公。
entries.en: The emperor already relied on him, and He Wuji argued that private spite must not override the public good.
entries.literal: The Emperor already trusted and employed him, and He Wuji said one should not let private resentment harm supreme fairness.

entries.zh: 毅雖止，猶謂武帝曰：「平生之舊，豈可孤信？
entries.en: Yi desisted, yet told the emperor, "A companion of long standing—can you trust him blindly?
entries.literal: Although Yi stopped, he still said to the Emperor, "An old friend of many years—can he be trusted alone?

entries.zh: 光武悔之于龐萌，曹公失之于孟卓。
entries.en: Emperor Guangwu regretted trusting Pang Meng; Cao Cao was betrayed by Zhang Miao.
entries.literal: Emperor Guangwu regretted Pang Meng; Cao Cao lost out with Meng Zhuo.

entries.zh: 宜深慎之。」
entries.en: You should be very careful."
entries.literal: You should be deeply cautious."

entries.zh: 毅出為荊州，謂敬宣曰：「欲屈卿為長史、南蠻，豈有見輔意乎？」
entries.en: Posted to Jing Province, Yi told Jingxuan, "I want you as chief aide and commander of the southern barbarians—will you serve under me?"
entries.literal: Yi went out to Jing Province and said to Jingxuan, "I wish to appoint you chief aide and southern barbarian commander—do you mean to assist me?"

entries.zh: 敬宣懼禍，以告武帝。
entries.en: Fearing a trap, Jingxuan reported this to the emperor.
entries.literal: Jingxuan feared disaster and told the Emperor.

entries.zh: 帝笑曰：「但令老兄平安，必無過慮。」
entries.en: The emperor laughed: "So long as your old friend keeps his head, you have nothing to fear."
entries.literal: The Emperor laughed and said, "Only let your old brother stay safe and you need not worry too much."

entries.zh: 後領冀州刺史。
entries.en: Later Jingxuan became inspector of Ji Province.
entries.literal: Later he held the post of Inspector of Ji Province.

entries.zh: 十一年，進號右軍將軍。
entries.en: the eleventh year of In he was promoted to General of the Right Army.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year he advanced in title to General of the Right Army.

entries.zh: 時晉宗室司馬道賜為敬宣參軍。
entries.en: Jin imperial clansman Sima Daosi then served on Jingxuan's staff.
entries.literal: At that time Jin clansman Sima Daosi was Jingxuan's staff officer.

entries.zh: 會武帝西征司馬休之，而道賜乃陰結同府辟閭道秀、左右小將王猛子等謀反。
entries.en: During the western campaign against Sima Xiuzhi, Daosi secretly conspired with staff officer Pilu Daoxiu and aides Wang Mengzi and others.
entries.literal: When the Emperor campaigned west against Sima Xiuzhi, Daosi secretly joined staff member Pilu Daoxiu and junior officers Wang Mengzi and others in plotting rebellion.

entries.zh: 道賜自號齊王，規據廣固，舉兵應休之。
entries.en: Daosi proclaimed himself Prince of Qi, aimed to seize Guanggu, and mustered forces for Xiuzhi.
entries.literal: Daosi styled himself Prince of Qi, planned to hold Guanggu, and raised troops to support Xiuzhi.

entries.zh: 猛子取敬宣刀殺敬宣，文武佐吏即討道賜、道秀、猛子斬之。
entries.en: Mengzi seized Jingxuan's sword and killed him; staff and officers immediately executed Daosi, Daoxiu, and Mengzi.
entries.literal: Mengzi took Jingxuan's sword and killed Jingxuan; civil and military aides at once punished Daosi, Daoxiu, and Mengzi and beheaded them.

entries.zh: 先是敬宣嘗夜與僚佐宴，空中有投一隻芒屩於坐，墜敬宣食盤上，長三尺五寸，已經人著，耳鼻間並欲壞，頃之而敗。
entries.en: Once at a night feast with his officers, a worn straw sandal three feet five inches long—reeking of a human wearer—dropped from nowhere into his dish; not long after he was killed.
entries.literal: Earlier Jingxuan had once feasted at night with his staff; from the air someone threw a single straw sandal onto the seat—it fell into Jingxuan's food tray, three chi five cun long, already worn by a person, nose and ears nearly ruined—and soon after he was destroyed.

entries.zh: 喪至，武帝臨哭甚哀。
entries.en: When the bier arrived the emperor mourned him in person, deeply grieved.
entries.literal: When the coffin arrived the Emperor came in person to mourn, very sorrowful.

entries.zh: 子光祖嗣。
entries.en: His son Guangzu succeeded him.
entries.literal: His son Guangzu inherited.

entries.zh: 宋受禪，國除。
entries.en: When Song took the throne the enfeoffment lapsed.
entries.literal: When Song received the abdication the fief was abolished.

entries.zh: 孫處字季高，會稽永興人也。
entries.en: Sun Chu, courtesy name Jigao, came from Yongxing in Kuaiji.
entries.literal: Sun Chu, styled Jigao, was a man of Yongxing in Kuaiji.

entries.zh: 籍注字，故以字行。
entries.en: The household register recorded his courtesy name, so he went by it.
entries.literal: Household register noted the style, so he was known by the style.

entries.zh: 少任氣，武帝征孫恩，季高樂從。
entries.en: Hot-blooded in youth, he eagerly joined the campaign against Sun En.
entries.literal: In youth he was spirited; when Emperor Wu campaigned against Sun En, Jigao gladly followed.

entries.zh: 及平建鄴，封新夷縣五等侯。
entries.en: After Jiankang fell he received the fifth-rank marquisate of Xinyi.
entries.literal: When Jiankang was pacified he was enfeoffed Fifth-rank Marquis of Xinyi.

entries.zh: 盧循之難，武帝謂季高曰：「此賊行破，非卿不能破其窟穴。」
entries.en: During Lu Xun's crisis the emperor told him, "This rebel is nearly finished—only you can destroy his lair."
entries.literal: In Lu Xun's crisis the Emperor said to Jigao, "This bandit is about to break—only you can smash his nest."

entries.zh: 即遣季高泛海襲番禺，拔之。
entries.en: He sent Jigao by sea against Panyu and captured it.
entries.literal: He at once sent Jigao by sea to strike Panyu and took it.

entries.zh: 循父嘏、長史孫建之、司馬虞尪夫等輕舟奔始興，即分遣振武將軍沈田子等討平嶺表諸郡。
entries.en: Xun's father Gu, chief clerk Sun Jianzhi, and marshal Yu Kuangfu fled by light boat to Shixing; Jigao sent Shen Tianzi to pacify the southern commanderies.
entries.literal: Xun's father Gu, Chief Clerk Sun Jianzhi, and Marshal Yu Kuangfu and others fled in light boats to Shixing; he then sent General Who Quells the Barbarians Shen Tianzi and others to pacify the Lingnan commanderies.

entries.zh: 循于左裏走還襲廣州，季高破走之。
entries.en: Xun doubled back from Zuoli to hit Guangzhou; Jigao beat him off.
entries.literal: Xun at Zuoli fled back to strike Guangzhou; Jigao defeated and drove him off.

entries.zh: 義熙七年，季高卒，追贈南海太守，封候官縣侯。
entries.en: In the seventh year of Yixi Jigao died; posthumously he was made administrator of Nanhai and marquis of Houguan.
entries.literal: In the seventh year of Yixi Jigao died; posthumously he was given Administrator of Nanhai and enfeoffed Marquis of Houguan.

entries.zh: 九年，武帝表贈交州刺史。
entries.en: the ninth year of In the emperor posthumously made him inspector of Jiao.
entries.literal: In the ninth year the Emperor memorialized giving him the post of Inspector of Jiao.

entries.zh: 及盧循逼都，孟昶等議奉天子過江，進廷議不可，面折昶等，武帝甚嘉之。
entries.en: When Lu Xun threatened the capital Meng Chang urged evacuating the emperor across the river; Jin argued against it in open court and won the emperor's praise.
entries.literal: When Lu Xun pressed the capital Meng Chang and others debated escorting the Son of Heaven across the river; Jin spoke in court that this could not be and openly refuted Chang and the rest; the Emperor greatly praised him.

entries.zh: 除鄱陽太守。
entries.en: He was appointed administrator of Poyang.
entries.literal: He was made Administrator of Poyang.

entries.zh: 後隨劉藩斬徐道覆。
entries.en: He later joined Liu Fan in killing Xu Daofu.
entries.literal: Later he followed Liu Fan in beheading Xu Daofu.

entries.zh: 義熙九年，以前後功，封望蔡縣男。
entries.en: In the ninth year of Yixi he received the barony of Wangcai for lifetime service.
entries.literal: In the ninth year of Yixi, for former and later merit, he was enfeoffed Baron of Wangcai.

entries.zh: 永初二年，累遷太子右衛率。
entries.en: In the second year of Yongchu he rose to right commandant of the heir's guard.
entries.literal: In the second year of Yongchu he rose repeatedly to Right Commandant of the Heir's Guard.

entries.zh: 卒，追論討司馬休之功，進爵為子。
entries.en: After death his campaign against Sima Xiuzhi was remembered and he was raised posthumously to viscount.
entries.literal: On death his merit against Sima Xiuzhi was recalled and he was advanced to viscount.

entries.zh: 傳國至曾孫，齊受禪，國除。
entries.en: The fief passed to a great-grandson; when Qi took the throne it lapsed.
entries.literal: The fief passed to a great-grandson; when Qi received the abdication the fief was abolished.

entries.zh: 孟懷玉，平昌安丘人也，世居京口。
entries.en: Meng Huaiyu of Anqiu in Pingchang came from a Jingkou family.
entries.literal: Meng Huaiyu was a man of Anqiu in Pingchang and for generations resided at Jingkou.

entries.zh: 宋武帝東伐孫恩，以為建武司馬。
entries.en: When the emperor marched east against Sun En he became marshal of the army that established might.
entries.literal: When Song Emperor Wu campaigned east against Sun En he was made marshal of the army that established might.

entries.zh: 豫義旗，從平京口，定建鄴，以功封鄱陽縣五等侯。
entries.en: He joined the revolt, helped take Jingkou and Jiankang, and received the fifth-rank marquisate of Poyang.
entries.literal: He joined the banner of righteousness, followed in pacifying Jingkou and settling Jiankang, and for merit was enfeoffed Fifth-rank Marquis of Poyang.

entries.zh: 盧循逼都，以戰功為中軍諮議參軍。
entries.en: When Lu Xun threatened the capital he became an advising aide in the central army for battlefield merit.
entries.literal: When Lu Xun pressed the capital, for battle merit he was made advising aide in the central army.

entries.zh: 循平，封陽豐縣男，位江州刺史、南中郎將。
entries.en: After Xun's defeat he became baron of Yangfeng, inspector of Jiangzhou, and General of the Southern Gentlemen.
entries.literal: When Xun was pacified he was enfeoffed Baron of Yangfeng, and held the posts of Inspector of Jiangzhou and General of the Southern Gentlemen.

entries.zh: 卒官。
entries.en: He died in office.
entries.literal: He died in office.

entries.zh: 無子，國除。
entries.en: He left no sons and the fief lapsed.
entries.literal: Without sons the fief was abolished.

entries.zh: 懷玉弟龍符，驍果有膽氣，早為武帝所知，以軍功封平昌縣五等子。
entries.en: Huaiyu's brother Longfu was daring and fierce; known early to the emperor, he earned the fifth-rank viscounty of Pingchang.
entries.literal: Huaiyu's younger brother Longfu was fierce and bold with courage; the Emperor knew him early and for military merit enfeoffed him Fifth-rank Viscount of Pingchang.

entries.zh: 從伐廣固，以車騎參軍加龍驤將軍、廣川太守。
entries.en: At Guanggu he served as chariot aide, Flying Dragon General, and administrator of Guangchuan.
entries.literal: Following the Guanggu campaign he was chariot-and-horse aide plus Flying Dragon General and Administrator of Guangchuan.

entries.zh: 乘勝追奔，被圍見害，追贈青州刺史，封臨沅縣男。
entries.en: Pursuing fleeing enemies he was surrounded and killed; posthumously he became inspector of Qingzhou and baron of Linjiang.
entries.literal: Pursuing the rout he was surrounded and killed; posthumously he was given Inspector of Qingzhou and enfeoffed Baron of Linjiang.

entries.zh: 藩轉參太尉大將軍相國軍事。
entries.en: Fan moved to staff duty under the grand marshal and chancellor.
entries.literal: Fan was transferred to staff officer on the Grand Marshal's and Chancellor's military affairs.

entries.zh: 宋武帝起兵，玄戰敗將出奔，藩扣馬曰：「今羽林射手猶有八百，皆是義故西人，一旦舍此，欲歸可復得乎？」
entries.en: When the emperor rose, Xuan prepared to flee; Fan grabbed his bridle: "You still have eight hundred western archers—leave now and you can never come back."
entries.literal: When Song Emperor Wu raised troops Xuan was defeated and about to flee; Fan seized his horse and said, "The palace archers still number eight hundred—all old followers from the west; once you abandon this, can you ever return?"

entries.zh: 玄直以鞭指天而已。
entries.en: Xuan only gestured skyward with his whip.
entries.literal: Xuan merely pointed heavenward with his whip.

entries.zh: 於是奔散相失，追及玄於蕪湖。
entries.en: They scattered in chaos; Fan caught Xuan again at Wuhu.
entries.literal: Thereupon they scattered and lost one another; he caught up with Xuan at Wuhu.

entries.zh: 玄見藩喜謂張須無曰：「卿州故為多士，今復見王修。」
entries.en: Seeing Fan, Xuan told Zhang Xu Wu, "Your region breeds real men—here is Wang Xiu again."
entries.literal: Xuan saw Fan and said joyfully to Zhang Xu Wu, "Your province truly breeds many scholars—now I see Wang Xiu again."

entries.zh: 桑落之敗，藩艦被燒，並鎧入水，潛行三十許步，方得登岸。
entries.en: At Sangluo his ship burned; armored, he swam thirty paces underwater before reaching shore.
entries.literal: At the defeat of Sangluo Fan's ship was burned; wearing armor he entered the water and stole thirty paces before he could climb ashore.

entries.zh: 乃還家。
entries.en: He went home.
entries.literal: He then returned home.

entries.zh: 武帝素聞藩直言于殷氏，又為玄盡節，召參鎮軍軍事。
entries.en: The emperor, knowing Fan had warned Yin and served Xuan faithfully, summoned him to the pacifying army staff.
entries.literal: The Emperor had long heard Fan's blunt words to the Yin clan and his full loyalty to Xuan; he summoned him to staff the army that pacifies the army.

entries.zh: 從征慕容超，超軍屯聚臨朐。
entries.en: Campaigning against Murong Chao, he found Chao's army massed at Linqu.
entries.literal: Following the campaign against Murong Chao, Chao's army gathered at Linqu.

entries.zh: 藩言于武帝曰：「賊屯軍城外，留守必寡，今往取其城而斬其旗幟，此韓信所以克趙也。」
entries.en: Fan told the emperor, "They camp outside—the city is empty; seize it and strike down their flags, as Han Xin did at Zhao."
entries.literal: Fan said to the Emperor, "The bandits camp outside the city—the garrison must be thin; go now, take the city and cut down their banners—this is how Han Xin conquered Zhao."

entries.zh: 帝乃遣檀韶與藩潛往，即克其城。
entries.en: The emperor sent Tan Shao and Fan by stealth and they captured it at once.
entries.literal: The Emperor then sent Tan Shao and Fan secretly; they at once took the city.

entries.zh: 賊見城陷，一時奔走，還保廣固。
entries.en: Seeing the city lost, the enemy fled back to Guanggu.
entries.literal: The bandits saw the city fall and at once fled, returning to hold Guanggu.

entries.zh: 圍之，將拔之夜，忽有鳥大如鵝，蒼黑色，飛入帝帳裏，眾以為不祥。
entries.en: On the eve of victory a goose-sized dark bird flew into the imperial tent; men took it for a bad sign.
entries.literal: Besieging it, on the night it was about to fall suddenly a bird large as a goose, dark blue-black, flew into the Emperor's tent; the crowd thought it ill-omened.

entries.zh: 藩賀曰：「蒼黑者，胡虜色。
entries.en: Fan declared, "Dark blue is the barbarians' color.
entries.literal: Fan congratulated him, "Dark blue is the color of the barbarians.

entries.zh: 胡虜歸我，大吉之祥。」
entries.en: Their surrender is a great omen."
entries.literal: Barbarians returning to us is a great auspice."

entries.zh: 明旦攻城，陷之。
entries.en: At dawn they stormed the city and took it.
entries.literal: At dawn he attacked the city and took it.

entries.zh: 從討盧循于左裏，頻戰有功，封吳平縣五等子。
entries.en: Fighting Lu Xun at Zuoli he won repeated honors and received the fifth-rank viscounty of Wuping.
entries.literal: Following the punitive action against Lu Xun at Zuoli he repeatedly won merit and was enfeoffed Fifth-rank Viscount of Wuping.

entries.zh: 尋除鄱陽太守，從伐劉毅。
entries.en: He soon became administrator of Poyang and marched against Liu Yi.
entries.literal: Soon he was made Administrator of Poyang and followed the campaign against Liu Yi.

entries.zh: 初，毅當之荊州，表求東道還建鄴辭墓。
entries.en: When Yi left for Jing Province he asked to swing by Jiankang to mourn at his family tombs.
entries.literal: At first when Yi was going to Jing Province he memorialized asking to travel the eastern route back to Jiankang to visit his ancestors' tombs.

entries.zh: 去都數十里，不過拜闕。
entries.en: He stopped tens of li from court without paying homage at the palace.
entries.literal: Several tens of li from the capital he did not pass to bow at the palace.

entries.zh: 帝出倪塘會毅，藩請殺之，乃謂帝曰：「公謂劉衛軍為公下乎？」
entries.en: The emperor met Yi at Nitang; Fan urged killing him: "Do you think Defender Liu serves under you?"
entries.literal: The Emperor went out to Nitang to meet Yi; Fan asked to kill him and said to the Emperor, "Do you think Defender Liu serves under you?"

entries.zh: 帝曰：「卿謂何如？」
entries.en: The emperor asked, "What do you think?"
entries.literal: The Emperor said, "What do you think?"

entries.zh: 對曰：「夫豁達大度，功高天下，連百萬之眾，允天人之望，毅固以此服公。
entries.en: Fan answered, "Your breadth and achievement command the realm—Yi submits to that.
entries.literal: He replied, "Broad-minded and magnanimous, merit high under heaven, commanding millions, fulfilling heaven and men's hopes—Yi for this submits to you.

entries.zh: 至於涉獵記傳，一詠一談，自許以雄豪，加以誇伐，搢紳白麵之士，輻湊而歸，此毅不肯為公下也。」
entries.en: But his salons, his poetry, his swagger—scholars flock to him. That is Yi refusing to serve under you."
entries.literal: As for browsing records and histories, reciting and conversing, styling himself a hero and adding boast—gentry and pale-faced scholars flock to him; this is Yi refusing to serve under you."

entries.zh: 帝曰：「吾與毅俱有克復功，其過未彰，不可自相圖。」
entries.en: The emperor said, "We both restored the dynasty; his disloyalty is not yet proven—we cannot turn on each other."
entries.literal: The Emperor said, "Yi and I both have merit in restoration; his fault is not yet clear—we cannot plot against each other."

entries.zh: 至是謂藩曰：「昔從卿倪塘之謀，無今舉也。」
entries.en: Now he told Fan, "If I had listened at Nitang I would not need this war."
entries.literal: Now he said to Fan, "Had I followed your Nitang counsel there would be no present campaign."

entries.zh: 又從征司馬休之，復為參軍。
entries.en: He again campaigned against Sima Xiuzhi as a staff officer.
entries.literal: He again followed the campaign against Sima Xiuzhi and again served as staff officer.

entries.zh: 徐逵之敗沒，帝怒，即日於馬頭岸度江。
entries.en: After Xu Daizhi's defeat the furious emperor crossed the Yangzi that same day at Matou.
entries.literal: When Xu Daizhi was defeated and lost the Emperor was angry and that same day crossed the Yangzi at Matou bank.

entries.zh: 江津岸壁立數丈，休之臨岸置陣，無由可登。
entries.en: The bank rose sheer for yards; Xiuzhi lined the top and offered no foothold.
entries.literal: The river crossing's bank was a cliff several zhang; Xiuzhi set battle lines on the bank with no way to climb.

entries.zh: 帝呼藩令上，藩有疑色。
entries.en: The emperor ordered Fan up; Fan hesitated.
entries.literal: The Emperor called Fan to ascend; Fan showed hesitation.

entries.zh: 帝怒，命左右錄來，欲斬之。
entries.en: Enraged, the emperor had him seized for execution.
entries.literal: The Emperor in anger ordered attendants to seize him and was about to behead him.

entries.zh: 藩不受命，顧曰：「寧前死耳。」
entries.en: Fan refused and said, "I would rather die advancing."
entries.literal: Fan would not obey the order and looked back, saying, "Better die going forward."

entries.zh: 以刀頭穿岸，劣容腳指徑上，隨之者稍多。
entries.en: He dug toeholds with his sword tip and climbed; others followed.
entries.literal: He pierced the bank with the sword-point, barely fitting his toes, and went up; those who followed gradually increased.

entries.zh: 及登，殊死戰，敗之。
entries.en: At the top they fought desperately and routed Xiuzhi.
entries.literal: Once atop they fought to the death and defeated the enemy.

entries.zh: 從伐關中，參太尉軍事，統別軍至河東。
entries.en: On the Guanzhong expedition he led a detached force to Hedong under the grand marshal.
entries.literal: Following the Guanzhong expedition he was staff officer on the Grand Marshal's military affairs, commanding a separate army to Hedong.

entries.zh: 暴風漂輜重艦度北岸，魏軍牽得此艦。
entries.en: A storm blew a supply ship to the north bank where Wei seized it.
entries.literal: A gale blew supply ships across to the north bank; Wei troops towed away this ship.

entries.zh: 藩氣憤，率左右十二人乘小船徑往。
entries.en: Furious, Fan took twelve men in a skiff straight after it.
entries.literal: Fan in fury led twelve men in a small boat straight there.

entries.zh: 魏騎五六百，見藩來並笑之。
entries.en: Five or six hundred Wei cavalry saw him and laughed.
entries.literal: Five or six hundred Wei horsemen saw Fan coming and all laughed at him.

entries.zh: 藩素善射，登岸射之，應弦而倒者十許人。
entries.en: A fine archer, he shot from shore and dropped a dozen at once.
entries.literal: Fan had long been skilled at archery; ashore he shot them and over ten fell at the twang of the string.

entries.zh: 魏軍皆退，悉收所失而反。
entries.en: The Wei riders fled and he recovered everything.
entries.literal: The Wei army all retreated and he fully recovered what was lost and returned.

entries.zh: 又遣藩及朱超石等追魏軍於半城，魏騎數萬合圍，藩及超石不盈五千，力戰，大破之。
entries.en: He sent Fan and Zhu Chao shi after Wei at Bancheng; though surrounded by tens of thousands with fewer than five thousand men they smashed the enemy.
entries.literal: He again sent Fan and Zhu Chao shi and others to pursue Wei forces at Bancheng; tens of thousands of Wei horsemen surrounded them; Fan and Chao shi had fewer than five thousand and fought fiercely, greatly defeating them.

entries.zh: 武帝還彭城，參相國軍事。
entries.en: Back at Pengcheng he joined the chancellor's staff.
entries.literal: When the Emperor returned to Pengcheng he served on the Chancellor's military staff.

entries.zh: 論平司馬休之及廣固功，封陽山縣男。
entries.en: For Xiuzhi and Guanggu he received the barony of Yangshan.
entries.literal: Recalling merit in pacifying Sima Xiuzhi and at Guanggu he was enfeoffed Baron of Yangshan.

entries.zh: 元嘉中，位太子左衛率。
entries.en: In Yuanjia he became left commandant of the heir's guard.
entries.literal: In Yuanjia he reached Left Commandant of the Heir's Guard.

entries.zh: 卒，諡曰壯侯。
entries.en: His posthumous title was Marquis Zhuang.
entries.literal: On death posthumous title Marquis Zhuang.

entries.zh: 子隆世嗣。
entries.en: Longshi succeeded him.
entries.literal: Longshi succeeded.

entries.zh: 列傳第七
entries.en: the seventh year of Biographies
entries.literal: Biographies 7

entries.zh: 介字茂鏡，少穎悟，有器識。
entries.en: Jie, courtesy name Maojing, was quick and perceptive from youth with capacity and discernment.
entries.literal: Jie, styled Maojing, was quick and perceptive from youth with capacity and discernment.

entries.zh: 梁大同中，武陵王紀為揚州刺史，以介為府長史，在職以清白稱。
entries.en: In Liang's Datong era Prince Wu Ling Ji governed Yang Province and made Jie chief administrator of his household; in office he was famed for integrity.
entries.literal: In Liang's Datong era Prince Wu Ling Ji governed Yang Province and made Jie chief administrator of his household; in office he was famed for integrity.

entries.zh: 武帝謂何敬容曰：「蕭介甚貧，可處以一郡。」
entries.en: Emperor Wu told He Jingrong, "Xiao Jie is very poor — he may be given a commandery."
entries.literal: Emperor Wu said to He Jingrong, "Xiao Jie is very poor — he may be given a commandery."

entries.zh: 復曰：「始興郡頻無良守，可以介為之。」
entries.en: He also said, "Shixing has often lacked good administrators — Jie may go there."
entries.literal: He also said, "Shixing Commandery has often lacked good administrators — Jie may be sent there."

entries.zh: 由是出為始興太守。
entries.en: For this he went out as administrator of Shixing.
entries.literal: For this he went out as Administrator of Shixing.

entries.zh: 及至，甚著威德。
entries.en: On reaching his post he showed great authority and virtue.
entries.literal: On reaching his post he showed great authority and virtue.

entries.zh: 禮，天子七廟，三昭三穆與太祖而七。
entries.en: Ritual: the Son of Heaven has seven temples — three zhao three mu with the Grand Ancestor making seven.
entries.literal: Ritual: the Son of Heaven has seven temples — three zhao three mu with the Grand Ancestor making seven.

entries.zh: 自考廟以至祖考五廟，皆月祭之。
entries.en: From the temple of self-examination to the five temples of ancestors and fathers, all receive monthly sacrifice.
entries.literal: From the temple of self-examination to the five temples of ancestors and fathers, all receive monthly sacrifice.

entries.zh: 遠廟為祧，有二祧，享嘗乃止。
entries.en: The distant temple becomes tiao; there are two tiao; offering and tasting then cease.
entries.literal: The distant temple becomes tiao; there are two tiao; offering and tasting then cease.

entries.zh: 去祧為壇，去壇為墠，有禱然後祭之，此宗廟之次、親疏之序也。
entries.en: Beyond tiao is the altar; beyond the altar is the open ground; when there is prayer then sacrifice is made — this is the order of ancestral temples and the sequence of near and far.
entries.literal: Beyond tiao is the altar; beyond the altar is the open ground; when there is prayer then sacrifice is made — this is the order of ancestral temples and the sequence of near and far.

entries.zh: 鄭玄以為祧者文王武王之廟，王肅以為五世六世之祖。
entries.en: Zheng Xuan held that tiao were the temples of King Wen and King Wu; Wang Su held they were ancestors of the fifth and sixth generations.
entries.literal: Zheng Xuan held that tiao were the temples of King Wen and King Wu; Wang Su held they were ancestors of the fifth and sixth generations.

entries.zh: 尋去祧之言，則祧非文、武之廟矣。
entries.en: Examining the words "beyond tiao," then tiao are not the temples of Wen and Wu.
entries.literal: Examining the words "beyond tiao," then tiao are not the temples of Wen and Wu.

entries.zh: 文、武，周之祖宗，何雲去祧為壇乎？
entries.en: Wen and Wu were Zhou's ancestors — how can one speak of beyond tiao as altar?
entries.literal: Wen and Wu were Zhou's ancestors — how can one speak of beyond tiao as altar?

entries.zh: 明遠廟為祧者，無服之祖也。
entries.en: Clearly the distant temple that becomes tiao is the ancestor beyond mourning.
entries.literal: Clearly the distant temple that becomes tiao is the ancestor beyond mourning.

entries.zh: 又遠廟則有享嘗之降，去祧則有壇墠之殊，明世遠者其義彌疏也。
entries.en: Again for distant temples there is the descent of offering and tasting; beyond tiao there is the difference of altar and open ground — clearly the more distant the generation the more sparse the meaning.
entries.literal: Again for distant temples there is the descent of offering and tasting; beyond tiao there is the difference of altar and open ground — clearly the more distant the generation the more sparse the meaning.

entries.zh: 若祧是文、武之廟，宜同月祭于太祖，雖推後稷以配天，由功德之所始，非尊崇之義每有差降也。
entries.en: If tiao were the temples of Wen and Wu they should like the Grand Ancestor receive monthly sacrifice; though Houji is elevated to match Heaven, that is from the beginning of merit, not that the meaning of honor has difference and descent each time.
entries.literal: If tiao were the temples of Wen and Wu they should like the Grand Ancestor receive monthly sacrifice; though Houji is elevated to match Heaven, that is from the beginning of merit, not that the meaning of honor has difference and descent each time.

entries.zh: 又禮有以多為貴者，故傳稱「德厚者流光，德薄者流卑」。
entries.en: Again ritual has what values the many; therefore tradition says, "Thick virtue shines far; thin virtue flows low."
entries.literal: Again ritual has what values the many; therefore tradition says, "Thick virtue shines far; thin virtue flows low."

entries.zh: 又言自上以下降殺以兩，禮也。
entries.en: Again it says from above to below reduction by twos — that is ritual.
entries.literal: Again it says from above to below reduction by twos — that is ritual.

entries.zh: 此則尊卑等級之典，上下殊異之文。
entries.en: This is the canon of honor and lowliness, the text of difference above and below.
entries.literal: This is the canon of honor and lowliness, the text of difference above and below.

entries.zh: 而雲天子諸侯俱祭五廟，何哉？
entries.en: Yet it says Son of Heaven and feudal lords alike sacrifice at five temples — why?
entries.literal: Yet it says Son of Heaven and feudal lords alike sacrifice at five temples — why?

entries.zh: 又王祭嫡殤，下及來孫。
entries.en: Again the king sacrifices for legitimate early-dead sons, extending down to coming generations.
entries.literal: Again the king sacrifices for legitimate early-dead sons, extending down to coming generations.

entries.zh: 而上祀之禮不過高祖。
entries.en: Yet sacrifice by superiors does not exceed the High Ancestor.
entries.literal: Yet sacrifice by superiors does not exceed the High Ancestor.

entries.zh: 推隆恩於下流，替誠敬於尊廟，亦非聖人制禮之意也。
entries.en: Pushing honor down the stream while replacing sincere reverence at the honored temple — this too is not the sage's intent in making ritual.
entries.literal: Pushing honor down the stream while replacing sincere reverence at the honored temple — this too is not the sage's intent in making ritual.

entries.zh: 是以泰始建廟，從王氏議，以禮父為士，子為天子諸侯，祭以天子諸侯，其屍服以士服。
entries.en: Therefore when Taishi established the temple they followed the Wang clan's argument: by ritual the father is a knight and the son Son of Heaven or feudal lord, yet sacrifice uses Son of Heaven and feudal lord while the corpse's garment uses knight's garment.
entries.literal: Therefore when Taishi established the temple they followed the Wang clan's argument: by ritual the father is a knight and the son Son of Heaven or feudal lord, yet sacrifice uses Son of Heaven and feudal lord while the corpse's garment uses knight's garment.

entries.zh: 故上及征西，以備六世之數。
entries.en: Thus upstream to Pacifying the West, to complete the number of six generations.
entries.literal: Thus upstream to Pacifying the West, to complete the number of six generations.

entries.zh: 宣皇雖為太祖，尚在子孫之位，至於殷祭之日，未申東向之禮，所謂子雖齊聖，不先父食者矣。
entries.en: Emperor Xuan though Grand Ancestor was still in the place of descendants; on the day of the great offering he had not yet received the east-facing rite — what is called though the son equals sainthood he does not eat before the father.
entries.literal: Emperor Xuan though Grand Ancestor was still in the place of descendants; on the day of the great offering he had not yet received the east-facing rite — what is called though the son equals sainthood he does not eat before the father.

entries.zh: 今京兆以上既遷，太祖始得居正，議者以昭穆未足，欲屈太祖于卑坐，臣以為非禮典之旨也。
entries.en: Now that Jingzhao and above have moved, the Grand Ancestor at last occupies the correct place; debaters, because zhao and mu are not full, wish to bend the Grand Ancestor to the low seat — your servant holds this is not the intent of ritual canon.
entries.literal: Now that Jingzhao and above have moved, the Grand Ancestor at last occupies the correct place; debaters, because zhao and mu are not full, wish to bend the Grand Ancestor to the low seat — your servant holds this is not the intent of ritual canon.

entries.zh: 所謂與太祖而七，自是昭穆既足，太廟在六世之外，非為須滿七廟乃得居太祖也。
entries.en: What is called "with the Grand Ancestor making seven" is itself that zhao and mu are already full and the Grand Temple lies outside the six generations — not that one must fill seven temples before the Grand Ancestor may occupy that place.
entries.literal: What is called "with the Grand Ancestor making seven" is itself that zhao and mu are already full and the Grand Temple lies outside the six generations — not that one must fill seven temples before the Grand Ancestor may occupy that place.

entries.zh: 議者又以四府君神主，宜永同于殷祫。
entries.en: Debaters also held the spirit tablets of the four lords should forever share the great offering like the yin sacrifice.
entries.literal: Debaters also held the spirit tablets of the four lords should forever share the great offering like the yin sacrifice.

entries.zh: 臣又以為不然。
entries.en: Your servant again holds this is not so.
entries.literal: Your servant again holds this is not so.

entries.zh: 傳所謂毀廟之主，陳乎太祖，謂太祖以下先君之主也。
entries.en: Tradition speaks of the destroyed temple's tablet displayed before the Grand Ancestor — meaning the tablets of former lords below the Grand Ancestor.
entries.literal: Tradition speaks of the destroyed temple's tablet displayed before the Grand Ancestor — meaning the tablets of former lords below the Grand Ancestor.

entries.zh: 故白虎通云：「禘祫祭遷廟者，以其繼君之體，持其統而不絕也。」
entries.en: Therefore the Baihu Tong says, "The di and ha sacrifices move destroyed temples because they continue the lord's body and hold the line without breaking."
entries.literal: Therefore the Baihu Tong says, "The di and ha sacrifices move destroyed temples because they continue the lord's body and hold the line without breaking."

entries.zh: 豈如四府君在太祖之前乎，非繼統之主，無靈命之瑞，非王業之基。
entries.en: How could the four lords be before the Grand Ancestor? They are not lords who continue the line, have no auspicious mandate, are not the foundation of royal enterprise.
entries.literal: How could the four lords be before the Grand Ancestor? They are not lords who continue the line, have no auspicious mandate, are not the foundation of royal enterprise.

entries.zh: 昔以世近而及，今則情禮已遠，而當長饗殷祫，永虛太祖之位，求之禮籍。
entries.en: Formerly because the generation was near they were included; now feeling and ritual are already far — yet they should long enjoy the great yin offering and forever leave the Grand Ancestor's place empty; seeking this in ritual texts —
entries.literal: Formerly because the generation was near they were included; now feeling and ritual are already far — yet they should long enjoy the great yin offering and forever leave the Grand Ancestor's place empty; seeking this in ritual texts —

entries.zh: 未見其可。
entries.en: one does not see that it may be done.
entries.literal: one does not see that it may be done.

entries.zh: 昔永和之初，大議斯禮，于時虞喜、范宣並以洪儒碩學，咸謂四府君神主無緣永存於百世。
entries.en: Formerly at the beginning of Yonghe there was great debate on this ritual; at that time Yu Xi and Fan Xuan, both great Confucian scholars, all held the four lords' spirit tablets had no reason to remain forever for a hundred generations.
entries.literal: Formerly at the beginning of Yonghe there was great debate on this ritual; at that time Yu Xi and Fan Xuan, both great Confucian scholars, all held the four lords' spirit tablets had no reason to remain forever for a hundred generations.

entries.zh: 或欲瘞之兩階，或欲藏之石室，或欲為之改築，雖所執小異，而大歸是同。
entries.en: Some wished to bury them at the two steps, some to store them in a stone chamber, some to rebuild for them — though what they held differed in small ways the great direction was the same.
entries.literal: Some wished to bury them at the two steps, some to store them in a stone chamber, some to rebuild for them — though what they held differed in small ways the great direction was the same.

entries.zh: 若宣皇既居群廟之上，而四主禘祫不已，則大晉殷祭長無太祖之位矣。
entries.en: If Emperor Xuan already stands above the group of temples and the four lords' di and ha offerings never cease, then Great Jin's great yin sacrifice would forever lack the Grand Ancestor's place.
entries.literal: If Emperor Xuan already stands above the group of temples and the four lords' di and ha offerings never cease, then Great Jin's great yin sacrifice would forever lack the Grand Ancestor's place.

entries.zh: 夫理貴有中，不必過厚，禮與世遷，豈可順而不斷？
entries.en: Principle values the mean — one need not exceed in thickness; ritual moves with the age — how can one follow without deciding?
entries.literal: Principle values the mean — one need not exceed in thickness; ritual moves with the age — how can one follow without deciding?

entries.zh: 故臣子之情雖篤，而靈、厲之諡彌彰，追遠之懷雖切，而遷毀之禮為用。
entries.en: Thus though ministers' and sons' feeling is deep, the posthumous titles of Ling and Li grow ever clearer; though longing for the distant is keen, the ritual of transfer and destruction is what applies.
entries.literal: Thus though ministers' and sons' feeling is deep, the posthumous titles of Ling and Li grow ever clearer; though longing for the distant is keen, the ritual of transfer and destruction is what applies.

entries.zh: 豈不有心于加厚，顧禮制不可踰耳。
entries.en: Is it not that the heart wishes to add thickness but ritual system cannot be overstepped?
entries.literal: Is it not that the heart wishes to add thickness but ritual system cannot be overstepped?

entries.zh: 石室則藏於廟北，改築則未知所處。
entries.en: Stone chamber means storing north of the temple; rebuilding means not knowing where to place them.
entries.literal: Stone chamber means storing north of the temple; rebuilding means not knowing where to place them.

entries.zh: 虞主所以依神，神移則有瘞埋之禮。
entries.en: The yu tablet exists to rely on the spirit; when the spirit moves there is the ritual of burial.
entries.literal: The yu tablet exists to rely on the spirit; when the spirit moves there is the ritual of burial.

entries.zh: 四主若饗祀宜廢，亦神之所不依也。
entries.en: If the four lords' offering sacrifice should be abolished, that too is what the spirit does not rely on.
entries.literal: If the four lords' offering sacrifice should be abolished, that too is what the spirit does not rely on.

entries.zh: 准傍事例，宜同虞主之瘞埋。
entries.en: Following parallel cases one should like the yu tablet's burial.
entries.literal: Following parallel cases one should like the yu tablet's burial.

entries.zh: 然經典難詳，群言錯繆，非臣淺識所能折中。
entries.en: Yet the classics are hard to detail and many words err — this is not what your servant's shallow understanding can reconcile.
entries.literal: Yet the classics are hard to detail and many words err — this is not what your servant's shallow understanding can reconcile.

entries.zh: 時學者多從燾議，竟未施行。
entries.en: At that time most scholars followed Dao's argument; in the end it was not implemented.
entries.literal: At that time most scholars followed Dao's argument; in the end it was not implemented.

entries.zh: 趙倫之蕭思話臧燾
entries.en: Zhao Lunzhi, Xiao Sihua, and Zang Dao
entries.literal: Zhao Lunzhi, Xiao Sihua, Zang Dao

entries.zh: 僧達孫 融
entries.en: Sengda's grandson Rong
entries.literal: Sengda's grandson Rong

entries.zh: 融字元長，少而神明警慧。
entries.en: Rong, courtesy name Yuanchang, was bright and precocious from childhood.
entries.literal: Rong, styled Yuanchang, from youth was bright and keenly intelligent.

entries.zh: 母臨川太守謝惠宣女，性敦敏，教融書學。
entries.en: His mother was a daughter of Xie Huixuan, Administrator of Linchuan; earnest and quick herself, she taught Rong reading and scholarship.
entries.literal: His mother was daughter of Xie Huixuan, Administrator of Linchuan; she was earnest and quick, and taught Rong letters and learning.

entries.zh: 博涉有文才，從叔儉謂人曰：「此兒至四十，名位自然及祖。」
entries.en: Well read and gifted in letters, his father's younger cousin Jian told others: "At forty this boy will naturally match his grandfather in rank and fame."
entries.literal: Broadly read and possessed of literary talent, his father's younger cousin Jian told others: "This boy at forty will naturally reach his grandfather's name and rank."

entries.zh: 舉秀才，累遷太子舍人。
entries.en: Recommended as Presented Scholar, he rose to Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: He was recommended as Presented Scholar and was promoted in succession to Attendant of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 以父宦不通，弱年便欲紹興家業，啟齊武帝求自試，遷秘書丞。
entries.en: His father's career had stalled; while still young Rong sought to revive the family fortunes, petitioned Emperor Wu of Qi for a trial appointment, and was made Secretary.
entries.literal: Because his father's official career had not prospered, in weak years he wished to revive the family estate; he memorialized Emperor Wu of Qi asking to prove himself and was transferred to Secretary.

entries.zh: 從叔儉初有儀同之授，贈儉詩及書，儉甚奇之，笑謂人曰：「穰侯印詎便可解。」
entries.en: When his cousin Jian first received appointment as Equal to the Three Excellencies, Rong sent him a poem and letter; Jian was astonished and smiled: "So the seal of Ranghou can be handed over already?"
entries.literal: When his father's younger cousin Jian first received appointment as Equal to the Three Excellencies, Rong sent him a poem and letter; Jian marveled greatly and smiling told others: "Can the seal of Ranghou really be taken off so soon?"

entries.zh: 曆丹陽丞，中書郎。
entries.en: He served as Assistant Magistrate of Danyang and Gentleman of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: He served as Assistant Magistrate of Danyang and Gentleman of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 永明末，武帝欲北侵，使毛惠秀畫漢武北伐圖，融因此上疏，開張北侵之議。
entries.en: At the end of Yongming, when Emperor Wu planned a northern campaign and had Mao Huixiu paint Han Wudi's northern expedition, Rong submitted a memorial urging invasion.
entries.literal: At the end of the Yongming era Emperor Wu wished to invade the north and had Mao Huixiu paint Emperor Wu of Han's northern campaign; Rong therefore submitted a memorial opening discussion of northern invasion.

entries.zh: 圖成，上置琅邪城射堂壁上，遊幸輒觀焉。
entries.en: When the painting was finished the emperor hung it in the archery hall at Langya city and viewed it on every visit.
entries.literal: When the painting was finished the emperor placed it on the wall of the archery hall at Langya city and viewed it whenever he toured.

entries.zh: 九年，芳林園禊宴，使融為曲水詩序，當時稱之。
entries.en: In the ninth year, at the Fanglin Garden spring purification, he had Rong write the preface to the winding-water poems; contemporaries praised it.
entries.literal: In the ninth year, at the Fanglin Garden spring purification feast, he had Rong compose the preface to the winding-water poems; men of the time praised it.

entries.zh: 上以融才辯，使兼主客，接魏使房景高、宋弁。
entries.en: The emperor, noting Rong's eloquence, also made him Chief of Guests to receive the Wei envoys Fang Jinggao and Song Bian.
entries.literal: The emperor, because Rong was talented and eloquent, had him additionally serve as Chief of Guests and receive the Wei envoys Fang Jinggao and Song Bian.

entries.zh: 弁見融年少，問：「主客年幾？」
entries.en: Bian saw that Rong was young and asked: "How old is the Chief of Guests?"
entries.literal: Bian saw Rong was young and asked: "How old is the Chief of Guests?"

entries.zh: 融曰：「五十之年，久踰其半。」
entries.en: Rong replied: "Fifty years—well past the halfway mark."
entries.literal: Rong said: "Of fifty years, long past the half."

entries.zh: 景高又云：「在北聞主客曲水詩序勝延年，實願一見。」
entries.en: Jinggao added: "In the north I heard your winding-water preface surpasses Yannian's—I long to see it."
entries.literal: Jinggao also said: "In the north I heard the Chief of Guests' preface to the winding-water poems surpasses Yannian; I truly wish to see it."

entries.zh: 融乃示之。
entries.en: Rong showed it to them.
entries.literal: Rong then showed it.

entries.zh: 後日，宋弁於瑤池堂謂融曰：「昔觀相如封禪，以知漢武之德，今覽王生詩序，用見齊主之盛。」
entries.en: Later at Yaochi Hall Song Bian told Rong: "Reading Sima Xiangru's feng-shan text revealed Han Wudi's virtue; reading Master Wang's preface reveals our lord's splendor."
entries.literal: Later, Song Bian at Yaochi Hall said to Rong: "Once reading Sima Xiangru's feng and shan text, one knew the virtue of Han Wu; now reading Master Wang's poem preface, one sees the splendor of the Qi lord."

entries.zh: 融曰：「皇家盛明，豈直比蹤漢武，更慚鄙制，無以遠匹相如。」
entries.en: Rong replied: "Our dynasty's brilliance far exceeds Han Wudi's; my humble piece cannot compare with Xiangru."
entries.literal: Rong said: "Our house's brilliance—how could it merely follow Han Wu? I am all the more ashamed of my crude composition; it cannot remotely match Xiangru."

entries.zh: 上以魏所送馬不稱，使融問之曰：「秦西冀北，實多駿驥，而魏之良馬，乃駑不若，將旦旦信誓，有時而爽，駉駉之牧，遂不能嗣？」
entries.en: Because the horses Wei sent were poor, the emperor had Rong ask: "Qin west and Ji north abound in fine steeds, yet Wei's gifts are nags—has sworn faith broken, and the pastures failed?"
