entries.literal: The emperor, because the horses Wei sent were unworthy, had Rong ask: "West of Qin and north of Ji truly have many fine steeds, yet Wei's good horses are inferior nags—is the daily sworn faith sometimes broken, and the pastures of spirited horses no longer bred?"

entries.zh: 宋弁曰：「當是不習地土。」
entries.en: Song Bian said: "Perhaps they are unused to the soil here."
entries.literal: Song Bian said: "Perhaps they are unused to the soil."

entries.zh: 融曰：「周穆馬跡遍於天下，若騏騮之性，因地而遷，則造父之策，有時而躓。」
entries.en: Rong said: "King Mu's horses ranged the world; if fine breeds change with soil, then Zaofu's art would sometimes fail."
entries.literal: Rong said: "King Mu of Zhou's horses' tracks covered the world; if the nature of qiji and juli shifts with land, then Zaofu's methods would sometimes stumble."

entries.zh: 弁曰：「王主客何為勤勤於千里？」
entries.en: Bian asked: "Why is the Chief of Guests so eager for horses from a thousand li away?"
entries.literal: Bian said: "Why is the Chief of Guests so earnest about a thousand li?"

entries.zh: 融曰：「卿國既異其優劣，聊復相訪，若千里斯至，聖上當駕鼓車。」
entries.en: Rong said: "Since your state disputes their quality, I ask again—if they truly come from afar, our emperor will drive the drum carriage to meet them."
entries.literal: Rong said: "Since your state differs on quality, I merely inquire again; if they arrive from a thousand li, the sage emperor will drive the drum carriage."

entries.zh: 弁曰：「向意既須，必不能駕鼓車也。」
entries.en: Bian said: "If you truly need them, you surely will not send the drum carriage."
entries.literal: Bian said: "Since the intent is need, they surely cannot drive the drum carriage."

entries.zh: 融曰：「買死馬之骨，亦以郭隗之故。」
entries.en: Rong said: "Even buying dead horses' bones honors Guo Kui's memory."
entries.literal: Rong said: "Buying the bones of dead horses is also for Guo Kui's sake."

entries.zh: 弁不能答。
entries.en: Bian had no reply.
entries.literal: Bian could not answer.

entries.zh: 融躁于名利，自恃人地，三十內望為公輔。
entries.en: Rong hungered for fame and office; trusting in birth and rank, before thirty he expected the highest posts.
entries.literal: Rong was impatient for fame and profit; relying on his birth and station, before thirty he looked to become chief minister and assistant.

entries.zh: 初為司徒法曹，詣王僧佑，因遇沈昭略，未相識。
entries.en: Early in his career, as Law Clerk of the Minister of Education, he called on Wang Sengyou and met Shen Zhaolüe, a stranger to him.
entries.literal: At first as Law Clerk of the Minister of Education he called on Wang Sengyou and chanced to meet Shen Zhaolüe, whom he did not know.

entries.zh: 昭略屢顧盼，謂主人曰：「是何年少？」
entries.en: Zhaolüe glanced back again and again and asked the host: "Who is this young man?"
entries.literal: Zhaolüe looked back repeatedly and said to the host: "What youth is this?"

entries.zh: 融殊不平，謂曰：「僕出於扶桑，入于湯穀，照耀天下，誰雲不知，而卿此問？」
entries.en: Rong was furious: "I rise from Fusang and set in Tanggu, shining over the world—who does not know me, that you should ask?"
entries.literal: Rong was greatly displeased and said: "I come from Fusang and enter Tanggu, shining on all under heaven—who says they do not know, yet you ask this?"

entries.zh: 昭略云：「不知許事，且食蛤蜊。」
entries.en: Zhaolüe said: "I know nothing of that—let us eat clams instead."
entries.literal: Zhaolüe said: "I know nothing of such things—let us eat clams."

entries.zh: 融曰：「物以群分，方以類聚，君長東隅，居然應嗜此族。」
entries.en: Rong retorted: "Things flock by kind and regions by class—you rule the eastern corner and naturally favor this tribe."
entries.literal: Rong said: "Things group by kind, regions by class—you preside over the eastern corner and naturally should love this tribe."

entries.zh: 其高自標置如此。
entries.en: Such was his towering self-regard.
entries.literal: Such was his lofty self-regard.

entries.zh: 及魏軍動，竟陵王子良于東府募人，板融甯朔將軍、軍主。
entries.en: When Wei armies mobilized, the Prince of Jingling Ziliang recruited at the Eastern Mansion and appointed Rong General Who Pacifies the North and Army Commander.
entries.literal: When Wei troops moved, the Prince of Jingling Ziliang at the Eastern Mansion recruited men and appointed Rong General Who Pacifies the North and Army Commander.

entries.zh: 融文辭捷速，有所造作，援筆可待，子良特相友好。
entries.en: Rong wrote with swift grace; whatever he undertook he finished at a stroke; Ziliang favored him especially.
entries.literal: Rong's literary phrasing was quick; whatever he wrote he could finish at the brush; Ziliang was especially friendly with him.

entries.zh: 晚節大習騎馬，招集江西傖楚數百人，並有幹用，融特為謀主。
entries.en: In his later years he took hard to horsemanship, gathered several hundred tough men from west of the river and Chu, all useful fighters, and made himself their chief strategist.
entries.literal: In late years he greatly practiced horsemanship, gathered several hundred rough men of Jiang west and Chu, all capable, and Rong alone was their chief planner.

entries.zh: 武帝病篤暫絕，子良在殿內，太孫未入，融戎服絳衫，於中書省合口斷東宮仗不得進，欲矯詔立子良。
entries.en: When Emperor Wu lay gravely ill and briefly lost consciousness, Ziliang remained in the palace while the heir had not entered; Rong in martial dress and scarlet shirt blocked the Eastern Palace guard at the Secretariat gate, intending to forge an edict and install Ziliang.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu was gravely ill and briefly lost consciousness, Ziliang was in the palace hall and the heir had not entered; Rong in martial dress and scarlet shirt blocked the Eastern Palace guard at the Secretariat gate from entering, wishing to forge an edict and install Ziliang.

entries.zh: 詔草已立，上重蘇，朝事委西昌侯鸞。
entries.en: The draft edict was already written; the emperor rallied and entrusted affairs to the Marquis of Xichang Luan.
entries.literal: The draft edict was already written; the emperor recovered and court affairs were entrusted to the Marquis of Xichang Luan.

entries.zh: 梁武謂範雲曰：「左手據天下圖，右手刎其喉，愚夫不為。
entries.en: Emperor Wu of Liang told Fan Yun: "Left hand on the empire's map, right hand at its throat—no fool would do that.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang said to Fan Yun: "Left hand holding the map of all under heaven, right hand cutting its throat—no fool would do that.

entries.zh: 主上大漸，國家自有故事，道路籍籍，將有非常之舉，卿聞之乎？」
entries.en: The emperor is failing; the state has its own precedents; the roads buzz with talk of something extraordinary—have you heard?"
entries.literal: The lord is failing; the state has its own precedents; on the roads there is clamor that something extraordinary will happen—have you heard?"

entries.zh: 雲不敢答。
entries.en: Yun dared not answer.
entries.literal: Yun did not dare answer.

entries.zh: 俄而帝崩，融乃處分以子良兵禁諸門，西昌侯聞，急馳到雲龍門，不得進，乃曰：「有敕召我。」
entries.en: Soon the emperor died; Rong deployed Ziliang's troops to seal the gates; the Marquis of Xichang galloped to Cloud Dragon Gate but could not enter and cried: "An edict summons me."
entries.literal: Soon the emperor died; Rong then disposed troops with Ziliang's soldiers to seal the gates; the Marquis of Xichang heard and galloped to Cloud Dragon Gate but could not enter; he then said: "There is an edict summoning me."

entries.zh: 仍排而入，奉太孫登殿，命左右扶出子良，指麾音響如鍾，殿內無不從命。
entries.en: He forced his way in, escorted the heir to the throne, ordered attendants to lead Ziliang out; his commands rang like a bell and none in the hall disobeyed.
entries.literal: He pushed in, escorted the heir to the throne, ordered attendants to lead Ziliang out; his commands rang like a bell and none in the hall disobeyed.

entries.zh: 融知不遂，乃釋服還省，歎曰：「公誤我。」
entries.en: Knowing he had failed, Rong changed out of martial dress, returned to his office, and sighed: "The duke misled me."
entries.literal: Rong knew he would not succeed, put off his martial dress and returned to his office, and sighed: "The duke misled me."

entries.zh: 郁林深怨融，即位十餘日，收下廷尉獄。
entries.en: Emperor Yulin deeply hated Rong; within ten days of enthronement he seized him and cast him into the Court of Justice.
entries.literal: Emperor Yulin deeply resented Rong; more than ten days after taking the throne he seized him and put him in the Court of Justice prison.

entries.zh: 使中丞孔珪倚為奏曰：「融姿性剛險，立身浮競，動跡驚群，抗言異類。
entries.en: He had Censor Kong Gui draft the impeachment: "Rong's nature is harsh and treacherous, his conduct restless and ambitious; his deeds startle the crowd and his words defy convention.
entries.literal: He had the Censor Kong Gui draft the memorial on his behalf: "Rong's nature is hard and dangerous, his conduct floating and competitive; his movements startle the crowd and his bold words differ from the kind.

entries.zh: 近塞外微塵，苦求將領，遂招納不逞，扇誘荒傖。
entries.en: Lately, with dust on the frontier, he bitterly sought command and recruited unruly men, stirring up wild northerners.
entries.literal: Lately at the frontier dust he bitterly sought command and thus recruited unruly men, inciting wild northerners.

entries.zh: 狡弄威聲，專行權利，反復唇齒之間，傾動頰舌之內，威福自己，無所忌憚，誹謗朝政，曆毀王公。
entries.en: He played at intimidation, grasped power for himself, whispered and shouted as he pleased, feared nothing, slandered the court, and repeatedly defamed princes and nobles.
entries.literal: Cunningly wielding threatening voice, exclusively exercising power and profit, back and forth between lips and teeth, shaking within cheek and tongue, authority and favor from himself, without dread; slandering court governance, repeatedly destroying kings and dukes.

entries.zh: 謂己才流，無所推下，事暴遠近，使融依源據答。」
entries.en: He claimed no man matched his talent and birth; the charges were known far and wide; let Rong answer point by point."
entries.literal: He said his talent and class had none beneath him; the matter was exposed far and near; let Rong answer according to source and evidence."

entries.zh: 融辭曰：「囚實頑蔽，觸行多愆。
entries.en: Rong replied: "The prisoner is indeed dull and erring; his conduct has many faults.
entries.literal: Rong replied: "The prisoner is indeed stubborn and blind; his conduct has many faults.

entries.zh: 但夙忝門素，得奉教君子。
entries.en: Yet from youth I have borne my family's name and received instruction from gentlemen.
entries.literal: Yet from old I have disgraced my gate and lineage by receiving instruction from gentlemen.

entries.zh: 爰自總發，迄將立年，州閭鄉党，見許愚慎。
entries.en: From boyhood until nearly adulthood, neighbors in district and village called me prudent.
entries.literal: From first tying the hair until nearly the age of standing, in district and village my neighbors called me cautious.

entries.zh: 過蒙大行皇帝獎育之恩，又荷文皇帝識擢之重，司徒公賜預士林，安陸王曲垂盼接，前後陳伐虜之計，亦仰簡先朝。
entries.en: I enjoyed the late Grand Emperor's nurturing favor and the late Literary Emperor's recognition; the Minister of Education admitted me to the literati, the Prince of Anlu favored me; my plans against the northern foe were also approved by the former court.
entries.literal: I overly received the late Grand Emperor's nurturing favor and also bore the late Literary Emperor's recognition and promotion; the Minister of Education granted me place among the literati, the Prince of Anlu graciously received me; my plans for campaigning against the barbarians were also approved by the former court.

entries.zh: 今段犬羊乍擾，令囚草撰符詔。
entries.en: When the northern barbarians suddenly stirred, I was ordered to draft edicts and warrants.
entries.literal: Now when the dogs and sheep suddenly stirred, the prisoner was ordered to draft edicts and warrants.

entries.zh: 及司徒宣敕招募，同例非一，實以戎事不小，不敢承教。
entries.en: The Minister of Education again proclaimed recruitment; others did the same—it was not because the war was minor that I refused.
entries.literal: Again the Minister of Education proclaimed orders to recruit; there were many like cases—not because military matters were small did I dare refuse instruction.

entries.zh: 續蒙軍號，賜使招集，銜敕而行，非敢虛扇。
entries.en: I received a military title and orders to gather troops; I carried out the command—I did not stir empty alarm.
entries.literal: I again received a military title and was granted orders to gather men; I carried the command and went—not daring to stir empty alarm.

entries.zh: 且張弄威聲，應有形跡。
entries.en: As for playing at intimidation, there should be visible evidence.
entries.literal: Moreover, cunningly wielding threatening voice should have visible traces.

entries.zh: 專行權利，又無贓賄。
entries.en: Grasping power for profit—again, there is no bribe.
entries.literal: Exclusively exercising power and profit—again there is no bribe.

entries.zh: 反復唇齒之間，未審悉與誰言？
entries.en: Whispering between lips and teeth—with whom was all this spoken?
entries.literal: Back and forth between lips and teeth—I do not know with whom all this was spoken?

entries.zh: 傾動頰舌之內，不容都無主此。
entries.en: Shouting within cheek and tongue—surely someone must have presided over it?
entries.literal: Shaking within cheek and tongue—surely there cannot be no one who presided over this?

entries.zh: 自上甘露頌及銀甕啟、三日詩序、接虜使語辭，竭思稱揚，得非誹謗。
entries.en: From the Sweet Dew hymn to the silver-jar memorial, the three-day poem preface, and my words with barbarian envoys—I exhausted myself in praise; how is that slander?
entries.literal: From the Sweet Dew hymn upward, the silver-jar memorial, the three-day poem preface, and the words receiving the barbarian envoys—I exhausted thought in praise; how can this be slander?

entries.zh: 囚才分本劣，謬被策用，悚怍之情，夙宵兢惕，自循自省，並愧流言。
entries.en: My talent is by nature modest; wrongly placed in office, I tremble day and night; examining myself, I am ashamed before gossip.
entries.literal: The prisoner's talent and measure are by nature inferior; wrongly chosen for use, my fearful shame day and night is vigilant; examining myself, I am ashamed before idle talk.

entries.zh: 伏惟明皇臨宇，普天蒙澤，戊寅赦恩，輕重必宥，百日曠期，始蒙旬日，一介罪身，獨嬰憲劾。」
entries.en: I bow before the bright emperor whose grace covers the realm; the Wuyin amnesty spares light and heavy alike, and within the hundred-day grace I had barely ten days—a lone guilty man alone bears punishment."
entries.literal: I bow that the bright emperor overlooks the realm and all heaven receives grace; the Wuyin amnesty must spare light and heavy alike, and the hundred-day grace period had only just granted ten days—a lone guilty body alone bears punishment."

entries.zh: 融被收，朋友部曲，參問北寺，相繼於道；
entries.en: When Rong was seized, friends and retainers lined the road to North Temple to inquire after him;
entries.literal: When Rong was seized, friends and retainers came to inquire at North Temple one after another on the road;

entries.zh: 請救於子良，子良不敢救；
entries.en: they begged Ziliang to save him, but Ziliang dared not;
entries.literal: they asked Ziliang for rescue, and Ziliang did not dare rescue;

entries.zh: 西昌侯固爭不得。
entries.en: the Marquis of Xichang argued fiercely but could not prevail.
entries.literal: the Marquis of Xichang argued hard but could not prevail.

entries.zh: 詔于獄賜死，時年二十七。
entries.en: An edict ordered death in prison; he was twenty-seven.
entries.literal: An edict granted death in prison; he was then twenty-seven.

entries.zh: 臨死歎曰：「我若不為百歲老母，當吐一言。」
entries.en: Facing death he sighed: "Were it not for my aged mother, I would speak one word."
entries.literal: Facing death he sighed: "If not for my hundred-year-old mother, I would speak one word."

entries.zh: 融意欲指斥帝在東宮時過失也。
entries.en: Rong meant to expose the emperor's misconduct from his days as heir.
entries.literal: Rong intended to denounce the emperor's faults when he was Eastern Palace heir.

entries.zh: 先是，太學生會稽魏准，以才學為融所賞，既欲奉子良，而准鼓成其事。
entries.en: Earlier Wei Zhun of Kuaiji, a Grand Academy student admired by Rong for talent, wished to support Ziliang and pressed the plot forward.
entries.literal: Earlier, Wei Zhun of Kuaiji, a Grand Academy student, was admired by Rong for talent and learning; wishing to support Ziliang, Zhun urged the matter on.

entries.zh: 太學生虞羲、丘國賓竊相謂曰：「竟陵才弱，王中書無斷，敗在眼中矣。」
entries.en: Grand Academy students Yu Xi and Qiu Guobin whispered: "Jingling's talent is weak and Wang the Secretariat Director lacks resolve—defeat is plain to see."
entries.literal: Grand Academy students Yu Xi and Qiu Guobin whispered to each other: "The Prince of Jingling's talent is weak and Director of the Secretariat Wang lacks resolve—defeat is before our eyes."

entries.zh: 及融誅，召准入舍人省詰問，遂懼而死，舉體皆青，時人以准膽破。
entries.en: When Rong was executed, Zhun was summoned to the Attendants' Office for questioning; terror killed him—his whole body turned blue—and men said his gall had burst.
entries.literal: When Rong was executed, Zhun was summoned to the Attendants' Office for questioning; in fear he died, his whole body turning blue; men of the time said Zhun's gall had burst.

entries.zh: 融文集行于時。
entries.en: Rong's collected writings circulated in his day.
entries.literal: Rong's collected writings circulated in his time.

entries.zh: 歷位驃騎將軍王晏長史。
entries.en: He served in succession as chief clerk to the Cavalry General Wang Yan.
entries.literal: He served in succession as chief clerk to the Cavalry General Wang Yan.

entries.zh: 晏誅，出為晉陵太守。
entries.en: When Yan was executed he was sent out as Administrator of Jinling.
entries.literal: When Yan was executed he went out as Administrator of Jinling.

entries.zh: 潔己為政，妻子不免饑寒，時號廉平。
entries.en: He governed cleanly; wife and children still knew hunger and cold; men called him incorrupt and fair.
entries.literal: He kept himself clean in governance; wife and children did not escape hunger and cold; men of the time called him incorrupt and fair.

entries.zh: 王敬則作亂，瞻赴都，敬則經晉陵郡，人多附之。
entries.en: When Wang Jingze rebelled, Zhan went to the capital; Jingze passed through Jinling and many people joined him.
entries.literal: When Wang Jingze rebelled, Zhan went to the capital; Jingze passed through Jinling commandery and many people attached to him.

entries.zh: 敬則敗，台軍討賊黨，瞻言愚人易動，不足窮法。
entries.en: When Jingze was defeated, court troops punished the rebels; Zhan argued that fools are easily swayed and need not be pursued to the full penalty.
entries.literal: When Jingze was defeated, court troops punished the rebel partisans; Zhan said foolish men are easily moved and need not be pursued to the full law.

entries.zh: 齊明帝從之。
entries.en: Emperor Ming of Qi agreed.
entries.literal: Emperor Ming of Qi followed this.

entries.zh: 所全萬數。
entries.en: Those he spared numbered in the tens of thousands.
entries.literal: Those he spared numbered in the tens of thousands.

entries.zh: 遷御史中丞。
entries.en: He was transferred to Imperial Censor.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Imperial Censor.

entries.zh: 論曰：語云：「不有君子，其能國乎？」。
entries.en: Commentary: The saying runs: "Without gentlemen, how can there be a state?"
entries.literal: Commentary says: The saying goes: "Without gentlemen, how can there be a state?"

entries.zh: 晉自中原沸騰，介居江左，以一隅之地，抗衡上國，年移三百，蓋有憑焉。
entries.en: From the time Jin's heartland boiled and they held east of the river, one corner balancing the northern empire for three hundred years—they surely had something to lean on.
entries.literal: From the time Jin's central plains seethed and they dwelt east of the river, with one corner of land balancing the upper state, years moved three hundred—surely there was reliance.

entries.zh: 其初諺云：「王與馬，共天下。」
entries.en: An early proverb said: "The Wangs and the Mas share the realm."
entries.literal: At the beginning the proverb said: "Wang and Ma share all under heaven together."

entries.zh: 蓋王氏人倫之盛，實始是矣。
entries.en: The Wang clan's eminence among men truly began here.
entries.literal: Truly the Wang clan's human excellence began here.

entries.zh: 及夫休元弟兄，並舉棟樑之任，下逮世嗣，無虧文雅之風。
entries.en: When Xiuyuan and his brothers together bore the weight of state, down through later heirs the refined literary tradition did not fail.
entries.literal: When Xiuyuan and his brothers together bore pillar-and-beam responsibility, down to later heirs, the refined literary wind was not lost.

entries.zh: 其所以簪纓不替，豈徒然也。
entries.en: That their line held rank without break—was it mere chance?
entries.literal: That their official caps were not replaced—was it for nothing?

entries.zh: 僧達倡狂成性，元長躁競不止。
entries.en: Sengda was wild arrogance incarnate; Yuanchang's restless ambition never ceased.
entries.literal: Sengda's wild arrogance was his nature; Yuanchang's restless striving never ceased.

entries.zh: 王弘，字休元，琅邪临沂人也。
entries.en: Wang Hong, courtesy name Xiuyuan, came from Langya commandery, Linyi county.
entries.literal: Wang Hong, styled Xiuyuan, was a man of Langya Linyi.

entries.zh: 曾祖导，晋丞相，祖洽，中领军，父珣，司徒。
entries.en: His great-grandfather Dao had served as Chancellor of Jin; his grandfather Qia as Central Army Commander; his father Xun as Minister of Education.
entries.literal: His great-grandfather Dao was Chancellor of Jin; his grandfather Qia was Central Army Commander; his father Xun was Minister of Education.

entries.zh: 性耿介，絕諸請托，雖儲副之尊，公侯之重，溺情相及，終不為屈。
entries.en: Stubbornly upright, he refused every pull of patronage—even when crown princes or great lords pleaded on private grounds, he would not bend.
entries.literal: By nature he was upright and severed all requests for favor; though the heir's dignity or the weight of dukes and marquises pressed him with personal feeling, he never yielded.

entries.zh: 始興王叔陵之在湘州，累諷有司，固求台鉉。
entries.en: Prince Shixing's son Shuling, while governing Xiang Province, repeatedly leaned on officials to demand a capital appointment.
entries.literal: When Prince Shixing's Shuling was in Xiang Province he repeatedly hinted to the relevant offices and stubbornly sought a post at the capital.

entries.zh: 奐曰：「袞章本以德重，未必皇枝。」
entries.en: Huan replied, "Grand seals belong to men of moral weight, not automatically to princes of the blood."
entries.literal: Huan said, "The imperial regalia of office rests on weight of virtue—not necessarily on imperial descent."

entries.zh: 因抗言于宣帝。
entries.en: He spoke bluntly against the demand before Emperor Xuan.
entries.literal: He therefore spoke boldly against this to Emperor Xuan.

entries.zh: 帝曰：「始興那忽望公，且朕兒為公，須在鄱陽王后。」
entries.en: The emperor said, "Shixing should not dream so high—and as my son he stands below the Queen of Poyang in precedence."
entries.literal: The emperor said, "How could Shixing harbor such hopes? And as my son he ranks after the Queen of Poyang."

entries.zh: 奐曰：「臣之所見，亦如聖旨。」
entries.en: Huan answered, "My view matches Your Majesty's own."
entries.literal: Huan said, "What I see accords with Your Majesty's intent."

entries.zh: 後主時在東宮，欲以江總為太子詹事，令管記陸瑜言之奐。
entries.en: The future Later Lord, then crown prince, wanted Jiang Zong as Grand Tutor and sent his recorder Lu Yu to sound Huan out.
entries.literal: At the time the Later Lord was in the Eastern Palace and wished to make Jiang Zong Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent; he had his recorder Lu Yu speak to Huan about it.

entries.zh: 奐曰：「江有潘、陸之華，而無園、綺之實，輔弼儲貳，竊謂非材。」
entries.en: Huan said, "Jiang has Pan Yue's polish and Lu Ji's glitter, not Yuan Ji's depth or Qi Wuhui's substance—he is no fit tutor for an heir."
entries.literal: Huan said, "Jiang has the brilliance of Pan and Lu but not the substance of Yuan and Qi; to assist the heir I privately deem him unfit."

entries.zh: 後主深以為恨，乃自言于宣帝。
entries.en: The crown prince nursed a deep grudge and complained directly to Emperor Xuan.
entries.literal: The Later Lord deeply resented this and spoke of it himself to Emperor Xuan.

entries.zh: 宣帝將許之，奐乃奏曰：「江總文華之人，今皇太子文華不少，無藉於總。
entries.en: Emperor Xuan nearly agreed until Huan memorialized: "Jiang Zong is ornamental prose—the crown prince already has ornament enough without him.
entries.literal: Emperor Xuan was about to consent; Huan then memorialized: "Jiang Zong is a man of literary brilliance; the Crown Prince already has brilliance enough and has no need of Zong.

entries.zh: 如臣愚見，願選敦重之才，以居輔導。」
entries.en: I urge appointing a man of sober weight to guide the heir."
entries.literal: In my humble view, I wish to select a man of solid weight to occupy the guiding post."

entries.zh: 帝曰：「誰可？」
entries.en: The emperor asked, "Whom do you propose?"
entries.literal: The emperor said, "Who would do?"

entries.zh: 奐曰：「都官尚書王廓，代有懿德，識性敦敏，可以居之。」
entries.en: Huan named Wang Kuo of the Palace Bureau—'a line of proven virtue, sharp and steady—he can hold the post."
entries.literal: Huan said, "Wang Kuo, Minister of the Palace Bureau, comes from generations of fine virtue and is discerning and earnest—he can hold the post."

entries.zh: 後主時亦在側，乃曰：「廓王泰之子，不可居太子詹事。」
entries.en: The crown prince, present at the audience, objected: "Wang Kuo is Wang Tai's son—unsuitable for Grand Tutor."
entries.literal: The Later Lord was also at the side and said, "Kuo is Wang Tai's son—he cannot hold the Grand Tutorship to the Heir Apparent."

entries.zh: 奐又曰：「宋朝范曄即範泰之子，亦為太子詹事。」
entries.en: Huan countered, "Under Song, Fan Ye—Fan Tai's own son—served as Grand Tutor."
entries.literal: Huan again said, "In the Song dynasty Fan Ye, who was Fan Tai's son, also served as Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent."

entries.zh: 後主固爭之，帝以總為詹事，由是忤旨。
entries.en: The prince pressed his case; the emperor named Jiang Zong Grand Tutor anyway, and Huan fell from favor.
entries.literal: The Later Lord stubbornly contested; the emperor made Zong Grand Tutor, and Huan thereby offended the imperial intent.

entries.zh: 會稽聞西軍稍近，將士多奔亡，覬不能復製。
entries.en: As imperial forces neared Kuaiji, troops deserted in droves and Xi lost control.
entries.literal: Kuaiji heard the western army drawing near; officers and soldiers mostly fled, and Xi could no longer control them.

entries.zh: 上虞令王晏起兵攻郡，覬憂遽不知所為。
entries.en: Shangyu magistrate Wang Yan raised troops against the prefecture; Xi panicked.
entries.literal: The magistrate of Shangyu, Wang Yan, raised troops to attack the commandery; Xi in panic knew not what to do.

entries.zh: 其夕率千人聲雲東討，實趨石賜。
entries.en: That night he led a thousand men, claiming an eastern expedition, but fled toward Shici.
entries.literal: That evening he led a thousand men, proclaiming an eastern campaign, but in fact hurried to Shici.

entries.zh: 遇潮涸不得去，眾叛都盡，門生載以小船，竄於山脊村。
entries.en: The tide went out and trapped him; his force melted away; a student rowed him in a skiff to a mountain hamlet.
entries.literal: The tide ebbed and he could not leave; the masses all rebelled and departed; a student loaded him in a small boat and hid on a mountain ridge village.

entries.zh: 村人縛以送晏，晏調曰：「此事孔璪所為，無豫卿事，可作首辭，當相為申上。」
entries.en: Villagers bound him for Wang Yan, who said lightly, "Kong Zuan did this, not you—write the lead confession and I will speak for you at court."
entries.literal: Villagers bound him and sent him to Yan; Yan jested, "This was Kong Zuan's doing—you had no part; you may compose the chief confession and I will plead for you above."

entries.zh: 覬曰：「江東處分，莫不由身，委罪求活，便是君輩行意耳。」
entries.en: Xi answered, "Every decision east of the Yang was mine—shift blame to live? That is your trade, not mine."
entries.literal: Xi said, "Dispositions east of the river all proceed from oneself—to shift guilt and seek life is your kind's way."

entries.zh: 晏乃斬之東合外。
entries.en: Yan beheaded him outside the eastern hall.
entries.literal: Yan then beheaded him outside the eastern pavilion.

entries.zh: 臨死求酒，曰：「此是平生所好。」
entries.en: At the block he asked for wine: "This was my lifelong pleasure."
entries.literal: Facing death he asked for wine, saying, "This was my lifelong delight."

entries.zh: 顧琛、王曇生、袁標等並詣吳喜歸罪，喜皆宥之。
entries.en: Gu Chen, Wang Tansheng, Yuan Biao, and others surrendered to Wu Xi for judgment; he pardoned them all.
entries.literal: Gu Chen, Wang Tansheng, Yuan Biao and others all went to Wu Xi to surrender and accept punishment; Xi pardoned them all.

entries.zh: 東軍主凡七十六人，於陣斬十七人，餘皆原宥。
entries.en: Seventy-six eastern commanders in all—seventeen killed in battle, the rest spared.
entries.literal: Eastern army commanders numbered seventy-six in all; seventeen were beheaded in battle, the rest pardoned.

entries.zh: 列傳第十七
entries.en: the seventeenth year of Biographies
entries.literal: Biographies 17

entries.zh: 子孺字季幼，幼聰敏，七歲能屬文。
entries.en: His son Liu Ru, courtesy name Jiyou, was clever from childhood and at seven could compose prose.
entries.literal: His son Ru, courtesy name Jiyou, was clever from childhood and at seven could compose prose.

entries.zh: 年十四居喪，毀瘠骨立，宗黨咸異之。
entries.en: At fourteen he kept mourning for a parent, wasted to skin and bone, and all his clan marveled at him.
entries.literal: At fourteen he kept mourning; wasted to the bone, all his clan marveled at him.

entries.zh: 叔父瑱為義興郡，攜以之官，常置坐側，謂賓客曰：「此吾家明珠也。」
entries.en: His uncle Zhen was magistrate of Yixing and took him to his post, always seating him at his side. He told guests: "This is the bright pearl of our house."
entries.literal: His uncle Zhen was magistrate of Yixing and took him to his post, always seating him at his side; he told guests: "This is the bright pearl of our house."

entries.zh: 及長，美風采，性通和，雖家人不見其喜慍。
entries.en: When grown, he had a fine bearing and an open, harmonious nature—even his family never saw him show joy or anger.
entries.literal: When grown, he had fine bearing; his nature was open and harmonious—even family never saw him show joy or anger.

entries.zh: 本州召迎主簿。
entries.en: His home province summoned him to serve as Chief Clerk.
entries.literal: His home province summoned him as Chief Clerk.

entries.zh: 起家中軍法曹行參軍，時鎮軍沈約聞其名，引為主簿，恒與遊宴賦詩，大為約所嗟賞。
entries.en: He entered office as Acting Army Controller in the Central Army Legal Bureau. Shen Yue, General Who Pacifies the Army, heard his name and took him as Chief Clerk; they often feasted and composed poetry together, and Yue greatly admired him.
entries.literal: He entered office as Acting Army Controller in the Central Army Legal Bureau; at the time General Who Pacifies the Army Shen Yue heard his name and took him as Chief Clerk, often feasting and composing poetry with him—greatly admired by Yue.

entries.zh: 累遷太子中舍人。
entries.en: He was repeatedly promoted to Attendant in the Crown Prince's household.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Attendant in the Crown Prince's household.

entries.zh: 孝綽字孝綽，本名冉。
entries.en: Liu Xiaochuo, courtesy name Xiaochuo, had the original given name Ran.
entries.literal: Xiaochuo, courtesy name Xiaochuo, original given name Ran.

entries.zh: 幼聰敏，七歲能屬文。
entries.en: From childhood he was clever; at seven he could compose prose.
entries.literal: From childhood he was clever; at seven he could compose prose.

entries.zh: 舅齊中書郎王融深賞異之，與同載以適親友，號曰神童。
entries.en: His uncle Wang Rong, Secretariat Gentleman of Qi, greatly admired him, took him in the same carriage to visit kin and friends, and called him a divine child.
entries.literal: His uncle Wang Rong, Secretariat Gentleman of Qi, greatly admired and favored him, took him in the same carriage to visit kin and friends, and called him a divine child.

entries.zh: 融每曰：「天下文章若無我，當歸阿士。」
entries.en: Rong often said: "If there were no me in the world's literature, it would belong to A Shi."
entries.literal: Rong often said: "If there were no me in the world's literature, it would belong to A Shi."

entries.zh: 阿士即孝綽小字也。
entries.en: A Shi was Xiaochuo's childhood name.
entries.literal: A Shi was Xiaochuo's childhood name.

entries.zh: 父繪，齊時掌詔誥，孝綽時年十四，繪常使代草之。
entries.en: His father Hui in Qi times controlled edicts and patents; when Xiaochuo was fourteen, Hui often had him draft them in his place.
entries.literal: His father Hui in Qi times was in charge of edicts and patents; when Xiaochuo was fourteen, Hui often had him draft them.

entries.zh: 父党沈約、任昉、范雲等聞其名，命駕造焉，昉尤相賞好。
entries.en: Shen Yue, Ren Fang, Fan Yun, and other friends of his father heard his name and came to visit; Fang especially prized and befriended him.
entries.literal: Shen Yue, Ren Fang, Fan Yun, and other friends of his father heard his name and ordered their carriages to visit him; Fang especially prized and befriended him.

entries.zh: 範雲年長繪十餘歲，其子孝才與孝綽年並十四五。
entries.en: Fan Yun was more than ten years older than Hui; his son Xiaocai and Xiaochuo were both fourteen or fifteen.
entries.literal: Fan Yun was more than ten years older than Hui; his son Xiaocai and Xiaochuo were both fourteen or fifteen.

entries.zh: 及雲遇孝綽，便申伯季，乃命孝才拜之。
entries.en: When Yun met Xiaochuo, he declared elder and younger brotherhood and ordered Xiaocai to bow to him.
entries.literal: When Yun met Xiaochuo, he declared elder and younger brotherhood and ordered Xiaocai to bow to him.

entries.zh: 兼善草隸，自以書似父，乃變為別體。
entries.en: He was also skilled in cursive and clerical script; thinking his writing resembled his father's, he changed to a different style.
entries.literal: He was also skilled in cursive and clerical script; thinking his writing resembled his father's, he changed to a different style.

entries.zh: 第五弟孝勝，位尚書右丞、兼散騎常侍。
entries.en: The fifth younger brother Xiaosheng held the posts of Right Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing and concurrent Privy Attendant.
entries.literal: The fifth younger brother Xiaosheng held the posts of Right Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing and concurrent Privy Attendant.

entries.zh: 聘魏還，為安西武陵王紀長史、蜀郡太守。
entries.en: After an embassy to Wei he returned and became Chief Clerk to Prince Anxi of Wuling and Administrator of Shujun.
entries.literal: After an embassy to Wei he returned and became Chief Clerk to Prince Anxi of Wuling and Administrator of Shujun.

entries.zh: 紀僭號於蜀，以為尚書僕射。
entries.en: When Ji usurped the title in Shu, he was made Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing.
entries.literal: When Ji usurped the title in Shu, he was made Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 隨紀出峽口，兵敗被執。
entries.en: Following Ji out of the gorge mouth, the army was defeated and he was captured.
entries.literal: Following Ji out of the gorge mouth, the army was defeated and he was captured.

entries.zh: 元帝宥之，以為司徒右長史。
entries.en: Emperor Yuan pardoned him and appointed him Right Chief Clerk of the Masters of Writing.
entries.literal: Emperor Yuan pardoned him and appointed him Right Chief Clerk of the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 第七弟孝先，位武陵王主簿，與兄孝勝俱隨紀軍出峽口。
entries.en: The seventh younger brother Xiaoxian served as Chief Clerk to Prince Wuling and, with his brother Xiaosheng, followed Ji's army out of the gorge mouth.
entries.literal: The seventh younger brother Xiaoxian was Chief Clerk to Prince Wuling and followed his brother Xiaosheng with Ji's army out of the gorge mouth.

entries.zh: 瑱字士溫，繪弟也。
entries.en: Liu Zhen, courtesy name Shiwen, was Hui's younger brother.
entries.literal: Zhen, courtesy name Shiwen, was Hui's younger brother.

entries.zh: 少有行業，文藻、篆隸、丹青並為當世所稱。
entries.en: From youth he had good conduct; literature, seal script, clerical script, and painting were all acclaimed in his age.
entries.literal: From youth he had good conduct; literature, seal script, clerical script, and painting were all acclaimed in his age.

entries.zh: 時有滎陽毛惠遠善畫馬，瑱善畫婦人，並為當世第一。
entries.en: At the time Mao Huiyuan of Xingyang was skilled at painting horses and Zhen at painting women—each was first in the age.
entries.literal: At the time Mao Huiyuan of Xingyang was skilled at painting horses, Zhen at painting women—both were first in the age.

entries.zh: 瑱妹為齊鄱陽王妃，伉儷甚篤。
entries.en: Zhen's younger sister was consort to the Princess of Poyang of Qi; husband and wife were deeply devoted.
entries.literal: Zhen's younger sister was consort to the Princess of Poyang of Qi; husband and wife were deeply devoted.

entries.zh: 王為齊明帝所誅，妃追傷遂成痼疾，醫所不療。
entries.en: The prince was executed by Emperor Ming of Qi; the consort grieved until she fell into chronic illness that physicians could not cure.
entries.literal: The prince was executed by Emperor Ming of Qi; the consort grieved and became chronically ill, beyond physicians' cure.

entries.zh: 有陳郡殷蒨善寫人面，與真不別，瑱令蒨畫王形像，並圖王平生所寵姬共照鏡狀，如欲偶寢。
entries.en: Yin Qian of Chen commandery could paint human faces indistinguishable from life. Zhen had Qian paint the prince's likeness together with the prince's favorite concubines gazing in a mirror, as if about to share the bed.
entries.literal: Yin Qian of Chen commandery was skilled at painting human faces indistinguishable from life; Zhen had Qian paint the prince's likeness together with the prince's favorite concubines gazing in a mirror as if about to share the bed.

entries.zh: 瑱乃密使媼奶示妃，妃視畫仍唾之，因罵云：「故宜其早死」。
entries.en: Zhen secretly had a nurse show the consort the painting. She looked at it and spat, cursing: "So it was right that he died early."
entries.literal: Zhen secretly had a nurse show the consort; she looked at the painting and spat at it, cursing: "So it was right that he died early."

entries.zh: 於是恩情即歇，病亦除差。
entries.en: Thereupon affection ceased and the illness was cured.
entries.literal: Thereupon affection ceased and the illness was cured.

entries.zh: 此姬亦被廢苦，因即以此畫焚之。
entries.en: This concubine too had suffered in disgrace and therefore burned the painting.
entries.literal: This concubine too had suffered in disgrace and therefore burned the painting.

entries.zh: 瑱仕齊，曆尚書吏部郎，義興太守。
entries.en: Zhen served Qi, holding posts as Director in the Ministry of Personnel and Administrator of Yixing.
entries.literal: Zhen served Qi, holding posts as Director in the Ministry of Personnel and Administrator of Yixing.

entries.zh: 先繪卒。
entries.en: He died before Hui.
entries.literal: He died before Hui.

entries.zh: 列傳第二十九
entries.en: the twenty-ninth year of Biography
entries.literal: Biographies 29

entries.zh: 性剛穎俊出，與諸王共作短句詩，學謝靈運體，以呈高帝。
entries.en: His temperament was bold, sharp, and outstanding; with the other princes he wrote short poems in the manner of Xie Lingyun and presented them to Emperor Gao.
entries.literal: His nature was firm, sharp, and outstanding; with the other princes he composed short-verse poems in Xie Lingyun's style and presented them to Emperor Gao.

entries.zh: 帝報曰：「見汝二十字，諸兒作中，最為優者。
entries.en: The emperor replied: "I have seen your twenty lines—among all my sons' compositions, yours is the finest.
entries.literal: The emperor replied: "Seeing your twenty characters—among all the boys' compositions yours is the finest.

entries.zh: 但康樂放蕩，作體不辨有首尾，安仁、士衡深可宗尚，顏延之抑其次也。」
entries.en: But Kangyue is unrestrained—his compositions lack clear structure from beginning to end. Anren and Shiheng are truly worthy of emulation; Yanzhi ranks below them."
entries.literal: But Xie Kangyue is unrestrained; his compositional form does not distinguish beginning from end. Pan Anren and Lu Shiheng are deeply worthy of reverence; Yan Yanzhi ranks below them."

entries.zh: 隆昌元年，為侍中，領驍騎將軍，尋加秘書監。
entries.en: In the first year of Longchang he became Palace Attendant and commanded the Valiant Cavalry; soon he was also Director of the Secretariat Archives.
entries.literal: In the first year of Longchang he became Palace Attendant and commanded the Valiant Cavalry; soon he was also made Director of the Secretariat Archives.

entries.zh: 及明帝知權，蕃邸危懼，江祏嘗謂王晏曰：「江夏王有才行，亦善能匿跡，以琴道授羊景之，景之著名，而江夏掩能於世，非唯七弦而已，百氏亦復如之。」
entries.en: When Emperor Ming seized power the princely residences were in peril; Jiang Shi once told Wang Yan, "The Prince of Jiangxia has talent and conduct and excels at concealing his abilities; he taught the zither to Yang Jingzhi—Jingzhi is famous while Jiangxia hides his skill from the world. It is not only the seven strings; the hundred schools are the same."
entries.literal: When Emperor Ming grasped power the princely residences were in peril; Jiang Shi once said to Wang Yan, "The Prince of Jiangxia has ability and conduct and is also skilled at concealing his talents; he taught the zither to Yang Jingzhi—Jingzhi is famous while Jiangxia hides his ability from the world. It is not only in the seven strings; the hundred schools are likewise."

entries.zh: 鋒聞歎曰：「江祏遂復為混沌畫眉，欲益反弊耳。
entries.en: When Feng heard of it he sighed and said, "Jiang Shi is again painting eyebrows on chaos—intending to help, he will only make things worse.
entries.literal: When Feng heard of it he sighed and said, "Jiang Shi is again painting eyebrows on chaos—he means to help but will only make things worse.

entries.zh: 寡人聲酒是耽，狗馬是好，豈復一豪于平生哉。」
entries.en: I am devoted to music and wine and fond of dogs and horses—how could I change a hair's breadth from the life I have always lived?"
entries.literal: I am devoted to sound and wine and fond of dogs and horses—how could I be a hair's breadth different from my whole life?"

entries.zh: 當時以為話言。
entries.en: At the time this was taken as a memorable saying.
entries.literal: At the time this was taken as a saying.

entries.zh: 常忽忽不樂，著修柏賦以見志，曰：「既殊群而抗立，亦含貞而挺正。
entries.en: He was often restless and unhappy and wrote the "Fu on the Evergreen Cypress" to express his intent: "Standing apart from the multitude yet rising up, it holds to integrity and stands upright.
entries.literal: He was often restless and unhappy and wrote the "Fu on the Evergreen Cypress" to express his intent, saying, "Standing apart from the multitude yet rising up, it holds steadfastness and stands upright.

entries.zh: 豈春日之自芳，在霜下而為盛。
entries.en: It is not that spring days are fragrant in themselves—it flourishes beneath the frost.
entries.literal: It is not that spring days are fragrant in themselves—it flourishes under frost.

entries.zh: 沖風不能摧其枝，積雪不能改其性。
entries.en: Gale winds cannot break its branches; piled snow cannot alter its nature.
entries.literal: Gale winds cannot break its branches; piled snow cannot alter its nature.

entries.zh: 雖坎壇于當年，庶後凋之可詠。」
entries.en: Though cut down in its season, its later withering may still be worthy of song."
entries.literal: Though it may be cut down in its season, later decline may still be sung of."

entries.zh: 時鼎業潛移，鋒獨慨然有匡復之意，逼之行事典簽，故不遂也。
entries.en: At the time the imperial enterprise was shifting in secret; Feng alone was stirred with intent to restore the dynasty, but the acting record-keeper constrained him, and so he did not succeed.
entries.literal: At the time the imperial enterprise was shifting in secret; Feng alone was stirred with intent to restore the dynasty, but the acting record-keeper pressed him, and therefore he did not succeed.

entries.zh: 嘗見明帝，言次及遙光才力可委之意，鋒答曰：「遙光之于殿下，猶殿下之于高皇，衛宗廟，安社稷，實有攸寄。」
entries.en: He once saw Emperor Ming and in passing mentioned that Yaoguang's talent and strength could be entrusted; Feng answered, "Yaoguang toward Your Highness is as Your Highness was toward Emperor Gao—guarding the ancestral temple and securing the state: the charge is real."
entries.literal: He once saw Emperor Ming and in conversation touched on the idea that Yaoguang's talent and strength could be entrusted; Feng answered, "Yaoguang toward Your Highness is as Your Highness was toward Emperor Gao—guarding the ancestral temple and securing the altars of soil and grain: the charge is real."

entries.zh: 明帝失色。
entries.en: Emperor Ming turned pale.
entries.literal: Emperor Ming turned pale.

entries.zh: 及延興元年，明帝誅高、武、文惠諸子，鏗聞之，馮左右從容雅步，詠陸機吊魏武云：「昔以四海為己任，死則以愛子托人。」
entries.en: In the first year of Yanxing, when Emperor Ming killed the sons of Gao, Wu, and Wenhu, Qiang heard of it and, supported by his attendants, walked with easy, graceful steps, reciting Lu Ji's elegy for Cao Cao: "Once he took the four seas as his charge; in death he entrusted his beloved son to another."
entries.literal: In the first year of Yanxing, when Emperor Ming killed the sons of Gao, Wu, and Wenhu, Qiang heard of it and, leaning on his attendants, walked with easy, graceful steps, reciting Lu Ji's elegy for Emperor Wu of Wei: "Once he took the four seas as his charge; in death he entrusted his beloved son to another."

entries.zh: 如此者三，左右皆泣。
entries.en: He did this three times; all around him wept.
entries.literal: He did this three times; those around all wept.

entries.zh: 後果遣呂文顯賚藥往，夜進聽事，正逢八關齋。
entries.en: Later Lü Wenxian was sent with poisoned medicine; at night he entered the audience hall, just as the Eightfold Fast was being observed.
entries.literal: Later Lü Wenxian was indeed sent with poisoned medicine; at night he entered the audience hall, just as the Eightfold Fast was being observed.

entries.zh: 鏗上高坐，謂文顯曰：「高皇昔寵任君，何事乃有今日之行？」
entries.en: Qiang sat on a high seat and said to Wenxian, "Emperor Gao once favored and trusted you—why this action today?"
entries.literal: Qiang sat on a high seat and said to Wenxian, "Emperor Gao once favored and trusted you—why today's action?"

entries.zh: 答云：「出不獲已。」
entries.en: He answered, "I had no choice."
entries.literal: He answered, "I could not do otherwise."

entries.zh: 於是仰藥。
entries.en: He therefore swallowed the medicine.
entries.literal: He therefore swallowed the medicine.

entries.zh: 時年十八。
entries.en: He was eighteen years old.
entries.literal: He was then eighteen years old.

entries.zh: 身長七尺，鏗狀似兄嶷，咸以國器許之。
entries.en: He stood seven chi tall; Qiang resembled his elder brother Ying in appearance, and all regarded him as fit for the highest office.
entries.literal: He stood seven chi in height; Qiang's appearance resembled his elder brother Ying, and all regarded him as material for the state.

entries.zh: 及死，有識者莫不痛惜。
entries.en: At his death all who knew him grieved.
entries.literal: At his death all who knew him grieved.

entries.zh: 鉉年稍長。
entries.en: Xuan gradually grew older.
entries.literal: Xuan gradually grew older.

entries.zh: 四年，誅王晏，以謀立鉉為名，鉉免官，以王還第，禁不得與外人交通。
entries.en: In the fourth year Wang Yan was executed on the charge of plotting to establish Xuan; Xuan was removed from office, returned to his residence as a prince, and forbidden contact with outsiders.
entries.literal: In the fourth year Wang Yan was executed on the charge of plotting to establish Xuan; Xuan was removed from office, returned to his residence as a prince, and forbidden to have contact with outsiders.

entries.zh: 永泰元年，明帝疾暴甚，乃見害。
entries.en: In the first year of Yongtai Emperor Ming's illness suddenly worsened sharply, and Xuan was then killed.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongtai Emperor Ming's illness suddenly worsened greatly, and Xuan was then killed.

entries.zh: 聞收至，欣然曰：「死生命也，終不斅建安乞為奴而不得。」
entries.en: When he heard the arrest had come he said gladly, "Death and life are fate; I would never imitate Jian'an begging to be a slave and failing."
entries.literal: When he heard the arrest had come he said gladly, "Death and life are fate; I would never imitate Jian'an begging to be a slave and not succeeding."

entries.zh: 仰藥而卒。
entries.en: He swallowed the medicine and died.
entries.literal: He swallowed the medicine and died.

entries.zh: 鉉二子在孩抱，亦見殺。
entries.en: Xuan's two sons were still in infancy and were also killed.
entries.literal: Xuan's two sons were still in infancy and were also killed.

entries.zh: 列傳第三十三齊高帝諸子下
entries.en: Biographies 33: Sons of Emperor Gao of Southern Qi, Part Two
entries.literal: Biographies 33: Sons of Emperor Gao of Qi, Part Two

entries.zh: 後為廣陵太守，行南兗州事。
entries.en: He was later made Administrator of Guangling and exercised authority over South Yan Province.
entries.literal: Later he became Administrator of Guangling and acted as overseer of South Yan Province affairs.

entries.zh: 齊高帝在淮陰，安人遙相結事。
entries.en: While Emperor Gao of Qi was still at Huaiyin, Li Anren sought him out from a distance and pledged his support.
entries.literal: When the Qi Emperor Gao was at Huaiyin, Anren from afar entered into alliance with him.

entries.zh: 元徽初，除司州刺史，領義陽太守。
entries.en: At the opening of the Yuanhui reign he was named Inspector of Si Province and also held the post of Administrator of Yiyang.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Yuanhui era he was appointed Inspector of Si Province and concurrently Administrator of Yiyang.

entries.zh: 及桂陽王休范起事，安人遣軍援都。
entries.en: When Prince Xiufan of Guiyang rebelled, Li Anren dispatched forces to relieve the capital.
entries.literal: When Prince Xiufan of Guiyang rose in rebellion, Anren sent troops to aid the capital.

entries.zh: 建平王景素起兵，安人破其軍于葛橋。
entries.en: Prince Jingsu of Jianping took up arms; Li Anren destroyed his force at Ge Bridge.
entries.literal: When Prince Jingsu of Jianping raised troops, Anren routed his army at Ge Bridge.

entries.zh: 景素誅，留安人行南徐州事。
entries.en: Once Jingsu had been put to death, Li Anren was left in charge of South Xu Province.
entries.literal: After Jingsu was executed, Anren was retained to oversee South Xu Province affairs.

entries.zh: 城局參軍王回素為安人所親，盜絹二匹。
entries.en: Wang Hui, a bureau staff officer whom Li Anren had long favored, stole two bolts of silk.
entries.literal: Wang Hui, a staff officer of the city bureau whom Anren favored, stole two bolts of silk.

entries.zh: 安人流涕謂曰：「我與卿契闊備嘗，今日犯王法，乃卿負我也。」
entries.en: Li Anren wept and told him, "We have been through everything together; by breaking the law today you are the one who has betrayed our bond."
entries.literal: Anren wept and said to him, "You and I have shared every hardship; today you have violated the royal law—it is you who have failed me."

entries.zh: 於軍門斬之，厚為斂祭，軍府皆震服。
entries.en: He had Wang Hui executed at the camp gate, then buried him with full honors. Every office in the command submitted in awe.
entries.literal: He had him beheaded at the army gate, gave him a lavish funeral, and the entire headquarters trembled in submission.

entries.zh: 轉東中郎司馬，行會稽郡事。
entries.en: He was transferred to Eastern Staff Major and governed Kuaiji commandery in an acting capacity.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Eastern Staff Major and acted as overseer of Kuaiji commandery affairs.

entries.zh: 時蒼梧縱虐，齊高帝憂迫無計。
entries.en: The Cangwu emperor was then raging in tyranny, and Emperor Gao of Qi, desperate and without a strategy,
entries.literal: At that time the Cangwu emperor ran wild in cruelty, and Emperor Gao of Qi was pressed with worry and had no plan.

entries.zh: 安人白高帝，欲于東奉江夏王躋起兵。
entries.en: Li Anren urged Emperor Gao to proclaim Prince Ji of Jiangxia in the east and march against the throne.
entries.literal: Anren told the Emperor Gao that he wished to raise troops in the east under Prince Ji of Jiangxia.

entries.zh: 高帝不許，乃止。
entries.en: Emperor Gao refused, and the plan went no further.
entries.literal: The Emperor Gao did not consent, and so he stopped.

entries.zh: 高帝即位，為中領軍，封康樂侯。
entries.en: When Emperor Gao ascended the throne, Anren became Central General-in-Chief and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Kangle.
entries.literal: When Emperor Gao ascended the throne, Anren became Central General-in-Chief and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Kangle.

entries.zh: 自宋泰始以來，內外頻有賊寇，將帥以下，各募部曲，屯聚都下。
entries.en: Since the Taishi era of Song, rebels and invaders had frequently appeared inside and outside the realm. Commanders and generals down the ranks each recruited retainers and gathered them in garrisons around the capital.
entries.literal: Since the Taishi era of Song, there had frequently been rebels and invaders inside and outside the realm, and commanders and generals down the ranks each recruited retainers and gathered them in garrisons around the capital.

entries.zh: 安人上表，以為自非淮北常備，其外餘軍悉皆輸遣，若親近宜立隨身者，聽限人數。
entries.en: Anren submitted a memorial saying that except for the standing defenses north of the Huai, all other troops should be sent away. If close attendants needed personal followers, the number should be limited.
entries.literal: Anren submitted a memorial saying that except for the standing defenses north of the Huai, all other remaining troops should be sent away; if close attendants needed to establish personal followers, the number should be limited.

entries.zh: 上納之，故詔斷眾募。
entries.en: The emperor accepted this, and an edict cut off the many recruitments.
entries.literal: The emperor accepted this, and so an edict cut off the many recruitments.

entries.zh: 時王敬則以勳誠見親，至於家國密事，上唯與安人論議。
entries.en: At the time Wang Jingze was treated with intimacy because of his merit and sincerity, but when it came to confidential affairs of house and state, the emperor discussed them only with Anren.
entries.literal: At the time Wang Jingze was treated with intimacy because of his merit and sincerity, but when it came to confidential affairs of house and state, the emperor discussed them only with Anren.

entries.zh: 謂曰：「署事有卿名，我便不復細覽也。」
entries.en: He told him, "If your name is on a signed matter, I no longer examine it in detail."
entries.literal: He told him, "If your name is on a signed matter, I no longer examine it in detail."

entries.zh: 尋為領軍將軍。
entries.en: Soon he became General-in-Chief.
entries.literal: Soon he became General-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 魏攻壽春至馬頭，詔安人禦之，魏軍退，安人沿淮進壽春。
entries.en: When Wei attacked Shouchun and reached Matou, an edict ordered Anren to resist them. The Wei army withdrew, and Anren advanced along the Huai to Shouchun.
entries.literal: When Wei attacked Shouchun and reached Matou, an edict ordered Anren to resist them; the Wei army withdrew, and Anren advanced along the Huai to Shouchun.

entries.zh: 先是宋時亡命王元初聚黨六合山，僭大號。
entries.en: Earlier, during Song, the fugitive Wang Yuanchu had gathered followers at Liuhe Mountain and usurped a grand title.
entries.literal: Earlier, during Song, the fugitive Wang Yuanchu had gathered followers at Liuhe Mountain and usurped a grand title.

entries.zh: 自雲垂手過膝。
entries.en: He claimed that when he lowered his hands they passed his knees.
entries.literal: He claimed that when he lowered his hands they passed his knees.

entries.zh: 州郡討不能禽，積十餘年。
entries.en: The provinces and commanderies campaigned against him but could not capture him, and this went on for more than ten years.
entries.literal: The provinces and commanderies campaigned against him but could not capture him, and this went on for more than ten years.

entries.zh: 安人生禽之，斬建康市。
entries.en: Anren captured him alive and beheaded him in the Jiankang marketplace.
entries.literal: Anren captured him alive and beheaded him in the Jiankang marketplace.

entries.zh: 高帝崩，遺詔加侍中。
entries.en: When Emperor Gao died, his final edict added the office of Attendant-in-Ordinary to Anren.
entries.literal: When Emperor Gao died, his final edict added the office of Attendant-in-Ordinary to Anren.

entries.zh: 武帝即位，為丹陽尹，遷尚書左僕射。
entries.en: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, Anren became Intendant of Danyang and was transferred to Left Director of the Masters of Writing.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, Anren became Intendant of Danyang and was transferred to Left Director of the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 安人時屢啟密謀見賞，又善結尚書令王儉，故世傳儉啟有此授。
entries.en: At the time Anren was repeatedly rewarded for submitting secret plans and was also good at forming ties with Wang Jian, Director of the Masters of Writing, so people said that Jian had recommended this appointment.
entries.literal: At the time Anren was repeatedly rewarded for submitting secret plans and was also good at forming ties with Wang Jian, Director of the Masters of Writing, so people said that Jian had recommended this appointment.

entries.zh: 尋上表，以年疾求退，為吳興太守。
entries.en: Soon he submitted a memorial requesting retirement because of age and illness, and he became Administrator of Wuxing.
entries.literal: Soon he submitted a memorial requesting retirement because of age and illness, and he became Administrator of Wuxing.

entries.zh: 于家載米往郡，時服其清。
entries.en: He loaded rice from his own household to take to the commandery, and people of the time admired his purity.
entries.literal: He loaded rice from his own household to take to the commandery, and people of the time admired his purity.

entries.zh: 吳興有項羽神護郡聽事，太守到郡，必須祀以軛下牛。
entries.en: In Wuxing there was a spirit of Xiang Yu that guarded the commandery audience hall. When an administrator arrived in the commandery, he had to sacrifice a yoke-ox to it.
entries.literal: In Wuxing there was a spirit of Xiang Yu that guarded the commandery audience hall; when an administrator arrived in the commandery, he had to sacrifice a yoke-ox to it.

entries.zh: 安人奉佛法，不與神牛，著屐上聽事，又於聽上八關齋。
entries.en: Anren followed the Buddhist law and did not give the spirit an ox. Wearing clogs, he went up into the audience hall and also held an Eight Precepts fast there.
entries.literal: Anren followed the Buddhist law and did not give the spirit an ox; wearing clogs, he went up into the audience hall and also held an Eight Precepts fast there.

entries.zh: 俄而牛死葬廟側，今呼為李公牛塚。
entries.en: Soon afterward the ox died and was buried beside the shrine; it is now called Lord Li's Ox Mound.
entries.literal: Soon afterward the ox died and was buried beside the shrine; it is now called Lord Li's Ox Mound.

entries.zh: 安人尋卒，世以神為祟。
entries.en: Anren died soon afterward, and people of the age thought the spirit had brought calamity on him.
entries.literal: Anren died soon afterward, and people of the age thought the spirit had brought calamity on him.

entries.zh: 諡肅侯。
entries.en: His posthumous title was Marquis Su.
entries.literal: His posthumous title was Marquis Su.

entries.zh: 子元履，幼有操業，甚閑政體，為司徒竟陵王子良法曹參軍。
entries.en: His son Yuanlü showed discipline from boyhood and a keen grasp of government procedure; he served as Legal Bureau Attendant to Prince Ziliang of Jingling, the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: His son Yuanlü, from childhood possessed moral conduct and was thoroughly versed in administrative forms; he served as Legal Bureau Attendant to the Prince of Jingling, the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 與王融遊狎，及王融誅，郁林敕元履隨右衛將軍王廣之北征，密令於北殺之。
entries.en: He was intimate with Wang Rong; after Wang Rong's execution, Emperor Yulin ordered Yuanlü to accompany Right Guard General Wang Guangzhi northward, secretly commanding that he be killed on the road.
entries.literal: He associated closely with Wang Rong; when Wang Rong was executed, Emperor Yulin ordered Yuanlü to follow the Right Guard General Wang Guangzhi on the northern campaign, secretly instructing him to kill Yuanlü in the north.

entries.zh: 廣之先為安人所厚，又知元履無過，甚擁護之。
entries.en: Wang Guangzhi had once owed much to Li Anren and knew Yuanlü was innocent, so he shielded him with all his might.
entries.literal: Guangzhi had earlier been greatly favored by Anren and knew Yuanlü was guiltless, so he protected him zealously.

entries.zh: 會郁林敗死，元履拜謝廣之，曰：「二十二載，父母之年，自此以外，丈人之賜也。」
entries.en: When Emperor Yulin met his downfall, Yuanlü thanked Wang Guangzhi and said, "Twenty-two years—the span my parents might have wished for me; anything beyond that I owe to you, sir."
entries.literal: When Emperor Yulin fell and died, Yuanlü bowed in thanks to Guangzhi and said, "Twenty-two years—the years of my parents; beyond that, it is the gift of my elder."

entries.zh: 仕梁為吳郡太守，度支尚書，衡、廣、青、冀四州刺史。
entries.en: Under Liang he rose to Administrator of Wu commandery, Minister of Revenue, and Inspector of Heng, Guang, Qing, and Ji provinces.
entries.literal: He served Liang as Administrator of Wu commandery, Minister of Revenue, and Inspector of the four provinces Heng, Guang, Qing, and Ji.

entries.zh: 沈攸之事起，高帝入朝堂，遣僧靜將腹心先至石頭經略袁粲。
entries.en: When Shen Youzhi rebelled, Emperor Gao went to court and sent Dai Sengjing with his closest followers to secure Stone City against Yuan Can.
entries.literal: When Shen Youzhi's affair arose, the Emperor Gao entered the audience hall and sent Sengjing with his trusted men ahead to Stone City to deal with Yuan Can.

entries.zh: 時蘇烈據倉城門，僧靜射書與烈，夜縋入城。
entries.en: Su Lie then held Cangcheng Gate. Dai Sengjing shot an arrow bearing a message to Lie and was hauled over the wall at night.
entries.literal: At that time Su Lie held Cangcheng Gate; Sengjing shot a letter to Lie and was lowered into the city by rope at night.

entries.zh: 粲登城西南門，列燭火坐，台軍至射之，火乃滅。
entries.en: Yuan Can took the southwest gate, set out rows of candles, and sat; when the imperial troops shot, every flame died.
entries.literal: Can mounted the southwest gate of the city, arrayed candles and sat; when the palace troops arrived and shot, the flames went out.

entries.zh: 回登東門，其党孫曇瓘驍勇善戰，每蕩一合，輒大殺傷，官軍死者百餘人。
entries.en: He went back to the east gate. His ally Sun Tanxun fought with terrifying skill: every clash left a great heap of dead, and over a hundred imperial soldiers fell.
entries.literal: He returned to the east gate; his partisan Sun Tanxun was fierce and skilled in battle—each time he swept through a formation he inflicted heavy slaughter, and more than a hundred government soldiers died.

entries.zh: 軍主王天生殊死拒戰，故得相持。
entries.en: Commander Wang Tiansheng held him off with suicidal courage, and the fight hung in balance.
entries.literal: The army commander Wang Tiansheng resisted with desperate valor, and thus they were able to stalemate each other.

entries.zh: 自亥至醜，有流星赤色照地墜城中，僧靜率力攻倉門，手斬粲於東門，外軍燒門入。
entries.en: From hai to chou a crimson meteor flamed down into the city. Dai Sengjing stormed Cang Gate, cut down Yuan Can with his own hand at the east gate, and the outer force burned its way in.
entries.literal: From the hai hour to the chou hour a crimson meteor blazed to the ground inside the city; Sengjing led his force in assault on Cang Gate, personally beheaded Can at the east gate, and the outer army burned the gate and entered.

entries.zh: 以功除前軍將軍、甯朔將軍。
entries.en: For this service he was made General of the Vanguard and General Who Pacifies the North.
entries.literal: For his merit he was appointed General of the Vanguard and General Who Pacifies the North.

entries.zh: 高帝即位，封建昌縣侯，位太子左衛率。
entries.en: When Emperor Gao ascended the throne, Sengjing was enfeoffed as Marquis of Jianchang County and held the office of Left Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guards.
entries.literal: When Emperor Gao ascended the throne, Sengjing was enfeoffed as Marquis of Jianchang County and held the office of Left Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guards.

entries.zh: 武帝踐阼，出為北徐州刺史。
entries.en: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, Sengjing went out as Inspector of Northern Xuzhou.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, Sengjing went out as Inspector of Northern Xuzhou.

entries.zh: 買牛給貧人令耕種，甚得荒情。
entries.en: He bought oxen and gave them to poor people so they could plow and plant, and greatly won the hearts of the famine-stricken.
entries.literal: He bought oxen and gave them to poor people so they could plow and plant, and greatly won the hearts of the famine-stricken.

entries.zh: 後除南中郎司馬、淮南太守。
entries.en: Later he was appointed Sima of the Southern Gentlemen-of-the-Household and Administrator of Huainan.
entries.literal: Later he was appointed Sima of the Southern Gentlemen-of-the-Household and Administrator of Huainan.

entries.zh: 永明八年，巴東王子響殺僚佐，武帝召僧靜使領軍向江陵。
entries.en: In the eighth year of Yongming, Prince Xiang of Badong murdered his officials. Emperor Wu ordered Dai Sengjing to take command and march on Jiangling.
entries.literal: In the eighth year of Yongming, Prince Xiang of Badong killed his staff officers; Emperor Wu summoned Sengjing to lead the army toward Jiangling.

entries.zh: 僧靜面啟上曰：「巴東王年少，長史司馬捉之太急，忿不思難故耳。
entries.en: Dai Sengjing spoke plainly: "Prince Xiang of Badong is young. His chief administrator and staff supervisor seized him too roughly; in anger he struck without weighing the cost.
entries.literal: Sengjing addressed the throne face to face, saying, "The Prince of Badong is young; the Chief Administrator and Staff Supervisor pressed him too hard, and in resentment he acted without thinking of the consequences.

entries.zh: 天子兒過誤殺人，有何大罪，今急遣軍西上，人情惶懼，無所不至。
entries.en: A son of the emperor who kills in a moment of passion—what capital crime is that? Dispatch an army west in haste and fear will spread everywhere.
entries.literal: When a Son of Heaven's son kills someone in a passing error, what great crime is there? Now to rush troops westward will fill every heart with panic beyond measure.

entries.zh: 臣不敢奉敕。」
entries.en: I dare not obey this order."
entries.literal: Your servant dares not accept the command."

entries.zh: 上不答而心善之。
entries.en: The emperor gave no reply yet was pleased in his heart.
entries.literal: The emperor did not answer but inwardly approved of him.

entries.zh: 徙廬陵王中軍司馬、高平太守。
entries.en: He was moved to Staff Major to the Prince of Luling and Administrator of Gaoping.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Staff Major to the Prince of Luling and Administrator of Gaoping.

entries.zh: 卒，諡壯侯。
entries.en: He died and received the posthumous title Marquis Zhuang.
entries.literal: He died and was given the posthumous title Marquis Zhuang.

entries.zh: 桓康，北蘭陵承人也。
entries.en: Huan Kang came from Cheng in North Lanling.
entries.literal: Huan Kang was a native of Cheng in North Lanling.

entries.zh: 勇果驍悍。
entries.en: He was courageous, fierce, and terrifying in battle.
entries.literal: He was brave, resolute, fierce, and formidable.

entries.zh: 宋大明中，隨齊高帝為軍容，從武帝在贛縣。
entries.en: In Emperor Xiaoming's Daming reign he served Emperor Gao of Qi as army retainer and followed Emperor Wu at Gan County.
entries.literal: During the Daming era of Song he followed Emperor Gao of Qi as army retainer and accompanied Emperor Wu at Gan County.

entries.zh: 泰始初，武帝起義，為郡所縶，眾皆散。
entries.en: When Emperor Wu first raised arms at the opening of Taishi, the commandery seized him and his followers scattered.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Taishi, Emperor Wu raised the righteous army and was bound by the commandery; the crowd all scattered.

entries.zh: 康裝擔，一頭貯穆後，一頭貯文惠太子及竟陵王子良，自負置山中。
entries.en: Huan Kang shouldered two carrying-poles: one basket held Empress Mu, the other Crown Prince Wenhuai and Prince Ziliang of Jingling, and he bore them into the hills.
entries.literal: Kang loaded two carrying-poles—one basket held Empress Mu, the other held Crown Prince Wenhuai and Prince Ziliang of Jingling—and bore them on his shoulders into the mountains.

entries.zh: 及閘客蕭欣祖等四十餘人相結，破郡獄，出武帝。
entries.en: He and over forty men, among them the gate guest Xiao Xingu, broke the jail and brought Emperor Wu out.
entries.literal: Together with more than forty men including the gate guest Xiao Xingu, they joined forces, broke the commandery prison, and freed Emperor Wu.

entries.zh: 郡追兵急，康等死戰破之。
entries.en: Pursuit from the commandery was hot; Huan Kang and his band fought to the death and smashed through.
entries.literal: The commandery pursuit was urgent; Kang and the others fought to the death and broke through.

entries.zh: 隨武帝起兵，摧堅陷陣，膂力絕人。
entries.en: He marched with Emperor Wu, tore through defenses, and possessed strength beyond any other man.
entries.literal: Following Emperor Wu in raising troops, he stormed strongpoints and shattered formations; his physical strength was unmatched.

entries.zh: 所經村邑，恣行暴害，江南人畏之，以其名怖小兒，畫其形於寺中。
entries.en: Every hamlet he entered suffered his violence. Jiangnan feared him; parents painted his figure in temples to scare children.
entries.literal: In every village he passed he committed outrages at will; the people of Jiangnan feared him and used his name to frighten small children, painting his likeness in temples.

entries.zh: 病瘧者寫形帖著床壁，無不立愈。
entries.en: Those with malaria who posted his portrait by the bed were said to recover at once.
entries.literal: Malaria sufferers who copied his image and pasted it on the bed wall were all instantly cured.

entries.zh: 建元元年，封吳平縣侯。
entries.en: In the first year of Jianyuan he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wuiping.
entries.literal: In the first year of Jianyuan he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wuiping County.

entries.zh: 高帝謂康曰：「卿隨我日久，未得方伯，亦當未解我意，正欲與卿先共滅虜耳。」
entries.en: Emperor Gao told him, "You have served me for years without a provincial post—you may still not grasp my meaning: I meant to crush the northern enemy with you first."
entries.literal: Emperor Gao said to Kang, "You have followed me long without receiving a regional command—I suppose you still do not understand my intent; I simply wished first to destroy the barbarians together with you."

entries.zh: 三年，魏軍動，康大破魏軍于淮陽。
entries.en: the third year of In the Wei advanced; at Huaiyang Huan Kang routed them utterly.
entries.literal: In the third year the Wei army moved; Kang inflicted a great defeat on the Wei army at Huaiyang.

entries.zh: 武帝即位，卒于驍騎將軍。
entries.en: After Emperor Wu ascended the throne, Huan Kang died in office as General of Valiant Cavalry.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu took the throne, Kang died while General of Valiant Cavalry.

entries.zh: 為人樸澀，欲就高帝求州，比及見，竟不涉一語。
entries.en: Simple and awkward, he meant to beg Emperor Gao for a provincial post, yet when they met he never broached the topic.
entries.literal: By nature he was plain and dull; he wished to ask Emperor Gao for a province, but when he came before him he did not manage a single word on the subject.

entries.zh: 帝以其不閑政事，竟不用。
entries.en: The emperor judged him unfit for civil rule and gave him nothing.
entries.literal: The emperor, seeing he was unskilled in government affairs, in the end did not employ him.

entries.zh: 後求竟陵郡，不知所以置辭，親人授之辭百餘言，度習誦數日，皆得上口。
entries.en: He later sought Jingling commandery. Unable to frame a petition, relatives coached him in a speech of a hundred-odd lines; he drilled for days until it flowed.
entries.literal: Later he sought Jingling commandery but did not know how to phrase his request; kinsmen supplied him with a speech of more than a hundred words, which Du studied for several days until he could recite it fluently.

entries.zh: 會高帝履行石頭城，度於大眾中欲自陳，臨時卒忘所教，乃大言曰：「度啟公，度啟公，度無食。」
entries.en: During an imperial tour of Stone City, Jiao Du tried to address the court in public, forgot every coached line, and blurted, "Du reports, my lord—Du reports—Du has no food!"
entries.literal: When Emperor Gao was inspecting Stone City, Du wished to speak before the crowd but at the last moment forgot what he had been taught and cried out loudly, "Du reports to my lord, Du reports to my lord—Du has no food."

entries.zh: 帝笑曰：「卿何憂無食。」
entries.en: The emperor laughed. "Why fear hunger?"
entries.literal: The emperor laughed and said, "Why should you worry about having no food?"

entries.zh: 即賜米百斛。
entries.en: He granted a hundred piculs of grain on the spot.
entries.literal: He immediately granted a hundred piculs of grain.

entries.zh: 建元四年，乃除淮陵太守。
entries.en: Only in the fourth year of Jianyuan was he named Administrator of Huailing.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Jianyuan he was at last appointed Administrator of Huailing.

entries.zh: 性好酒，醉輒暴怒，上常使人節之。
entries.en: He drank heavily; in his cups he turned savage, and the throne repeatedly sent men to curb him.
entries.literal: He loved wine by nature; drunk he would fly into violent rage, and the emperor often sent men to restrain him.

entries.zh: 年雖老而氣力如故，除遊擊將軍，卒。
entries.en: Age did not sap his strength. He was made General Who Roams in Attack, then died.
entries.literal: Though old in years his strength was as before; he was appointed General Who Roams in Attack and died.

entries.zh: 曹武字士威，下邳人也。
entries.en: Cao Wu, styled Shiwei, was a man of Xiapi.
entries.literal: Cao Wu, styled Shiwei, was a man of Xiapi.

entries.zh: 本名虎頭。
entries.en: His original name was Hutou.
entries.literal: His original name was Hutou.

entries.zh: 齊高帝鎮東府，使武與戴僧靜各領白直三百人。
entries.en: When Emperor Gao of Qi garrisoned the Eastern Headquarters, he had Wu and Dai Sengjing each command three hundred white-duty guards.
entries.literal: When Emperor Gao of Qi garrisoned the Eastern Headquarters, he had Wu and Dai Sengjing each command three hundred white-duty guards.

entries.zh: 後為屯騎校尉，帶南城令。
entries.en: Later Wu became Colonel of Garrison Cavalry and concurrently Magistrate of Nancheng.
entries.literal: Later Wu became Colonel of Garrison Cavalry and concurrently Magistrate of Nancheng.

entries.zh: 石頭平，封羅江縣男。
entries.en: When Stone Fort was pacified, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Luojiang County.
entries.literal: When Stone Fort was pacified, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Luojiang County.

entries.zh: 及高帝受禪，改封監利縣。
entries.en: When Emperor Gao received the abdication, Wu's fief was changed to Jianli County.
entries.literal: When Emperor Gao received the abdication, Wu's fief was changed to Jianli County.

entries.zh: 武帝即位，累遷驍騎將軍。
entries.en: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, Wu rose through successive promotions to General of Agile Cavalry.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, Wu was repeatedly promoted, reaching General of Agile Cavalry.

entries.zh: 帝以虎頭名鄙，敕改之。
entries.en: The emperor considered the name Hutou vulgar and ordered him to change it.
entries.literal: The emperor considered the name Hutou vulgar and ordered him to change it.

entries.zh: 郁林即位，進號前將軍。
entries.en: When Yulin ascended the throne, Wu's title was advanced to General of the Van.
entries.literal: When Yulin ascended the throne, Wu's title was advanced to General of the Van.

entries.zh: 隆昌元年，為雍州刺史。
entries.en: In the first year of Longchang, he became Inspector of Yongzhou.
entries.literal: In the first year of Longchang, he became Inspector of Yongzhou.

entries.zh: 建武二年，進爵為侯。
entries.en: In the second year of Jianwu (495), his title was advanced to marquis.
entries.literal: In the second year of Jianwu, his title was advanced to marquis.

entries.zh: 東昏即位，為前將軍、鎮軍司馬。
entries.en: When Donghun ascended the throne, Wu became General of the Van and Sima of the Pacifying Army.
entries.literal: When Donghun ascended the throne, Wu became General of the Van and Sima of the Pacifying Army.

entries.zh: 永元元年，始安王遙光反，武領軍屯青溪大橋，事寧，轉散騎常侍、右衛將軍。
entries.en: In the first year of Yongyuan (499), when Prince Yaoguang of Shi'an rebelled, Wu led troops to garrison the Qingxi Great Bridge. When the affair was pacified, he was transferred to Cavalier Attendant and General of the Right Guard.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongyuan, when Prince Yaoguang of Shi'an rebelled, Wu led troops to garrison the Qingxi Great Bridge; when the affair was pacified, he was transferred to Cavalier Attendant and General of the Right Guard.

entries.zh: 呂安國
entries.en: Lu Anguo
entries.literal: Lu Anguo

entries.zh: 宋大明末，以將領見任，隱重有幹局，為劉勉所稱。
entries.en: At the end of the Daming era of Song, Anguo was employed as a military commander. He was reserved, grave, capable, and organized, and was praised by Liu Mian.
entries.literal: At the end of the Daming era of Song, Anguo was employed as a military commander; he was reserved, grave, capable, and organized, and was praised by Liu Mian.

entries.zh: 泰始二年，為勉軍副，征殷琰，以功封鍾武縣男。
entries.en: In the second year of Taishi, he served as deputy in Mian's army and campaigned against Yin Yan; for his merit he was enfeoffed as Baron of Zhongwu County.
entries.literal: In the second year of Taishi, he served as deputy in Mian's army and campaigned against Yin Yan; for his merit he was enfeoffed as Baron of Zhongwu County.

entries.zh: 累遷兗州刺史。
entries.en: He rose through successive promotions to Inspector of Yanzhou.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly promoted, reaching Inspector of Yanzhou.

entries.zh: 及沈攸之事起，齊高帝以安國為湘州刺史。
entries.en: When Shen Youzhi rose in revolt, Emperor Gao of Qi made Anguo Inspector of Xiangzhou.
entries.literal: When the affair of Shen Youzhi arose, Emperor Gao of Qi made Anguo Inspector of Xiangzhou.

entries.zh: 建元元年，進爵為侯，轉右衛將軍，加給事中。
entries.en: In the first year of Jianyuan (479), his title was advanced to marquis, he was transferred to General of the Right Guard, and the office of Palace Attendant was added.
entries.literal: In the first year of Jianyuan, his title was advanced to marquis, he was transferred to General of the Right Guard, and the office of Palace Attendant was added.

entries.zh: 後改封湘鄉侯。
entries.en: Later his fief was changed to Marquis of Xiangxiang.
entries.literal: Later his fief was changed to Marquis of Xiangxiang.

entries.zh: 武帝即位，累遷光祿大夫，加散騎常侍。
entries.en: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, Anguo rose through successive promotions to Grandee of Splendid Happiness, with the added office of Cavalier Attendant.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, Anguo was repeatedly promoted to Grandee of Splendid Happiness, with the added office of Cavalier Attendant.

entries.zh: 齊高帝輔政，山圖密啟沈攸之久有異圖，宜為之備。
entries.en: As regent, Emperor Gao of Qi received Shantu's secret report that Shen Youzhi had long plotted rebellion and must be watched.
entries.literal: When Emperor Gao of Qi held the regency, Shantu secretly reported that Shen Youzhi had long harbored a different design and ought to be guarded against.

entries.zh: 帝笑而納之。
entries.en: The emperor smiled and took the warning to heart.
entries.literal: The emperor smiled and accepted it.

entries.zh: 攸之事起，武帝為西討都督，啟山圖為軍副。
entries.en: When Youzhi rebelled, Emperor Wu commanded the western campaign and named Shantu his deputy.
entries.literal: When Youzhi's affair arose, Emperor Wu was Western Campaign Commander-in-Chief and requested Shantu as army deputy.

entries.zh: 攸之攻郢城，武帝令山圖量其形勢。
entries.en: Youzhi besieged Ying; Emperor Wu asked Shantu to read the field.
entries.literal: Youzhi attacked Ying City; Emperor Wu ordered Shantu to assess the situation.

entries.zh: 山圖曰：「攸之為人，性度險刻，無以結固士心。
entries.en: Shantu said, "Youzhi is harsh by nature and cannot bind his officers' loyalty.
entries.literal: Shantu said, "Youzhi as a man is by nature harsh and cutting and cannot firmly bind the hearts of his officers.

entries.zh: 如頓兵堅城之下，適所以為離散之漸耳。」
entries.en: Pin him under a strong wall and his host will melt away."
entries.literal: If he camps his host under a strong city, that will only hasten their scattering."

entries.zh: 及攸之敗，高帝謂曰：「周公前言，可謂明於見事矣。」
entries.en: After Youzhi's fall, Emperor Gao said, "Your forecast showed true foresight."
entries.literal: When Youzhi was defeated, Emperor Gao said, "Your earlier words can be called clear-sighted in reading events."

entries.zh: 建元元年，封晉興縣男。
entries.en: In the first year of Jianyuan (479), Shantu was enfeoffed as Baron of Jinxing County.
entries.literal: In the first year of Jianyuan, Shantu was enfeoffed as Baron of Jinxing County.

entries.zh: 武帝踐阼，遷竟陵王鎮北司馬，帶南平昌太守。
entries.en: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, Shantu was transferred to Sima of the Prince of Jingling's Army That Guards the North and concurrently Administrator of Southern Pingchang.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, Shantu was transferred to Sima of the Prince of Jingling's Army That Guards the North and concurrently Administrator of Southern Pingchang.

entries.zh: 以盆城之舊，出入殿省，甚見親信。
entries.en: Because of their old association at Pencheng, he entered and exited the palace offices and was deeply trusted.
entries.literal: Because of their old association at Pencheng, he entered and exited the palace offices and was deeply trusted.

entries.zh: 義鄉縣長風廟神姓鄧，先經為縣令，死遂發靈，山圖啟乞加神位輔國將軍。
entries.en: The spirit of Changfeng Shrine in Yixiang County had the surname Deng. He had once served as county magistrate, and after death manifested numinous power, so Shantu requested that the spirit's rank be increased to General Who Assists the State.
entries.literal: The spirit of Changfeng Shrine in Yixiang County had the surname Deng; he had once served as county magistrate, and after death manifested numinous power, so Shantu submitted a request that the spirit's rank be increased to General Who Assists the State.

entries.zh: 上答曰：「足狗肉便了事，何用階級為。」
entries.en: The emperor replied, "Enough dog meat will settle the matter; what use is rank?"
entries.literal: The emperor replied, "Enough dog meat will settle the matter; what use is rank?"

entries.zh: 永明五年，為大司馬，加征虜將軍、濟陽太守。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Yongming he became Grand Marshal, with added rank as General Who Subdues the Barbarians and Administrator of Jiyang.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Yongming he was made Grand Marshal, with the additional titles General Who Subdues the Barbarians and Administrator of Jiyang.

entries.zh: 武帝數講武，嘗令盤龍領馬軍，校騎騁矟。
entries.en: The emperor often held war games and had Panlong lead the horse corps in spear drills.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu often held martial lectures and would have Panlong lead the cavalry, comparing horses in spear charges.

entries.zh: 後以疾，為光祿大夫。
entries.en: Illness later made him Grand Master of the Palace.
