entries.literal: Later because of illness he was made Grand Master of the Palace.

entries.zh: 還為散騎常侍、光祿大夫。
entries.en: He returned as Regular Attendant and Grand Master of the Palace.
entries.literal: On return he was made Regular Attendant and Grand Master of the Palace.

entries.zh: 武帝戲之曰：「卿著貂蟬，何如兜鍪？」
entries.en: The emperor teased him: "You wear court finery—how is that like a helm?"
entries.literal: Emperor Wu jested with him, saying, "You wear the cicada and fur finial—how does that compare to a helmet?"

entries.zh: 盤龍曰：「此貂蟬從兜鍪中生耳。」
entries.en: Panlong answered, "This finery grew out of the helmet."
entries.literal: Panlong said, "This finery was born from the helmet."

entries.zh: 尋病卒，年七十九。
entries.en: He soon died of illness, aged seventy-nine.
entries.literal: Soon he died of illness at age seventy-nine.

entries.zh: 子奉叔，勇力絕人，少隨盤龍征討，所在暴掠。
entries.en: His son Fengshu possessed matchless strength. From youth he campaigned with Panlong and looted wherever he marched.
entries.literal: His son Fengshu had strength surpassing others; from youth he followed Panlong on campaigns and wherever he went he plundered violently.

entries.zh: 為東宮直合將軍。
entries.en: He became Direct Guard General of the Eastern Palace.
entries.literal: He was Direct Guard General of the Eastern Palace.

entries.zh: 郁林在西州，奉叔密得自進，及即位，與直合將軍曹道剛為心膂。
entries.en: While Yulin was heir in the Western Quarter, Fengshu found private access to him. On Yulin's accession he and Cao Daogang became the emperor's inner circle.
entries.literal: When Yulin was in the Western Quarter, Fengshu secretly gained access to present himself; when Yulin took the throne he and Direct Guard General Cao Daogang became his inner confidants.

entries.zh: 奉叔善騎馬，帝從其學騎，尤見親寵，得入內，無所忌憚。
entries.en: Fengshu rode superbly; the emperor learned horsemanship from him and favored him so that he entered the inner palace without restraint.
entries.literal: Fengshu was skilled at riding horses; the emperor learned riding from him and favored him especially, gaining entry within the palace without restraint or fear.

entries.zh: 陵轢朝士，就司空王敬則換米二百斛，敬則以百斛與之，不受。
entries.en: He bullied officials. Demanding two hundred piculs of grain from Wang Jingze, he refused the hundred piculs offered.
entries.literal: He bullied court gentlemen; he went to Minister of Works Wang Jingze to exchange for two hundred piculs of grain; Jingze gave him one hundred piculs and he would not accept it.

entries.zh: 敬則大懼，乃更餉二百斛並金鉿等物。
entries.en: Terrified, Jingze sent another two hundred piculs plus gold hairpins and gifts.
entries.literal: Jingze was greatly afraid and therefore sent another two hundred piculs together with gold hairpins and other objects.

entries.zh: 敬則有一內妓，帝令奉叔求。
entries.en: Jingze kept a palace woman; the emperor ordered Fengshu to take her.
entries.literal: Jingze had a palace concubine; the emperor ordered Fengshu to demand her.

entries.zh: 奉叔不通徑前，從者執單刀皆半拔，敬則跣走入內。
entries.en: Fengshu stormed in without ceremony, followers' blades half drawn. Jingze fled barefoot indoors.
entries.literal: Fengshu would not go by the proper path; his followers drew single blades half unsheathed; Jingze ran in barefoot into the inner quarters.

entries.zh: 既而自計不免，乃出，遙呼奉叔曰：「弟那忽能顧？」
entries.en: Seeing escape impossible, he came out and called, "Brother, how can you treat me so?"
entries.literal: Then calculating he could not escape, he came out and called from afar to Fengshu, "Younger brother, how could you suddenly turn on me?"

entries.zh: 奉叔宣旨求妓意，乃得釋。
entries.en: Fengshu stated the imperial demand for the woman, and Jingze was spared.
entries.literal: Fengshu announced the imperial intent seeking the concubine, and only then was he released.

entries.zh: 與綦母珍、曹道剛、朱隆之共相唇齒，煽弄威權。
entries.en: With Qi Mu Zhen, Cao Daogang, and Zhu Longzhi he formed a clique that twisted power at will.
entries.literal: With Qi Mu Zhen, Cao Daogang, and Zhu Longzhi they were like lips and teeth, fanning and wielding authority.

entries.zh: 奉叔常翼單刀二十口，出入禁闈，既無別詔，門衛莫敢訶。
entries.en: He routinely carried twenty swords through the forbidden gates; without a special edict guards dared not stop him.
entries.literal: Fengshu commonly carried twenty single blades at his side entering and leaving the forbidden gates; as there was no separate edict, the gate guards dared not challenge him.

entries.zh: 每語人云：「周郎刀不識君。」
entries.en: He would say, "Young Zhou's blade knows no master but me."
entries.literal: He often told people, "Young Zhou's blade does not know you."

entries.zh: 求武帝御角及輿，並求禦仗以給左右。
entries.en: He demanded the emperor's horn bow, carriage, and imperial arms for his men.
entries.literal: He sought the emperor's horn bow and carriage and also sought imperial arms to supply his attendants.

entries.zh: 事無不從。
entries.en: Nothing was refused.
entries.literal: In affairs nothing was refused him.

entries.zh: 又求黃門郎，明帝作輔，固執不能得，乃令蕭諶、蕭坦之說帝出奉叔為外鎮，樹腹心。
entries.en: He sought Palace Attendant rank; regent Emperor Ming refused. Xiao Chen and Xiao Tanzhi then persuaded the emperor to post Fengshu abroad and plant a loyal man within.
entries.literal: He also sought the post of Palace Attendant; when Emperor Ming was regent he firmly would not grant it; then he had Xiao Chen and Xiao Tanzhi persuade the emperor to send Fengshu out to a frontier command and plant a trusted man in his place.

entries.zh: 又說奉叔以方伯之重，奉叔納其言。
entries.en: They flattered him with a provincial command; he agreed.
entries.literal: They also persuaded Fengshu with the weight of a regional command; Fengshu accepted their words.

entries.zh: 隆昌元年，出為青、冀二州刺史。
entries.en: In the first year of Longchang he was sent out as Inspector of Qing and Ji.
entries.literal: In the first year of Longchang he went out as Inspector of Qing and Ji provinces.

entries.zh: 奉叔就帝求千戶侯，帝許之。
entries.en: He asked the throne for a thousand-household marquisate; the emperor agreed.
entries.literal: Fengshu asked the emperor for a marquisate of one thousand households; the emperor consented.

entries.zh: 明帝以為不可。
entries.en: Emperor Ming objected.
entries.literal: Emperor Ming thought it could not be done.

entries.zh: 忽謂蕭諶曰：「若不能見與千戶侯，不復應減五百戶；
entries.en: He told Xiao Chen sharply, "Deny me a thousand-household marquis and I will not take five hundred less either;
entries.literal: Suddenly he said to Xiao Chen, "If you cannot give me a thousand-household marquisate, I will not accept even five hundred households being reduced;

entries.zh: 不爾，周郎當就刀頭取辦耳。」
entries.en: or Young Zhou will settle it at sword point."
entries.literal: otherwise Young Zhou will settle the matter at the blade's point."

entries.zh: 既而封曲江縣男，奉叔大怒，於眾中攘刀，厲目切齒。
entries.en: He was given only Viscount of Qujiang. Fengshu raged, drew his blade in the assembly, glaring and gnashing his teeth.
entries.literal: Soon he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Qujiang; Fengshu was furious and in the crowd brandished his blade, glaring and grinding his teeth.

entries.zh: 明帝說諭乃受。
entries.en: Emperor Ming talked him down before he accepted.
entries.literal: Emperor Ming persuaded and instructed him and only then did he accept.

entries.zh: 及將之鎮，明帝慮其不可復製，因其早入，引往後堂，執送廷尉盡之。
entries.en: Before he could depart, Emperor Ming feared losing control. Lured early to the rear hall, he was seized and executed to the last man at court.
entries.literal: When he was about to go to his command, Emperor Ming feared he could not be controlled again; because he entered early, he was led to the rear hall, seized, and sent to the Minister of Justice, where he was executed to the last man.

entries.zh: 王廣之字士林，一字林之，沛郡相人也。
entries.en: Wang Guangzhi, courtesy names Shilin and Linzhi, came from Xiang in Pei commandery.
entries.literal: Wang Guangzhi, style Shilin, also styled Linzhi, was a native of Xiang in Pei commandery.

entries.zh: 少好弓馬，便捷有勇力。
entries.en: From youth he loved bow and horse, was quick, brave, and strong.
entries.literal: From youth he loved bow and horse; he was nimble and possessed courage and strength.

entries.zh: 初為馬隊主，隨劉勉征殷琰。
entries.en: He began as horse detachment chief under Liu Mian against Yin Yan.
entries.literal: At first he was chief of a horse detachment and followed Liu Mian in campaigning against Yin Yan.

entries.zh: 兵既盛而合肥戍又阻兵為寇。
entries.en: The army was strong, but the Hefei garrison also blocked them as enemies.
entries.literal: The army was already strong yet the Hefei garrison also blocked the army as bandits.

entries.zh: 勉宣令軍中求征合肥者，以大郡賞之。
entries.en: Mian called for volunteers to take Hefei, promising a great commandery as prize.
entries.literal: Mian proclaimed throughout the army seeking one to campaign against Hefei, with a great commandery as reward.

entries.zh: 廣之曰：「若得將軍所乘馬，判能制之。」
entries.en: Guangzhi said, "Give me the general's own horse and I will take it."
entries.literal: Guangzhi said, "If I obtain the general's own mount, I can surely subdue it."

entries.zh: 勉幢主皇甫肅謂勉曰：「廣之敢奪節下馬，可斬。」
entries.en: Mian's banner chief Huangfu Su said, "Guangzhi dares seize your horse—cut him down."
entries.literal: Mian's banner chief Huangfu Su said to Mian, "Guangzhi dares seize my lord's horse—he should be beheaded."

entries.zh: 勉曰：「觀其意必能立功。」
entries.en: Mian said, "He means to win glory—let him try."
entries.literal: Mian said, "Judging his intent he will surely be able to achieve merit."

entries.zh: 即推鞍下馬與之。
entries.en: He dismounted and gave him the horse.
entries.literal: He immediately pushed off the saddle and dismounted, giving the horse to him.

entries.zh: 及行，合肥果拔，勉大賞之，即擢為軍主。
entries.en: Hefei fell. Mian richly rewarded him and made him army commander at once.
entries.literal: When they marched, Hefei was indeed taken; Mian greatly rewarded him and immediately promoted him to army commander.

entries.zh: 廣之於勉前謂肅曰：「節下若從卿言，非唯斬壯士，亦自無以平賊。
entries.en: Before Mian, Guangzhi told Su, "Had your lord listened to you, he would have killed a hero and never pacified the enemy.
entries.literal: Before Mian, Guangzhi said to Su, "If my lord had followed your advice, he would not only have beheaded a stalwart but also himself have had no means to pacify the bandits.

entries.zh: 卿不賞才乃至此邪！」
entries.en: You cannot recognize talent—that is your fault!"
entries.literal: You do not reward talent and have come to this!"

entries.zh: 廣之由此知名。
entries.en: From this Guangzhi became famous.
entries.literal: Guangzhi thereby became renowned.

entries.zh: 初封蒲圻子。
entries.en: He was first enfeoffed Viscount of Puqi.
entries.literal: At first he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Puqi.

entries.zh: 肅有學術，善舉止，廣之亦雅相推慕。
entries.en: Su was learned and graceful; Guangzhi admired him sincerely.
entries.literal: Su had learning and fine deportment; Guangzhi also in refined fashion admired and looked up to him.

entries.zh: 勉亡後，肅更依廣之，廣之盛相賞接，啟武帝以為東海太守，不念舊惡如此。
entries.en: After Mian's death Su clung to Guangzhi, who favored him and recommended him to Emperor Wu as Administrator of Donghai—forgetting old quarrels.
entries.literal: After Mian died, Su again relied on Guangzhi; Guangzhi greatly favored and received him and reported to Emperor Wu to make him Administrator of Donghai—so little did he bear old grudges.

entries.zh: 廣之後以征伐功，位給事中、冠軍將軍，改封寧都縣子。
entries.en: For campaigns he became Gentleman of the Palace and General Who Vanquishes Champions, re-enfeoffed Viscount of Ningdu.
entries.literal: Later Guangzhi for campaign merit held the post of Gentleman of the Palace and General Who Vanquishes Champions and his enfeoffment was changed to Viscount of Ningdu.

entries.zh: 齊高帝廢蒼梧，出廣之為徐州刺史、鍾離太守。
entries.en: When Emperor Gao deposed the Cangwu emperor, Guangzhi was sent as Inspector of Xu and Administrator of Zhongli.
entries.literal: When Emperor Gao of Qi deposed the Cangwu emperor, he sent Guangzhi out as Inspector of Xu Province and Administrator of Zhongli.

entries.zh: 沈攸之事起，廣之留都下，豫平石頭，仍從高帝頓新亭。
entries.en: When Shen Youzhi rebelled, Guangzhi stayed in the capital, helped take Stone City, and followed Emperor Gao to Xinting.
entries.literal: When Shen Youzhi's affair arose, Guangzhi remained in the capital, took part in pacifying Stone City, and still followed Emperor Gao to encamp at Xinting.

entries.zh: 高帝誅黃回，回弟駟及從弟馬、兄子奴亡逸。
entries.en: When Huang Hui was executed, his brother Si, cousin Ma, and nephew Nu fled.
entries.literal: When Emperor Gao executed Huang Hui, Hui's younger brother Si and cousin Ma and elder brother's son Nu fled and vanished.

entries.zh: 高帝與廣之書曰：「黃回雖有微勳，而罪過轉不可容。
entries.en: Emperor Gao wrote Guangzhi: "Huang Hui's small merits could not balance his crimes.
entries.literal: Emperor Gao wrote to Guangzhi, "Huang Hui though he had slight merit, his crimes in the end could not be tolerated.

entries.zh: 近遂啟請禦大小二輿為刺史服飾，吾乃不惜為其啟聞，政恐得輿復求畫輪車。
entries.en: He lately asked for imperial carriages fit for an inspector; I would have reported it, fearing he would next demand a painted imperial coach.
entries.literal: Recently he even requested the great and small imperial carriages for inspector's regalia; I was not unwilling to report it for him, but only feared that obtaining the carriage he would again request a painted-wheel carriage.

entries.zh: 此外罪不可勝數，弟自悉之。
entries.en: His other crimes are countless—you know them.
entries.literal: Beyond this his crimes are beyond counting—you yourself know them.

entries.zh: 今啟依法。」
entries.en: Execute the law now."
entries.literal: Now I report according to law."

entries.zh: 令廣之於江西搜捕駟等。
entries.en: He ordered Guangzhi to hunt Si and the rest west of the Yangzi.
entries.literal: He ordered Guangzhi to search west of the river and capture Si and the others.

entries.zh: 建元元年，進爵為侯。
entries.en: In the first year of Jianyuan (479), Guangzhi's title was advanced to marquis.
entries.literal: In the first year of Jianyuan, Guangzhi's title was advanced to marquis.

entries.zh: 武帝即位，累遷右衛將軍，散騎常侍，前軍將軍。
entries.en: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, he rose through successive promotions to General of the Right Guard, Cavalier Attendant, and General of the Van.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, he was repeatedly promoted to General of the Right Guard, Cavalier Attendant, and General of the Van.

entries.zh: 延興元年，為豫州刺史，豫廢郁林。
entries.en: In the first year of Yanxing, he became Inspector of Yuzhou and took part in deposing Yulin.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yanxing, he became Inspector of Yuzhou and took part in deposing Yulin.

entries.zh: 後拜鎮南將軍、江州刺史，進應城縣公。
entries.en: Later he was appointed General Who Guards the South and Inspector of Jiangzhou, and his title was advanced to Duke of Yingcheng County.
entries.literal: Later he was appointed General Who Guards the South and Inspector of Jiangzhou, and his title was advanced to Duke of Yingcheng County.

entries.zh: 建武中，位侍中、鎮軍將軍，給扶。
entries.en: During Jianwu, he held the offices of Attendant-in-Ordinary and General Who Guards the Army and was granted an armrest.
entries.literal: During Jianwu, he held the offices of Attendant-in-Ordinary and General Who Guards the Army and was granted an armrest.

entries.zh: 後卒，贈車騎將軍，諡壯公。
entries.en: Later he died, was posthumously given the office of General of Chariots and Cavalry, and received the posthumous title Duke Zhuang.
entries.literal: Later he died, was posthumously given the office of General of Chariots and Cavalry, and received the posthumous title Duke Zhuang.

entries.zh: 永明初，遷桂陽內史，討捕賊盜，境內肅清。
entries.en: Early in Yongming he governed Guiyang, crushed bandits, and cleared the region.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Yongming he was transferred to Interior Administrator of Guiyang, pursued and captured bandits and robbers, and within the borders was cleared and pacified.

entries.zh: 罷任還都，路經江州，刺史柳世隆臨渚餞別，見珍國還裝輕素，歎曰：「此真良二千石也，」還為大司馬中兵參軍。
entries.en: Returning to court via Jiang Province, Liu Shilong saw his light baggage and sighed, "A true two-thousand-dan official," then named him Major under the Grand Marshal.
entries.literal: Leaving office and returning to the capital, his route passed Jiang Province; Inspector Liu Shilong came to the ford to bid farewell; seeing Zhenguo's return baggage light and plain, he sighed and said, "This is truly a good two-thousand-dan official," and on return he was made Major in the Grand Marshal's central army.

entries.zh: 武帝雅相知賞，謂其父廣之曰：「珍國應堪大用，卿可謂老蚌也。」
entries.en: Emperor Wu prized him and told Guangzhi, "Zhenguo deserves high office—you are the old oyster that bore the pearl."
entries.literal: Emperor Wu in refined fashion knew and appreciated him and said to his father Guangzhi, "Zhenguo should be fit for great employment—you may be called an old oyster."

entries.zh: 廣之曰：「臣不敢辭。」
entries.en: Guangzhi said, "I dare not refuse the praise."
entries.literal: Guangzhi said, "Your servant dares not decline."

entries.zh: 帝大笑。
entries.en: The emperor laughed aloud.
entries.literal: The emperor laughed greatly.

entries.zh: 帝每歎曰：「晚代將家子弟如珍國者少矣。」
entries.en: He often said, "Few sons of generals in this age match Zhenguo."
entries.literal: The emperor often sighed, "In this late age there are few sons of general's houses like Zhenguo."

entries.zh: 累遷遊擊將軍，父憂去職。
entries.en: He rose to General Who Roams in Attack, then left for mourning his father.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to General Who Roams in Attack and left office for his father's mourning.

entries.zh: 李安人
entries.en: Li Anren
entries.literal: Li Anren

entries.zh: 祖嶷，衛軍將軍。
entries.en: His grandfather Yi served as General of the Guards.
entries.literal: His grandfather Yi was General of the Guards.

entries.zh: 父欽之，薛令。
entries.en: His father Qinzhi served as magistrate of Xue.
entries.literal: His father Qinzhi was magistrate of Xue.

entries.zh: 高帝重伯玉盡心，愈見信任，使掌軍國密事，權動朝右。
entries.en: Emperor Gao valued Boyu's wholehearted devotion and trusted him ever more, putting him in charge of secret military and state affairs; his power moved the right side of court.
entries.literal: The Emperor Gao valued Boyu's wholehearted devotion and trusted him ever more, putting him in charge of secret military and state affairs; his power moved the right side of court.

entries.zh: 每暫休外，軒蓋填門。
entries.en: Whenever he briefly rested outside office, carriage canopies filled his gate.
entries.literal: Whenever he briefly rested outside [office], carriage canopies filled his gate.

entries.zh: 嘗遭母憂，成服日，左率蕭景先、侍中王晏共載吊之。
entries.en: When he suffered his mother's mourning, on the day he completed mourning dress Left Commander Xiao Jingxian and Attendant-in-Ordinary Wang Yan rode together to offer condolences.
entries.literal: He once suffered his mother's mourning; on the day he completed mourning dress, the Left Commander Xiao Jingxian and the Attendant-in-Ordinary Wang Yan rode together to offer condolences.

entries.zh: 五更便巾車，未到伯玉宅二里許，王侯朝士已盈巷，至下鼓尚未得前，司徒褚彥回、衛軍王儉俱進繼後方得前，又倚聽事久之。
entries.en: At the fifth watch they set out in a covered carriage. Before they were within about two li of Boyu's residence, princes and court gentlemen already filled the lane. By the evening drum they still had not been able to advance. Minister of Works Chu Yanhui and Defender-in-Chief Wang Jian both pressed forward in succession behind others before they could advance, and leaned on the reception hall a long while.
entries.literal: At the fifth watch they set out in a covered carriage; before reaching within about two li of Boyu's residence, princes and court gentlemen already filled the lane; by the time of the evening drum they still had not been able to advance. The Minister of Works Chu Yanhui and the Defender-in-Chief Wang Jian both pressed forward in succession behind others before they could advance, and leaned on the reception hall a long while.

entries.zh: 中詔遣中書舍人徐希秀斷哭止客，久方得吊。
entries.en: A central edict sent Secretariat Gentleman Xu Xixiu to cut off weeping and stop visitors; only after a long while could they offer condolences.
entries.literal: A central edict sent the Secretariat Gentleman Xu Xixiu to cut off weeping and stop visitors; only after a long while could they offer condolences.

entries.zh: 比出，二人饑乏，氣息惙然，切齒形於聲貌。
entries.en: By the time they came out, the two men were hungry and exhausted, their breath faint; grinding their teeth showed in voice and countenance.
entries.literal: By the time they came out, the two men were hungry and exhausted, their breath faint; grinding their teeth showed in voice and countenance.

entries.zh: 明日入宮，言便云：「臣等所見二宮門及齋合方荀伯玉宅，政可設雀羅。」
entries.en: The next day they entered the palace and at once said, "What we saw—the two palace gates and the fasting hall were just Xun Boyu's residence; one might as well set up a net for sparrows."
entries.literal: The next day they entered the palace and at once said: "What we saw—the two palace gates and the fasting hall were just Xun Boyu's residence; one might as well set up a net for sparrows."

entries.zh: 續復言：「外論云，千敕萬令，不如荀公一命。」
entries.en: They went on, "Outside it is said, a thousand edicts and ten thousand orders are not equal to one word from Lord Xun."
entries.literal: They went on to say: "Outside it is said, a thousand edicts and ten thousand orders are not equal to one word from Lord Xun."

entries.zh: 郁林王立，兼大匠卿，起休安陵，於陵所受局下牛酒，坐免官。
entries.en: When Emperor Yulin was established, Cong concurrently held the post of Grand Master of Works and raised the Xiuan Mausoleum; for oxen and wine received from subordinates at the mausoleum he was dismissed from office.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yulin was established, Cong concurrently held the post of Grand Master of Works and raised the Xiuan Mausoleum; for oxen and wine received from subordinates at the mausoleum he was dismissed from office.

entries.zh: 隆昌元年，以白衣領職。
entries.en: In the first year of Longchang he held the post in plain dress.
entries.literal: In the first year of Longchang he held the post in plain dress.

entries.zh: 郁林廢，悰竊歎曰：「王、徐遂縛袴廢天子，天下豈有此理耶？」
entries.en: When Yulin was deposed, Cong sighed privately, "Wang and Xu have bound their trousers and deposed the Son of Heaven—can there be such a principle under Heaven?"
entries.literal: When Yulin was deposed, Cong sighed privately: "Wang and Xu have bound their trousers and deposed the Son of Heaven—can there be such a principle under Heaven?"

entries.zh: 延興元年，領右軍。
entries.en: In the first year of Yanxing he led the Right Army.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yanxing he led the Right Army.

entries.zh: 明帝立，悰稱疾不陪位。
entries.en: When Emperor Ming was established, Cong claimed illness and did not take part in the enthronement.
entries.literal: When Emperor Ming was established, Cong claimed illness and did not take part in the enthronement.

entries.zh: 帝使尚書令王晏齎廢立事示悰，以悰舊人，引參佐命。
entries.en: The emperor sent Secretariat Director Wang Yan to carry the matter of deposition and establishment to show Cong; because Cong was an old associate, he was invited to participate in assisting the mandate.
entries.literal: The Emperor sent Secretariat Director Wang Yan to carry the matter of deposition and establishment to show Cong; because Cong was an old associate, he was invited to participate in assisting the mandate.

entries.zh: 悰謂晏曰：「主上聖明，公卿戮力，寧假朽老以匡贊惟新乎，不敢聞命。」
entries.en: Cong said to Yan, "The sovereign is sagely and bright; the dukes and ministers exert their strength together—would you borrow a decayed old man to assist the renewal? I dare not accept the command."
entries.literal: Cong said to Yan: "The sovereign is sagely and bright; the dukes and ministers exert their strength together—would you borrow a decayed old man to assist the renewal? I dare not accept the command."

entries.zh: 因慟不自勝。
entries.en: He thereupon grieved beyond controlling himself.
entries.literal: He thereupon grieved beyond controlling himself.

entries.zh: 朝議欲糾之，僕射徐孝嗣曰：「此亦古之遺直。」
entries.en: Court discussion wished to censure him; Vice Director Xu Xiaosi said, "This too is an upright remnant of antiquity."
entries.literal: Court discussion wished to censure him; Vice Director Xu Xiaosi said: "This too is an upright remnant of antiquity."

entries.zh: 眾議乃止。
entries.en: The multitude's discussion then ceased.
entries.literal: The multitude's discussion then ceased.

entries.zh: 元徽中，為尚書右丞。
entries.en: In Yuanhui he was Right Assistant Minister of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: In Yuanhui he was Right Assistant Minister of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 齊高帝參政，與玩之書曰：「張華為度支尚書，事不徒然。
entries.en: When Emperor Gao of Qi assisted in government he wrote to Wanzhi, "Zhang Hua as Minister of Revenue—the affair was not in vain.
entries.literal: When the Qi Emperor Gao assisted in government he wrote to Wanzhi: "Zhang Hua as Minister of Revenue—the affair was not in vain.

entries.zh: 今漕藏有闕，吾賢居右丞，已覺金粟可積也。」
entries.en: Now the transport stores have gaps; my worthy man holds the right assistant post—I already feel gold and grain can be accumulated."
entries.literal: Now the transport stores have gaps; my worthy man holds the right assistant post—I already feel gold and grain can be accumulated."

entries.zh: 玩之上表，陳府庫錢帛，器械役力，所懸轉多，興用漸廣，慮不支歲月。
entries.en: Wanzhi submitted a memorial stating that the headquarters' cash, silk, implements, labor, and suspended items grew ever more, expenditures gradually widened, and he feared they would not last the year.
entries.literal: Wanzhi submitted a memorial stating that the headquarters' cash, silk, implements, labor, and suspended items grew ever more, expenditures gradually widened, and he feared they would not last the year.

entries.zh: 朝議優報之。
entries.en: Court discussion favorably replied.
entries.literal: Court discussion favorably replied.

entries.zh: 高帝鎮東府，朝廷致敬，玩之為少府，猶躡屐造席。
entries.en: When Emperor Gao garrisoned the Eastern Headquarters, the court showed respect; Wanzhi was Minister of the Privy Purse and still wore clogs to take his seat.
entries.literal: When the Emperor Gao garrisoned the Eastern Headquarters, the court showed respect; Wanzhi was Minister of the Privy Purse and still wore clogs to take his seat.

entries.zh: 高帝取屐親視之，訛黑斜銳，蒵斷以芒接之。
entries.en: Emperor Gao took the clog and examined it personally—worn black, slanting and sharp, the rush broken and joined with awn.
entries.literal: The Emperor Gao took the clog and examined it personally—worn black, slanting and sharp, the rush broken and joined with awn.

entries.zh: 問曰：「卿此屐已幾載？」
entries.en: He asked, "How many years have you worn these clogs?"
entries.literal: He asked: "How many years have you worn these clogs?"

entries.zh: 玩之曰：「初釋褐拜征北行佐買之，著已三十年，貧士竟不辦易。」
entries.en: Wanzhi said, "When I first left the cloth and was appointed Northern Expedition traveling staff officer I bought them; I have worn them thirty years—a poor gentleman truly cannot afford to replace them."
entries.literal: Wanzhi said: "When I first left the cloth and was appointed Northern Expedition traveling staff officer I bought them; I have worn them thirty years—a poor gentleman truly cannot afford to replace them."

entries.zh: 高帝咨嗟，因賜以新屐。
entries.en: Emperor Gao sighed in admiration and bestowed new clogs.
entries.literal: The Emperor Gao sighed in admiration and bestowed new clogs.

entries.zh: 玩之不受。
entries.en: Wanzhi did not accept them.
entries.literal: Wanzhi did not accept them.

entries.zh: 帝問其故，答曰：「今日之賜，恩華俱重，但蓍簪弊席，復不可遺，所以不敢當。」
entries.en: The emperor asked the reason; he replied, "Today's gift—favor and splendor together are weighty; but worn rush hairpin and broken mat cannot be discarded, so I dare not accept."
entries.literal: The Emperor asked the reason; he replied: "Today's gift—favor and splendor together are weighty; but worn rush hairpin and broken mat cannot be discarded, so I dare not accept."

entries.zh: 帝善之。
entries.en: The emperor approved.
entries.literal: The Emperor approved.

entries.zh: 拜驃騎諮議參軍。
entries.en: He was appointed Valiant Cavalry Adviser.
entries.literal: He was appointed Valiant Cavalry Adviser.

entries.zh: 霸府初開，賓客輻湊，高帝留意簡接。
entries.en: When the Hegemon's headquarters first opened, guests gathered in crowds; Emperor Gao paid attention to selective reception.
entries.literal: When the Hegemon's headquarters first opened, guests gathered in crowds; the Emperor Gao paid attention to selective reception.

entries.zh: 玩之與樂安任遐俱以應對有席上之美，齊名見遇。
entries.en: Wanzhi and Ren Xia of Le'an together had beauty in banquet repartee and were equally famed and favored.
entries.literal: Wanzhi and Ren Xia of Le'an together had beauty in banquet repartee and were equally famed and favored.

entries.zh: 玩之遷黃門郎。
entries.en: Wanzhi was transferred to Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.
entries.literal: Wanzhi was transferred to Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.

entries.zh: 先時，宋世人籍欺巧，及高帝即位，敕玩之與驍騎將軍傅堅意檢定之。
entries.en: Previously, under Song, people practiced fraud and trickery in the household registers. When Emperor Gao ascended the throne, he ordered Wanzhi and General of Agile Cavalry Fu Jianyi to inspect and settle them.
entries.literal: Previously, under Song, people practiced fraud and trickery in the household registers; when Emperor Gao ascended the throne, he ordered Wanzhi and General of Agile Cavalry Fu Jianyi to inspect and settle them.

entries.zh: 建元二年，詔朝臣曰：「黃籍人之大綱，國之政端。
entries.en: In the second year of Jianyuan (480), an edict addressed the court ministers, saying, "The yellow registers are the great framework of the people and the foundation of state governance.
entries.literal: In the second year of Jianyuan, an edict addressed the court ministers, saying, "The yellow registers are the great framework of the people and the beginning point of the state's governance.

entries.zh: 自頃甿俗巧偽，乃至竊注爵位，盜易年月，增損三狀，貿襲萬端。
entries.en: Recently common people have grown cunning and false, even secretly entering titles and ranks, illicitly altering years and months, increasing and decreasing the three descriptions, and exchanging and usurping in countless ways.
entries.literal: Recently common people's customs have become cunning and false, even to the point of secretly entering titles and ranks, illicitly altering years and months, increasing and decreasing the three descriptions, and exchanging and usurping in ten thousand ways.

entries.zh: 或戶存而文書已絕，或人在而反托死叛，停私而云隸役，身強而稱六疾。
entries.en: In some cases the household remains but the documents have vanished; in some the person is alive yet falsely claims death or flight; some remain privately while claiming to be in service, and some are healthy yet claim the six illnesses.
entries.literal: In some cases the household remains but the documents have already vanished; in some the person is alive yet falsely claims death or flight; some remain privately while claiming to be in service, and some are healthy yet claim the six illnesses.

entries.zh: 此皆政之巨蠹，教之深疵。
entries.en: These are all grave pests in government and deep flaws in instruction.
entries.literal: These are all great worms in government and deep flaws in instruction.

entries.zh: 若約之以刑，則人偽已遠，若綏之以德，則勝殘未易。
entries.en: If they are restrained by punishments, the people's falsity has already gone far; if they are soothed by virtue, overcoming the remaining evil will not be easy.
entries.literal: If they are restrained by punishments, the people's falsity has already gone far; if they are soothed by virtue, overcoming the remnant evil will not be easy.

entries.zh: 諸賢並深明政體，各獻嘉謀。」
entries.en: You worthies all deeply understand the structure of government; each of you should offer excellent plans."
entries.literal: You worthies all deeply understand the structure of government; each of you should offer excellent plans."

entries.zh: 玩之表言便宜，多見採納。
entries.en: Wanzhi submitted a memorial discussing suitable measures, and many of them were adopted.
entries.literal: Wanzhi submitted a memorial discussing suitable measures, and many of them were adopted.

entries.zh: 於是朝廷乃別置校籍官，置令史，限人一日得數巧，以防懈怠。
entries.en: Thereupon the court separately established officials for checking registers and appointed clerks, limiting the number of register frauds each person could process in one day to guard against slackness.
entries.literal: Thereupon the court separately established officials for checking registers and appointed clerks, limiting the number of deceptions each person could process in one day to guard against slackness.

entries.zh: 既連年不已，貨賄潛通，百姓怨望。
entries.en: After this continued year after year without end, bribes circulated secretly, and the common people grew resentful.
entries.literal: After this continued year after year without end, bribes and gifts circulated secretly, and the common people were resentful.

entries.zh: 荀伯玉
entries.en: Xun Boyu
entries.literal: Xun Boyu

entries.zh: 梁簡文帝諸子元帝諸子
entries.en: The Sons of Emperor Jianwen of Liang; The Sons of Emperor Yuan of Liang
entries.literal: Sons of Emperor Jianwen of Liang; Sons of Emperor Yuan of Liang

entries.zh: 哀太子大器字仁宗，簡文嫡長子也。
entries.en: The Lamented Crown Prince Dadqi, styled Renzong, was the legitimate eldest son of Emperor Jianwen.
entries.literal: The Lamented Crown Prince Dadqi, style name Renzong, was Emperor Jianwen's eldest son by his principal consort.

entries.zh: 中大通四年，封宣城郡王。
entries.en: In the fourth year of Zhongdatong he was enfeoffed as Prince of Xuancheng.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Zhongdatong, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Xuancheng commandery.

entries.zh: 太清二年十月，侯景寇建鄴，敕太子為台內大都督。
entries.en: In the tenth month of the second year of Taiqing, when Hou Jing attacked Jianye, an edict named the crown prince Grand Commander within the Terrace.
entries.literal: In the tenth month of the second year of Taiqing, when Hou Jing raided Jianye, an edict appointed the crown prince Grand Commander within the Terrace.

entries.zh: 三年五月，簡文即位。
entries.en: In the fifth month of the third year, Emperor Jianwen took the throne.
entries.literal: In the fifth month of the third year, Emperor Jianwen ascended the throne.

entries.zh: 六月丁亥，立為皇太子。
entries.en: On the day dinghai in the sixth month he was installed as crown prince.
entries.literal: On the day dinghai of the sixth month, he was installed as crown prince.

entries.zh: 尋陽王大心字仁恕，簡文第二子也。
entries.en: Prince Daxin of Xunyang, styled Renshu, was the second son of Emperor Jianwen.
entries.literal: Prince Daxin of Xunyang, style name Renshu, was Emperor Jianwen's second son.

entries.zh: 幼而聰朗，善屬文。
entries.en: As a boy he was clever and lucid, and skilled at writing.
entries.literal: In youth he was bright and clear, and skilled at literary composition.

entries.zh: 中大通四年，以皇孫封當陽縣公。
entries.en: In the fourth year of Zhongdatong he was enfeoffed as Duke of Dangyang while still an imperial grandson.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Zhongdatong, as imperial grandson he was enfeoffed Duke of Dangyang county.

entries.zh: 大同元年，為都督、郢州刺史，時年十三。
entries.en: In the first year of Datong he was made Commander-in-chief and Inspector of Yingzhou, at the age of thirteen.
entries.literal: In the first year of Datong, he became Commander-in-chief and Inspector of Yingzhou, at age thirteen.

entries.zh: 簡文以其幼，戒之曰：「事無大小，悉委行事。」
entries.en: Emperor Jianwen, finding him still young, warned him: "Whether the matter is great or small, leave it all to your staff officer."
entries.literal: Emperor Jianwen, because he was young, admonished him, saying, "In matters great or small, entrust everything to your staff officer."

entries.zh: 大心雖不親州務，發言每合於理，眾皆驚服。
entries.en: Though Daxin did not manage provincial affairs himself, his words always accorded with reason, and everyone marveled.
entries.literal: Though Daxin did not personally handle provincial affairs, whenever he spoke it accorded with reason, and all were astonished and submitted.

entries.zh: 太清元年，為雲麾將軍、江州刺史。
entries.en: In the first year of Taiqing he became General of the Cloudy Pennant and Inspector of Jiangzhou.
entries.literal: In the first year of Taiqing, he became General of the Cloudy Pennant and Inspector of Jiangzhou.

entries.zh: 貪冒財賄，不能綏接百姓。
entries.en: Greedy for bribes, he could not win the people's loyalty.
entries.literal: Greedy for bribes, he could not soothe and win over the common people.

entries.zh: 二年，侯景寇都，大心招集士卒，與上流諸軍赴援宮闕。
entries.en: In the second year, when Hou Jing attacked the capital, Daxin raised troops and marched with the upper Yangzi armies to rescue the palace.
entries.literal: In the second year, when Hou Jing raided the capital, Daxin gathered troops and, with the armies of the upper reaches, hurried to relieve the palace.

entries.zh: 三年，台城陷，上甲侯蕭韶南奔宣密詔，加散騎常侍，進號平南將軍。
entries.en: In the third year the Terrace City fell; Marquis Xiao Shao of Shangjia fled south with a secret edict, and Daxin was promoted to Regular Attendant and given the title General Who Pacifies the South.
entries.literal: In the third year the Terrace City fell; Marquis Xiao Shao of Shangjia fled south bearing a secret edict, and Daxin was promoted to Regular Attendant and advanced to General Who Pacifies the South.

entries.zh: 大寶元年，封尋陽王。
entries.en: In the first year of Dabao he was enfeoffed Prince of Xunyang.
entries.literal: In the first year of Dabao, he was enfeoffed Prince of Xunyang.

entries.zh: 大寶二年八月，景廢簡文，將害太子。
entries.en: In the eighth month of the second year of Dabao, Jing deposed Emperor Jianwen and intended to kill the crown prince.
entries.literal: In the eighth month of the second year of Dabao, Jing deposed Emperor Jianwen and was about to kill the crown prince.

entries.zh: 時景党稱景命召之，太子方講老子，將下床而刑人掩至。
entries.en: Jing's men then arrived, summoning him in Jing's name; the crown prince was expounding the Laozi and had just risen from his couch when the executioners were upon him.
entries.literal: At the time Jing's partisans, claiming Jing's command, summoned him; the crown prince was lecturing on the Laozi and was about to rise from his couch when executioners burst in.

entries.zh: 太子顏色不變，徐曰：「久知此事，嗟其晚耳。」
entries.en: The crown prince did not change color. He said calmly, "I have known this for a long time—it is only a pity that it comes so late."
entries.literal: The crown prince's countenance did not change, and he said slowly, "I have long known this would happen—only that it comes late."

entries.zh: 刑者將以衣帶絞之，太子曰：「此不能見殺。」
entries.en: The executioners were about to strangle him with a belt; the crown prince said, "That is not how I shall die."
entries.literal: The executioners were about to strangle him with a sash; the crown prince said, "That cannot be how I am put to death."

entries.zh: 乃指系帳竿下繩，命取絞之而絕。
entries.en: He pointed to the rope tied beneath the tent pole and told them to take it and strangle him with that.
entries.literal: He then pointed to the rope beneath the tent pole and ordered them to take it and strangle him to death.

entries.zh: 時年二十八。
entries.en: He was twenty-eight.
entries.literal: He was then twenty-eight years old.

entries.zh: 太子性寬和，兼神用端嶷，在賊中每不屈意。
entries.en: The crown prince was gentle and forbearing, with a dignified presence and keen intelligence; among the rebels he never bent his will.
entries.literal: The crown prince was by nature mild and magnanimous, and moreover of dignified bearing and keen spirit; among the rebels he never bowed his will.

entries.zh: 左右竊問其故，答曰：「賊若未須見殺，雖復陵傲呵叱，其終不敢言。
entries.en: His attendants asked him privately why; he replied, "If the rebels do not yet mean to kill me, then even if I am arrogant and shout at them, they will not dare say a word in the end.
entries.literal: Those about him asked in secret the reason, and he answered, "If the rebels do not yet need to kill me, even if I am overbearing and shout at them, in the end they will not dare speak of it.

entries.zh: 若見害時至，雖一日百拜，無益於死。」
entries.en: But if the hour of death has come, even a hundred bows in a day will not save me from death."
entries.literal: If the time to be killed has come, even a hundred prostrations in a day will not help one escape death."

entries.zh: 問者又曰：「官今憂逼而神貌怡然，未喻此意。」
entries.en: They asked again, "Your Highness is beset with troubles, yet your face is calm—we do not understand."
entries.literal: The questioner said again, "Your Highness is now pressed by worry, yet your spirit and bearing are serene—we do not understand this."

entries.zh: 答曰：「吾自度死必在賊前，若諸叔外來，平夷羯寇，必前見殺，然後就死。
entries.en: He answered, "I am sure I must die before the rebels do. If my uncles arrive from outside and crush the Jie invaders, I shall be killed first and only then die.
entries.literal: He answered, "I reckon for myself that death must come before the rebels; if my uncles come from outside and pacify the Jie bandits, I shall certainly be killed first and only then meet death.

entries.zh: 若其遂開拓上流，必先見殺，後取富貴。
entries.en: If they push up the Yangzi and win, I shall still be killed first and only then will others take wealth and honors.
entries.literal: If they should open up the upper reaches, I shall still be killed first and only afterward gain wealth and rank.

entries.zh: 何能以無益之愁，橫憂必死之命。」
entries.en: Why should I waste useless sorrow on a life that is certain to end in death?"
entries.literal: How could I heap useless grief upon a fate that is sure to end in death?"

entries.zh: 景之西上，攜太子同行，及敗歸，船往往相失。
entries.en: When Jing marched west he took the crown prince along; on his defeat and return, their boats often lost contact.
entries.literal: When Jing marched west, he took the crown prince with him; when he was defeated and returned, their boats often lost one another.

entries.zh: 所乘船入樅陽浦，舟中腹心並勸因此入北。
entries.en: His vessel entered Zongyang Ford; those closest to him aboard all urged him to seize the moment and flee north.
entries.literal: The boat he was on entered Zongyang Ford; the trusted men in the boat all urged that he use this chance to go north.

entries.zh: 太子曰：「自國家喪敗，志不圖生。
entries.en: The crown prince said, "Since the realm has been ruined, I have no wish to live.
entries.literal: The crown prince said, "Since the state has fallen, I have no thought of living.

entries.zh: 主上蒙塵，寧忍違離。
entries.en: The Son of Heaven is in exile in the dust—how could I bear to abandon him?
entries.literal: The sovereign suffers in the dust—how could I bear to leave him?

entries.zh: 吾今若去，乃是叛父，非謂避賊。
entries.en: If I go now, I rebel against my father; I am not simply avoiding the rebels.
entries.literal: If I leave now, I would be rebelling against my father, not merely fleeing the rebels.

entries.zh: 天下豈有無父之國。」
entries.en: Can there be a country in the world without a father?"
entries.literal: Is there a realm in the world without a father?"

entries.zh: 便涕泗鳴咽，命即前進。
entries.en: He wept aloud and ordered them to advance immediately.
entries.literal: He then wept aloud with streaming tears and ordered them to press on at once.

entries.zh: 賊以太子有器度，每憚之。
entries.en: The rebels feared the crown prince's bearing and always held him in awe.
entries.literal: The rebels, because the crown prince had presence of mind, always feared him.

entries.zh: 恐為後患，故先及禍。
entries.en: Fearing future trouble, they struck at him first.
entries.literal: Fearing he would be a future trouble, they brought disaster upon him first.

entries.zh: 承聖元年四月，追諡哀太子，祔太廟陰室。
entries.en: In the fourth month of the first year of Chengsheng he was posthumously titled the Lamented Crown Prince and enshrined in the yin side-chamber of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Chengsheng, he was posthumously titled the Lamented Crown Prince and enshrined in the yin chamber of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

entries.zh: 初，曆陽太守莊鐵以城降侯景，既而又奉其母來奔。
entries.en: At first Zhuang Tie, prefect of Liyang, surrendered his city to Hou Jing, then came over with his mother.
entries.literal: At first, Zhuang Tie, Administrator of Liyang, surrendered the city to Hou Jing, but afterward he brought his mother and came over as a refugee.

entries.zh: 大心以鐵舊將，厚為其禮，軍旅之事，悉以委之，以為豫章內史。
entries.en: Daxin, knowing Tie as a veteran commander, honored him richly and entrusted all military affairs to him, making him Interior Governor of Yuzhang.
entries.literal: Daxin, because Tie was an old officer, treated him with great courtesy and entrusted all military affairs to him, appointing him Interior Governor of Yuzhang.

entries.zh: 景數遣軍西上寇抄，大心輒令鐵擊破之，禽其將趙加婁，賊不能進。
entries.en: Jing sent troops west again and again to raid; Daxin had Tie repulse them each time and capture the general Zhao Jialou, so the rebels could not advance.
entries.literal: Jing repeatedly sent armies west to raid; Daxin always had Tie defeat them and capture the general Zhao Jialou, so the rebels could not advance.

entries.zh: 時鄱陽王範率眾棄合肥，屯於柵口，待援兵總集，欲俱進。
entries.en: Prince Fan of Poyang had abandoned Hefei and camped at Shankou, waiting for all relief forces to gather before advancing together.
entries.literal: At the time Prince Fan of Poyang led his forces, abandoning Hefei and encamping at Shankou, waiting for relief armies to assemble before advancing together.

entries.zh: 大心聞之，遣要範西上，以盆城處之，廩饋甚厚，欲與戮力共除禍難。
entries.en: Hearing this, Daxin invited Fan west, quartered him at Pencheng, fed his troops generously, and hoped to join in removing the disaster.
entries.literal: When Daxin heard of this, he invited Fan west, lodged him at Pencheng, supplied him generously, and wished to join forces to remove the calamity.

entries.zh: 會鐵據豫章反，大心令中兵參軍韋約討之，鐵敗乞降。
entries.en: When Tie rebelled and held Yuzhang, Daxin sent Wei Yue to attack; Tie was defeated and begged to surrender.
entries.literal: When Tie seized Yuzhang and rebelled, Daxin sent the Central Army Major Wei Yue to attack him; Tie was defeated and begged to surrender.

entries.zh: 鄱陽世子嗣先與鐵善，乃謂範曰：「昔與鐵遊處，其人才略從橫，若降江州，必不全其首領，請援之。」
entries.en: Si, the heir of Poyang, had previously been friendly with Tie and told Fan, "I used to keep company with Tie—he is clever and bold. If he surrenders to Jiangzhou they will not spare his life. Please aid him."
entries.literal: The heir of Poyang, Si, was previously friendly with Tie and said to Fan, "In the past I associated with Tie; his talent and stratagems are resourceful—if he surrenders to Jiangzhou, his head will surely not be spared. Please rescue him."

entries.zh: 乃遣將侯瑱救鐵，夜破韋約等營。
entries.en: He sent Hou Zhen to rescue Tie, who by night smashed Wei Yue's camp.
entries.literal: He then sent the general Hou Zhen to rescue Tie, who by night broke Wei Yue's camp.

entries.zh: 大心大懼。
entries.en: Daxin was deeply alarmed.
entries.literal: Daxin was greatly afraid.

entries.zh: 於是二蕃釁起。
entries.en: From this, strife broke out between the two princely domains.
entries.literal: Thus trouble arose between the two princely domains.

entries.zh: 南海王大臨字仁宣，簡文帝第四子也。
entries.en: Prince Dalin of Nanhai, styled Renxuan, was the fourth son of Emperor Jianwen.
entries.literal: Prince Dalin of Nanhai, style name Renxuan, was the fourth son of Emperor Jianwen.

entries.zh: 大同二年，封甯國縣公。
entries.en: In the second year of Datong he was enfeoffed Duke of Ningguo.
entries.literal: In the second year of Datong, he was enfeoffed Duke of Ningguo county.

entries.zh: 少而敏慧。
entries.en: As a boy he was clever and quick.
entries.literal: In youth he was clever and quick-witted.

entries.zh: 年十一，遭左夫人憂，哭泣毀瘠，以孝聞。
entries.en: At eleven he mourned Lady Zuo, weeping until he was wasted away, and became known for filial devotion.
entries.literal: At eleven he suffered the mourning for Lady Zuo; weeping he wasted away, and became known for filial piety.

entries.zh: 後入國學，明經射策甲科，拜中書侍郎，遷給事黃門侍郎。
entries.en: He later entered the Imperial Academy, took first rank in the Classics examination, was made Secretariat Gentleman, and promoted to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
entries.literal: He later entered the Imperial Academy, took first rank in the Classics examination, was appointed Secretariat Gentleman, and was promoted to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

entries.zh: 十一年，長兼侍中，出為琅邪、彭城二郡太守。
entries.en: In the eleventh year he served concurrently as Palace Attendant and went out as prefect of Langye and Pengcheng.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year he served concurrently as Palace Attendant and went out as Prefect of Langye and Pengcheng commanderies.

entries.zh: 侯景亂，屯端門，都督城南諸軍事。
entries.en: When Hou Jing rebelled, he camped at the Duan Gate and commanded all forces south of the city.
entries.literal: When Hou Jing rebelled, he encamped at the Duan Gate and commanded all military affairs south of the city.

entries.zh: 大寶元年，封南海郡王，出為都督、東揚州刺史，又除吳郡太守。
entries.en: In the first year of Dabao he was enfeoffed Prince of Nanhai, made Commander-in-chief and Inspector of Dongyang, and also appointed Prefect of Wu.
entries.literal: In the first year of Dabao he was enfeoffed Prince of Nanhai commandery, went out as Commander-in-chief and Inspector of Eastern Yangzhou, and was also appointed Prefect of Wu commandery.

entries.zh: 時張彪起義於會稽，吳人陸令公、潁川庾孟卿等勸大臨投之。
entries.en: Zhang Biao had raised forces in Kuaiji; Lu Linggong of Wu and Yu Mengqing of Yingchuan urged Dalin to join him.
entries.literal: At the time Zhang Biao raised a righteous army in Kuaiji; Lu Linggong of Wu and Yu Mengqing of Yingchuan urged Dalin to join him.

entries.zh: 大臨曰：「彪若成功，不藉我力；
entries.en: Dalin said, "If Biao succeeds, he will not need me;
entries.literal: Dalin said, "If Biao succeeds, he will not need my strength;

entries.zh: 如其撓敗，以我說焉，不可往也。」
entries.en: and if he is crushed and defeated, they would blame it on me—I must not go."
entries.literal: if he is crushed and defeated, to go to him because of my words—one must not go."

entries.zh: 二年遇害。
entries.en: In the second year he was killed.
entries.literal: In the second year he was killed.

entries.zh: 景將任約略地至盆城，大心遣司馬韋質拒戰敗績，時帳下猶有勇士千餘人，咸說曰：「既無糧儲，難以守固，若輕騎往建州，以圖後舉，策之上也。」
entries.en: When Jing's general Ren Yue reached Pencheng, Daxin sent Wei Zhi to fight and was beaten. More than a thousand brave men remained in camp; all urged, "Without provisions we cannot hold—if we ride lightly to Jianzhou and plan our next move, that is best."
entries.literal: When Jing's general Ren Yue advanced to Pencheng, Daxin sent the Marshal Wei Zhi to resist; he was defeated. There were still more than a thousand brave men in the camp, who all said, "With no grain stores, it is hard to hold firm; if we ride lightly to Jianzhou to plan a later effort, that is the best stratagem."

entries.zh: 其母陳淑容不從，撫胸慟哭，大心乃止，遂與約和。
entries.en: His mother Lady Chen Shurong refused; she beat her breast and wept, and Daxin halted and made peace with Yue.
entries.literal: His mother Lady Chen Shurong would not agree; beating her breast she wept bitterly, and Daxin then stopped and made peace with Yue.

entries.zh: 二年，將遇害，遶床謂賊廂公王僧貴曰：「我以全州歸命，何忍相苦。」
entries.en: In the second year, about to be killed, he circled his bed and said to the rebel chamberlain Wang Senggui, "I surrendered my whole province—how can you treat me so harshly?"
entries.literal: In the second year, when he was about to be killed, he walked around the bed and said to the rebel chamberlain Wang Senggui, "I have surrendered my whole province—how can you bear to torment me so?"

entries.zh: 乃見射而殞。
entries.en: He was shot and died.
entries.literal: He was then shot and died.

entries.zh: 南郡王大連字仁靖，簡文第五子也。
entries.en: Prince Dalian of Nanjun, styled Renjing, was the fifth son of Emperor Jianwen.
entries.literal: Prince Dalian of Nanjun, style name Renjing, was Emperor Jianwen's fifth son.

entries.zh: 少俊爽，能屬文。
entries.en: In youth he was handsome and spirited, and skilled at writing.
entries.literal: In youth he was handsome and spirited, and skilled at literary composition.

entries.zh: 舉止風流，雅有巧思，妙達音樂，兼善丹青。
entries.en: His manner was refined, he had a gift for invention, understood music deeply, and was also skilled at painting.
entries.literal: His bearing was elegant, he had fine ingenuity, was masterful in music, and also excelled at painting.

entries.zh: 大同二年，封臨城縣公。
entries.en: In the second year of Datong he was enfeoffed Duke of Lincheng.
entries.literal: In the second year of Datong, he was enfeoffed Duke of Lincheng county.

entries.zh: 七年，與南海王俱入國學，並射策甲科，皆拜中書侍郎。
entries.en: In the seventh year he and the Prince of Nanhai entered the Imperial Academy together; both took first rank and were made Secretariat Gentlemen.
entries.literal: In the seventh year he entered the Imperial Academy together with the Prince of Nanhai; both took top rank in the examination and were appointed Secretariat Gentlemen.

entries.zh: 十年，武帝幸朱方，大連與兄大臨並從。
entries.en: In the tenth year Emperor Wu visited Zhufang; Dalian went with his elder brother Dalin.
entries.literal: In the tenth year Emperor Wu visited Zhufang; Dalian followed together with his elder brother Dalin.

entries.zh: 武帝問曰：「汝等習騎不？」
entries.en: The Emperor asked, "Have you practiced horsemanship?"
entries.literal: Emperor Wu asked, "Have you practiced riding?"

entries.zh: 對曰：「臣等未奉詔，不敢輒習。」
entries.en: They answered, "We have not received Your Majesty's command and did not dare practice on our own."
entries.literal: They answered, "We have not received Your Majesty's command and did not dare practice on our own."

entries.zh: 敕令給馬試之。
entries.en: He ordered horses given them for a trial.
entries.literal: An edict ordered horses given them for a trial.

entries.zh: 大連兄弟據鞍往還，各得馳驟之節。
entries.en: Dalian and his brother mounted and rode back and forth, each showing proper control at the gallop.
entries.literal: Dalian and his brother, seated in the saddle, rode back and forth, each showing the proper pace of a gallop.

entries.zh: 帝大說，即賜所乘馬。
entries.en: The Emperor was delighted and gave them the horses he had been riding.
entries.literal: The Emperor was greatly pleased and at once bestowed the horses he himself rode.

entries.zh: 及為啟謝，辭又甚美。
entries.en: Their memorial of thanks was also beautifully worded.
entries.literal: When they submitted a memorial of thanks, the wording was also very fine.

entries.zh: 帝他日謂簡文曰：「昨見大臨、大連，風韻可愛，足慰吾老年。」
entries.en: Another day the Emperor told Emperor Jianwen, "Yesterday I saw Dalin and Dalian—their grace is lovely and enough to comfort me in my old age."
entries.literal: Another day the Emperor said to Emperor Jianwen, "Yesterday I saw Dalin and Dalian—their bearing is delightful and enough to comfort me in my old age."

entries.zh: 遷給事黃門侍郎，轉侍中。
entries.en: He was promoted to Attendant of the Yellow Gate and then to Palace Attendant.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Attendant of the Yellow Gate and transferred to Palace Attendant.

entries.zh: 太清元年，出為東揚州刺史。
entries.en: In the first year of Taiqing he went out as Inspector of Eastern Yangzhou.
entries.literal: In the first year of Taiqing, he went out as Inspector of Eastern Yangzhou.

entries.zh: 侯景入寇建鄴，大連率眾四萬來赴。
entries.en: When Hou Jing raided Jianye, Dalian led forty thousand men to the rescue.
entries.literal: When Hou Jing raided Jianye, Dalian led forty thousand men to the rescue.

entries.zh: 及台城沒，援軍散還東揚州。
entries.en: When the Terrace City fell, the relief armies scattered and he returned to Eastern Yangzhou.
entries.literal: When the Terrace City fell, the relief armies scattered and he returned to Eastern Yangzhou.

entries.zh: 會稽豐沃，糧仗山積，東人懲景苛虐，咸樂為用，而大連恒沈湎於酒。
entries.en: Kuaiji was fertile and rich, with grain and weapons piled like mountains. The easterners, chastened by Jing's harsh cruelty, were glad to serve him—but Dalian constantly drowned himself in wine.
entries.literal: Kuaiji was fertile and rich; grain and weapons piled like mountains. The people of the east, chastened by Jing's harsh cruelty, were all glad to serve him—but Dalian constantly drowned himself in wine.

entries.zh: 宋子仙攻之，大連棄城走，追及于信安縣，大連猶醉弗之覺。
entries.en: Song Zixian attacked him; Dalian abandoned the city and fled. Overtaken at Xin'an county, Dalian was still drunk and did not realize it.
entries.literal: Song Zixian attacked him; Dalian abandoned the city and fled. Overtaken at Xin'an county, Dalian was still drunk and did not realize it.

entries.zh: 於是三吳悉為賊有。
entries.en: Thereupon the Three Wu regions all fell to the rebels.
entries.literal: Thereupon the Three Wu regions all fell into the rebels' hands.

entries.zh: 大寶元年，封南郡王。
entries.en: In the first year of Dabao he was enfeoffed as Prince of Nanjun.
entries.literal: In the first year of Dabao he was enfeoffed as Prince of Nanjun.

entries.zh: 賊遣將趙伯超、劉神茂來攻。
entries.en: The rebels sent the generals Zhao Bochao and Liu Shenmao to attack.
entries.literal: The rebels sent the generals Zhao Bochao and Liu Shenmao to attack.

entries.zh: 大連專委部將留異，以城應賊，大連棄走，為賊所獲。
entries.en: Dalian wholly entrusted affairs to his subordinate general Liu Yi, who surrendered the city to the rebels; Dalian fled and was captured.
entries.literal: Dalian wholly entrusted affairs to his subordinate general Liu Yi, who surrendered the city to the rebels; Dalian fled in abandonment and was captured by the rebels.

entries.zh: 侯景以為江州刺史。
entries.en: Hou Jing appointed him Inspector of Jiangzhou.
entries.literal: Hou Jing appointed him Inspector of Jiangzhou.

entries.zh: 二年遇害。
entries.en: In the second year he was killed.
entries.literal: In the second year he was killed.

entries.zh: 安陸王大春字仁經，簡文第六子也。
entries.en: Prince Dachun of Anlu, styled Renjing, was the sixth son of Emperor Jianwen.
entries.literal: Prince Dachun of Anlu, style name Renjing, was Emperor Jianwen's sixth son.

entries.zh: 少博涉書記，善吹笙。
entries.en: In youth he was widely read in documents and records and skilled at the sheng flute.
entries.literal: In youth he was broadly versed in documents and records, and skilled at playing the sheng.

entries.zh: 天性孝謹，體貌瑰偉，腰帶十圍。
entries.en: By nature he was filial and careful; his build was imposing and his waist measured ten arm-spans.
entries.literal: By nature filial and cautious, his physique was magnificent and his waist belt ten arm-spans around.

entries.zh: 大同六年，封西豐縣公，拜中書侍郎。
entries.en: In the sixth year of Datong he was enfeoffed Duke of Xifeng and made Secretariat Gentleman.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Datong, he was enfeoffed Duke of Xifeng county and appointed Secretariat Gentleman.

entries.zh: 後為甯遠將軍，知石頭戍軍事。
entries.en: He later became General Who Pacifies the Distance and took charge of the Shitou garrison.
entries.literal: Later he became General Who Pacifies the Distance and supervised military affairs at the Shitou garrison.

entries.zh: 侯景內寇，大春奔京口，隨邵陵王入援，戰於鍾山。
entries.en: When Hou Jing invaded, Dachun fled to Jingkou and followed the Prince of Shaoling to the rescue, fighting at Zhongshan.
entries.literal: When Hou Jing invaded within, Dachun fled to Jingkou and followed the Prince of Shaoling in relief, fighting at Zhongshan.

entries.zh: 軍敗，肥大不能行，為賊所獲。
entries.en: The army was beaten; too heavy to walk, he was taken by the rebels.
entries.literal: The army was defeated; too stout to walk, he was captured by the rebels.

entries.zh: 大寶元年，封安陸郡王，出為東揚州刺史。
entries.en: In the first year of Dabao he was enfeoffed Prince of Anlu and made Inspector of Eastern Yangzhou.
entries.literal: In the first year of Dabao, he was enfeoffed Prince of Anlu commandery and went out as Inspector of Eastern Yangzhou.

entries.zh: 二年遇害。
entries.en: In the second year he was killed.
entries.literal: In the second year he was killed.

entries.zh: 瀏陽公大雅字仁風，簡文第十二子也。
entries.en: Duke Daya of Liuyang, styled Renfeng, was the twelfth son of Emperor Jianwen.
entries.literal: Duke Daya of Liuyang, style name Renfeng, was Emperor Jianwen's twelfth son.

entries.zh: 大同九年，封瀏陽縣公。
entries.en: In the ninth year of Datong he was enfeoffed Duke of Liuyang.
entries.literal: In the ninth year of Datong, he was enfeoffed Duke of Liuyang county.

entries.zh: 少聰警，美姿儀，特為武帝所愛。
entries.en: As a boy he was clever and alert, handsome in bearing, and especially loved by Emperor Wu.
entries.literal: In youth he was clever and alert, of fine bearing, and especially beloved by Emperor Wu.

entries.zh: 台城陷，大雅猶命左右格戰。
entries.en: When the Terrace City fell, Daya still ordered his men to fight at close quarters.
entries.literal: When the Terrace City fell, Daya still ordered those about him to fight hand to hand.

entries.zh: 賊至漸眾，乃自縋而下，發憤感疾薨。
entries.en: As the rebels grew in number, he let himself down by rope; stricken with grief he fell ill and died.
entries.literal: The rebels grew steadily more numerous; he then lowered himself by rope, and in indignant grief fell ill and died.

entries.zh: 西陽王大鈞字仁博，簡文第十四子也。
entries.en: Prince Dajun of Xiyang, styled Renbo, was the fourteenth son of Emperor Jianwen.
entries.literal: Prince Dajun of Xiyang, style name Renbo, was Emperor Jianwen's fourteenth son.

entries.zh: 性厚重，不妄戲弄。
entries.en: He was grave and steady and did not play about lightly.
entries.literal: His nature was weighty and steady; he did not play about rashly.

entries.zh: 年七歲，武帝嘗問讀何書，對曰學詩。
entries.en: At seven, Emperor Wu asked what book he was reading; he said he was studying the Odes.
entries.literal: At age seven, Emperor Wu once asked what book he was reading; he answered that he was studying the Odes.

entries.zh: 因令諷誦，即誦周南，音韻清雅。
entries.en: The Emperor had him recite, and he at once recited the Zhou Nan in clear, elegant tones.
entries.literal: He was therefore ordered to recite aloud, and at once recited the Zhou Nan; his tones were clear and elegant.

entries.zh: 帝重之，因賜王羲之書一卷。
entries.en: The Emperor prized him and gave him a scroll of Wang Xizhi's writing.
entries.literal: The Emperor valued him and bestowed a scroll of Wang Xizhi's calligraphy.

entries.zh: 大寶元年，封西陽郡王，位丹陽尹。
entries.en: In the first year of Dabao he was enfeoffed Prince of Xiyang and made Governor of Danyang.
entries.literal: In the first year of Dabao, he was enfeoffed Prince of Xiyang commandery and held the post of Governor of Danyang.

entries.zh: 二年，監揚州，遇害。
entries.en: In the second year he supervised Yangzhou and was killed.
entries.literal: In the second year he supervised Yangzhou and was killed.

entries.zh: 建平王大球字仁玉，簡文帝第十七子也。
entries.en: Prince Daqiu of Jianping, styled Renyu, was the seventeenth son of Emperor Jianwen.
entries.literal: Prince Daqiu of Jianping, style name Renyu, was the seventeenth son of Emperor Jianwen.

entries.zh: 大寶元年，封建平郡王。
entries.en: In the first year of Dabao he was enfeoffed Prince of Jianping.
entries.literal: In the first year of Dabao, he was enfeoffed Prince of Jianping commandery.

entries.zh: 性明慧夙成。
entries.en: He was bright and clever from early childhood.
entries.literal: His nature was bright and clever from early youth.

entries.zh: 初，侯景圍台城，武帝素歸心釋教，每發誓願，恒云：「若有眾生應受諸苦，衍身代當。」
entries.en: When Hou Jing first besieged the Terrace City, Emperor Wu had long devoted himself to Buddhism; whenever he made a vow he would say, "If any living being must suffer every pain, let me take it in their stead."
entries.literal: At first, when Hou Jing besieged the Terrace City, Emperor Wu had long turned his heart to Buddhism; whenever he made a vow he always said, "If there are living beings who ought to suffer every pain, let Yan take their place."

entries.zh: 時大球年甫七歲，聞而驚謂母曰：「官家尚爾，兒安敢辭。」
entries.en: Daqiu was then only seven; startled, he told his mother, "If the Emperor is still like this, how dare I refuse?"
entries.literal: At the time Daqiu was only seven; hearing this he was startled and said to his mother, "If the sovereign is still like this, how dare his son refuse?"

entries.zh: 乃六時禮佛，亦云：「凡有眾生應獲苦報，悉大球代受。」
entries.en: He then worshiped at the six hours and likewise said, "Whatever suffering living beings must receive, let Daqiu take it all."
entries.literal: He then worshiped the Buddha at the six hours and likewise said, "Whatever living beings ought to receive the retribution of suffering, let Daqiu take it all."

entries.zh: 其早慧如此。
entries.en: Such was his precocity.
entries.literal: His precocity was thus.

entries.zh: 二年遇害。
entries.en: In the second year he was killed.
entries.literal: In the second year he was killed.

entries.zh: 義安王大昕字仁朗，簡文帝第十八子也。
entries.en: Prince Daxin of Yian, styled Renlang, was the eighteenth son of Emperor Jianwen.
entries.literal: Prince Daxin of Yian, style name Renlang, was Emperor Jianwen's eighteenth son.

entries.zh: 年四歲，母陳夫人卒，便哀毀有若成人，晨夕涕泣，眼為之傷。
entries.en: At four, when his mother Lady Chen died, he grieved and wasted away like an adult, weeping morning and evening until his eyes were injured.
entries.literal: At four years old, when his mother Lady Chen died, he grieved and wasted away as though an adult, weeping morning and evening until his eyes were injured.

entries.zh: 及武帝崩，大昕奉慰簡文，嗚噎不自勝，左右莫不掩泣。
entries.en: When Emperor Wu died, Daxin came to console Emperor Jianwen, sobbing uncontrollably; none beside him failed to cover their faces and weep.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu died, Daxin came to console Emperor Jianwen, sobbing beyond control; those beside him none failed to cover their faces and weep.

entries.zh: 大寶元年，封義安郡王。
entries.en: In the first year of Dabao he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yian.
entries.literal: In the first year of Dabao he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yian commandery.

entries.zh: 二年遇害。
entries.en: In the second year he was killed.
entries.literal: In the second year he was killed.

entries.zh: 元帝諸子。
entries.en: The sons of Emperor Yuan.
entries.literal: The sons of Emperor Yuan.

entries.zh: 徐妃生武烈世子方等。
entries.en: Consort Xu bore the Martial and Fierce Heir Apparent Fangdeng.
entries.literal: Consort Xu bore the Martial and Fierce Heir Apparent Fangdeng.

entries.zh: 王貴嬪生貞惠世子方諸、始安王方略。
entries.en: Honored Consort Wang bore the Chaste and Gracious Heir Apparent Fangzhu and Prince Fanglue of Shian.
entries.literal: Honored Consort Wang bore the Chaste and Gracious Heir Apparent Fangzhu and Prince Fanglue of Shian.

entries.zh: 袁貴人生湣懷太子方矩。
entries.en: Honored Lady Yuan bore the Lamented and Cherished Crown Prince Fangju.
entries.literal: Honored Lady Yuan bore the Lamented and Cherished Crown Prince Fangju.

entries.zh: 夏貴妃生敬皇帝。
entries.en: Honored Consort Xia bore Emperor Jing.
entries.literal: Honored Consort Xia bore Emperor Jing.

entries.zh: 自餘不顯。
entries.en: The remainder are not recorded.
entries.literal: The rest are not recorded.

entries.zh: 武烈世子方等字實相，元帝長子也。
entries.en: The Martial and Fierce Heir Apparent Fangdeng, styled Shixiang, was the eldest son of Emperor Yuan.
entries.literal: The Martial and Fierce Heir Apparent Fangdeng, style name Shixiang, was Emperor Yuan's eldest son.

entries.zh: 少聰敏，有俊才，善騎射，尤長巧思。
entries.en: In youth he was clever and keen, gifted and skilled at riding and archery, and especially ingenious.
entries.literal: In youth he was clever and keen, had outstanding talent, was skilled at riding and shooting, and especially excelled in ingenious contrivances.

entries.zh: 性愛林泉，特好散逸。
entries.en: He loved forests and streams by nature and especially favored a life of ease.
entries.literal: By nature he loved forests and springs and was especially fond of untrammeled ease.

entries.zh: 嘗著論曰：「人生處世，如白駒過隙耳。
entries.en: He once wrote a treatise: "Life in the world is like a white colt flashing past a crack in the wall.
entries.literal: He once wrote a discourse, saying, "Life in the world is like a white colt flashing past a crack in the wall.

entries.zh: 一壺之酒，足以養性，一簞之食，足以怡形。
entries.en: A pot of wine is enough to nourish the nature; a basket of food is enough to please the body.
entries.literal: A pot of wine is enough to nourish one's nature; a basket of food is enough to delight one's form.

entries.zh: 生在蒿蓬，死葬溝壑，瓦棺石槨，何以異茲。
entries.en: Born in the weeds, buried in a ditch—a tile coffin or a stone sarcophagus, what difference is there?
entries.literal: Born amid artemisia and fleabane, buried in ditches and gullies—tile coffin or stone sarcophagus, how do they differ from this?

entries.zh: 吾嘗夢為魚，因化為鳥。
entries.en: I once dreamed I was a fish, and then became a bird.
entries.literal: I once dreamed I was a fish and thereby became a bird.

entries.zh: 方其夢也，何樂如之，及其覺也，何憂斯類，良由吾之不及魚鳥者遠矣。
entries.en: While dreaming, what joy could match it; when I woke, what sorrow—because I am so far beneath fish and birds.
entries.literal: While dreaming, what joy could equal it; when awake, what sorrow of this kind—truly because I fall far short of fish and birds.

entries.zh: 故魚鳥飛浮，任其志性，吾之進退，恒在掌握。
entries.en: Fish and birds fly and float as their natures dictate; my comings and goings are always in another's hand.
entries.literal: Thus fish and birds fly and float, following their natures; my coming and going are always in another's grasp.

entries.zh: 舉首懼觸，搖足恐墮。
entries.en: I lift my head in fear of striking something; I shift my foot in fear of falling.
entries.literal: I raise my head fearing I will strike something; I move my foot fearing I will fall.

entries.zh: 若使吾終得與魚鳥同遊，則去人間如脫屣耳。」
entries.en: If I could roam with fish and birds at last, I would leave the human world as easily as kicking off shoes."
entries.literal: If I could at last roam with fish and birds, I would leave the human world as though casting off shoes."

entries.zh: 初，徐妃以嫉妒失寵，方諸母王氏以冶容幸嬖。
entries.en: At first Consort Xu lost favor through jealousy; Fangzhu's mother Lady Wang, with her alluring looks, won the Emperor's favor.
entries.literal: At first Consort Xu lost favor through jealousy; Fangzhu's mother Lady Wang, with her seductive beauty, won intimate favor.

entries.zh: 及王夫人終，元帝歸咎徐妃，方等意不自安。
entries.en: When Lady Wang died, Emperor Yuan blamed Consort Xu; Fangdeng grew uneasy.
entries.literal: When Lady Wang died, Emperor Yuan blamed Consort Xu; Fangdeng felt ill at ease.

entries.zh: 元帝聞之，又惡方等，方等益懼，故述此論以申其志。
entries.en: Emperor Yuan heard of it and disliked Fangdeng still more; Fangdeng grew more afraid and wrote this treatise to declare his mind.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yuan heard of it, he disliked Fangdeng still more; Fangdeng grew still more afraid, and therefore set forth this discourse to declare his intent.

entries.zh: 時武帝年高，欲見諸王長子。
entries.en: Emperor Wu was then old and wished to see each prince's eldest son.
entries.literal: At the time Emperor Wu was advanced in years and wished to see the eldest sons of the princes.

entries.zh: 元帝遣方等，方等欣然升舟，冀免憂辱。
entries.en: Emperor Yuan sent Fangdeng; Fangdeng gladly boarded the boat, hoping to escape distress and shame.
entries.literal: Emperor Yuan sent Fangdeng; Fangdeng gladly boarded the boat, hoping to escape worry and humiliation.

entries.zh: 行至繇水，遇侯景亂，元帝召之，方等啟曰：「昔申生不愛其死，方等豈顧其生。」
entries.en: At the Yao River he met Hou Jing's rebellion; Emperor Yuan recalled him, and Fangdeng wrote, "Long ago Shen Sheng did not cling to life—why should Fangdeng cling to his?"
entries.literal: When he reached the Yao River he met Hou Jing's rebellion; Emperor Yuan summoned him, and Fangdeng reported, "In the past Shen Sheng did not value his life—how should Fangdeng care for his?"

entries.zh: 元帝省書歎息，知無還意，乃配步騎一萬，使援台城。
entries.en: Emperor Yuan read it, sighed, knew he would not return, and gave him ten thousand foot and horse to relieve the Terrace City.
entries.literal: Emperor Yuan read the report, sighed, knew he had no wish to return, and then assigned him ten thousand foot and horse to relieve the Terrace City.

entries.zh: 賊每來攻，方等必身當矢石。
entries.en: Whenever the rebels attacked, Fangdeng always placed himself in the path of arrows and stones.
entries.literal: Whenever the rebels came to attack, Fangdeng always placed himself in the path of arrows and stones.

entries.zh: 城陷，方等歸荊州，收集士馬，甚得眾和。
entries.en: When the city fell he returned to Jingzhou, gathered troops and horses, and won great support among the people.
entries.literal: When the city fell, Fangdeng returned to Jingzhou, gathered soldiers and horses, and won the people's hearts exceedingly.

entries.zh: 元帝始歎其能。
entries.en: Emperor Yuan began to admire his ability.
entries.literal: Emperor Yuan began to admire his ability.

entries.zh: 方等又勸修築城柵，以備不虞，既成，樓雉相望，周回七十餘里。
entries.en: Fangdeng also urged building palisades against surprise; when done, towers and battlements faced one another for more than seventy li around.
entries.literal: Fangdeng also urged building city palisades against the unexpected; when finished, towers and battlements faced one another, the circuit more than seventy li.

entries.zh: 元帝觀之甚說，入謂徐妃曰：「若更有一子如此，吾復何憂。」
entries.en: Emperor Yuan viewed them with delight and told Consort Xu, "If I had another son like this, what would I have to fear?"
entries.literal: Emperor Yuan viewed them with great pleasure and went in to tell Consort Xu, "If I had another son like this, what would I have to worry about?"

entries.zh: 徐妃不答，垂泣而退。
entries.en: Consort Xu did not answer; weeping, she withdrew.
entries.literal: Consort Xu did not answer; weeping, she withdrew.

entries.zh: 元帝忿之，因疏其穢行牓於大合，方等入見，益以自危。
entries.en: Emperor Yuan was angry and posted a bill of her shameful conduct in the great hall; when Fangdeng came to audience, he felt still more endangered.
entries.literal: Emperor Yuan was angry at this and therefore posted a bill of her shameful conduct in the great hall; when Fangdeng came in to see him, he felt still more endangered.

entries.zh: 時河東王為湘州刺史，不受令。
entries.en: The Prince of Hedong was then Inspector of Xiangzhou and would not obey orders.
entries.literal: At the time the Prince of Hedong was Inspector of Xiangzhou and did not accept orders.

entries.zh: 方等求征之，元帝謂曰：「汝有水厄，深宜慎之。」
entries.en: Fangdeng asked to campaign against him; Emperor Yuan said, "You have a water doom in your fate—you must be very careful."
entries.literal: Fangdeng asked to campaign against him; Emperor Yuan said to him, "You have a water calamity in your fate—you must be deeply cautious."

entries.zh: 拜為都督，令南討。
entries.en: He was made Commander-in-chief and ordered south.
entries.literal: He was appointed Commander-in-chief and ordered to campaign south.

entries.zh: 方等臨行謂所親曰：「吾此段出征，必死無二，死而獲所，吾豈愛生。」
entries.en: Before he set out he told his intimates, "On this campaign I am sure to die; if I die and gain my aim, why should I cling to life?"
entries.literal: On the eve of departure Fangdeng told those close to him, "On this campaign I am certain to die without alternative; if I die and gain my goal, how should I love life?"

entries.zh: 及至麻溪，軍敗溺死，求屍不得。
entries.en: At Maxi the army was beaten and he drowned; his body could not be found.
entries.literal: When he reached Maxi the army was defeated and he drowned; his corpse could not be found.

entries.zh: 元帝聞之心喜，不以為戚。
entries.en: When Emperor Yuan heard, he was secretly glad and did not grieve.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yuan heard of it, his heart rejoiced and he did not regard it as grief.

entries.zh: 後追思其才，贈侍中、中軍將軍、揚州刺史，諡忠壯世子，並招魂以葬之。
entries.en: Later, remembering his ability, he posthumously made him Palace Attendant and General of the Central Army, Inspector of Yangzhou, titled him the Loyal and Martial Heir Apparent, and buried him by summoning his soul.
entries.literal: Later, recalling his talent, he posthumously granted him Palace Attendant, General of the Central Army, and Inspector of Yangzhou, titled the Loyal and Martial Heir Apparent, and buried him by summoning his soul.

entries.zh: 元帝即位，改諡武烈世子。
entries.en: When Emperor Yuan ascended the throne, he changed the posthumous title of the Martial and Fierce Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yuan ascended the throne, he changed the posthumous title of the Martial and Fierce Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 封子莊為永嘉王。
entries.en: He enfeoffed his son Zhuang as Prince of Yongjia.
entries.literal: He enfeoffed his son Zhuang as Prince of Yongjia.

entries.zh: 及魏克江陵，莊年甫七歲，為人家所匿。
entries.en: When Wei captured Jiangling, Zhuang was only seven years old and was hidden in a common household.
entries.literal: When Wei captured Jiangling, Zhuang was only seven years old and was hidden in a common household.

entries.zh: 後王琳迎送建鄴。
entries.en: Later Wang Lin welcomed him and escorted him to Jianye.
entries.literal: Later Wang Lin welcomed him and escorted him to Jianye.

entries.zh: 及敬帝立，出質于齊。
entries.en: When Emperor Jing was established, Zhuang was sent as hostage to Qi.
entries.literal: When Emperor Jing was established, Zhuang was sent as hostage to Qi.

entries.zh: 敬帝太平二年，陳武帝將受禪，王琳請莊于齊以主梁嗣，自盆城濟江。
entries.en: In the second year of Taiping under Emperor Jing, as Chen Wudi was about to accept the abdication, Wang Lin requested Zhuang from Qi to head the Liang succession and crossed the river from Pencheng.
entries.literal: In the second year of Taiping under Emperor Jing, as Chen Wudi was about to accept the abdication, Wang Lin requested Zhuang from Qi to head the Liang succession, and crossed the river from Pencheng.

entries.zh: 二月，即帝位於郢州，年號天啟，置百官。
entries.en: In the second month he took the throne at Yingzhou, era name Tianqi, and established the hundred offices.
entries.literal: In the second month he took the throne at Yingzhou, reign era Tianqi, and established the hundred offices.

entries.zh: 王琳總其軍國。
entries.en: Wang Lin directed all military and state affairs.
entries.literal: Wang Lin directed all military and state affairs.

entries.zh: 明年，莊為陳人所敗，其御史中丞劉仲威奉以奔壽陽，遂入齊。
entries.en: The next year Zhuang was defeated by Chen men; his Censor-in-Chief Liu Zhongwei escorted him in flight to Shouyang, and he then entered Qi.
entries.literal: The next year Zhuang was defeated by Chen men; his Censor-in-Chief Liu Zhongwei escorted him in flight to Shouyang, and he then entered Qi.

entries.zh: 齊武平元年，授特進、開府儀同三司，封梁王。
entries.en: In the first year of Wu Ping of Qi, he was appointed Special Advance, Grand Master Unequaled in Ceremonial with the Three Departments, and enfeoffed as Prince of Liang.
entries.literal: In the first year of Wu Ping of Qi, he was appointed Special Advance, Grand Master Unequaled in Ceremonial with the Three Departments, and enfeoffed as Prince of Liang.

entries.zh: 齊朝許以興復，竟不果而齊亡，莊在鄴飲氣而死。
entries.en: The court of Qi promised restoration of Liang, but in the end it did not come to pass; Qi perished, and Zhuang died in Ye from pent-up grief.
entries.literal: The court of Qi promised restoration of Liang, but in the end it did not come to pass; Qi perished, and Zhuang died in Ye from pent-up grief.

entries.zh: 貞惠世子方諸字明智，元帝第二子也。
entries.en: The Chaste and Gracious Heir Apparent Fangzhu, styled Mingzhi, was the second son of Emperor Yuan.
entries.literal: The Chaste and Gracious Heir Apparent Fangzhu, style name Mingzhi, was Emperor Yuan's second son.

entries.zh: 幼聰警博學，明老、易，善談玄，風采清越，特為元帝所愛，母王氏又有寵。
entries.en: As a boy he was clever, widely learned, versed in the Laozi and Changes, skilled at metaphysical discourse, of refined bearing, and especially beloved by Emperor Yuan; his mother Lady Wang was also favored.
entries.literal: In youth he was clever, alert, and broadly learned; he mastered the Laozi and Changes, was skilled at discussing the abstruse, his bearing clear and surpassing, and was especially loved by Emperor Yuan; his mother Lady Wang also enjoyed favor.

entries.zh: 及方等敗後，元帝謂曰：「不有所廢，其何以興。
entries.en: After Fangdeng's defeat, Emperor Yuan told him, "Unless something is discarded, how can anything arise?
entries.literal: After Fangdeng's defeat, Emperor Yuan said to him, "Unless something is cast aside, how can anything rise?

entries.zh: 勿以汝兄為念。」
entries.en: Do not dwell on your elder brother."
entries.literal: Do not brood on your elder brother."

entries.zh: 因拜中撫軍將軍以自副。
entries.en: He was then made General of the Central Pacification Army as the Emperor's deputy.
entries.literal: He was then appointed General of the Central Pacification Army as the Emperor's deputy.

entries.zh: 又出為郢州刺史，鎮江夏，以鮑泉為行事。
entries.en: He went out as Inspector of Yingzhou, stationed at Jiangxia, with Bao Quan as his executive officer.
entries.literal: He also went out as Inspector of Yingzhou, garrisoned Jiangxia, and Bao Quan served as his staff officer.

entries.zh: 時元帝遣徐文盛與侯景將任約相持，方諸年十五，童心未革，恃文盛在近，不恤軍政，日與鮑泉蒱酒為樂。
