entries.en: Emperor Yuan had sent Xu Wensheng to hold Ren Yue, Hou Jing's general; Fangzhu was fifteen, still a boy, trusting that Wensheng was near and neglecting military affairs, passing his days drinking and gambling with Bao Quan.
entries.literal: At the time Emperor Yuan sent Xu Wensheng to contend with Hou Jing's general Ren Yue; Fangzhu was fifteen, his childish heart not yet changed, relying on Wensheng being near and heedless of military affairs, daily drinking and gambling with Bao Quan for pleasure.

entries.zh: 侯景知之，乃遣其將宋子仙從間道襲之。
entries.en: Hou Jing learned of this and sent Song Zixian by a secret path to attack.
entries.literal: When Hou Jing learned of this, he sent his general Song Zixian to strike by a hidden route.

entries.zh: 百姓奔告，方諸與鮑泉並不信，曰：「文盛大軍在下，虜安得來？」
entries.en: The people came with urgent news; Fangzhu and Bao Quan would not believe them: "Wensheng's main force is downstream—how could the enemy get here?"
entries.literal: The common people ran to report it; Fangzhu and Bao Quan both disbelieved, saying, "Wensheng's great army is below—how could the barbarians come?"

entries.zh: 始命閉門，賊已入城。
entries.en: Only then did he order the gates shut—the rebels were already in the city.
entries.literal: Only then did he order the gates closed—the rebels were already inside the city.

entries.zh: 方諸方踞泉腹，以五色毦辮其須。
entries.en: Fangzhu was sprawled on Bao Quan's belly, braiding his beard with colored wool.
entries.literal: Fangzhu was just sitting astride Bao Quan's belly, braiding his beard with five-colored wool.

entries.zh: 子仙執方諸以歸。
entries.en: Zixian seized Fangzhu and carried him off.
entries.literal: Zixian seized Fangzhu and took him back.

entries.zh: 王僧辯軍至蔡洲，景遂害之。
entries.en: When Wang Sengbian's army reached Caizhou, Hou Jing killed him.
entries.literal: When Wang Sengbian's army reached Caizhou, Jing then killed him.

entries.zh: 元帝追諡貞惠世子。
entries.en: Emperor Yuan posthumously titled him the Chaste and Gracious Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: Emperor Yuan posthumously titled him the Chaste and Gracious Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 湣懷太子方矩字德規，元帝第四子也。
entries.en: The Lamented and Cherished Crown Prince Fangju, styled Degui, was the fourth son of Emperor Yuan.
entries.literal: The Lamented and Cherished Crown Prince Fangju, style name Degui, was Emperor Yuan's fourth son.

entries.zh: 少勤學，美容止。
entries.en: In youth he studied diligently and had handsome bearing.
entries.literal: In youth he studied diligently and had handsome bearing.

entries.zh: 初封南安侯。
entries.en: At first he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Nan'an.
entries.literal: At first he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Nan'an.

entries.zh: 太清初，累遷侍中，中衛將軍。
entries.en: At the beginning of Taiqing he rose in succession to Palace Attendant and General of the Central Guard.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Taiqing he rose in succession to Palace Attendant and General of the Central Guard.

entries.zh: 元帝承制，拜王太子，改名元良。
entries.en: When Emperor Yuan acted under imperial mandate, he appointed him princely heir and changed his name to Yuanliang.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yuan acted under imperial mandate, he appointed him princely heir and changed his name to Yuanliang.

entries.zh: 承聖元年十一月丙子，立為皇太子。
entries.en: In the eleventh month of Chengsheng 1, on the day bingzi, he was installed as crown prince.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month of Chengsheng 1, on the day bingzi, he was installed as crown prince.

entries.zh: 及升儲位，昵狎群下，好著微服。
entries.en: Once he ascended the heir's position, he was intimate with his subordinates and liked to wear plain dress.
entries.literal: Once he ascended the heir's position, he was intimate with his subordinates and liked to wear plain dress.

entries.zh: 嘗入朝，公服中著碧絲布袴，摳衣高，元帝見之大怪，遣尚書周弘正責之，因使太子師弘正。
entries.en: Once when he came to court in official dress he wore blue silk trousers inside, hiking up his robe high; Emperor Yuan was greatly shocked, sent Minister of the Masters of Writing Zhou Hongzheng to rebuke him, and made Hongzheng the crown prince's tutor.
entries.literal: Once when he came to court in official dress he wore blue silk cloth trousers inside, hiking up his robe high; Emperor Yuan saw it and was greatly shocked. He sent Minister of the Masters of Writing Zhou Hongzheng to rebuke him, and made Hongzheng the crown prince's tutor.

entries.zh: 佗日，弘正謁見，元帝問曰：「太子比頗受卿導不？」
entries.en: Another day, when Hongzheng had an audience, Emperor Yuan asked, "Has the crown prince lately been guided by you much?"
entries.literal: Another day, when Hongzheng had an audience, Emperor Yuan asked: "Has the crown prince lately been guided by you much?"

entries.zh: 對曰：「太子聖德乃未極日新，幸無大過。」
entries.en: He answered, "The crown prince's sacred virtue has not yet reached perfection day by day; fortunately there are no great faults."
entries.literal: He answered: "The crown prince's sacred virtue has not yet reached perfection day by day; fortunately there are no great faults."

entries.zh: 帝曰：「卿以我父子故未直言，從容之間，無失和嶠之對。」
entries.en: The Emperor said, "Because we are father and son you did not speak plainly; in your composed reply, you failed to match He Qiao's answer."
entries.literal: The Emperor said: "Because we are father and son you did not speak plainly; in your composed reply, you failed to match He Qiao's answer."

entries.zh: 便有廢立計。
entries.en: He then formed a plan to depose and replace him.
entries.literal: He then formed a plan to depose and replace him.

entries.zh: 未及行而江陵喪亡，遇害。
entries.en: Before it could be carried out Jiangling was lost and destroyed, and he was killed.
entries.literal: Before it could be carried out Jiangling was lost and destroyed, and he was killed.

entries.zh: 太子聰穎凶暴猜忍，俱有元帝風。
entries.en: The crown prince was clever, fierce, violent, and cruelly suspicious—all in Emperor Yuan's manner.
entries.literal: The crown prince was clever, fierce, violent, and cruelly suspicious—all in Emperor Yuan's manner.

entries.zh: 敬帝承制，追諡湣懷太子。
entries.en: Emperor Jing, acting under imperial mandate, posthumously titled him the Lamented and Cherished Crown Prince.
entries.literal: Emperor Jing, acting under imperial mandate, posthumously titled him the Lamented and Cherished Crown Prince.

entries.zh: 始安王方略，元帝第十子，貞惠世子母弟也。
entries.en: Prince Fanglue of Shian was Emperor Yuan's tenth son and the Chaste and Gracious Heir Apparent's younger brother by the same mother.
entries.literal: Prince Fanglue of Shian was Emperor Yuan's tenth son, the younger brother by the same mother as the Chaste and Gracious Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 母王氏，王琳之次姊，元帝即位，拜貴嬪，次妹又為良人，並蒙寵倖，方略益鍾愛。
entries.en: His mother Lady Wang was Wang Lin's second elder sister; when Emperor Yuan took the throne she became Honored Consort, and her younger sister became Honored Lady; both were favored, and Fanglue was especially doted on.
entries.literal: His mother was Lady Wang, the second elder sister of Wang Lin; when Emperor Yuan ascended the throne she was made Honored Consort, and her younger sister was also made Honored Lady; both enjoyed favor, and Fanglue was especially cherished.

entries.zh: 侯景亂，元帝結好于魏，方略年數歲便遣入關。
entries.en: During Hou Jing's rebellion Emperor Yuan sought ties with Wei and sent Fanglue into the passes while he was still a small child.
entries.literal: During Hou Jing's rebellion, Emperor Yuan sought friendship with Wei and, when Fanglue was only a few years old, sent him into the passes.

entries.zh: 元帝親送近畿，執手歔欷，既而旋駕憶之，賦詩曰：「如何吾幼子，勝衣已別離，十日無由宴，千里送遠垂。」
entries.en: Emperor Yuan escorted him to the suburbs himself, took his hand and wept; turning back he missed him and wrote: "How is it with my little son—already in short coats and parted from me; ten days without a shared meal, a thousand li seeing him off in tears."
entries.literal: Emperor Yuan personally escorted him to the near suburbs, took his hand and sobbed; afterward, as he turned his carriage back he thought of him and composed a poem: "How is it with my little son—already past the age of short coats and parted from me; ten days without a feast together, a thousand li sending him off in tears."

entries.zh: 至長安即得還，贈遺甚厚。
entries.en: At Chang'an he was soon allowed to return; the gifts sent back were lavish.
entries.literal: When he reached Chang'an he was allowed to return at once; the gifts sent back were very generous.

entries.zh: 江陵喪亡，遇害。
entries.en: When Jiangling fell, he was killed.
entries.literal: When Jiangling fell, he was killed.

entries.zh: 貴嬪、良人並更誕子，未出合，無封失名。
entries.en: The Honored Consort and Honored Lady each bore more sons; they had not yet left the inner quarters, received no titles, and their names are unrecorded.
entries.literal: The Honored Consort and Honored Lady each bore sons again; they had not yet left the palace quarters, received no fiefs, and their names are lost.

entries.zh: 論曰：簡文提挈寇戎，元帝崎嶇危亂，諸子之備踐艱棘，蓋時運之所鍾乎。
entries.en: The commentary says: Emperor Jianwen bore the realm through invasion; Emperor Yuan struggled through danger and chaos—the sons' full measure of hardship—was this not the allotment of the age?
entries.literal: The commentary says: Emperor Jianwen led the realm through invaders; Emperor Yuan struggled through peril and chaos—the sons' full share of hardship and thorn—was this not what the times had allotted?

entries.zh: 武烈以幹蠱之材，居塚嗣之任，竟亦當年擯落，通塞亦云命也，哀哉！
entries.en: The Martial and Fierce heir had talent to stem ruin and bore the heir's charge—yet that very year he was cast aside; rise and fall are also called fate. Alas!
entries.literal: The Martial and Fierce heir, with talent fit to manage his father's unfinished work, held the charge of the primary heir—yet in the end he was cast aside that same year; fortune and misfortune, too, are said to be fate. Alas!

entries.zh: 列傳第四十四
entries.en: Biography 44
entries.literal: Biography 44

entries.zh: 後為司徒竟陵王記室參軍。
entries.en: Later he served as recorder-aide to the Minister of Education, Prince Jingling.
entries.literal: Later he served as recorder-aide to the Minister of Education, Prince Jingling.

entries.zh: 時琅邪王融有才俊，自謂無對當時，見昉之文，怳然自失。
entries.en: At that time Wang Rong of Langya had literary talent and brilliance and considered himself without rival in the age. When he saw Fang's writings he was suddenly lost to himself.
entries.literal: At that time Wang Rong of Langya had literary talent and brilliance; he considered himself without rival in the age; when he saw Fang's writings he was suddenly lost to himself.

entries.zh: 以父喪去官，泣血三年，杖而後起。
entries.en: On his father's death he left office. He wept blood for three years and only rose with a staff.
entries.literal: On his father's death he left office; he wept blood for three years and only rose with a staff.

entries.zh: 齊武帝謂昉伯遐曰：「聞昉哀瘠過禮，使人憂之，非直亡卿之寶，亦時才可惜。
entries.en: Emperor Wu of Qi told Fang's elder uncle Xia, "I hear Fang's mourning emaciation exceeds the rites and causes worry. It is not only the loss of your treasure but also a pity for the talent of the age.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu of Qi said to Fang's elder uncle Xia, "I hear Fang's mourning emaciation exceeds the rites and causes one worry; it is not only the loss of your treasure but also a pity for the talent of the age.

entries.zh: 宜深相全譬。」
entries.en: You should deeply comfort and instruct him."
entries.literal: You should deeply comfort and instruct him."

entries.zh: 遐使進飲食，當時勉勵，回即歐出。
entries.en: Xia had food and drink brought in and urged him on, but as soon as he returned Fang vomited it out.
entries.literal: Xia had food and drink brought in and at the time urged him on, but as soon as he returned he vomited it out.

entries.zh: 昉父遙本性重檳榔，以為常餌，臨終嘗求之，剖百許口，不得好者，昉亦所嗜好，深以為恨，遂終身不嚐檳榔。
entries.en: Fang's father Yao prized betel nut as a regular food. On his deathbed he once asked for it, but of a hundred or so split open none was good. Fang too was fond of it and deeply regretted this, and never tasted betel nut for the rest of his life.
entries.literal: Fang's father Yao by nature prized betel nut as a regular food; on his deathbed he once asked for it; they split open a hundred or so, but could not find a good one; Fang too was fond of it and deeply regretted this, and therefore never tasted betel nut for his whole life.

entries.zh: 遭繼母憂，昉先以毀瘠，每一慟絕，良久乃蘇，因廬於墓側，以終喪禮。
entries.en: When he met with mourning for his stepmother, Fang had already been emaciated by grief. Each time he wailed he fainted and only after a long while revived. He built a hut by the tomb and completed the mourning rites there.
entries.literal: When he met with mourning for his stepmother, Fang had already been emaciated by grief; each time he wailed he fainted and only after a long while revived; he therefore built a hut by the tomb and completed the mourning rites there.

entries.zh: 哭泣之地，草為不生。
entries.en: At the place of his weeping the grass would not grow.
entries.literal: At the place of his weeping the grass did not grow.

entries.zh: 昉素強壯，腰帶甚充，服闋後不復可識。
entries.en: Fang had always been robust and his waist belt very full. After the mourning period ended he could no longer be recognized.
entries.literal: Fang had always been robust; his waist belt was very full; after the mourning period ended he could no longer be recognized.

entries.zh: 仕齊為太學博士，尚書僕射王晏深相賞好。
entries.en: He served Qi as Erudite of the Imperial Academy. Wang Yan, Vice Director of the Secretariat, deeply appreciated and favored him.
entries.literal: He served Qi as Erudite of the Imperial Academy; Wang Yan, Vice Director of the Secretariat, deeply appreciated and favored him.

entries.zh: 晏為丹陽尹，召補功曹，使撰東宮新記。
entries.en: When Yan was Administrator of Danyang he summoned him to fill the post of merit officer and had him compile a New Record of the Eastern Palace.
entries.literal: When Yan was Administrator of Danyang he summoned him to fill the post of merit officer and had him compile a New Record of the Eastern Palace.

entries.zh: 司徒竟陵王子良開西邸，招文學，僧孺與太學生虞羲、丘國賓、蕭文琰、丘令楷、江洪、劉孝孫並以善辭藻遊焉。
entries.en: The Minister of Education, Prince Jingling, opened the Western Lodge and recruited men of letters. Sengru together with the academy students Yu Xi, Qiu Guobin, Xiao Wenyan, Qiu Lingkai, Jiang Hong, and Liu Xiaosun all gathered there for skill in literary ornament.
entries.literal: The Minister of Education, Prince Jingling, opened the Western Lodge and recruited men of letters; Sengru together with the academy students Yu Xi, Qiu Guobin, Xiao Wenyan, Qiu Lingkai, Jiang Hong, and Liu Xiaosun all wandered there for skill in literary ornament.

entries.zh: 而僧孺與高平徐夤俱為學林。
entries.en: Sengru together with Xu Yin of Gaoping were both pillars of the scholarly grove.
entries.literal: Sengru together with Xu Yin of Gaoping were both forest of learning.

entries.zh: 文惠太子欲以為宮僚，乃召入直崇明殿。
entries.en: Crown Prince Wenhui wished to make him a palace aide and therefore summoned him to attend directly at Chongming Hall.
entries.literal: Crown Prince Wenhui wished to make him a palace aide and therefore summoned him to attend directly at Chongming Hall.

entries.zh: 會薨，出為晉安郡丞，仍除候官令。
entries.en: It happened that the prince died. He went out as assistant magistrate of Jin'an commandery and was then appointed magistrate of Houguan.
entries.literal: It happened that the prince died; he went out as assistant magistrate of Jin'an commandery and was then appointed magistrate of Houguan.

entries.zh: 建武初舉士，為始安王遙光所薦，除儀曹郎，遷書侍御史，出為錢唐令。
entries.en: At the beginning of Jianwu he was nominated as a scholar. Recommended by Prince Yao'guang of Shi'an, he was appointed Gentleman of the Ceremonial Office, transferred to Attending Censor of Documents, and went out as magistrate of Qiantang.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Jianwu he was nominated as a scholar; recommended by Prince Yao'guang of Shi'an, he was appointed Gentleman of the Ceremonial Office, transferred to Attending Censor of Documents, and went out as magistrate of Qiantang.

entries.zh: 初僧孺與樂安任昉遇于竟陵王西邸，以文學會友，及將之縣，昉贈詩曰：「唯子見知，唯餘知子，觀行視言，要終猶始。
entries.en: Earlier Sengru and Ren Fang of Le'an met at Prince Jingling's Western Lodge and formed friendship through literature. When he was about to go to the county, Fang presented a poem saying, "Only you know me, only I know you. Observing conduct and viewing words, the essential end is still like the beginning.
entries.literal: Earlier Sengru and Ren Fang of Le'an met at Prince Jingling's Western Lodge and formed friendship through literature; when he was about to go to the county, Fang presented a poem saying, "Only you know me, only I know you; observing conduct and viewing words, the essential end is still like the beginning.

entries.zh: 敬之重之，如蘭如芷，形應影隨，曩行今止。
entries.en: I revere and value you, like orchid like angelica. Form answers shadow and follows, former conduct now stops.
entries.literal: Revere and value you, like orchid like angelica; form answers shadow and follows, former conduct now stops.

entries.zh: 百行之首，立人斯著，子之有之，誰毀誰譽。
entries.en: The head of the hundred conducts, in establishing a person thus made manifest. You have it—who will slander, who will praise?
entries.literal: The head of the hundred conducts, in establishing a person thus made manifest; you have it—who will slander, who will praise?

entries.zh: 修名既立，老至何遽，誰其執鞭，吾為子禦。
entries.en: Cultivated name already established, old age arrives how swiftly. Who will hold the whip? I will drive for you.
entries.literal: Cultivated name already established, old age arrives how swiftly; who will hold the whip? I will drive for you.

entries.zh: 劉略班藝，虞志荀錄，伊昔有懷，交相欣勖。
entries.en: Liu's outline and Ban's craft, Yu's will and Xun's record—in former days we had these thoughts, mutually rejoicing and urging one another.
entries.literal: Liu's outline and Ban's craft, Yu's will and Xun's record—in former days we had these thoughts, mutually rejoicing and urging one another.

entries.zh: 下帷無倦，升高有屬，嘉爾晨登，惜餘夜燭。」
entries.en: Lowering the curtain without weariness, ascending high with what belongs. I praise your morning climb, regret my remaining night candle."
entries.literal: Lowering the curtain without weariness, ascending high with what belongs; I praise your morning climb, regret my remaining night candle."

entries.zh: 其為士友推重如此。
entries.en: Thus was he esteemed and pushed forward by scholar-friends.
entries.literal: Thus was he esteemed and pushed forward by scholar-friends.

entries.zh: 列傳第四十九
entries.en: Biography Forty-Nine
entries.literal: Biography 49

entries.zh: 休源十一而孤，居喪盡禮，每見父手所寫書，必哀慟流涕不能自勝，見者莫不為之垂泣。
entries.en: Xiuyuan was orphaned at eleven and observed the mourning rites with complete devotion. Whenever he saw books written in his father's hand, he would weep uncontrollably, and those who witnessed his grief wept with him.
entries.literal: Xiuyuan was orphaned at eleven; he observed mourning to the full rites. Whenever he saw books written in his father's hand, he would mourn and weep beyond control; those who saw it all wept for him.

entries.zh: 後就吳興沈麟士受經，略通大義。
entries.en: He later studied the classics under Shen Linshi of Wuxing and gained a general understanding of their essential meaning.
entries.literal: Later he studied the classics under Shen Linshi of Wuxing and gained a general grasp of their essential meaning.

entries.zh: 州舉秀才，太尉徐孝嗣省其策，深善之，謂同坐曰：「董仲舒、華令思何以尚此，可謂後生之准的也。
entries.en: The province recommended him as a cultivated talent. Grand Commandant Xu Xiaosi examined his examination answer and was deeply impressed, saying to those present, "How could Dong Zhongshu or Hua Lingsi surpass this? He is a standard by which later generations may be measured.
entries.literal: The province recommended him as a cultivated talent. Grand Commandant Xu Xiaosi examined his examination answer and deeply approved it, saying to those seated with him: "How could Dong Zhongshu or Hua Lingsi surpass this? He may be called the target for later generations.

entries.zh: 觀此足稱王佐之才。」
entries.en: From this one can see that he truly possesses the talent of a chief minister."
entries.literal: Judging from this, he fully deserves to be called talent for assisting a king."

entries.zh: 琅邪王融雅相友善，乃薦之于司徒竟陵王，為西邸學士。
entries.en: Wang Rong of Langya became his close friend and recommended him to Prince Jingling, Minister of Works, who appointed him a scholar of the Western Lodge.
entries.literal: Wang Rong of Langya was elegantly friendly with him and recommended him to Prince Jingling, Minister of Works, as a scholar of the Western Lodge.

entries.zh: 革幼而聰敏，早有才思，六歲便解屬文。
entries.en: Ge was intelligent from childhood and showed early literary talent; at the age of six he could already compose prose.
entries.literal: Ge from youth was intelligent and keen; early he had literary talent, and at six he could already compose prose.

entries.zh: 柔之深加賞器，曰：「此兒必興吾門。」
entries.en: Rouzhi admired him deeply, saying, "This boy will surely bring honor to our house."
entries.literal: Rouzhi deeply admired him, saying: "This child will surely raise up our house."

entries.zh: 九歲丁父艱，與第四弟觀同生，少孤貧，傍無師友，兄弟自相訓勖，讀書精力不倦。
entries.en: At nine he entered mourning for his father. He and his fourth younger brother Guan, born of the same mother, were orphaned young and poor, with no teachers or friends nearby. The brothers encouraged each other in study and read with tireless energy.
entries.literal: At nine he entered mourning for his father. He and his fourth younger brother Guan were born of the same mother; orphaned young and poor, with no teachers or friends nearby, the brothers encouraged each other in study, reading with tireless energy.

entries.zh: 十六喪母，以孝聞。
entries.en: When his mother died at sixteen, he became renowned for his filial devotion.
entries.literal: At sixteen his mother died; he became known for filial piety.

entries.zh: 服闋，與觀俱詣太學，補國子生，舉高第。
entries.en: When mourning ended, he and Guan both entered the Imperial University as students of the National University and were recommended with the highest marks.
entries.literal: When mourning ended, he and Guan both went to the Imperial University, were enrolled as students of the National University, and were recommended with highest marks.

entries.zh: 齊中書郎王融、吏部郎謝朓雅相欽重。
entries.en: Wang Rong, Director of the Secretariat under Qi, and Xie Tiao, Director of the Personnel Bureau, both deeply admired and esteemed him.
entries.literal: Wang Rong, Director of the Secretariat under Qi, and Xie Tiao, Director of the Personnel Bureau, both deeply admired and esteemed him.

entries.zh: 朓嘗行還過候革，時大寒雪，見革弊絮單席，而耽學不倦，嗟歎久之，乃脫其所著襦，並手割半氈與革充臥具而去。
entries.en: Tiao once returned from a journey and stopped to visit Ge. It was bitterly cold and snowing; he found Ge in worn cotton clothing on a single mat, yet still devoted to study without rest. Tiao sighed at length, then took off his own padded jacket and cut half a felt rug by hand to serve as Ge's bedding before departing.
entries.literal: Tiao once returned from a journey and stopped to visit Ge. It was bitterly cold with snow; he saw Ge in worn cotton and on a single mat, yet devoted to study without weariness. Tiao sighed long, then took off his own padded jacket and with his own hands cut half a felt rug to serve as Ge's bedding before departing.

entries.zh: 司徒竟陵王聞其名，引為西邸學士。
entries.en: Prince Jingling, Minister of Works, heard of him and recruited him as a scholar of the Western Lodge.
entries.literal: Prince Jingling, Minister of Works, heard his name and recruited him as a scholar of the Western Lodge.

entries.zh: 弱冠舉南徐州秀才。
entries.en: At his capping he was recommended as a cultivated talent of South Xuzhou.
entries.literal: At his capping he was recommended as a cultivated talent of South Xuzhou.

entries.zh: 時豫章胡諧之行州事，王融與諧之書令薦革。
entries.en: At the time Hu Xiezhi of Yuzhang was acting in provincial affairs. Wang Rong wrote to Xiezhi instructing him to recommend Ge.
entries.literal: At the time Hu Xiezhi of Yuzhang was acting in provincial affairs; Wang Rong wrote to Xiezhi instructing him to recommend Ge.

entries.zh: 諧之方貢琅邪王泛，便以革代之。
entries.en: Xiezhi had just presented Wang Fan of Langya as tribute and therefore substituted Ge in his place.
entries.literal: Xiezhi had just presented Wang Fan of Langya as tribute and therefore replaced him with Ge.

entries.zh: 僕射江祏深相引接，祏為太子詹事，啟革為丞。
entries.en: Vice Director Jiang Si received him warmly. When Si became Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household, he recommended Ge as assistant.
entries.literal: Vice Director Jiang Si deeply received and welcomed him. When Si became Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household, he recommended Ge as assistant.

entries.zh: 祏時權傾朝右，以革才堪經國，令參掌機務，詔誥文檄皆委以具。
entries.en: At the time Si wielded enormous power at court. Considering Ge's talent fit for governing the state, he had him take part in managing secret affairs. Edicts, proclamations, and dispatches were all entrusted to Ge to draft.
entries.literal: At the time Si's power tilted the right side of the court; considering Ge's talent fit for governing the state, he had him take part in managing secret affairs. Edicts, proclamations, and dispatches were all entrusted to Ge to draft.

entries.zh: 革防杜形跡，外人不知。
entries.en: Ge kept his involvement concealed, and outsiders knew nothing of it.
entries.literal: Ge guarded against revealing traces; outsiders did not know.

entries.zh: 祏誅，賓客皆罹其罪，革獨以智免。
entries.en: When Si was executed, his retainers all suffered for the crime, but Ge alone escaped through his shrewdness.
entries.literal: When Si was executed, his retainers all suffered for the crime; Ge alone escaped through wisdom.

entries.zh: 除尚書駕部郎。
entries.en: He was appointed Director of the Chariot Bureau of the Imperial Secretariat.
entries.literal: He was appointed Director of the Chariot Bureau of the Imperial Secretariat.

entries.zh: 時武陵王紀在東州，頗驕縱，上以臧盾性弱，不能匡正，召革慰遣，乃除武陵王長史、會稽郡丞，行府州事。
entries.en: At the time Prince Wuling Ji was in the eastern province, rather arrogant and unrestrained. The emperor, thinking Zang Dun's nature too weak to correct him, summoned Ge and dispatched him to the post of chief clerk to Prince Wuling, Assistant Administrator of Kuaiji Commandery, and acting prefectural and provincial affairs.
entries.literal: At the time Prince Wuling Ji was in the eastern province, rather arrogant and unrestrained. The emperor, thinking Zang Dun's nature weak and unable to correct him, summoned Ge to comfort and dispatch him, then appointed him chief clerk to Prince Wuling, Assistant Administrator of Kuaiji Commandery, and acting prefectural and provincial affairs.

entries.zh: 革門生故吏家多在東，聞革應至，並賚持緣道迎候。
entries.en: Many of Ge's disciples and former subordinates had homes in the east. Hearing that Ge was coming, they all brought gifts and waited along the road to welcome him.
entries.literal: Many of Ge's disciples and former subordinates had homes in the east; hearing Ge was coming, they all brought gifts and waited along the road to welcome him.

entries.zh: 革曰：「我通不受餉，不容獨當故人筐篚。」
entries.en: Ge said, "I have never accepted gifts; I cannot alone receive my old friends' baskets and boxes."
entries.literal: Ge said: "I have never accepted gifts; I cannot alone receive my old friends' baskets and boxes."

entries.zh: 至鎮唯資公俸，食不兼味。
entries.en: Upon reaching his post he relied only on his official salary and ate no more than one dish at a meal.
entries.literal: Upon reaching his post he relied only on official salary; his meals had no second dish.

entries.zh: 郡境殷廣，辭訟日數百，革分判辯析，曾無疑滯，人安吏畏，百城震恐。
entries.en: The commandery's territory was broad and populous, with hundreds of lawsuits each day. Ge divided, judged, and analyzed them without hesitation. The people were at peace, the clerks feared him, and the hundred cities trembled in awe.
entries.literal: The commandery's territory was broad and populous; lawsuits numbered hundreds each day. Ge divided, judged, and analyzed them without ever hesitating. The people were at peace and the clerks feared him; the hundred cities trembled in awe.

entries.zh: 琅邪王騫為山陰令，贓貨狼籍，望風自解。
entries.en: Prince Qian of Langya served as magistrate of Shanyin, his ill-gotten goods scattered everywhere. At the news of Ge's arrival he resigned of his own accord.
entries.literal: Prince Qian of Langya served as magistrate of Shanyin, his ill-gotten goods scattered everywhere; at the news he resigned of his own accord.

entries.zh: 府王憚之。
entries.en: The prince of the domain feared him.
entries.literal: The prince of the domain feared him.

entries.zh: 每侍燕，言論必以詩、書，王因此耽學好文。
entries.en: Whenever he attended banquets, his discourse always drew on the Book of Songs and the Book of Documents. Because of this the prince became devoted to study and fond of literature.
entries.literal: Whenever he attended banquets, his discourse always drew on the Book of Songs and the Book of Documents; because of this the prince became devoted to study and fond of literature.

entries.zh: 典簽沈熾文以王所制詩呈武帝，帝謂僕射徐勉曰：「革果稱職。」
entries.en: Chief Clerk Shen Chiwen presented to Emperor Wu poems composed by the prince. The emperor said to Vice Director Xu Mian, "Ge truly fills his post."
entries.literal: Chief Clerk Shen Chiwen presented to Emperor Wu poems composed by the prince. The emperor said to Vice Director Xu Mian: "Ge truly fills his post."

entries.zh: 乃除都官尚書。
entries.en: He then appointed him Minister of Justice.
entries.literal: He then appointed him Minister of Justice.

entries.zh: 將還，贈遺一無所受，送故依舊訂舫，革並不納，唯乘台所給一舸。
entries.en: When about to return, he accepted no gifts whatsoever. The farewell escort arranged boats as usual, but Ge accepted none and took only the single skiff provided by the administration.
entries.literal: When about to return, he accepted no gifts whatsoever. The farewell escort arranged boats as usual, but Ge accepted none and took only the single skiff provided by the administration.

entries.zh: 舸艚偏欹，不得安臥。
entries.en: The skiff listed to one side and he could not lie down in comfort.
entries.literal: The skiff listed to one side and he could not lie down in comfort.

entries.zh: 或請濟江徙重物以迮輕艚，革既無物，乃於西陵岸取石十餘片以實之。
entries.en: Someone suggested crossing the river and moving heavy objects to ballast the light skiff. Ge had no possessions, so he took more than ten stones from the bank at Xiling to fill it.
entries.literal: Someone suggested crossing the river and moving heavy objects to ballast the light skiff. Ge had no possessions, so he took more than ten stones from the bank at Xiling to fill it.

entries.zh: 其清貧如此。
entries.en: Such was his purity and poverty.
entries.literal: Such was his purity and poverty.

entries.zh: 武陵王出鎮江州，乃曰：「我得江革文，得革清貧，豈能一日忘之，當與其同飽。」
entries.en: When Prince Wuling went out to command Jiangzhou, he said, "I have gained Jiang Ge's writing and gained Ge's purity and poverty—how can I forget this for a single day? I shall share my table with him."
entries.literal: When Prince Wuling went out to command Jiangzhou, he said: "I have gained Jiang Ge's writing and gained Ge's purity and poverty—how can I forget this for a single day? I shall share fullness with him."

entries.zh: 乃表革同行。
entries.en: He then memorialized requesting Ge to accompany him.
entries.literal: He then memorialized requesting Ge to accompany him.

entries.zh: 除南中郎長史、尋陽太守。
entries.en: Ge was appointed chief clerk of the Southern Palace Guard and Administrator of Xunyang.
entries.literal: Ge was appointed chief clerk of the Southern Palace Guard and Administrator of Xunyang.

entries.zh: 征入為度支尚書。
entries.en: He was summoned to the capital as Minister of Revenue.
entries.literal: He was summoned to the capital as Minister of Revenue.

entries.zh: 好獎進閭閻，為後生延譽，由是衣冠士子翕然歸之。
entries.en: He loved to encourage and advance men of the lanes and wards, extending reputation for younger generations. Thereby gentry and scholars converged upon him.
entries.literal: He loved to encourage and advance men of the lanes and wards, extending reputation for younger generations; thereby gentry and scholars converged upon him.

entries.zh: 時尚書令何敬容掌選，序用多非其人。
entries.en: At the time Director of the Imperial Secretariat He Jingrong managed selection, and many of those he appointed were not the right men.
entries.literal: At the time Director of the Imperial Secretariat He Jingrong managed selection, and many of those he appointed in order were not the right men.

entries.zh: 革性強直，每朝宴恒有褒貶，以此為權貴所疾。
entries.en: Ge's nature was forceful and upright. At every court banquet he always had praise and blame to offer, and for this the powerful and noble resented him.
entries.literal: Ge's nature was forceful and upright; at every court banquet he always had praise and blame, and for this was resented by the powerful and noble.

entries.zh: 乃謝病還家，除光祿大夫，優遊閑放，以文酒自娛。
entries.en: He then pleaded illness and returned home. Appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, he lived at leisure and found pleasure in literature and wine.
entries.literal: He then pleaded illness and returned home, was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and lived at leisure in ease, finding pleasure in literature and wine.

entries.zh: 卒，諡曰強子。
entries.en: When he died, he was given the posthumous name Qiangzi.
entries.literal: When he died, his posthumous title was Qiangzi.

entries.zh: 有集二十卷行於世。
entries.en: His collected works of twenty scrolls circulated widely.
entries.literal: He had a collection of writings of twenty scrolls circulating in the world.

entries.zh: 革曆官八府長史，四王行事，三為二千石，傍無姬侍，家徒壁立，時以此高之。
entries.en: Ge successively served as chief clerk in eight princely administrations, acted in affairs for four princes, and three times held the rank of two-thousand-dan official. He had no concubines at his side and his household was bare as walls; the age honored him for this.
entries.literal: Ge successively served as chief clerk in eight princely administrations, acted in affairs for four princes, three times held the rank of two-thousand-dan official, had no concubines at his side, and his household was bare as walls; the age honored him for this.

entries.zh: 長子行敏早卒，次子德藻。
entries.en: His eldest son Xingmin died early; his second son was Dezao.
entries.literal: His eldest son Xingmin died early; his second son was Dezao.

entries.zh: 勉幼孤貧，早勵清節。
entries.en: Mian was orphaned young and poor, and early cultivated purity of conduct.
entries.literal: Mian was orphaned young and poor, and early cultivated purity of conduct.

entries.zh: 年六歲，屬霖雨，家人祈霽，率爾為文，見稱耆宿。
entries.en: At six, during prolonged rain, when the family prayed for clear skies, he spontaneously composed a text and was praised by elders.
entries.literal: At six, during prolonged rain, when the family prayed for clear skies, he spontaneously composed a text and was praised by elders.

entries.zh: 及長好學，宗人孝嗣見之歎曰：「此所謂人中之騏驥，必能致千里。」
entries.en: When grown he loved learning. His clansman Xiaosi saw him and sighed, saying, "This is what they call a thoroughbred among men—he will surely reach a thousand li."
entries.literal: When grown he loved learning. His clansman Xiaosi saw him and sighed, saying: "This is what they call a thoroughbred among men—he will surely reach a thousand li."

entries.zh: 又嘗謂諸子曰：「此人師也，爾等則而行之。」
entries.en: He also once told his sons, "This man is a teacher; you should take him as your model and follow him."
entries.literal: He also once told his sons: "This man is a teacher; you should take him as your model and follow him."

entries.zh: 年十八，召為國子生，便下帷專學，精力無怠。
entries.en: At eighteen he was summoned as a student of the National University, drew the curtain and devoted himself to study, his energy never slackening.
entries.literal: At eighteen he was summoned as a student of the National University, drew the curtain and devoted himself to study, his energy never slackening.

entries.zh: 同時儕輩肅而敬之。
entries.en: Contemporaries of the same generation were solemn and respectful toward him.
entries.literal: Contemporaries of the same generation were solemn and respectful toward him.

entries.zh: 祭酒王儉每見，常目送之，曰：「此子非常器也。」
entries.en: Chancellor Wang Jian whenever he saw him would gaze after him and say, "This youth is no ordinary vessel."
entries.literal: Chancellor Wang Jian whenever he saw him would gaze after him and say: "This youth is no ordinary vessel."

entries.zh: 每稱有宰輔之量。
entries.en: He often declared that Mian had the capacity of a chief minister.
entries.literal: He often declared that Mian had the capacity of a chief minister.

entries.zh: 射策甲科，起家王國侍郎，補太學博士。
entries.en: In the archery-and-policy examination he ranked in the top class. He began his career as Gentleman of a princely domain and was appointed erudite of the Imperial University.
entries.literal: In the archery-and-policy examination he ranked in the top class. He began his career as Gentleman of a princely domain and was appointed erudite of the Imperial University.

entries.zh: 時每有議定，勉理證明允，莫能貶奪，同官咸取則焉。
entries.en: Whenever there was deliberation and decision at the time, Mian's reasoning was clear and fair. None could diminish or overturn it, and colleagues all took him as their standard.
entries.literal: Whenever there was deliberation and decision at the time, Mian's reasoning was clear and fair; none could diminish or overturn it, and colleagues all took him as their standard.

entries.zh: 遷臨海王西中郎田曹行參軍，俄徙署都曹。
entries.en: He was transferred to Acting Military Affairs Aide in the Field Bureau of the Western Palace Guard under Prince Linhai, and soon moved to serve in the Capital Bureau.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Acting Military Affairs Aide in the Field Bureau of the Western Palace Guard under Prince Linhai, and soon moved to serve in the Capital Bureau.

entries.zh: 時琅邪王融一時才俊，特相慕悅，嘗請交焉。
entries.en: At the time Wang Rong of Langya was a leading talent of the age and especially admired him, once requesting friendship.
entries.literal: At the time Wang Rong of Langya was a leading talent of the age and especially admired and delighted in him, once requesting friendship.

entries.zh: 勉謂所親曰：「王郎名高望促，難可輕霹衣裾。」
entries.en: Mian said to those close to him, "Master Wang's fame is high but his prospects are short; one cannot lightly attach oneself to his hem."
entries.literal: Mian said to those close to him: "Master Wang's fame is high but his prospects are short; one cannot lightly attach oneself to his hem."

entries.zh: 融後果陷於法，以此見推識鑒。
entries.en: Rong later indeed fell afoul of the law; for this Mian was praised for his discernment.
entries.literal: Rong later indeed fell afoul of the law; for this Mian was praised for his discernment.

entries.zh: 累遷領軍長史。
entries.en: He was repeatedly promoted to chief clerk of the Army of the Guard.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to chief clerk of the Army of the Guard.

entries.zh: 後為左衛將軍，領太子中庶子，侍東宮。
entries.en: Later he served as General of the Left Guard, concurrently Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household, attending the Eastern Palace.
entries.literal: Later he served as General of the Left Guard, concurrently Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household, attending the Eastern Palace.

entries.zh: 昭明太子尚幼，敕知宮事，太子禮之甚重，每事詢謀。
entries.en: Crown Prince Zhaoming was still young. By edict Mian was ordered to manage palace affairs. The crown prince honored him greatly and consulted him on every matter.
entries.literal: Crown Prince Zhaoming was still young; by edict Mian was ordered to manage palace affairs. The crown prince honored him greatly and consulted him on every matter.

entries.zh: 嘗於殿講孝經，臨川王宏、尚書令沈約備二傅，勉與國子祭酒張充為執經，王瑩、張稷、柳憕、王暕為侍講。
entries.en: Once in the hall he lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety. Prince Linchuan Hong and Director of the Imperial Secretariat Shen Yue served as the two mentors; Mian and Chancellor of the Imperial University Zhang Chong held the classic; Wang Ying, Zhang Ji, Liu Zong, and Wang Yan served as lecture attendants.
entries.literal: Once in the hall he lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety. Prince Linchuan Hong and Director of the Imperial Secretariat Shen Yue served as the two mentors; Mian and Chancellor of the Imperial University Zhang Chong held the classic; Wang Ying, Zhang Ji, Liu Zong, and Wang Yan served as lecture attendants.

entries.zh: 時選極親賢，妙盡人譽。
entries.en: The selection at the time drew on the closest kin and worthiest men, winning universal praise.
entries.literal: The selection at the time was of the closest kin and worthiest men, wonderfully exhausting human praise.

entries.zh: 勉陳讓數四，又與沈約書，求換侍講，詔弗許，然後就焉。
entries.en: Mian declined several times, then wrote to Shen Yue requesting to exchange for lecture attendant. An edict did not permit it, and only then did he take up the post.
entries.literal: Mian declined several times, then wrote to Shen Yue requesting to exchange for lecture attendant; an edict did not permit it, and only then did he take up the post.

entries.zh: 舊揚、徐首迎主簿，盡選國華中正，取勉子崧充南徐選首。
entries.en: By old custom the chief clerks who welcomed the prince in Yang and Xu were all selected from the finest men of the state. Mian's son Song was chosen to fill the South Xu selection chief.
entries.literal: By old custom the chief clerks who welcomed the prince in Yang and Xu were all selected from the finest men of the state; Mian's son Song was chosen to fill the South Xu selection chief.

entries.zh: 帝敕之曰：「卿寒士，而子與王志子同迎，偃王以來未之有也。」
entries.en: The emperor instructed him, "You are a humble scholar, yet your son welcomes the prince together with Wang Zhi's son—since King Yan there has been nothing like it."
entries.literal: The emperor instructed him: "You are a humble scholar, yet your son welcomes the prince together with Wang Zhi's son—since King Yan there has been nothing like it."

entries.zh: 勉恥以其先為戲，答旨不恭，由是左遷散騎常侍，領遊擊將軍。
entries.en: Mian was ashamed that his ancestors were made a jest. His reply to the edict was disrespectful, and for this he was demoted to Regular Attendant and concurrently General of the Mobile Corps.
entries.literal: Mian was ashamed that his ancestors were made a jest; his reply to the edict was disrespectful, and for this he was demoted to Regular Attendant and concurrently General of the Mobile Corps.

entries.zh: 列傳第五十
entries.en: the 50th year of Biographies
entries.literal: Biographies, number fifty.

entries.zh: 神念少善騎射，及老不衰。
entries.en: Shennian had been skilled in horsemanship and archery since youth, and even in old age he had not lost his edge.
entries.literal: Shennian from youth was skilled in mounted archery, and even when old he did not decline.

entries.zh: 嘗于武帝前手執二刀楯，左右交度，馭馬往來，冠絕群伍。
entries.en: Once before Emperor Wu he took two sabers and shields in hand, crossing them left and right as he drove his horse to and fro—a feat unmatched in the whole company.
entries.literal: Once before Emperor Wu he held two sabers and shields in his hands, crossing them left and right, driving his horse back and forth, surpassing all the ranks.

entries.zh: 時復有楊華者，能作驚軍騎，亦一時妙捷，帝深賞之。
entries.en: At the same time there was Yang Hua, who could perform startling cavalry feats—another marvel of the day whom the Emperor greatly admired.
entries.literal: At the same time there was also Yang Hua, who could perform startling cavalry maneuvers; he too was a marvel of agility for the age, and the Emperor deeply admired him.

entries.zh: 華本名白花，武都仇池人。
entries.en: Hua had originally been named Bai Hua and came from Chouchi in Wudu.
entries.literal: Hua's original name was Bai Hua; he was a man of Chouchi in Wudu.

entries.zh: 父大眼為魏名將。
entries.en: His father Dahuan was a celebrated Wei general.
entries.literal: His father Dahuan was a famous general of Wei.

entries.zh: 華少有勇力，容貌瑰偉，魏胡太后逼幸之。
entries.en: In youth Hua was brave and powerfully built, with a striking appearance; Empress Dowager Hu of the Northern Wei took him as her lover.
entries.literal: Hua in youth had courage and strength, and his appearance was magnificent; Empress Dowager Hu of Wei forced her favor upon him.

entries.zh: 華懼禍，及大眼死，擁部曲，載父屍，改名華，來降。
entries.en: Fearing ruin, Hua waited until Dahuan died, then gathered his followers, bore his father's body away, changed his name to Hua, and defected to the Liang.
entries.literal: Hua feared disaster; when Dahuan died he gathered his troops, loaded his father's corpse, changed his name to Hua, and came to surrender.

entries.zh: 胡太后追思不已，為作楊白花歌辭，使宮人晝夜連臂蹋蹄歌之，聲甚淒斷。
entries.en: Empress Dowager Hu could not stop mourning him; she had the lyrics of the Song of Yang Bai Hua written and set palace women to link arms and stamp their feet in song day and night—the melody was heartbreakingly sad.
entries.literal: Empress Dowager Hu could not cease her longing and composed the lyrics of the Song of Yang Bai Hua, ordering palace women day and night to link arms and stamp their feet singing it; the sound was exceedingly mournful and broken.

entries.zh: 華後位太子左衛率，卒于侯景軍中。
entries.en: Hua later served as Commander of the Left Guard of the Heir Apparent and died in Hou Jing's forces.
entries.literal: Hua later held the post of Commander of the Left Guard of the Heir Apparent and died in Hou Jing's army.

entries.zh: 先是，天監中沙門釋寶志為讖云：「太歲龍，將無理。
entries.en: Earlier, during the Tianjian reign, the monk Baozhi uttered a prophecy: "When the Tai Sui year is the Dragon, the leader will lose legitimacy.
entries.literal: Earlier, in the Tianjian era, the monk Shi Baozhi made a prophecy saying: "In the year of the Dragon of Tai Sui, the general will be without reason.

entries.zh: 蕭經霜，草應死。
entries.en: The House of Xiao passes through frost; the grass must wither.
entries.literal: The Xiao clan meets frost; the grass should die.

entries.zh: 餘人散，十八子。」
entries.en: The commoners disperse; 'ten,' 'eight,' and 'son.'"
entries.literal: The rest of the people scatter; eighteen sons."

entries.zh: 時言蕭氏當滅，李氏代興。
entries.en: People read the verses as foretelling the fall of the Xiao and the rise of the Li.
entries.literal: At the time it was said the Xiao clan would perish and the Li clan would rise in its place.

entries.zh: 及湘州賊陸納等攻破衡州刺史丁道貴，而李洪雅又自零陵稱助討納。
entries.en: When the rebel Lu Na of Xiangzhou overran Hengzhou and its inspector Ding Daogui, Li Hongya proclaimed from Lingling that he had come to help crush Na.
entries.literal: When the Xiangzhou rebels Lu Na and others attacked and broke Hengzhou Inspector Ding Daogui, Li Hongya moreover from Lingling declared himself aiding in punishing Na.

entries.zh: 既而朝廷未達其心，詔征僧辯就宜豐侯循南征，為都督東上諸軍事。
entries.en: The court still misread his intentions and ordered Senbian to march south with the Marquis of Yifeng, appointing him commander of all eastern armies.
entries.literal: Soon the court did not fathom his heart; an edict summoned Senbian to join Marquis Xun of Yifeng in a southern campaign, making him Commander-in-Chief of all eastern forces.

entries.zh: 以陳武帝為都督西下諸軍事。
entries.en: Chen Wudi was placed in command of all western forces.
entries.literal: Chen Wudi was made Commander-in-Chief of all western-downward military affairs.

entries.zh: 先是，陳武讓都督于僧辯，僧辯不受，故元帝分為東西都督而俱南討焉。
entries.en: Earlier Chen Wu had offered Senbian supreme command, which Senbian refused; Emperor Yuan therefore split command into eastern and western wings and sent both south.
entries.literal: Earlier, Chen Wu had yielded the commandership to Senbian, but Senbian did not accept; therefore Emperor Yuan divided east and west commanderships and both marched south to punish.

entries.zh: 尋而洪雅降納，納以為應符，於是共議拜洪雅為大將軍，尊事為主。
entries.en: Hongya soon joined Na, who took this as confirmation of the prophecy; the rebels then agreed to make Hongya their generalissimo and acknowledged him as their sovereign.
entries.literal: Soon Hongya surrendered to Na; Na took it as fulfillment of the prophecy, and they jointly deliberated to invest Hongya as Grand General and honor him as lord.

entries.zh: 洪雅乘平肩大輿，傘蓋、鼓吹，羽儀悉備，翼從入長沙城。
entries.en: Hongya entered Changsha in a state carriage with parasols, musical escort, and full ceremonial guard.
entries.literal: Hongya rode a level-shoulder great carriage; parasols, canopies, drums and pipes—all regalia fully prepared—he entered Changsha city with wings of attendants.

entries.zh: 時納等據車輪，夾岸為城，士卒皆百戰之餘，器甲精嚴，徒黨勇銳，蒙沖鬥艦，亙水陵山。
entries.en: Na held Chelun, fortifying both banks; his troops were hardened veterans with superb arms, his followers fierce, and his covered ships lined the waterway from shore to hill.
entries.literal: At the time Na and others held Chelun, building walls on both banks; the soldiers were all veterans of a hundred battles, weapons and armor exquisitely strict, followers brave and sharp, covered raiders and fighting ships spanning water and overrunning hills.

entries.zh: 時天日清明，初無雲霧，軍發之際，忽然風雨，時人謂為泣軍，百姓竊言知其敗也。
entries.en: The sky had been clear, yet the moment the army marched a storm broke; people called it the army weeping, and locals whispered that defeat was foretold.
entries.literal: At the time heaven's sun was clear and bright, at first without cloud or mist; at the moment the army set out, suddenly wind and rain—people of the time called it a weeping army, and common people whispered that they knew defeat was coming.

entries.zh: 三月庚寅，有兩龍自城西江中騰躍升天，五色分明，遙映江水。
entries.en: On the third month's gengyin day, two dragons rose from the river west of the city into the sky, their five colors vivid against the distant water.
entries.literal: On the gengyin day of the third month, two dragons leapt from the river west of the city soaring up to heaven, five colors distinct, reflecting distantly in the river water.

entries.zh: 百姓咸仰面目之，父老或聚而悲，竊相謂曰：「地龍已去，國其亡乎。」
entries.en: People gazed up at them; some elders wept together and murmured: "The earth dragons have gone—surely the realm is doomed."
entries.literal: The common people all looked up at their faces; elders sometimes gathered and wept, whispering to one another: "The earth dragons have departed—will the state perish?"

entries.zh: 初，納造大艦，一名曰三王艦者，邵陵王、河東王、桂陽嗣王三人並為元帝所害，故立其像於艦，祭乙太牢，加其節蓋羽儀鼓吹，每戰輒祭之以求福。
entries.en: Na had built a great warship, the Three Kings Ship, for the three princes Shaoling, Hedong, and Guiyang whom Emperor Yuan had killed; he set up their images aboard, sacrificed oxen to them with full honors, and before every battle offered prayers for luck.
entries.literal: Earlier, Na built a great ship called the Three Kings Ship—for the Prince of Shaoling, Prince of Hedong, and Prince of Guiyang, three men all killed by Emperor Yuan—therefore he erected their images on the ship, offering yi and ta lao sacrifices, adding their banners, canopies, regalia, drums and pipes; before each battle he would sacrifice to them seeking fortune.

entries.zh: 又造二艦，一曰青龍艦，一曰白虎艦，皆衣以牛皮，並高十五丈，選其中尤勇健者乘之。
entries.en: He also built two tower ships, the Azure Dragon and the White Tiger, sheathed in ox hide and fifteen zhang tall, crewed by his fiercest warriors.
entries.literal: He also built two ships—one called the Azure Dragon Ship, one called the White Tiger Ship—both clad in ox hide, each fifteen zhang high, selecting from among them the most courageous and strong to man them.

entries.zh: 僧辯憚之，稍作連城以逼焉。
entries.en: Senbian, wary of these vessels, began building linked fortifications to press in on them.
entries.literal: Senbian feared them, and slightly built linked ramparts to press upon them.

entries.zh: 賊不敢交鋒，並懷懈怠。
entries.en: The rebels would not engage and grew complacent.
entries.literal: The rebels did not dare cross blades, and all harbored slackness.

entries.zh: 僧辯因其無備，親執旗鼓以誡進止，群賊大敗，歸保長沙。
entries.en: Senbian seized their negligence, personally directing the drums and banners; the rebels were routed and fled back to Changsha.
entries.literal: Senbian, because they were unprepared, personally took drum and banner to admonish advance and halt; the rebel host was greatly defeated and returned to defend Changsha.

entries.zh: 僧辯乃命築壘圍之，而自出臨視。
entries.en: Senbian ordered siege works built and went out personally to supervise them.
entries.literal: Senbian then ordered building ramparts to besiege them, and himself went out to oversee in person.

entries.zh: 賊知不設備，其党吳藏、李賢明等蒙楯直進，僧辯尚據胡床不為之動，指麾勇敢，遂斬賢明，賊乃退歸。
entries.en: The rebels thought him undefended; Wu Zang, Li Xianming, and others charged under shield cover. Senbian did not rise from his camp chair, coolly directing the fight until Xianming was slain and the attackers fell back.
entries.literal: The rebels, knowing he was unguarded, his partisans Wu Zang, Li Xianming and others covered with shields advanced straight on; Senbian still sat on a folding camp chair unmoved, directing with bravery, and thereupon cut down Xianming—the rebels then withdrew.

entries.zh: 初，陵納作逆，以王琳為辭，云：「若放琳則自服」。
entries.en: When Lu Na first rebelled, he declared: "If Wang Lin were freed, I would submit."
entries.literal: Earlier, when Lu Na rebelled, he used Wang Lin as his pretext, saying: "If Lin is released, I will submit myself."

entries.zh: 時眾軍未之許，而武陵王紀擁眾上流，內外駭懼。
entries.en: The allied armies refused, even as Prince Ji of Wuling massed forces upriver; court and camp alike were terrified.
entries.literal: At the time the various armies did not agree to it, while Prince Ji of Wuling gathered troops upstream; inside and outside were alarmed and fearful.

entries.zh: 元帝乃遣琳和解之，湘州乃平。
entries.en: Emperor Yuan dispatched Wang Lin to negotiate; Xiangzhou was finally pacified.
entries.literal: Emperor Yuan then sent Lin to mediate and reconcile; Xiangzhou was then pacified.

entries.zh: 因被詔會眾軍西討。
entries.en: He was then ordered to gather the armies for the western campaign.
entries.literal: Thereupon he received an edict to assemble the armies for a western punitive campaign.

entries.zh: 尋而武陵敗績。
entries.en: Prince Ji of Wuling was soon crushed.
entries.literal: Soon Wuling suffered defeat.

entries.zh: 初，僧辯平建鄴，遣陳武守京口，推以赤心，結廉、藺之分。
entries.en: After Senbian pacified Jiankang, he placed Chen Wu at Jingkou in the trust of sworn friendship, like Lian Po and Lin Xiangru.
entries.literal: Earlier, when Senbian pacified Jiankang, he sent Chen Wu to guard Jingkou, extending with a red heart, forming the bond of Lian and Lin.

entries.zh: 且為第三子頠許娶陳武章後所生女，未昏而僧辯母亡，然情好甚密，其長子顗屢諫不聽。
entries.en: He even betrothed his third son Yi to Chen Wu's daughter by Lady Zhang; though Senbian's mother died before the wedding, the two remained intimate, despite repeated warnings from his eldest son Yan.
entries.literal: Moreover he betrothed his third son Yi to the daughter born to Chen Wu's wife Zhang; before marriage Senbian's mother died, yet their affection was very close; his eldest son Yan repeatedly remonstrated but was not heeded.

entries.zh: 至是，會江淮人報云：「齊兵大舉至壽春」，僧辯謂齊軍必出江表，因遣記室參軍江旰以事報陳武，仍使整舟艦器械。
entries.en: Just then a man from the Jiang-Huai region reported: "Qi troops are massing at Shouchun"; Senbian assumed they would cross the Yangtze and sent his secretary Jiang Gan to inform Chen Wu and prepare the fleet.
entries.literal: At this point, a person from the Jiang-Huai region reported: "Qi troops in great force have reached Shouchun"; Senbian thought Qi army would surely come out onto the Jiang region, and therefore sent Recorder of the Headquarters Jiang Gan to report the matter to Chen Wu, still ordering him to put ships and weapons in order.

entries.zh: 陳武宿有圖僧辯志，乃聞命，留旰城中，銜枚而進。
entries.en: Chen Wu had long planned Senbian's downfall; he kept Gan in the city and marched silently on Stone City.
entries.literal: Chen Wu had long harbored intent to plot against Senbian; upon hearing the order, he kept Gan in the city and advanced with gags in mouths.

entries.zh: 知謀者唯侯安都、周文育而已，外人但謂江旰徵兵扞北。
entries.en: Only Hou Andu and Zhou Wenyu knew the real plan; everyone else thought Jiang Gan was simply mobilizing against the northern threat.
entries.literal: Those who knew the plot were only Hou Andu and Zhou Wenyu; outsiders merely thought Jiang Gan was raising troops to repel the north.

entries.zh: 安都舟艦將趣石頭，陳武控馬未進。
entries.en: As Hou Andu's fleet bore down on Stone City, Chen Wu held his horse back and would not advance.
entries.literal: Andu's ships and warships were about to make for Stone City; Chen Wu reined his horse and did not advance.

entries.zh: 安都大懼，乃追陳武罵曰：「今日作賊，事勢已成，生死須決，在後欲何所望？
entries.en: Terrified, Hou Andu galloped after Chen Wu and shouted: "We are rebels today and there is no turning back—if we fail we die together; what do you expect by hanging back?
entries.literal: Andu was greatly afraid; he then pursued Chen Wu and cursed: "Today we play rebel—the situation is already settled; life and death must be decided; hanging back, what do you hope for?

entries.zh: 若敗俱死，後期得免斫頭邪？」
entries.en: If we lose we all die—do you think hanging back will save your neck?"
entries.literal: If defeated we die together—do you think hanging back will spare you beheading?"

entries.zh: 陳武曰：「安都嗔我。」
entries.en: Chen Wu said: "Andu is furious with me."
entries.literal: Chen Wu said: "Andu is angry at me."

entries.zh: 乃敢進，遂克之，時壽春竟無齊軍，又非陳武之譎，殆天授也。
entries.en: Only then did he advance and take the city; as it happened there were no Qi troops at Shouchun at all—it was no ruse of Chen Wu's, but almost as if heaven had granted him the moment.
entries.literal: Only then did he dare advance, and thus captured it; at the time Shouchun ultimately had no Qi army, and it was not Chen Wu's stratagem—perhaps heaven conferred it.

entries.zh: 顗承聖初位侍中，魏克江陵，隨王琳入齊，為竟陵郡守。
entries.en: Yan became Palace Attendant early in the Chengsheng era; when Wei conquered Jiangling he went north with Wang Lin and served as governor of Jingling.
entries.literal: Yan in the beginning of Chengsheng held Palace Attendant; when Wei took Jiangling, he followed Wang Lin into Qi and served as Administrator of Jingling Commandery.

entries.zh: 齊遣王琳鎮壽春，將圖江左。
entries.en: Qi sent Wang Lin to hold Shouchun, aiming to reconquer the south.
entries.literal: Qi dispatched Wang Lin to garrison Shouchun, intending to scheme against the Jiang left bank.

entries.zh: 及陳平淮南殺琳，顗聞之，乃出郡城南登高塚上，號哭一慟而絕。
entries.en: When Chen conquered Huainan and killed Wang Lin, Yan climbed a mound south of the city, gave one great cry of grief, and died on the spot.
entries.literal: When Chen pacified Huainan and killed Lin, Yan heard of it; he then went south of the commandery city and climbed a high mound, wailing one great grief and expiring.

entries.zh: 顗弟頒，少有志節，恒隨梁元帝。
entries.en: Yan's younger brother Ban was spirited from youth and always followed Emperor Yuan of Liang.
entries.literal: Yan's younger brother Ban, from youth had aspiration and integrity, always following Liang Emperor Yuan.

entries.zh: 及荊州覆滅，入于魏。
entries.en: When Jingzhou fell he passed into Wei territory.
entries.literal: When Jingzhou was overthrown and destroyed, he entered into Wei.

entries.zh: 僧辯既亡，弟僧智得就任約。
entries.en: After Senbian's death, his brother Sengzhi joined Ren Yue.
entries.literal: After Senbian had perished, his younger brother Sengzhi obtained Ren Yue's appointment.

entries.zh: 敗走，僧智肥不能行，又遇害。
entries.en: In defeat Sengzhi fled, but he was too heavy to run and was killed.
entries.literal: Defeated, he fled; Sengzhi was fat and could not walk, and again met with harm.

entries.zh: 侃以大通三年至建鄴，授徐州刺史，並其兄默及三弟忱、給、元皆拜刺史。
entries.en: Kan reached Jianye in the third year of Datong. He was made governor of Xuzhou, and his elder brother Mo and younger brothers Chen, Gei, and Yuan were each given a provincial governorship as well.
entries.literal: Kan in the third year of Datong arrived at Jianye; he was appointed Governor of Xuzhou, and together with his elder brother Mo and his three younger brothers Chen, Gei, and Yuan all were invested as governors.

entries.zh: 侃封高昌縣侯，累遷太子左衛率，中。
entries.en: He was created Marquis of Gaoxiang County and rose in successive appointments to Left Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard.
entries.literal: He was created Marquis of Gaoxiang County and rose in successive appointments to Left Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard.

entries.zh: 車駕幸樂游苑，侃預宴。
entries.en: When the emperor visited Leyou Park, Kan was among those invited to the feast.
entries.literal: The imperial carriage visited Leyou Park; Kan was present at the banquet.

entries.zh: 時少府奏新造兩刃矟成，長二丈四尺，圍一尺三寸。
entries.en: The Chamberlain of Palace Revenues announced that a new double-edged spear had been completed: twenty-four feet long with a shaft a foot and three inches around.
entries.literal: At that time the Chamberlain for the Palace Revenues reported that a newly made double-edged spear was complete — length two zhang four chi, girth one chi three cun.

entries.zh: 帝因賜侃河南國紫騮令試之。
entries.en: The emperor gave Kan a famed purple horse from Henan and told him to put the weapon through its paces.
entries.literal: The emperor thereupon bestowed on Kan a purple stallion from Henan Commandery and ordered him to test it.

entries.zh: 侃執矟上馬，左右擊刺，特盡其妙。
entries.en: Kan mounted with the spear in hand and struck right and left with perfect mastery of the weapon.
entries.literal: Kan took the spear, mounted, and thrust and stabbed to left and right, displaying its artistry to the utmost.

entries.zh: 觀者登樹。
entries.en: Spectators scrambled up into the trees for a better view.
entries.literal: Those watching climbed trees.

entries.zh: 帝曰：「此樹必為侍中折矣。」
entries.en: The emperor remarked, "That tree won't survive the Attendant-in-Ordinary's display."
entries.literal: The emperor said: "This tree will surely be broken by the Attendant-in-Ordinary."

entries.zh: 俄而果折，因號此矟為折樹矟。
entries.en: Sure enough, the tree soon snapped, and from then on the spear was called the Tree-Breaker.
entries.literal: Before long it indeed broke, and so this spear was named the Tree-Breaking Spear.

entries.zh: 北人降者，唯侃是衣冠餘緒，帝寵之踰於他者，謂曰：「朕少時捉矟，形勢似卿，今失其舊體，殊覺不奇。」
entries.en: Of all the northern defectors, only Kan came from the old gentry in cap and gown. The emperor favored him above the rest and said, "When I was young my spear-play looked much like yours. These days I've lost that old form, and by comparison nothing seems quite so marvelous."
entries.literal: Among northerners who had surrendered, only Kan was descended from the robe-and-cap elite; the emperor favored him beyond the others and said: "In my youth when I wielded the spear my form resembled yours; now having lost my former build, I find it quite lacking in wonder."

entries.zh: 上又制武宴詩三十韻示侃，侃即席上應詔。
entries.en: The emperor then composed a thirty-couplet poem for the martial banquet and presented it to Kan, who answered on the spot from his seat.
entries.literal: The emperor also composed a thirty-rhyme Martial Banquet Poem and showed it to Kan; Kan immediately at the feast responded to the imperial command.

entries.zh: 帝覽曰：「吾聞仁者有勇，今見勇者有仁，可謂鄒、魯遺風，英賢不絕。」
entries.en: After reading it the emperor said, "They say the humane are brave; today I see bravery joined with humanity — the spirit of the sages of Zou and Lu still lives, and worthy men are not extinct."
entries.literal: The emperor on reading said: "I have heard that the benevolent have courage; now I see one courageous who also has benevolence — truly the lingering wind of Zou and Lu, noble worthies never exhausted."

entries.zh: 是日詔入直殿省，啟尚方仗不堪用。
entries.en: That same day he was ordered into attendance at the Palace Secretariat, where he reported that the weapons in the imperial armory were shoddy and unusable.
entries.literal: That day he was ordered to enter and stand duty in the Palace Secretariat; he reported that the arsenal weapons were unfit for use.

entries.zh: 上大怒，坐者非一。
entries.en: The emperor flew into a rage, and several officials present were held accountable.
entries.literal: The emperor was greatly angered; more than one person present was punished.

entries.zh: 及侯景作逆，果弊於仗粗。
entries.en: When Hou Jing rose in rebellion, the dynasty paid dearly for those worthless arms.
entries.literal: When Hou Jing rebelled, they indeed suffered disaster from the crude quality of the weapons.

entries.zh: 二年，復為都官尚書。
entries.en: The following year he was again appointed Minister of Justice.
entries.literal: In the second year he again became Minister of the Ministry of Justice.

entries.zh: 侯景反，攻陷曆陽，帝問侃討景之策。
entries.en: When Hou Jing rebelled and took Liyang, the emperor asked Kan how best to destroy him.
entries.literal: Hou Jing rebelled, captured Liyang, and the emperor asked Kan for a strategy to suppress Jing.

entries.zh: 侃求以二千人急據採石，令邵陵王襲取壽春，使景進不得前，退失巢窟，烏合之眾，自然瓦解。
entries.en: Kan asked for two thousand men to seize Caishi immediately and urged the Prince of Shaoling to take Shouchun by surprise, so Hou Jing could neither advance nor retreat to a secure base; his ragtag following would fall apart on its own.
entries.literal: Kan requested two thousand men to seize Caishi in haste, and ordered the Prince of Shaoling to strike and take Shouchun, so that Jing advancing could not proceed and retreating would lose his nest — the mob gathered at random would naturally disintegrate.

entries.zh: 議者謂景未敢便逼都，遂寢其策。
entries.en: The counsellors argued that Hou Jing would never dare march straight on the capital, and Kan's plan was set aside.
entries.literal: Those in council said Jing would not dare promptly press on the capital, and so his plan was shelved.

entries.zh: 令王質往。
entries.en: They sent Wang Zhi in his place.
entries.literal: Wang Zhi was ordered to go instead.

entries.zh: 侃曰：「今茲敗矣。」
entries.en: Kan said, "We've lost already."
entries.literal: Kan said: "This time we are defeated."

entries.zh: 乃令侃率千餘騎頓望國門。
entries.en: Kan was then ordered to take a thousand-plus cavalry and hold position before the Capital Gate.
entries.literal: He was then ordered to lead more than a thousand horsemen and encamp facing the Capital Gate.

entries.zh: 景至新林，追侃入副宣城王都督城內諸軍事。
entries.en: When Hou Jing reached Xinlin, Kan was rushed inside to serve as deputy to the Prince of Xuancheng in commanding the city's defenses.
entries.literal: When Jing reached Xinlin, Kan was urgently summoned to enter the city as deputy to the Prince of Xuancheng in directing all military affairs within the walls.

entries.zh: 賊既頻攻不捷，乃築長圍。
entries.en: After repeated assaults failed, the rebels settled in to build a full circumvallation.
entries.literal: Since the rebels had repeatedly attacked without success, they then built a long encirclement.

entries.zh: 朱異、張綰議出擊之。
entries.en: Zhu Yi and Zhang Wan urged a sortie against the encirclement.
entries.literal: Zhu Yi and Zhang Wan debated sallying out to strike them.

entries.zh: 帝以問侃，侃曰：「不可，賊多日攻城，既不能下，故立長圍，欲引城中降者耳。
entries.en: The emperor asked Kan's view. Kan said, "No. They have failed to take the city by assault, so they are building a long siege line to tempt defectors inside the walls — that is all.
entries.literal: The emperor questioned Kan; Kan said: "It cannot be done. The rebels have besieged for many days and could not take the city, so they establish a long encirclement intending only to lure those in the city who would surrender.

entries.zh: 今擊之，出人若少，不足破賊；
entries.en: If we sortie with too few men, we won't break them;
entries.literal: If we strike now and send out few men, it is insufficient to break the rebels;

entries.zh: 若多，則一旦失利，門隘橋小，必大致挫衄。」
entries.en: but if we send out many and lose, the gates are narrow and the bridges small — a retreat would become a slaughter."
entries.literal: if many, then once defeated the gates are narrow and the bridges small — there will surely be great rout and disaster."

entries.zh: 不從，遂使千餘人出戰。
entries.en: His counsel was ignored, and more than a thousand men were sent out to fight.
entries.literal: The advice was not followed; more than a thousand men were then sent out to battle.

entries.zh: 未及交鋒，望風退走，果以爭橋赴水，死者太半。
entries.en: They never even closed with the enemy but broke and ran. In the crush at the bridge men tumbled into the water, and more than half perished.
entries.literal: Before they could cross blades they fled at sight of the enemy; indeed in the scramble for the bridge they plunged into the water — more than half died.

entries.zh: 羊鴉仁字孝穆，泰山钜平人也。
entries.en: Yang Ren, courtesy name Xiaomu, was a native of Juping in Taishan commandery.
entries.literal: Yang Ren, styled Xiaomu, was a man of Juping in Taishan.

entries.zh: 少驍勇，仕郡為主簿。
entries.en: As a young man he was bold and brave and served his commandery as chief clerk.
entries.literal: In youth he was valiant and brave; in the commandery he served as Chief Clerk.

entries.zh: 並通中，率兄弟自魏歸梁，封廣晉侯。
entries.en: In the Datong era he led his brothers in defecting from Wei to the Liang and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Guangjin.
entries.literal: In the Datong era he led his brothers in coming from Wei to Liang and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Guangjin.

entries.zh: 征伐青、齊間，累有功績，位至都督、北司州刺史。
entries.en: On campaigns between Qing and Qi he won repeated distinction, rising to area commander and Inspector of Northern Sizhou.
entries.literal: Campaigning between Qing and Qi he repeatedly achieved merit, rising to Grand Commander and Inspector of Northern Sizhou.

entries.zh: 及侯景降，詔鴉仁督土州刺史桓和之、仁州刺史湛海珍等趣縣瓠應接。
entries.en: When Hou Jing submitted, Ren was ordered to lead Inspector of Tuzhou Huan Hezhi, Inspector of Renzhou Zhan Haizhen, and others to Xuanhuo to coordinate support.
entries.literal: When Hou Jing surrendered, an edict ordered Ren to direct Inspector of Tuzhou Huan Hezhi, Inspector of Renzhou Zhan Haizhen, and others to hasten to Xuanhuo to link up in support.

entries.zh: 景至，仍為都督、司豫二州刺史，鎮縣瓠。
entries.en: When Hou Jing arrived, Ren remained area commander and Inspector of Si and Yu provinces, holding Xuanhuo.
entries.literal: When Jing arrived, he remained Grand Commander and Inspector of the two provinces Si and Yu, garrisoning Xuanhuo.

entries.zh: 會侯景敗于渦陽，魏軍漸逼，鴉仁恐糧運不繼，遂還北司，上表陳謝。
entries.en: When Hou Jing was defeated at Woyang and Wei forces closed in, Ren, fearing his supply lines would fail, withdrew to Northern Sizhou and submitted a confession to the throne.
entries.literal: It happened that Hou Jing was defeated at Woyang; Wei armies gradually pressed in; Ren feared grain supply would not continue, so he returned to Northern Sizhou and submitted a memorial confessing fault.

entries.zh: 帝大怒鴉仁，鴉仁懼，頓軍於淮上。
entries.en: The emperor was furious with Ren. Afraid, he halted his army on the Huai.
entries.literal: The emperor was greatly angry at Ren; Ren was afraid and halted his army on the Huai.

entries.zh: 及侯景反，鴉仁率所部入援。
entries.en: When Hou Jing rose in rebellion, Ren led his troops to the capital's relief.
entries.literal: When Hou Jing rebelled, Ren led his division to enter as relief.

entries.zh: 列傳第五十三
entries.en: the 53th year of Biographies
entries.literal: Biographies, Number Fifty-Three

entries.zh: 及長，好學，善屬文。
entries.en: As an adult he loved learning and wrote with skill.
entries.literal: When grown, he loved learning and was skilled at composition.

entries.zh: 性沖靜，有棲遁志。
entries.en: He was gentle and withdrawn by nature and aspired to a life of seclusion.
entries.literal: His nature was mild and still; he had the resolve to dwell in seclusion.

entries.zh: 弱冠舉秀才，對策高第。
entries.en: At his coming of age he was recommended as Cultivated Talent and placed at the top of the policy examination.
entries.literal: At weak cap he was recommended as Cultivated Talent and ranked high in the policy response.

entries.zh: 起家梁宣城王國左常侍。
entries.en: He began his career as Left Regular Attendant in the establishment of the Liang Prince of Xuancheng.
entries.literal: He began his career as Left Regular Attendant in the Liang Prince of Xuancheng's establishment.

entries.zh: 大同中，嘗驟雨，殿前往往有雜色寶珠，梁武觀之，甚有喜色，寄因上瑞雨頌。
entries.en: During the Datong era a sudden rain once left multicolored pearls scattered before the hall. Emperor Wu looked on with delight, and Ji submitted an Ode on the Auspicious Rain.
entries.literal: In the Datong era, once during a sudden rain, before the hall there often appeared multicolored precious pearls; Liang Wu viewed them with great pleasure; Ji thereupon submitted an Ode on Auspicious Rain.

entries.zh: 帝謂寄兄荔曰：「此頌典裁清拔，卿之士龍也，將如何擢用？」
entries.en: The Emperor told Ji's elder brother Li, "This ode is elegant and elevated. He is your Lu Ji—how shall we promote him?"
entries.literal: The Emperor said to Ji's elder brother Li: "This ode's style is clear and elevated; he is your Shi Long—how shall we promote and employ him?"

entries.zh: 寄聞之歎曰：「美盛德之形容，以申擊壤之情耳，吾豈買名求仕者乎？」
entries.en: When Ji heard this he sighed. "I only meant to praise the Emperor's virtue and voice the people's joy. Am I the sort to trade on a name for office?"
entries.literal: When Ji heard, he sighed: "To praise the sage virtue's likeness and express the feeling of beating clods—that is all; am I one who buys a name to seek office?"

entries.zh: 乃閉門稱疾，唯以書籍自娛。
entries.en: He shut his gate, pleaded illness, and amused himself with books alone.
entries.literal: He then shut his gate and claimed illness, amusing himself only with books.

entries.zh: 岳陽王察為會稽太守，寄為中記室，領郡五官掾。
entries.en: When the Prince of Yueyang, Cha, became Administrator of Kuaiji, Ji served as Central Recorder with concurrent duty as Commandery Five-Officials Assistant.
entries.literal: When the Prince of Yueyang Cha was Administrator of Kuaiji, Ji was Central Recorder and concurrent Commandery Five-Officials Assistant.

entries.zh: 在職簡略煩苛，務存大體，曹局之內，終日寂然。
entries.en: In office he cut through petty bureaucracy and kept to essentials. His bureau was silent all day long.
entries.literal: In office he simplified what was tedious and exacting, keeping to the great pattern; within the bureau all day was silence.

entries.zh: 自天厭梁德，多難薦臻，寰宇分崩，英雄互起，不可勝紀，人人自以為得之。
entries.en: Since Heaven grew weary of the Liang and hardships followed one upon another, the realm split apart and heroes rose beyond counting, each believing he held destiny in his hand.
entries.literal: Since Heaven grew weary of Liang's virtue and many hardships came in succession, the realm split apart and heroes rose against one another beyond counting; each man thought he had grasped success.

entries.zh: 然夷凶翦亂，拯溺扶危，四海樂推，三靈眷命，揖讓而居南面者，陳氏也。
entries.en: Yet it was the house of Chen that quelled the wicked, rescued the drowning, and upheld the endangered; that the four seas joyfully advanced, that the three numina favored, and that through abdication took the throne.
entries.literal: Yet it was the Chen who quelled the barbarous and cut down disorder, rescued the drowning and upheld the endangered, were joyfully advanced by the four seas, were favored by the three numina, and through yielding ceremony took the facing-south position.

entries.zh: 豈非歷數有在，惟天所授，當璧應運，其事甚明，一也。
entries.en: Is this not because the mandate of fate was fixed and Heaven alone bestowed it, the jade disk answering the age? This is clear—the first point.
entries.literal: Is this not because the cycle of fate had its place and Heaven alone bestowed it—the jade disk answering the age? This matter is very clear—the first point.

entries.zh: 主上承基，明德遠被，天綱再張，地維重紐。
entries.en: Our sovereign has inherited the foundation. His bright virtue spreads far. Heaven's net is stretched anew and Earth's cords are bound again.
entries.literal: The sovereign inherits the foundation; bright virtue spreads far; Heaven's net is stretched anew; Earth's cords are bound again.

entries.zh: 夫以王琳之強，侯瑱之力，進足以搖盪中原，爭衡天下，退足以屈強江外，雄張偏隅。
entries.en: Consider Wang Lin's strength and Hou Tian's power. Advancing, they could shake the central plains and contend for the realm. Retreating, they could hold the Yangzi south and dominate a corner.
entries.literal: Consider Wang Lin's strength and Hou Tian's power: advancing, they were enough to shake the central plains and contend for the realm; retreating, enough to bend the strong beyond the Yangzi and dominate a corner.

entries.zh: 然或命一旅之師，或資一士之說，琳即瓦解冰泮，投身異域，瑱則厥角稽顙，委命闕庭。
entries.en: Yet with a single brigade sent, or with one man's counsel relied upon, Lin dissolved like melting ice and fled to foreign lands, while Tian bowed his forehead to the ground and surrendered at the imperial court.
entries.literal: Yet with only a single brigade sent, or relying on one man's persuasion, Lin at once dissolved like ice melting, casting himself into foreign lands; Tian bowed forehead to ground and entrusted his fate to the imperial court.

entries.zh: 斯又天假之威，而除其患，其事甚明，二也。
entries.en: This again is Heaven lending its might to remove such threats. This is clear—the second point.
entries.literal: This again is Heaven lending its might to remove their peril—this matter is very clear—the second point.

entries.zh: 今將軍以藩戚之重，擁東南之眾，盡忠奉上，戮力勤王，豈不勳高竇融，寵過吳芮，析珪判野，南面稱孤，其事甚明，三也。
entries.en: You bear the weight of an imperial kinsman on the frontier and command the hosts of the southeast. If you devote your loyalty to the throne and join your strength to the royal cause, would your merit not exceed Dou Rong's and your favor surpass Wu Rui's, with jade tallies divided and lands apportioned, reigning in your domain? This is clear—the third point.
entries.literal: Now the General, with the weight of a frontier kinsman, holds the hosts of the southeast; if you exhaust loyalty in serving above and join strength to aid the throne, would your merit not exceed Dou Rong's, your favor surpass Wu Rui's, with jade tallies divided and fields apportioned, facing south and styled solitary lord? This matter is very clear—the third point.

entries.zh: 且聖朝棄瑕忘過，寬厚待人，改過自新，咸加敘擢。
entries.en: Moreover the court discards flaws and forgets faults, treats men with generous breadth, and promotes all who reform and renew themselves.
entries.literal: Moreover the holy court discards flaws and forgets faults, treats men with generous breadth, and those who reform and renew themselves are all promoted in rank.

entries.zh: 至如余孝頃、潘純陀、李孝欽、歐陽頠等，悉委以心腹，任以爪牙，胸中豁然，曾無纖芥。
entries.en: Men such as Yu Xiaoxiang, Pan Chuntuo, Li Xiaoqin, and Ouyang Hui were all entrusted as inner confidants and employed as his claws and fangs. The sovereign's heart remained open, without the slightest grudge.
entries.literal: As for Yu Xiaoxiang, Pan Chuntuo, Li Xiaoqin, Ouyang Hui, and the like—all were entrusted as inner confidants and employed as claws and fangs; the breast was open and clear, never a fiber of resentment.

entries.zh: 況將軍釁非張繡，罪異畢諶，當何慮于危亡，何失于富貴？
entries.en: Your offense is not Zhang Xiu's, your crime differs from Bi Chen's. Why should you fear ruin or lose wealth and honor?
entries.literal: How much more so for the General, whose offense is not Zhang Xiu's, whose crime differs from Bi Chen's—why should you fear ruin, why lose wealth and honor?

entries.zh: 此又其事甚明，四也。
entries.en: This too is clear—the fourth point.
entries.literal: This again is very clear—the fourth point.

entries.zh: 方今周、齊鄰睦，境外無虞，並兵一向，匪朝伊夕。
entries.en: At present Northern Zhou and Qi are friendly neighbors. Beyond the borders there is no worry, yet their united armies may strike at any moment—not merely tomorrow or the day after.
entries.literal: At present Zhou and Qi are neighbors in harmony; beyond the borders there is no worry; united armies will strike in one direction—not merely tomorrow or the day after.

entries.zh: 非有劉、項競逐之機，楚、趙連從之事，可得雍容高拱，坐論西伯，其事甚明，五也。
entries.en: There is no occasion like Liu Bang and Xiang Yu contending for the realm, no alliance like Chu and Zhao joining forces. You cannot at ease with folded hands sit and discourse like the Earl of the West. This is clear—the fifth point.
entries.literal: There is no occasion like Liu and Xiang contending, no matter like Chu and Zhao joining in alliance—you cannot at ease with hands folded sit and discourse like the Earl of the West. This is very clear—the fifth point.

entries.zh: 且留將軍狼顧一隅，亟經摧衄，聲實虧喪，膽氣衰沮。
entries.en: Moreover General Liu, holding one corner like a wolf glancing backward, has suffered defeat after defeat. His reputation is ruined and his courage broken.
entries.literal: Moreover General Liu, wolf-glancing in one corner, has repeatedly suffered defeats; reputation and substance are diminished, courage and spirit decayed.

entries.zh: 高瓖、向文政、留瑜、黃子玉此數人者，將軍所知，首鼠兩端，唯利是視，其餘將帥亦可見矣。
