entries.en: Gao Rang, Xiang Wenzheng, Liu Yu, and Huang Ziyu—these men you know well—are fence-sitters who look only to profit. The rest of your commanders are no better.
entries.literal: Gao Rang, Xiang Wenzheng, Liu Yu, Huang Ziyu—these several men, as the General knows, are rats with two heads, looking only to profit; the rest of the commanders may likewise be seen.

entries.zh: 孰能被堅執銳，長驅深入，系馬埋輪，奮不顧命，以先士卒者乎？
entries.en: Who among them can don hard armor, grasp sharp blades, drive deep into enemy territory, tether horses and bury wheels, and charge ahead of the ranks without regard for his life?
entries.literal: Who among them can don hard armor and grasp sharp blades, drive far in deep penetration, tether horses and bury wheels, strive without regard for life, and lead before the soldiers?

entries.zh: 此又其事甚明，六也。
entries.en: This too is clear—the sixth point.
entries.literal: This again is very clear—the sixth point.

entries.zh: 且將軍之強，孰如侯景？
entries.en: Moreover, is your strength equal to Hou Jing's?
entries.literal: Moreover, is the General's strength equal to Hou Jing's?

entries.zh: 將軍之眾，孰如王琳？
entries.en: Are your troops equal to Wang Lin's?
entries.literal: Are the General's hosts equal to Wang Lin's?

entries.zh: 武皇滅侯景於前，今上摧王琳於後，此乃天時，非復人力。
entries.en: The Martial Emperor destroyed Hou Jing before; our present sovereign crushed Wang Lin after. This is Heaven's season, not human strength alone.
entries.literal: The Martial Emperor destroyed Hou Jing before; the present sovereign crushed Wang Lin after—this is Heaven's season, no longer human effort.

entries.zh: 且兵革已後，人皆厭亂，其孰能棄墳墓，捐妻子，出萬死不顧之計，從將軍于白刃之間乎？
entries.en: After years of war, all men are weary of disorder. Who would abandon his ancestors' graves, cast off wife and children, and follow you between flashing blades in a plan that courts ten thousand deaths?
entries.literal: Moreover, after arms and armor, all men are weary of disorder—who could abandon graves, cast off wife and children, adopt a plan of ten thousand deaths without regard, and follow the General between flashing blades?

entries.zh: 此又其事甚明，七也。
entries.en: This too is clear—the seventh point.
entries.literal: This again is very clear—the seventh point.

entries.zh: 曆觀前古，鑒之往事，子陽、季孟傾覆相尋，餘善、右渠危亡繼及，天命可畏，山川難恃。
entries.en: Surveying former ages and taking past events as mirror, Ziyang and Jimeng fell in succession, Yushan and Youqu perished one after another. Heaven's mandate is to be feared; mountains and rivers are hard to rely on.
entries.literal: Reviewing former ages and taking past events as mirror, Ziyang and Jimeng fell in succession, Yushan and Youqu perished one after another—Heaven's mandate is to be feared, mountains and rivers are hard to rely on.

entries.zh: 況將軍欲以數郡之地，當天下之兵，以諸侯之資，拒天子之命，強弱逆順，可得侔乎？
entries.en: How much less can you, with the lands of a few commanderies, meet the armies of the realm, or with a feudal lord's resources refuse the Son of Heaven's command? Can strength and weakness, obedience and rebellion, be matched?
entries.literal: How much more if the General wishes with the lands of a few commanderies to meet the armies of the realm, with a feudal lord's resources to refuse the Son of Heaven's command—can strength and weakness, obedience and rebellion, be matched?

entries.zh: 此又其事甚明，八也。
entries.en: This too is clear—the eighth point.
entries.literal: This again is very clear—the eighth point.

entries.zh: 且非我族類，其心必異，不愛其親，豈能及物？
entries.en: Moreover, those not of our kindred must differ in heart. If one does not love his kin, how can he care for others?
entries.literal: Moreover, those not of our kindred—their hearts must differ; if one does not love his kin, how can he reach to other things?

entries.zh: 留將軍身縻國爵，子尚王姬，猶且棄天屬而弗顧，背明君而孤立，危急之日，豈能同憂共患，不背將軍者乎？
entries.en: General Liu holds state rank and his son is married to an imperial princess, yet he still abandons his kin and turns his back on the enlightened sovereign to stand alone. In days of peril, how could he share your worry and not turn against you?
entries.literal: General Liu is bound by state rank, his son married to an imperial princess—yet he still abandons Heaven's kin without regard and turns his back on the enlightened lord to stand alone; in days of peril, how could he share worry and disaster and not turn against the General?

entries.zh: 至於師老力屈，懼誅利賞，必有韓、智晉陽之謀，張、陳井陘之事。
entries.en: When troops grow weary and strength fails, when men fear punishment and covet reward, there will surely be plots like those of Han and Zhi at Jinyang and affairs like those of Zhang and Chen at Jingxing Pass.
entries.literal: As for troops worn and strength spent, fearing punishment and coveting reward—there will surely be plots like Han and Zhi at Jinyang, affairs like Zhang and Chen at Jingxing Pass.

entries.zh: 此又其事甚明，九也。
entries.en: This too is clear—the ninth point.
entries.literal: This again is very clear—the ninth point.

entries.zh: 且北軍萬里遠鬥，鋒不可當，將軍自戰其地，人多顧後，梁安背向為心，修忤匹夫之力，眾寡不敵，將帥不侔，師以無名而出，事以無機而動，以此稱兵，未知其利。
entries.en: The northern army fights from ten thousand li away, yet its edge cannot be withstood. You fight on your own ground, yet your men look behind them. Liang An's heart has turned away. Xiu can defy only a common man's strength. Many and few do not match; commanders are unequal. Your army goes forth without righteous cause and moves without opportune moment. To raise arms on this basis—I do not see the profit.
entries.literal: Moreover the northern army fights from ten thousand li away yet its edge cannot be withstood; the General fights on your own ground—men mostly look behind; Liang An's heart turns away; Xiu defies a common man's strength; many and few do not match, commanders are not equal; the army goes forth without righteous name, the affair moves without opportune moment—by this to raise arms, one does not know the profit.

entries.zh: 夫以漢朝吳、楚，晉室穎、顒，連城數十，長戟百萬，拔本塞源，自圖家國，其有成功者乎？
entries.en: Consider Han's Wu and Chu, Jin's Ying and Yong—linked cities by the tens, long halberds by the million, uprooting the root and blocking the source to plot for themselves—were there any who succeeded?
entries.literal: Consider Han's Wu and Chu, Jin's Ying and Yong—linked cities by the tens, long halberds by the million, uprooting the root and blocking the source, plotting state and clan for themselves—were there any who succeeded?

entries.zh: 此又其事甚明，十也。
entries.en: This too is clear—the tenth point.
entries.literal: This again is very clear—the tenth point.

entries.zh: 時有吳興章華，字仲宗，家本農夫，至華獨好學，與士君子游處，頗通經史，善屬文。
entries.en: At that time there was Zhang Hua of Wuxing, courtesy name Zhongzong. His family were farmers, but he alone loved learning, kept company with scholars, was well versed in the classics and histories, and wrote with skill.
entries.literal: At the time there was Zhang Hua of Wuxing, courtesy name Zhongzong; his family were originally farmers, but Hua alone loved learning, associated with gentlemen and scholars, was fairly versed in the classics and histories, and skilled at composition.

entries.zh: 侯景之亂，游嶺南，居羅浮山寺，專精習業。
entries.en: During Hou Jing's rebellion he went to Lingnan and lived at Luofu Mountain Temple, devoting himself wholly to study.
entries.literal: During Hou Jing's turmoil he traveled to Lingnan and dwelt at Luofu Mountain Temple, devoting himself wholly to study.

entries.zh: 歐陽頠為廣州刺史，署為南海太守。
entries.en: When Ouyang Hui became Inspector of Guangzhou, he appointed Hua Administrator of Nanhai.
entries.literal: When Ouyang Hui was Inspector of Guangzhou, he appointed Hua Administrator of Nanhai.

entries.zh: 頠子紇敗，乃還都。
entries.en: When Hui's son He was defeated, Hua returned to the capital.
entries.literal: When Hui's son He was defeated, Hua then returned to the capital.

entries.zh: 後主時，除太市令，非其所好，乃辭以疾。
entries.en: Under the Later Sovereign he was appointed Director of the Grand Market, a post he disliked, and he declined on grounds of illness.
entries.literal: Under the Later Sovereign he was made Director of the Grand Market—not to his liking, so he declined on grounds of illness.

entries.zh: 禎明初，上書極諫，其大略曰：「陛下即位，於今五年，不思先帝之艱難，不知天命之可畏。
entries.en: At the beginning of the Zhenming era he submitted a memorial of the strongest remonstrance, which in essence read: "Your Majesty has reigned five years without reflecting on the former emperor's hardships or knowing that Heaven's mandate is to be feared.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Zhenming he submitted a memorial of utmost remonstrance; its general purport said: "Your Majesty has reigned now five years, not reflecting on the former emperor's hardships, not knowing that Heaven's mandate is to be feared.

entries.zh: 溺于嬖寵，惑於酒色。
entries.en: You are drowned in favorites and deluded by wine and women.
entries.literal: Drowned in favorites, deluded by wine and women.

entries.zh: 祠七廟而不出，拜妃嬪而臨軒。
entries.en: You neglect the sacrifices at the seven temples yet attend to your consorts at court.
entries.literal: You sacrifice at the seven temples yet do not go forth; you bow to consorts and concubines yet ascend the hall.

entries.zh: 老臣宿將，棄之草莽，諂佞讒邪，升之朝廷。
entries.en: You cast old ministers and veteran generals into the wilderness while raising flatterers and slanderers to the court.
entries.literal: Old ministers and veteran generals you cast into the wild grass; flatterers, sycophants, slanderers, and the wicked you raise to the court.

entries.zh: 今疆埸日蹙，隋軍壓境，陛下如不改弦易張，臣見麋鹿復游于姑蘇矣。」
entries.en: The borders shrink daily and Sui armies press the frontier. If Your Majesty does not change course, I see elk roaming Gusu once more."
entries.literal: Now the borders daily shrink and Sui armies press the frontier; if Your Majesty does not change the strings and stretch anew, your servant sees elk and deer roaming Gusu again."

entries.zh: 書奏，後主大怒，即日斬之。
entries.en: When the memorial was submitted, the Later Sovereign flew into a rage and executed him that same day.
entries.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the Later Sovereign was greatly angry and executed him that same day.

entries.zh: 時有蕭濟字孝康，東海蘭陵人也。
entries.en: At the time there was Xiao Ji, courtesy name Xiaokang, from Lanling in Donghai commandery.
entries.literal: At the time there was Xiao Ji, courtesy name Xiaokang, a native of Lanling in Donghai.

entries.zh: 好學，博通經史。
entries.en: He loved learning and was broadly versed in the classics and histories.
entries.literal: He loved learning and was broadly versed in the classics and histories.

entries.zh: 仕梁為太子舍人。
entries.en: Under Liang he served as Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: Under Liang he served as Attendant of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 預平侯景功，封松陽縣侯。
entries.en: He shared in pacifying Hou Jing and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Songyang county.
entries.literal: He shared in pacifying Hou Jing and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Songyang county.

entries.zh: 陳文帝為會稽太守，以濟為宣毅府長史。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen was Administrator of Kuaiji, he made Ji chief secretary of the firm-resolution establishment.
entries.literal: When Chen Emperor Wen was Administrator of Kuaiji, he made Ji Chief Secretary of the Firm Resolution Establishment.

entries.zh: 及即位，授侍中。
entries.en: When he took the throne, Ji was appointed Palace Attendant.
entries.literal: When he took the throne, Ji was appointed Palace Attendant.

entries.zh: 太建中，歷位五兵、度支、祠部三尚書，卒。
entries.en: During the Taijian era he successively served as Minister of Armaments, Minister of Revenue, and Minister of Rites, then died.
entries.literal: During the Taijian era he successively held the three posts of Minister of Armaments, Minister of Revenue, and Minister of Rites, then died.

entries.zh: 陳永定中，吏部尚書徐陵領大著作，復引為史佐。
entries.en: In the Yongding era Xu Ling, Minister of Personnel, headed the Grand Historiographer's office and again brought Cha in as history assistant.
entries.literal: In Chen's Yongding era, Minister of Personnel Xu Ling headed the Grand Historiographer's office and again brought him in as history assistant.

entries.zh: 太建初，補宣明殿學士。
entries.en: At the beginning of Taijian he was appointed Scholar of the Hall of Illuminated Proclamation.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Taijian he was appointed Scholar of the Hall of Illuminated Proclamation.

entries.zh: 尋為通直散騎常侍，報聘于周。
entries.en: Soon he became Regular Attendant of the Direct and Upright Cavalry and went on a return mission to the Northern Zhou.
entries.literal: Soon he was Regular Attendant of the Direct and Upright Cavalry and returned courtesy on a mission to Zhou.

entries.zh: 江左耆舊先在關右者，咸相傾慕。
entries.en: Elder scholars of the south who were already in the northwest all admired him.
entries.literal: Elders of the left of the Yangzi who were already in the Guan west all inclined toward him in admiration.

entries.zh: 沛國劉臻竊於公館訪漢書疑事十餘條，並為剖析，皆有經據。
entries.en: Liu Zhen of Pei privately raised more than ten doubtful points from the Book of Han at the guest house. Cha analyzed each with canonical grounding.
entries.literal: Liu Zhen of Pei, privately at the guest house, inquired about more than ten doubtful points in the Book of Han; Cha analyzed them all, each with canonical grounding.

entries.zh: 臻謂所親曰：「名下定無虛士。」
entries.en: Zhen told those close to him, "When a name is established, the man behind it is never hollow."
entries.literal: Zhen told those close to him: "When the name is settled, there is certainly no empty gentleman."

entries.zh: 著西聘道里記。
entries.en: He composed a Record of Routes on the Western Mission.
entries.literal: He composed a Record of Routes on the Western Mission.

entries.zh: 使還，補東宮學士，遷尚書祠部侍郎。
entries.en: On his return he was appointed Eastern Palace Scholar and promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat Rites Section.
entries.literal: When the mission returned, he was appointed Eastern Palace Scholar and promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat Rites Section.

entries.zh: 列傳第五十九
entries.en: the 59th year of Biography
entries.literal: Biographies number fifty-nine

entries.zh: 徐爰，字長玉，南琅邪開陽人也。
entries.en: Xu Ai, styled Changyu, came from Kaiyang in Southern Langye.
entries.literal: Xu Ai, style name Changyu, was a native of Kaiyang in Southern Langye.

entries.zh: 本名瑗，後以與傅亮父同名，亮啟改為爰。
entries.en: He was originally named Yuan; because this matched the name of Fu Liang's father, Liang petitioned to have it changed to Ai.
entries.literal: His original name was Yuan; later, because it was the same as Fu Liang's father's name, Liang memorialized to have it changed to Ai.

entries.zh: 初為晉琅邪王大司馬府中典軍，從北征，微密有意理，為武帝所知。
entries.en: He first served as barracks officer on Prince Langye of Jin's staff; on the northern campaign his shrewd judgment won Emperor Wu's notice.
entries.literal: He first served as barracks officer in the great marshal's staff of Prince Langye of Jin; on the northern campaign he showed subtle understanding and sound judgment and came to Emperor Wu's notice.

entries.zh: 少帝在東宮，入侍左右。
entries.en: When Emperor Shao was crown prince, Ai entered service at his side.
entries.literal: When Emperor Shao was in the Eastern Palace he entered to attend at the ruler's side.

entries.zh: 文帝初，又見親任，遂至殿中侍御史。
entries.en: Early in Emperor Wen's reign he again won personal favor and rose to palace investigating censor.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Wen's reign he was again treated with personal trust and rose to palace attendant investigating censor.

entries.zh: 元嘉十二年，轉南台御史，始興王浚後軍行參軍。
entries.en: In the twelfth year of Yuanjia he became a southern bureau censor and acting staff officer on Prince Shixing Jun's rear army.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year of Yuanjia he was transferred to censor of the southern bureau and became acting staff officer on the rear army of Prince Shixing Jun.

entries.zh: 復侍太子于東宮，遷員外散騎侍郎。
entries.en: He again served the crown prince in the Eastern Palace and was promoted to supernumerary attendant cavalier.
entries.literal: He again attended the crown prince in the Eastern Palace and was promoted to supernumerary attendant cavalier.

entries.zh: 文帝每出軍，常懸授兵略。
entries.en: Whenever Emperor Wen campaigned, he often gave Ai his battle plans in advance.
entries.literal: Whenever Emperor Wen took the field he would often entrust Ai with military plans in advance.

entries.zh: 二十九年，重遣王玄謨等北侵，配爰五百人，隨軍碻磝，銜中旨臨時宣示。
entries.en: the twenty-ninth year of In he again sent Wang Xuanmo north; Ai was given five hundred men to accompany the army to Quepo and proclaim the emperor's secret orders as events unfolded.
entries.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he again sent Wang Xuanmo and others north on campaign, assigning Ai five hundred men to follow the army to Quepo, bearing the emperor's secret intent to proclaim on the spot.

entries.zh: 孝武至新亭，江夏王義恭南奔，爰時在殿內，詐劭追義恭，因即得南走。
entries.en: When Emperor Xiaowu reached Xinting and Prince Jiangxia Yigong fled south, Ai was in the hall; pretending Shao was pursuing Yigong, he slipped away south as well.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu reached Xinting, Prince Jiangxia Yigong fled south; Ai was then inside the hall and pretended that Shao was pursuing Yigong, thus managing to flee south himself.

entries.zh: 時孝武將即大位，軍府造次，不曉朝章，爰素諳其事，及至，莫不喜悅，以兼太常丞撰立儀注。
entries.en: As Emperor Xiaowu prepared to ascend the throne, the military headquarters was in chaos and knew nothing of court ritual—Ai, who knew these matters thoroughly, was welcomed with relief and made vice-director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to draft the accession ceremonies.
entries.literal: At that time Emperor Xiaowu was about to take the great throne; the army headquarters was in disarray and did not understand court regulations—Ai had long been versed in such matters, and when he arrived everyone was delighted; he was made concurrently vice-director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to draft the ritual protocols for accession.

entries.zh: 後兼尚書右丞，遷左丞。
entries.en: He later served concurrently as right vice-director of the Secretariat and was promoted to left vice-director.
entries.literal: Later he was concurrently right vice-director of the Secretariat and was promoted to left vice-director.

entries.zh: 先是，元嘉中使著作郎何承天草創國史，孝武初又使奉朝請山謙之、南台御史蘇寶生踵成之。
entries.en: Before this, during Yuanjia, the court had ordered Composition Gentleman He Chengtian to make a first draft of the state history; at the beginning of Xiaowu's reign it further ordered Court Gentleman Shan Qianzhi and Southern Office censor Su Baosheng to continue and complete it.
entries.literal: Before this, during Yuanjia, the court had ordered Composition Gentleman He Chengtian to make a first draft of the state history; at the beginning of Xiaowu's reign it further ordered Court Gentleman Shan Qianzhi and Southern Office censor Su Baosheng to continue and complete it.

entries.zh: 孝建六年，又以爰領著作郎，使終其業。
entries.en: In the sixth year of Xiaojian, it again made Xu Ai acting Composition Gentleman and ordered him to finish the work.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Xiaojian, it again made Xu Ai acting Composition Gentleman and ordered him to finish the work.

entries.zh: 爰雖因前作，而專為一家之書。
entries.en: Although Xu Ai built on the earlier drafts, he made the book entirely his own family's work.
entries.literal: Although Xu Ai built on the earlier drafts, he made the book entirely his own family's work.

entries.zh: 上表「起元義熙，為王業之始，載序宣力，為功臣之斷」。
entries.en: He submitted a memorial: "Begin with the first year of Yixi, taking it as the start of the royal enterprise; record and arrange those who exerted themselves, taking this as the cutoff for meritorious ministers."
entries.literal: He submitted a memorial: "Begin with the first year of Yixi, taking it as the start of the royal enterprise; record and arrange those who exerted themselves, taking this as the cutoff for meritorious ministers."

entries.zh: 於是內外博議。
entries.en: Thereupon those inside and outside the court debated the matter broadly.
entries.literal: Thereupon those inside and outside the court debated the matter broadly.

entries.zh: 太宰江夏王義恭等三十五人同爰，宜以義熙元年為斷。
entries.en: Grand Steward Prince Yigong of Jiangxia and thirty-four others agreed with Xu Ai that the cutoff should be the first year of Yixi.
entries.literal: Grand Steward Prince Yigong of Jiangxia and thirty-four others agreed with Xu Ai that the cutoff should be the first year of Yixi.

entries.zh: 散騎常侍巴陵王休若、尚書金部郎檀道鸞二人謂宜以元興三年為始。
entries.en: Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary Prince Xiuruo of Baling and Tan Daoluan, Gentleman of the Treasury Section of the Secretariat, held that it should begin with the third year of Yuanxing.
entries.literal: Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary Prince Xiuruo of Baling and Tan Daoluan, Gentleman of the Treasury Section of the Secretariat, held that it should begin with the third year of Yuanxing.

entries.zh: 太學博士虞和謂宜以開國為宋西元年。
entries.en: Imperial Academy erudite Yu He said it should take the founding of the state as the first year of Song.
entries.literal: Imperial Academy erudite Yu He said it should take the founding of the state as the first year of Song.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「項籍、聖公，編錄二漢，前史已有成例。桓玄傳宜在宋典，餘如爰議。」
entries.en: The edict said, "Xiang Ji and Shenggong are compiled and recorded in the histories of the two Han; earlier histories already provide a settled precedent. Huan Xuan's biography should be placed in the Song records. For the rest, follow Xu Ai's proposal."
entries.literal: The edict said, "Xiang Ji and Shenggong are compiled and recorded in the histories of the two Han; earlier histories already provide a settled precedent. Huan Xuan's biography should be placed in the Song records. For the rest, follow Xu Ai's proposal."

entries.zh: 高帝疾甚，令僧真典遺詔。
entries.en: When Emperor Gao's illness grew grave, he had Sengzhen oversee the drafting of his final testament.
entries.literal: When Emperor Gao's illness grew severe, he had Sengzhen supervise the drafting of his final testament.

entries.zh: 永明元年，丁父喪。
entries.en: In the first year of Yongming he went into mourning for his father's death.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongming he observed mourning for his father's death.

entries.zh: 起為建威將軍，尋除南泰山太守，又為舍人。
entries.en: Recalled from mourning as General Who Establishes Might, he was soon appointed administrator of South Taishan and then again served as Confidential Adjunct.
entries.literal: Recalled to service as General Who Establishes Might, he was soon made Administrator of South Taishan, then again served as Confidential Adjunct.

entries.zh: 僧真容貌言吐，雅有士風，武帝嘗目送之，笑曰：「人生何必計門戶，紀僧真堂堂，貴人所不及也。」
entries.en: Sengzhen's appearance and speech had an elegant scholar's bearing. Emperor Wu once watched him go and laughed, "In life why must one count one's lineage? Ji Sengzhen is truly imposing—noblemen cannot match him."
entries.literal: Sengzhen's bearing and speech had an elegant scholar's style. Emperor Wu once watched him depart and laughed, "In life why must one count one's lineage? Ji Sengzhen is truly imposing—noblemen cannot match him."

entries.zh: 諸權要中最被眄遇。
entries.en: Among all the powerful favorites, he was the most favored.
entries.literal: Among all the powerful favorites he was most favored with attention.

entries.zh: 後除前軍將軍。
entries.en: Later he was appointed General of the Vanguard.
entries.literal: Later he was appointed General of the Vanguard.

entries.zh: 遭母喪，開塚得五色兩頭蛇。
entries.en: When his mother died, a five-colored two-headed serpent was found upon opening the tomb.
entries.literal: When his mother died, upon opening the tomb a five-colored two-headed serpent was found.

entries.zh: 明帝以僧真歷朝驅使，建武初，除遊擊將軍，兼司農，待之如舊。
entries.en: Because Sengzhen had been employed through successive reigns, Emperor Ming, at the beginning of Jianwu, appointed him General of Mobile Cavalry and concurrently Minister of Agriculture, treating him as before.
entries.literal: Because Sengzhen had been employed through successive reigns, Emperor Ming, at the beginning of Jianwu, appointed him General of Mobile Cavalry and concurrently Minister of Agriculture, treating him as before.

entries.zh: 欲令僧真臨郡，僧真啟進其弟僧猛為鎮蠻護軍、晉熙太守。
entries.en: The emperor wished to have Sengzhen govern a commandery, but Sengzhen memorialized recommending his younger brother Sengmeng as Protector Who Suppresses the Man and administrator of Jinxi.
entries.literal: The emperor wished to have Sengzhen govern a commandery, but Sengzhen memorialized recommending his younger brother Sengmeng as Protector Who Suppresses the Man and administrator of Jinxi.

entries.zh: 永泰元年，除司農卿。
entries.en: In the first year of Yongtai, Sengzhen was appointed Chamberlain for the National Treasury.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongtai, Sengzhen was appointed Chamberlain for the National Treasury.

entries.zh: 明帝崩，掌山陵事，出為廬陵內史。
entries.en: When Emperor Ming died, he managed the mountain mausoleum affairs and was then sent out as internal administrator of Luling.
entries.literal: When Emperor Ming died, he managed the mountain mausoleum affairs and was then sent out as internal administrator of Luling.

entries.zh: 卒於官。
entries.en: He died in office.
entries.literal: He died in office.

entries.zh: 僧猛後卒于晉熙太守。
entries.en: Sengmeng later died while serving as administrator of Jinxi.
entries.literal: Sengmeng later died while serving as administrator of Jinxi.

entries.zh: 兄弟皆有風姿舉止，並善隸書。
entries.en: The brothers both had graceful bearing and deportment, and both were skilled in clerical script.
entries.literal: The brothers both had graceful bearing and deportment, and both were skilled in clerical script.

entries.zh: 僧猛又能飛白書，作飛白賦。
entries.en: Sengmeng was also skilled in flying-white script and composed a "Rhapsody on Flying-White Script."
entries.literal: Sengmeng was also skilled in flying-white script and composed a "Rhapsody on Flying-White Script."

entries.zh: 僧真子交卿，甚有解用。
entries.en: Sengzhen's son Jiaoqing was very capable in practical matters.
entries.literal: Sengzhen's son Jiaoqing was very capable in practical matters.

entries.zh: 武帝崩，僧真號泣思慕。
entries.en: When Emperor Wu died, Sengzhen wailed and mourned him with deep devotion.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu died, Sengzhen wailed and mourned in deep longing.

entries.zh: 系宗久在朝省，閑於職事，武帝常云：「學士輩不堪經國，唯大讀書耳。
entries.en: Xizong had long served in court offices and was adept at administrative work. Emperor Wu often said, "These scholar-officials cannot govern the state—they merely read books at great length.
entries.literal: Xizong had long served in court offices and was adept at administrative affairs. Emperor Wu often said, "These scholar-officials cannot manage the state—they merely read books extensively.

entries.zh: 經國，一劉系宗足矣。
entries.en: For governing the state, one Liu Xizong is enough.
entries.literal: For governing the state, one Liu Xizong is enough.

entries.zh: 沈約、王融數百人，于事何用。」
entries.en: Of what use are Shen Yue, Wang Rong, and their hundreds for practical affairs?"
entries.literal: Of what use are Shen Yue, Wang Rong, and their hundreds for practical matters?"

entries.zh: 其重吏事如此。
entries.en: Such was the weight he placed on practical administration.
entries.literal: Such was the weight he placed on practical administration.

entries.zh: 建武二年，卒官。
entries.en: In the second year of Jianwu he died in office.
entries.literal: In the second year of Jianwu he died in office.

entries.zh: 茹法亮，吳興武康人也。
entries.en: Ru Faliang was a native of Wukang in Wuxing.
entries.literal: Ru Faliang was a native of Wukang in Wuxing.

entries.zh: 宋大明中，出身為小史。
entries.en: During the Daming era of Emperor Ming of Song he began his career as a petty clerk.
entries.literal: During Emperor Ming of Song's Daming era he began his career as a petty clerk.

entries.zh: 曆齋幹扶侍。
entries.en: He served in turn as orderly in the fast hall and as attendant.
entries.literal: He served successively as orderly in the fast hall and as attendant.

entries.zh: 孝武末年，鞭罰過度，校獵江右，選白衣左右百八十人，皆面首富室，從至南州，得鞭者過半。
entries.en: Near the end of Emperor Xiaowu of Song's reign, floggings were excessive. During a hunting expedition on the right bank of the Yangtze, one hundred eighty attendants in plain dress were selected—all wealthy men from prominent households. They accompanied him to the southern regions, and more than half were flogged.
entries.literal: Near the end of Emperor Xiaowu of Song's reign, floggings were excessive. During a hunting expedition on the right bank of the Yangtze, one hundred eighty attendants in plain dress were selected—all were wealthy men of prominent households. They accompanied him to the southern regions, and more than half received floggings.

entries.zh: 法亮憂懼，因緣啟出家得為道人。
entries.en: Anxious and afraid, Faliang seized an opportunity to petition to leave home and become a Daoist monk.
entries.literal: Faliang, anxious and afraid, seized an opportunity to petition to leave home and become a Daoist monk.

entries.zh: 明帝初，罷道，結事阮佃夫，累至齊高帝冠軍府行參軍。
entries.en: At the beginning of Emperor Ming's reign he left the monastic life, attached himself to Ruan Dianfu, and rose to Acting Staff Officer in Emperor Gao of Qi's Champion General headquarters.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Ming's reign he left the monastic life, attached himself to Ruan Dianfu, and rose to Acting Staff Officer in Emperor Gao of Qi's Champion General headquarters.

entries.zh: 及武帝鎮盆城，須舊驅使人，法亮求留為武帝江州典簽，除南台御史，帶松滋令。
entries.en: When Emperor Wu was garrisoned at Pencheng and needed his old runners and attendants, Faliang asked to remain as Chief Clerk of Jiangzhou for the future emperor. He was appointed Censor of the Southern Office and concurrent magistrate of Songzi.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu was garrisoned at Pencheng and needed his old runners and attendants, Faliang asked to remain as Chief Clerk of Jiangzhou for the future emperor; he was appointed Censor of the Southern Office and concurrent Magistrate of Songzi.

entries.zh: 法亮便僻解事，善於承奉，稍見委信。
entries.en: Faliang was quick-witted and capable, skilled at flattery and service, and gradually won trust.
entries.literal: Faliang was quick-witted and capable, skilled at flattery and service, and gradually won trust.

entries.zh: 建元初，度東宮主書，除奉朝請，補東宮通事舍人。
entries.en: At the beginning of Jianyuan he transferred to serve as chief secretary in the Eastern Palace, was made Court Gentleman, and appointed Confidential Messenger in the Eastern Palace.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Jianyuan he crossed over to serve as chief secretary in the Eastern Palace, was made Court Gentleman, and appointed Confidential Messenger in the Eastern Palace.

entries.zh: 武帝即位，仍為中書通事舍人，除員外郎，帶南濟陰太守。
entries.en: When Emperor Wu took the throne, he remained Confidential Messenger of the Central Secretariat, was appointed Supernumerary Gentleman, and served concurrently as administrator of South Jiyin.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu took the throne, he remained Confidential Messenger of the Central Secretariat, was appointed Supernumerary Gentleman, and served concurrently as Administrator of South Jiyin.

entries.zh: 與會稽呂文度、臨海呂文顯並以奸佞諂事武帝。
entries.en: Together with Lü Wendu of Kuaiji and Lü Wenxian of Linhai, he relied on sycophancy and deceit to serve Emperor Wu.
entries.literal: Together with Lü Wendu of Kuaiji and Lü Wenxian of Linhai, he relied on sycophancy and deceit to serve Emperor Wu.

entries.zh: 文度為外監，專制兵權，領軍將軍守虛位而已。
entries.en: Wendu served as Outer Supervisor with monopolistic control of military authority, while the General of the Guards held nothing but an empty title.
entries.literal: Wendu served as Outer Supervisor with monopolistic control of military authority; the General of the Guards held nothing but an empty title.

entries.zh: 天文寺常以上將星占文度吉凶。
entries.en: The Astronomical Bureau regularly used the general's star to read Wendu's fortune.
entries.literal: The Astronomical Bureau regularly used the general's star to read Wendu's fortune.

entries.zh: 文度尤見委信，上嘗云：「公卿中有憂國如文度者，復何憂天下不寧。」
entries.en: Wendu was especially trusted. The emperor once said, "If among the ministers and nobles there were one who cared for the state as Wendu does, what worry would there be that the realm would not be at peace?"
entries.literal: Wendu was especially trusted. The emperor once said, "If among the ministers and nobles there were one who cared for the state as Wendu does, what worry would there be that the realm would not be at peace?"

entries.zh: 巴東王子響于荊州殺僚佐，上遣軍西上，使法亮宣旨安撫子響。
entries.en: Prince Zixiang of Badong killed his staff officers in Jingzhou. The emperor dispatched troops westward and sent Faliang to proclaim the imperial will and pacify him.
entries.literal: Prince Zixiang of Badong killed his staff officers in Jingzhou; the emperor dispatched troops westward and sent Faliang to proclaim the imperial will and pacify Zixiang.

entries.zh: 法亮至江津，子響呼法亮，疑畏不肯往。
entries.en: When Faliang reached Jiangjin, Zixiang summoned him, but Faliang, suspicious and afraid, refused to go.
entries.literal: When Faliang reached Jiangjin, Zixiang summoned him, but Faliang, suspicious and afraid, refused to go.

entries.zh: 又求見傳詔，法亮又不遣。
entries.en: Zixiang also asked to see the edict-bearer, and Faliang again refused to send him.
entries.literal: Zixiang also requested to see the edict-bearer, and Faliang again would not send him.

entries.zh: 故子響怒，遣兵破尹略軍。
entries.en: Zixiang thereupon grew angry and sent troops to crush Yin Lue's army.
entries.literal: Thereupon Zixiang grew angry and sent troops to crush Yin Lue's army.

entries.zh: 事平，法亮至江陵，誅賞處分，皆稱敕斷決。
entries.en: Once the affair was settled, Faliang went to Jiangling. Executions, rewards, and dispositions were all said to have been decided by imperial edict.
entries.literal: When the affair was settled, Faliang went to Jiangling; executions, rewards, and dispositions all were said to have been decided by imperial edict.

entries.zh: 軍還，上悔誅子響，法亮被責，少時親任如舊。
entries.en: When the army returned, the emperor regretted executing Zixiang. Faliang was rebuked, but before long he enjoyed the emperor's intimate trust as before.
entries.literal: When the army returned, the emperor regretted executing Zixiang; Faliang was rebuked, but before long he was trusted as intimately as before.

entries.zh: 廣開宅宇，杉齋光麗，與延昌殿相埒。
entries.en: He greatly expanded his residence. His cedar hall was bright and splendid, rivaling the Yanchang Hall.
entries.literal: He greatly expanded his residence; his cedar hall was bright and splendid, matching the Yanchang Hall.

entries.zh: 延昌殿，武帝中齋也。
entries.en: Yanchang Hall was Emperor Wu's inner fast hall.
entries.literal: Yanchang Hall was Emperor Wu's inner fast hall.

entries.zh: 宅後為魚池釣台，土山樓館，長廊將一里。
entries.en: Behind the residence lay a fish pond and angling terrace, earthen hills with pavilions, and a corridor nearly a li in length.
entries.literal: Behind the residence were a fish pond and angling terrace, earthen hills with pavilions, and a corridor nearly a li long.

entries.zh: 竹林花藥之美，公家苑囿所不能及。
entries.en: The beauty of its bamboo groves, flowers, and medicinal plants surpassed even the imperial gardens.
entries.literal: The beauty of its bamboo groves, flowers, and herbs surpassed what the palace gardens could match.

entries.zh: 郁林即位，除步兵校尉。
entries.en: When Emperor Yulin ascended the throne, Faliang was appointed commandant of footsoldiers.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yulin ascended the throne, Faliang was appointed Commandant of Footsoldiers.

entries.zh: 時有綦母珍之，居舍人之任，凡所論薦，事無不允。
entries.en: At this time Qimu Zhenzhi held the post of attendant, and whatever nominations he put forward were invariably approved.
entries.literal: At this time there was Qimu Zhenzhi, who held the post of attendant; whatever nominations he put forward were invariably approved.

entries.zh: 內外要職及郡丞尉，皆論價而後施行。
entries.en: Important posts inside and outside the court, as well as county assistant magistrates and commandants, were all sold by negotiated price before appointment.
entries.literal: Important posts inside and outside the court, as well as county assistant magistrates and commandants, all were sold by negotiated price before appointment.

entries.zh: 貨賄交至，旬月之間，累至千金。
entries.en: Bribes poured in without cease, and within a month or so they accumulated to a thousand gold pieces.
entries.literal: Bribes flowed in without cease; within a month or so they accumulated to a thousand gold pieces.

entries.zh: 帝給珍之宅，宅邊又有空宅，從即並取，輒令材官營作，不關詔旨。
entries.en: The emperor granted Zhenzhi a residence. There was another empty residence beside it, which he seized on the spot as well, then ordered the construction officer to build there without any imperial edict.
entries.literal: The emperor granted Zhenzhi a residence; there was another empty residence beside it, which he took on the spot as well, then ordered the construction officer to build there without reference to an edict.

entries.zh: 材官將軍細作丞相語云：「寧拒至尊敕，不可違舍人命。」
entries.en: The construction officer general wittily echoed the prime minister's words: "Better to refuse the supreme sovereign's edict than to disobey an attendant's order."
entries.literal: The construction officer general finely mimicked the prime minister's speech, saying, "Better to refuse the supreme sovereign's edict than to disobey an attendant's order."

entries.zh: 珍之母隨弟欽之作暨陽令，欽之罷縣還，珍之迎母至湖熟，輒將青氅百人自隨，鼓角橫吹，都下富人追從者百數。
entries.en: Zhenzhi's mother had accompanied his younger brother Qinzhi when the latter served as magistrate of Jiyang. When Qinzhi left office and returned, Zhenzhi went to meet his mother at Hushu with a hundred green-cloaked guards, drums, horns, and wind instruments playing, and scores of wealthy men of the capital followed in his train.
entries.literal: Zhenzhi's mother followed his younger brother Qinzhi when the latter served as magistrate of Jiyang; when Qinzhi left office and returned, Zhenzhi went to meet his mother at Hushu, bringing with him a hundred green-cloaked guards, with drums, horns, and wind instruments playing; wealthy men of the capital followed in scores.

entries.zh: 欽之自行佐作縣，還除廬陵王驃騎正將軍，又詐宣敕使欽之領青氅。
entries.en: Qinzhi had himself served as assistant magistrate in the county. On his return he was appointed regular general under the Prince of Luling's fast cavalry headquarters, and Zhenzhi also falsely proclaimed an edict appointing Qinzhi to command the green-cloaked guards.
entries.literal: Qinzhi had himself served as assistant magistrate in the county; on his return he was appointed Regular General under the Fast Cavalry headquarters of the Prince of Luling, and Zhenzhi also falsely proclaimed an edict appointing Qinzhi to command the green-cloaked guards.

entries.zh: 珍之有一銅鏡，背有「三公」字，常語人云：「征祥如此，何患三公不至。」
entries.en: Zhenzhi owned a bronze mirror with the characters "Three Dukes" on the back. He often told people, "With such an omen, why worry that the rank of Three Dukes will not come?"
entries.literal: Zhenzhi had a bronze mirror with the characters "Three Dukes" on the back; he often told people, "With such an omen, why worry that the rank of Three Dukes will not come?"

entries.zh: 乃就蔣王廟乞願得三公，封郡王。
entries.en: He went to the Temple of Prince Jiang to pray that he might attain the Three Dukes and be enfeoffed as a commandery prince.
entries.literal: He went to the Temple of Prince Jiang to pray for attainment of the Three Dukes and enfeoffment as a commandery prince.

entries.zh: 啟帝求封，朝議未許。
entries.en: He petitioned the emperor for enfeoffment, but the court deliberation did not approve.
entries.literal: He petitioned the emperor for enfeoffment, but court deliberation did not approve.

entries.zh: 又自陳曰：「珍之西州伏事，侍從入宮，契闊心膂，竭盡誠力。
entries.en: He also declared in person, "Zhenzhi served humbly in the Western Province, followed the emperor into the palace, shared hardships heart and soul, and exhausted my loyalty and strength.
entries.literal: He also declared in his own person, "Zhenzhi served humbly in the Western Province, followed into the palace, shared hardships heart and soul, and exhausted my loyalty and strength.

entries.zh: 王融奸謀潛構，自非珍之翼衛扶持，事在不測。
entries.en: Wang Rong secretly plotted treachery. Had it not been for Zhenzhi's protection and support, the outcome would have been unpredictable.
entries.literal: Wang Rong secretly plotted treachery; had it not been for Zhenzhi's protection and support, the outcome would have been unpredictable.

entries.zh: 今惜千戶侯，誰為官使者。」
entries.en: If you begrudge me now a marquisate of a thousand households, who will serve as your agent at court?"
entries.literal: Now if you begrudge me a marquisate of a thousand households, who will serve as your agent at court?"

entries.zh: 又有牒自論於朝廷曰：「當世祖晏駕之時，內外紛擾，珍之手抱至尊，口行處分，忠誠契闊，人誰不知。
entries.en: He also submitted a memorial arguing before the court, "When Emperor Shizu passed away, turmoil reigned within and without. Zhenzhi held the sovereign in his arms and issued orders by word of mouth—such loyal devotion in hardship is known to all.
entries.literal: He also submitted a memorial arguing before the court, "At the time of Emperor Shizu's death, turmoil reigned within and without; Zhenzhi held the supreme sovereign in his arms and issued orders by word of mouth—such loyal devotion in hardship is known to all.

entries.zh: 今希千戶侯，於分非過。」
entries.en: To hope now for a marquisate of a thousand households would not exceed my due."
entries.literal: To hope now for a marquisate of a thousand households would not exceed my due."

entries.zh: 乃許三百戶。
entries.en: Thereupon he was granted three hundred households.
entries.literal: Thereupon he was granted three hundred households.

entries.zh: 瞋恚形於言色，進為五百戶，又不肯受。
entries.en: Anger showed in his speech and countenance. The grant was raised to five hundred households, yet he still refused to accept.
entries.literal: Anger showed in his speech and countenance; the grant was raised to five hundred households, yet he still refused to accept.

entries.zh: 明帝議誅之，乃許封汝南縣。
entries.en: When Emperor Ming deliberated on executing him, the court finally granted him enfeoffment as count of Runan county.
entries.literal: When Emperor Ming deliberated on executing him, he finally granted enfeoffment as Count of Runan county.

entries.zh: 明帝即位，高、武舊人鮮有存者，法亮以主署文事，故不見疑，位任如故。
entries.en: When Emperor Ming ascended the throne, few of the old associates of Gao and Wu survived. Faliang, because he chiefly handled documentary affairs, was not suspected and retained his post and duties as before.
entries.literal: When Emperor Ming ascended the throne, few of the old associates of Gao and Wu survived; Faliang, because he chiefly handled documentary affairs, was not suspected and retained his post and duties as before.

entries.zh: 先是延昌殿為武帝陰室，藏諸服御，二少帝並居西殿。
entries.en: Earlier, Yanchang Hall had served as Emperor Wu's private chamber, storing his robes and accoutrements. The two young emperors both resided in the West Hall.
entries.literal: Earlier, Yanchang Hall had served as Emperor Wu's private chamber, storing his robes and accoutrements; the two young emperors both resided in the West Hall.

entries.zh: 及明帝居東齋，開陰室，出武帝白紗帽、防身刀，法亮歔欷流涕。
entries.en: When Emperor Ming took up residence in the Eastern Fast Hall and opened the private chamber, bringing out Emperor Wu's white gauze cap and personal dagger, Faliang sobbed and wept.
entries.literal: When Emperor Ming took up residence in the Eastern Fast Hall and opened the private chamber, bringing out Emperor Wu's white gauze cap and personal dagger, Faliang sobbed and wept.

entries.zh: 永泰元年，王敬則事平，法亮復受敕宣慰諸郡，無所納受。
entries.en: In the first year of Yongtai, after Wang Jingze's revolt was settled, Faliang again received orders to proclaim comfort to the various commanderies and accepted no gifts.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongtai, after Wang Jingze's revolt was settled, Faliang again received orders to proclaim comfort to the various commanderies and accepted no gifts.

entries.zh: 東昏即位，出法亮為大司農。
entries.en: When Emperor Donghun ascended the throne, Faliang was transferred out as minister of grand agriculture.
entries.literal: When Emperor Donghun ascended the throne, Faliang was transferred out as Minister of Grand Agriculture.

entries.zh: 中書權利之職，法亮不樂去，固辭不受。
entries.en: The Secretariat was the post of power and profit. Faliang was unwilling to leave and firmly declined, refusing to accept.
entries.literal: The Secretariat was the post of power and profit; Faliang was unwilling to leave and firmly declined, refusing to accept.

entries.zh: 既而代人已到，法亮垂涕而出，卒官。
entries.en: Before long his replacement arrived. Faliang wept as he departed and died in office.
entries.literal: Before long his replacement arrived; Faliang wept as he departed and died in office.

entries.zh: 戴法興 徐爰 阮佃夫 紀僧真 劉系宗 茹法亮 呂文顯 茹法珍 周石珍 陸驗 司馬申 施文慶 沈客卿 孔範
entries.en: Dai Faxing, Xu Ai, Ruan Dianfu, Ji Sengzhen, Liu Xizong, Ru Faliang, Lü Wenxian, Ru Fazhen, Zhou Shizhen, Lu Yan, Sima Shen, Shi Wenqing, Shen Keqing, and Kong Fan
entries.literal: Dai Faxing, Xu Ai, Ruan Dianfu, Ji Sengzhen, Liu Xizong, Ru Faliang, Lü Wenxian, Ru Fazhen, Zhou Shizhen, Lu Yan, Sima Shen, Shi Wenqing, Shen Keqing, and Kong Fan

entries.zh: 歷代天文誌，自《史記·天官書》後，唯晉、隋兩誌，備述天體、儀象、星占，唐、宋加詳，皆未盡也。
entries.en: Dynastic astronomy monographs after Sima Qian's Heavenly Offices are fully descriptive only in the Jin and Sui versions; Tang and Song expanded them, but gaps remain.
entries.literal: Astronomical treatises of successive dynasties, after the Records of the Grand Historian's Treatise on the Heavenly Offices, only the Jin and Sui treatises fully describe celestial bodies, instruments, and star divination; the Tang and Song added detail, yet none is complete.

entries.zh: 至元，景測益精明，占候較密，然疆宇所囿，聲教未宏，齊政窺璣，尚多略焉。
entries.en: Yuan observers refined instruments and tightened forecasts, but within a limited empire their cosmological governance still fell short.
entries.literal: Under the Yuan, instrumental observation grew more precise and prognostication denser, yet the realm they enclosed and cultural sway they spread were not broad; aligning government with the celestial pivot still left much omitted.

entries.zh: 有清統一區夏，聖聖相承。
entries.en: The Qing unified China, one sage emperor following another.
entries.literal: The Qing unified All-under-Heaven, sage succeeding sage.

entries.zh: 聖祖親釐象數，究極精微，前後制新儀七，測日月星辰，則窮極分秒；
entries.en: The Kangxi emperor personally mastered calendrical astronomy, devised seven new instruments, and measured the sun, moon, and stars to the second.
entries.literal: The Sacred Ancestor personally rectified numerology and celestial phenomena, penetrating the utmost subtlety; before and after he devised seven new instruments; in measuring sun, moon, and stars he exhausted fractions of seconds;

entries.zh: 度輿圖經緯，則穹歷幅隕。
entries.en: In surveying terrestrial longitude and latitude, he covered every corner of the realm.
entries.literal: in surveying the maps' longitude and latitude, he traversed every corner of the realm.

entries.zh: 世宗復以歲久積差，準監臣改用橢圓術。
entries.en: Yongzheng, seeing accumulated error over the years, had supervising astronomers adopt elliptical theory.
entries.literal: The Shizong Emperor again, because long years had accumulated discrepancy, ordered supervising officials to adopt the elliptical method.

entries.zh: 高宗又以舊記星紀，間有疏漏，御製璣衡撫辰儀，重加測候。
entries.en: Qianlong, finding gaps in older star catalogs, built the Armillary Sphere and Chronographic Instrument and remeasured the sky.
entries.literal: The Gaozong Emperor again, because old star records had occasional gaps, personally made the Armillary Sphere and Chronographic Instrument and took new observations.

entries.zh: 迨平定回疆及兩金川，復令重度裏差，增入時憲。
entries.en: After pacifying Xinjiang and the two Jinchuan campaigns, he ordered li-cha remeasured and entered into the Shixian calendar.
entries.literal: When the Muslim borderlands and the Two Jinchuan were pacified, he again ordered remeasurement of li-cha and added the results to the Time Constitution calendar.

entries.zh: 理明數確，器精法密，自古以來，所未有也。
entries.en: Clarity of principle, exactitude of number, refinement of instrument, and density of method were unmatched in earlier ages.
entries.literal: Principles clear, numbers exact, instruments refined, methods dense—from antiquity there has never been the like.

entries.zh: 今為天文誌，備載推驗之法，其天象昭垂，見於歷朝實錄及所司載記者，亦悉書之。
entries.en: This Astronomy Treatise records computational methods and every celestial phenomenon noted in dynastic Veritable Records and observatory logs.
entries.literal: Now for the Astronomy Treatise we fully record methods of computation and verification; celestial phenomena manifest overhead, as seen in successive dynasties' Veritable Records and the offices' records, are also all written.

entries.zh: 乾隆六十年以後，國史無徵，則從闕焉。
entries.en: After Qianlong 60 the Veritable Records offer no material, so the account stops there.
entries.literal: After Qianlong year 60 the National History has no testimony, and those years are therefore omitted.

entries.zh: 裏差者，因人所居有南北東西之不同，則天頂地平亦異，可以計裏而定，故名裏差，其所關於仰觀甚鉅。
entries.en: Li-cha ("li difference") names the shift in zenith and horizon when observers stand at different longitudes and latitudes; it matters greatly for what one sees overhead.
entries.literal: Li-cha arises because where people dwell differs in north, south, east, and west — the zenith and horizon also differ — and can be fixed by computing li; hence the name li-cha; its bearing on observations overhead is very great.

entries.zh: 蓋恒星之隱見，晝夜之永短，七曜之出沒，節氣之早晚，交食之深淺先後，莫不因之而各殊。
entries.en: Star visibility, day length, planetary risings, seasonal timing, and eclipse depth and order all vary with place.
entries.literal: For fixed stars' hiding and appearing, day and night's length, the seven luminaries' rising and setting, solar terms' earliness and lateness, and eclipses' depth and sequence — all differ thereby.

entries.zh: 惟得其所差之數，則各殊之故，皆可豫知，不致詫為失行而生飾說矣。
entries.en: Once the correction is known, local variation is predictable and need not be mistaken for errant heavens.
entries.literal: Only by obtaining the difference's number can the reasons for each difference be foreknown, so one does not marvel at seeming irregular motion and invent specious explanations.

entries.zh: 新法算書所載各省北極高及東西偏度，大概據輿圖道里定之，多有未確。
entries.en: Earlier manuals listed provincial polar heights and longitudinal offsets from map distances — often inaccurate.
entries.literal: The New Methods Calculation Book's recorded north polar altitudes and east-west offsets for each province were largely fixed from map routes and li — many are inexact.

entries.zh: 今以康熙年間實測各省及諸蒙古高度、偏度，並乾隆時憲所增省分，與回疆部落、兩金川土司等，晝夜永短，節氣早晚，推得高度、偏度備列焉。
entries.en: Here Kangxi surveys, Qianlong additions, Xinjiang, and Jinchuan observations yield revised polar altitudes and longitudinal offsets.
entries.literal: Now from Kangxi-era actual surveys of each province and Mongol banners, plus provinces added in the Qianlong Time Constitution, together with Muslim borderland tribes and the two Jinchuan chieftaincies — day and night length, solar-term timing — heights and offsets are derived and fully listed.

entries.zh: 漢創渾天儀，謂即璣衡遺制，唐、宋皆仿為之。
entries.en: Under the Han the armillary sphere was built, held to be the heir of the ancient armillary chronograph; Tang and Song followed the same design.
entries.literal: The Han created the armillary sphere, calling it the surviving form of the Armillary and Chronographic device; Tang and Song all copied it.

entries.zh: 至元始有簡儀、仰儀、闚幾、景符等器，視古加詳焉。
entries.en: The Yuan added the simplified armillary, altitude instrument, sighting tablet, and shadow marker—finer in make than older models.
entries.literal: Only under the Yuan did instruments such as the simplification armillary, the altitude instrument, the sighting tablet, and the shadow marker appear, more detailed than antiquity.

entries.zh: 明于北京齊化門內倚城築觀象臺，仿元制作渾儀、簡儀、天體三儀，置於臺上。
entries.en: In Ming Beijing, beside Qihua Gate, they raised the Observatory Terrace against the wall and placed Yuan-style armillary, simplified armillary, and celestial globe instruments upon it.
entries.literal: The Ming, within Beijing's Qihua Gate, built the Observatory Terrace against the city wall, copying Yuan models to make the armillary sphere, simplification armillary, and celestial globe, and set them on the terrace.

entries.zh: 台下有晷景堂、圭表、壺漏，清初因之。
entries.en: Beneath the terrace stood the Gnomon Hall, a gnomon and table, and clepsydras, retained unchanged at the dynasty's founding.
entries.literal: Below the terrace were the Gnomon Hall, gnomon and table, and clepsydra; the early Qing kept them as they were.

entries.zh: 康熙八年，聖祖用監臣南懷仁言，改造六儀，曰黃道經緯儀、赤道經緯儀、地平經儀、地平緯儀、紀限儀、天體儀。
entries.en: In Kangxi 8 the Kangxi emperor, on Verbiest's advice, commissioned six new instruments: ecliptic theodolite, equatorial theodolite, azimuth theodolite, altitude quadrant, sextant, and celestial globe.
entries.literal: In the eighth year of Kangxi, the Sacred Ancestor, following supervising official Ferdinand Verbiest's counsel, remade six instruments: the ecliptic theodolite, equatorial theodolite, horizontal azimuth instrument, horizontal altitude quadrant, limit-measuring quadrant, and celestial globe.

entries.zh: 五十二年，復將地平經、緯合為一儀。
entries.en: In Kangxi 52 the azimuth and altitude instruments were merged into a single combined instrument.
entries.literal: In the fifty-second year, the horizontal azimuth and altitude instruments were again combined into one instrument.

entries.zh: 乾隆九年，高宗御製璣衡撫辰儀，並安置臺上。
entries.en: In Qianlong 9 the Qianlong emperor built the Armillary Sphere and Chronographic Instrument and set it on the Observatory Terrace.
entries.literal: In the ninth year of Qianlong, the High Ancestor personally made the Armillary Sphere and Chronographic Instrument and also installed it on the terrace.

entries.zh: 今考各形制用法，悉著於篇。
entries.en: What follows records the design and operation of every instrument in full.
entries.literal: Now each instrument's form and use are fully set down in this chapter.

entries.zh: 順治二年，南京平，豫王班師還。
entries.en: In the second year of Shunzhi, Nanjing was pacified, and the Prince of Yu withdrew the army and returned.
entries.literal: In the second year of Shunzhi, Nanjing was pacified, and the Prince of Yu withdrew the army and returned.

entries.zh: 世祖赴南苑迎勞，樹十餘大纛，如初禮。
entries.en: The Shizu went to the Southern Park to welcome and reward them, erected more than ten great standards, as in the original rites.
entries.literal: The Shizu went to the Southern Park to welcome and reward them, erected more than ten great standards, as in the original rites.

entries.zh: 十三年，定制出征王大臣凱旋，遣王公一人偕大臣郊勞。
entries.en: In the thirteenth year it was established by regulation that when expedition princes and grand ministers returned triumphant, one imperial prince together with a minister was dispatched to welcome them in the suburbs.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year it was fixed by regulation that when expedition princes and grand ministers returned triumphant, one imperial prince together with a minister was dispatched to welcome them in the suburbs.

entries.zh: 乾隆時，版圖日廓。
entries.en: In the Qianlong period, the realm's borders expanded daily.
entries.literal: In the Qianlong period, the realm's borders expanded daily.

entries.zh: 二十年，剿平準噶爾，獲達瓦齊暨青海羅卜藏丹津，先後檻入。
entries.en: In the twentieth year, the Dzungars were suppressed and pacified; Dawachi and Lubuzangdanjin of Qinghai were captured and successively sent to the capital in caged carts.
entries.literal: In the twentieth year, the Dzungars were suppressed and pacified; Dawachi and Lubuzangdanjin of Qinghai were captured and successively sent in caged carts.

entries.zh: 一歲中兩行斯典。
entries.en: Within one year these ceremonies were performed twice.
entries.literal: Within one year these ceremonies were performed twice.

entries.zh: 越五年，底定回疆，討平攢拉促浸，皆遞舉盛儀。
entries.en: Five years later, the Muslim regions were fully settled and Zanla and Cujin were suppressed and pacified—all in succession occasioning grand ceremonies.
entries.literal: Five years later, the Muslim regions were fully settled, and Zanla and Cujin were suppressed and pacified—all in succession occasioned grand ceremonies.

entries.zh: 先後六歲，凱歌四奏，時論稱極盛雲。
entries.en: Over six years in all, the victory song was performed four times; commentators of the time called it the pinnacle of grandeur.
entries.literal: Over six years in all, the victory song was performed four times; commentators of the time called it the height of glory.

entries.zh: 乾隆二年，大閱，幸南苑，御帳殿。
entries.en: In the second year of Qianlong, a grand review was held; he visited the Southern Park and took his seat in the canopy hall.
entries.literal: In the second year of Qianlong, a grand review was held; he visited the Southern Park and took his seat in the canopy hall.

entries.zh: 軍隊既齊，步軍整列進。
entries.en: Once the armies were assembled, the infantry formed ranks and advanced in order.
entries.literal: Once the armies were assembled, the infantry formed ranks and advanced in order.

entries.zh: 以十丈為率，餘儀同。
entries.en: Taking ten zhang as the standard measure, the rest of the ceremony followed the same pattern.
entries.literal: Taking ten zhang as the standard measure, the rest of the ceremony followed the same pattern.

entries.zh: 令甲，大閱日，行宮外陳鹵簿，駕出，作鐃歌大樂，奏壯軍容章。
entries.en: By regulation, on the day of the grand review, the imperial retinue was displayed outside the traveling palace. When the imperial procession set out, the great naoge music was performed and the "Zhuang Junrong" anthem was played.
entries.literal: By regulation, on the day of the grand review, the imperial retinue was displayed outside the traveling palace. When the imperial procession set out, the great music of the naoge was performed and the "Zhuang Junrong" anthem was played.

entries.zh: 及還，作清樂，奏鬯皇威章。
entries.en: Upon returning, clear music was performed and the "Chang Huangwei" anthem was played.
entries.literal: Upon returning, clear music was performed and the "Chang Huangwei" anthem was played.

entries.zh: 凡操時鳴砲三，駕出及還同。
entries.en: Whenever drills were held, three cannon shots sounded—the same when setting out and when returning.
entries.literal: Whenever drills were held, three cannon shots sounded; the same when setting out and returning.

entries.zh: 即日賜各旗饌筵、羊豕、薪炭。
entries.en: That same day, each banner was granted feast provisions, sheep and pigs, firewood and charcoal.
entries.literal: That same day, each banner was granted feast provisions, sheep and pigs, firewood and charcoal.

entries.zh: 迄嘉慶間，皆如故事行。
entries.en: Down through the Jiaqing period, all was conducted according to precedent.
entries.literal: Down through the Jiaqing period, all was conducted according to precedent.

entries.zh: 秋獮清自太祖奮跡東陲，率臣下講武校獵習兵，太宗踵行之。
entries.en: Autumn Hunt: From the time the Taizu raised his banner on the eastern frontier, he led his ministers in martial training and hunting drills to keep troops in practice; the Taizong followed and continued this practice.
entries.literal: Autumn Hunt: From the time the Taizu raised his banner on the eastern frontier, he led his ministers in martial training, reviewing hunts to drill troops; the Taizong followed and continued this practice.

entries.zh: 世祖統一區夏，數幸南苑，令禁旅行圍，始立大狩扈從例。
entries.en: The Shizu unified the realm; he frequently visited the Southern Park and ordered that hunting encampments be forbidden in the capital region, establishing for the first time the protocol for attendants on the great autumn hunt.
entries.literal: The Shizu unified the realm; he frequently visited the Southern Park and ordered prohibition of hunting encampments in the capital region, establishing for the first time the protocol for attendants on the great autumn hunt.

entries.zh: 志六十五
entries.en: Treatise 65
entries.literal: Treatise 65.

entries.zh: 外國公使覲見禮康熙初，外洋始入貢，中朝款接，稍異籓服。
entries.en: Protocol for Audiences with Foreign Envoys: At the beginning of Kangxi, Western countries first began sending tribute; the central court received them in a manner slightly different from that for tributary domains.
entries.literal: Protocol for Audiences with Foreign Envoys: At the beginning of Kangxi, Western countries first began sending tribute; the central court received them with a manner slightly different from that for tributary domains.

entries.zh: 南懷仁官欽天監，贈工部侍郎，凡內廷召見，並許侍立，不行拜跪禮。
entries.en: Ferdinand Verbiest held office in the Directorate of Astronomy and was posthumously granted the rank of vice minister of works; whenever summoned to the inner court, he was permitted to stand in attendance and was not required to kneel or kowtow.
entries.literal: Ferdinand Verbiest held office in the Directorate of Astronomy and was posthumously granted the rank of vice minister of works; whenever summoned to the inner court, he was permitted to stand in attendance and was not required to perform kneeling or kowtowing rites.

entries.zh: 雍正間，羅馬教皇遣使來京，世宗許行西禮，且與握手。
entries.en: During Yongzheng, the Pope of Rome sent envoys to the capital; the Yongzheng Emperor permitted them to use Western etiquette and even shook hands with them.
entries.literal: During Yongzheng, the Pope of Rome sent envoys to the capital; the Yongzheng Emperor permitted them to use Western etiquette and even shook hands with them.

entries.zh: 乾隆季葉，英使馬格里入覲，禮臣與議儀式，彼以覲見英王為言，特旨允用西禮。
entries.en: In the late Qianlong period, the English envoy Markham was received in audience; ritual officials discussed the ceremony with him; citing the manner of audience before the King of England, a special edict permitted the use of Western etiquette.
entries.literal: In the late Qianlong period, the English envoy Markham was received in audience; ritual officials discussed the ceremony with him; citing the manner of audience before the King of England, a special edict permitted the use of Western etiquette.

entries.zh: 筵宴日，且親賜卮酒。
entries.en: On the banquet day, the emperor personally bestowed a cup of wine.
entries.literal: On the banquet day, the emperor personally bestowed a cup of wine.

entries.zh: 商約既締，將命頻繁。
entries.en: Once commercial treaties were concluded, diplomatic missions became frequent.
entries.literal: Once commercial treaties were concluded, diplomatic missions became frequent.

entries.zh: 咸、同間，外國使臣嘗求入覲，時以禮制乖異，力拒之。
entries.en: During the Xianfeng and Tongzhi reigns, foreign envoys repeatedly sought audiences, but because ritual forms differed, they were firmly refused.
entries.literal: During the Xianfeng and Tongzhi reigns, foreign envoys repeatedly sought audiences, but at the time, because ritual forms differed, they were firmly refused.

entries.zh: 同治時，英、法使臣固請再四，我猶繩以華制，莫之應。
entries.en: During Tongzhi, British and French envoys repeatedly pressed their requests, yet the court still held them to Chinese protocol and did not accede.
entries.literal: During Tongzhi, British and French envoys repeatedly pressed their requests, yet we still held them to Chinese protocol and did not accede.

entries.zh: 彼且曰，宜亟修好，阻其入覲，是靳以客禮也。
entries.en: They said in reply that good relations ought to be promptly restored, and that barring them from audience was to stint them of the courtesy due to guests.
entries.literal: They said in reply that good relations ought to be promptly restored, and that barring them from audience was to stint them of guest courtesy.

entries.zh: 康熙五十九年，定朝覲年例。
entries.en: In the fifty-ninth year of Kangxi, the annual schedule for court audiences was fixed.
entries.literal: In the fifty-ninth year of Kangxi, the annual schedule for court audiences was fixed.

entries.zh: 蒙古二十四部為兩班，喀爾喀札薩克等為四班。
entries.en: The twenty-four Mongol banners formed two rotations; the Khalkha jasaks and others formed four rotations.
entries.literal: The twenty-four Mongol banners formed two rotations; the Khalkha jasaks and others formed four rotations.

entries.zh: 雍正四年，帝念四十九旗王公台吉遠至勤勞，詔改三班，二歲一朝。
entries.en: In the fourth year of Yongzheng, the emperor, mindful of the long journey and labor of the princes and taiji of the forty-nine banners, decreed a change to three rotations, with audiences every two years.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Yongzheng, the emperor, mindful of the long journey and labor of the princes and taiji of the forty-nine banners, decreed a change to three rotations, with audiences every two years.

entries.zh: 咸豐八年，以蒙古汗王等遠道輸將，諭令停止年班。
entries.en: In the eighth year of Xianfeng, because the Mongol khans and princes made the long journey to bring tribute, an edict ordered the annual rotation to cease.
entries.literal: In the eighth year of Xianfeng, because the Mongol khans and princes made the long journey to bring tribute, an edict ordered the annual rotation to cease.

entries.zh: 御前行走者，番上如故。
entries.en: Those who served at the imperial presence continued to rotate on duty as before.
entries.literal: Those who served at the imperial presence continued to rotate on duty as before.

entries.zh: 順治初，定制，諸國朝貢，齎表及方物，限船三艘，艘百人，貢役二十人。
entries.en: At the beginning of Shunzhi regulations were fixed: for tribute missions from the various states, bearing memorials and local products, the limit was three ships, one hundred men per ship, and twenty tribute bearers.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Shunzhi regulations were fixed: for tribute missions from the various states, bearing memorials and local products, the limit was three ships, one hundred men per ship, and twenty tribute bearers.

entries.zh: 十三年，俄國察罕汗遣使入貢，以不諳朝儀，卻其貢，遣之歸。
entries.en: In the thirteenth year, the Tsar of Russia sent envoys to present tribute; because they were unfamiliar with court ritual, their tribute was refused and they were sent home.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year, the Tsar of Russia sent envoys to present tribute; because they were unfamiliar with court ritual, their tribute was refused and they were sent home.

entries.zh: 明年復表貢，途經三載，表文仍不合體制。
entries.en: The next year they again presented a memorial tribute; the journey took three years, and the memorial still did not conform to required form.
entries.literal: The next year they again presented a memorial tribute; the journey took three years, and the memorial still did not conform to required form.

entries.zh: 世祖以外邦從化，宜予涵容，量加恩賞，諭令毋入覲。
entries.en: The Shunzhi Emperor, deeming the foreign state had submitted in good faith, granted generous rewards and ordered that they need not seek audience.
entries.literal: The Shunzhi Emperor, deeming the foreign state had submitted in good faith, granted generous rewards and ordered that they need not seek audience.

entries.zh: 初，琉球、安南、暹羅諸使來，議政大臣咸會集，賜坐及茶。
entries.en: At first, when envoys from Ryukyu, Annam, and Siam came, the grand secretaries all assembled and were granted seated reception and tea.
entries.literal: At first, when envoys from Ryukyu, Annam, and Siam came, the grand secretaries all assembled and were granted seated reception and tea.

entries.zh: 乾隆初元，諭停止。
entries.en: At the beginning of the Qianlong reign, an edict ordered this discontinued.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Qianlong reign, an edict ordered this discontinued.

entries.zh: 時屬國陪臣增擴，敕所司給皇清職貢圖，以詔方來。
entries.en: At that time, as tributary attendants expanded in number, officials were ordered to distribute the Imperial Tribute Atlas to instruct those who would come.
entries.literal: At that time, as tributary attendants expanded in number, officials were ordered to distribute the Imperial Tribute Atlas to instruct those who would come.

entries.zh: 四十七年正月，紫光閣錫燕，朝鮮、琉球、南掌陪臣與焉。
entries.en: In the first month of the forty-seventh year, a feast was granted at the Ziguang Pavilion; attendant ministers from Korea, Ryukyu, and Lan Xang were among those present.
entries.literal: In the first month of the forty-seventh year, a feast was granted at the Ziguang Pavilion; attendant ministers from Korea, Ryukyu, and Lan Xang were among those present.

entries.zh: 燕罷，賜珍物。
entries.en: When the banquet ended, precious gifts were granted.
entries.literal: When the banquet ended, precious gifts were granted.

entries.zh: 五十年，舉千叟宴，特命朝鮮賀正陪臣齒逾六十者充正、副使，預宴賦詩。
entries.en: In the fiftieth year, at the banquet of a thousand elders, Korean New Year envoys over sixty were specially appointed chief and deputy envoys to attend the feast and compose poetry.
entries.literal: In the fiftieth year, at the banquet of a thousand elders, Korean New Year envoys over sixty were specially appointed chief and deputy envoys to attend the feast and compose poetry.

entries.zh: 越五年，安南國王阮光平來京祝壽，定行禮班序，列親王、郡王間，其陪臣仍附班末。
entries.en: Five years later, the king of Annam, Nguyen Quang Binh, came to the capital to congratulate the emperor on his birthday; his ceremonial rank was fixed between princes of the first and second rank, while his attendants still stood at the end of the ranks.
entries.literal: Five years later, the king of Annam, Nguyen Quang Binh, came to the capital to congratulate the emperor on his birthday; his ceremonial rank was fixed between princes of the first and second rank, while his attendants still stood at the end of the ranks.

entries.zh: 五十八年，英吉利入貢，使臣瑪戛爾等覲見，自陳不習拜跪，及至御前，而跽伏自若。
entries.en: In the fifty-eighth year, England presented tribute; the envoys Macartney and others were received in audience; they declared themselves unaccustomed to kneeling and kowtowing, yet when they came before the throne they prostrated themselves quite naturally.
entries.literal: In the fifty-eighth year, England presented tribute; the envoys Macartney and others were received in audience; they declared themselves unaccustomed to kneeling and kowtowing, yet when they came before the throne they prostrated themselves quite naturally.

entries.zh: 各國親王覲見儀，始光緒二十四年。
entries.en: The protocol for audiences with foreign princes began in the twenty-fourth year of Guangxu.
entries.literal: The protocol for audiences with foreign princes began in the twenty-fourth year of Guangxu.

entries.zh: 德國親王亨利入覲，帝幸頤和園，御仁壽殿，亨利公服入，遞國書，帝慰勞之。
entries.en: The German Prince Henry was received in audience; the emperor went to the Summer Palace and held court in the Hall of Benevolent Longevity; Prince Henry entered in formal dress, presented his credentials, and the emperor comforted him.
entries.literal: The German Prince Henry was received in audience; the emperor went to the Summer Palace and held court in the Hall of Benevolent Longevity; Prince Henry entered in formal dress, presented his credentials, and the emperor comforted him.

entries.zh: 既，亨利慾覲皇太后，帝奉懿旨代見。
entries.en: Afterward Prince Henry wished to pay respects to the empress dowager; the emperor received him on her behalf by her express command.
entries.literal: Afterward Prince Henry wished to pay respects to the empress dowager; the emperor received him on her behalf by her express command.

entries.zh: 是日巳刻，御玉瀾堂，亨利偕德使海靖等入，外部司官引殿東便門外入布幄少憩。
entries.en: That day at the si hour, the emperor held court at the Hall of Jade Ripples; Prince Henry entered together with the German envoy Heyking and others; officials of the foreign ministry led them in through the east side gate of the hall to rest briefly in the canvas tent.
entries.literal: That day at the si hour, the emperor held court at the Hall of Jade Ripples; Prince Henry entered together with the German envoy Heyking and others; officials of the foreign ministry led them in through the east side gate of the hall to rest briefly in the canvas tent.

entries.zh: 駕至，扈從如儀，鳴鞭三，升座。
entries.en: When the imperial procession arrived, the escort formed as prescribed; the whip was cracked three times, and the emperor ascended the throne.
entries.literal: When the imperial procession arrived, the escort formed as prescribed; the whip was cracked three times, and the emperor ascended the throne.

entries.zh: 慶親王等侍左右，外部長官率亨利等自中門入，北鄉一鞠躬，行數武又一鞠躬，至龍柱前又一鞠躬。
entries.en: Prince Qing and others attended at his sides; the chief of the foreign ministry led Prince Henry and the others in through the central gate; facing north, they bowed once, after several paces bowed again, and upon reaching the dragon pillars bowed once more.
entries.literal: Prince Qing and others attended at his sides; the chief of the foreign ministry led Prince Henry and the others in through the central gate; facing north, they bowed once, after several paces bowed again, and upon reaching the dragon pillars bowed once more.

entries.zh: 然後奉國書進，慶親王降左階接受，陳玉案，亨利等又一鞠躬，帝頷首答之，操國語慰勞。
entries.en: They then advanced to present their credentials; Prince Qing descended the left steps to receive them and placed them on the jade table; Prince Henry and the others bowed again, and the emperor nodded in reply and offered words of comfort in the national language.
entries.literal: They then advanced to present their credentials; Prince Qing descended the left steps to receive them and placed them on the jade table; Prince Henry and the others bowed again, and the emperor nodded in reply and offered words of comfort in the national language.

entries.zh: 慶親王跪案左聆玉音，降階，操漢語傳宣。
entries.en: Prince Qing knelt at the left of the table to listen to the imperial words, then descended the steps and relayed the message in Chinese.
entries.literal: Prince Qing knelt at the left of the table to listen to the jade voice, then descended the steps and relayed the message in Chinese.

entries.zh: 德繙譯官譯畢，亨利等又一鞠躬，帝仍頷首答之。
entries.en: When the German interpreter had finished translating, Prince Henry and the others bowed again, and the emperor again nodded in reply.
entries.literal: When the German interpreter had finished translating, Prince Henry and the others bowed again, and the emperor again nodded in reply.

entries.zh: 亨利等退數武又一鞠躬，退至堂左，又一鞠躬。
entries.en: Prince Henry and the others withdrew several paces and bowed again, then withdrew to the left of the hall and bowed once more.
entries.literal: Prince Henry and the others withdrew several paces and bowed again, then withdrew to the left of the hall and bowed once more.

entries.zh: 禮成。
entries.en: The rites were complete.
entries.literal: The rites were complete.

entries.zh: 二十七年，聯軍平拳匪，各國挾求更改禮節。
entries.en: In the twenty-seventh year, the allied armies suppressed the Boxer rebels, and the various powers demanded changes to ceremonial protocol.
entries.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, the allied armies suppressed the Boxer rebels, and the various powers demanded changes to ceremonial protocol.

entries.zh: 謂各使臣會同覲見，必在太和殿。
entries.en: They insisted that joint audiences of all envoys must take place in the Hall of Supreme Harmony.
entries.literal: They insisted that joint audiences of all envoys must take place in the Hall of Supreme Harmony.

entries.zh: 一國使臣單行覲見者，必在乾清宮。
entries.en: Audiences for a single envoy from one country must take place in the Palace of Heavenly Purity.
entries.literal: Audiences for a single envoy from one country must take place in the Palace of Heavenly Purity.

entries.zh: 呈遞國書，必遣乘輿往迓，至宮殿前降輿，禮成送歸。
entries.en: When presenting credentials, an imperial sedan must be dispatched to meet them; they were to dismount before the palace hall, and after the rites were complete they were to be escorted back.
entries.literal: When presenting credentials, an imperial sedan must be dispatched to meet them; they dismounted before the palace hall, and after the rites were complete they were escorted back.

entries.zh: 齎奏國書，必自中門入，帝必躬親接受。
entries.en: When bearing memorials and credentials, they must enter through the central gate, and the emperor must personally receive them.
entries.literal: When bearing memorials and credentials, they must enter through the central gate, and the emperor must personally receive them.

entries.zh: 設宴乾清宮，帝必躬親入座。
entries.en: Banquets were to be held in the Palace of Heavenly Purity, and the emperor must personally take his seat.
entries.literal: Banquets were to be held in the Palace of Heavenly Purity, and the emperor must personally take his seat.

entries.zh: 嗣復允會同覲見改在乾清宮，而轎用黃色。
entries.en: Later it was also agreed that joint audiences would be moved to the Palace of Heavenly Purity and that yellow sedans would be used.
entries.literal: Later it was also agreed that joint audiences would be moved to the Palace of Heavenly Purity, while the sedans used would be yellow.

entries.zh: 於是慶親王奕劻等以天澤堂廉之辨，不能每事曲從。
entries.en: Thereupon Prince Qing and others, mindful of the distinction between imperial majesty and the dignity of the hall, could not accede to every demand.
entries.literal: Thereupon Prince Qing and others, mindful of the distinction between imperial majesty and the dignity of the hall, could not accede to every demand.

entries.zh: 遂與各使磋商，歷時數月，始將乘坐黃轎、太和殿覲見暨宮殿階前降輿三事酌議改易，而爭議始息。
entries.en: They then negotiated with the various envoys; after several months, agreement was finally reached to modify the three points concerning yellow sedans, audiences in the Hall of Supreme Harmony, and dismounting before the palace steps—and only then did the disputes cease.
entries.literal: They then negotiated with the various envoys; after several months, agreement was finally reached to modify the three points concerning yellow sedans, audiences in the Hall of Supreme Harmony, and dismounting before the palace steps—and only then did the disputes cease.

entries.zh: 志六十六
entries.en: Treatise 66
entries.literal: Treatise 66

entries.zh: 皇太子皇子及皇子福晉喪儀皇太子喪儀，有清家法，不立儲貳。
entries.en: Mourning rites for the crown prince, imperial sons, and consorts of imperial sons. Mourning rites for the crown prince: by Qing dynastic custom no heir apparent was formally installed.
entries.literal: Mourning rites for the crown prince, imperial sons, and consorts of imperial sons. As for mourning rites for the crown prince: under Qing household law the heir apparent is not established.

entries.zh: 至乾隆三年，皇次子永璉薨。
entries.en: In Qianlong 3, the second imperial son Yonglian died.
entries.literal: In the third year of the Qianlong reign, the second imperial son, Yonglian, died.

entries.zh: 高宗諭曰：「永璉為朕嫡子，雖未冊立，已定建儲大計，其典禮應視皇太子行。」
entries.en: The Qianlong Emperor decreed: "Yonglian was my son by the empress. Though he had not yet been installed as heir, the plan to make him successor was already settled; his funeral observances should follow those of a crown prince."
entries.literal: The Gaozong Emperor decreed: "Yonglian was my son by the empress; although he had not yet been enfeoffed as heir, the great plan to establish him as successor was already fixed; the rites should be observed as for a crown prince."

entries.zh: 禮臣奏言：「皇太子喪禮，會典未載。
entries.en: The rites officials memorialized: "Mourning rites for a crown prince are not recorded in the Collected Statutes.
entries.literal: The rites officials memorialized: "Mourning rites for a crown prince are not recorded in the Collected Statutes.

entries.zh: 舊制，沖齡薨，不成服。
entries.en: Under the old regulations, when a child died in infancy no full mourning was observed.
entries.literal: Under the old regulations, when one died in infancy no mourning garments were worn.

entries.zh: 今議，皇帝素服，輟朝七日。
entries.en: It was now proposed that the emperor wear plain mourning dress and suspend court for seven days.
entries.literal: It was now proposed that the emperor wear plain mourning dress and suspend court audiences for seven days.

entries.zh: 若親臨奠醊，冠摘纓。
entries.en: If he came in person to offer libations, he was to remove the tassels from his cap.
entries.literal: If he came in person to offer libations, he was to remove the tassels from his cap.

entries.zh: 典喪大臣、奏遣之王公暨皇太子侍從官咸成服，內務府佐領、內管領下護軍、驍騎校等成服，以六百人為率，並初祭日除。
entries.en: The minister overseeing the funeral, princes and nobles sent on memorial business, and all the crown prince's attendants were to wear mourning; assistant commandants, chief stewards, guards, adjutants, and the like—about six hundred men in all—were likewise to mourn and lay aside mourning on the day of the first sacrifice.
