entries.literal: The minister in charge of the funeral, the princes and nobles dispatched on memorial business, and all attendants of the crown prince were to don mourning dress; assistant commandants and chief stewards of the Imperial Household Department, the guards and adjutants under them, and the like were to don mourning dress at the rate of six hundred men, all to lay aside mourning on the day of the first sacrifice.

entries.zh: 直省官奉文日，咸摘冠纓素服三日，停嫁娶、輟音樂，京師四十日，外省半之。
entries.en: When provincial officials received the document, all were to remove cap tassels and wear plain dress for three days, suspend weddings, and cease music—for forty days in the capital and half that in the provinces.
entries.literal: On the day provincial officials received the document, all were to remove cap tassels and wear plain dress for three days, suspend weddings, and cease music; in the capital for forty days, in the provinces half that.

entries.zh: 幼殤例無引幡，今請依雍正時懷親王喪儀，引幡仍用。
entries.en: Early death in infancy normally allowed no funeral banner; it was now requested that, following the mourning rites for Prince Huai under Yongzheng, the banner still be used.
entries.literal: For early death in infancy there was normally no funeral banner; it was now requested that, following the mourning rites for Prince Huai in the Yongzheng reign, the banner still be used.

entries.zh: 外籓額駙、王、公、台吉、公主、福晉、郡主服內來京，男摘冠纓，女去首飾。
entries.en: Imperial sons-in-law of the outer domains, princes, dukes, taiji, princesses, consorts, and commandery princesses who came to the capital while in mourning were to have men remove cap tassels and women remove head ornaments.
entries.literal: Imperial sons-in-law of the outer domains, princes, dukes, taiji, princesses, consorts, and commandery princesses who came to the capital while in mourning: men removed cap tassels, women removed head ornaments.

entries.zh: 朝鮮使臣素服七日。
entries.en: Korean envoys wore plain mourning dress for seven days.
entries.literal: Korean envoys wore plain dress for seven days.

entries.zh: 金棺用桐木。」
entries.en: The gilt coffin was to be of paulownia wood."
entries.literal: The gilt coffin was to be of paulownia wood."

entries.zh: 啟奠帝親祭酒，奉移親視送。
entries.en: At the opening of mourning the emperor offered wine in person and personally viewed the removal of the coffin.
entries.literal: At the opening of mourning the emperor offered wine in person and personally viewed the removal of the coffin for escort.

entries.zh: 禮部長官祭轝。
entries.en: The chief minister of rites sacrificed at the funeral carriage.
entries.literal: The chief minister of rites sacrificed at the bier.

entries.zh: 初祭內外會集，帝至殯殿奠酒三爵，每奠眾一拜，是日除服薙髮。
entries.en: At the first sacrifice the inner and outer courts assembled; the emperor came to the mourning hall and offered three libations of wine, the assembly bowing once at each; on that day mourning was laid aside and the hair was cut.
entries.literal: At the first sacrifice the inner and outer courts assembled; the emperor came to the mourning hall and offered wine in three libations, and at each libation the assembly bowed once; on that day mourning was laid aside and the hair was cut.

entries.zh: 將冊諡，先期遣告太廟後殿、奉先殿，諡曰端慧。
entries.en: Before investiture with a posthumous title, envoys were dispatched to announce at the rear hall of the Imperial Ancestral Temple and at the Hall for Veneration of Ancestors; his posthumous title was Duanhui.
entries.literal: When he was to be given a posthumous title, envoys were dispatched beforehand to announce at the rear hall of the Imperial Ancestral Temple and at the Hall for Veneration of Ancestors; his posthumous title was Duanhui.

entries.zh: 禮成。
entries.en: The rites were completed.
entries.literal: The rites were completed.

entries.zh: 禮部頒行各省，並牒朝鮮國王，文到率百官素服，軍民罷嫁娶、音樂各三日。
entries.en: The Ministry of Rites promulgated this to all provinces and dispatched notice to the king of Korea; on receipt all officials wore plain dress, and soldiers and civilians suspended weddings and music for three days.
entries.literal: The Ministry of Rites promulgated this to all provinces and also sent a dispatch to the king of Korea; when the document arrived all officials wore plain dress, and soldiers and civilians suspended weddings and music for three days each.

entries.zh: 八年，葬硃華山園寢。
entries.en: In the eighth year he was buried in the garden mausoleum at Zhuhua Mountain.
entries.literal: In the eighth year he was buried in the garden mausoleum at Zhuhua Mountain.

entries.zh: 忌辰順治十年，定盛京、興京三陵忌辰，遣守陵官行禮，獻酒果，不讀祝，不奠帛。
entries.en: Anniversary sacrifices: in Shunzhi 10 anniversaries of the three mausoleums at Shengjing and Xingjing were fixed; tomb-guard officials performed the rites with wine and fruit, without reading prayers or offering silks.
entries.literal: Anniversary sacrifices: in the tenth year of Shunzhi it was fixed that on the anniversaries of the three mausoleums at Shengjing and Xingjing, tomb-guard officials performed the rites, offering wine and fruit, without reading prayers or offering silks.

entries.zh: 十二年，改定忌辰遣官，禮部具題請旨。
entries.en: In the twelfth year dispatch of officials for anniversary sacrifices was changed to require memorialization by the Ministry of Rites for imperial order.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year it was changed that officials dispatched for anniversary sacrifices were memorialized by the Ministry of Rites for imperial order.

entries.zh: 康熙三年，復定三陵忌辰在隆恩殿神牌前揭幔致祭。
entries.en: In Kangxi 3 it was again fixed that the three mausoleums' anniversaries were offered before the spirit tablets in the Hall of Imperial Grace with the curtain drawn aside.
entries.literal: In the third year of Kangxi it was again fixed that anniversaries of the three mausoleums were offered before the spirit tablets in the Hall of Imperial Grace with the curtain drawn aside.

entries.zh: 雍正四年，帝以聖祖喪滿，哀慕無窮，思依三年內祭禮舉行，下禮臣議。
entries.en: In Yongzheng 4, with mourning for Kangxi complete but grief unbounded, the emperor wished to follow three-year mourning sacrifices and ordered rites officials to deliberate.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Yongzheng, as the emperor's mourning for the Sagely Ancestor was complete yet grief was boundless, he wished to follow the sacrificial rites within the three-year period and ordered the rites officials to deliberate.

entries.zh: 尋議上，依周年祭祀例，遣在京或陵寢王公大臣一人承祭，在京王公百官遣三之一陪祭。
entries.en: The deliberation was soon submitted: following anniversary-sacrifice precedent, one prince or grand minister at capital or mausoleum presided; at the capital one-third of princes and officials assisted.
entries.literal: Shortly the deliberation was submitted: following the precedent for anniversary sacrifices, one prince or grand minister at the capital or mausoleum was dispatched to preside; at the capital one-third of princes and officials were dispatched to assist.

entries.zh: 著為令。
entries.en: Established as regulation.
entries.literal: Established as regulation.

entries.zh: 十三年，高宗嗣服，議定聖祖忌辰，依陵寢四時大祭，用太牢，獻帛爵，讀祝文，遣官承祭，陵寢官悉陪祀，罷遣京官往。
entries.en: In the thirteenth year, when Qianlong succeeded, the Sagely Ancestor's anniversary was fixed to follow mausoleum four-season great sacrifices with full ox, silks, libation cups, and prayers; an official presided with all mausoleum officials assisting; capital officials were no longer dispatched.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year, when the Gaozong succeeded to mourning, it was deliberated and fixed that on the Sagely Ancestor's anniversary, following the four-season great sacrifices at the mausoleum, a full ox was used, silks and libation cups offered, prayers read, an official dispatched to preside, all mausoleum officials assisting; dispatch of capital officials was discontinued.

entries.zh: 嗣後列聖、列後忌辰，永如例行。
entries.en: Thereafter anniversaries of successive emperors and empresses followed this precedent permanently.
entries.literal: Thereafter anniversaries of successive emperors and empresses followed this precedent permanently.

entries.zh: 定制，一品官以上予否請上裁，二品官以下不獲請。
entries.en: By regulation first-rank and above required imperial discretion; second rank and below could not request.
entries.literal: By regulation, for first-rank officials and above grant or not was at imperial discretion; second rank and below might not request.

entries.zh: 其得諡者，率出自特旨，或以勤勞，或以節義，或以文學，或以武功。
entries.en: Recipients were mostly by special edict—for diligence, integrity, letters, or arms.
entries.literal: Those who received posthumous titles were mostly by special edict—for diligence, integrity, literary accomplishment, or military merit.

entries.zh: 破格崇褒，用示激勸。
entries.en: Exceptional honors beyond precedent encouraged merit.
entries.literal: Exceptional honors beyond precedent showed encouragement.

entries.zh: 嘉、道以前，諡典從嚴，往往有階至一品例可得而未得者。
entries.en: Before Jiaqing and Daoguang the canon was strict; many who qualified by first rank did not receive titles.
entries.literal: Before Jiaqing and Daoguang the posthumous canon was strict; often those who had risen to first rank by precedent could have but did not.

entries.zh: 世宗朝，一等公福善，大學士魏裔介，將軍佛尼勒、莽依圖，都統馮國相，尚書湯斌、徐潮、瑪爾罕輩，望實素高，入祀賢良。
entries.en: Under Yongzheng, Duke Fushan, Grand Secretary Wei Yijie, Generals Foniye and Manggitu, Commander Feng Guoxiang, Ministers Tang Bin, Xu Chao, Maerhan, and others of high repute entered the shrine of worthies.
entries.literal: In the Yongzheng reign, First-rank Duke Fushan, Grand Secretary Wei Yijie, Generals Foniye and Manggitu, Commander Feng Guoxiang, Ministers Tang Bin, Xu Chao, and Maerhan and others were of high repute and entered the shrine of worthies.

entries.zh: 逮至高宗初元，始獲追諡。
entries.en: Only at the beginning of Qianlong did they receive posthumous titles.
entries.literal: Only at the beginning of the Gaozong reign did they receive posthumous titles.

entries.zh: 易名盛典，殊不易得。
entries.en: The great honor of a posthumous name was especially hard to obtain.
entries.literal: The great honor of changing the name was especially hard to obtain.

entries.zh: 乾隆十三年，皇子永琮甫二周薨，帝言：「建儲之意，朕雖默定，然未若端慧太子旨已封貯，喪儀應視皇子為優。」
entries.en: In Qianlong 13 the imperial son Yongcong died at barely two; the emperor said: "Though I had silently fixed my intent to establish an heir, it was not like the Duanhui Crown Prince, whose edict was already sealed away; his mourning rites should exceed those for an ordinary imperial son."
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year of Qianlong, the imperial son Yongcong died at barely two years of age; the emperor said: "My intent to establish an heir, though fixed in silence, was not like that of the Duanhui Crown Prince, whose edict was already sealed in storage; the mourning rites should be preferred over those for an ordinary imperial son."

entries.zh: 大祭親臨奠醊，諡悼敏，後追封哲親王。
entries.en: At the great sacrifice the emperor came in person to offer libations; his posthumous title was Daomin, and later he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince Zhe.
entries.literal: At the great sacrifice the emperor came in person to offer libations; his posthumous title was Daomin, and later he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince Zhe.

entries.zh: 越二年，皇長子永璜薨，金棺用杉木，其福晉及皇孫綿德等翦發去首飾，成服百日而除，素服二十七月。
entries.en: Two years later the eldest imperial son Yonghuang died; the gilt coffin was of fir; his consort and the imperial grandson Miande and others cut their hair, removed ornaments, wore full mourning for a hundred days and plain dress for twenty-seven months.
entries.literal: Two years later the eldest imperial son Yonghuang died; the gilt coffin was of fir wood; his consort and the imperial grandson Miande and others cut their hair and removed head ornaments, wore mourning for a hundred days and then laid it aside, and wore plain dress for twenty-seven months.

entries.zh: 成服王公大祭日除。
entries.en: Princes and nobles in mourning laid it aside on the day of the great sacrifice.
entries.literal: Princes and nobles who had worn mourning laid it aside on the day of the great sacrifice.

entries.zh: 禮部以第三日移殯，請輟朝三日，詔改五日，追封定親王，諡曰安。
entries.en: The Ministry of Rites proposed moving the coffin on the third day and suspending court for three days; an edict changed this to five; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince Ding with the posthumous title An.
entries.literal: The Ministry of Rites proposed moving the coffin on the third day and requested suspending court for three days; an edict changed this to five days; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince Ding with the posthumous title An.

entries.zh: 初祭、大祭並親臨奠醊。
entries.en: At the first sacrifice and the great sacrifice the emperor came in person to offer libations.
entries.literal: At the first sacrifice and the great sacrifice the emperor came in person to offer libations.

entries.zh: 二十五年，皇三子永璋薨，詔用郡王例治喪，輟朝二日。
entries.en: In the twenty-fifth year the third imperial son Yongzhang died; an edict ordered the funeral by commandery-prince precedent with court suspended two days.
entries.literal: In the twenty-fifth year the third imperial son Yongzhang died; an edict ordered the funeral conducted by commandery-prince precedent and court suspended for two days.

entries.zh: 大內、宗室素服咸五日，不祭神。
entries.en: The inner palace and imperial clan wore plain dress for five days and did not sacrifice to the gods.
entries.literal: Within the inner palace and the imperial clan plain dress was worn for five days each; sacrifices to the gods were not performed.

entries.zh: 追封循郡王。
entries.en: He was posthumously enfeoffed as commandery prince of Xun.
entries.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as commandery prince of Xun.

entries.zh: 四十一年，皇十二子永璂薨，詔用宗室公例治喪。
entries.en: In the forty-first year the twelfth imperial son Yongji died; an edict ordered the funeral by clan-duke precedent.
entries.literal: In the forty-first year the twelfth imperial son Yongji died; an edict ordered the funeral conducted by the precedent for a clan duke.

entries.zh: 嘉慶四年，追封貝勒。
entries.en: In Jiaqing 4 he was posthumously enfeoffed as beile.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Jiaqing he was posthumously enfeoffed as beile.

entries.zh: 雍正六年，皇八子福惠卒，帝輟朝，大內素服各三日，不祭神，詔用親王禮葬。
entries.en: In Yongzheng 6 the eighth imperial son Fuhui died; the emperor suspended court; the inner palace wore plain dress for three days and did not sacrifice to the gods, and an edict ordered burial by princely rites.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Yongzheng, the eighth imperial son Fuhui died; the emperor suspended court; within the inner palace plain dress was worn for three days each, sacrifices to the gods were not performed, and an edict ordered burial by princely rites.

entries.zh: 十三年，追封親王，諡曰懷。
entries.en: In the thirteenth year he was posthumously enfeoffed as prince with the posthumous title Huai.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year he was posthumously enfeoffed as prince and given the posthumous title Huai.

entries.zh: 賜祭葬世祖初入關，沿崇德間例，超品公，一、二、三等公卒，遣官祭三次；
entries.en: Bestowal of sacrifice and burial: when Shunzhi first entered the Pass, following Chongde precedent, super-rank and first-, second-, and third-rank dukes received three official sacrifices;
entries.literal: Bestowal of sacrificial rites and burial: when the Shizu first entered the Pass, following the Chongde precedent, for super-rank dukes and first-, second-, and third-rank dukes who died, officials were dispatched to sacrifice three times;

entries.zh: 子、副都統二次；
entries.en: for sons and vice commanders-in-chief, twice;
entries.literal: for sons and vice commanders-in-chief, twice;

entries.zh: 參領、佐領一次。
entries.en: for battalion commanders and assistant commandants, once.
entries.literal: for battalion commanders and assistant commandants, once.

entries.zh: 陣亡與有勛勞者，遣官治喪，出自上裁。
entries.en: For those killed in battle or with merit, officials conducted the funeral at imperial discretion.
entries.literal: For those killed in battle or with meritorious service, officials conducted the funeral at the emperor's discretion.

entries.zh: 乾隆四十年，高宗特旨允以獨子兼祧，於是始定兼祧例。
entries.en: In the fortieth year of Qianlong, Emperor Gaozong issued a special edict allowing an only son to continue two ancestral lines, thereby establishing the precedent for dual-line succession.
entries.literal: In the fortieth year of Qianlong, Emperor Gaozong specially approved by edict that an only son could continue two ancestral lines; from this the precedent for dual-line succession was established.

entries.zh: 兼祧者從權以濟經，足補古禮之闕。
entries.en: Dual-line succession used expedient means to aid the canonical, supplementing gaps in ancient ritual.
entries.literal: Dual-line succession used expedient authority to aid the canonical, sufficient to supplement gaps in ancient ritual.

entries.zh: 會典服制別大宗、小宗，以大宗為重。
entries.en: The Collected Statutes distinguished great and lesser descent-lines, the great line being weighty.
entries.literal: The Collected Statutes mourning dress distinguished great descent-line and lesser descent-line, taking the great line as weighty.

entries.zh: 大宗依服制本條持服，兼祧依降服持服。
entries.en: The great line followed the main mourning article; dual-line succession followed reduced mourning.
entries.literal: The great line wore mourning by the garment regulation's main article; dual-line succession wore mourning by reduced grade.

entries.zh: 乾隆間，諭京旗文武官遇親喪，百日後即入署治事，持服如故。
entries.en: Under Qianlong, capital banner officials on parents' mourning entered office after a hundred days while still in mourning dress.
entries.literal: In the Qianlong reign an edict ordered capital banner civil and military officials on parents' mourning to enter office after a hundred days while still wearing mourning.

entries.zh: 罷與祭祀、朝會。
entries.en: Sacrifices and court assemblies were discontinued.
entries.literal: Participation in sacrifices and court assemblies was discontinued.

entries.zh: 志六十八
entries.en: Treatise Sixty-Eight
entries.literal: Treatise Sixty-Eight

entries.zh: 清自太宗天聰六年定儀仗之制，凡國中往來，御前旗三對，傘二柄，校尉六人，其制甚簡。
entries.en: Under Taizong, in the sixth year of Tiancong, the Qing first set regulations for ceremonial regalia. For journeys within the realm the emperor was preceded by three pairs of imperial flags, two umbrellas, and six guardsmen—a notably spare establishment.
entries.literal: From the sixth year of Tiancong under Taizong, the Qing fixed regulations for ceremonial regalia. For travel within the realm there were three pairs of imperial front flags, two umbrellas, and six guardsmen—the system was very simple.

entries.zh: 自天聰十年改元崇德，始定御仗數目及品官儀從。
entries.en: In the tenth year of Tiancong, when the reign title was changed to Chongde, the court first fixed how many pieces of imperial regalia there should be and what ceremonial retinues ranked officials might use.
entries.literal: From the tenth year of Tiancong, when the era name was changed to Chongde, the numbers of imperial regalia and the ceremonial retinues of ranked officials were first fixed.

entries.zh: 迨世祖入關定鼎，參稽往制，量加增飾。
entries.en: After the Shizu emperor entered the passes and established the dynasty at its new capital, he consulted earlier regulations and added further ornamentation in due measure.
entries.literal: When the Shizu emperor entered the passes and established the capital, he consulted past regulations and added ornamentation in measured degree.

entries.zh: 原定皇帝儀衛有大駕鹵簿、行駕儀仗、行幸儀仗之別，乾隆十三年，復就原定器數增改釐訂，遂更大駕鹵簿為法駕鹵簿，行駕儀仗為鑾駕鹵簿，行幸儀仗為騎駕鹵簿。
entries.en: Under the original regulations the emperor's ceremonial guard was divided into the Grand Imperial halberd guard, traveling imperial regalia, and regalia for imperial progresses. In the thirteenth year of Qianlong the court again revised the originally fixed inventories of equipment and renamed them: the Grand Imperial halberd guard became the Statutory Imperial halberd guard, traveling imperial regalia became the Imperial Palanquin halberd guard, and regalia for imperial progresses became the Mounted Imperial halberd guard.
entries.literal: The original regulations for the emperor's ceremonial guard distinguished the Grand Imperial halberd guard, the traveling imperial regalia, and the regalia for imperial progresses. In the thirteenth year of Qianlong, the originally fixed numbers of implements were again increased, revised, and ordered; thereupon the Grand Imperial halberd guard was renamed the Statutory Imperial halberd guard, the traveling imperial regalia became the Imperial Palanquin halberd guard, and the regalia for imperial progresses became the Mounted Imperial halberd guard.

entries.zh: 三者合，則為大駕鹵簿。
entries.en: Combined, the three constituted the Grand Imperial halberd guard.
entries.literal: When the three were combined, they formed the Grand Imperial halberd guard.

entries.zh: 而凡皇后儀駕、妃嬪儀仗采仗以及親王以下儀衛，均視原定加詳。
entries.en: The empress's ceremonial escort, the ceremonial regalia and colored staffs of consorts, and the ceremonial guards of princes and below were all elaborated beyond the original regulations.
entries.literal: As for the empress's ceremonial escort, the ceremonial regalia and colored staffs of consorts, and the ceremonial guards of princes and below, all were made more detailed than the original regulations.

entries.zh: 茲依乾隆朝所定者標目，而以原定器數及崇德初年所定者附見於後。
entries.en: The headings below follow the Qianlong regulations, with the originally fixed inventories and the early Chongde provisions appended afterward.
entries.literal: Here the headings follow what was fixed in the Qianlong reign, while the originally fixed numbers of implements and what was fixed in the early Chongde years are appended afterward.

entries.zh: 又太上皇鹵簿、皇太子儀衛，皆一時之制，非同常設，亦並著於篇。
entries.en: The retired emperor's halberd guard and the crown prince's ceremonial guard were likewise included, though both were temporary arrangements rather than standing institutions.
entries.literal: Moreover, the retired emperor's halberd guard and the crown prince's ceremonial guard were both temporary institutions, not regularly established, and are also recorded in this chapter.

entries.zh: 庶考因革者，得以沿流溯源，詳稽一代之制焉。
entries.en: Readers tracing institutional change may thus follow the stream to its source and examine in detail how the dynasty's ceremonial system took shape.
entries.literal: Thus those who examine change and continuity may follow the current downstream to its source and scrutinize in detail the regulations of the dynasty.

entries.zh: 皇帝大駕鹵簿，圜丘、祈穀、常雩三大祀用之。
entries.en: The Emperor's Grand Imperial halberd guard was employed for the three great sacrifices at the Circular Mound, for prayer for grain, and for the regular rain sacrifice.
entries.literal: The emperor's Grand Imperial halberd guard was used for the three great sacrifices at the Circular Mound, for prayer for grain, and for the regular rain sacrifice.

entries.zh: 大閱時詣行宮，禮成還宮，亦用之。
entries.en: It was also used when the emperor went to the traveling palace for a grand military review and when he returned to the palace after the rites were concluded.
entries.literal: When proceeding to the traveling palace during a grand review, and when returning to the palace after the rites were completed, it was also used.

entries.zh: 其制，前列導象四，次寶象五，次靜鞭四。
entries.en: Its order of march placed four guide elephants in the van, followed by five treasure elephants and four silent whips.
entries.literal: Its arrangement: first came four guide elephants; next five treasure elephants; next four silent whips.

entries.zh: 次前部大樂，其器大銅角四，小銅角四，金口角四。
entries.en: Next came the front-section grand music, with four large bronze horns, four small bronze horns, and four gilt bronze mouth-horns.
entries.literal: Next came the front-section grand music, its instruments being four large bronze horns, four small bronze horns, and four gilt bronze mouth-horns.

entries.zh: 次革輅駕馬四，木輅駕馬六，象輅駕馬八，金輅駕象一，玉輅駕象一。
entries.en: Next came the five ceremonial chariots: the leather chariot with four horses, the wooden chariot with six, the elephant chariot with eight, the gold chariot with one elephant, and the jade chariot with one elephant.
entries.literal: Next the leather chariot drawn by four horses, the wooden chariot drawn by six horses, the elephant chariot drawn by eight horses, the gold chariot drawn by one elephant, and the jade chariot drawn by one elephant.

entries.zh: 次鐃歌樂，鐃歌鼓吹與行幸樂並設，名鐃歌樂。
entries.en: Next came naoge music—the naoge drum-and-blow ensemble and progress music were deployed together under that single name.
entries.literal: Next the naoge music; naoge drum-and-blow music and progress music were both set out together and called naoge music.

entries.zh: 其器金二，銅鼓四，銅鈸二，扁鼓二，銅點二，龍篴二，平篴二，雲鑼二，管二，笙二，金口角八，大銅角十六，小銅角十六，蒙古角二，金鉦四，畫角二十四，龍鼓二十四，龍篴十二，拍板四，仗鼓四，金四，龍鼓二十四，間以紅鐙六。
entries.en: Its instruments comprised two gongs, four bronze drums, two bronze cymbals, two flat drums, two bronze clappers, two dragon flutes, two level flutes, two cloud gongs, two pipes, two sheng, eight gilt bronze mouth-horns, sixteen large and sixteen small bronze horns, two Mongol horns, four gilt cymbals, twenty-four painted horns, twenty-four dragon drums, twelve dragon flutes, four clappers, four guard drums, four additional gongs, another twenty-four dragon drums, and six red lanterns interspersed among them.
entries.literal: Its instruments: two gongs; four bronze drums; two bronze cymbals; two flat drums; two bronze clappers; two dragon flutes; two level flutes; two cloud gongs; two pipes; two sheng; eight gilt bronze mouth-horns; sixteen large bronze horns; sixteen small bronze horns; two Mongol horns; four gilt cymbals; twenty-four painted horns; twenty-four dragon drums; twelve dragon flutes; four clappers; four guard drums; four gongs; twenty-four dragon drums, interspersed with six red lanterns.

entries.zh: 次引仗六，御仗十六，吾仗十六，立瓜、臥瓜各十六，星、鉞各十六，出警、入蹕旗各一，五色金龍小旗四十，次翠華旗二，金鼓旗二，門旗八，日、月旗各一，五雲旗五，五雷旗五，八風旗八，甘雨旗四，列宿旗二十八，五星旗五，五嶽旗五，四瀆旗四，神武、硃雀、青龍、白虎旗各一，天馬、天鹿、辟邪、犀牛、赤熊、黃羆、白澤、角端、游麟、彩獅、振鷺、鳴鳶、赤烏、華蟲、黃鵠、白雉、雲鶴、孔雀、儀鳳、翔鸞旗各一。
entries.en: Next came six guide staffs, sixteen imperial staffs, sixteen wu staffs, sixteen standing-melon and sixteen reclining-melon emblems, sixteen star-maces and sixteen battle-axes, one exit-guard flag and one enter-forbidden-zone flag, and forty small five-colored golden-dragon flags; then two emerald-splendor flags, two golden-drum flags, eight gate flags, the sun and moon flags, five-cloud flags, five-thunder flags, eight-wind flags, four sweet-rain flags, twenty-eight constellation flags, five planetary flags, five sacred-mountain flags, four great-river flags, the Divine Martial, Vermilion Bird, Azure Dragon, and White Tiger flags, and one each of the heavenly horse, heavenly deer, ward-off-evil, rhinoceros, red bear, yellow bear, white marsh-beast, horned tip, roaming qilin, colored lion, vibrating egret, crying kite, red crow, patterned insect, yellow swan-goose, white pheasant, cloud crane, peacock, ceremonial phoenix, and soaring luan flags.
entries.literal: Next six guide staffs, sixteen imperial staffs, sixteen wu staffs, sixteen standing-melon and sixteen reclining-melon [weapons], sixteen star-emblems and sixteen battle-axes, one each of the exit-guard and enter-forbidden-zone flags, forty small five-colored golden-dragon flags; next two emerald-splendor flags, two golden-drum flags, eight gate flags, one each of sun and moon flags, five five-cloud flags, five five-thunder flags, eight eight-wind flags, four sweet-rain flags, twenty-eight lodge flags, five five-star flags, five five-mountain flags, four four-river flags, one each of the Divine Martial, Vermilion Bird, Azure Dragon, and White Tiger flags, and one each of the heavenly horse, heavenly deer, ward-off-evil, rhinoceros, red bear, yellow bear, white marsh-beast, horned tip, roaming qilin, colored lion, vibrating egret, crying kite, red crow, patterned insect, yellow swan-goose, white pheasant, cloud crane, peacock, ceremonial phoenix, and soaring luan flags.

entries.zh: 五色龍纛四十，前鋒纛八，護軍纛八，驍騎纛二十四。
entries.en: Forty five-colored dragon banners followed, with eight vanguard banners, eight guard-army banners, and twenty-four bold-cavalry banners.
entries.literal: Forty five-colored dragon banners, eight vanguard banners, eight guard-army banners, and twenty-four bold-cavalry banners.

entries.zh: 次黃麾四，儀鍠氅四，金節四，進善納言、敷文振武、褒功懷遠、行慶施惠、明刑弼教、教孝表節旌各二。
entries.en: Next came four yellow command banners, four ceremonial gong-canopies, four golden staffs of office, and two each of the banners bearing the slogans for receiving good counsel, spreading culture and invigorating arms, praising merit and cherishing the distant, bestowing celebration and extending grace, clarifying punishments and assisting instruction, and teaching filial piety and displaying integrity.
entries.literal: Next four yellow command banners, four ceremonial gong-canopies, four golden staffs of office, and two each of the banners for receiving good counsel, spreading culture and invigorating arms, praising merit and cherishing the distant, bestowing celebration and extending grace, clarifying punishments and assisting instruction, and teaching filial piety and displaying integrity.

entries.zh: 龍頭幡四，豹尾幡四，絳引幡四，信幡四。
entries.en: Four dragon-head banners, four leopard-tail banners, four crimson guide banners, and four trust banners followed.
entries.literal: Four dragon-head banners, four leopard-tail banners, four crimson guide banners, and four trust banners.

entries.zh: 羽葆幢四，霓幢四，紫幢四，長壽幢四。
entries.en: Four feather-canopy banners, four rainbow banners, four purple banners, and four longevity banners came next.
entries.literal: Four feather-canopy banners, four rainbow banners, four purple banners, and four longevity banners.

entries.zh: 次鸞鳳赤方扇八，雉尾扇八，孔雀扇八，單龍赤團扇八，單龍黃團扇八，雙龍赤團扇八，雙龍黃團扇八，赤滿單龍團扇六，黃滿雙龍團扇六，壽字黃扇八。
entries.en: Next came eight square luan-phoenix red fans, eight pheasant-tail fans, eight peacock fans, eight single-dragon red round fans, eight single-dragon yellow round fans, eight double-dragon red round fans, eight double-dragon yellow round fans, six red full single-dragon round fans, six yellow full double-dragon round fans, and eight yellow fans emblazoned with the character for longevity.
entries.literal: Next eight square luan-phoenix red fans, eight pheasant-tail fans, eight peacock fans, eight single-dragon red round fans, eight single-dragon yellow round fans, eight double-dragon red round fans, eight double-dragon yellow round fans, six red full single-dragon round fans, six yellow full double-dragon round fans, and eight yellow fans bearing the character for longevity.

entries.zh: 次赤素方傘四，紫素方傘四，五色花傘十，五色妝緞傘十，間以五色九龍團傘十。
entries.en: Next came four plain red square umbrellas, four plain purple square umbrellas, ten five-colored floral umbrellas, ten five-colored figured-satin umbrellas, and ten five-colored nine-dragon round umbrellas interspersed among them.
entries.literal: Next four plain red square umbrellas, four plain purple square umbrellas, ten five-colored floral umbrellas, ten five-colored figured-satin umbrellas, interspersed with ten five-colored nine-dragon round umbrellas.

entries.zh: 次九龍黃蓋二十，紫芝蓋二，翠華蓋二，九龍曲柄黃蓋四。
entries.en: Next came twenty yellow nine-dragon canopies, two purple lingzhi canopies, two emerald-splendor canopies, and four curved-handle yellow nine-dragon canopies.
entries.literal: Next twenty yellow nine-dragon canopies, two purple lingzhi canopies, two emerald-splendor canopies, and four curved-handle yellow nine-dragon canopies.

entries.zh: 次戟四，殳四，豹尾槍三十，弓矢三十，儀刀三十。
entries.en: Next came four halberds, four ceremonial staffs, thirty leopard-tail spears, thirty bows and arrows, and thirty ceremonial swords.
entries.literal: Next four halberds, four shu [ceremonial staffs], thirty leopard-tail spears, thirty bows and arrows, and thirty ceremonial swords.

entries.zh: 次仗馬十。
entries.en: Next came ten ceremonial horses.
entries.literal: Next ten ceremonial horses.

entries.zh: 次金方几一，金交椅一，金瓶二，金盥盤一，金盂一，金盒二，金爐二，拂二。
entries.en: Next came one square golden table, one golden armchair, two golden vases, one golden wash-basin, one golden bowl, two golden boxes, two golden censers, and two fly-whisks.
entries.literal: Next one square golden table, one golden armchair, two golden vases, one golden wash-basin, one golden bowl, two golden boxes, two golden censers, and two fly-whisks.

entries.zh: 次九龍曲柄黃蓋一。
entries.en: Next came one curved-handle yellow nine-dragon canopy.
entries.literal: Next one curved-handle yellow nine-dragon canopy.

entries.zh: 前引佩刀大臣十人，提爐二，玉輦在中。
entries.en: Ten sword-bearing ministers led in front, two attendants carried censers, and the jade imperial carriage rode at the center.
entries.literal: Ten sword-bearing ministers led in front, two incense-bearers, and the jade imperial carriage in the center.

entries.zh: 後扈佩刀大臣二人，豹尾班執槍佩儀刀侍衛各十人，佩弓矢侍衛二十人，領侍衛內大臣一人，侍衛班領二人。
entries.en: Two sword-bearing ministers brought up the rear; the leopard-tail company comprised ten guards with spears and ten with ceremonial swords, while twenty guards bore bows and arrows; a chief grand guard of the inner service and two guard company leaders completed the escort.
entries.literal: Two sword-bearing ministers guarded the rear; the leopard-tail company had ten guards each bearing spears and ceremonial swords, and twenty guards bearing bows and arrows; one chief grand guard of the inner service, and two guard company leaders.

entries.zh: 後管宗人府王、公二人，散秩大臣一人，前鋒護軍統領一人，給事中、御史二人，各部郎中、員外郎四人，侍衛班領一人，署侍衛班領一人，侍衛什長二人。
entries.en: Behind them followed two princes and dukes from the Imperial Clan Court, a minister without regular portfolio, the commander of vanguard and guard armies, two supervising secretaries and censors, four department directors and vice directors, a guard company leader, an acting guard company leader, and two guard squad chiefs.
entries.literal: Following them were two princes and dukes from the Imperial Clan Court, one minister without regular portfolio, one commander of vanguard and guard armies, two supervising secretaries and censors, four department directors and vice directors, one guard company leader, one acting guard company leader, and two guard squad chiefs.

entries.zh: 次黃龍大纛二，領侍衛內大臣一人，司纛侍衛什長二人，建纛親軍四人，鳴佩螺親軍六人。
entries.en: The procession closed with two great yellow-dragon banners, attended by a chief grand guard of the inner service, two guard squad chiefs in charge of banners, four personal guards who raised the banners, and six personal guards who sounded conch shells.
entries.literal: Next two great yellow-dragon banners; one chief grand guard of the inner service, two guard squad chiefs in charge of banners, four personal guards who raised the banners, and six personal guards who sounded conch shells.

entries.zh: 太宗崇德元年，備大駕鹵簿，玉璽四顆。
entries.en: In Taizong's first Chongde year the court prepared the Grand Imperial halberd guard, including four jade seals.
entries.literal: In the first year of Chongde under Taizong, the Grand Imperial halberd guard was prepared, with four jade seals.

entries.zh: 黃傘五，團扇二。
entries.en: There were five yellow umbrellas and two round fans.
entries.literal: Five yellow umbrellas and two round fans.

entries.zh: 纛十，旗十。
entries.en: Ten great banners and ten flags were provided.
entries.literal: Ten great banners and ten flags.

entries.zh: 大刀六，戟六。
entries.en: Six great swords and six halberds were included.
entries.literal: Six great swords and six halberds.

entries.zh: 立瓜、臥瓜、骨朵各二，吾仗六。
entries.en: Two each of standing-melon, reclining-melon, and mace emblems, plus six wu staffs.
entries.literal: Two each of standing-melon, reclining-melon, and mace; six wu staffs.

entries.zh: 馬十。
entries.en: Ten ceremonial horses were provided.
entries.literal: Ten horses.

entries.zh: 金椅、金杌、香盒、香爐、金水盆、金唾壺、金瓶、樂器全設。
entries.en: A golden chair, golden stool, incense box, incense burner, golden water basin, golden spittoon, golden vase, and the full complement of musical instruments were all provided.
entries.literal: Golden chair, golden stool, incense box, incense burner, golden water basin, golden spittoon, golden vase, and the full set of musical instruments were all provided.

entries.zh: 嗣復定儀仗數目，用金漆椅一，金漆杌一，蠅拂四，金唾盂一，金壺一，金瓶、金盆各一，香爐、香盒各二。
entries.en: The court later revised the inventory again: one gilt chair, one gilt stool, four fly-whisks, one golden spittoon-bowl, one golden ewer, one golden vase, one golden basin, and two each of incense burners and incense boxes.
entries.literal: Later the numbers of ceremonial regalia were again fixed: one gilt chair, one gilt stool, four fly-whisks, one golden spittoon-bowl, one golden ewer, one golden vase and one golden basin each, and two incense burners and two incense boxes each.

entries.zh: 曲柄傘一，直柄傘四，扇二，節四。
entries.en: One curved-handle umbrella, four straight-handle umbrellas, two fans, and four staffs of office were specified.
entries.literal: One curved-handle umbrella, four straight-handle umbrellas, two fans, and four staffs of office.

entries.zh: 骨朵二，立瓜、臥瓜各二，吾仗六，紅仗四。
entries.en: Two maces, two each of standing-melon and reclining-melon emblems, six wu staffs, and four red staffs were added.
entries.literal: Two maces, two each of standing-melon and reclining-melon, six wu staffs, and four red staffs.

entries.zh: 鑼二，鼓二，畫角四，簫二，笙二，架鼓四，橫笛二，龍頭橫笛二，檀板二，小銅鈸四，小銅鑼二，大銅鑼四，雲鑼二，鎖吶四。
entries.en: Musical equipment comprised two gongs, two drums, four painted horns, two xiao, two sheng, four frame drums, two transverse flutes, two dragon-head transverse flutes, two clapper boards, four small bronze cymbals, two small bronze gongs, four large bronze gongs, two cloud gongs, and four suona.
entries.literal: Two gongs, two drums, four painted horns, two xiao, two sheng, four frame drums, two transverse flutes, two dragon-head transverse flutes, two clapper boards, four small bronze cymbals, two small bronze gongs, four large bronze gongs, two cloud gongs, and four suona.

entries.zh: 世祖入關，一仍舊制。
entries.en: When the Shizu emperor entered the passes, the court kept the old system unchanged.
entries.literal: When the Shizu emperor entered the passes, the old system was retained unchanged.

entries.zh: 迨順治三年以後，更定皇帝鹵簿，有大駕鹵簿、行駕儀仗、行幸儀仗之別。
entries.en: From the third year of Shunzhi onward the emperor's halberd guard was reorganized into the Grand Imperial halberd guard, traveling imperial regalia, and regalia for imperial progresses.
entries.literal: From the third year of Shunzhi onward, the emperor's halberd guard was revised, with distinctions among the Grand Imperial halberd guard, traveling imperial regalia, and regalia for imperial progresses.

entries.zh: 大駕鹵簿之制，曲柄九，龍傘四，直柄九龍傘十六，直柄瑞草傘六，直柄花傘六，方傘八。
entries.en: Under the Grand Imperial halberd guard there were nine curved-handle canopies, four dragon umbrellas, sixteen straight-handle nine-dragon umbrellas, six straight-handle auspicious-grass umbrellas, six straight-handle floral umbrellas, and eight square umbrellas.
entries.literal: The regulations for the Grand Imperial halberd guard: nine curved-handle [canopies], four dragon umbrellas, sixteen straight-handle nine-dragon umbrellas, six straight-handle auspicious-grass umbrellas, six straight-handle floral umbrellas, and eight square umbrellas.

entries.zh: 大刀二十，弓矢二十，豹尾槍二十，龍頭方天戟四。
entries.en: Twenty great swords, twenty bows and arrows, twenty leopard-tail spears, and four dragon-head square-heaven halberds were specified.
entries.literal: Twenty great swords, twenty bows and arrows, twenty leopard-tail spears, and four dragon-head square-heaven halberds.

entries.zh: 黃麾二，絳引幡四，信幡、傳教幡、告止幡、政平訟理幡各四，儀鍠氅八，羽葆幢四，青龍、白虎、硃雀、神武幢各一，豹尾幡、龍頭竿幡各四。
entries.en: Two yellow command banners, four crimson guide banners, four each of the trust, teaching, stop-proclamation, and government-in-order banners, eight ceremonial gong-canopies, four feather-canopy banners, the Azure Dragon, White Tiger, Vermilion Bird, and Divine Martial banners, and four each of leopard-tail and dragon-pole banners were included.
entries.literal: Two yellow command banners, four crimson guide banners, four each of trust, teaching, stop-proclamation, and government-in-order banners, eight ceremonial gong-canopies, four feather-canopy banners, one each of Azure Dragon, White Tiger, Vermilion Bird, and Divine Martial banners, and four each of leopard-tail and dragon-pole banners.

entries.zh: 金節四。
entries.en: Four golden staffs of office were provided.
entries.literal: Four golden staffs of office.

entries.zh: 銷金龍纛、銷金龍小旗各二十。
entries.en: Twenty gilded-dragon great banners and twenty gilded-dragon small flags were specified.
entries.literal: Twenty gilded-dragon great banners and twenty gilded-dragon small flags.

entries.zh: 金鉞六。
entries.en: Six golden battle-axes were included.
entries.literal: Six golden battle-axes.

entries.zh: 馬十。
entries.en: Ten ceremonial horses were provided.
entries.literal: Ten horses.

entries.zh: 鸞鳳扇八，單龍扇十二，雙龍扇二十。
entries.en: Eight luan-phoenix fans, twelve single-dragon fans, and twenty double-dragon fans were specified.
entries.literal: Eight luan-phoenix fans, twelve single-dragon fans, and twenty double-dragon fans.

entries.zh: 拂子二，紅鐙六，金香爐、金瓶、金香盒各二，金唾壺、金盆、金杌、金交椅、金腳踏各一。
entries.en: Two fly-whisks, six red lanterns, two each of golden incense burners, vases, and incense boxes, and one each of golden spittoon, basin, stool, armchair, and footrest were provided.
entries.literal: Two fly-whisks, six red lanterns, two each of golden incense burners, golden vases, and golden incense boxes, and one each of golden spittoon, golden basin, golden stool, golden armchair, and golden footrest.

entries.zh: 御仗六，星六。
entries.en: Six imperial staffs and six star-emblems were included.
entries.literal: Six imperial staffs and six star-emblems.

entries.zh: 篦頭八。
entries.en: Eight comb-head emblems were specified.
entries.literal: Eight comb-heads.

entries.zh: 棕薦三十。
entries.en: Thirty palm-fiber mats were provided.
entries.literal: Thirty palm-fiber mats.

entries.zh: 靜鞭三十。
entries.en: Thirty silent whips were included.
entries.literal: Thirty silent whips.

entries.zh: 品級山七十二。
entries.en: Seventy-two rank-indicator screens were deployed.
entries.literal: Seventy-two rank-indicator screens.

entries.zh: 肅靜旗、金鼓旗、白澤旗各二，門旗八，日、月、風、雲、雷、雨旗各一，五緯旗五，二十八宿旗各一，北斗旗一，五嶽旗五，四瀆旗四，青龍、白虎、硃雀、神武、天鹿、天馬、鸞麟、熊羆旗各一。
entries.en: Two each of the silence, golden-drum, and white marsh-beast flags were set out, with eight gate flags, the sun, moon, wind, cloud, thunder, and rain flags, five planetary flags, the twenty-eight constellation flags, one Big Dipper flag, five sacred-mountain flags, four great-river flags, and the Azure Dragon, White Tiger, Vermilion Bird, Divine Martial, heavenly deer, heavenly horse, luan-qilin, and bear flags.
entries.literal: Two each of the silence, golden-drum, and white marsh-beast flags; eight gate flags; one each of sun, moon, wind, cloud, thunder, and rain flags; five five-planet flags; one each of the twenty-eight lodge flags; one Big Dipper flag; five five-mountain flags; four four-river flags; and one each of the Azure Dragon, White Tiger, Vermilion Bird, Divine Martial, heavenly deer, heavenly horse, luan-qilin, and bear flags.

entries.zh: 立瓜、臥瓜、吾仗各六。
entries.en: Six each of standing-melon, reclining-melon, and wu staffs were provided.
entries.literal: Six each of standing-melon, reclining-melon, and wu staffs.

entries.zh: 畫角二十四，鼓四十八，大銅號、小銅號各八，金、金鉦、仗鼓各四，龍頭笛十二，板四串。
entries.en: Musical equipment comprised twenty-four painted horns, forty-eight drums, eight large and eight small bronze horns, four each of gongs, gilt cymbals, and guard drums, twelve dragon-head flutes, and four strings of clappers.
entries.literal: Twenty-four painted horns, forty-eight drums, eight each of large and small bronze horns, four each of gongs, gilt cymbals, and guard drums, twelve dragon-head flutes, and four strings of clappers.

entries.zh: 凡郊祀大典，萬壽、元旦、冬至三大朝會及諸典禮皆用之。
entries.en: It was employed for suburban sacrifice grand ceremonies, the three great court assemblies of Longevity, New Year's Day, and Winter Solstice, and all other state rituals.
entries.literal: It was used for all suburban sacrifice grand ceremonies, the three great court assemblies of Longevity, New Year's Day, and Winter Solstice, and all other ritual occasions.

entries.zh: 太上皇鹵簿，原定無之。
entries.en: The original regulations made no provision for a retired emperor's halberd guard.
entries.literal: The retired emperor's halberd guard was not provided for in the original regulations.

entries.zh: 嘉慶元年，因授璽禮成，陳太上皇鹵簿於寧壽宮。
entries.en: In the first year of Jiaqing, after the seal-bestowal rite was completed, the retired emperor's halberd guard was arrayed at the Palace of Tranquil Longevity.
entries.literal: In the first year of Jiaqing, because the seal-bestowal rite was completed, the retired emperor's halberd guard was arrayed at the Palace of Tranquil Longevity.

entries.zh: 其制，引仗六，御仗十六，吾仗十六，立瓜、臥瓜各十六，星、鉞各十六，旗、纛二百二十四，麾、氅、節各四，旌十六，幡十二，幢二十，扇八十六，傘六十六，戟殳各四，豹尾槍、弓矢、儀刀各三十，金交椅、金馬杌各一，拂二，金器八，銀水、火壺各一，雨傘二，盤線鐙二，紅鐙六。
entries.en: The array comprised six guide staffs, sixteen imperial staffs, sixteen wu staffs, sixteen each of standing-melon and reclining-melon emblems, star-maces, and battle-axes, two hundred twenty-four flags and banners, four each of command banners, gong-canopies, and staffs of office, sixteen pennants, twelve streamers, twenty banner-poles, eighty-six fans, sixty-six umbrellas, four halberds and four ceremonial staffs, thirty leopard-tail spears, thirty bows and arrows, thirty ceremonial swords, a golden armchair and golden horse-stool, two fly-whisks, eight golden vessels, silver water and fire ewers, two rain umbrellas, two coiled-line lanterns, and six red lanterns.
entries.literal: Its arrangement: six guide staffs, sixteen imperial staffs, sixteen wu staffs, sixteen each of standing-melon and reclining-melon, sixteen each of star-emblems and battle-axes, two hundred twenty-four flags and banners, four each of command banners, gong-canopies, and staffs of office, sixteen pennants, twelve streamers, twenty banner-poles, eighty-six fans, sixty-six umbrellas, four each of halberds and shu, thirty each of leopard-tail spears, bows and arrows, and ceremonial swords, one each of golden armchair and golden horse-stool, two fly-whisks, eight golden vessels, one each of silver water and fire ewers, two rain umbrellas, two coiled-line lanterns, and six red lanterns.

entries.zh: 樂器備設，笙、管、雲鑼、平篴、鈸、點鼓各二，金及金鉦、銅鼓、扁鼓、仗鼓各四，架鼓、金口角各十二，龍篴十四，大銅角、小銅角、蒙古畫角各二十四，龍鼓四十八。
entries.en: A full musical establishment was provided: two each of sheng, pipes, cloud gongs, level flutes, cymbals, and clapper drums; four each of gongs, gilt cymbals, bronze drums, flat drums, and guard drums; twelve frame drums and twelve gilt bronze mouth-horns; fourteen dragon flutes; twenty-four large bronze horns, twenty-four small bronze horns, twenty-four Mongol painted horns; and forty-eight dragon drums.
entries.literal: Musical instruments were fully provided: two each of sheng, pipes, cloud gongs, level flutes, cymbals, and clapper drums; four each of gongs, gilt cymbals, bronze drums, flat drums, and guard drums; twelve each of frame drums and gilt bronze mouth-horns; fourteen dragon flutes; twenty-four each of large bronze horns, small bronze horns, and Mongol painted horns; and forty-eight dragon drums.

entries.zh: 皇太子儀衛，清自康熙五十二年後不復建儲，故國初雖有皇太子儀仗，幾同虛設。
entries.en: The crown prince's ceremonial guard: after the fifty-second year of Kangxi the Qing ceased naming heirs apparent, so although crown prince ceremonial regalia existed from the dynasty's founding, it was nearly never used.
entries.literal: The crown prince's ceremonial guard: from the fifty-second year of Kangxi the Qing no longer established an heir apparent, so although there was crown prince ceremonial regalia at the founding of the dynasty, it was nearly a dead letter.

entries.zh: 乾隆六十年，以明年將行內禪，九月，議定皇太子出入內朝，用導從侍衛四人，乾清門侍衛二人。
entries.en: In the sixtieth year of Qianlong, with an inner abdication planned for the following year, the court decided in the ninth month that when the crown prince entered and left the inner court he would be attended by four guiding guards and two Gate of Pure Brightness guards.
entries.literal: In the sixtieth year of Qianlong, because an inner abdication was to take place the following year, in the ninth month it was decided that when the crown prince entered and left the inner court he would have four guiding guards and two Gate of Pure Brightness guards.

entries.zh: 如出外朝及城市內外，隨從散秩大臣一人，侍衛十人，領侍衛內大臣一人，乾清門侍衛四人。
entries.en: When he went to the outer court or traveled within or beyond the city, he was accompanied by a minister without regular portfolio, ten guards, a chief grand guard of the inner service, and four Gate of Pure Brightness guards.
entries.literal: If he went to the outer court or within and without the city, he was accompanied by one minister without regular portfolio, ten guards, one chief grand guard of the inner service, and four Gate of Pure Brightness guards.

entries.zh: 前設虎槍六，後設豹尾槍八。
entries.en: Six tiger spears preceded him and eight leopard-tail spears followed.
entries.literal: Six tiger spears were set in front and eight leopard-tail spears behind.

entries.zh: 是年復諭禮臣，以冊立皇太子典禮既不舉行，其一切儀仗製造需時，亦毋庸另行備辦。
entries.en: That same year the emperor instructed the ritual officials that since the ceremony for investing the crown prince would not be held, there was no need to prepare the full ceremonial regalia, whose manufacture would take considerable time.
entries.literal: That year the emperor again instructed the ritual officials that since the ceremony for investing the crown prince would not be held, there was no need to prepare separately all ceremonial regalia, whose manufacture required time.

entries.zh: 原定皇太子儀仗，曲柄九龍傘三，直柄龍傘四，直柄瑞草傘二，方傘四，雙龍扇四，孔雀扇四。
entries.en: The original crown prince ceremonial regalia comprised three curved-handle nine-dragon umbrellas, four straight-handle dragon umbrellas, two straight-handle auspicious-grass umbrellas, four square umbrellas, four double-dragon fans, and four peacock fans.
entries.literal: Under the original crown prince ceremonial regalia: three curved-handle nine-dragon umbrellas, four straight-handle dragon umbrellas, two straight-handle auspicious-grass umbrellas, four square umbrellas, four double-dragon fans, and four peacock fans.

entries.zh: 白澤旗二。
entries.en: Two white marsh-beast flags were included.
entries.literal: Two white marsh-beast flags.

entries.zh: 金節二。
entries.en: Two golden staffs of office were provided.
entries.literal: Two golden staffs of office.

entries.zh: 羽葆幢二，傳教幡、告止幡、信幡、絳引幡各二，儀鍠氅二。
entries.en: Two feather-canopy banners, two each of the teaching, stop-proclamation, trust, and crimson guide banners, and two ceremonial gong-canopies were specified.
entries.literal: Two feather-canopy banners, two each of teaching, stop-proclamation, trust, and crimson guide banners, and two ceremonial gong-canopies.

entries.zh: 銷金龍纛十，銷金龍小旗十。
entries.en: Ten gilded dragon great banners and ten gilded dragon small flags were provided.
entries.literal: Ten gilded dragon great banners and ten gilded dragon small flags.

entries.zh: 豹尾槍十，弓矢十，大刀十，馬八，金鉞四，立瓜、臥瓜、骨朵、吾仗各四。
entries.en: Ten leopard-tail spears, ten bows and arrows, ten great swords, eight horses, four golden battle-axes, and four each of standing-melon, reclining-melon, mace, and wu staffs were included.
entries.literal: Ten leopard-tail spears, ten bows and arrows, ten great swords, eight horses, four golden battle-axes, and four each of standing-melon, reclining-melon, mace, and wu staffs.

entries.zh: 拂二。
entries.en: Two fly-whisks were provided.
entries.literal: Two fly-whisks.

entries.zh: 畫角十二，花匡鼓二十四，大銅號八，小銅號二，金、金鉦、仗鼓各二，龍頭篴二，板二。
entries.en: Musical equipment comprised twelve painted horns, twenty-four floral frame drums, eight large and two small bronze horns, two each of gongs, gilt cymbals, and guard drums, two dragon-head flutes, and two clappers.
entries.literal: Twelve painted horns, twenty-four floral frame drums, eight large bronze horns, two small bronze horns, two each of gongs, gilt cymbals, and guard drums, two dragon-head flutes, and two clappers.

entries.zh: 金香爐、金瓶、金香盒各二，金唾壺，金盆各一，金杌一，金交椅一，金腳踏一。
entries.en: Two each of golden incense burners, vases, and incense boxes, one golden spittoon and one golden basin, and a golden stool, armchair, and footrest were provided.
entries.literal: Two each of golden incense burners, golden vases, and golden incense boxes; one each of golden spittoon and golden basin; one golden stool, one golden armchair, and one golden footrest.

entries.zh: 志八十
entries.en: Treatise 80
entries.literal: Treatise 80

entries.zh: 凡京察一等、大計卓異有定額，京官七而一，筆帖式八而一，道、府、廳、州、縣十五而一，佐雜、教官百三十而一，以是為率。
entries.en: Quotas governed first-grade capital ratings and outstanding grand-assessment nominations: one in seven for metropolitan officials, one in eight for clerks, one in fifteen for circuit and county-level officers, one in one hundred thirty for assistants and instructors.
entries.literal: First-grade capital inspection and outstanding grand-assessment nominations had fixed quotas: one in seven for capital officials, one in eight for clerks, one in fifteen for circuit, prefectural, subprefectural, department, and county officials, one in one hundred thirty for assistants, clerks, and instructors—such were the ratios.

entries.zh: 非歷俸滿者，未及年限者，革職留任或錢糧未完者，滿官不射布靶、不諳清語者，均不得膺上考。
entries.en: Officials who had not completed required tenure, those with incomplete fiscal accounts, those dismissed but retained in post, and Banner officers unable to pass archery or speak Manchu were all barred from top ratings.
entries.literal: Those who had not completed the full salary term, those not yet at the required tenure, those dismissed but retained or with grain and tax accounts unfinished, and Manchu officials who could not shoot the cloth target or did not know Manchu were all ineligible for top ratings.

entries.zh: 其大較也。
entries.en: Such were the general rules.
entries.literal: Such were the general provisions.

entries.zh: 順治八年，京察始著為令，以六年為期。
entries.en: In Shunzhi 8 (1651), the capital inspection was first codified on a six-year cycle.
entries.literal: In the eighth year of Shunzhi, the capital inspection was first established by statute, on a six-year cycle.

entries.zh: 十三年，吏部奏定則例，三品以上自陳，四品等官吏部、都察院察考議奏，親定去留。
entries.en: In Shunzhi 13 (1656), the Board codified rules: third-rank officials and above submitted self-assessments; fourth-rank and below were examined by the Board and Censorate, with the emperor deciding retention or removal.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year, the Board of Civil Appointments memorialized fixed regulations: third rank and above submitted self-assessments; fourth rank and below were inspected by the Board and the Censorate, deliberated, memorialized, and the emperor personally decided retention or removal.

entries.zh: 筆帖式照有職官例一體考察。
entries.en: Clerks were examined under the same rules as regular officials.
entries.literal: Clerks were examined together with regular officials according to the same rules.

entries.zh: 遇京察時，各官暫停升轉。
entries.en: During the capital inspection, promotions and transfers were suspended.
entries.literal: When the capital inspection occurred, all officials temporarily ceased promotion or transfer.

entries.zh: 尋復定考滿議敘例，三年考滿與六年察典並行。
entries.en: Soon rules for triennial review rewards were restored, running the three-year completion review alongside the six-year inspection.
entries.literal: Soon regulations for consideration upon completion of review were re-established; triennial completion of review and the six-year inspection were conducted in parallel.

entries.zh: 十七年，從左都御史魏裔介請，行糾拾之法，以補甄別所未及。
entries.en: In Shunzhi 17 (1660), at the request of Left Censor-in-Chief Wei Yijie, supplementary impeachment procedures were introduced to catch what regular screening missed.
entries.literal: In the seventeenth year, following the request of the Left Censor-in-Chief Wei Yijie, the method of supplementary impeachment was instituted to remedy what screening had missed.

entries.zh: 唐熙元年罷京察，專用三年考滿例。
entries.en: In Kangxi 1 (1662), the capital inspection was abolished in favor of the triennial completion review alone.
entries.literal: In the first year of Kangxi, the capital inspection was abolished and only the triennial completion review was used.

entries.zh: 三品以上仍自陳。
entries.en: Third-rank officials and above still submitted self-assessments.
entries.literal: Third rank and above still submitted self-assessments.

entries.zh: 餘官分五等：一等稱職者紀錄，二等稱職者賞賚，平常者留任，不及者降調，不稱職者革職。
entries.en: Other officials were graded in five tiers: top competent officials were recorded for promotion; second-tier competent ones received rewards; average ones kept their posts; substandard ones demoted; incompetent ones dismissed.
entries.literal: The remaining officials were divided into five grades: first-grade competent ones were recorded; second-grade competent ones received rewards; average ones were retained; those falling short were demoted or transferred; incompetent ones were dismissed.

entries.zh: 三年，御史季振宜請停考滿三疏，極言徇情鑽營，章奏繁擾，無裨勸懲。
entries.en: In Kangxi 3 (1664), Censor Ji Zhenyi submitted three memorials to abolish the completion review, arguing that favoritism and careerism dominated, paperwork overwhelmed the court, and the system failed to reward merit or punish failure.
entries.literal: In the third year, Censor Ji Zhenyi memorialized three times to halt the completion review, strongly arguing that favoritism and scheming prevailed, memorials were numerous and disruptive, and it did nothing to encourage or punish.

entries.zh: 因停考滿自陳例。
entries.en: Self-assessment upon completion of review was accordingly abolished.
entries.literal: Accordingly the practice of self-assessment upon completion of review was halted.

entries.zh: 六年，復行京察。
entries.en: In Kangxi 6 (1667), the capital inspection was restored.
entries.literal: In the sixth year, the capital inspection was restored.

entries.zh: 明年，甄別不及官三十七員。
entries.en: The following year, thirty-seven substandard officials were identified.
entries.literal: The following year, thirty-seven officials who failed screening were identified.

entries.zh: 嗣以各部、院甄別司員，類多末職，二十三年，嚴諭指名題參，復甄汰王三省等三十六人。
entries.en: Because ministries mostly culled junior staff, Kangxi 23 (1684) brought an edict demanding named impeachments of senior officials; thirty-six more, including Wang Sansheng, were removed.
entries.literal: Thereafter, as ministries and agencies screened their clerks, most culled were low-ranking posts; in the twenty-third year a stern edict ordered impeachment by name, and thirty-six more including Wang Sansheng were screened out.

entries.zh: 明年，京察又停。
entries.en: The capital inspection was suspended again the next year.
entries.literal: The following year, the capital inspection was again suspended.

entries.zh: 雍正元年復舉行，改為三年，自是為定制。
entries.en: It was revived in Yongzheng 1 (1723) on a three-year cycle, which thereafter became standard.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng it was revived, changed to a three-year cycle, and thereafter became the established rule.

entries.zh: 初，京察一等無定額，康熙三年，御史張沖翼疏請以部、院員數之多寡定一、二等名數，以息奔競，從之。
entries.en: Initially first-grade capital ratings had no quota; in Kangxi 3 (1664), Censor Zhang Chongyi proposed fixing first- and second-grade numbers by ministry size to curb favor-seeking, and the court agreed.
entries.literal: At first there was no fixed quota for first-grade capital inspection; in the third year of Kangxi, Censor Zhang Chongyi memorialized that first- and second-grade numbers should be set according to the size of each ministry and agency, to quell scrambling for favor, and this was approved.

entries.zh: 乾隆間，部、院保送一等，或浮濫溢舊額，詔停兼部行走，仍歸本衙門另班聲敘，暨到任未滿半年，仍由原衙門註考等例。
entries.en: Under Qianlong, first-grade nominations often exceeded quotas; edicts ended concurrent cross-ministry service, required separate ranking within home offices, and kept officials of less than six months' tenure under their original ministry's evaluation.
entries.literal: During the Qianlong reign, when ministries recommended first-grade nominees, nominations sometimes exceeded old quotas; an edict halted concurrent service in other ministries, required separate ranking within one's home office, and provided that those in post less than half a year were still evaluated by their original office.

entries.zh: 又罷未授職庶吉士保列一等之例，以示限制。
entries.en: Unassigned Hanlin bachelors were also barred from first-grade nomination as a further restriction.
entries.literal: The practice of recommending unassigned Hanlin bachelors for first grade was also abolished, to show restraint.

entries.zh: 四十二年，命部、院保送一等人數，毋庸過泥上屆成例，遞行裁減，以防溢額。
entries.en: In Qianlong 42 (1777), ministries were told not to match previous sessions' first-grade numbers but to reduce nominations progressively to prevent quota inflation.
entries.literal: In the forty-second year, ministries and agencies were ordered that first-grade nominations need not rigidly follow the previous session's precedent but should be progressively reduced to prevent exceeding quotas.

entries.zh: 應將上兩次數目比較，酌中定制。
entries.en: Quotas were to be set by comparing the last two sessions and striking a moderate balance.
entries.literal: The numbers of the last two sessions should be compared and a moderate standard fixed.

entries.zh: 既無慮濫膺保薦，亦不至屈抑人才。
entries.en: This would curb inflated nominations without unfairly suppressing able officials.
entries.literal: Thus there was no fear of reckless recommendation, nor of unjustly suppressing talent.

entries.zh: 五十年，定例保送一等人數，以不溢四十八年原額為準。
entries.en: In Qianlong 50 (1785), regulations capped first-grade nominations at the Qianlong 48 quota.
entries.literal: In the fiftieth year, it was fixed by regulation that first-grade nominations should not exceed the original quota of the forty-eighth year.

entries.zh: 後世踵行，間有增損，無甚懸殊也。
entries.en: Later reigns followed this practice with minor adjustments but no major change.
entries.literal: Later ages followed suit, with occasional increases or decreases, but no great divergence.

entries.zh: 向例部、院司官由吏部、都察院考覈，雍正四年，命內閣大學士同閱。
entries.en: Traditionally the Board and Censorate examined ministry staff; in Yongzheng 4 (1726), Grand Secretaries were ordered to review jointly.
entries.literal: By former practice, ministry and agency officials were examined by the Board of Civil Appointments and the Censorate; in the fourth year of Yongzheng, Grand Secretaries of the Grand Secretariat were ordered to review jointly.

entries.zh: 乾隆九年，帝慮部、院堂官有瞻徇情面濫列一等者，敕大學士驗看，慎重甄別，不稱一等者裁去。
entries.en: In Qianlong 9 (1744), fearing ministry chiefs favored protégés with first-grade ratings, the emperor ordered grand ministers to verify nominations and strike unworthy candidates.
entries.literal: In the ninth year of Qianlong, the emperor, fearing that ministry chiefs showed favoritism in listing first-grade nominees, ordered grand ministers to verify, scrutinize carefully, and strike those unworthy of first grade.

entries.zh: 十一年諭曰：「前命大學士分別去留，亦權宜辦理之道。
entries.en: In Qianlong 11 (1746) an edict stated: "Having grand ministers decide retention was only an expedient.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year an edict said: "The earlier order for grand ministers to decide retention or removal was also an expedient measure.

entries.zh: 察覈司員，惟堂官最為親切。
entries.en: Department chiefs know their staff best and are best placed to evaluate them.
entries.literal: In examining clerks, only the department chiefs are most intimate with them.

entries.zh: 要在平日留心體察，臨時舉措公平。
entries.en: They should observe staff daily and act fairly at inspection time.
entries.literal: What matters is daily attentive observation and fair action when the time comes.

entries.zh: 如上次定一等者，三年中行走平常，當改為二、三等。
entries.en: Officials rated first grade last time but merely average since should be downgraded to second or third grade.
entries.literal: If one rated first grade last time has performed only ordinarily in three years, he should be changed to second or third grade.

entries.zh: 上次原列二、三等者，三年中知所奮勉，即改為一等。
entries.en: Those previously in second or third grade who have improved should be promoted to first grade.
entries.literal: Those previously listed in second or third grade who in three years have shown exertion should be raised to first grade.

entries.zh: 庶察典肅而人知勸懲。」
entries.en: Only then would inspections be rigorous and officials know that merit and failure have consequences."
entries.literal: Thus the inspection would be rigorous and people would know encouragement and punishment."

entries.zh: 厥後考察權責，悉屬吏部，驗看特奉行故事而已。
entries.en: Thereafter examination authority reverted entirely to the Board, and grand-minister verification became a mere formality.
entries.literal: Thereafter examination authority rested entirely with the Board of Civil Appointments; verification became mere observance of precedent.

entries.zh: 大臣循例自陳求斥罷，候旨照舊供職，國初以來行之。
entries.en: Since the dynasty's founding, senior ministers had ritually submitted self-assessments requesting dismissal, then continued in office upon imperial leave.
entries.literal: Grand ministers routinely submitted self-assessments asking to be dismissed, awaited edict, and continued in office as before—practiced since the founding of the dynasty.

entries.zh: 乾隆八年，曾諭大臣自陳罷斥者舉賢自代。
entries.en: In Qianlong 8 (1743), ministers submitting self-dismissal assessments were ordered to recommend worthy successors.
entries.literal: In the eighth year of Qianlong, an edict once ordered ministers who submitted self-assessments asking dismissal to recommend worthy successors.

entries.zh: 嗣以所舉不得其人，或樹黨營私，行不久即罷。
entries.en: The practice was soon dropped because nominees proved unfit or factional, or recommenders were themselves soon dismissed.
entries.literal: Later, because those recommended were unfit, or formed factions for private gain, the practice was soon abandoned.

entries.zh: 十七年，帝以「內、外大臣親自簡擢，隨時黜陟，奚待三年？
entries.en: In Qianlong 17 (1752) the emperor declared: "I personally appoint and dismiss inner and outer ministers at will—why wait three years?
entries.literal: In the seventeenth year the emperor said: "Inner and outer grand ministers are personally selected and promoted, dismissed or advanced at any time—why wait three years?

entries.zh: 自陳繁文，相率為偽，甚無謂也」。
entries.en: These self-assessments are empty formalities, universally hypocritical and utterly pointless."
entries.literal: Self-assessment is verbose paperwork; all follow one another in hypocrisy—it is quite meaningless."

entries.zh: 詔罷其例。
entries.en: An edict abolished the practice.
entries.literal: An edict abolished the practice.

entries.zh: 先是京堂官無甄敘例，乾隆十五年，帝以三品以上堂官，具本自陳，部、院司員，皆令引見，而四、五品京堂不在自陳之列，亦無引見之例，吏部、都察院考語無實，龍鍾庸劣者得姑容，才具優長者無由見。
entries.en: Previously fourth- and fifth-rank metropolitan officials had no promotion review: third-rank and above submitted self-assessments and ministry staff were presented, but fourth- and fifth-rank officials were neither assessed nor presented; Board evaluations were perfunctory, mediocre officials were tolerated, and able ones had no chance to advance.
entries.literal: Previously metropolitan officials of ministerial rank had no evaluation-for-promotion precedent; in the fifteenth year of Qianlong the emperor noted that third-rank and above submitted memorial self-assessments, ministry clerks were all presented, but fourth- and fifth-rank metropolitan officials were neither in the self-assessment list nor presented; Board and Censorate evaluations lacked substance; doddering and mediocre men were tolerated while the talented had no avenue to be seen.

entries.zh: 特派王、大臣分別等第，奏聞引見。
entries.en: Princes and senior ministers were specially assigned to grade them, memorialize, and present them to the throne.
entries.literal: Princes and grand ministers were specially dispatched to grade them separately, memorialize, and present them.

entries.zh: 十八年，敕吏部開列三品京堂事實，親為裁奪。
entries.en: In Qianlong 18 (1753) the emperor ordered the Board to submit factual records on third-rank metropolitan officials for his personal decision.
entries.literal: In the eighteenth year the Board of Civil Appointments was ordered to list the facts on third-rank metropolitan officials for the emperor's personal decision.

entries.zh: 四十八年，以三品京堂不便派大臣驗看，令吏部帶額引見。
entries.en: In Qianlong 48 (1783), third-rank metropolitan officials were presented by the Board within quota rather than by assigned verifying ministers.
entries.literal: In the forty-eighth year, because it was inconvenient to assign ministers to verify third-rank metropolitan officials, the Board was ordered to present them within quota.

entries.zh: 嘉慶十二年，以三、四品京堂，向來京察但有降黜無甄敘，既與內、外大臣辦理兩歧，並不得與部、院司員同邀加級。
entries.en: In Jiaqing 12 (1807), because third- and fourth-rank metropolitan officials faced only demotion in the capital inspection, unlike other senior officials and ministry staff who could earn rank increments—
entries.literal: In the twelfth year of Jiaqing, because third- and fourth-rank metropolitan officials in the capital inspection had only demotion without evaluation for promotion—diverging from inner and outer grand ministers and unable to receive rank increments like ministry clerks—

entries.zh: 於是予太常少卿色克精額等議敘，而予陳鍾琛等休致。
entries.en: Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices Sekejing'e and others were granted promotion consideration, while Chen Zhongchen and others were retired.
entries.literal: accordingly Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices Sekejing'e and others were granted consideration for promotion, while Chen Zhongchen and others were retired.

entries.zh: 自後三品以下京堂始有甄敘之例矣。
entries.en: From then on, metropolitan officials below third rank could receive promotion consideration through the capital inspection.
entries.literal: From then on metropolitan officials below third rank first had the precedent of evaluation for promotion.

entries.zh: 乾隆二年，部議出兵效力人員，年老休致，令子弟一人入伍食糧，無子弟亦給守糧養贍。
entries.en: In Qianlong 2 (1737) the Board ruled that campaign veterans retiring on age could have one son enter the ranks for rations, or receive guard-ration support if they had no son.
entries.literal: In the second year of Qianlong the ministry deliberated that campaign veterans who retired on age should have one son enter the ranks for rations; if no son, guard-ration support was given.

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: The proposal was approved.
entries.literal: This was approved.

entries.zh: 時直省保題員弁，類以明白勤敏、才堪辦事列上選。
entries.en: Provincial nominations then typically cited clarity, diligence, and administrative competence for top selection.
entries.literal: At that time in the provinces, recommended officers were generally listed for top selection as clear, diligent, keen, and capable of handling affairs.

entries.zh: 十一年，諭嗣後保題，務重弓馬漢仗。
entries.en: In Qianlong 11 (1746) an edict required future nominations to emphasize archery, horsemanship, and weapons drill.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year an edict ordered that henceforth nominations must emphasize archery, horsemanship, and Chinese weapons.

entries.zh: 十五年，以各省所保總兵官鮮當意，諭曰：「年滿千總一項，類多猥瑣。
entries.en: In Qianlong 15 (1750), because nominated regional commanders rarely satisfied the emperor, an edict declared: "Battalion commanders completing tenure are mostly petty and trivial.
entries.literal: In the fifteenth year, because recommended regional commanders in the provinces rarely pleased the emperor, an edict said: "The category of battalion commanders completing tenure is mostly petty and trivial.

entries.zh: 國家擢用武職，營伍為正途，拔補將弁，必選之若輩。
entries.en: The state promotes military officers through the camps—the proper path—and must select generals and officers from among them.
entries.literal: The state promotes military officers; the camps are the proper path; selecting and filling generals and officers must choose from such men.

entries.zh: 緣次而升，皆自年滿千總始。
entries.en: Stepwise promotion all begins with battalion commanders completing tenure.
entries.literal: Promotion by steps all begins from battalion commanders completing tenure.

entries.zh: 折衝禦侮之用，豫籌於昇平無事之日，不可視為緩圖。」
entries.en: Defense against enemies must be prepared in peacetime and cannot be deferred."
entries.literal: The use of repelling enemies and defending insult must be prepared in days of peace and ease; it cannot be treated as a matter to defer."

entries.zh: 二十四年，以大臣自陳例既罷，敕兵部于軍政年，將在京都統、副都統，在外駐防將軍、都統、副都統，各省提督、總兵官，分別三本，條舉事實候鑒裁，以重考績。
entries.en: In Qianlong 24 (1759), with ministerial self-assessment abolished, the Board of War ordered capital and provincial commanders to submit three memorials listing facts during military inspection years, strengthening performance review.
entries.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, because the grand-minister self-assessment precedent had been abolished, the Board of War was ordered that in military inspection years, capital lieutenant-generals and deputy lieutenant-generals, garrison generals, commandants, and deputy commandants in the provinces, and provincial and regional commanders should each submit three memorials listing facts for imperial judgment, to strengthen performance evaluation.

entries.zh: 四十二年，定衛、所綠營武職薦舉卓異尚未升轉，再遇軍政列平等者，將上次卓異註銷。
entries.en: In Qianlong 42 (1777), Green Standard officers nominated as outstanding but not yet promoted had that nomination cancelled if rated average at the next military inspection.
entries.literal: In the forty-second year it was fixed that Green Standard military officials in guards and posts recommended as outstanding but not yet promoted, if at the next military inspection listed as average, had the previous outstanding nomination cancelled.

entries.zh: 嘉慶四年，定侍衛軍政考試，向例軍政年不許告病乞休，以杜規避。
entries.en: In Jiaqing 4 (1799), guard military inspections were regulated; illness retirement was forbidden in inspection years to prevent evasion.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Jiaqing, guard military inspection examinations were fixed; by precedent illness retirement was not permitted in inspection years, to prevent evasion.

entries.zh: 八年，申諭查閱營伍年分，事關考覈，照軍政例，不得告病、乞休。
entries.en: In Jiaqing 8 (1803) it was reiterated that illness retirement was forbidden in camp-inspection years, as in military inspection years.
entries.literal: In the eighth year it was reiterated that in years of camp inspection, which concerned evaluation, following military inspection precedent, illness retirement was not permitted.

entries.zh: 咸、同軍興，百度稍弛，軍政大典，相沿不廢。
entries.en: During the Xianfeng and Tongzhi wars many regulations lapsed, yet the great military inspection continued.
entries.literal: During the Xianfeng and Tongzhi military campaigns, many regulations grew lax, yet the great military inspection ritual continued without abolition.

entries.zh: 咸豐二年，黑龍江將軍英隆以俄兵窺伺，派將弁扼守要隘，疏請本年軍政展限舉行。
entries.en: In Xianfeng 2 (1852), Heilongjiang General Yinglong, facing Russian probing, dispatched officers to key passes and requested postponing that year's military inspection.
entries.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng, Heilongjiang General Yinglong, because Russian troops were watching, dispatched officers to hold key passes and memorialized requesting extension of that year's military inspection.

entries.zh: 不允。
entries.en: The request was denied.
entries.literal: This was not approved.

entries.zh: 嗣湖廣總督程矞采等以軍務未竣，疏請展限，令凱撤後再行補考。
entries.en: Later Huguang Governor-General Cheng Yucai and others, citing unfinished military affairs, requested extension and supplementary examination after victory.
entries.literal: Later Huguang Governor-General Cheng Yucai and others, because military affairs were unfinished, memorialized requesting extension, ordering supplementary examination after victory and withdrawal.

entries.zh: 並諭年老力衰者，隨時參辦。
entries.en: Aged and weak officers could also be impeached at any time.
entries.literal: It was also ordered that the aged and weak might be impeached at any time.

entries.zh: 沿及德宗，雖加意振飭，勢成弩末，展限之舉，史不絕書。
entries.en: Under the Guangxu Emperor, despite efforts at revival, momentum failed; extensions were endlessly recorded.
entries.literal: Down to the Guangxu Emperor, though he strove to revive and rectify, momentum was like an arrow at the end of its flight; extensions were recorded endlessly in history.

entries.zh: 康熙二十三年，以籓、臬與督、撫親近，停其卓異。
entries.en: In Kangxi 23 (1684), outstanding nominations for provincial and judicial officials were halted because they were too close to governors.
entries.literal: In the twenty-third year of Kangxi, because provincial and judicial officials were close to governors-general and governors, their outstanding nominations were halted.

entries.zh: 凡卓異官紀錄即升，不次擢用。
entries.en: Outstanding officials were recorded for immediate promotion, often out of turn.
entries.literal: All outstanding officials were recorded and immediately promoted, appointed out of turn.

entries.zh: 歷朝最重其選，徇私濫保者罪之。
entries.en: Every dynasty prized this selection, and favoritism in nominations was punished.
entries.literal: Successive dynasties most valued this selection; those who showed favoritism in reckless recommendation were punished.

entries.zh: 康熙初，御史張沖翼請申嚴卓異定額，以詳覈事迹，使名實相副為言。
entries.en: Early in Kangxi, Censor Zhang Chongyi urged strict outstanding quotas, detailed verification of records, and matching reputation to reality.
entries.literal: Early in Kangxi, Censor Zhang Chongyi requested strict enforcement of outstanding quotas, detailed verification of facts, and that name and reality should match.

entries.zh: 下部議。
entries.en: The memorial was referred to the Board.
entries.literal: The matter was sent to the ministry for deliberation.

entries.zh: 六年，從御史田六善請，卓異官以清廉為本，司、道等官必註明不派節禮、索餽送，州、縣等官必註明不派雜差、重火耗、虧損行戶、強貸富民。
entries.en: In Kangxi 6 (1667), following Censor Tian Liushan, outstanding officials had to be fundamentally honest: circuit officials had to certify they took no festival gifts or supply levies; county officials had to certify they imposed no illegal corvée, excessive meltage fees, merchant losses, or forced loans on the wealthy.
entries.literal: In the sixth year, following Censor Tian Liushan's request, outstanding officials were to take integrity as foundation; circuit and commissioner officials must note that they did not assign festival gifts or demand supply deliveries; prefectural and county officials must note that they did not assign miscellaneous corvée, impose heavy meltage fees, harm merchants, or force loans on the wealthy.

entries.zh: 以清吏之有無，定督、撫之賢否。
entries.en: Governors' merit was judged by whether their subordinates were honest.
entries.literal: Whether subordinates were honest determined whether governors were worthy.

entries.zh: 其時廉吏輩出，靈壽令陸隴其等擢隸憲府，吏治蒸蒸，稱極盛焉。
entries.en: Honest officials flourished; Magistrate Lu Longqi of Lingshou and others were promoted to judicial posts, and local administration reached its zenith.
entries.literal: At that time honest officials emerged in succession; Ling Shou magistrate Lu Longqi and others were promoted to judicial posts; administration flourished, called the greatest prosperity.

entries.zh: 四十四年，詔舉卓異，務期無加派，無濫刑，無盜案，無錢糧拖久、倉庫虧空，民生得所，地方日有起色。
entries.en: In Kangxi 44 (1705) an edict required outstanding nominations only for officials with no extra levies, abusive punishments, bandit cases, fiscal arrears, granary deficits, and with improving livelihoods and local conditions.
entries.literal: In the forty-fourth year an edict ordered outstanding nominations, requiring no extra levies, no abusive punishment, no bandit cases, no prolonged grain and tax arrears or granary deficits, the people's livelihood settled, and the locality daily improving.

entries.zh: 其他虛文，不必開載。
entries.en: Empty formalities need not be recorded.
entries.literal: Other empty verbiage need not be entered.

entries.zh: 乾隆八年，命督、撫以務農本計察覈屬員，論者謂以勸農為勸吏之要，深得治本，與漢詔同風。
