entries.en: In Qianlong 8 (1743), governors were ordered to evaluate subordinates on agricultural policy; commentators praised this as grasping the root of governance, in the spirit of Han dynasty edicts.
entries.literal: In the eighth year of Qianlong, governors-general and governors were ordered to examine subordinates with promotion of agriculture as fundamental policy; commentators said that taking encouragement of farming as the key to encouraging officials deeply grasped governing the root, in the same spirit as Han edicts.

entries.zh: 先是雍正六年，定卓異薦舉失實處分，自行奏參者免。
entries.en: Earlier, in Yongzheng 6 (1728), penalties were set for false outstanding nominations, with exemption for self-reporting.
entries.literal: Earlier, in the sixth year of Yongzheng, disposition was fixed for false outstanding recommendations; those who reported themselves were exempted.

entries.zh: 卓異官有貪酷不法，或錢糧、盜案未清，發覺者，原薦督、撫處分較司、道、府為輕。
entries.en: When nominated outstanding officials proved corrupt or had uncleared fiscal or bandit cases, recommending governors were punished more lightly than circuit, commissioner, or prefectural officials.
entries.literal: When outstanding officials proved greedy, cruel, or lawless, or had uncleared grain, tax, or bandit cases, the recommending governor was punished more lightly than circuit, commissioner, or prefectural officials.

entries.zh: 乾隆四十八年，改定卓異官犯贓，覈其年月在原薦上司離任前後，分別議處。
entries.en: In Qianlong 48 (1783), when outstanding officials were found corrupt, penalties for their recommenders depended on whether the offense occurred before or after the recommender left office.
entries.literal: In the forty-eighth year of Qianlong it was revised that when outstanding officials committed corruption, the date relative to their recommender's departure from office should be verified and disposition made accordingly.

entries.zh: 臬司、道、府減督、撫一等，籓司照督、撫例，以道、府按例轉詳督、撫、籓司親為覈定也。
entries.en: Surveillance commissioners, circuit officials, and prefects were punished one grade less than governors; provincial administration commissioners followed governors' precedent, since circuit and prefectural officials reported through them for governors' personal verification.
entries.literal: Surveillance commissioners, circuit officials, and prefects received one grade lighter punishment than governors; provincial administration commissioners followed governors' precedent, because circuit and prefectural officials reported through routine channels for governors, provincial administration commissioners, and surveillance commissioners to verify personally.

entries.zh: 五十年，帝以保薦卓異，向分正附，未明定限制，易開徼幸之漸。
entries.en: In Qianlong 50 (1785) the emperor noted that primary and supplementary outstanding nominations lacked clear limits, encouraging opportunism.
entries.literal: In the fiftieth year the emperor noted that in recommending outstanding officials, primary and supplementary nominations were distinguished but limits were not clearly fixed, easily opening the way to opportunism.

entries.zh: 敕部詳覈各省大小、缺分多寡，酌中定制，裁去附薦名目。
entries.en: The Board was ordered to calculate provincial post numbers, set moderate quotas, and abolish supplementary nominations.
entries.literal: The ministry was ordered to examine carefully the size and number of posts in each province, fix a moderate standard, and abolish supplementary nomination titles.

entries.zh: 於是各省卓異官有定額，終清世無大變更也。
entries.en: Each province then had fixed outstanding quotas, which changed little for the rest of the dynasty.
entries.literal: Thus each province had fixed outstanding quotas, with no great change through the Qing.

entries.zh: 八法處分，行之既久，長吏或視為具文，每將微員細故，填註塞責。
entries.en: The eight disciplinary categories, long in force, were often treated as empty form, with chiefs padding evaluations with minor details about junior staff.
entries.literal: The eight categories of disposition, long in practice, were sometimes treated as empty form by superiors, who filled in minor details of low officials to meet obligation.

entries.zh: 歷朝訓諭諄諄，力戒瞻徇，猶防冤抑。
entries.en: Successive dynasties earnestly warned against favoritism while also guarding against wrongful suppression.
entries.literal: Successive dynasties admonished earnestly, strictly forbidding favoritism, yet still guarding against wrongful suppression.

entries.zh: 雍正元年，詔大計降級罰俸官，例不許卓異，果有居官廉幹因公詿誤者，淮與卓異。
entries.en: In Yongzheng 1 (1723) an edict barred demoted or fined officials from outstanding nomination, except honest capable officials wronged by official duty.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng an edict stated that officials demoted or fined at the grand assessment were by rule not permitted outstanding nomination, but if truly honest and capable yet wronged by public duty, they might receive outstanding nomination.

entries.zh: 又以卓異八法舉劾不過數十人，其不列舉劾之平等官，自知縣以上，令督、撫註考，報部察核。
entries.en: Because outstanding nominations and eight-category impeachments involved only dozens of officials, governors were also to evaluate average officials from district magistrate rank upward and report to the Board.
entries.literal: Also, since outstanding nominations and eight-category impeachment involved only several tens of people, average officials from district magistrates upward who were neither recommended nor impeached were ordered evaluated by governors and reported to the ministry for review.

entries.zh: 四年，諭參劾人員或有冤抑及避重就輕等弊，除貪酷官無庸引見外，其不謹、浮躁、不及等被劾官，督、撫給咨送部引見。
entries.en: In Yongzheng 4 (1726) an edict noted wrongful suppression and lenient treatment of serious offenses; except corrupt officials, those impeached as careless, frivolous, or inadequate were to be presented to the Board for review.
entries.literal: In the fourth year an edict stated that impeached persons might suffer wrongful suppression or the abuse of avoiding serious charges for light ones; apart from greedy and cruel officials who need not be presented, those impeached as careless, frivolous, or inadequate should be given credentials by governors and sent to the ministry for presentation.

entries.zh: 乾隆二十四年，帝以八法參本內不謹、浮躁官，未將何事不謹、何事浮躁、一一聲敘，或有公事無誤而節目闊疏，才具有為而氣質粗率，上司以意見不洽，概登白簡，不無可惜。
entries.en: In Qianlong 24 (1759) the emperor noted that careless and frivolous impeachments often lacked specifics; some capable officials were impeached for procedural looseness or coarse manner, or because superiors disliked them—wasteful of talent.
entries.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Qianlong the emperor noted that in eight-category impeachment memorials, careless and frivolous officials did not have what acts were careless or frivolous stated one by one; some had no error in public business but were loose in procedure, some had capacity but coarse temperament, some were listed wholesale because superiors' views did not agree—it was not without regret.

entries.zh: 其或敗檢逾閒，僅與避重就輕，均非整飭官方之意。
entries.en: Serious moral failures treated leniently were equally contrary to rectifying official conduct.
entries.literal: Or moral failure and excess might receive only lenient treatment, avoiding serious for light charges—all contrary to the intent of rectifying officialdom.

entries.zh: 命詳註實跡，不得籠統參劾。
entries.en: Detailed factual records were required; vague impeachments were forbidden.
entries.literal: Detailed factual records were ordered; vague impeachment was forbidden.

entries.zh: 嘉慶八年，定督、撫隨時參劾闒冗平庸等事，未列敘寶跡，被劾官情原赴部引見者，得援大計六法例。
entries.en: In Jiaqing 8 (1803), officials impeached at any time for mediocrity without detailed facts could request presentation to the Board under the grand-assessment six-category precedent.
entries.literal: In the eighth year of Jiaqing it was fixed that when governors impeached at any time for incompetence, mediocrity, and the like without listing detailed facts, if the impeached official wished to go to the ministry for presentation, the grand-assessment six-category precedent might be invoked.

entries.zh: 此則考覈不厭詳密，冀搜求遺才，輔計典之不及也。
entries.en: This reflected exhaustive review hoping to find overlooked talent beyond what formal assessments could reach.
entries.literal: This showed that examination did not tire of detail, hoping to seek overlooked talent and supplement what the assessment ritual could not reach.

entries.zh: 嘉、道以後，計典一循舊例，督、撫奉行故事，鮮克振刷。
entries.en: After Jiaqing and Daoguang, assessments followed old precedent; governors observed form but rarely reformed.
entries.literal: After Jiaqing and Daoguang, the assessment ritual followed old precedent; governors observed form, rarely able to revive and reform.

entries.zh: 道光八年，山東大計卓異，護撫賀長齡原註新城令容昺悃愊慈祥等語，詔以寬厚難膺上考，令各省薦舉體用兼備、熟明治理者。
entries.en: In Daoguang 8 (1828), Acting Governor He Changling of Shandong nominated Magistrate Rong Bing of Xincheng as sincere and benevolent; an edict ruled that lenience alone did not qualify for top rating and ordered nominations of officials skilled in practical governance.
entries.literal: In the eighth year of Daoguang, in Shandong's grand assessment outstanding nomination, Acting Governor He Changling originally noted Xincheng magistrate Rong Bing as sincere, kind, and benevolent; an edict held that mere lenience could not qualify for top rating, ordering each province to recommend those combining substance and function who were skilled in governance.

entries.zh: 咸、同軍興，或地方甫收復，有待撫綏，或疆圉偪寇氛，亟籌保衛，敕各督、撫留心存記廉能之員，列上考，備擢用。
entries.en: During the Xianfeng and Tongzhi wars, some regions needed pacification and others faced bandit threats; governors were ordered to note honest capable officials for top ratings and promotion.
entries.literal: During the Xianfeng and Tongzhi military campaigns, some places had just been recovered and awaited pacification, some frontiers faced bandit threat and urgently needed defense; each governor was ordered to note honest and capable men, list them for top rating, and prepare them for promotion.

entries.zh: 時督、撫權宜行事，用人不拘資格，隨時舉措，固不能以大計常例繩其後也。
entries.en: Governors then acted expediently, appointing without regard to seniority; normal grand-assessment rules could not bind them afterward.
entries.literal: At that time governors acted expediently, employing men without regard to qualifications, taking measures as needed—they could not be bound afterward by grand-assessment routine.

entries.zh: 年老休致，例有明文。
entries.en: Mandatory retirement by age was clearly regulated.
entries.literal: Retirement on account of age had clear regulations.

entries.zh: 乾隆二十二年，定部、院屬官五十五歲以上，堂官詳加甄別。
entries.en: In Qianlong 22 (1757), ministry officials aged fifty-five and above were to be carefully screened by their chiefs.
entries.literal: In the twenty-second year of Qianlong, it was fixed that subordinate officials of ministries and agencies aged fifty-five and above should be carefully screened by department chiefs.

entries.zh: 三十三年，改定京察二、三等留任各官，六十五歲以上引見。
entries.en: In Qianlong 33 (1768), second- and third-grade officials retained in post who were sixty-five or older were to be presented to the throne.
entries.literal: In the thirty-third year it was revised that officials retained in second or third grade at the capital inspection who were sixty-five and above should be presented.

entries.zh: 嘉慶三年，命京察二、三等官引見，以年逾七十為限。
entries.en: In Jiaqing 3 (1798), second- and third-grade officials were presented only if over seventy.
entries.literal: In the third year of Jiaqing, second- and third-grade officials at the capital inspection were ordered presented, with the limit of over seventy years of age.

entries.zh: 尋復舊例。
entries.en: The earlier rule was soon restored.
entries.literal: Soon the former rule was restored.

entries.zh: 六法處分綦嚴，長官往往博寬大之名，每屆京察，祗黜退數人，虛應故事，餘概優容，而被劾者又不免屈抑。
entries.en: Though the six disciplinary categories were strict, chiefs often sought reputations for leniency: each inspection dismissed only a few officials as a formality, indulged the rest, yet still wrongfully suppressed those impeached.
entries.literal: The six categories of disposition were extremely strict, yet superiors often sought a reputation for leniency; at each capital inspection only a few were dismissed, empty compliance with form, the rest broadly indulged, while the impeached were not spared wrongful suppression.

entries.zh: 雍正中，汪景祺、查嗣庭輩論列時政，以部員壅滯為言，有「十年不調、白首為郎」等語。
entries.en: Under Yongzheng, Wang Jingqi, Zha Siting, and others criticized current affairs, citing ministry congestion with lines such as "ten years without promotion, white-haired yet still a gentleman-attendant."
entries.literal: In the Yongzheng era, Wang Jingqi, Zha Siting, and others discussed current affairs, speaking of congestion among ministry staff, with phrases such as "ten years without transfer, white-haired yet still a gentleman-attendant."

entries.zh: 帝責以怨望誹謗，而事實不得謂誣。
entries.en: The emperor condemned them for seditious slander, though their facts were not false.
entries.literal: The emperor rebuked them for resentful slander, yet the facts could not be called false.

entries.zh: 蓋部員冗濫，康、雍時已然矣。
entries.en: Ministry overstaffing was already a problem under Kangxi and Yongzheng.
entries.literal: For ministry staff were redundant and excessive—already so in the Kangxi and Yongzheng eras.

entries.zh: 國初未立限制，順治九年，定六年一舉，是為軍政考覈之始。
entries.en: Initially no cycle was fixed; in Shunzhi 9 (1652) a six-year military inspection was established.
entries.literal: At the founding no limit was set; in the ninth year of Shunzhi a six-year cycle was fixed—this was the beginning of military inspection examination.

entries.zh: 十一年，改定五年為期。
entries.en: In Shunzhi 11 (1654) the cycle was changed to five years.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year it was changed to a five-year cycle.

entries.zh: 十三年，從給事中張文光請，軍政卓異，照文官賜服旌勸，後改為加一級。
entries.en: In Shunzhi 13 (1656), following Supervising Secretary Zhang Wenguang, outstanding military nominees received ceremonial rewards like civil officials; later this became a one-rank increment.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year, following Supervising Secretary Zhang Wenguang's request, outstanding military inspection nominees, like civil officials, received ceremonial robes and commendation; later this was changed to one rank increment.

entries.zh: 康熙元年，停軍政，專行考滿。
entries.en: In Kangxi 1 (1662), military inspection was halted in favor of completion review alone.
entries.literal: In the first year of Kangxi, military inspection was halted and only completion of review was conducted.

entries.zh: 既而兵部疏請直省武職應依文官例，按年限由總督、提督會同舉劾。
entries.en: Soon the Board of War proposed that provincial military officers follow civil precedent, with governors-general and provincial commanders jointly recommending and impeaching by years of service.
entries.literal: Soon the Board of War memorialized that provincial military posts should follow civil precedent, with governors-general and provincial military commanders jointly recommending and impeaching according to years of service.

entries.zh: 御史季振宜疏言：「武職考滿，營謀優等，剋扣軍饟，貽誤封疆。
entries.en: Censor Ji Zhenyi memorialized: "In military completion reviews, officers scheme for top grades, embezzle army pay, and harm frontier defense.
entries.literal: Censor Ji Zhenyi memorialized: "In military completion of review, scheming for top grades, embezzling military pay, and harming frontier defense.

entries.zh: 請按歷俸功次升轉。」
entries.en: Promotions should follow salary history and merit ranking."
entries.literal: Request promotion and transfer according to salary history and merit ranking."

entries.zh: 於是六年定舉行軍政事宜，京、外武職長官，註以四格，並詳列履行、軍功，分別去留，咨部。
entries.en: In Kangxi 6 (1667) military inspection procedures were codified: capital and provincial military chiefs were rated by four criteria, with detailed service records and military merit, then retained or removed and reported to the Board.
entries.literal: Accordingly in the sixth year matters for conducting military inspection were fixed; capital and provincial military chiefs were noted according to four criteria, with service records and military merit listed in detail, retention or removal distinguished, and the matter communicated to the ministry.

entries.zh: 必註明行止端方、弓馬嫻熟、管轄嚴肅、供職勤慎、不擾害地方等考語，方許薦舉。
entries.en: Nominations required noting upright conduct, skilled archery and horsemanship, strict command, diligent service, and no harm to local populations.
entries.literal: Evaluation phrases such as upright conduct, skilled archery and horsemanship, strict jurisdiction, diligent service, and not harming the locality had to be noted before recommendation was permitted.

entries.zh: 必有八法等款實跡，始行糾參。
entries.en: Impeachment required factual records under the eight disciplinary categories.
entries.literal: There had to be factual records under the eight categories before impeachment could proceed.

entries.zh: 復令提督、總兵官自陳，提督由總督註考，總兵官由總督、提督註考。
entries.en: Provincial and regional commanders submitted self-assessments; provincial commanders were evaluated by governors-general, regional commanders by governors-general and provincial commanders.
entries.literal: Provincial military commanders and regional commanders were again ordered to submit self-assessments; provincial commanders were evaluated by governors-general, regional commanders by governors-general and provincial commanders.

entries.zh: 無總督省分，巡撫註考。
entries.en: In provinces without a governor-general, the governor recorded evaluations.
entries.literal: In provinces without a governor-general, the governor noted evaluations.

entries.zh: 嗣以滇省用兵，海內騷動，羽書倥傯，軍政曠不舉行者十年。
entries.en: War in Yunnan then disturbed the empire; urgent dispatches piled up, and military inspection was suspended for ten years.
entries.literal: Later, because Yunnan was at war and the realm was disturbed, urgent dispatches piled up, and military inspection was not conducted for ten years.

entries.zh: 至二十一年，滇逆蕩平，從給事中碩穆科請，舉行軍政大典，各官事實履行，自康熙十一年軍政後開起。
entries.en: In Kangxi 21 (1682), after the Yunnan rebellion was suppressed, Supervising Secretary Shuomuke's request restored the great military inspection, with service records dating from the Kangxi 11 inspection.
entries.literal: By the twenty-first year the Yunnan rebels were pacified; following Supervising Secretary Shuomuke's request, the great military inspection was held, with each officer's factual service record starting from after the Kangxi eleventh-year inspection.

entries.zh: 九門千總等由九門提督註考。
entries.en: Nine Gates battalion commanders were evaluated by the Nine Gates commander.
entries.literal: Battalion commanders of the Nine Gates and others were evaluated by the Nine Gates commander.

entries.zh: 候補總兵官亦令自陳。
entries.en: Candidate regional commanders also submitted self-assessments.
entries.literal: Candidate regional commanders were also ordered to submit self-assessments.

entries.zh: 副將以下候缺者，照舊例考察。
entries.en: Brigade generals and below awaiting posts were examined under the old rules.
entries.literal: Brigade generals and below awaiting posts were examined according to old precedent.

entries.zh: 六十一年，命在京武職領侍衛內大臣，八旗都統，前鋒、護軍、步軍統領，副都統等，毋庸自陳。
entries.en: In Kangxi 61 (1722), capital military officials including inner palace guard ministers, Banner lieutenant-generals, vanguard, guard, and foot-soldier commanders, and deputy lieutenant-generals were exempted from self-assessment.
entries.literal: In the sixty-first year, capital military officials including inner palace guards bearing the title of minister, Banner lieutenant-generals, vanguard, guard, and foot-soldier commanders, and deputy lieutenant-generals were ordered not to submit self-assessments.

entries.zh: 考選軍政時，屬員註考，照外省舉劾例。
entries.en: During military inspection, subordinates were evaluated under the same commendation and impeachment rules as provincial officials.
entries.literal: At military inspection selection, subordinates' evaluations followed the provincial recommendation and impeachment precedent.

entries.zh: 各省駐防將軍、副都統等，照提、鎮例自陳。
entries.en: Provincial garrison generals and deputy lieutenant-generals submitted self-assessments like provincial and regional commanders.
entries.literal: Garrison generals and deputy lieutenant-generals in the provinces submitted self-assessments following provincial and regional commander precedent.

entries.zh: 屬員照京城例。
entries.en: Their subordinates followed capital rules.
entries.literal: Subordinates followed the capital precedent.

entries.zh: 德州等處城守尉、協領，派大臣往考，會同察覈其屬，註考以聞。
entries.en: Garrison commandants and assistant commandants at Dezhou and elsewhere were examined by dispatched ministers who jointly reviewed subordinates and reported evaluations.
entries.literal: Garrison commandants and assistant commandants at Dezhou and elsewhere were examined by dispatched ministers, who jointly inspected their subordinates, noted evaluations, and reported.

entries.zh: 雍正元年，命平等官守備以上，督、撫、提、鎮註考。
entries.en: In Yongzheng 1 (1723), average officials from garrison commander rank upward were evaluated by governors and military commanders.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng, average officials from garrison commanders upward were ordered evaluated by governors-general, governors, provincial commanders, and regional commanders.

entries.zh: 其冬，詔曰：「初次考選軍政，有出兵效力、年老俸深、尚能坐理者，留任。
entries.en: That winter an edict stated: "At the first military inspection, veterans with long service who could still manage affairs were retained.
entries.literal: That winter an edict said: "At the first military inspection selection, those who served in campaigns, were old with deep salary tenure, and could still manage affairs were retained.

entries.zh: 不宜留任者，另奏加恩。
entries.en: Those unsuitable for retention were separately memorialized for special grace.
entries.literal: Those unsuitable for retention were separately memorialized for special grace.

entries.zh: 或雖未效力行間，而供職年久者，亦留心驗看。」
entries.en: Even those without campaign service but with long tenure were to be carefully examined."
entries.literal: Or though they had not served in campaigns, if their tenure was long, they should also be carefully examined."

entries.zh: 此則垂念資勞，特頒寬典，非常例也。
entries.en: This showed concern for long service—a special leniency, not ordinary precedent.
entries.literal: This showed concern for senior merit and labor, a specially issued lenient measure—not ordinary precedent.

entries.zh: 二年，諭各省所保副、參、游擊，輪流引見，察其人材弓馬，督、撫、提、鎮以其操守訓練，分別等第密陳。
entries.en: In Yongzheng 2 (1724) recommended brigade generals, regimental colonels, and battalion commanders were presented in rotation; governors and commanders secretly reported grades based on integrity, training, and horsemanship.
entries.literal: In the second year it was ordered that recommended brigade generals, regimental colonels, and battalion commanders in the provinces be presented in rotation, their talent and horsemanship inspected, and governors and commanders secretly memorialize grades according to integrity and training.

entries.zh: 六年，山西太原總兵官袁立松疏陳平垣營守備梁玉廉潔敏練，以年老入參劾。
entries.en: In Yongzheng 6 (1728), Regional Commander Yuan Lisong of Taiyuan memorialized that Garrison Commander Liang Yu of Pingyuan was honest, keen, and skilled, yet was impeached for age.
entries.literal: In the sixth year, Taiyuan regional commander Yuan Lisong of Shanxi memorialized that Pingyuan garrison commander Liang Yu was honest, keen, and skilled, yet was impeached on account of age.

entries.zh: 帝以諳練才不可多得，命酌量以游擊題補，尤殊恩也。
entries.en: The emperor ruled that seasoned talent was rare and ordered him considered for battalion commander—a special grace.
entries.literal: The emperor held that seasoned talent was hard to find and ordered him considered for appointment as battalion commander—a special grace indeed.

entries.zh: 是年定卓異官原任有貪酷不法，或升調他省，別犯贓罪，原舉長官，分別處分。
entries.en: That year penalties were set for recommenders when outstanding officials proved corrupt, including offenses committed after transfer to another province.
entries.literal: That year it was fixed that when outstanding officials in their original posts were greedy, cruel, and lawless, or after transfer to another province separately committed corruption, the original recommending superior would be punished according to circumstances.

entries.zh: 道光四年，候際清贖罪舞弊一案，刑部司員恩德等朋謀撞騙堂官，以謬登薦牘，保列一等，下部議處。
entries.en: In Daoguang 4 (1824), in the Hou Jiqing bribery case, Ministry of Justice clerks including Ende conspired to deceive their chiefs into recommending unworthy officials for first grade; the case was referred for disciplinary action.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Daoguang, in the case of Hou Jiqing's ransomed punishment and fraud, Ministry of Justice clerks Ende and others conspired in a gang to deceive department chiefs and had them wrongly entered on recommendation lists as first grade; the matter was sent down for deliberation and disposition.

entries.zh: 諭嗣後京察有冒濫徇私者連坐。
entries.en: An edict decreed collective punishment for future capital inspections marred by favoritism or inflated nominations.
entries.literal: An edict ordered that thereafter in the capital inspection those who recklessly exceeded quotas or showed favoritism would be punished collectively.

entries.zh: 七年，給事中吳傑奏：「大計、軍政，皆有舉有劾。
entries.en: In Daoguang 7 (1827), Supervising Secretary Wu Jie memorialized: "The grand assessment and military inspections both include commendation and impeachment.
entries.literal: In the seventh year, Supervising Secretary Wu Jie memorialized: "The grand assessment and military inspections all have both recommendation and impeachment.

entries.zh: 近年六部辦理京察，除保舉一等外，不問賢否，概列二等。
entries.en: Recently the Six Ministries rated nearly everyone second grade regardless of merit, recommending only a few for first grade.
entries.literal: In recent years the Six Ministries conducted the capital inspection: apart from recommending first grade, regardless of merit all were listed second grade.

entries.zh: 間有三等數人，仍予留任。
entries.en: A handful received third grade yet were still retained.
entries.literal: Occasionally a few in third grade were still retained in office.

entries.zh: 六法不施，有勸無懲。
entries.en: The six disciplinary categories went unused—reward without punishment.
entries.literal: The six categories were not applied; there was encouragement without punishment.

entries.zh: 應申明舊章，舉劾並用。」
entries.en: Old regulations should be enforced so commendation and impeachment work together."
entries.literal: The old regulations should be declared and recommendation and impeachment used together."

entries.zh: 帝韙其言，降諭飭行。
entries.en: The emperor agreed and issued an edict ordering compliance.
entries.literal: The emperor approved his words and issued an edict ordering compliance.

entries.zh: 十五年，令於京察外隨時糾參，以為補救。
entries.en: In Daoguang 15 (1835), officials could be impeached at any time outside the regular inspection as a corrective measure.
entries.literal: In the fifteenth year, it was ordered that outside the capital inspection impeachment might occur at any time as a remedy.

entries.zh: 咸豐十年，刑部堂官濫保不諳例案之員，朝廷務循寬大，輒以相習成風，不獨刑部為然，多為原宥。
entries.en: In Xianfeng 10 (1860), Ministry of Justice chiefs recommended officials ignorant of legal precedent; the court's habitual leniency extended across ministries, and most offenders were pardoned.
entries.literal: In the tenth year of Xianfeng, Ministry of Justice chiefs recklessly recommended staff ignorant of case precedents; the court pursued leniency, and this became habitual—not only in the Ministry of Justice; most were pardoned.

entries.zh: 僅予大學士桂良等鐫級留任，出考堂官罰俸而已。
entries.en: Only Grand Secretary Gui Liang and others lost a rank increment while retaining office; inspecting chiefs received only salary fines.
entries.literal: Only Grand Secretary Gui Liang and others had a rank inscription removed but were retained; the chiefs who conducted the inspection were merely fined.

entries.zh: 穆宗即位，大難未平，厲精澄敘。
entries.en: When the Tongzhi Emperor acceded amid ongoing crisis, he strove to tighten official evaluation.
entries.literal: When the Muzong emperor acceded, great calamity was not yet settled, yet he strove to clarify evaluation.

entries.zh: 同治五年，詔部、院堂官謹遵嘉慶五年備冊密識賢否、公議同覽之諭，並常川進署，與司員講求公事，藉覘其屬賢否。
entries.en: In Tongzhi 5 (1866) an edict ordered ministry chiefs to follow Jiaqing's private merit registers and collective review, attend office regularly, discuss business with staff, and thereby assess subordinates.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Tongzhi an edict ordered ministry chiefs strictly to follow the Jiaqing fifth-year instruction on keeping registers secretly noting merit, joint review, and regularly attending office to discuss public business with clerks, thereby observing subordinates' merit.

entries.zh: 八年，又諭京察不得有舉無劾，冀湔滌舊習，一新庶政。
entries.en: In Tongzhi 8 (1869) another edict required both commendation and impeachment in the capital inspection, hoping to break old habits and renew governance.
entries.literal: In the eighth year another edict stated that the capital inspection must not have recommendation without impeachment, hoping to wash away old habits and renew common governance.

entries.zh: 然積重之勢，不能復返。
entries.en: Yet entrenched habits could not be reversed.
entries.literal: Yet the weight of accumulated custom could not be reversed.

entries.zh: 光緒七年，禮部侍郎寶廷疏陳京察積弊，言之痛切，謂：「瞻徇情面之弊，不專在部、院堂官，當責樞臣考察，必公必嚴。
entries.en: In Guangxu 7 (1881), Vice Minister of Rites Baoting memorialized on capital-inspection abuses, arguing forcefully that: "Favoritism was not limited to ministry chiefs; Grand Council ministers must conduct inspections that were fair and strict.
entries.literal: In the seventh year of Guangxu, Vice Minister of Rites Baoting memorialized on accumulated abuses in the capital inspection, speaking with painful urgency, saying: "The abuse of showing favoritism lies not only with ministry chiefs; the Grand Council ministers should be charged with inspection, which must be fair and strict.

entries.zh: 樞臣果精白乃心，破除情面，不特能考察部、院司員之賢否，並能考察內、外大臣之賢否。
entries.en: If council ministers were truly impartial and broke with favoritism, they could evaluate not only ministry staff but also all senior civil and military officials.
entries.literal: If the Grand Council ministers truly purify their hearts and break through favoritism, they can not only inspect the merit of ministry clerks but also inspect inner and outer grand ministers.

entries.zh: 而考察樞臣功過，在聖明獨斷。
entries.en: Judging the council ministers themselves, however, rested with the emperor alone.
entries.literal: As for inspecting the achievements and faults of council ministers, that rests in the sage emperor's sole decision.

entries.zh: 若朝廷先以京察為故事具文，何責乎樞臣，更何責乎部、院堂官！」
entries.en: If the court treated the capital inspection as empty formality, how could one blame council ministers—or ministry chiefs?"
entries.literal: If the court first treats the capital inspection as empty precedent, how can one blame council ministers, much less ministry chiefs!"

entries.zh: 論雖切中而難實行，徒託空言而已。
entries.en: His argument was sound but impracticable—mere empty rhetoric.
entries.literal: Though the argument hit the mark, it was hard to implement—mere empty words.

entries.zh: 宣統二年，吏部設立憲政籌備處，改考功司為考績科，主文職功過應行變通事宜。
entries.en: In Xuantong 2 (1910), the Board established a Constitutional Preparation Office, renamed the Department of Merit Records the Performance Evaluation Section, and oversaw reforms to civil performance review.
entries.literal: In the second year of Xuantong, the Board of Civil Appointments established a Constitutional Preparation Office, changed the Department of Merit Records to the Performance Evaluation Section, and oversaw matters of reward and punishment for civil officials requiring reform.

entries.zh: 其時浮議紛紜，新舊雜糅，吏部等於贅疣矣。
entries.en: By then debate swirled, old and new systems overlapped, and the Board had become largely redundant.
entries.literal: At that time floating opinions were numerous, old and new mixed together, and the Board of Civil Appointments was like a superfluous growth.

entries.zh: 志八十六
entries.en: Treatise 86
entries.literal: Treatise eighty-six.

entries.zh: 文官捐始康熙十三年，以用兵三籓，軍需孔亟，暫開事例。
entries.en: Civil-office purchases began in Kangxi 13 (1674), when war against the Three Feudatories created desperate need for military funds and temporary regulations were opened.
entries.literal: Civil-office contributions began in the thirteenth year of Kangxi, when war against the Three Feudatories made military supplies urgently needed and regulations were opened temporarily.

entries.zh: 十六年，左都御史宋德宜言：「開例三載，知縣捐至五百餘人。
entries.en: In Kangxi 16 (1677), Left Censor-in-Chief Song Deyi said: "Regulations have been open three years, and more than five hundred district magistrates have been purchased.
entries.literal: In the sixteenth year, Left Censor-in-Chief Song Deyi said: "Regulations have been open three years; district magistrates purchased by contribution have reached more than five hundred.

entries.zh: 始因缺多易得，踴躍爭趨。
entries.en: At first vacancies were plentiful and easy to obtain, so contributors rushed to compete.
entries.literal: At first, because vacancies were many and easy to obtain, people eagerly rushed forward.

entries.zh: 今見非數年不克選授，徘徊觀望。
entries.en: Now they see that appointment takes years, and they hang back in hesitation.
entries.literal: Now they see that without several years they cannot be selected and appointed, and they hesitate and watch.

entries.zh: 宜限期停止，俾輸捐恐後。
entries.en: A deadline for closing should be set, so that latecomers fear missing their chance to contribute.
entries.literal: It is fitting to set a deadline for stopping, so that those paying contributions will fear being too late.

entries.zh: 既有濟軍需，亦慎重名器。」
entries.en: This would meet military needs while safeguarding the dignity of official ranks."
entries.literal: This would both aid military supplies and honor prestigious titles."

entries.zh: 帝納其言。
entries.en: The emperor accepted his advice.
entries.literal: The emperor accepted his words.

entries.zh: 滇南收復，捐例停。
entries.en: When Yunnan was recovered, purchase regulations were halted.
entries.literal: When Yunnan was recovered, contribution regulations ceased.

entries.zh: 嗣以西安、大同飢，又永定河工，復開事例。
entries.en: Later famine in Xi'an and Datong and works on the Yongding River led to reopening the regulations.
entries.literal: Later, because of famine in Xi'an and Datong and Yongding River works, regulations were opened again.

entries.zh: 五十一年，增置通州倉廒，科臣有請開捐者，廷議如所請。
entries.en: In Kangxi 51 (1712), when Tongzhou granaries were to be expanded, a censor requested opening contributions, and the court approved.
entries.literal: In the fifty-first year, when granaries at Tongzhou were to be expanded, a censor requested opening contributions; the court deliberated and agreed.

entries.zh: 侍郎王掞抗疏言：「鄉里童騃，一旦捐資，儼然民上。
entries.en: Vice Minister Wang Yan submitted a forceful memorial: "Country simpletons who pay once suddenly stand above the people they govern.
entries.literal: Vice Minister Wang Yan submitted a forceful memorial saying: "Village simpletons, once they contribute funds, suddenly stand above the people.

entries.zh: 或分一縣之符，或擁一道之節，不惟濫傷名器，抑且為累地方。
entries.en: Some hold a county seal, others wield a circuit's authority—this not only debases prestigious ranks but burdens the regions they govern.
entries.literal: Some hold a county's seal, others wield a circuit's authority—not only injuring prestigious titles excessively, but also becoming a burden on local regions.

entries.zh: 宜禁止，以塞僥倖之路，杜言利之門。」
entries.en: It should be forbidden, to block opportunism and shut the door to profiteering."
entries.literal: It is fitting to forbid this, to block the path of opportunism and shut the door to profit-seeking."

entries.zh: 帝韙之，為飭九卿再議。
entries.en: The emperor approved and ordered the Nine Ministers to reconsider.
entries.literal: The emperor approved this and ordered the Nine Ministers to deliberate again.

entries.zh: 青海用兵，饋餉不繼，內大臣議停各途守選及遷補，專用捐資助餉者。
entries.en: During the Qinghai campaign, when supplies ran short, inner ministers proposed suspending normal selection and transfers and relying solely on contributors to fund the army.
entries.literal: When Qinghai was at war and supplies did not keep up, inner ministers proposed halting selection and transfer along all routes and using only those who contributed funds to aid supplies.

entries.zh: 刑部尚書張廷樞言；
entries.en: Minister of Justice Zhang Tingshu said:
entries.literal: Minister of Justice Zhang Tingshu said:

entries.zh: 「惟捐納所分員缺可用捐員，正途及遷補者宜仍舊。」
entries.en: "Only posts reserved for purchased officials should use contributors; regular-route and transfer appointees should remain unchanged."
entries.literal: "Only the posts allotted to contribution appointees may use contributed officials; the regular route and transfer appointees should remain as before."

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: The proposal was adopted.
entries.literal: This was followed.

entries.zh: 官吏緣事罷譴，降革留任，非數年無過，不得開復。
entries.en: Officials dismissed, demoted, or dismissed-but-retained could not be restored without several years without fault.
entries.literal: Officials dismissed or punished for affairs, demoted or dismissed but retained, could not be restored without several years without fault.

entries.zh: 康熙間，大同賑飢，部議京察、大計罷黜者，悉予捐復。
entries.en: During the Kangxi era, for Datong famine relief, the ministry proposed granting restoration by purchase to all officials dismissed in capital and provincial evaluations.
entries.literal: During Kangxi, for Datong famine relief, the ministry deliberated granting contribution restoration to all dismissed in capital and provincial evaluations.

entries.zh: 徐元文力言不可。
entries.en: Xu Yuanwen strongly objected.
entries.literal: Xu Yuanwen strongly said this was impermissible.

entries.zh: 議遂寢。
entries.en: The proposal was shelved.
entries.literal: The deliberation was then shelved.

entries.zh: 三十三年，河道總督于成龍以黃、運兩河，工費繁鉅，請仿陝西賑飢例開捐，革職、年老、患疾、休致人員得捐復。
entries.en: In Kangxi 33, River Conservancy Governor Yu Chenglong, citing vast costs for Yellow River and Grand Canal works, requested purchase regulations modeled on Shaanxi famine relief, allowing dismissed, aged, ill, and retired officials to restore by purchase.
entries.literal: In the thirty-third year, River Conservancy Governor Yu Chenglong, because the Yellow and Grand Canal works costs were vast, requested opening contributions modeled on Shaanxi famine relief, permitting dismissed, aged, ill, and retired personnel to restore by contribution.

entries.zh: 帝面諭捐納稱貸者多，非朘削無以償逋負，事不可行。
entries.en: The emperor said in person that many purchased officials were in debt and could repay only by embezzlement—the proposal could not proceed.
entries.literal: The emperor said in person that many contributed officials were in debt; without embezzlement they could not repay arrears—the matter could not proceed.

entries.zh: 尚書薩穆哈等議成龍懷私妄奏，擬褫職，得旨從寬留任。
entries.en: Minister Samuha and others ruled Chenglong had acted from private motives and proposed stripping his office; an edict leniently retained him.
entries.literal: Minister Samuha and others deliberated that Chenglong had private motives in a reckless memorial and proposed stripping his office; an edict leniently retained him in post.

entries.zh: 乾隆九年，直賑捐，部議捐復條款，京察、大計及犯私罪者，降調人員，無論是否因公，及比照六法條例，武職軍政糾參及貪婪者，不準捐復。
entries.en: In Qianlong 9, for Zhili relief purchases, the ministry set restoration terms: officials dismissed in evaluations, private offenders, demoted personnel, and those compared to the six disciplinary statutes; military officials impeached in military evaluations and the greedy could not restore by purchase.
entries.literal: In the ninth year of Qianlong, for Zhili relief contributions, the ministry deliberated restoration terms: those dismissed in capital and provincial evaluations, private offenders, demoted personnel whether or not for public business, and by comparison to the six disciplinary statutes; military personnel impeached in military evaluations and the greedy were not permitted restoration by contribution.

entries.zh: 因公罣誤無餘罪，悉得捐復。
entries.en: Those faulted for public business without further crimes could all restore by purchase.
entries.literal: Those faulted for public business without further crime could all restore by contribution.

entries.zh: 三十五年，帝念降革留任人員，因公處分，輒停升轉，詔許捐復。
entries.en: In Qianlong 35, mindful that demoted-and-retained officials were often blocked from promotion for public-business punishments, the emperor decreed permitting restoration by purchase.
entries.literal: In the thirty-fifth year, the emperor, mindful that demoted-and-retained personnel were often halted in promotion for public-business punishments, decreed permitting restoration by contribution.

entries.zh: 三十九年，川運例增進士、舉人捐復原資例。
entries.en: In Qianlong 39, Sichuan transport regulations added restoration of original seniority for jinshi and juren.
entries.literal: In the thirty-ninth year, Sichuan transport regulations added jinshi and juren restoration of original seniority.

entries.zh: 四十八年，定革職、降調官，分段承修南運河工程捐復例。
entries.en: In Qianlong 48, dismissed and demoted officials were assigned sections of Southern Grand Canal works for restoration by purchase.
entries.literal: In the forty-eighth year, regulations were fixed for dismissed and demoted officials to undertake sections of the Southern Grand Canal works for restoration by contribution.

entries.zh: 嘉慶三年，川楚善後，推廣其例，凡常捐不準捐復人員，酌核情節，得酌加報捐。
entries.en: In Jiaqing 3, for Sichuan-Huguang pacification, the precedent was extended: normally ineligible officials could have circumstances weighed and make additional contributions.
entries.literal: In the third year of Jiaqing, for Sichuan-Huguang pacification, the precedent was extended: all normally ineligible for restoration could have circumstances weighed and report additional contributions as appropriate.

entries.zh: 奉旨，降革除犯六法外，因公情節尚輕人員，得加倍捐復。
entries.en: By imperial order, apart from those guilty under the six statutes, demoted officials whose public-business faults were minor could restore at double the standard rate.
entries.literal: By imperial order, apart from those guilty under the six statutes, demoted and dismissed personnel whose public-business circumstances were still light could restore at double contribution.

entries.zh: 大計劾參，有疾休致，調治就痊，及特旨降革留任限年開復人員，加十分之五捐復。
entries.en: Officials impeached in provincial evaluation, retired for illness and recovered, and those demoted-but-retained under special edict paid an additional fifty percent for restoration.
entries.literal: Those impeached in provincial evaluation, retired for illness and recovered, and those demoted-and-retained by special edict with fixed years for restoration, paid an additional fifty percent for restoration.

entries.zh: 十年，部臣疏請於常例捐復外，增文、武大員捐復革職留任例。
entries.en: In Jiaqing 10, ministry officials requested adding restoration for dismissed-but-retained senior civil and military officials beyond standing regulations.
entries.literal: In the tenth year, ministry officials memorialized requesting, beyond standing restoration, to add civil and military senior officials' restoration for dismissed-but-retained posts.

entries.zh: 帝曰：「大員身罣吏議應罷斥，經改革職留任，開復有一定年限。
entries.en: The emperor said: "Senior officials subject to censure should be dismissed; after demotion and retention, restoration has a fixed term.
entries.literal: The emperor said: "Senior officials subject to personnel censure should be dismissed; after demotion and retention in post, restoration has a fixed term.

entries.zh: 若甫罹重譴，即可捐復，此例一開，亳無畏忌。
entries.en: If they could restore by purchase immediately after heavy censure, once this precedent opened there would be no restraint whatsoever.
entries.literal: If they have just suffered heavy censure yet can immediately restore by contribution, once this precedent opens there will be no fear at all.

entries.zh: 有資者脫然為無過之人，無資者日久不能開復。
entries.en: The wealthy would instantly become blameless; the poor could not be restored even after long years.
entries.literal: Those with resources would suddenly become faultless; those without resources could not be restored even after long time.

entries.zh: 殊失政體。」
entries.en: This would grossly violate proper governance."
entries.literal: This greatly violates proper governance."

entries.zh: 不允行。
entries.en: The proposal was rejected.
entries.literal: It was not permitted.

entries.zh: 咸豐二年，王、大臣等議寬籌軍餉。
entries.en: In Xianfeng 2, princes and grand ministers deliberated expanded military fund-raising.
entries.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng, princes and grand ministers deliberated expanded military fund-raising.

entries.zh: 凡降革不準捐復人員，除實犯贓私外，餘准加倍半捐復。
entries.en: All normally ineligible demoted and dismissed officials, apart from actual embezzlement, were permitted restoration at one and a half times the rate.
entries.literal: All demoted and dismissed personnel normally ineligible for restoration, apart from actual embezzlement and private gain, were permitted restoration at one and a half times the rate.

entries.zh: 降革一、二品文、武官，向不在捐復之列者，許捐復原官頂帶，允行。
entries.en: First- and second-rank civil and military officials previously ineligible for restoration were permitted to restore their original rank insignia; this was approved.
entries.literal: First- and second-rank civil and military officials demoted and dismissed, who had never been in the restoration list, were permitted to restore original rank insignia; this was approved.

entries.zh: 但飭一、二品大員捐復原銜須請旨。
entries.en: But first- and second-rank officials restoring original rank required imperial approval.
entries.literal: But first- and second-rank senior officials restoring original rank had to request imperial approval.

entries.zh: 嗣復推廣，文職京察、大計六法，武職軍政被劾，無奸贓情罪，亦許捐復原銜。
entries.en: Later this was extended: civil officials under the six evaluation statutes and military officials impeached without corruption were also permitted to restore original rank by purchase.
entries.literal: Later this was extended again: civil officials under capital evaluation and provincial evaluation six statutes, and military officials impeached in military evaluation without corruption, were also permitted to restore original rank by contribution.

entries.zh: 終清世踵行，不復更也。
entries.en: This practice continued through the end of the Qing without further change.
entries.literal: Through the end of the Qing it was followed without further change.

entries.zh: 捐納官或非捐納官，於本班上輸資若干，俾班次較優，銓補加速，謂之花樣。
entries.en: Whether purchased officials or not, paying extra on one's quota to gain priority in selection and faster appointment was called a patterned contribution.
entries.literal: Contributed officials or non-contributed officials, paying a certain sum on their quota to make their quota rank higher and accelerate selection and appointment, was called patterned contribution.

entries.zh: 康熙十三年，知縣得納先用、即用班，工部侍郎田六善極言其弊，謂宜停止。
entries.en: In Kangxi 13, district magistrates could purchase prior-use and immediate-use quotas; Vice Minister of Works Tian Liushan forcefully denounced the abuse and urged stopping it.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year of Kangxi, district magistrates could purchase prior-use and immediate-use quotas; Vice Minister of Works Tian Liushan spoke forcefully of the abuses and said they should be stopped.

entries.zh: 三十三年，戶部議行輸送草豆例，台臣請增應升、先用捐。
entries.en: In Kangxi 33, the Ministry of Revenue implemented forage-transport regulations; censors requested adding promotion-eligible and prior-use purchase categories.
entries.literal: In the thirty-third year, the Ministry of Revenue deliberated implementing forage-transport regulations; censorial officials requested adding promotion-eligible and prior-use contributions.

entries.zh: 御史陸機言：「前此有納先用一例，正途為之壅滯。
entries.en: Censor Lu Ji said: "A prior-use purchase regulation had previously blocked the regular route.
entries.literal: Censor Lu Ji said: "Previously there was a prior-use purchase regulation, and the regular route was blocked thereby.

entries.zh: 皇上灼見其弊，久經停止。
entries.en: The emperor had clearly seen its harm and long since halted it.
entries.literal: The emperor clearly saw its abuses and had long since stopped it.

entries.zh: 納先用者，大都奔兢躁進。
entries.en: Prior-use purchasers were mostly eager and impatient climbers.
entries.literal: Those purchasing prior use were mostly eager and impatient for advancement.

entries.zh: 多一先用之人，即多一害民之人。
entries.en: Each additional prior-use appointee was one more official who would harm the people.
entries.literal: Each additional prior-use person was one more person who harmed the people.

entries.zh: 不待辨而知其不可。」
entries.en: No debate was needed to see it was impermissible."
entries.literal: Without debate one knows this is impermissible."

entries.zh: 乾隆年事例屢開，惟雙月、單月，不論雙月選用及雙月先用，不論雙、單月即用等尋常班次。
entries.en: During the Qianlong era regulations reopened repeatedly, but only for ordinary quota categories such as bi-monthly, monthly, regardless-of-bi-monthly selection, bi-monthly prior-use, and regardless-of-bi-monthly-or-monthly immediate-use.
entries.literal: In the Qianlong years regulations were opened repeatedly, but only ordinary quotas: bi-monthly, monthly, regardless-of-bi-monthly selection and bi-monthly prior-use, and regardless-of-bi-monthly-or-monthly immediate-use.

entries.zh: 蓋是時正途銓補，未病雍滯，無庸加捐花樣，納資者亦至是而止。
entries.en: At that time the regular route was not yet congested; patterned contributions were unnecessary, and contributors went no further.
entries.literal: For at that time regular-route selection was not yet congested; there was no need to add patterned contributions, and contributors stopped at that.

entries.zh: 七年，部議鼓勵江省賑捐，各班選用特優。
entries.en: In Qianlong 7, the ministry encouraged Jiangsu relief contributions with especially favorable selection priority.
entries.literal: In the seventh year, the ministry deliberated encouraging Jiangsu relief contributions with especially favorable selection across quotas.

entries.zh: 道光年，增插班間選、抽班間選、遇缺、遇缺前等名目。
entries.en: In the Daoguang era came inserted inter-quota selection, drawn inter-quota selection, vacancy appointment, and pre-vacancy categories.
entries.literal: In the Daoguang years were added inserted inter-quota selection, drawn inter-quota selection, vacancy appointment, and pre-vacancy categories.

entries.zh: 咸豐元年，省遇缺、遇缺前，而增分缺先、本班侭先。
entries.en: In Xianfeng 1, vacancy categories were trimmed while split-vacancy priority and full-quota priority were added.
entries.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng, vacancy and pre-vacancy categories were reduced, while split-vacancy priority and full-quota priority were added.

entries.zh: 三年，復增分缺間、不積班。
entries.en: In Xianfeng 3, split-vacancy inter-quota and non-accumulating quota categories were added.
entries.literal: In the third year, split-vacancy inter-quota and non-accumulating quota were added again.

entries.zh: 九年，先後奏設新班遇缺、新班侭先、分缺先前，分缺間前、本班侭先前、不論班侭遇缺選補等班。
entries.en: In Xianfeng 9, a succession of new quotas was established: new-quota vacancy, new-quota priority, split-vacancy pre-priority, split-vacancy inter-pre, full-quota pre-priority, and regardless-of-quota vacancy selection.
entries.literal: In the ninth year, new-quota vacancy, new-quota priority, split-vacancy pre-priority, split-vacancy inter-pre, full-quota pre-priority, and regardless-of-quota vacancy selection quotas were established in succession.

entries.zh: 推廣捐例，又有保舉捐入候補班、候補捐本班先用例。
entries.en: Extended regulations also added recommendation purchases into awaiting-appointment quotas and awaiting-appointment prior-use within one's quota.
entries.literal: Under extended regulations there were also recommendation contributions into awaiting-appointment quotas and awaiting-appointment contributions for prior use within one's quota.

entries.zh: 花樣繁多，至斯已極。
entries.en: Patterned contributions had multiplied to their utmost extreme.
entries.literal: Patterned contributions were numerous; by then they had reached their extreme.

entries.zh: 志八十七
entries.en: Treatise 87
entries.literal: Treatise Eighty-Seven

entries.zh: 二十四年，令各省稽察缺額攤派之弊，嚴行革除。
entries.en: In year 24 provinces were ordered to root out padded rolls and illegal levies.
entries.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, each province was ordered to investigate abuses of quota shortfalls and levies and strictly eliminate them.

entries.zh: 至操練之法，宜不拘成格，儘力變通，飭督辦軍務王大臣議之。
entries.en: Drill methods should break old patterns; the prince-minister in charge of military affairs was told to decide.
entries.literal: As for drill methods, they should not be bound by fixed patterns but strive to adapt flexibly; the prince-minister supervising military affairs was ordered to deliberate.

entries.zh: 尋以神機營、火器營、健銳營、武勝新隊，操演嫺熟，賞統兵大臣有差。
entries.en: Soon the Shenji, firearms, elite, and Martial Victory units drilled well and their commanders were rewarded.
entries.literal: Soon because the Shenji Camp, Firearms Brigade, Elite Sharp-shooters Brigade, and Martial Victory new corps drilled with proficiency, commanding grand ministers were rewarded in differing degrees.

entries.zh: 令滿、蒙、漢各軍驍騎營、兩翼前鋒、護軍營，五成改習洋操，五成改用洋槍，八旗漢軍砲隊營、藤牌營，一併改練，神機營汰弱留強，共練馬步兵萬人。
entries.en: Half of Manchu, Mongol, and Han vanguard and guards units took foreign drill and half foreign rifles; Han artillery and shield units retrained; the Shenji Camp cut the weak and trained ten thousand horse and foot.
entries.literal: Manchu, Mongol, and Chinese forces' vanguard cavalry, both wings' vanguard, and guards brigades were ordered: half to switch to foreign drill, half to switch to foreign muskets; Eight Banners Chinese-banner artillery and rattan-shield camps were all changed to new drill; the Shenji Camp eliminated the weak and kept the strong, together drilling ten thousand horse and foot.

entries.zh: 其陣法器械營制餉章，酌仿泰西兵制。
entries.en: Formations, arms, organization, and pay followed Western models in part.
entries.literal: Their formations, weapons, camp organization, and pay regulations were adapted in part from Western military systems.

entries.zh: 是年秋，上親詣團河及天津大閱新操。
entries.en: That autumn the emperor reviewed the new drill at Tuanhe and Tianjin in person.
entries.literal: That autumn the sovereign personally went to Tuanhe and Tianjin for a grand review of the new drill.

entries.zh: 又令各省增水師學堂學額，增造練船，習駕駛諸術。
entries.en: Provinces were also told to expand naval schools, build training ships, and teach navigation.
entries.literal: Each province was also ordered to increase naval academy enrollment, build more training ships, and practice navigation and related skills.

entries.zh: 二十五年，以北洋各軍訓練三年，飭統兵大臣取各種操法，繪圖貼說以聞。
entries.en: In year 25, after three years of Beiyang training, commanders were told to report every drill method with illustrated explanations.
entries.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, because Beiyang armies had trained three years, commanding grand ministers were ordered to take every drill method, draw diagrams with explanations attached, and report.

entries.zh: 步隊以起伏分合為主。
entries.en: Infantry stressed advancing, halting, and splitting and reforming.
entries.literal: Infantry focused chiefly on rising, falling, dividing, and combining.

entries.zh: 砲隊以攻堅挫銳為期。
entries.en: Artillery aimed at breaching works and breaking enemy strength.
entries.literal: Artillery aimed at storming fortifications and breaking sharp enemy forces.

entries.zh: 馬隊以出奇馳驟為能。
entries.en: Cavalry specialized in surprise and rapid charges.
entries.literal: Cavalry's skill lay in surprise raids and rapid charges.

entries.zh: 工程隊以擴地利、備軍資為事。
entries.en: Engineers worked terrain and supplies.
entries.literal: Engineers' work was to expand terrain advantage and prepare military supplies.

entries.zh: 以平時操練之法，備異日戰陣之需。
entries.en: Peacetime drill was meant to ready men for war.
entries.literal: Peacetime drill methods were to prepare for future battle needs.

entries.zh: 二十六年，鄧華熙於安徽省城設立武備學堂，習槍砲戰陣諸學。
entries.en: In year 26 Deng Huaxi opened a military academy in Anhui's capital for guns, artillery, and tactics.
entries.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, Deng Huaxi established a military academy in the Anhui provincial capital to study firearms, artillery, and battle formations.

entries.zh: 志一百十四
entries.en: Treatise 114
entries.literal: Treatise 114.

entries.zh: 順治十五年定軍馬，親王出征，馬四百匹，郡王三百，貝勒二百，貝子百五十，鎮國公百匹，輔國公八十，不入八分鎮國公七十，輔國公六十五，將軍八十，副將軍七十，護軍統領、前鋒統領、副都統皆六十，其下各有差，最少者護軍、領催各六匹。
entries.en: Shunzhi 15 (1658) fixed campaign horse allotments: princes 400, commandery princes 300, beile 200, beise 150, imperial dukes 100, second-rank dukes 80, and so on down the ranks to six horses each for guards and squad leaders.
entries.literal: In the fifteenth year of Shunzhi military horse quotas were fixed: a prince on campaign four hundred horses, a commandery prince three hundred, a beile two hundred, a beise one hundred fifty, a duke of the imperial clan one hundred, a second-rank duke eighty, a duke not in the eight privileges seventy, a second-rank duke sixty-five, a general eighty, a lieutenant general seventy, a guards commander, vanguard commander, and vice president of the banner each sixty, with graded reductions below, the minimum being six horses each for guards and squad leaders.

entries.zh: 康熙三十五年，敕出徵兵一人馬四匹，四人為伍，一伍主從騎八匹，馱器糧用具亦八匹。
entries.en: Kangxi 35 (1696) ordered four horses per campaign soldier; four men formed a squad with eight riding mounts and eight pack animals for gear and provisions.
entries.literal: In the thirty-fifth year of Kangxi an edict fixed that each soldier on campaign had four horses; four men formed a squad; one squad had eight riding horses for master and followers, and eight pack horses for equipment, grain, and utensils.

entries.zh: 是歲，征噶爾丹，以兵丁馬瘦，褫兵部尚書索諾和職。
entries.en: That year, during the Galdan campaign, emaciated troop horses cost War Minister Suo Nuohe his post.
entries.literal: That year, in the campaign against Galdan, because the troops' horses were thin, the minister of war Suo Nuohe was stripped of office.

entries.zh: 五十一年，覈定軍中職官馬數，大學士、尚書、左都御史十六匹，侍郎以下遞減，經略、大將軍各二十五匹，副將軍以下遞減。
entries.en: In Kangxi 51 (1712) official horse quotas were audited: grand secretaries and ministers received sixteen each, with graded reductions below; grand coordinators and commanders-in-chief received twenty-five.
entries.literal: In the fifty-first year the horse quotas for military officeholders were verified: grand secretaries, ministers, and the censor-in-chief sixteen horses each, vice ministers and below in descending grades, grand coordinators and commanders-in-chief twenty-five each, lieutenant generals and below in descending grades.

entries.zh: 乾隆十六年，八旗牧官馬二萬七千七百餘匹，以萬匹於都城外牧養，熱河千匹，各庄頭二千匹，餘者分畀直隸標營。
entries.en: Qianlong 16 (1751) the Eight Banners pastured 27,700-odd government horses: 10,000 outside the capital, 1,000 at Rehe, 2,000 with estate managers, and the rest assigned to Zhili garrisons.
entries.literal: In the sixteenth year of Qianlong the Eight Banners pastured twenty-seven thousand seven hundred-odd government horses; ten thousand were kept outside the capital, one thousand at Rehe, two thousand at various estate heads, and the remainder distributed to Zhili banner garrisons.

entries.zh: 圈馬之設，始乾隆二十八年，從都統舒赫德請也。
entries.en: Corral-horse herds date from Qianlong 28 (1763), at the request of banner commander Shuhede.
entries.literal: The establishment of corral horses began in the twenty-eighth year of Qianlong, following the request of the banner commander Shuhede.

entries.zh: 滿洲八旗，旗養馬二百匹。
entries.en: Each Manchu banner pastured 200 corral horses.
entries.literal: For the Manchu Eight Banners, each banner pastured two hundred horses.

entries.zh: 蒙古八旗，旗百匹。
entries.en: Each Mongol banner pastured 100.
entries.literal: For the Mongol Eight Banners, each banner one hundred.

entries.zh: 洎五十九年撤圈，分給各兵拴養。
entries.en: By Qianlong 59 (1794) the corrals were dissolved and horses issued for soldiers to keep individually.
entries.literal: By the fifty-ninth year the corrals were abolished and the horses distributed for individual soldiers to tether and raise.

entries.zh: 嘉慶十二年，諭成親王永星議復圈馬，大學士戴衢亨等會議，立章程十條，圈馬仍舊。
entries.en: Jiaqing 12 (1807) the throne ordered Prince Cheng Yongxing to study restoring corral herds; Grand Secretary Dai Yuheng's conference produced ten regulations and reinstated the old system.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year of Jiaqing the emperor ordered Prince Cheng Yongxing to discuss restoring corral horses; Grand Secretary Dai Yuheng and others met in conference, established ten articles of regulation, and corral horses were restored as before.

entries.zh: 道光末，軍興遂廢，後亦不復籌矣。
entries.en: Late in Daoguang, war ended the practice for good and it was never revived.
entries.literal: At the end of Daoguang, with warfare arising, it was abandoned, and afterward was never revived.

entries.zh: 同治元年諭曰：「馬政廢弛，積弊已深，以致軍馬罷瘠。
entries.en: Tongzhi 1 (1862) brought an edict: "Horse administration has decayed; abuses run so deep that army mounts are spent and thin.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi an edict stated: "Horse administration has fallen into neglect; long-standing abuses run deep, so that military horses are exhausted and emaciated.

entries.zh: 牧廠大臣等應妥實整頓，差功罪以挽頹風，著為令。」
entries.en: Pasture officials must set things right, rewarding merit and punishing fault to reverse the decline—let this stand as permanent law."
entries.literal: Pasture ministers and the like should thoroughly rectify matters, distinguishing merit and fault to reverse the declining trend, and this is to be established as regulation."

entries.zh: 溯自世祖入關，迄於康、乾之際，盛京、吉林、黑龍江、直隸、江南、浙江、廣東、福建、湖北、四川、陝、甘、山東、山西諸省設駐防滿洲營，馬凡十萬六千四百餘匹，惟福建水師駐防僅數十匹。
entries.en: From Shizu's entry through the Pass down to the Kangxi and Qianlong era, Manchu garrison camps were established in Shengjing, Jilin, Heilongjiang, Zhili, Jiangnan, Zhejiang, Guangdong, Fujian, Hubei, Sichuan, Shaanxi-Gansu, Shandong, and Shanxi, with 106,400-odd horses in all; only the Fujian naval garrison had just several dozen.
entries.literal: Tracing from when the founding emperor entered the Pass down to the Kangxi and Qianlong era, garrison Manchu camps were established in Mukden, Jilin, Heilongjiang, Zhili, Jiangnan, Zhejiang, Guangdong, Fujian, Hubei, Sichuan, Shaanxi-Gansu, Shandong, and Shanxi, with horses totaling one hundred six thousand four hundred-odd; only the Fujian naval garrison had several tens.

entries.zh: 乾隆季年，定西藏兵制，前藏供差營馬六十匹，後藏二十匹，舊塘四十三，共塘馬二百二十匹，新設番塘二十四，共番馬九十八匹。
entries.en: Late in Qianlong, Tibet's military horse quotas were set: 60 for front Tibet, 20 for rear Tibet, 220 for 43 old courier stations, and 98 for 24 new Tibetan stations.
entries.literal: In the late Qianlong years Tibet's military establishment was fixed: front Tibet duty horses sixty, rear Tibet twenty, old courier stations forty-three totaling two hundred twenty station horses, newly established Tibetan stations twenty-four totaling ninety-eight Tibetan horses.

entries.zh: 黑龍江兵向無額馬，道光十六年，從哈豐阿請，始設置之。
entries.en: Heilongjiang troops had no allotted horses until Daoguang 16 (1836), when Hafeng'a's memorial led to their establishment.
entries.literal: Heilongjiang troops had never had allotted horses; in the sixteenth year of Daoguang, following Hafeng'a's request, they were first established.

entries.zh: 志一百十六
entries.en: Treatise 116
entries.literal: Treatise one hundred sixteen.

entries.zh: 有清起自遼左，不三四十年混一區宇。
entries.en: The Qing arose in eastern Liao; within three or four decades they unified the realm.
entries.literal: The Qing arose from the eastern Liao region; in barely three or four decades they unified the realm.

entries.zh: 聖祖沖年踐阼，與天下休養，六十餘稔，寬恤之詔，歲不絕書。
entries.en: The Sacred Ancestor came to the throne in his youth and gave the realm its repose; for more than sixty years, edicts of clemency and relief were issued without cease.
entries.literal: The Sacred Ancestor ascended the throne in his minority and rested the realm in peace with All-under-Heaven; for more than sixty years, edicts of clemency and relief were issued without cease year after year.

entries.zh: 高宗運際昌明，一代法制，多所裁定。
entries.en: When Gaozong's reign coincided with a flourishing age, many of the legal institutions of that generation were definitively settled.
entries.literal: When Gaozong's fortune coincided with a glorious age, the legal institutions of that generation were largely settled.

entries.zh: 仁宗以降，事多因循，未遑改作。
entries.en: From Renzong onward, affairs were largely left to inertia, without time to undertake reform.
entries.literal: From Renzong onward, affairs were largely pursued by inertia, without leisure to reform.

entries.zh: 綜其終始，列朝刑政，雖不盡清明，然如明代之廠衛、廷杖，專意戮辱士大夫，無有也。
entries.en: Taken as a whole from beginning to end, the penal administration of successive reigns was not wholly lucid, yet nothing like the Ming practice of the Factory Guards and court beating, devoted to humiliating and killing scholar-officials, ever appeared.
entries.literal: Taking their course from beginning to end, the penal administration of successive reigns, though not entirely lucid and clear, yet such things as the Ming dynasty's Factory Guards and court beating, devoted to humiliating and killing scholar-officials, did not exist.

entries.zh: 治獄者雖不盡仁恕，然如漢、唐之張湯、趙禹、周興、來俊臣輩，深文慘刻，無有也。
entries.en: Those who ran the prisons were not always humane, yet there were none like Zhang Tang and Zhao Yu of Han or Zhou Xing and Lai Junchen of Tang, who twisted the law into cruel severity.
entries.literal: Those who administered prisons were not entirely humane and forgiving, yet such men as Zhang Tang and Zhao Yu of Han and Zhou Xing and Lai Junchen of Tang, who twisted the law cruelly and severally—none such existed.

entries.zh: 德宗末葉，庚子拳匪之變，創巨痛深，朝野上下，爭言變法，於是新律萌芽。
entries.en: In Dezong's final years, after the catastrophe of the 1900 Boxer uprising, with wounds still fresh and pain still deep, court and country alike clamored for reform, and the new penal code began to take shape.
entries.literal: In the closing years of Dezong, at the upheaval of the Boxer year 1900, with wounds fresh and pain deep, court and country alike clamored for reform, and thus the new penal code began to sprout.

entries.zh: 迨宣統遜位，而中國數千年相傳之刑典俱廢。
entries.en: When Xuantong abdicated, the penal codes that China had transmitted for thousands of years were all abolished.
entries.literal: By the time Xuantong abdicated, the penal codes handed down in China for thousands of years were all abolished.

entries.zh: 是故論有清一代之刑法，亦古今絕續之交也。
entries.en: Thus in treating Qing penal law as a whole, one stands at the very juncture where ancient and modern legal continuity was severed.
entries.literal: Therefore in discussing Qing dynasty penal law as a whole, it stands also at the juncture where ancient and modern continuity was severed.

entries.zh: 爰備志之，俾後有考焉。
entries.en: Accordingly it is set down here in full, that posterity may have material for study.
entries.literal: Accordingly this is recorded in full in the treatise, that posterity may have material for inquiry.

entries.zh: 又國初以來，凡纂修律例，類必欽命二三大臣為總裁，特開專館。
entries.en: Moreover, from the founding of the state, whenever the code and precedents were compiled and revised, two or three great ministers were invariably appointed by imperial command as chief compilers, and a special office was opened.
entries.literal: Moreover, from the founding of the state, whenever code and precedents were compiled and revised, two or three great ministers were invariably appointed by imperial command as chief compilers, and a special office was opened.

entries.zh: 維時各部院則例陸續成書，苟與刑律相涉，館員俱一一釐正，故鮮乖牾。
entries.en: At that time the precedents of the various ministries and courts were completed one after another; whenever they touched on penal statutes, the office members corrected them one by one, so conflicts were rare.
entries.literal: At that time the precedents of the various ministries and courts were completed one after another; if they touched on penal statutes, the office members all corrected them one by one, so there was rarely conflict.

entries.zh: 自乾隆元年，刑部奏准三年修例一次。
entries.en: From Qianlong 1 the Ministry of Punishments obtained approval to revise precedents once every three years.
entries.literal: From the first year of Qianlong the Ministry of Punishments memorialized approval to revise precedents once every three years.

entries.zh: 十一年，內閣等衙門議改五年一修。
entries.en: In the eleventh year the Inner Court and other offices deliberated changing this to revision once every five years.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year the Inner Court and other offices deliberated changing this to revision once every five years.

entries.zh: 由是刑部專司其事，不復簡派總裁，律例館亦遂附屬於刑曹，與他部往往不相關會。
entries.en: Thereupon the Ministry of Punishments took exclusive charge of the matter; chief compilers were no longer specially appointed, and the Code and Precedents Office was attached to the penal bureaucracy, often without coordination with other ministries.
entries.literal: Thereupon the Ministry of Punishments took exclusive charge of the matter; chief compilers were no longer specially appointed, and the Code and Precedents Office was thus attached to the penal bureaucracy, often without coordination with other ministries.

entries.zh: 高宗臨御六十年，性矜明察，每閱讞牘，必求其情罪曲當，以萬變不齊之情，欲御以萬變不齊之例。
entries.en: The Qianlong Emperor reigned for sixty years. By nature meticulous and keenly discerning, he scrutinized every criminal case that came before him, insisting that the facts and the sentence fit together justly. He sought to meet the infinite variety of human circumstances with an equally varied body of legal precedent.
entries.literal: The High Emperor reigned for sixty years. By nature he was proud and keenly perceptive. Whenever he reviewed criminal dossiers, he always sought whether the facts and the punishment were properly matched. He wished to govern circumstances that varied in ten thousand ways with precedents that likewise varied in ten thousand ways.

entries.zh: 故乾隆一朝纂修八九次，刪原例、增例諸名目，而改變舊例及因案增設者為獨多。
entries.en: During the Qianlong reign the code was therefore compiled and revised eight or nine times. Revisions took many forms—deleting original precedents, adding new ones, altering old rules, and creating precedents in response to individual cases—but changes to existing precedents and case-driven additions were by far the most common.
entries.literal: Therefore, in the Qianlong reign the code was compiled and revised eight or nine times. Under such headings as deleted original precedents and added precedents, changes to old precedents and precedents added because of cases were especially numerous.

entries.zh: 嘉慶以降，按期開館，沿道光、咸豐以迄同治，而條例乃增至一千八百九十有二。
entries.en: From the Jiaqing reign onward, compilation offices opened at regular intervals, continuing through Daoguang and Xianfeng into Tongzhi, until the body of precedents swelled to 1,892 articles.
entries.literal: From the Jiaqing reign onward, offices were opened on schedule, continuing through Daoguang and Xianfeng down to Tongzhi, and the articles of precedent eventually increased to one thousand eight hundred and ninety-two.

entries.zh: 蓋清代定例，一如宋時之編敕，有例不用律，律既多成虛文，而例遂愈滋繁碎。
entries.en: In essence, the Qing practice of codifying precedent resembled the Song dynasty's compilation of edicts: when a precedent applied, the statute did not. As the statutes themselves largely became dead letter, precedent grew ever more fragmented and prolix.
entries.literal: In general, the Qing establishment of precedents was just like the Song compilation of edicts: where precedents existed, the statutes were not used. Since the statutes largely became empty words on paper, the precedents grew ever more fragmented and numerous.

entries.zh: 其間前後牴觸，或律外加重，或因例破律，或一事設一例，或一省一地方專一例，甚且因此例而生彼例，不惟與他部則例參差，即一例分載各門者，亦不無歧異。
entries.en: These provisions often contradicted one another. Some imposed penalties harsher than the statutes allowed; others overrode the statutes entirely through precedent. A single case might spawn its own rule; a single province or locality might receive a rule of its own. One precedent might even beget another. The result was inconsistency not only with regulations in other ministries, but also internal disagreement when the same precedent was recorded under different sections of the code.
entries.literal: Among them, some contradicted one another from beginning to end; some imposed penalties beyond what the statutes allowed; some broke the statutes through precedent; some established one precedent for one matter, or one special precedent for one province or one locality; some even gave rise to one precedent from another. Not only did they fail to align with the regulations of other ministries—even when a single precedent was divided and recorded under different sections, discrepancies were not lacking.

entries.zh: 展轉糾紛，易滋高下。
entries.en: Disputes multiplied and entangled with one another, making arbitrary and uneven enforcement all too easy.
entries.literal: As disputes wound on and on, unevenness in application was easily bred.

entries.zh: 雍正十三年，世宗遺詔有曰：「國家刑罰禁令之設，所以詰奸除暴，懲貪黜邪，以端風俗，以肅官方者也。
entries.en: In the thirteenth year of Yongzheng, the Yongzheng Emperor's deathbed edict declared: "The state establishes punishments and prohibitions to root out wickedness and violence, punish greed and drive out corruption, rectify public morals, and keep officialdom in order.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year of Yongzheng, the late Emperor Shizong's testamentary edict stated: "The establishment of the state's punishments, prohibitions, and bans is meant to interrogate the wicked and eliminate violence, punish greed and dismiss the corrupt, to rectify customs and to awe officialdom.

entries.zh: 然寬嚴之用，又必因乎其時。
entries.en: Yet whether to apply the law leniently or severely must always depend on the times.
entries.literal: Yet the application of leniency and severity must also accord with the times.

entries.zh: 從前朕見人情淺薄，官吏營私，相習成風，罔知省改，不得不懲治整理，以戒將來。
entries.en: In the past I saw that public morals had grown shallow, that officials pursued private gain until corruption had become habit, and that none knew how to restrain themselves or reform. I had no choice but to punish and set things in order, so as to warn those who would come after.
entries.literal: Previously I saw that human sentiment was shallow and base, that officials pursued private gain until it became custom, knowing no restraint or reform. I had no choice but to punish and rectify, to warn the future.

entries.zh: 今人心共知警惕矣，凡各衙門條例，有前嚴而改寬者，此乃從前部臣定議未協，朕與廷臣悉心酌核而後更定，自可垂諸永久。
entries.en: Now everyone knows to be on guard. Where regulations in the various yamens were once strict and have been relaxed, this is because the ministries' earlier deliberations had not been sound. After the court ministers and I examined them carefully and revised them, such changes may stand permanently.
entries.literal: Now all hearts alike know to be on guard. Among the regulations of each yamen, those that were formerly strict and were changed to lenient—this was because the previous deliberations of ministerial officials were not harmonious. After I and the court ministers carefully weighed and revised them, they can naturally endure forever.

entries.zh: 若前寬而改嚴者，此乃整飭人心風俗之計，原欲暫行於一時，俟諸弊革除，仍可酌復舊章，此朕本意也。
entries.en: Where rules once lenient were made strict, that was a measure to discipline public morals and reform custom, originally meant to be temporary. Once the abuses had been removed, the old regulations could be restored as appropriate. That was my original intent.
entries.literal: If those formerly lenient were changed to strict—this was a plan to discipline the hearts of the people and correct customs, originally intended to be applied temporarily for a time. Once the various abuses were eliminated, the old regulations could still be restored at discretion. This was my original intent.

entries.zh: 向後遇事斟酌，如有應從舊例者，仍照舊例行。」
entries.en: Henceforth, when cases arise, weigh each matter on its merits. Where the old precedents should apply, follow the old precedents.'
entries.literal: Going forward, when matters arise, deliberate as needed. If old precedents should be followed, still act according to the old precedents.'

entries.zh: 惜後世議法諸臣，未盡明世輕世重之故，每屆修例，第將歷奉諭旨及議准臣工條奏節次編入，從未統合全書，逐條釐正。
entries.en: Alas, the ministers who debated law in later generations never fully grasped why penalties should be lighter in one age and heavier in another. At each revision they merely appended, in chronological order, the edicts previously received and the memorials approved by the bureaucracy. They never consolidated the whole corpus and corrected it provision by provision.
entries.literal: Alas, the ministers who deliberated on law in later generations did not fully understand the reasons for lighter penalties in one age and heavier penalties in another. Each time precedents were revised, they merely compiled in sequence the imperial edicts received over time and the memorials submitted and approved by officials, never synthesizing the entire book and correcting it article by article.

entries.zh: 穆宗號稱中興，母后柄政，削平發、捻、回疆之亂，百端待理，尚於同治九年纂修一次。
entries.en: Emperor Tongzhi was hailed as restoring the dynasty. With the Empress Dowager holding power and the Taiping, Nian, and Muslim frontier rebellions newly suppressed, the court faced a hundred pressing tasks—yet in the ninth year of Tongzhi it still undertook one full revision of the code.
entries.literal: Emperor Muzong was hailed as restoring the dynasty. The Empress Dowager held power. The Taiping, Nian, and Muslim frontier rebellions were suppressed. Though a hundred matters awaited attention, still in the ninth year of Tongzhi the code was compiled and revised once.

entries.zh: 德宗幼沖繼統，未遑興作。
entries.en: The Guangxu Emperor succeeded the throne while still a child and had no opportunity to launch such projects.
entries.literal: Emperor Dezong succeeded the throne while still young and had no leisure for such undertakings.

entries.zh: 兼之時勢多故，章程叢積，刑部既憚其繁猥，不敢議修，群臣亦未有言及者，因循久之。
entries.en: The times were also unsettled, and regulations accumulated in overwhelming numbers. The Board of Punishments, intimidated by the sheer bulk and complexity of the material, dared not propose a revision, and no minister raised the matter. Inertia therefore persisted for years.
entries.literal: Moreover the times were troubled, regulations piled up in profusion. The Board of Punishments already feared their tedium and complexity and dared not propose revision, and no minister spoke of it either. Thus delay went on for a long time.

entries.zh: 逮光緒二十六年，聯軍入京，兩宮西狩。
entries.en: By the twenty-sixth year of Guangxu, the allied armies entered Beijing and the two sovereigns fled west.
entries.literal: By the twenty-sixth year of Guangxu, the allied armies entered the capital and both sovereigns fled west.

entries.zh: 憂時之士，咸謂非取法歐、美，不足以圖強。
entries.en: Men anxious for the fate of the realm agreed that China could not become strong unless it learned from Europe and America.
entries.literal: Men concerned for the times all said that unless they took Europe and America as models, it would not suffice to pursue national strength.

entries.zh: 於是條陳時事者，頗稍稍議及刑律。
entries.en: Memorialists on current affairs then began, little by little, to touch upon criminal law as well.
entries.literal: Thereupon those who memorialized on current affairs began, little by little, to discuss criminal law as well.

entries.zh: 二十八年，直隸總督袁世凱、兩江總督劉坤一、湖廣總督張之洞，會保刑部左侍郎沈家本、出使美國大臣伍廷芳修訂法律，兼取中西。
entries.en: In the twenty-eighth year, Viceroy Yuan Shikai of Zhili, Viceroy Liu Kunyi of Liangjiang, and Viceroy Zhang Zhidong of Huguang jointly recommended Left Vice Minister of Punishments Shen Jiaben and Minister to the United States Wu Tingfang to revise the laws, combining Chinese and Western approaches.
