entries.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, the Viceroy of Zhili Yuan Shikai, the Viceroy of Liangjiang Liu Kunyi, and the Viceroy of Huguang Zhang Zhidong jointly recommended the Left Vice Minister of Punishments Shen Jiaben and the Minister Plenipotentiary to the United States Wu Tingfang to revise the laws, drawing on both Chinese and Western sources.

entries.zh: 旨如所請，並諭將一切現行律例，按照通商交涉情形，參酌各國法律，妥為擬議，務期中外通行，有裨治理。
entries.en: The throne approved the request and further ordered that all current statutes and precedents be reconsidered in light of treaty and commercial relations, with reference to foreign legal systems, and carefully redrafted so that the law might serve both domestic and international needs and strengthen governance.
entries.literal: An edict approved the request and further instructed that all current statutes and precedents be, in accordance with commercial and diplomatic circumstances, deliberated upon with reference to the laws of various countries, properly drafted, with the aim that they would prevail both within and without China and benefit governance.

entries.zh: 自此而議律者，乃群措意於領事裁判權。
entries.en: From this time onward, those debating legal reform focused above all on consular jurisdiction.
entries.literal: From this point those who discussed law collectively turned their attention to consular jurisdiction.

entries.zh: 世祖順治元年，攝政睿親王入關定亂，六月，即令問刑衙門准依明律治罪。
entries.en: In Shunzhi 1, while the regent Prince Rui was entering the passes to quell disorder, in the sixth month he ordered the judicial yamen to adjudicate crimes according to the Ming Code.
entries.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi under Shizu, the regent Prince Rui entered the passes to settle disorder; in the sixth month he at once ordered the judicial yamen to adjudicate crimes according to the Ming Code.

entries.zh: 八月，刑科給事中孫襄陳刑法四事，一曰定刑書：「刑之有律，猶物之有規矩準繩也。
entries.en: In the eighth month, Criminal Affairs supervising secretary Sun Xiang submitted four proposals on penal law. The first was to fix the penal code: "Law in penal matters is to things what compass and square are to measurement.
entries.literal: In the eighth month, Criminal Affairs supervising secretary Sun Xiang submitted four matters on penal law, the first being to fix the penal text: "To have law in penal matters is like having compass and square for things.

entries.zh: 今法司所遵及故明律令，科條繁簡，情法輕重，當稽往憲，合時宜，斟酌損益，刊定成書，布告中外，俾知畫一遵守，庶奸慝不形，風俗移易。」
entries.en: The statutes now followed by the judicial offices and the former Ming codes vary in complexity and in how circumstance and law weigh light or heavy. These should be checked against past statutes, fitted to present needs, carefully revised, engraved as a fixed book, and promulgated at home and abroad so that all may observe a single standard; then wickedness may not take shape and customs may change for the better."
entries.literal: The statutes now followed by the judicial offices and the old Ming codes and ordinances—whether articles are numerous or few, whether circumstances and law are light or heavy—should be examined against past statutes, fitted to present needs, weighed for addition and subtraction, engraved and fixed as a book, promulgated within and without, so that all may know and uniformly observe; then wickedness may not take form and customs may change."

entries.zh: 疏上，攝政王諭令法司會同廷臣詳繹明律，參酌時宜，集議允當，以便裁定成書，頒行天下。
entries.en: When the memorial was submitted, the regent ordered the judicial offices, together with court ministers, to expound the Ming Code in detail, weigh present needs, deliberate until agreement was reached, and then fix the code as a book to be promulgated throughout the realm.
entries.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the regent ordered the judicial offices together with court ministers to expound the Ming Code in detail, weigh present needs, assemble discussion until satisfactory, and thereby fix and promulgate the book throughout the realm.

entries.zh: 十月，世祖入京，即皇帝位。
entries.en: In the tenth month Shizu entered the capital and assumed the throne.
entries.literal: In the tenth month Shizu entered the capital and at once assumed the imperial throne.

entries.zh: 刑部左侍郎黨崇雅奏，在外官吏，乘茲新制未定，不無憑臆舞文之弊。
entries.en: Left vice minister of the Ministry of Punishments Dang Chongya memorialized that local officials, taking advantage of the unsettled new system, were not above twisting the law to suit their whims.
entries.literal: Left vice minister of the Ministry of Punishments Dang Chongya memorialized that local officials, taking advantage of the fact that the new system was not yet fixed, were not without the abuse of twisting the text according to whim.

entries.zh: 並乞暫用明律，候國制畫一，永垂令甲。
entries.en: He also asked that the Ming Code be used temporarily until the national system was unified and could be handed down as permanent law.
entries.literal: He also requested that the Ming Code be used temporarily, until the national system was unified and might be handed down forever as binding ordinance.

entries.zh: 得旨：「在外仍照明律行，如有恣意輕重等弊，指參重處。」
entries.en: The rescript read: "Outside the capital, continue to follow the Ming Code. If officials arbitrarily vary punishments in severity, report them for severe punishment."
entries.literal: An imperial rescript was received: "Outside the capital, continue to act according to the Ming Code; if there are abuses such as arbitrary lightness or heaviness, report and refer for severe punishment."

entries.zh: 二年，命修律官參稽滿、漢條例，分輕重等差，從刑科都給事中李士焜請也。
entries.en: In the second year he ordered the code-revising officials to examine Manchu and Han regulations and distinguish grades of severity, following a request from Criminal Affairs chief supervising secretary Li Shikun.
entries.literal: In the second year he ordered the officials revising the code to examine Manchu and Han regulations and distinguish grades of lightness and heaviness, following the request of Criminal Affairs chief supervising secretary Li Shikun.

entries.zh: 三年五月，大清律成，世祖御制序文曰：「朕惟太祖、太宗創業東方，民淳法簡，大辟之外，惟有鞭笞。
entries.en: In the fifth month of the third year the Great Qing Code was completed. Shizu wrote a preface in his own hand: "I reflect that Taizu and Taizong founded the enterprise in the east, where the people were simple and the law was spare—apart from capital punishment there was only flogging.
entries.literal: In the fifth month of the third year the Great Qing Code was completed; Shizu composed a preface in his own hand, saying: "I consider that Taizu and Taizong founded the enterprise in the east; the people were simple and the law was spare—apart from capital punishment there was only flogging.

entries.zh: 朕仰荷天休，撫臨中夏，人民既眾，情偽多端。
entries.en: I, bearing Heaven's favor, now rule central China; the people are numerous, and truth and falsehood take many forms.
entries.literal: I, bearing Heaven's favor, rule over central China; the people are already numerous, and truth and falsehood take many forms.

entries.zh: 每遇奏讞，輕重出入，頗煩擬議。
entries.en: Whenever cases came up for judgment, punishments varied inconsistently in severity, and deliberation became burdensome.
entries.literal: Whenever cases were reported for judgment, lightness and heaviness varied, and deliberation was quite troublesome.

entries.zh: 律例未定，有司無所稟承。
entries.en: With statutes and precedents still unfixed, officials had no authority to follow.
entries.literal: With statutes and precedents unfixed, the responsible officials had nothing to receive and follow.

entries.zh: 爰敕法司官廣集廷議，詳譯明律，參以國制，增損劑量，期於平允。
entries.en: Therefore I charged the judicial offices to gather broad court discussion, translate the Ming Code in detail, consult our national institutions, revise it with care, and aim at fairness.
entries.literal: Therefore I charged the judicial officials to gather broad court discussion, translate the Ming Code in detail, consult the national system, add and subtract and measure, aiming at fairness.

entries.zh: 書成奏進，朕再三覆閱，仍命內院諸臣校訂妥確，乃允刊布，名曰大清律集解附例。
entries.en: When the book was completed and submitted, I reviewed it repeatedly, ordered the Inner Court ministers to collate it until correct, and then authorized its publication under the title Great Qing Code with Collected Exegesis and Attached Precedents.
entries.literal: When the book was completed and submitted, I reviewed it again and again, still ordered the Inner Court ministers to collate it until correct, and then permitted its engraving and promulgation, naming it the Great Qing Code with Collected Exegesis and Attached Precedents.

entries.zh: 爾內外有司官吏，敬此成憲，勿得任意低昂，務使百官萬民，畏名義而重犯法，冀幾刑措之風，以昭我祖宗好生之德。
entries.en: You officials at court and in the provinces, revere this established code; do not arbitrarily raise or lower punishments. See that officials and common people alike fear disgrace and hold the law in awe, so that punishments may fall into disuse and our ancestors' virtue of cherishing life may be made manifest.
entries.literal: You officials within and without, revere this established statute; do not arbitrarily raise or lower punishments. Endeavor to make the hundred officials and ten thousand people fear reputation and right conduct and regard violation of law as weighty, hoping for the wind of punishments set aside, to display our ancestors' virtue of cherishing life.

entries.zh: 子孫臣民，其世世守之。」
entries.en: Descendants and subjects, guard it generation after generation."
entries.literal: Descendants and subjects, guard it generation after generation."

entries.zh: 十三年，復頒滿文大清律。
entries.en: In the thirteenth year the Great Qing Code in Manchu was promulgated again.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year the Great Qing Code in Manchu was again promulgated.

entries.zh: 雍正元年，巡視東城御史湯之旭奏：「律例最關緊要，今六部見行則例，或有從重改輕，從輕擬重，有先行而今停，事同而法異者，未經畫一。
entries.en: In Yongzheng 1, Eastern Metropolitan censor Tang Zhixu memorialized: "The code and precedents are matters of the utmost importance. The currently enforced precedents of the Six Ministries sometimes change severity to leniency or leniency to severity; some were once enforced and are now suspended; the facts are the same but the law differs—they have not been unified.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng, Eastern Metropolitan censor Tang Zhixu memorialized: "Code and precedents are matters of the utmost importance. The currently enforced precedents of the Six Ministries sometimes change severity to leniency or leniency to severity; some were enforced before and are stopped now; the facts are the same but the law differs—they have not been unified.

entries.zh: 乞簡諳練律例大臣，專掌律例館總裁，將康熙六十一年以前之例並大清會典，逐條互訂，庶免參差。」
entries.en: I ask that a minister skilled in code and precedents be selected to serve exclusively as chief compiler of the Code and Precedents Office, and that precedents before Kangxi 61 together with the Great Qing Statutes be checked article by article against one another, so that discrepancies may be avoided."
entries.literal: I beg that a minister skilled in code and precedents be selected to take exclusive charge as chief compiler of the Code and Precedents Office, and that precedents before the sixty-first year of Kangxi together with the Great Qing Statutes be checked article by article against one another, so that discrepancies may be avoided."

entries.zh: 世宗允之，命大學士硃軾等為總裁，諭令於應增應減之處，再行詳加分晰，作速修完。
entries.en: The Shizong approved, appointed Grand Secretary Zhu Shi and others as chief compilers, and instructed that where additions and subtractions were needed they should be analyzed in detail and the revision completed swiftly.
entries.literal: The Shizong approved, appointed Grand Secretary Zhu Shi and others as chief compilers, and instructed that where additions and subtractions were needed they should again be analyzed in detail and the revision completed swiftly.

entries.zh: 三年書成，五年頒布。
entries.en: The book was completed in the third year and promulgated in the fifth.
entries.literal: In the third year the book was completed; in the fifth year it was promulgated.

entries.zh: 蓋明律以名例居首，其次則分隸於六部，合計三十門，都凡四百六十條。
entries.en: The Ming Code placed General Principles first; the statutes were then distributed under the Six Ministries, totaling thirty sections and four hundred sixty articles in all.
entries.literal: The Ming Code placed General Principles first; next the statutes were distributed under the Six Ministries, totaling thirty sections and four hundred sixty articles in all.

entries.zh: 順治初，釐定律書，將公式門之信牌移入職制，漏泄軍情移入軍政，於公式門刪漏用鈔印，於倉庫門刪鈔法，於詐偽門刪偽造寶鈔。
entries.en: At the beginning of Shunzhi, when the law book was put in order, the section on credentials was moved from Administrative Forms to Official Regulations, and leaking military intelligence was moved into Military Administration; from Administrative Forms the article on omitting stamped documents was deleted, from Granaries the article on paper money was deleted, and from Fraud the article on forging treasure notes was deleted.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Shunzhi, when the law book was put in order, the section on credentials from the Administrative Forms chapter was moved into Official Regulations; leaking military intelligence was moved into Military Administration; from Administrative Forms the article on omitting to use stamped documents was deleted; from the Granaries chapter the article on paper money was deleted; from the Fraud chapter the article on forging treasure notes was deleted.

entries.zh: 後又於名例增入邊遠充軍一條。
entries.en: Later one article on military exile to remote regions was added to General Principles.
entries.literal: Later one article on military exile to remote regions was added to General Principles.

entries.zh: 雍正三年之律，其刪除者：名例律之吏卒犯死罪、殺害軍人、在京犯罪軍民共三條，職制門選用軍職、官吏給由二條，婚姻門之蒙古、色目人婚姻一條，宮衛門之懸帶關防牌面一條。
entries.en: In the Yongzheng 3 code, the following were deleted: from General Principles three articles on clerks and runners guilty of capital crimes, killing soldiers, and military and civilian offenders in the capital; from Official Regulations two articles on selecting military posts and officials receiving credentials; from Marriage one article on Mongol and Semu marriages; and from Palace Guard one article on wearing pass tokens and seals.
entries.literal: In the code of Yongzheng 3, what was deleted: from General Principles the three articles on clerks and runners guilty of capital crimes, killing soldiers, and military and civilian offenders in the capital; from Official Regulations the two articles on selecting military posts and officials receiving credentials; from Marriage the one article on Mongol and Semu marriages; from Palace Guard the one article on wearing pass tokens and seals.

entries.zh: 其併入者：名例之邊遠充軍並於充軍地方，公式門之毀棄制書印信並二條為一，課程門之鹽法並十二條為一，宮衛門之衝突儀仗並三條為一，郵驛門之遞送公文並三條為一。
entries.en: What was merged: remote military exile in General Principles was merged into the article on places of military exile; in Administrative Forms two articles on destroying imperial documents and seals were combined into one; in Revenue Duties twelve articles on salt law were combined into one; in Palace Guard three articles on clashing with ceremonial guards were combined into one; and in Postal Stations three articles on forwarding official documents were combined into one.
entries.literal: What was merged: remote military exile in General Principles was merged into the article on places of military exile; in Administrative Forms the two articles on destroying imperial documents and seals were merged into one; in Revenue Duties the twelve articles on salt law were merged into one; in Palace Guard the three articles on clashing with ceremonial guards were merged into one; in Postal Stations the three articles on forwarding official documents were merged into one.

entries.zh: 其改易者：名例之軍官軍人免發遣更為犯罪免發遣，軍官有犯更為軍籍有犯；
entries.en: What was altered: in General Principles "military officers and soldiers exempt from banishment" was changed to "offenders exempt from banishment," and "officers who commit offenses" to "offenders registered in the military rolls";
entries.literal: What was altered: in General Principles "military officers and soldiers exempt from banishment" was changed to "offenders exempt from banishment," and "officers who commit offenses" to "offenders registered in the military rolls";

entries.zh: 儀制門之收藏禁書及私習天文生節為收藏禁書。
entries.en: in Rites and Ceremonies the article on collecting forbidden books and privately studying astronomy was abridged to the article on collecting forbidden books alone.
entries.literal: in Rites and Ceremonies the article on collecting forbidden books and privately studying astronomy was abridged to the article on collecting forbidden books.

entries.zh: 其增入者：名例之天文生有犯充軍地方二條。
entries.en: What was added: in General Principles two articles on astronomy students who offend and on places of military exile.
entries.literal: What was added: in General Principles two articles on astronomy students who offend and places of military exile.

entries.zh: 總計名例律四十六條。
entries.en: In all, General Principles contained forty-six articles.
entries.literal: In all, General Principles contained forty-six articles.

entries.zh: 吏律：曰職制十四條，曰公式十四條。
entries.en: Officials Code: Official Regulations, fourteen articles; Administrative Forms, fourteen articles.
entries.literal: Officials Code: Official Regulations fourteen articles, Administrative Forms fourteen articles.

entries.zh: 戶律：曰戶役十五條，曰田宅十一條，曰婚姻十七條，曰倉庫二十三條，曰課程八條，曰市廛五條。
entries.en: Households Code: Household Service, fifteen articles; Fields and Dwellings, eleven; Marriage, seventeen; Granaries, twenty-three; Revenue Duties, eight; Markets, five.
entries.literal: Households Code: Household Service fifteen articles, Fields and Dwellings eleven articles, Marriage seventeen articles, Granaries twenty-three articles, Revenue Duties eight articles, Markets five articles.

entries.zh: 禮律：曰祭祀六條，曰儀制二十條。
entries.en: Rites Code: Sacrifices, six articles; Rites and Ceremonies, twenty articles.
entries.literal: Rites Code: Sacrifices six articles, Rites and Ceremonies twenty articles.

entries.zh: 兵律：曰宮衛十六條，曰軍政二十一條，曰關津七條，曰廄牧十一條，曰郵驛十六條。
entries.en: Military Code: Palace Guard, sixteen articles; Military Administration, twenty-one; Passes and Ferries, seven; Stables and Herds, eleven; Postal Stations, sixteen.
entries.literal: Military Code: Palace Guard sixteen articles, Military Administration twenty-one articles, Passes and Ferries seven articles, Stables and Herds eleven articles, Postal Stations sixteen articles.

entries.zh: 刑律：曰賊盜二十八條，曰人命二十條，曰鬥毆二十二條，曰罵詈八條，曰訴訟十二條，曰受贓十一條，曰詐偽十一條，曰犯奸十條，曰雜犯十一條，曰捕亡八條，曰斷獄二十九條。
entries.en: Punishments Code: Robbery and Theft, twenty-eight articles; Homicide, twenty; Assault, twenty-two; Abuse, eight; Litigation, twelve; Accepting Bribes, eleven; Fraud, eleven; Sexual Offenses, ten; Miscellaneous Offenses, eleven; Apprehension of Fugitives, eight; Trial and Judgment, twenty-nine.
entries.literal: Punishments Code: Robbery and Theft twenty-eight articles, Homicide twenty articles, Assault twenty-two articles, Abuse eight articles, Litigation twelve articles, Accepting Bribes eleven articles, Fraud eleven articles, Sexual Offenses ten articles, Miscellaneous Offenses eleven articles, Apprehension of Fugitives eight articles, Trial and Judgment twenty-nine articles.

entries.zh: 工律：曰營造九條，曰河防四條。
entries.en: Works Code: Construction, nine articles; River Control, four articles.
entries.literal: Works Code: Construction nine articles, River Control four articles.

entries.zh: 蓋仍明律三十門，而總為四百三十六條。
entries.en: It still followed the Ming Code's thirty sections, but totaled four hundred thirty-six articles.
entries.literal: Thus it still followed the Ming Code's thirty sections, but totaled four hundred thirty-six articles.

entries.zh: 律首六贓圖、五刑圖、獄具圖、喪服圖，大都沿明之舊。
entries.en: At the head of the code were diagrams of the six categories of bribery, the five punishments, prison implements, and mourning garments—mostly following the Ming as before.
entries.literal: At the head of the code were diagrams of the six categories of bribery, the five punishments, prison implements, and mourning garments—mostly following the Ming as before.

entries.zh: 納贖諸例圖、徒限內老疾收贖圖、誣輕為重收贖圖，銀數皆從現制。
entries.en: Diagrams of commutation by payment, of the aged and infirm redeemed within the term of penal servitude, and of treating a light offense as heavy for redemption—all silver amounts followed the current system.
entries.literal: Diagrams of commutation by payment, of the aged and infirm redeemed within the term of penal servitude, and of treating light error as heavy for redemption—all silver amounts followed the current system.

entries.zh: 其律文及律注，頗有增損改易。
entries.en: The statutory text and annotations underwent considerable additions, deletions, and revisions.
entries.literal: The statutory text and statutory annotations had considerable additions, subtractions, and alterations.

entries.zh: 律後總注，則康熙年間所創造。
entries.en: The general annotations after the statutes were a Kangxi-era innovation.
entries.literal: The general annotations after the statutes were a creation of the Kangxi period.

entries.zh: 律末並附比引律三十條。
entries.en: At the end of the code were also attached thirty articles of analogous citation statutes.
entries.literal: At the end of the code were also attached thirty articles of analogous citation statutes.

entries.zh: 此其大較也。
entries.en: Such was the general outline.
entries.literal: This is the general outline.

entries.zh: 自時厥後，雖屢經纂修，然僅續增附律之條例，而律文未之或改。
entries.en: From that time onward, although the code was revised repeatedly, only the supplementary precedents were continually added; the statutory text itself was never changed.
entries.literal: From that time onward, although there were repeated compilations and revisions, only the supplementary precedents attached to the code were continually added; the statutory text itself was never altered.

entries.zh: 惟乾隆五年，館修奏准芟除總注，並補入過失殺傷收贖一圖而已。
entries.en: Only in Qianlong 5 did the compiling office obtain approval to remove the general annotations and add one diagram on redemption for negligent killing and wounding—and that alone.
entries.literal: Only in the fifth year of Qianlong did the compiling office memorialize approval to cut away the general annotations and add one diagram on redemption for negligent killing and wounding—that alone.

entries.zh: 志一百十七
entries.en: Treatise 117
entries.literal: Treatise 117

entries.zh: 清太祖、太宗之治遼東，刑制尚簡，重則斬，輕則鞭撲而已。
entries.en: During the early Qing rule of the eastern Liao under the Taizu and Taizong emperors, penal law remained simple: serious offenses meant decapitation, minor ones no more than whipping and beating.
entries.literal: Under the Taizu and Taizong emperors of the Qing, when they ruled the eastern Liao region, the penal system was still simple: serious cases were punished by decapitation, light ones by whipping and beating only.

entries.zh: 迨世祖入關，沿襲明制，初頒刑律，笞、杖以五折十，注入本刑各條。
entries.en: After the Shizu emperor crossed into China proper, the Qing adopted Ming practice and issued its first penal code, applying the five-for-ten reduction to light-bamboo and stick penalties and embedding it in the relevant articles.
entries.literal: When the Shizu emperor entered the pass and took the throne, he followed the Ming system and first promulgated the penal code; light-bamboo and stick punishments were calculated on the principle of counting five blows as ten, and this was inserted into the articles on each principal punishment.

entries.zh: 康熙朝現行則例改為四折除零。
entries.en: Under Kangxi, the operative sub-statutes replaced this with a fourfold reduction, dropping remainders.
entries.literal: In the Kangxi reign the current sub-statutes changed this to a fourfold reduction with odd numbers dropped.

entries.zh: 雍正三年之律，乃依例各於本律註明板數。
entries.en: The Yongzheng code of 1725, following sub-statutory practice, specified the exact number of blows in each principal article.
entries.literal: The code of the third year of the Yongzheng reign, following the sub-statutes, noted the number of blows in each relevant article of the principal code.

entries.zh: 徒、流加杖，亦至配所照數折責。
entries.en: Additional stick blows attached to servitude and exile were likewise reduced to the prescribed count once the convict reached his place of assignment.
entries.literal: For penal servitude and exile, the additional stick blows were also reduced according to the prescribed number upon arrival at the place of assignment.

entries.zh: 蓋恐撲責過多，致傷生命，法外之仁也。
entries.en: The aim was to avoid so much beating that life was endangered—a mercy extending beyond strict legal requirement.
entries.literal: This was because they feared that excessive beating and flogging might endanger life—an act of mercy beyond what the letter of the law required.

entries.zh: 文武官犯笞、杖，則分別公私，代以罰俸、降級、降調，至革職而止。
entries.en: Civil and military officials subject to light-bamboo or stick penalties were treated according to whether the offense was public or private: fines, demotion, transfer, or dismissal replaced corporal punishment.
entries.literal: When civil and military officials incurred light-bamboo or stick punishment, public and private offenses were distinguished, and in place of physical punishment they received salary fines, demotion in rank, or transfer to a lower post, up to dismissal from office.

entries.zh: 志一百十八
entries.en: Treatise 118
entries.literal: Treatise Number 118

entries.zh: 世祖入主中夏，仍明舊制，凡訴訟在外由州縣層遞至於督撫，在內歸總於三法司。
entries.en: After the Shizu took possession of China proper, he retained the Ming framework: lawsuits in the provinces ascended step by step from county and prefecture to the governor-general or governor, while capital cases were consolidated in the Three Judicial Offices.
entries.literal: When the Shizu entered and ruled the Central Plains, he still followed the Ming old system: all lawsuits outside passed layer by layer from prefecture and county up to governor-general and governor; inside, all were gathered under the Three Judicial Offices.

entries.zh: 然明制三法司，刑部受天下刑名，都察院糾察，大理寺駮正。
entries.en: Under the Ming arrangement, the Three Judicial Offices divided labor: the Ministry of Justice received criminal cases from across the empire, the Censorate conducted surveillance and impeachment, and the Court of Revision reviewed and corrected judgments.
entries.literal: Yet under the Ming system of the Three Judicial Offices, the Ministry of Justice received criminal cases from all under Heaven, the Censorate investigated and censured, and the Court of Revision reviewed and corrected.

entries.zh: 清則外省刑案，統由刑部核覆。
entries.en: Under the Qing, criminal cases from the provinces were uniformly reviewed and ratified by the Ministry of Justice.
entries.literal: Under the Qing, criminal cases from outer provinces were uniformly reviewed and confirmed by the Ministry of Justice.

entries.zh: 不會法者，院寺無由過問，應會法者，亦由刑部主稿。
entries.en: For cases that did not require joint deliberation, the Court of Revision and Censorate had no avenue to intervene; even when joint deliberation was required, the Ministry of Justice still drafted the memorial.
entries.literal: Cases not requiring joint deliberation— the Court and Censorate had no means to intervene; cases requiring joint deliberation were also drafted chiefly by the Ministry of Justice.

entries.zh: 在京訟獄，無論奏咨，俱由刑部審理，而部權特重。
entries.en: All litigation and detention in the capital, whether submitted by memorial or routine report, fell to the Ministry of Justice, whose authority was exceptionally heavy.
entries.literal: Lawsuits and prisons in the capital, whether memorialized or reported, were all tried by the Ministry of Justice, and the ministry's authority was especially weighty.

entries.zh: 刑部初設十四司。
entries.en: The Ministry of Justice was first organized into fourteen bureaus.
entries.literal: The Ministry of Justice was first set up with fourteen bureaus.

entries.zh: 雍正元年，添置現審左右二司，審理八旗命盜及各衙門欽發事件。
entries.en: In the first year of Yongzheng, Left and Right Bureaus of Current Review were added to handle Banner homicides and robberies and cases dispatched by imperial order from other agencies.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng, the Left and Right Bureaus of Current Review were added to try cases of homicide and robbery among the Eight Banners and matters dispatched by imperial order from the various yamen.

entries.zh: 後復改並，定為十八清吏司：曰直隸，曰奉天，曰江蘇，曰安徽，曰江西，曰福建，曰浙江，曰湖廣，曰山東，曰山西，曰陝西，曰四川，曰廣東，曰廣西，曰雲南，曰貴州。
entries.en: They were later reorganized again into eighteen Bureaus of Pure Officials: Zhili, Fengtian, Jiangsu, Anhui, Jiangxi, Fujian, Zhejiang, Huguang, Shandong, Shanxi, Shaanxi, Sichuan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, and Guizhou.
entries.literal: Later they were again reorganized and merged, fixed as eighteen Bureaus of Pure Officials: namely Zhili, Fengtian, Jiangsu, Anhui, Jiangxi, Fujian, Zhejiang, Huguang, Shandong, Shanxi, Shaanxi, Sichuan, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, and Guizhou.

entries.zh: 凡各省刑名咨揭到部，各司具稿呈堂，以定準駮。
entries.en: Whenever provincial criminal reports reached the ministry, each bureau drafted a recommendation for the chief ministers, who then decided approval or rejection.
entries.literal: Whenever criminal reports and memorials from the provinces arrived at the ministry, each bureau prepared drafts and presented them to the hall to fix approval or rejection.

entries.zh: 吉林、黑龍江附諸奉天，甘肅、新疆附諸陝西，京曹各署關涉文件，亦分隸於十七司。
entries.en: Jilin and Heilongjiang were handled under Fengtian; Gansu and Xinjiang under Shaanxi; and paperwork from capital agencies was likewise distributed among the seventeen bureaus.
entries.literal: Jilin and Heilongjiang were attached to Fengtian; Gansu and Xinjiang to Shaanxi; documents from the capital bureaus were also divided and subordinated among the seventeen bureaus.

entries.zh: 現審則輪流簽分。
entries.en: Current-review cases were assigned in rotation by signature.
entries.literal: Current review cases were assigned by rotation through signing.

entries.zh: 順治十年，設督捕衙門，置侍郎滿、漢各一員，其屬有前司、後司。
entries.en: In the tenth year of Shunzhi, the Office of Pursuit and Capture was established with one Manchu and one Han vice minister, supported by Front and Rear Bureaus.
entries.literal: In the tenth year of Shunzhi, the Office of Pursuit and Capture was established, with one Manchu and one Han vice minister each; its subordinates had a Front Bureau and a Rear Bureau.

entries.zh: 初隸兵部，專理緝捕逃旗事宜。
entries.en: It was initially subordinate to the Ministry of War and specialized in hunting down fugitive bannermen.
entries.literal: At first subordinate to the Ministry of War, it specialized in pursuing and capturing fugitive bannermen.

entries.zh: 康熙三十八年裁撤，將前後司改隸刑部。
entries.en: In the thirty-eighth year of Kangxi it was abolished, and its Front and Rear Bureaus were transferred to the Ministry of Justice.
entries.literal: In the thirty-eighth year of Kangxi it was abolished, and the Front and Rear Bureaus were transferred to subordination under the Ministry of Justice.

entries.zh: 嗣復並為督捕一司，不掌外省刑名，亦不分現審。
entries.en: They were later merged into a single Bureau of Pursuit and Capture, which neither handled provincial criminal cases nor took part in current-review rotation.
entries.literal: Later they were again merged into one Bureau of Pursuit and Capture, which did not manage outer-province criminal cases and also did not share current review.

entries.zh: 刑部收受訟案，已結未結，每月匯奏。
entries.en: The Ministry of Justice reported monthly on all cases received, concluded or pending.
entries.literal: Cases received by the Ministry of Justice, whether concluded or not, were summarized and memorialized monthly.

entries.zh: 設督催所，而督以例限。
entries.en: A Supervision and Urging Office was established to enforce the statutory deadlines.
entries.literal: A Supervision and Urging Office was established to supervise by statutory time limits.

entries.zh: 審結尋常徒、流、軍、遣等罪，按季匯題。
entries.en: Routine sentences of penal servitude, exile, military exile, and banishment, once concluded, were reported quarterly in summary memorials.
entries.literal: Ordinary cases of penal servitude, exile, military exile, and banishment, once tried and concluded, were summarized by topic each quarter.

entries.zh: 案系奏交，情雖輕，專案奏結。
entries.en: Cases referred to the throne by memorial, however light the circumstances, required a separate concluding memorial.
entries.literal: Cases referred by imperial memorial, though the circumstances were light, were concluded by special memorial.

entries.zh: 死罪既取供，大理寺委寺丞或評事，都察院委御史，赴本司會審，謂之會小法。
entries.en: After confessions were obtained in capital cases, the Court of Revision sent a vice director or reviewer and the Censorate a censor to join the responsible bureau for a preliminary joint review—the "minor joint review."
entries.literal: Once capital crimes had obtained confession, the Court of Revision delegated a vice director or reviewer, the Censorate delegated a censor, and they went to the bureau for joint trial—called the minor joint review.

entries.zh: 獄成呈堂，都察院左都御史或左副都御史，大理寺卿或少卿，挈同屬員赴刑部會審，謂之會大法。
entries.en: When the file was complete and brought before the chief ministers, the left censor-in-chief or left vice censor-in-chief of the Censorate and the chief or vice chief of the Court of Revision, with their staffs, joined the Ministry of Justice for the "major joint review."
entries.literal: When the case was complete and presented to the hall, the Censorate's left censor-in-chief or left vice censor-in-chief and the Court's chief or vice chief, leading their subordinates, went to the Ministry of Justice for joint trial—called the major joint review.

entries.zh: 如有翻異，發司覆審，否則會稿分別題奏。
entries.en: If the parties changed their testimony, the case was sent back for retrial; otherwise the joint draft was memorialized in the usual form.
entries.literal: If there was reversal or discrepancy, the bureau was ordered to re-try; otherwise the joint draft was separately memorialized.

entries.zh: 罪干立決，旨下，本司派員監刑。
entries.en: For crimes warranting immediate execution, once the edict arrived the responsible bureau dispatched officers to supervise the sentence.
entries.literal: Crimes touching immediate execution—once the edict descended, the bureau dispatched officers to supervise the punishment.

entries.zh: 監候則入朝審。
entries.en: Prisoners held awaiting execution were referred to the court review.
entries.literal: Those held awaiting execution entered the court review.

entries.zh: 各省戶、婚、田土及笞、杖輕罪，由州縣完結，例稱自理。
entries.en: In the provinces, household, marriage, land, and minor beating offenses were concluded at the county or prefecture level—cases "adjudicated locally."
entries.literal: In each province, household, marriage, land, and light crimes of beating with the rod or the stick were concluded by prefecture and county, customarily called self-adjudication.

entries.zh: 詞訟每月設立循環簿，申送督、撫、司、道查考。
entries.en: Each month a rotating litigation register was kept and forwarded to the governor-general, governor, provincial judge, and circuit intendant for review.
entries.literal: Litigation each month established a rotating register, reported upward to governor-general, governor, provincial judge, and circuit intendant for inspection.

entries.zh: 巡道巡歷所至，提簿查核，如有未完，勒限催審。
entries.en: When a circuit intendant made his inspection rounds, he examined the register on the spot and, if cases remained open, imposed deadlines to hurry them to judgment.
entries.literal: Wherever the touring circuit intendant traveled on inspection, he took up the register to check; if cases were unfinished, he set a deadline and urged trial.

entries.zh: 徒以上解府、道、臬司審轉，徒罪由督撫匯案咨結。
entries.en: Sentences of penal servitude and above were escalated through prefecture, circuit, and provincial judicial commissioner; penal-servitude cases were bundled by the governor or governor-general and reported for closure.
entries.literal: Penal servitude and above were sent up to prefecture, circuit, and provincial judicial commissioner for review and transmission; penal-servitude cases were gathered by governor-general or governor and reported for conclusion.

entries.zh: 有關人命及流以上，專咨由部匯題。
entries.en: Cases involving loss of life or exile and heavier punishments were reported separately to the ministry for inclusion in summary memorials.
entries.literal: Cases involving human life and exile and above were specially reported to the ministry and summarized by topic.

entries.zh: 死罪系謀反、大逆、惡逆、不道、劫獄、反獄、戕官，並洋盜、會匪、強盜、拒殺官差，罪干凌遲、斬、梟者，專摺具奏，交部速議。
entries.en: Capital crimes of treason, great sedition, wicked sedition, impiety, prison raids or revolts, murder of officials, foreign piracy, secret-society banditry, robbery, or killing officials or runners while resisting—when the sentence was dismemberment, decapitation, or exposure of the head—were reported by special folded memorial for rapid ministry deliberation.
entries.literal: Capital crimes involving treason, great sedition, wicked sedition, impiety, prison raid, prison revolt, killing officials, together with foreign pirates, secret-society bandits, robbers, and killing officials or runners while resisting— crimes touching dismemberment, decapitation, or display of the head— were specially memorialized by folded dispatch and handed to the ministry for rapid deliberation.

entries.zh: 殺一家二命之案，交部速題。
entries.en: Cases involving two deaths in a single household were sent to the ministry for expedited memorial.
entries.literal: Cases of killing two persons in one household were handed to the ministry for rapid memorial.

entries.zh: 其餘斬、絞，俱專本具題，分送揭帖於法司科道，內閣票擬，交三法司核議。
entries.en: All other decapitation and strangulation cases were likewise submitted by special memorial; summary slips went to the judicial offices, the offices of scrutiny, and the censors; the Grand Secretariat drafted rescripts, and the Three Judicial Offices conducted joint review.
entries.literal: All other decapitation and strangulation cases were likewise memorialized by special report; summary slips were distributed to the judicial censors of the Three Offices, the Grand Secretariat drafted rescripts, and they were handed to the Three Judicial Offices for joint deliberation.

entries.zh: 如情罪不符及引律錯誤者，或駮令覆審，或徑行改正，合則如擬核定。
entries.en: If the facts did not match the charge or the statutes were misapplied, the case might be sent back for retrial or corrected outright; if correct, the proposed sentence was ratified.
entries.literal: If circumstances and crime did not match or statutes were wrongly cited, either rejection ordered re-trial, or correction was made directly; if fitting, approval followed the proposed sentence.

entries.zh: 議上立決，命下，釘封飛遞各州縣正印官或佐貳，會同武職行刑。
entries.en: Once immediate execution was approved and the order issued, sealed dispatches were rushed to the chief civil officer or deputy at each prefecture and county, who carried out the sentence jointly with the local military officer.
entries.literal: When deliberation approved immediate execution and the command descended, sealed dispatches were rushed to each prefecture and county's seal-holding official or deputy, who together with military officers carried out the punishment.

entries.zh: 監候則入秋審。
entries.en: Prisoners held awaiting execution entered the autumn review.
entries.literal: Those held awaiting execution entered the autumn review.

entries.zh: 順治十三年，諭刑部：「朝審秋決，系刑獄重典。
entries.en: In Shunzhi 13 the throne instructed the Ministry of Justice: "Court review and autumn execution are grave matters of criminal justice.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year of Shunzhi, an instruction was issued to the Ministry of Justice: "Court review and autumn execution are great statutes of the prisons.

entries.zh: 朕必詳閱招案始末，情形允協，令死者無冤。
entries.en: I must read each casebook through from start to finish, ensure the facts fit the charge, and see that the condemned die without injustice.
entries.literal: I must read in detail the beginning and end of each casebook, that the circumstances accord, and let the dead be without injustice.

entries.zh: 今烸期伊邇，朝審甫竣，招冊繁多，尚未及詳細簡閱，驟行正法，朕心不忍。
entries.en: The execution season is upon us, court review has only just ended, and the casebooks are too many for me to have reviewed them all in detail. To put them to death at once—I cannot bear it.
entries.literal: Now the execution date draws near; court review has just ended, the casebooks are numerous, and I have not yet had time to review them in detail; to carry out execution at once—my heart cannot bear it.

entries.zh: 今年姑著暫停秋決，昭朕矜恤至意。」
entries.en: Suspend autumn executions for this year, to show my utmost regard for human life."
entries.literal: This year let autumn execution be temporarily suspended, to display my utmost compassionate regard.

entries.zh: 自是列朝於秋讞俱勤慎校閱。
entries.en: Thereafter every reign handled autumn verdicts with scrupulous care.
entries.literal: From this time onward, successive reigns all reviewed autumn verdicts with diligence and care.

entries.zh: 康熙二十二年，聖袓御懋勤殿，召大學士、學士等入，酌定在京秋審情實重犯。
entries.en: In Kangxi 22 the Sage Ancestor held court in the Hall of Diligent Government, summoned Grand Secretaries and academicians, and classified capital prisoners for autumn review.
entries.literal: In the twenty-second year of Kangxi, the Sage Ancestor held court in the Hall of Diligent Government, summoned Grand Secretaries, academicians, and others to enter, and weighed the capital autumn-review cases deserving execution.

entries.zh: 聖袓取罪案逐一親閱，再三詳審，其斷無可恕者，始定情實。
entries.en: He read every case himself, examining each again and again; only those beyond all excuse were marked deserving execution.
entries.literal: The Sage Ancestor took each crime case and personally read it one by one, examining again and again in detail; only those absolutely without forgiveness were fixed as deserving execution.

entries.zh: 因諭曰：「人命事關重大，故召爾等共相商酌。
entries.en: He said: "Human life is a grave matter, which is why I have called you to deliberate together.
entries.literal: He thereupon instructed: "Human life concerns weighty matters; therefore I have summoned you to deliberate together.

entries.zh: 情有可原，即開生路。」
entries.en: Where circumstances permit mercy, open a path to life."
entries.literal: If circumstances permit excuse, open a path to life at once.

entries.zh: 雍正十一年，世宗御洞明堂，閱秋審情實招冊，諭刑部曰：「諸臣所進招冊，俱經細加斟酌，擬定情實。
entries.en: In Yongzheng 11 the Shizong held court in the Bright Hall of Enlightenment, reviewed autumn-review casebooks, and told the Ministry of Justice: "The casebooks your officials have submitted have all been carefully weighed and classified as deserving execution.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year of Yongzheng, the Shizong held court in the Bright Hall of Enlightenment, reviewed the autumn-review casebooks of those deserving execution, and instructed the Ministry of Justice: "The casebooks submitted by the various officials have all been finely weighed and deliberated, fixing deserving execution.

entries.zh: 但此內有一線可生之機，爾等亦當陳奏。
entries.en: But if even a thread of life remains possible, you must say so in memorial.
entries.literal: Yet if within them there is a thread of possibility for life, you also ought to memorialize.

entries.zh: 在前日定擬情實，自是執法，在此刻句到商酌，又當原情，斷不可因前奏難更，遂爾隱默也。」
entries.en: Fixing deserving execution earlier was enforcing the law; at the moment of execution you must weigh the human circumstances again—you must not stay silent because an earlier memorial is hard to change."
entries.literal: To fix deserving execution on a prior day was of course enforcing the law; at this moment, when execution is at hand and deliberation is held, one must also consider the circumstances—by no means may you remain silent because a prior memorial is hard to change.

entries.zh: 高宗尤垂意刑名，秋審冊上，每干飭責。
entries.en: The Gaozong paid special attention to criminal matters and often reprimanded officials on the autumn-review registers.
entries.literal: The Gaozong especially attended to criminal matters; on autumn-review registers he often issued reprimands.

entries.zh: 乾隆三十一年，湖南官犯饒佺，以其回護己過予句。
entries.en: In Qianlong 31 the Hunan official offender Rao Qian was marked for execution for shielding his own misconduct.
entries.literal: In the thirty-first year of Qianlong, the Hunan official offender Rao Qian was marked for execution for shielding his own fault.

entries.zh: 迨閱浙省招冊，知府高象震亦以承審回護，原題僅擬軍台效力。
entries.en: When he reviewed the Zhejiang casebook, he found Prefect Gao Xiangzhen had likewise shielded himself during trial, though the original memorial had proposed only service at a military post.
entries.literal: When he came to review the Zhejiang casebook, Prefect Gao Xiangzhen likewise shielded himself in trial, yet the original memorial had only proposed service at a military post.

entries.zh: 急諭湖南巡撫將饒佺暫停處決，令刑部查明兩案情節不同，始行明諭處分。
entries.en: He urgently ordered the Hunan governor to suspend Rao Qian's execution, ordered the Ministry of Justice to ascertain the circumstances of the two cases, and only after they were found to differ issued clear instructions on punishment.
entries.literal: He urgently instructed the Hunan governor to suspend Rao Qian's execution, ordered the Ministry of Justice to ascertain that the circumstances of the two cases differed, and only then issued clear instructions on disposition.

entries.zh: 其慎重讞典如此。
entries.en: Such was the care the throne took with capital verdicts.
entries.literal: Such was the care taken with verdict statutes.

entries.zh: 仁宗亦嫻習法律。
entries.en: The Renzong was likewise well versed in law.
entries.literal: The Renzong was also well versed in law.

entries.zh: 嘉慶七年，御史廣興會議秋審，奏請將斗殺擬緩之廣東姚得輝改入情實，援引乾隆十八年「一命必有一抵」之旨。
entries.en: In Jiaqing 7, at the autumn-review conference, Censor Guangxing asked that Yao Dehui of Guangdong—a brawl killer proposed for deferral—be reclassified as deserving execution, citing the Qianlong 18 instruction that "one life must have one compensation."
entries.literal: In the seventh year of Jiaqing, Censor Guangxing at the autumn-review conference memorialized requesting that Yao Dehui of Guangdong, proposed for deferral in a brawl killing, be changed to deserving execution, citing the Qianlong eighteenth-year instruction that "one life must have one compensation."

entries.zh: 仁宗謂：「一命一抵，原指械鬥等案而言，至尋常鬥毆，各斃各命，自當酌情理之平，分別實緩。
entries.en: The Renzong replied: "One life for one compensation referred to armed brawls and the like. In ordinary brawls each side kills and dies; reason and feeling must be weighed to distinguish deserving execution from deferral.
entries.literal: The Renzong said: "One life for one compensation originally referred to cases of armed brawls and the like; as for ordinary brawls, each side kills and each dies—one should weigh the balance of reason and feeling and distinguish deserving execution from deferral.

entries.zh: 若拘泥『一命必有一抵』之語，則是秋讞囚徒，凡殺傷斃命之案，將盡行問擬情實，可不必有緩決一項。
entries.en: If we rigidly applied 'one life must have one compensation' to every killing, every autumn-review prisoner would be marked deserving execution and the category of deferred decision would become pointless."
entries.literal: If one rigidly clings to the phrase 'one life must have one compensation,' then among autumn-review prisoners, for all cases of killing or wounding with death, all would be proposed as deserving execution, and there would be no need for the category of deferred decision.

entries.zh: 有是理乎？」
entries.en: Would that make any sense?"
entries.literal: Is there such a principle?

entries.zh: 命仍照原擬入緩。
entries.en: He ordered the original classification of deferral to stand.
entries.literal: He ordered that the original proposal of deferral still be followed.

entries.zh: 其剖析法意，致為明允。
entries.en: His parsing of the law was exceptionally clear and fair.
entries.literal: His parsing of legal meaning reached exceptional clarity and fairness.

entries.zh: 自後宣宗、文宗遵循前軌，罕可紀述。
entries.en: The Xuanzong and Wenzong followed precedent, with little worth recording.
entries.literal: Thereafter the Xuanzong and Wenzong followed the former track, with little worth recording.

entries.zh: 穆宗、德宗兩經垂簾，每逢句到，命大學士一人捧單入內閣恭代，後遂沿為故事。
entries.en: Under the Muzong and Dezong, during two regencies, whenever execution dates arrived one Grand Secretary carried the list into the Grand Secretariat to act for the throne; this later became fixed practice.
entries.literal: Under the Muzong and Dezong, during two regencies, whenever execution dates arrived, one Grand Secretary was ordered to carry the list into the Grand Secretariat to perform the ceremony by proxy; later this became a standing practice.

entries.zh: 熱審之制，順治初賡續舉行。
entries.en: The summer-review system was continued from early Shunzhi.
entries.literal: The summer-review system was continued and implemented from early Shunzhi.

entries.zh: 康熙十年，定每年小滿後十日起，至立秋前一日止，非實犯死罪及軍、流，俱量予減等。
entries.en: In Kangxi 10 it was fixed that from ten days after Lesser Fullness until the day before Beginning of Autumn, all except true capital crimes and military exile or banishment might receive appropriate reduction.
entries.literal: In the tenth year of Kangxi it was fixed that from ten days after Lesser Fullness each year until the day before the Beginning of Autumn, for all except true capital crimes and military exile or banishment, reductions by degree were granted as appropriate.

entries.zh: 四十三年，諭刑部停止。
entries.en: In the forty-third year the ministry was ordered to stop.
entries.literal: In the forty-third year, the Ministry of Justice was instructed to stop.

entries.zh: 雍正初復行。
entries.en: It was revived in early Yongzheng.
entries.literal: In early Yongzheng it was revived.

entries.zh: 乾隆以後，第准免笞、杖，則遞行八折決放，枷號漸釋，餘不之及。
entries.en: After Qianlong only rod and stick punishments were exempted, applied at eight-tenths of the statutory penalty with gradual release from the cangue; other punishments were unaffected.
entries.literal: After Qianlong, only exemption from rod and stick was allowed; then eight-tenths sentencing and release were applied in succession, cangue gradually released, the rest not touched.

entries.zh: 且惟京師行之，外省笞、杖自理，無從考核，具文而已，列朝無寒審，而有軍、流、遣犯隆冬停遣之例。
entries.en: It applied only in the capital; in the provinces rod and stick cases were locally adjudicated without oversight—empty form. No dynasty had winter review, but military exiles, banished persons, and deportees were not dispatched in deep winter.
entries.literal: Moreover it was practiced only in the capital; in outer provinces rod and stick were self-adjudicated, without means of inspection—mere form on paper. No dynasty had winter review, but there was the precedent of suspending dispatch of military exiles, banished persons, and deportees in deep winter.

entries.zh: 未起解者，十月至正月終及六月俱停遣。
entries.en: Prisoners not yet dispatched were not sent from the tenth month through the first month, nor in the sixth month.
entries.literal: Those not yet escorted were not dispatched from the tenth month through the end of the first month, nor in the sixth month.

entries.zh: 若已至中途，至十一月初一日准停。
entries.en: Those already en route might be halted from the first day of the eleventh month.
entries.literal: If already on the road, suspension was permitted from the first day of the eleventh month.

entries.zh: 倘抵配不遠，並發往東南省分，人犯有情原前進者，一體起解。
entries.en: If the destination was near, or if prisoners were bound for southeastern provinces and were willing to proceed, they were dispatched as usual.
entries.literal: If the place of assignment was not far, or if sent to southeastern provinces, and the prisoner had circumstances warranting advance, all alike were escorted.

entries.zh: 志一百十九
entries.en: Treatise 119
entries.literal: Treatise 119.

entries.zh: 二十五年，大學士徐桐言電報局獲利不貲，並無裨益公家之實。
entries.en: In 1899, Grand Secretary Xu Tong argued that the telegraph bureau reaped enormous profits while bringing no real benefit to the state.
entries.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, Grand Secretary Xu Tong stated that the telegraph bureau reaped immeasurable profit yet brought no real benefit to the state.

entries.zh: 廷臣亦有以招商、電報各局假公濟私為言者。
entries.en: Court officials also charged that the China Merchants and telegraph bureaus used public office for private gain.
entries.literal: Court officials also spoke of the China Merchants and telegraph bureaus using public office for private gain.

entries.zh: 俱下協辦大學士剛毅查復。
entries.en: All were referred to Associate Grand Secretary Gangyi for investigation.
entries.literal: All were referred to Associate Grand Secretary Gangyi for investigation and reply.

entries.zh: 剛毅時以事銜命赴蘇，尋疏陳：「電局自恰線成後，所虧至鉅，俟有贏餘，歲輸南北洋學款十二萬四千兩。」
entries.en: Gangyi was then on assignment in Suzhou. He soon reported: "Since the Kyakhta line was completed, the telegraph bureau's losses have been enormous. When surpluses arise, it remits 124,000 taels annually for Northern and Southern Seas educational funds."
entries.literal: Gangyi was then on assignment in Suzhou on imperial orders. He soon memorialized: "Since the Kyakhta line was completed, the telegraph bureau's losses have been enormous. When there are surpluses, it remits one hundred twenty-four thousand taels annually for Northern and Southern Seas educational funds."

entries.zh: 報可。
entries.en: The report was approved.
entries.literal: The report was approved.

entries.zh: 明年，廷臣復言電局利權太重，宜遴員接辦。
entries.en: The following year, court officials again argued that the telegraph bureau wielded too much profit and authority, and that suitable officials should be appointed to take over.
entries.literal: The following year, court officials again stated that the telegraph bureau's profit and authority were too great, and that suitable officials should be selected to take over.

entries.zh: 詔飭宣懷按年冊報收支款目，官電應免收費。
entries.en: An edict ordered Sheng Xuanhuai to submit annual accounts of income and expenditures, and mandated that official telegrams be sent free of charge.
entries.literal: An edict ordered Sheng Xuanhuai to report income and expenditures annually in registers, and that official telegrams should be sent free of charge.

entries.zh: 宣懷上疏，略言：「電局本系集華商合眾之力，以與洋商爭衡，旁觀每驚為大利所叢，其實析分千百股商，仍皆寸寸銖銖之微利。
entries.en: Sheng Xuanhuai submitted a memorial arguing: "The telegraph bureau was founded to pool Chinese merchant capital against foreign competition. Outsiders marvel at its profits, but divided among thousands of shareholders, each earns only modest returns.
entries.literal: Sheng Xuanhuai submitted a memorial stating in summary: "The telegraph bureau originally gathered the combined strength of Chinese merchants to compete with foreign merchants. Observers often marvel at it as a concentration of great profit, but in fact, divided among thousands of shareholders, each receives only tiny incremental gains.

entries.zh: 近年電線開拓日廣，則局用及修線養線之費亦日增。
entries.en: As telegraph lines have expanded in recent years, bureau expenses and line maintenance costs have risen accordingly.
entries.literal: In recent years, as telegraph lines have expanded daily, bureau expenses and costs for maintaining and repairing lines have also increased daily.

entries.zh: 上年因中俄條約，接造恰克圖之線用費六十餘萬兩，未請官款，悉系電商集貲辦成。
entries.en: Last year, under the Sino-Russian treaty, the Kyakhta connecting line cost over six hundred thousand taels—all raised by telegraph merchants, with no government funds requested.
entries.literal: Last year, pursuant to the Sino-Russian treaty, the Kyakhta connecting line cost over six hundred thousand taels. No official funds were requested—all was raised and completed by telegraph merchants.

entries.zh: 沙漠荒僻之區，絕少報費，而常年用數尤鉅。
entries.en: Desert and remote regions generate almost no telegram revenue, yet operating costs remain enormous.
entries.literal: In desert and remote regions, telegram fees are extremely scarce, yet annual operating expenses are especially heavy.

entries.zh: 至本年應辦之工，因辦理鐵路，盧溝橋至保定線已造成，又須造保定至漢口幹線。
entries.en: This year's projects include the completed Lugou Bridge-Baoding line for railway construction, and the Baoding-Hankou trunk line still to be built.
entries.literal: As for this year's required work: because of railway construction, the Lugou Bridge-Baoding line has been completed, and the Baoding-Hankou trunk line must also be built.

entries.zh: 因辦理海防，乃須造寧波至溫州之線。
entries.en: For coastal defense, the Ningbo-Wenzhou line must be built.
entries.literal: Because of coastal defense, the Ningbo-Wenzhou line must be built.

entries.zh: 總理衙門因洋人之請，則須造山東泰安、沂州之線。
entries.en: At foreign request through the Zongli Yamen, lines to Taian and Yizhou in Shandong must be built.
entries.literal: At the Zongli Yamen's request on behalf of foreigners, the Shandong Taian and Yizhou lines must be built.

entries.zh: 此外各路加線要工，絡繹不絕，官款並無可籌，皆借股商之力，以赴公家之急。
entries.en: Branch lines and essential work continue without cease. With no government funds available, merchant shareholders bear the burden of meeting the state's urgent needs.
entries.literal: Beyond this, branch lines and essential work on various routes continue without cease. No official funds can be raised—all rely on merchant shareholders' strength to meet the state's urgent needs.

entries.zh: 總局收支各賬，均系按年刊布。
entries.en: The head office publishes all income and expenditure accounts annually.
entries.literal: All accounts of income and expenditure at the head office are published annually.

entries.zh: 各局詳細坐簿，亦任股商隨時查閱。
entries.en: Detailed ledgers at each office are open for shareholder inspection at any time.
entries.literal: Detailed ledgers at each office are also open for shareholders to inspect at any time.

entries.zh: 一出一入，眾見眾聞，非如官中所辦報銷，出於一二人之手者可比。
entries.en: Every transaction is open to public scrutiny—unlike official reimbursements handled by one or two individuals.
entries.literal: Every expenditure and receipt is seen and known by all—not comparable to official reimbursement handled by one or two persons.

entries.zh: 原奏所疑各節，似屬不知此中原委。
entries.en: The doubts raised in the original memorial seem to stem from ignorance of these facts.
entries.literal: The various points doubted in the original memorial seem to stem from ignorance of these underlying facts.

entries.zh: 至官報之費，前定章程，擬一半報效，一半給貲，期於官商兼顧，持久不廢，仍宜照舊辦理，以維大局。」
entries.en: Regarding official telegram fees, the established regulations split costs evenly between tribute and payment to balance government and merchant interests for long-term sustainability. These arrangements should remain in place to preserve stability."
entries.literal: As for official telegram fees, the previously established regulations proposed half as tribute and half as payment, aiming to balance government and merchant interests for lasting operation. These should still be handled as before to preserve the overall arrangement."

entries.zh: 報聞。
entries.en: The memorial was submitted and acknowledged.
entries.literal: The memorial was submitted and acknowledged.

entries.zh: 電報之法，自英吉利人初設於其國都，推及於印度，再及於上海。
entries.en: Telegraphy was first introduced by the British in their capital, then spread to India, and from there reached Shanghai.
entries.literal: The method of telegraphy was first established by the English in their national capital, extended to India, and then extended to Shanghai.

entries.zh: 同治十三年，日本犯台灣，兩江總督沈葆楨疏言電報之利，詔旨飭辦，不果行。
entries.en: In 1874, when Japan invaded Taiwan, Shen Baozhen, Governor-General of Liangjiang, submitted a memorial on the advantages of telegraphy. The court ordered action, but the plan never went forward.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year of Tongzhi, Japan invaded Taiwan. The Governor-General of Liangjiang Shen Baozhen memorialized on the benefits of telegraphy. An imperial edict ordered it to be carried out, but it was not implemented.

entries.zh: 光緒五年，直隸總督李鴻章始於大沽、北塘海口砲台設線達天津，試行之而利，明年因有安設南北洋電報之請。
entries.en: In 1879, Li Hongzhang, Governor-General of Zhili, ran telegraph lines from the Dagu and Beitang coastal batteries to Tianjin. The trial proved successful, and the next year he petitioned to establish a telegraph network connecting the northern and southern coasts.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Guangxu, Li Hongzhang, Governor-General of Zhili, first installed lines from the Dagu and Beitang coastal fort batteries to Tianjin. The trial proved beneficial, and the following year a request was made to install telegraphs linking the Northern and Southern Seas.

entries.zh: 先是同治間，英使阿禮國請設電線於中國境內，力拒之，乃已。
entries.en: Earlier, during the Tongzhi era, the British minister Alcock had asked to lay telegraph lines inside China. The request was firmly refused and dropped.
entries.literal: Previously, during the Tongzhi reign, the British envoy Alcock requested to install telegraph lines within Chinese territory. It was firmly rejected and thus ceased.

entries.zh: 九年，其使臣威妥瑪復申前議，易陸線為水線，自廣州經閩、浙以達上海，爭之數月，卒如所請。
entries.en: In the ninth year [of Tongzhi, 1870], Wade revived the proposal, substituting submarine cables for land lines running from Guangzhou through Fujian and Zhejiang to Shanghai. After months of negotiation, the request was finally approved.
entries.literal: In the ninth year, the envoy Wade again raised the earlier proposal, changing land lines to submarine cables from Guangzhou through Fujian and Zhejiang to Shanghai. After disputing for several months, it was ultimately granted as requested.

entries.zh: 嗣是香港海線循廣州達天津，陸線達九龍。
entries.en: Hong Kong's submarine cable then ran via Guangzhou to Tianjin, while its land line reached Kowloon.
entries.literal: Subsequently, Hong Kong's submarine cable ran along Guangzhou to Tianjin, and its land line reached Kowloon.

entries.zh: 而丹國陸線亦由吳淞至滬上，駸駸有闌入內地之勢。
entries.en: Denmark's land line from Wusong to Shanghai, meanwhile, was steadily pushing inward toward the interior.
entries.literal: Meanwhile, Denmark's land line also ran from Wusong to Shanghai, gradually showing a tendency to encroach into the interior.

entries.zh: 七年，平南王尚可喜徇廣東，師自南安入，武元遣副將栗養志以兵從，克南雄、韶州二府。
entries.en: In the seventh year Prince of Pingnan Shang Kexi campaigned in Guangdong. The army entered from Nan'an; Wuyuan sent deputy commander Li Yangzhi in support, and they took Nanxiong and Shaozhou.
entries.literal: In the seventh year, the Prince of Pingnan, Shang Kexi, subjugated Guangdong; the army entered from Nan'an, and Wuyuan sent deputy commander Li Yangzhi with troops to follow, capturing the two prefectures of Nanxiong and Shaozhou.

entries.zh: 又遣副將高進庫，游擊楊繼、洪起元等剿寧都土寇彭順慶，副將楊遇明、劉伯祿、賈熊、董大用等剿大庾土寇羅榮。
entries.en: He also sent deputy commander Gao Jinku and battalion commanders Yang Ji and Hong Qiyuan against the Ningdu bandit Peng Shunqing, and deputy commanders Yang Yuming, Liu Bolu, Jia Xiong, and Dong Dayong against the Dayu bandit Luo Rong.
entries.literal: He also sent deputy commander Gao Jinku, battalion commanders Yang Ji and Hong Qiyuan, and others to suppress the Ningdu bandit Peng Shunqing; and deputy commanders Yang Yuming, Liu Bolu, Jia Xiong, Dong Dayong, and others to suppress the Dayu bandit Luo Rong.

entries.zh: 順慶應聲桓為亂，自號軍門，窺伺郡邑；
entries.en: Peng Shunqing had joined Shengwan's revolt, styled himself Military Gate, and eyed the surrounding prefectures;
entries.literal: Shunqing had answered Shengwan's rebellion, styled himself Military Gate, and watched for chances against the prefectures and counties;

entries.zh: 榮自明季倡亂楚、粵間，自號五軍都督，聚眾數万，阻山結寨二十餘，四出劫掠：至是皆就戮。
entries.en: Luo Rong had raised trouble between Huguang and Guangdong since the late Ming, called himself Commander-in-chief of the Five Armies, mustered tens of thousands in more than twenty mountain stockades, and raided widely—all were put to death on this occasion.
entries.literal: Rong had stirred rebellion between Chu and Yue since the late Ming, styled himself Commander-in-chief of the Five Armies, gathered tens of thousands, blocked the mountains and built more than twenty stockades, and raided on all sides: by this time all were executed.

entries.zh: 敘功，加太子太保、兵部尚書。
entries.en: For his merit he was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Minister of War.
entries.literal: Merit was reviewed: he was given the additional titles of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Minister of War.

entries.zh: 遇恩詔，進世職一等阿達哈哈番又一拖沙喇哈番。
entries.en: On an amnesty edict his line was raised to first-class Adahafan with an additional Tosahafan.
entries.literal: On an amnesty edict, his hereditary rank was advanced to first-class Adahafan with an additional Tosahafan.

entries.zh: 十年，引疾還京。
entries.en: In the tenth year he pleaded illness and returned to Beijing.
entries.literal: In the tenth year, he cited illness and returned to the capital.

entries.zh: 十一年，卒，贈少保，諡明靖。
entries.en: He died in the eleventh year and was posthumously made Junior Guardian with the posthumous name Mingjing (Bright and Tranquil).
entries.literal: In the eleventh year, he died; he was posthumously made Junior Guardian and given the posthumous title Mingjing.

entries.zh: 李國英，漢軍正紅旗人，初籍遼東。
entries.en: Li Guoying belonged to the Han Army Bordered Red Banner and was originally registered in Liaodong.
entries.literal: Li Guoying, a man of the Han Army Bordered Red Banner, was originally registered in Liaodong.

entries.zh: 仕明隸左良玉部下，官至總兵。
entries.en: Under the Ming he served under Zuo Liangyu and eventually became a regional commander.
entries.literal: He served the Ming under Zuo Liangyu and rose to the rank of regional commander.

entries.zh: 順治二年，與良玉子夢庚來降。
entries.en: In Shunzhi 2 (1645), he surrendered together with Liangyu's son Menggeng.
entries.literal: In the second year of Shunzhi, he came to surrender with Liangyu's son Menggeng.

entries.zh: 三年，從肅親王豪格下四川，討張獻忠，授成都總兵。
entries.en: In the third year he marched into Sichuan with Prince Su Hoge to suppress Zhang Xianzhong and was made regional commander at Chengdu.
entries.literal: In the third year, he followed Prince Su Hoge into Sichuan to campaign against Zhang Xianzhong and was appointed regional commander at Chengdu.

entries.zh: 五年，擢四川巡撫。
entries.en: In the fifth year he was promoted to governor of Sichuan.
entries.literal: In the fifth year, he was promoted to Sichuan provincial governor.

entries.zh: 世祖定鼎，進世職二等甲喇章京。
entries.en: After the Shizu established the capital, he was promoted to second-rank jalan janggin in hereditary office.
entries.literal: When the Shizu established the capital, he was promoted to second-rank jalan janggin in hereditary office.

entries.zh: 三年、四年，迭主會試。
entries.en: In the third and fourth years he presided over the metropolitan examinations in turn.
entries.literal: In the third and fourth years he presided over the metropolitan examinations in succession.

entries.zh: 考滿，進世職一等阿達哈哈番。
entries.en: When his performance review was complete, he was promoted to first-rank adaha hafan in hereditary office.
entries.literal: When his term of assessment was complete, he was promoted to first-rank adaha hafan in hereditary office.

entries.zh: 五年，復進三等阿思哈尼哈番，賜號「巴克什」。
entries.en: In the fifth year he was further promoted to third-rank ashan i hafan and granted the title "Bakshi."
entries.literal: In the fifth year he was further promoted to third-rank ashan i hafan and given the title "Bakshi."

entries.zh: 六年，充太宗實錄總裁，復主會試。
entries.en: In the sixth year he served as chief compiler of the Taizong Veritable Records and again presided over the metropolitan examination.
entries.literal: In the sixth year he served as chief compiler of the Veritable Records of the Taizong and again presided over the metropolitan examination.

entries.zh: 疏請令六科錄諸臣章奏並批答，月送史館，備纂修國史，報可。
entries.en: He memorialized asking that the Six Offices of Scrutiny copy all ministers' memorials together with imperial replies and send them monthly to the Historiography Institute for compiling the national history; the request was approved.
entries.literal: He memorialized asking that the Six Offices of Scrutiny record all ministers' memorials together with imperial replies and send them monthly to the Historiography Institute for use in compiling the national history; the request was approved.

entries.zh: 八年，以編撰明史闕天啟四年至七年實錄，請敕懸賞購求；
entries.en: In the eighth year, because the compilation of the History of the Ming lacked the veritable records for Tianqi 4 through 7, he asked that an edict be issued offering rewards for their purchase;
entries.literal: In the eighth year, because the compilation of the History of the Ming lacked the veritable records for Tianqi years four through seven, he asked that an edict be issued offering rewards for their purchase;

entries.zh: 崇禎一朝事責無考，其有野史、外傳，並令訪送。
entries.en: For the Chongzhen reign there was no one who could be held accountable; any unofficial histories and outside accounts were likewise to be sought out and submitted.
entries.literal: For events of the Chongzhen reign there was no one to answer for them; any unofficial histories and external accounts were also to be sought out and submitted.

entries.zh: 章下所司。
entries.en: The memorial was referred to the responsible office.
entries.literal: The memorial was sent down to the appropriate office.

entries.zh: 順治元年，睿親王既定京師，以書徵銓，銓聞命即至，賚冠服、鞍馬、銀幣。
entries.en: In Shunzhi 1, after the Prince Regent had secured the capital, he summoned Feng Quan by letter; Quan came at once and was rewarded with court dress, saddle horses, and silver.
entries.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi, after the Prince Regent had secured the capital, he summoned Feng Quan by letter; Quan came as soon as he received the order and was rewarded with court dress, saddle horses, and silver coins.

entries.zh: 令以大學士原銜入內院佐理機務，與大學士洪承疇疏請復明票擬舊制，又與大學士謝升等議定郊社、宗廟樂章。
entries.en: He was ordered to enter the Inner Court to assist in state affairs under his former grand secretary title; with Grand Secretary Hong Chengchou he memorialized to restore the Ming practice of drafting memorials with approval slips, and with Grand Secretary Xie Sheng and others he also settled the ceremonial music for suburban sacrifices and the ancestral temple.
entries.literal: He was ordered to enter the Inner Court to assist in state affairs with his former grand secretary title, and together with Grand Secretary Hong Chengchou memorialized to restore the Ming practice of memorial drafting with approval slips; together with Grand Secretary Xie Sheng and others he also settled the ceremonial music for suburban sacrifices and the ancestral temple.

entries.zh: 十月朔，世祖禦皇極門受賀，給事中孫承澤疏糾朝班雜亂，語侵內院。
entries.en: On the first day of the tenth month the Shizu received congratulations at the Huangji Gate; supervising secretary Sun Chengze memorialized against the disorder in the court ranks, with language that impugned the Inner Court.
entries.literal: On the first day of the tenth month the Shizu received congratulations at the Huangji Gate; supervising secretary Sun Chengze memorialized criticizing the disorder in the court ranks, with language impugning the Inner Court.

entries.zh: 銓與升、承疇乞罷，諭令益殫忠猷，以襄新治。
entries.en: Quan, together with Sheng and Chengchou, asked to resign; an edict ordered them instead to devote themselves more fully and assist the new regime.
entries.literal: Quan together with Sheng and Chengchou begged to resign; an edict ordered them instead to devote themselves more fully in loyalty and assist the new governance.

entries.zh: 八年，上親覈諸大臣功績，諭：「銓先經吳達奏劾得叛將薑瓖賄，便當引去；
entries.en: In the eighth year the emperor personally reviewed the achievements of the great ministers and instructed: "When Quan was earlier memorialized against by Wu Da for taking bribes from the rebellious general Jiang Xiang, he ought to have withdrawn;
entries.literal: In the eighth year the emperor personally verified the achievements of the great ministers and instructed: "When Quan was earlier memorialized against by Wu Da for receiving bribes from the rebellious general Jiang Xiang, he ought to have withdrawn;

entries.zh: 乃隱忍居官，七年以來，無所建白：令致仕。
entries.en: yet he quietly remained in office and in seven years has offered nothing constructive: order him to retire.
entries.literal: yet he concealedly remained in office, and in seven years has offered nothing constructive: order him to retire.

entries.zh: 李若琳憸險專擅，與銓朋比為奸，奪官，永不敘用。」
entries.en: Li Ruolin is crafty, dangerous, and monopolizes power; together with Quan he forms a faction to do evil—strip his office and never employ him again."
entries.literal: Li Ruolin is crafty, dangerous, and monopolizes power; together with Quan he forms a faction to do evil—strip his office and never employ him again."

entries.zh: 銓既罷，代以陳名夏，坐事奪官；
entries.en: After Quan was dismissed, Chen Mingxia replaced him but was stripped of office for an offense;
entries.literal: After Quan was dismissed, Chen Mingxia replaced him but was stripped of office for an offense;

entries.zh: 代以陳之遴，亦不久罷。
entries.en: Chen Zhilin replaced him but was also soon dismissed.
entries.literal: Chen Zhilin replaced him but was also soon dismissed.

entries.zh: 上復召銓還，諭曰：「國家用人，使功不如使過。
entries.en: The emperor recalled Quan and instructed: "In employing men, the state finds it better to use those who have erred than those who have merely succeeded.
entries.literal: The emperor again recalled Quan and instructed: "In employing men the state finds it better to use those who have erred than those who have merely succeeded.

entries.zh: 銓素有才學，博洽諳練，朕特召用，以觀自新。」
entries.en: Quan has long had talent and learning and is broadly versed and experienced; I specially recall him to see whether he will reform."
entries.literal: Quan has long had talent and learning, is broadly versed and experienced—I specially recall him to see whether he will reform."

entries.zh: 銓至，召見，又與承疇、文程等同夕對論翰林官賢否，上曰：「朕將親試之！」
entries.en: When Quan arrived and was granted audience, the emperor that evening discussed with Chengchou, Wencheng, and others whether the Hanlin officials were worthy, and said: "I shall examine them myself!"
entries.literal: When Quan arrived and was granted audience, the emperor again discussed that evening with Chengchou, Wencheng, and others whether Hanlin officials were worthy or not, and said: "I shall personally examine them!"

entries.zh: 銓奏曰：「南人優於文而行不符，北人短於文而行或善。
entries.en: Quan replied: "Southerners are superior in letters but their conduct does not match; northerners are weaker in letters but their conduct may be good.
entries.literal: Quan memorialized: "Southerners are superior in letters but their conduct does not match; northerners are deficient in letters but their conduct may be good.

entries.zh: 今取文行兼優者用之可也。」
entries.en: Take those who excel in both letters and conduct and employ them."
entries.literal: Now take those who excel in both letters and conduct and employ them."

entries.zh: 上頷之，仍授弘文院大學士。
entries.en: The emperor nodded in agreement and again appointed him Grand Secretary of the Hongwen Institute.
entries.literal: The emperor nodded in agreement and again appointed him Grand Secretary of the Hongwen Institute.

entries.zh: 以議總兵任珍罪坐欺飾論絞，上命寬之。
entries.en: For discussing the punishment of Regional Commander Ren Zhen and being convicted of deceitful concealment with a sentence of strangulation, the emperor ordered leniency.
entries.literal: For discussing the punishment of Regional Commander Ren Zhen and being convicted of deceitful concealment with a sentence of strangulation, the emperor ordered leniency.

entries.zh: 銓入謝，奏對失旨，諭誡之。
entries.en: Quan entered to give thanks; his replies missed the imperial intent and he was admonished by edict.
entries.literal: Quan entered to give thanks; his replies missed the imperial intent and he was admonished by edict.

entries.zh: 龔鼎孳為左都御史，复劾銓，上命指實。
entries.en: Gong Dingzi, as Censor-in-Chief of the Left, again memorialized against Quan; the emperor ordered him to cite specific facts.
entries.literal: Gong Dingzi, as Censor-in-Chief of the Left, again memorialized against Quan; the emperor ordered specific facts.

entries.zh: 鼎孳言銓罪過頗多，惟以密勿票擬，非如諸曹有實可指，上切責鼎孳。
entries.en: Dingzi said Quan's offenses were many, but because he handled confidential memorial drafting with approval slips, unlike other offices there were no concrete facts to cite; the emperor sharply rebuked Dingzi.
entries.literal: Dingzi said Quan's offenses were many, but because he handled confidential memorial drafting with approval slips, unlike other offices there were no concrete facts to cite; the emperor sharply rebuked Dingzi.

entries.zh: 十二年，居母喪，命入直如故。
entries.en: In the twelfth year, while in mourning for his mother, he was ordered to continue entering duty as before.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year, while in mourning for his mother, he was ordered to enter duty as before.

entries.zh: 尋加少師兼太子太師。
entries.en: Soon he was given the added titles of Junior Preceptor and Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: Soon he was given the added titles of Junior Preceptor and Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 十三年，上以銓衰老，加太保致仕，仍令在左右備顧問，銓疏請回籍，許之。
entries.en: In the thirteenth year, because the emperor considered Quan aged, he was given the added title of Grand Guardian and ordered to retire, yet still to remain nearby as a consultant; Quan memorialized asking to return to his native place and was permitted.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year, because the emperor considered Quan aged, he was given the added title of Grand Guardian and ordered to retire, yet still to remain nearby as consultant; Quan memorialized asking to return to his native place and was permitted.

entries.zh: 十六年，改設內閣，命以原銜兼中和殿大學士。
entries.en: In the sixteenth year the Cabinet was newly established, and he was ordered to serve concurrently as Grand Secretary of the Zhonghe Hall under his former title.
entries.literal: In the sixteenth year the Cabinet was newly established and he was ordered to serve concurrently as Grand Secretary of the Zhonghe Hall with his former title.

entries.zh: 康熙十一年，卒，諡文敏。
entries.en: In Kangxi 11 he died and was given the posthumous title Wenmin.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year of Kangxi he died and was given the posthumous title Wenmin.

entries.zh: 旋命削諡。
entries.en: Shortly afterward he was ordered stripped of the posthumous title.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward he was ordered stripped of the posthumous title.

entries.zh: 十六年，上以正宗器量狹隘，終日務詩文，廷議輒以己意為是，降旨嚴飭，並諭曰：「朕委任大臣，期始終相成，以愜簡拔初念。
entries.en: In the sixteenth year, because the emperor considered Zhengzong narrow in capacity, devoted all day to poetry and prose, and in court deliberations always held his own opinion correct, a stern admonitory edict was issued, also instructing: "I entrust great ministers expecting mutual completion from start to finish, to satisfy the original intent of selection.
entries.literal: In the sixteenth year, because the emperor considered Zhengzong narrow in capacity, devoted all day to poetry and prose, and in court deliberations always held his own opinion correct, a stern admonitory edict was issued, also instructing: "I entrust great ministers expecting mutual completion from start to finish, to satisfy the original intent of selection.

entries.zh: 故不忍加罪，時加申戒。
entries.en: Therefore I have been unwilling to punish him and have repeatedly issued warnings.
entries.literal: Therefore I have been unwilling to punish him and have repeatedly issued warnings.

entries.zh: 當痛改前非，稱朕優容寬恕之意。」
entries.en: He ought to reform his past faults thoroughly and respond to my intent of forbearance and forgiveness."
entries.literal: He ought to reform his past faults thoroughly and respond to my intent of forbearance and forgiveness."

entries.zh: 十七年，自陳乞罷，不允。
entries.en: In the seventeenth year he memorialized on his own asking to be dismissed; the request was not granted.
entries.literal: In the seventeenth year he memorialized on his own asking to be dismissed; the request was not granted.

entries.zh: 左都御史魏裔介劾「正宗自陳奏內不敘上諭切責，無人臣禮。
entries.en: Censor-in-Chief of the Left Wei Yijie memorialized: "In his self-statement memorial Zhengzong did not recount the emperor's stern rebuke—this lacks the propriety of a minister.
