entries.literal: Censor-in-Chief of the Left Wei Yijie memorialized: "In his self-statement memorial Zhengzong did not recount the emperor's stern rebuke—this lacks the propriety of a minister.

entries.zh: 李昌祚叛案有名，票擬內升。
entries.en: Li Changzuo was named in the rebel case, yet on the approval slip he was drafted for promotion.
entries.literal: Li Changzuo was named in the rebel case, yet on the approval slip he was drafted for promotion.

entries.zh: 先後薦董國祥、梁羽明，今皆事敗，被劾不自檢舉。
entries.en: He had successively recommended Dong Guoxiang and Liang Yuming; now both their affairs have failed, yet when memorialized against he did not report himself.
entries.literal: He had successively recommended Dong Guoxiang and Liang Yuming; now both their affairs have failed, yet when memorialized against he did not report himself.

entries.zh: 欺君之罪何辭？
entries.en: What excuse is there for the offense of deceiving the ruler?
entries.literal: What excuse is there for the offense of deceiving the ruler?

entries.zh: 正宗與張縉彥為友，縉彥序正宗詩曰'將明之才'，詭譎尤不可解。
entries.en: Zhengzong and Zhang Jinyan were friends; Jinyan prefaced Zhengzong's poetry with the words "talent to govern and clarify," which is especially inexplicable and sinister.
entries.literal: Zhengzong and Zhang Jinyan were friends; Jinyan prefaced Zhengzong's poetry with the words "talent to govern and clarify," which is especially inexplicable and sinister.

entries.zh: 正宗弟正學，為鄭成功總兵，正宗囑巡撫耿焞躐升中軍。
entries.en: Zhengzong's younger brother Zhengxue was a regional commander under Zheng Chenggong; Zhengzong instructed Governor Geng Tun to promote him by skipping ranks to middle army commander.
entries.literal: Zhengzong's younger brother Zhengxue was a regional commander under Zheng Chenggong; Zhengzong instructed Governor Geng Tun to promote him by skipping ranks to middle army commander.

entries.zh: 蠹國亂政，其事非一端。
entries.en: Harming the state and disordering government—his offenses were not limited to one kind.
entries.literal: Harming the state and disordering government—his offenses were not limited to one kind.

entries.zh: 請乾斷以杜禍萌」。
entries.en: I ask for decisive judgment to cut off the sprouting of calamity."
entries.literal: I ask for decisive judgment to cut off the sprouting of calamity."

entries.zh: 御史季振宜繼劾，亦及國祥、正學，並正宗貪賄營利諸事。
entries.en: Censor Ji Zhenyi followed with a memorial, also implicating Guoxiang and Zhengxue, together with Zhengzong's taking bribes and seeking profit in various matters.
entries.literal: Censor Ji Zhenyi followed with a memorial, also implicating Guoxiang and Zhengxue, together with Zhengzong's taking bribes and seeking profit in various matters.

entries.zh: 正宗疏辨，略謂：「李昌祚為叛黨，裔介身為法司，何不早行糾參？
entries.en: Zhengzong memorialized in his defense, stating in part: "Li Changzuo was of the rebel faction—Yijie himself was in the judiciary; why did he not memorialize against him early?
entries.literal: Zhengzong memorialized in his defense, stating in part: "Li Changzuo was of the rebel faction—Yijie himself was in the judiciary; why did he not memorialize against him early?

entries.zh: 例凡薦舉之官，在本任不職，追坐舉主。
entries.en: By precedent, whenever an official who was recommended fails in his current post, the recommender is held accountable.
entries.literal: By precedent, whenever an official who was recommended fails in his current post, the recommender is held accountable.

entries.zh: 國祥、羽明皆升任後得罪。
entries.en: Guoxiang and Yuming both offended only after being promoted to higher posts.
entries.literal: Guoxiang and Yuming both offended only after being promoted to higher posts.

entries.zh: 縉彥序臣詩有曰'將明之才'，臣詩稿見存，縉彥序未見此語。」
entries.en: Jinyan's preface to my poetry is said to contain the words "talent to govern and clarify"; my poetry manuscript still exists, and Jinyan's preface does not contain this phrase."
entries.literal: Jinyan's preface to my poetry is said to contain the words "talent to govern and clarify"; my poetry manuscript still exists, and Jinyan's preface does not contain this phrase."

entries.zh: 疏入，上奪正宗官，下王大臣會鞫；
entries.en: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor stripped Zhengzong of office and sent the case to the prince and great ministers for joint interrogation;
entries.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor stripped Zhengzong of office and sent the case down to the prince and great ministers for joint interrogation;

entries.zh: 亦責裔介、振宜不早糾參，並奪官待質。
entries.en: he also rebuked Yijie and Zhenyi for not memorializing early, and stripped both of office pending verification.
entries.literal: he also rebuked Yijie and Zhenyi for not memorializing early, and stripped both of office pending verification.

entries.zh: 旋議上裔介、振宜劾正宗罪狀鞫實者十一事，罪當絞。
entries.en: Shortly afterward the deliberation found eleven counts in Yijie and Zhenyi's memorial against Zhengzong substantiated by interrogation; the offense warranted strangulation.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward the deliberation submitted upward found eleven counts in Yijie and Zhenyi's memorial against Zhengzong substantiated by interrogation; the offense warranted strangulation.

entries.zh: 上斥「正宗性質暴戾，器量褊淺，持論偏私，處事執謬。
entries.en: The emperor rebuked him: "Zhengzong's nature is violent and harsh, his capacity narrow and shallow, his opinions partial and private, and his handling of affairs stubbornly mistaken.
entries.literal: The emperor rebuked him: "Zhengzong's nature is violent and harsh, his capacity narrow and shallow, his opinions partial and private, and his handling of affairs stubbornly mistaken.

entries.zh: 惟事沽名好勝，罔顧大體，罪戾滋甚。
entries.en: He cares only for reputation and rivalry, heedless of the larger interest, and his offenses grow ever worse.
entries.literal: He cares only for reputation and rivalry, heedless of the larger interest, and his offenses grow ever worse.

entries.zh: 從寬免死，籍家產之半，入旗，不許回籍」。
entries.en: Showing leniency he is spared death; half his household property is confiscated; he enters the banner and is not permitted to return to his native place."
entries.literal: Showing leniency he is spared death; half his household property is registered and confiscated; he enters the banner and is not permitted to return to his native place."

entries.zh: 十八年，聖祖即位，以世祖遺詔及正宗罪狀，當置重典，愍其衰老，貸之。
entries.en: In the eighteenth year, when the Shengzu ascended the throne, in view of the Shizu's testamentary edict and Zhengzong's offenses he ought to have received severe punishment; pitying his age, the emperor pardoned him.
entries.literal: In the eighteenth year, when the Shengzu ascended the throne, in view of the Shizu's testamentary edict and Zhengzong's offenses he ought to have received severe punishment; pitying his age, the emperor pardoned him.

entries.zh: 未幾病卒。
entries.en: Before long he died of illness.
entries.literal: Before long he died of illness.

entries.zh: 十三年，上幸南苑，召諸大臣入對，諭之遴曰：「朕不念爾前罪，屢申誥誡，嘗以朕言告人乎？
entries.en: In the thirteenth year the emperor visited the Southern Park and summoned the great ministers for audience; he instructed Zhilin: "I do not hold your former offenses against you and have repeatedly issued admonitory edicts—have you ever told others what I have said?
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year the emperor visited the Southern Park and summoned the great ministers for audience; he instructed Zhilin: "I do not hold your former offenses against you and have repeatedly issued admonitory edicts—have you ever told others what I have said?

entries.zh: 抑自思所行亦曾少改乎？」
entries.en: Or do you yourself think your conduct has changed even a little?"
entries.literal: Or do you yourself think your conduct has changed even a little?"

entries.zh: 之遴奏曰：「上教臣，臣安敢不改？
entries.en: Zhilin replied: "Your Majesty has instructed me—how would I dare not reform?
entries.literal: Zhilin memorialized: "Your Majesty has instructed me—how would I dare not reform?

entries.zh: 特臣才疏學淺，不能仰報上恩。」
entries.en: It is only that my talent is meager and my learning shallow, and I cannot repay Your Majesty's grace."
entries.literal: It is only that my talent is meager and my learning shallow, and I cannot repay Your Majesty's grace from below."

entries.zh: 上曰：「朕非不知之遴等朋黨而用之，但欲資其才，故任以職。
entries.en: The emperor said: "It is not that I do not know Zhilin and others form factions—I employ them only to make use of their talent, and therefore assign them office.
entries.literal: The emperor said: "It is not that I do not know Zhilin and others form factions—I employ them only to make use of their talent, and therefore assign them office.

entries.zh: 且時時教飭之者，亦冀其改過效忠耳。」
entries.en: Moreover, in constantly instructing and admonishing them, I also hope they will reform their faults and serve loyally."
entries.literal: Moreover, in constantly instructing and admonishing them, I also hope they will reform their faults and serve loyally."

entries.zh: 因責左副都御史魏裔介等媕阿緘默，裔介退，具疏劾之遴植黨營私，當上詰問，但云「才疏學淺」，良心已昧；
entries.en: He thereupon rebuked Left Vice Censor-in-Chief Wei Yijie and others for fawning compliance and silence; Yijie withdrew and submitted a detailed memorial impeaching Zhilin for forming factions and pursuing private ends; when the emperor questioned him, he could only say "my talent is meager and my learning shallow"—his conscience was already clouded;
entries.literal: He thereupon rebuked Left Vice Censor-in-Chief Wei Yijie and others for fawning compliance and silence; Yijie withdrew and submitted a detailed memorial impeaching Zhilin for forming factions and pursuing private ends; when the emperor questioned him, he could only say "my talent is meager and my learning shallow"—his conscience was already clouded;

entries.zh: 並言之遴諷禮部尚書胡世安舉知府沈令式，旋為總督李輝祖所劾，是為結黨之據。
entries.en: he also stated that Zhilin had prompted Minister of Rites Hu Shi'an to recommend Prefect Shen Lingshi, who was soon memorialized against by Governor-General Li Huizu—this was evidence of faction forming.
entries.literal: he also stated that Zhilin had prompted Minister of Rites Hu Shi'an to recommend Prefect Shen Lingshi, who was soon memorialized against by Governor Li Huizu—this was evidence of faction forming.

entries.zh: 給事中王楨又劾之遴市權豪縱，昨蒙詰責，不思閉門省罪，即於次日遨遊靈佑宮，逍遙恣肆，罪不容誅。
entries.en: Supervising secretary Wang Zhen again memorialized against Zhilin for trading in power and acting with arrogant license; having just received imperial rebuke, he did not think to shut his doors and reflect on his guilt but on the very next day wandered at leisure in the Lingyou Palace, roaming freely and unrestrained—an offense that could not be spared execution.
entries.literal: Supervising secretary Wang Zhen again memorialized against Zhilin for trading in power and acting with arrogant license; having just received imperial rebuke, he did not think to shut his doors and reflect on his guilt but on the very next day wandered at leisure in the Lingyou Palace, roaming freely and unrestrained—an offense that could not be spared execution.

entries.zh: 之遴疏引罪，有云：「南北各親其親，各友其友。」
entries.en: Zhilin memorialized accepting guilt, stating: "North and south each honor their own kin and each befriend their own friends."
entries.literal: Zhilin memorialized accepting guilt, stating: "North and south each honor their own kin and each befriend their own friends."

entries.zh: 上益不懌，下吏部嚴議，命以原官發盛京居住。
entries.en: The emperor grew still more displeased; the matter was referred to the Ministry of Personnel for strict deliberation, and he was ordered sent to live at Mukden under his former title.
entries.literal: The emperor grew still more displeased; the matter was sent down to the Ministry of Personnel for strict deliberation, and he was ordered sent to live at Mukden under his former title.

entries.zh: 是冬，復命回京入旗。
entries.en: That winter he was again ordered to return to the capital and enter the banner.
entries.literal: That winter he was again ordered to return to the capital and enter the banner.

entries.zh: 十五年，復坐賄結內監吳良輔，鞫實，論斬，命奪官，籍其家，流徙尚陽堡，死徙所。
entries.en: In the fifteenth year he was again convicted of bribing and forming ties with eunuch Wu Liangfu; when interrogation established the facts he was sentenced to decapitation; he was stripped of office, his household property was confiscated, and he was exiled to Shangyang Fort, where he died in exile.
entries.literal: In the fifteenth year he was again convicted of bribing and forming ties with eunuch Wu Liangfu; when interrogation established the facts he was sentenced to decapitation; he was ordered stripped of office, his household property registered and confiscated, and he was exiled to Shangyang Fort, where he died in exile.

entries.zh: 劉正宗，字可宗，山東安丘人。
entries.en: Liu Zhengzong, styled Kezong, was a native of Anqiu in Shandong.
entries.literal: Liu Zhengzong, styled Kezong, was a native of Anqiu in Shandong.

entries.zh: 明崇禎進士，自推官授編修。
entries.en: A jinshi of the Ming Chongzhen reign, he was promoted from magistrate's aide to compiler.
entries.literal: A jinshi in the Chongzhen reign of the Ming, he was promoted from magistrate's aide to compiler.

entries.zh: 福王時，授中允。
entries.en: Under the Prince of Fu he was appointed junior mentor.
entries.literal: In the time of the Prince of Fu he was appointed junior mentor.

entries.zh: 順治二年，以薦起國史院編修。
entries.en: In Shunzhi 2, on recommendation, he was appointed compiler of the Historiography Institute.
entries.literal: In the second year of Shunzhi, on recommendation, he was appointed compiler of the Historiography Institute.

entries.zh: 累遷秘書院學士。
entries.en: He rose in succession to academician of the Secretariat Institute.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to academician of the Secretariat Institute.

entries.zh: 十四年，授吏部侍郎，擢弘文院大學士。
entries.en: In the fourteenth year he was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel and promoted to Grand Secretary of the Hongwen Institute.
entries.literal: In the fourteenth year he was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel and promoted to Grand Secretary of the Hongwen Institute.

entries.zh: 吏部尚書缺員，諭以「正宗清正耿介，堪勝此任，加太子太保，管吏部尚書」。
entries.en: When the post of Minister of Personnel fell vacant, an edict stated: "Zhengzong is upright, pure, and firm—he can bear this responsibility; give him the added title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and charge him with managing the Ministry of Personnel."
entries.literal: When the post of Minister of Personnel fell vacant, an edict stated: "Zhengzong is upright, pure, and firm—he can bear this responsibility; give him the added title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and charge him with managing the Ministry of Personnel."

entries.zh: 剛林，瓜爾佳氏，字公茂，滿洲正黃旗人，世居蘇完。
entries.en: Ganglin, of the Guwalgiya clan, styled Gongmao, was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner from a family that had long lived in Suwan.
entries.literal: Ganglin, of the Guwalgiya clan, styled Gongmao, was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner whose family had long resided in Suwan.

entries.zh: 初來歸，隸正藍旗，屬郡王阿達禮。
entries.en: When he first came over to submit, he was assigned to the Plain Blue Banner and placed under Prince Adali.
entries.literal: When he first came to submit, he was enrolled in the Plain Blue Banner and placed under Prince of the Second Rank Adali.

entries.zh: 授筆帖式，掌繙譯漢文。
entries.en: He was appointed a bithe clerk and placed in charge of translating Chinese documents.
entries.literal: He was appointed a bithe clerk and put in charge of translating Chinese texts.

entries.zh: 天聰八年，以漢文應試，中式舉人，命直文館。
entries.en: In Tiancong 8 he sat for the examination in Chinese, passed as a provincial graduate, and was ordered to serve in the Literary Institute.
entries.literal: In the eighth year of Tiancong he entered the examination in Chinese, passed as a provincial graduate, and was ordered to serve in the Literary Institute.

entries.zh: 崇德元年，授國史院大學士，與範文程、希福等參與政事。
entries.en: In Chongde 1 he was made Grand Secretary of the Historiography Institute and, with Fan Wencheng, Xifu, and others, took part in state affairs.
entries.literal: In the first year of Chongde he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Historiography Institute and, together with Fan Wencheng, Xifu, and others, participated in governing affairs.

entries.zh: 疏請重定部院承政以下官各五等，又疏請定試士之法，皆報可。
entries.en: He submitted memorials asking that officials from ministry and office chiefs downward be graded in five ranks each, and again asking that the method of examining scholars be fixed; both requests were approved.
entries.literal: He memorialized asking that the ranks of officials from chief administrators of ministries and offices downward be set at five grades each, and again memorialized to fix the method of examining scholars; all were approved.

entries.zh: 太宗四征不庭，疆宇日闢。
entries.en: The Taizong campaigned four times against recalcitrant foes, and the empire steadily expanded.
entries.literal: The Taizong four times campaigned against those who did not submit, and the realm daily expanded.

entries.zh: 剛林屢奉使軍前，宣布威德，咸稱上旨。
entries.en: Ganglin was repeatedly sent to the front to proclaim the throne's majesty and virtue, and everywhere he spoke in the emperor's name.
entries.literal: Ganglin repeatedly went on missions to the front, proclaiming majesty and virtue, and everywhere conveyed the emperor's will.

entries.zh: 積功，授世職牛錄章京。
entries.en: For accumulated merit he was granted the hereditary rank of niru janggin.
entries.literal: For accumulated merit he was granted the hereditary office of niru janggin.

entries.zh: 八年，阿達禮有罪，改隸正黃旗。
entries.en: In the eighth year Adali was found guilty, and Ganglin was transferred to the Plain Yellow Banner.
entries.literal: In the eighth year Adali was guilty of an offense, and Ganglin was transferred to the Plain Yellow Banner.

entries.zh: 七年，睿親王薨，上命吏、刑、工三部增設滿洲尚書各一，授譚泰吏部尚書。
entries.en: In the seventh year, after Prince Rui's death, the throne added a Manchu minister to each of the Personnel, Punishments, and Works boards; Tan Tai became Minister of Personnel.
entries.literal: In the seventh year Prince Rui died; the sovereign ordered that each of the Boards of Personnel, Punishments, and Works add one Manchu minister, and Tan Tai was appointed Minister of Personnel.

entries.zh: 八年，世祖親政，追論睿親王罪狀，大學士剛林、祁充格皆坐誅，罪不及譚泰。
entries.en: In the eighth year the Shizu took power and prosecuted Prince Rui's crimes; Gang Lin and Qi Chongge were executed, but Tan Tai was not implicated.
entries.literal: In the eighth year the Shizu assumed personal rule and reviewed Prince Rui's crimes; Grand Secretaries Gang Lin and Qi Chongge were both executed, but the guilt did not reach Tan Tai.

entries.zh: 時圖賴已卒，索尼方罪廢，譚泰毀圖賴墓室，洩舊忿。
entries.en: Tulai was dead and Sonin had just been disgraced; Tan Tai wrecked Tulai's tomb, settling an old score.
entries.literal: Tulai was already dead and Sonin had just been punished and dismissed; Tan Tai destroyed Tulai's tomb chamber, venting an old grudge.

entries.zh: 五月，御史張煊劾大學士陳名夏等，下王大臣會鞫。
entries.en: In the fifth month Censor Zhang Xuan impeached Chen Mingxia and other grand secretaries; princes and ministers were convened to try the case.
entries.literal: In the fifth month Censor Zhang Xuan impeached Grand Secretary Chen Mingxia and others; the case was sent to the princes and ministers for joint trial.

entries.zh: 譚泰袒名夏，讞上，命未下，譚泰前奏，言煊劾皆虛，且所舉諸事皆在赦前，煊以外轉嫌，誣名夏等死罪，當反坐，煊遂見法。
entries.en: Tan Tai protected Mingxia; before the sentence was issued he argued that Zhang's charges were false and predated the amnesty—that Zhang, posted elsewhere, bore a grudge and had framed Mingxia for death, and should suffer the penalty himself; Zhang was executed.
entries.literal: Tan Tai shielded Mingxia; when the verdict was submitted the order had not yet been issued; Tan Tai advanced and memorialized that Xuan's charges were all false and that the matters cited had all occurred before the amnesty—Xuan, transferred outside, bore a grudge and had falsely charged Mingxia and others with capital crimes and should suffer the penalty in reverse; Xuan was then executed.

entries.zh: 睿親王攝政，諸王多與忤。
entries.en: Under Prince Rui's regency many princes fell foul of him.
entries.literal: When Prince Rui acted as regent, many princes clashed with him.

entries.zh: 鄭親王濟爾哈朗降郡王，旋复爵。
entries.en: Prince Zheng Jirhalang was demoted to commandery prince, then restored.
entries.literal: Prince Zheng Jirhalang was reduced to commandery prince, then soon had his rank restored.

entries.zh: 初以端重親王博洛、敬謹親王尼堪佐理事，亦以專擅降爵。
entries.en: Princes Duanzhong Boluo and Jingjin Nikan, who had helped govern, were likewise demoted for overreaching.
entries.literal: At first Princes Duanzhong Boluo and Jingjin Nikan assisted in government and were also reduced for arbitrary conduct.

entries.zh: 博爾輝及諸大臣羅什、額克親、吳拜、蘇拜皆謹事睿親王，從王獵喀喇城。
entries.en: Boerhui and ministers Roshi, Ekeqin, Wubai, and Subai all served Prince Rui faithfully and hunted with him at Kalacheng.
entries.literal: Boerhui and the ministers Roshi, Ekeqin, Wubai, and Subai all dutifully served Prince Rui and accompanied the prince hunting at Kalacheng.

entries.zh: 王薨，喪還。
entries.en: When the prince died the funeral cortege returned.
entries.literal: When the prince died the funeral procession returned.

entries.zh: 英親王阿濟格為睿親王同母兄，欲繼王柄政，博爾輝等與阿爾津共發其罪，英親王奪爵幽禁，賞諸告者，博爾輝進世職二等精奇尼哈番。
entries.en: Prince Ying Ajige, Dorgon's elder brother, sought his power; Boerhui and A'erjin exposed him; Prince Ying was disgraced and confined; the informers were rewarded and Boerhui raised to second-class jingqi nihaan.
entries.literal: Prince Ying Ajige, Prince Rui's elder brother by the same mother, wished to succeed to the prince's power; Boerhui and others, together with A'erjin, exposed his crimes; Prince Ying was stripped of rank and confined; the informers were rewarded; Boerhui was advanced to hereditary second-rank jingqi nihaan.

entries.zh: 博爾輝等傳睿親王遺言，复理事二王親王爵，以告兩黃旗大臣。
entries.en: Boerhui relayed Prince Rui's last wish to restore Boluo and Nikan to princely rank and told the Yellow Banner ministers.
entries.literal: Boerhui and others transmitted Prince Rui's dying words, restoring the two princes who had assisted in government to princely rank, and reported this to the two Yellow Banner ministers.

entries.zh: 居月餘，命未下，博爾輝有疾，穆爾泰往視之，博爾輝以為言。
entries.en: After a month no order came; Boerhui fell ill; Murutai visited him and Boerhui complained of the delay.
entries.literal: After more than a month the order had not been issued; Boerhui fell ill; Murutai visited him, and Boerhui spoke of the matter.

entries.zh: 穆爾泰告額爾德赫，額爾德赫告敬謹郡王尼堪，遂與端重郡王博洛訴於鄭親王。
entries.en: Murutai told E'erdehe, who told Prince Jingjin Nikan; they and Prince Duanzhong Boluo appealed to Prince Zheng.
entries.literal: Murutai told E'erdehe; E'erdehe told Commandery Prince Jingjin Nikan; they then appealed with Commandery Prince Duanzhong Boluo to Prince Zheng.

entries.zh: 八年正月，复二王爵。
entries.en: In the first month of the eighth year the two princes were restored.
entries.literal: In the first month of the eighth year the two princes' ranks were restored.

entries.zh: 越八日，執博爾輝等下獄，坐博爾輝、羅什動搖國事，蠱惑人心，論死，籍其家。
entries.en: Eight days later Boerhui and Roshi were arrested for subverting the state and misleading the court; death was proposed and their estates seized.
entries.literal: Eight days later Boerhui and others were seized and imprisoned; Boerhui and Roshi were charged with shaking state affairs and deluding hearts; death was proposed and their households confiscated.

entries.zh: 額克親削宗室籍，及吳拜、蘇拜皆奪官為民。
entries.en: Ekeqin was struck from the clan rolls; Wubai and Subai were reduced to commoners.
entries.literal: Ekeqin was struck from the imperial clan register; Wubai and Subai were all stripped of office and made commoners.

entries.zh: 議上，得旨：「朕每聞刑人，殊不忍。
entries.en: When the verdict went up, the emperor replied: "I shrink from every execution.
entries.literal: When the deliberation was submitted, an edict came: "Whenever I hear of punishing people, I am deeply unwilling.

entries.zh: 二人罪當誅，姑宥死何如？」
entries.en: These two deserve death—might we spare them for now?"
entries.literal: These two men's crimes merit death—might we for now spare their lives?"

entries.zh: 王大臣復以初議上，乃誅死。
entries.en: The princes and ministers resubmitted the original sentence, and both were executed.
entries.literal: The princes and ministers resubmitted the original proposal, and they were executed.

entries.zh: 何洛會隸肅親王豪格，頗見任使。
entries.en: He Luohui served under Prince Su Hooge and was much trusted.
entries.literal: He Luohui was attached to Prince Su Hooge and was much employed and trusted.

entries.zh: 世祖即位，睿親王攝政，與肅親王有隙。
entries.en: When the Shizu came to the throne, Prince Rui was regent and at odds with Prince Su.
entries.literal: When the Shizu ascended the throne, Prince Rui acted as regent and was at odds with Prince Su.

entries.zh: 何洛會訐肅親王與兩黃旗大臣揚善、俄莫克圖、伊成格、羅碩將謀亂，肅親王坐削爵，揚善等皆棄市。
entries.en: He Luohui accused Prince Su and the Plain and Bordered Yellow Banner ministers Yangshan, Emoketu, Yichengge, and Luoshuo of plotting revolt; Prince Su lost his title and they were executed.
entries.literal: He Luohui denounced Prince Su and the two Yellow Banner ministers Yangshan, Emoketu, Yichengge, and Luoshuo as plotting rebellion; Prince Su was stripped of his rank, and Yangshan and the others were all executed in the market.

entries.zh: 賞何洛會告姦，籍俄莫克圖、伊成格家畀之，授世職二等甲喇章京。
entries.en: He Luohui was rewarded for the denunciation; Emoketu and Yichengge's estates were given him, and he received a hereditary second-rank jalan colonelcy.
entries.literal: He Luohui was rewarded for exposing treachery; the households of Emoketu and Yichengge were confiscated and given to him, and he was granted a hereditary office as second-rank jalan janggin.

entries.zh: 尋從睿親王入關，擊李自成，逐至慶都。
entries.en: He soon followed Prince Rui into China, fought Li Zicheng, and pursued him to Qingdu.
entries.literal: Soon he followed Prince Rui in entering the Pass, attacked Li Zicheng, and pursued him to Qingdu.

entries.zh: 還，睿親王令奉表迎世祖，擢內大臣，留守盛京。
entries.en: On the return march Prince Rui sent him to welcome the Shizu; he was made an inner minister and left to hold Mukden.
entries.literal: On returning, Prince Rui ordered him to present a memorial welcoming the Shizu; he was promoted to inner minister and left to guard Mukden.

entries.zh: 阿哈尼堪將左翼，碩詹將右翼，並於熊耀城、錦州、寧遠、鳳凰城、興京、義州、新城、牛莊、岫岩城各置城守官，皆統於何洛會。
entries.en: Ahanikan led the left wing and Shuozhan the right; garrisons were posted at Xiongyao, Jinzhou, Ningyuan, Fenghuang, Xingjing, Yizhou, Xincheng, Niuzhuang, and Xiuyan—all under He Luohui.
entries.literal: Ahanikan commanded the left wing and Shuozhan the right; garrison commanders were placed at Xiongyao, Jinzhou, Ningyuan, Fenghuangcheng, Xingjing, Yizhou, Xincheng, Niuzhuang, and Xiuyancheng—all under He Luohui's overall command.

entries.zh: 肅親王師還，貝子屯齊等訐王諸悖妄狀，何洛會復從而證之，遂坐奪爵，以幽系終。
entries.en: When Prince Su returned, Beizi Tunqi and others impeached him; He Luohui testified again, and the prince lost his title and died under house arrest.
entries.literal: When Prince Su's army returned, Beile Tunqi and others denounced the prince's many rebellious acts; He Luohui again bore witness, and the prince was stripped of his rank and ended his life in close confinement.

entries.zh: 睿親王取肅親王福金，召肅親王諸子入府校射，何洛會詈之曰：「見此鬼魅，不覺心悸！」
entries.en: Prince Rui took Prince Su's consort Fujin and summoned Su's sons to shoot in his mansion; He Luohui swore at them: "These specters make my heart quail!"
entries.literal: Prince Rui took Prince Su's consort Fujin and summoned Prince Su's sons into the mansion for archery practice; He Luohui cursed them, saying: "At the sight of these demons my heart cannot but tremble!"

entries.zh: 尚書譚泰聞其語。
entries.en: Minister Tan Tai heard what he said.
entries.literal: Minister Tan Tai heard his words.

entries.zh: 及睿親王薨，世祖親政，何洛會語貝子錫翰曰：「兩黃旗大臣與我相惡，我嘗訐告肅親王，今豈肯容我？」
entries.en: After Prince Rui's death, when the Shizu took power, He Luohui told Beizi Xi Han: "The Yellow Banner ministers hate me; I denounced Prince Su—will they spare me now?"
entries.literal: When Prince Rui died and the Shizu assumed personal rule, He Luohui said to Beile Xi Han: "The two Yellow Banner ministers bear me ill will; I once denounced Prince Su—will they now tolerate me?"

entries.zh: 八年二月，蘇克薩哈等訐睿親王將率兩白旗移駐永平，且私具上服禦，及薨用斂，何洛會、羅什、博爾惠等皆知狀。
entries.en: In the second month of the eighth year Sukesaha charged that Prince Rui had planned to move the White Banners to Yongping, had secretly made imperial robes, and had been buried in them—He Luohui, Roshi, Boerhui, and others knew it all.
entries.literal: In the second month of the eighth year Sukesaha and others denounced Prince Rui for intending to move the two White Banners to garrison at Yongping, for privately preparing imperial robes, and for using them at his burial when he died—He Luohui, Roshi, Boerhui, and others all knew the circumstances.

entries.zh: 時羅什、博爾惠已先誅，執何洛會，下王大臣會鞫。
entries.en: Roshi and Boerhui were already dead; He Luohui was arrested and tried by the princes and ministers.
entries.literal: Roshi and Boerhui had already been executed; He Luohui was seized and the case sent to the princes and ministers for joint trial.

entries.zh: 譚泰、錫翰各以何洛會語告，又追論誣告肅親王罪，與其兄胡錫並磔死，籍其家。
entries.en: Tan Tai and Xi Han repeated his words; his false charge against Prince Su was reviewed as well; he and his brother Husu were executed by dismemberment and their estates seized.
entries.literal: Tan Tai and Xi Han each reported He Luohui's words; his crime of falsely denouncing Prince Su was also reviewed; he and his elder brother Husu were dismembered and executed together, and their households were confiscated.

entries.zh: 崇德二年，固山額真都類坐事下兵部待鞫，兵部參政穆爾泰令諸在系者避都類。
entries.en: In Chongde 2 banner commander Dulei was held at the Board of War; Murutai ordered other prisoners to avoid him.
entries.literal: In the second year of Chongde gusa ejen Dulei was implicated in a case and held at the Board of War awaiting trial; participating secretary Murutai of the Board ordered all detainees to avoid Dulei.

entries.zh: 或以告冷僧機，聞於上，穆爾泰及同官皆坐降罰，授冷僧機一等侍衛。
entries.en: Someone told Leng Sengji; the emperor heard; Murutai and his colleagues were demoted; Leng Sengji was made a first-rank guardsman.
entries.literal: Someone reported this to Leng Sengji; it reached the sovereign; Murutai and his colleagues were all punished with demotion; Leng Sengji was appointed first-rank guardsman.

entries.zh: 七年，祖大壽來歸，上幸牧馬所，命內大臣侍衛與大壽等校射，中的者有所賜，冷僧機得駝一。
entries.en: In the seventh year Zu Dashou submitted; at an archery contest with him Leng Sengji hit the mark and won a camel.
entries.literal: In the seventh year Zu Dashou came over; the sovereign visited the horse pastures and ordered inner ministers and guardsmen to compete in archery with Dashou and others; those who hit the target received gifts; Leng Sengji won a camel.

entries.zh: 世祖即位，授內大臣。
entries.en: When the Shizu came to the throne he was made an inner minister.
entries.literal: When the Shizu ascended the throne he was appointed inner minister.

entries.zh: 順治二年，進二等阿思哈尼哈番兼拖沙喇哈番。
entries.en: In Shunzhi 2 he was raised to second-class ashan nihaan with an added tosara haan.
entries.literal: In the second year of Shunzhi he was advanced to second-rank ashan nihaan with an additional tosara haan.

entries.zh: 譚泰訐索尼，引冷僧機為證，謝未聞，坐徇庇，當削世職籍沒，上貰之。
entries.en: When Tan Tai denounced Sonin and called Leng Sengji as witness, he pleaded ignorance; though liable to lose rank and estate for favoritism, the emperor spared him.
entries.literal: Tan Tai denounced Sonin and cited Leng Sengji as witness; Leng Sengji declined, saying he had not heard; he was charged with favoritism and should have been stripped of hereditary rank and had his household confiscated; the sovereign pardoned him.

entries.zh: 旋進世職三等精奇尼哈番。
entries.en: He was soon raised to third-class jingqi nihaan.
entries.literal: Soon his hereditary office was advanced to third-rank jingqi nihaan.

entries.zh: 譚泰，舒穆祿氏，滿洲正黃旗人，揚古利從弟也。
entries.en: Tan Tai, of the Šumuru clan, belonged to the Plain Yellow Banner; he was Yangguli's younger cousin.
entries.literal: Tan Tai, of the Šumuru clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner and a younger cousin of Yangguli.

entries.zh: 初授牛錄額真。
entries.en: He was first made a company commander.
entries.literal: At first he was appointed niru ejen.

entries.zh: 天聰八年，擢巴牙喇章京，與固山額真圖爾格分統左右翼兵，略錦州。
entries.en: In the eighth year of Tiancong he rose to bayara banner colonel and, with banner commander Turgut, led the left and right wings in a raid on Jinzhou.
entries.literal: In the eighth year of Tiancong he was promoted to bayara janggin; with gusa ejen Turgut he jointly commanded the left and right wing forces and raided Jinzhou.

entries.zh: 還從太宗伐明，自上方堡毀邊牆以入，敗明兵，克保安州。
entries.en: On the return march he joined Taizong's campaign against Ming, broke through the frontier wall at Shangfangbao, routed the Ming army, and took Bao'an.
entries.literal: Returning, he followed the Taizong in attacking Ming; entering by destroying the border wall at Shangfangbao, he defeated Ming troops and captured Bao'an prefecture.

entries.zh: 擢巴牙喇纛章京，令關白諸事。
entries.en: He was raised to chief of the bayara guard and charged with bringing matters before the throne.
entries.literal: He was promoted to bayara banner standard-bearer and ordered to report on all affairs.

entries.zh: 九年，揚古利賜第，侍衛宗室濟馬護欲得其舊居，揚古利不可。
entries.en: In the ninth year Yangguli received a grand residence; the guardsman Jimalu, a member of the imperial clan, wanted his old house, but Yangguli would not yield it.
entries.literal: In the ninth year, when Yangguli was granted a residence, the imperial guardsman Jimalu of the imperial clan wished to obtain his old dwelling; Yangguli refused.

entries.zh: 濟馬護囑譚泰入奏，譚泰匿不以聞，濟馬護訴於上，上責譚泰曰：「爾為朕耳目，凡事當無隱。
entries.en: Jimalu asked Tan Tai to present the matter in memorial; Tan Tai kept it back and did not report it. When Jimalu appealed to the throne, the emperor rebuked Tan Tai: "You are my eyes and ears—nothing should be hidden from me.
entries.literal: Jimalu had Tan Tai enter with a memorial; Tan Tai concealed it and did not report it. Jimalu complained to the sovereign, who reproached Tan Tai, saying: "You are my eyes and ears; in all matters there should be nothing concealed.

entries.zh: 濟馬護乃朕叔父之子，其言尚不能達，民間勞苦嗟怨，何由得使朕知？
entries.en: Jimalu is my uncle's son; if even he cannot be heard, how will I ever learn of the people's labor and grief?
entries.literal: Jimalu is my uncle's son—if even his words cannot reach me, how can the people's toil, sighs, and complaints ever come to my knowledge?

entries.zh: 爾恃宗族強盛，欺陵愚弱，朕所深惡！」
entries.en: You lean on your powerful kin to oppress the weak—that I loathe above all!"
entries.literal: You rely on your clan's strength to bully the simple and weak—this is what I deeply abhor!"

entries.zh: 下刑部質訊，奪官。
entries.en: The case went to the Board of Punishments; he lost his post.
entries.literal: He was handed to the Board of Punishments for interrogation and stripped of office.

entries.zh: 尋复授本旗固山額真。
entries.en: Before long he was restored as banner commander of his regiment.
entries.literal: Soon he was again appointed gusa ejen of his own banner.

entries.zh: 圖海李之芳圖海，字麟洲，馬佳氏，滿洲正黃旗人。
entries.en: Tu Hai and Li Zhifang. Tu Hai, whose style was Linzhou, belonged to the Majia clan and was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner.
entries.literal: Tu Hai, Li Zhifang. Tu Hai, style name Linzhou, of the Majia clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner.

entries.zh: 父穆哈達，世居綏芬。
entries.en: His father was Mu-hada, and the family had long lived at Suifen.
entries.literal: His father was Mu-hada; the family had long dwelt at Suifen.

entries.zh: 圖海自筆帖式歷國史院侍讀。
entries.en: Tu Hai advanced from clerk to reader in the National History Academy.
entries.literal: Tu Hai rose from clerk to reader in the National History Academy.

entries.zh: 世祖嘗幸南苑，負寶從，顧其舉止，以為非常人。
entries.en: When the Shunzhi Emperor once visited the Southern Park, Tu Hai attended carrying the imperial seals. The emperor noted his bearing and judged that he was no ordinary man.
entries.literal: The Shunzhi Emperor once visited the Southern Park; Tu Hai carried the imperial seals in attendance. The emperor watched his bearing and thought him no ordinary man.

entries.zh: 擢內秘書院學士，授拜他喇布勒哈番，遷弘文院大學士、議政大臣。
entries.en: He was promoted to bachelor of the Inner Secretariat, granted the rank of baitalabule hašan, and then appointed grand secretary of the Hongwen Academy and councilor of state.
entries.literal: He was promoted to bachelor of the Inner Secretariat, granted the rank of baitalabule hašan, and transferred to grand secretary of the Hongwen Academy and councilor of state.

entries.zh: 順治十二年，加太子太保，攝刑部尚書事。
entries.en: In the twelfth year of Shunzhi he received the additional title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and served as acting Minister of Justice.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year of Shunzhi he was given the additional title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and acted as Minister of Justice.

entries.zh: 與大學士巴哈納等同訂律例。
entries.en: Together with Grand Secretary Bahana and others, he helped revise the legal code.
entries.literal: Together with Grand Secretary Bahana and others he revised the legal code.

entries.zh: 侍衛阿拉那與公額爾克戴青兩家奴鬥於市，讞失實，坐欺罔，免死，削職。
entries.en: When the household slaves of Bodyguard Alana and of Duke Erke Daiqing fought in the market, his ruling did not accord with the facts. He was convicted of deception, spared execution, and dismissed from office.
entries.literal: When the household slaves of Bodyguard Alana and of Duke Erke Daiqing fought in the market, his judgment did not match the facts; he was found guilty of deception, spared death, and stripped of office.

entries.zh: 世祖崩，遺命起用。
entries.en: After the Shunzhi Emperor's death, his testamentary edict ordered Tu Hai restored to service.
entries.literal: When the Shunzhi Emperor died, his testamentary edict ordered Tu Hai restored to office.

entries.zh: 聖祖即位，授正黃旗滿洲都統。
entries.en: When the Kangxi Emperor took the throne, Tu Hai was appointed commander-in-chief of the Manchu Plain Yellow Banner.
entries.literal: When the Kangxi Emperor acceded, Tu Hai was appointed commander-in-chief of the Manchu Plain Yellow Banner.

entries.zh: 李之芳，字鄴園，山東武定人。
entries.en: Li Zhifang, whose style was Yeyuan, was a native of Wuding in Shandong.
entries.literal: Li Zhifang, style name Yeyuan, was a native of Wuding in Shandong.

entries.zh: 順治四年進士，授金華府推官。
entries.en: Having passed the metropolitan examination in the fourth year of Shunzhi, he was appointed reviewing official of Jinhua Prefecture.
entries.literal: A metropolitan graduate in the fourth year of Shunzhi, he was appointed reviewing official of Jinhua Prefecture.

entries.zh: 卓異，擢刑部主事。
entries.en: Rated outstanding in performance, he was promoted to principal in the Ministry of Justice.
entries.literal: Rated outstanding, he was promoted to principal in the Ministry of Justice.

entries.zh: 累遷郎中，授廣西道御史。
entries.en: He rose through successive posts to department director and was appointed investigating censor for the Guangxi circuit.
entries.literal: He rose through successive posts to department director and was made investigating censor for the Guangxi circuit.

entries.zh: 疏請革錢糧陋規，禁州縣官迎送。
entries.en: He memorialized to abolish corrupt practices in tax collection and to forbid prefectural and county officials from the elaborate welcoming and escorting of superiors.
entries.literal: He memorialized to abolish corrupt practices in tax collection and forbid prefectural and county officials from welcoming and escorting superiors.

entries.zh: 十七年，巡按山西。
entries.en: In the seventeenth year he served as touring inspector of Shanxi.
entries.literal: In the seventeenth year he toured as inspector of Shanxi.

entries.zh: 聖祖即位，裁巡按，召回。
entries.en: When the Kangxi Emperor took the throne, the touring inspector posts were abolished and he was recalled to the capital.
entries.literal: When the Kangxi Emperor acceded, the touring inspector posts were cut and he was recalled.

entries.zh: 康熙元年，乞假歸。
entries.en: In the first year of Kangxi he asked for leave to return home.
entries.literal: In the first year of Kangxi he asked leave to return home.

entries.zh: 二年，复授湖廣道御史。
entries.en: In the second year he was again appointed investigating censor for the Huguang circuit.
entries.literal: In the second year he was again appointed investigating censor for the Huguang circuit.

entries.zh: 五年，巡視浙江鹽政。
entries.en: In the fifth year he inspected salt administration in Zhejiang.
entries.literal: In the fifth year he inspected salt administration in Zhejiang.

entries.zh: 入掌河南道事。
entries.en: He was then put in charge of affairs for the Henan circuit.
entries.literal: He entered to direct affairs of the Henan circuit.

entries.zh: 大學士班布爾善坐鰲拜黨誅，之芳疏言：「昔大學士俱內直，諸司章奏，即日票擬。
entries.en: Grand Secretary Banbu'ershan was executed as a member of Oboi's faction. Zhifang memorialized: "In former times all grand secretaries served on inner duty, and memorials from the ministries received draft responses the same day.
entries.literal: Grand Secretary Banbu'ershan was executed as a member of Oboi's faction. Zhifang memorialized: "Formerly all grand secretaries were on inner duty, and all documents from the ministries received draft responses the same day.

entries.zh: 自鰲拜輔政，大學士皆不入直，疏奏俱至次日看詳。
entries.en: Since Oboi dominated the government, no grand secretaries entered inner duty, and memorials were not reviewed until the following day.
entries.literal: Since Oboi held power, no grand secretaries entered inner duty; memorials and reports were all reviewed only the next day.

entries.zh: 請復舊制，杜任意更改之弊。」
entries.en: He asked that the old system be restored to prevent arbitrary alterations."
entries.literal: He asked to restore the old system and block the abuse of arbitrary changes."

entries.zh: 又疏言：「世祖時賞罰出至公，督撫不敢恣睢無忌。
entries.en: He also wrote: "Under the Shunzhi Emperor rewards and punishments issued from perfect impartiality, and governors-general did not dare act with reckless impunity.
entries.literal: He also memorialized: "Under the Shunzhi Emperor rewards and punishments issued from perfect impartiality, and governors-general dared not act wantonly without restraint.

entries.zh: 十八年以後，督撫率多夤緣而得，有恃無恐。
entries.en: After the eighteenth year most governors-general obtained their posts through patronage and acted without fear of consequences.
entries.literal: After the eighteenth year most governors-general obtained their posts through patronage and acted without fear.

entries.zh: 勒索屬員，擾害百姓。
entries.en: They extorted their subordinates and harassed the common people.
entries.literal: They extorted from subordinates and harassed the people.

entries.zh: 夫直省億萬之眾，皆世祖留遺之群黎，我皇上愛養之赤子，何堪此輩朘削？
entries.en: The hundreds of millions in the provinces are the people the late emperor bequeathed and the children our present emperor nourishes—how can they endure such exploitation?
entries.literal: The hundreds of millions in the provinces are all the masses the late emperor bequeathed and children whom our present emperor nourishes—how can they bear such exploitation?

entries.zh: 自與受同罪之法嚴，與者不承，則言者即涉虛，非特不敢糾督撫，且不敢糾司道守令。
entries.en: Because the law that punishes both giver and taker alike is strictly enforced, if the taker does not confess the accuser is deemed to have lied—so men dare not impeach governors-general, and dare not even impeach circuit intendants, prefects, or magistrates.
entries.literal: With the law that giver and taker share guilt strictly applied, if the taker does not confess, the accuser is deemed false—so not only do they dare not impeach governors-general, they dare not impeach circuit intendants, prefects, and magistrates.

entries.zh: 有貪之利，無貪之害，又何憚而不怙惡自恣？
entries.en: When corruption brings profit and no penalty, why should they not cling to evil and act as they please?
entries.literal: With gain in corruption and no harm, why would they not persist in evil without restraint?

entries.zh: 今皇上親政，乞親裁，罷黜溺職督撫，以肅吏治。」
entries.en: Now that Your Majesty has taken power in person, he begged that you personally decide the matter, dismiss negligent governors-general, and restore discipline among officials."
entries.literal: Now that the emperor has taken power in person, he begged that the emperor personally decide and dismiss negligent governors-general to rectify official conduct."

entries.zh: 疏下部，尋甄別各省督撫，黜其尤者數人。
entries.en: The memorial was sent to the ministries, and before long governors-general throughout the provinces were screened and several of the worst offenders were removed.
entries.literal: The memorial was sent to the ministries; soon governors-general in each province were screened and several of the worst were removed.

entries.zh: 進秩視四品，擢左副都御史。
entries.en: He was promoted in rank to the equivalent of fourth grade and appointed left vice censor-in-chief.
entries.literal: He was promoted in rank to fourth-grade equivalent and made left vice censor-in-chief.

entries.zh: 之芳數上封事，請嚴巡鹽考績，慎外官罰俸，皆關治體。
entries.en: Zhifang repeatedly submitted sealed memorials calling for strict evaluation of salt patrols and careful use of salary fines against field officials—measures that all touched the foundations of good government.
entries.literal: Zhifang repeatedly submitted sealed memorials asking for strict inspection of salt patrol performance and careful application of fines to outside officials—all concerned fundamentals of governance.

entries.zh: 遷吏部侍郎。
entries.en: He was transferred to vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
entries.literal: He was transferred to vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel.

entries.zh: 之芳既卒，聖祖思其功，嘗諭群臣曰：「人能效命，即為勇士。
entries.en: After Zhifang's death the Kangxi Emperor recalled his achievements and once told his ministers, "A man who stakes his life in service is a true warrior.
entries.literal: After Zhifang's death the Kangxi Emperor thought of his achievements and once told the ministers: "One who gives his life in service is a brave man.

entries.zh: 耿精忠叛，時之芳為總督，雖不諳騎射，執刀立船首，率眾突前破敵。
entries.en: When Geng Jingzhong rebelled, Zhifang was governor. Though unskilled in riding and archery, he stood at the bow with a blade in hand and led his men in a frontal charge that broke the enemy.
entries.literal: When Geng Jingzhong rebelled, Zhifang was governor; though unskilled in riding and archery, he held a blade at the bow of the boat and led the men in a frontal assault that broke the enemy.

entries.zh: 彼時同出征者，還京皆稱其勇。
entries.en: Those who had campaigned with him all praised his bravery on their return to the capital.
entries.literal: Those who campaigned with him at the time all praised his bravery on return to the capital.

entries.zh: 今承平久，善射，能約束士卒，尚不乏人。
entries.en: In these long years of peace, men skilled in archery who can discipline troops are still not hard to find.
entries.literal: Now in long peace those skilled in archery who can discipline troops are still not lacking.

entries.zh: 若屢經戰陣者，甚難得也！」
entries.en: But men who have repeatedly seen battle are very hard to find!"
entries.literal: But those who have repeatedly seen battle are very hard to find!"

entries.zh: 世宗命立賢良祠，諭曰：「德若湯斌、功若之芳者，祀之。」
entries.en: The Yongzheng Emperor ordered the Hall of Worthy Officials built and instructed, "Enshrine those whose virtue is like Tang Bin's and whose achievement is like Zhifang's."
entries.literal: The Yongzheng Emperor ordered the Hall of Worthy Officials erected and said: "Enshrine those whose virtue is like Tang Bin's and whose achievement is like Zhifang's."

entries.zh: 乾隆間，錄勳臣後，命予恩騎尉，世襲。
entries.en: In the Qianlong reign, when recording descendants of meritorious officials, his line was granted the Enjiwei rank, inheritable in perpetuity.
entries.literal: In the Qianlong reign, when recording descendants of meritorious officials, his line was granted Enjiwei, hereditary.

entries.zh: 列傳三十八
entries.en: Biography 38.
entries.literal: Biographies 38.

entries.zh: 五十二年，與千叟宴，賜賚有加。
entries.en: In the fifty-second year he attended the banquet for elders of a thousand years and received especially generous gifts.
entries.literal: In the fifty-second year he attended the banquet for a thousand elders and received especially generous gifts.

entries.zh: 頃之，以病乞休，溫旨慰留。
entries.en: Before long he asked to retire on grounds of illness; a warm edict comforted him and urged him to stay.
entries.literal: Before long, on account of illness he requested retirement; a warm edict comforted him and asked him to remain.

entries.zh: 越二年，復以為請，且言母喪未葬，許給假二年，賜詩寵行。
entries.en: Two years later he asked again, adding that his mother's burial was still unfinished. He was granted two years' leave and sent off with an imperial poem.
entries.literal: Two years later he again made the request, and also said his mother's funeral had not yet been conducted; he was granted two years' leave and received an imperial poem honoring his departure.

entries.zh: 五十六年，還朝，累疏乞罷，上以大學士王掞方在告，暫止之。
entries.en: In the fifty-sixth year he returned to court and repeatedly asked to be dismissed, but the emperor held off because Grand Secretary Wang Yan was already away on leave.
entries.literal: In the fifty-sixth year he returned to court, repeatedly memorialized asking to be dismissed, and the emperor temporarily stopped this because Grand Secretary Wang Yan was already on leave.

entries.zh: 五十七年，卒，年七十七，遣恆親王允祺奠醊，賜金千兩，諡文貞。
entries.en: In the fifty-seventh year he died at seventy-seven. Prince Heng Yinqi was sent to offer libations, one thousand taels of silver were granted, and he was posthumously honored as Wen Zhen.
entries.literal: In the fifty-seventh year he died at the age of seventy-seven; Prince Heng Yinqi was sent to offer libations, one thousand taels of silver were granted, and he was posthumously given the honorific Wen Zhen.

entries.zh: 使工部尚書徐元夢護其喪歸，复諭閣臣：「李光地謹慎清勤，始終一節，學問淵博。
entries.en: Minister of Works Xu Yuanmeng was sent to escort the bier home, and the emperor again told the grand secretaries, "Li Guangdi was careful, pure, and diligent, unwavering to the end, and his learning was broad and deep.
entries.literal: Minister of Works Xu Yuanmeng was sent to escort the funeral home, and the emperor again instructed the grand secretaries: "Li Guangdi was careful, pure, and diligent, consistent from beginning to end, and his learning was broad and deep.

entries.zh: 朕知之最真，知朕亦無過光地者！」
entries.en: I know this better than anyone, and among those who truly know me, none surpasses Li Guangdi!"
entries.literal: I know this most truly, and among those who know me none surpasses Guangdi!

entries.zh: 雍正初，贈太子太傅，祀賢良祠。
entries.en: Early in the Yongzheng reign he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and entered the Shrine of Worthy Ministers.
entries.literal: In the early Yongzheng reign he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and enshrined in the Shrine of Worthy Ministers.

entries.zh: 魏裔介，字石生，直隸柏鄉人。
entries.en: Wei Yijie, whose style was Shisheng, came from Baixiang in Zhili.
entries.literal: Wei Yijie, styled Shisheng, was a man of Baixiang in Zhili.

entries.zh: 順治三年進士，選庶吉士。
entries.en: In Shunzhi 3 (1646) he passed the jinshi examination and was chosen as a Hanlin bachelor.
entries.literal: In the third year of Shunzhi he became a jinshi and was selected as a Hanlin bachelor.

entries.zh: 四年，授工科給事中。
entries.en: The following year he was made supervising secretary of the Ministry of Works.
entries.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed supervising secretary of the Ministry of Works.

entries.zh: 五年，疏請舉經筵及時講學，以隆治本。
entries.en: In the fifth year he submitted a memorial asking that the emperor hold regular Classics Lectures and study without delay, so as to strengthen the foundations of rule.
entries.literal: In the fifth year he memorialized requesting that the Classics Lecture be held and study pursued in timely fashion, to elevate fundamental governance.

entries.zh: 又言：「燕、趙之民，椎牛裹糧，首先歸命。
entries.en: He also wrote: "The people of Yan and Zhao slaughtered cattle and packed provisions to be the first to submit to the new dynasty.
entries.literal: He also said: "The people of Yan and Zhao slaughtered cattle and wrapped grain, being the first to submit.

entries.zh: 此漢高之關中，光武之河內也。
entries.en: They were to the Qing what Guanzhong had been to Gaozu of Han and Henei to Emperor Guangwu.
entries.literal: This is like Gaozu of Han's Guanzhong and Guangwu's Henei.

entries.zh: 今天下初定，屢奉詔蠲賦，而畿輔未霑實惠，宜切責奉行之吏，彰信於民。」
entries.en: Now that the realm is newly pacified, repeated edicts have remitted taxes, yet the capital districts have not felt the real benefit. Officials charged with carrying out these orders should be held strictly accountable so that the government's word is made credible to the people."
entries.literal: Now that the realm is newly settled, decrees for tax remission have been issued repeatedly, yet the capital region has not received the real benefit; the officials charged with implementation should be sternly held accountable, so that trust is made clear to the people."

entries.zh: 俱報聞。
entries.en: All of these proposals were noted by the throne.
entries.literal: All were acknowledged.

entries.zh: 尋遷右、左通政。
entries.en: He was soon promoted to right and then left vice commissioner of the Communications Office.
entries.literal: Soon he was promoted right and left vice commissioner of the Communications Office.

entries.zh: 十一年，疏言：「嘉魚知縣李世錫告湖廣巡撫林天擎索賄，以此知餽遺不絕，苞苴尚行，較世祖朝有司不敢餽遺督撫、不敢輕至省會風氣迥殊。
entries.en: In the eleventh year he memorialized: "Jiayu magistrate Li Shixi reported that Huguang governor Lin Tianqing had demanded bribes — from this one knows that gifts never cease and graft still flourishes; compared with the Shizu reign, when local officials dared not send gifts to governors and dared not lightly visit the provincial capital, the climate is utterly different.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year he memorialized: "Jiayu magistrate Li Shixi reported that Huguang governor Lin Tianqing demanded bribes — by this one knows gifts never cease and graft still goes on; compared with the Shizu reign, when local officials dared not gift governors and dared not lightly visit the provincial capital, the climate is utterly different.

entries.zh: 督撫初受命，群餽裘馬、弓矢，而為督撫者亦飾觀瞻、趨奢侈，一時費累萬。
entries.en: When governors-general and governors first receive appointment, crowds gift them furs, horses, bows, and arrows — and the men who take such posts also dress for show and rush toward extravagance, so that expenses at once mount to tens of thousands.
entries.literal: When governors-general and governors first receive appointment, crowds gift furs, horses, bows, and arrows — and those who become governors-general also dress for show and rush toward extravagance, so that expenses at once mount to tens of thousands.

entries.zh: 上官後，為酬報取償地，遂苛索屬吏，貽累於民。
entries.en: After taking office, to repay the gifts they had received they squeezed their subordinates for compensation and thus burdened the people.
entries.literal: After taking office, to repay gifts they had received they exacted compensation from subordinates and thus oppressed the people.

entries.zh: 請敕督撫赴官之先，屏絕餽送，勿鋪張行色，以儉養廉。
entries.en: I ask that before governors-general and governors take up their posts they refuse all gifts, travel without ostentation, and cultivate integrity through frugality.
entries.literal: I request orders that before governors-general and governors take up office they refuse all gifts, do not display extravagant travel, and cultivate integrity through frugality.

entries.zh: 督撫參罰科條甚密，部院亦當知督撫艱難繁重，依例處分，毋過為吹索，俾得專心吏治民生，無旁顧之憂。」
entries.en: The regulations for censuring governors-general and governors are very strict; the ministries and courts should also recognize how arduous their duties are, punish according to rule, and not press excessively, so that they may devote themselves to government and the people's livelihood without distraction."
entries.literal: The regulations for impeachment and punishment of governors-general and governors are very strict; the ministries and courts should also know how arduous and heavy their duties are, dispose of cases according to rule, and not press excessively, so that they may devote themselves to administration and the people's livelihood without distraction."

entries.zh: 先後諸疏並下部議行。
entries.en: All these memorials in succession were sent to the ministries for deliberation and execution.
entries.literal: All these memorials in succession were referred to the ministries for discussion and implementation.

entries.zh: 十五年，充會試同考官，出闈，疏言：「伏讀上諭，令各衙門條奏興利除弊。
entries.en: In the fifteenth year he served as associate metropolitan examiner; when he left the examination compound he memorialized: "I have read Your Majesty's instruction ordering every yamen to memorialize on promoting benefit and removing harm.
entries.literal: In the fifteenth year he served as associate metropolitan examiner; upon leaving the examination hall he memorialized: "I have read Your Majesty's instruction ordering each yamen to memorialize on promoting profit and removing harm.

entries.zh: 時近兩月，僅見宗人府一疏，各衙門遲疑觀望。
entries.en: Nearly two months have passed and only one memorial from the Court of the Imperial Clan has appeared; every yamen hesitates and waits.
entries.literal: It has been nearly two months and only one memorial from the Court of the Imperial Clan has appeared; every yamen hesitates and watches.

entries.zh: 竊謂其病有二：一則因循既久，發論方新，恐無以贖往日曠官之咎；
entries.en: I think there are two afflictions: one is that after long inertia, with fresh calls for reform, officials fear they cannot atone for past dereliction;
entries.literal: I think there are two afflictions: one is that long-standing inertia, with discourse just renewed, breeds fear of no way to atone for past dereliction in office;

entries.zh: 一則瞻望多端，指陳無隱，恐無以留後來遷就之門。
entries.en: the other is manifold hesitation — speak frankly without concealment and one fears leaving no door for later compromise.
entries.literal: the other is manifold hesitation — speak frankly without concealment and one fears no door left for later compromise.

entries.zh: 臣子報國，止有朴忠，遇事直陳；
entries.en: A subject serves the state only through plain loyalty and speaking straight in affairs;
entries.literal: A subject's service to the state admits only plain loyalty and speaking straight in affairs;

entries.zh: 稍一轉念，便持兩端，勢必摭拾瑣屑，剿說雷同，不能慷慨論列，又安望設誠致行？
entries.en: at the slightest second thought one wavers, and inevitably gathers trifles and repeats what others say, unable to argue boldly — how then can one hope to establish sincerity and carry it into action?
entries.literal: at the slightest second thought one holds two ends, and inevitably gathers trifles and copies commonplaces, unable to argue boldly in array — how then can one hope to establish sincerity and carry it into action?

entries.zh: 乞嚴飭不得浮泛塞責，並鑑別當否，示以勸懲。」
entries.en: I beg strict orders that none may answer with empty generalities, and that right and wrong be distinguished for encouragement and warning."
entries.literal: I beg strict orders that none may answer with empty generalities, and that approval or rejection be distinguished for encouragement and warning."

entries.zh: 又疏言：「近以各衙門胥役作姦犯科，詔令諸臣計議指摘。
entries.en: He also memorialized: "Recently, because clerks in various yamens have committed crimes, an edict ordered officials to devise plans and point out abuses.
entries.literal: He also memorialized: "Recently, because clerks in various yamens committed crimes, an edict ordered officials to devise plans and point out abuses.

entries.zh: 臣以為懲於弊後，不若杜於弊先，如吏部文選司推升原有定序，應先懸榜部門，序列姓名、資俸、薦紀、參罰，使共見共聞；
entries.en: I think punishment after abuse is inferior to stopping abuse beforehand — for example the Ministry of Personnel's bureau of appointments has a fixed order for promotions; the list should first be posted at the ministry gate with names, salary grades, recommendation records, and censure penalties for all to see and hear;
entries.literal: Your servant thinks punishment after abuse is inferior to stopping abuse beforehand — for example the Ministry of Personnel's bureau of appointments has a fixed order for promotions; the list should first be posted at the gate with names, salary grades, recommendation records, and censure penalties for all to see and hear;

entries.zh: 考功司議處條例，亦畫一頒發，使不得輕重增減。
entries.en: regulations for the bureau of evaluation should also be issued uniformly so that none may lightly add to or subtract from them.
entries.literal: regulations for the bureau of evaluation should also be issued uniformly so that none may lightly add or subtract.

entries.zh: 至各官開缺，以科鈔為憑，向以發鈔後先轉移舞弊。
entries.en: When any post falls vacant, the credential is the basis; formerly, after credentials were issued, precedence was shifted by fraud.
entries.literal: When any post falls vacant, the credential is the basis; formerly after credentials were issued, precedence was shifted by fraud.

entries.zh: 如當逮問，先下刑部，與事止奪官、迳下吏部者遲速有異。
entries.en: When interrogation is required, the Ministry of Punishments is notified first — depending on whether the matter ends with stripping of office or goes straight to the Ministry of Personnel, speed differs.
entries.literal: When interrogation is required, the Ministry of Punishments is notified first — depending on whether the matter ends at office-stripping or goes straight to the Ministry of Personnel, speed differs.

entries.zh: 應令即日鈔發，使不容操縱。」
entries.en: Credentials should be issued the same day so that manipulation has no room."
entries.literal: Credentials should be issued the same day so that manipulation has no room."

entries.zh: 上以所奏切中時弊，下部詳議行。
entries.en: The emperor, finding that the memorial struck at the abuses of the time, ordered the ministry to deliberate in detail and carry it out.
entries.literal: The emperor, finding the memorial struck at the abuses of the time, ordered the ministry to deliberate in detail and implement.

entries.zh: 劉鴻儒，字魯一，直隸遷安人。
entries.en: Liu Hongru, whose courtesy name was Luyi, came from Qian'an in Zhili.
entries.literal: Liu Hongru, styled Luyi, was a native of Qian'an in Zhili.

entries.zh: 順治三年進士，授兵科給事中。
entries.en: He took his jinshi degree in the third year of Shunzhi and was made supervising secretary of the Office of War.
entries.literal: He passed the jinshi in the third year of Shunzhi and was appointed supervising secretary of the Office of War.

entries.zh: 疏言：「開國之始，首重安民，宜輕賦徭，革積弊。
entries.en: He memorialized: "At the founding of the state, settling the people comes first; taxes and corvée should be lightened and long-standing abuses reformed.
entries.literal: He memorialized: "At the founding of the state, settling the people comes first; assessments and corvée should be lightened and long-standing abuses reformed.

entries.zh: 伏讀恩詔，賦制悉依萬曆初年，及觀順治二年徵數，並不減少，且復增重，請敕有司核實。
entries.en: I have read the gracious edict that the tax system should wholly follow the early Wanli standard, yet the levies of the second year of Shunzhi have not been reduced and have even been increased — I ask that local officials be ordered to verify the facts.
entries.literal: I have read the gracious edict that the tax system should wholly follow the early Wanli standard, yet observing the levies of the second year of Shunzhi, they have not been reduced and have even been increased — I request orders to local officials to verify the facts.

entries.zh: 州縣六房書吏，初房各二人，今則增至七、八十人，並請敕有司核簡。」
entries.en: In prefectures and counties the six bureaus originally had two clerks each; now they have grown to seventy or eighty — I also ask that local officials be ordered to verify and reduce them."
entries.literal: In prefectures and counties the six bureaus originally had two clerks each; now they have increased to seventy or eighty — I also request orders to local officials to verify and reduce them."

entries.zh: 上命指實，鴻儒復言：「臣籍遷安，明季丁銀，下下二錢，下中四錢，上地一畝七分有奇。
entries.en: The emperor ordered specific facts; Hongru again said: "I am registered in Qian'an. Under the Ming, poll silver was two qian for the lowest-lower grade, four qian for the lower-middle grade, and a little over seven fen per mu for upper land.
entries.literal: The emperor ordered specific facts; Hongru again said: "Your servant is registered in Qian'an. Under the Ming, poll silver was two qian for lowest-lower land, four qian for lower-middle land, and seven-plus fen per mu for upper land.

entries.zh: 民苦輸將，猶多逋賦。
entries.en: The people suffered under the burden of payment and many taxes were still in arrears.
entries.literal: The people suffered in paying and many taxes were still in arrears.

entries.zh: 今蒙恩詔蠲免，而二年徵數，二錢者增至三錢六分，四錢者增至七錢二分，上地每畝增至八分有奇。
entries.en: Now, though we have received a gracious edict of remission, the second-year levies raised two qian to three qian six fen, four qian to seven qian two fen, and upper land per mu to a little over eight fen.
entries.literal: Now under the gracious edict of remission, yet the second-year levies raised two qian to three qian six fen, four qian to seven qian two fen, and upper land per mu to a little over eight fen.

entries.zh: 一邑如此，他邑可知。
entries.en: If one county is like this, the others may be imagined.
entries.literal: If one county is thus, other counties may be known.

entries.zh: 乞敕清查蠲免。」
entries.en: I beg that orders be given for investigation, clearing, and remission."
entries.literal: I beg orders for investigation, clearing, and remission."

entries.zh: 下部確察。
entries.en: The matter was referred to the ministry for thorough investigation.
entries.literal: The matter was referred to the ministry for thorough investigation.

entries.zh: 四年，調戶部。
entries.en: During the fourth year he was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.
entries.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.

entries.zh: 五年，坐糾鉅鹿知縣勞有學失實，左遷上林苑蕃育署署丞。
entries.en: During the fifth year he was demoted for impeaching Julu magistrate Lao Youxue on false grounds to assistant director of the Breeding Office in the Imperial Park.
entries.literal: In the fifth year he was demoted for impeaching Julu magistrate Lao Youxue on false grounds to assistant director of the Breeding Office in the Imperial Park.

entries.zh: 十年，命復故官。
entries.en: During the tenth year he was ordered restored to his former post.
entries.literal: In the tenth year he was ordered restored to his former post.

entries.zh: 十三年，補兵科，疏言：「畿輔近地，劫掠時聞。
entries.en: In the thirteenth year he was restored to the Office of War and memorialized: "In the metropolitan region and nearby districts, robbery is reported from time to time.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year he was restored to the Office of War and memorialized: "In the metropolitan region and nearby districts, robbery is heard of from time to time.

entries.zh: 請嚴責成，謹防捕。」
entries.en: I ask for strict accountability and careful prevention and arrest."
entries.literal: I request strict accountability and careful prevention and arrest."

entries.zh: 下部如所請。
entries.en: The ministry acted as requested.
entries.literal: The ministry acted as requested.

entries.zh: 郝維訥，字敏公，直隸霸州人。
entries.en: Hao Weine, whose courtesy name was Mingong, came from Bazhou in Zhili.
entries.literal: Hao Weine, styled Mingong, was a native of Bazhou in Zhili.

entries.zh: 父傑，明崇禎進士。
entries.en: His father Jie had passed the jinshi examination in the Chongzhen era of the Ming.
entries.literal: His father Jie was a jinshi of the Chongzhen reign of the Ming.

entries.zh: 順治初，授行人，遷戶部給事中。
entries.en: At the beginning of the Shunzhi reign he was made a Bearer and later promoted to supervising secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.
entries.literal: In the early Shunzhi period, he was appointed Bearer, then promoted to supervising secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.

entries.zh: 迭疏請開經筵，祀闕里，廢斥諸臣才堪錄用者量予自新，朝賀大典內監不得入班行禮，俱下部議行。
entries.en: He sent repeated memorials asking that the emperor resume the lecture series, that sacrifices be offered at Qufu, that dismissed officials still fit for service be allowed to rehabilitate themselves as appropriate, and that eunuchs be barred from joining the ceremonial ranks at great court audiences; each proposal was sent to the appropriate ministry for deliberation and execution.
entries.literal: In memorial after memorial he requested that the imperial lecture be opened, that sacrifices be performed at Qufu, that dismissed officials whose talents were fit for employment be given reinstatement as appropriate, and that eunuchs not be allowed to join the ranks at grand court ceremonies — all referred to the relevant ministries for discussion and implementation.

entries.zh: 累遷戶部侍郎。
entries.en: He rose through repeated promotions to vice minister of revenue.
entries.literal: He was promoted repeatedly to vice minister of revenue.

entries.zh: 卒。
entries.en: He passed away.
entries.literal: He died.

entries.zh: 尋命巡視北城。
entries.en: He was soon assigned to inspect the North City.
entries.literal: Soon he was ordered to inspect the North City.

entries.zh: 試俸滿，部議調外，因假歸。
entries.en: When his probation ended, the ministries proposed transferring him outside the capital, and he went home on leave.
entries.literal: When his probationary salary period ended, the ministries deliberated transferring him outside the capital, and he took leave to return home.

entries.zh: 三十一年，卒。
entries.en: He died in 1692.
entries.literal: In the thirty-first year he died.

entries.zh: 三十三年，江南學政缺，上欲用隴其，侍臣奏隴其已卒，乃用邵嗣堯，嗣堯故與隴其同以清廉行取者也。
entries.en: In 1694 the Jiangnan education post fell vacant; the emperor wanted Longqi, but was told he had died, so Shao Siyao was appointed—another man who had entered the capital on a reputation for integrity like Longqi's.
entries.literal: In the thirty-third year the Jiangnan education commissionership was vacant; the emperor wished to use Longqi, but attendants reported Longqi had already died, so Shao Siyao was used—Siyao had formerly been selected to the capital together with Longqi for integrity.

entries.zh: 雍正二年，世宗臨雍，議增從祀諸儒，隴其與焉。
entries.en: In 1724 the Yongzheng Emperor visited the Imperial Academy and approved additional Confucians for attendant sacrifice, including Longqi.
entries.literal: In the second year of Yongzheng the Shizong Emperor attended the Imperial Academy and deliberated increasing attendant sacrifice for various Confucians; Longqi was among them.

entries.zh: 乾隆元年，特諡清獻，加贈內閣學士兼禮部侍郎。
entries.en: In 1736 he was given the posthumous title Qingxian and posthumously made Grand Secretariat academician and Vice Minister of Rites.
entries.literal: In the first year of Qianlong he was specially posthumously titled Qingxian and additionally granted Grand Secretariat academician and Vice Minister of Rites.

entries.zh: 列傳五十二
entries.en: Biography 52
entries.literal: Biographies 52

entries.zh: 米思翰，富察氏，滿洲鑲黃旗人。
entries.en: Mi Sihan, of the Fuca clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
entries.literal: Mi Sihan, of the Fuca clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner.

entries.zh: 先世居沙濟。
entries.en: His family had long resided at Shaji.
entries.literal: His ancestors had lived at Shaji.

entries.zh: 曾祖旺吉努，當太祖時，率族來歸，授牛錄額真。
entries.en: His great-grandfather Wangjinu submitted with the clan during the Taizu's reign and was appointed niru commander.
entries.literal: His great-grandfather Wangjinu, in the time of the Taizu, led the clan to submit and was appointed niru commander.

entries.zh: 父哈什屯，事太宗，以侍衛襲管牛錄。
entries.en: His father Hashun served the Taizong and, as an imperial guardsman, inherited command of the family niru.
entries.literal: His father Hashun served the Taizong; as a bodyguard he inherited management of the niru.

entries.zh: 擢禮部參政，改副理事官。
entries.en: He rose to Vice Commissioner in the Ministry of Rites and was later made Associate Commissioner.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Vice Commissioner of the Ministry of Rites and then transferred to Associate Commissioner.

entries.zh: 討瓦爾喀，招明總兵沈志祥。
entries.en: On campaign against Warka he won over the Ming regional commander Shen Zhixiang.
entries.literal: Campaigning against Warka, he induced the Ming regional commander Shen Zhixiang to surrender.

entries.zh: 從攻錦州，明總兵曹變蛟夜襲御營，先眾扞禦，被創，力戰卻之。
entries.en: At the siege of Jinzhou, when the Ming commander Cao Bianjiao struck the imperial camp by night, Hashun was first to meet the assault. Though wounded, he fought hard and repulsed the attack.
entries.literal: He followed the attack on Jinzhou; the Ming regional commander Cao Bianjiao raided the imperial camp by night—he was first among the troops to resist, was wounded, and fought fiercely to drive the enemy back.

entries.zh: 順治初，授內大臣、議政大臣，世職屢進一等阿達哈哈番兼拖沙喇哈番。
entries.en: Early in the Shunzhi reign he became a Grand Minister of the Imperial Household and a Grand Councilor, and his hereditary rank was raised repeatedly until he held first-class adahahafan with an additional tashalahafan.
entries.literal: Early in Shunzhi he was appointed Grand Minister of the Imperial Household and Grand Councilor; his hereditary rank was repeatedly advanced to first-class adahahafan with tashalahafan attached.

entries.zh: 睿親王多爾袞攝政，諸大臣鞏阿岱等並附之，哈什屯獨持正，忤睿親王，降世職拜他喇布勒哈番。
entries.en: While Prince Regent Dorgon governed, ministers including Gongadai rallied to him, but Hashun alone stood firm. He offended the prince regent and was demoted to batalabulehafan.
entries.literal: When Prince Regent Dorgon held power, ministers such as Gongadai all sided with him; Hashun alone held to what was right, offended the Prince Regent, and had his hereditary rank reduced to batalabulehafan.

entries.zh: 肅親王豪格以非罪死，鞏阿岱等議殺其子富綬，哈什屯與巴哈力持，事乃已。
entries.en: When Prince Su Haoge was put to death on trumped-up charges, Gongadai and others urged that his son Fushou be killed as well. Hashun and Bahali resisted, and the proposal was abandoned.
entries.literal: Prince Su Haoge died on a false charge; Gongadai and others proposed killing his son Fushou—Hashun and Bahali held firm against it, and the matter was dropped.

entries.zh: 世祖親政，累進世職一等阿思哈尼哈番加拖沙喇哈番。
entries.en: Once the Shizu Emperor assumed personal rule, Hashun's hereditary rank was restored and raised step by step to first-class ashanihanafan with an added tashalahafan.
entries.literal: When the Shizu took personal rule, Hashun's hereditary rank was repeatedly advanced to first-class ashanihanafan with tashalahafan added.

entries.zh: 十二年，獎奉職恪勤諸大臣，加太子太保。
entries.en: In year 12 he was honored among the dutiful ministers still in service and was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year he was among the diligent ministers in office who were rewarded and was given the additional title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 康熙初卒，諡恪僖。
entries.en: He died early in the Kangxi reign and was posthumously titled Keixi.
entries.literal: He died early in Kangxi and was given the posthumous name Keixi.

entries.zh: 顧八代直尚書房時，世宗從受學；
entries.en: While Gu Badai served in the Imperial Study, the future Yongzheng Emperor studied under him;
entries.literal: When Gu Badai attended the Imperial Study, the Shizong received instruction from him;

entries.zh: 及卒，貧無以斂，世宗親臨奠，為經紀其喪。
entries.en: When he died his family was too poor to bury him properly. The Yongzheng Emperor came in person to mourn and arranged the funeral.
entries.literal: when he died, his family was too poor to bury him; the Shizong came in person to offer mourning and arranged his funeral.

entries.zh: 雍正四年，詔复官，加太傅，予祭葬，諡文端，又以其貧，賜其家​​白金萬。
entries.en: In Yongzheng year 4 an edict restored his office, made him Grand Tutor posthumously, granted state funeral honors, and gave him the posthumous title Wenduan. Because he had died poor, the court also gave his family ten thousand taels of silver.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Yongzheng an edict restored his office, added Grand Tutor, granted funeral rites, posthumously titled Wenduan, and because of his poverty gave his family ten thousand taels of silver.

entries.zh: 八年，建賢良祠京師，諭滿洲大臣當入祀者五人，大學士圖海、都統賚塔，次即顧八代，及尚書瑪爾漢、齊蘇勒。
entries.en: In year 8 the Worthy and Good Shrine was built in the capital. An edict named five Manchu ministers for enshrinement: Grand Secretary Tuhai and Commander-in-chief Ceben, then Gu Badai, and Ministers Ma Erhan and Qisuole.
entries.literal: In the eighth year the Worthy and Good Shrine was built in the capital; an edict named five Manchu ministers who should be enshrined—Grand Secretary Tuhai and Commander-in-chief Ceben, next Gu Badai, and Ministers Ma Erhan and Qisuole.

entries.zh: 二十三年，命直尚書房，累遷禮部侍郎。
entries.en: In year 23 he was ordered to serve in the Imperial Study and was promoted in stages to Vice Minister of Rites.
entries.literal: In the twenty-third year he was ordered to attend in the Imperial Study and was repeatedly promoted to Vice Minister of Rites.

entries.zh: 二十八年，授尚書。
entries.en: In year 28 he was appointed Minister.
entries.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was appointed Minister.

entries.zh: 三十二年，坐事，上責其不稱職，奪官，留世職，仍直尚書房。
entries.en: In year 32 he was charged with an offense. The emperor rebuked him as unfit for office, removed him from his post, but kept his hereditary rank and still had him attend in the Imperial Study.
entries.literal: In the thirty-second year he was charged with an offense; the emperor reproached him as unfit for office, stripped his post, retained his hereditary rank, and still had him attend in the Imperial Study.

entries.zh: 三十七年，以病乞休。
entries.en: In year 37 he requested retirement on grounds of illness.
entries.literal: In the thirty-seventh year he begged leave on grounds of illness.

entries.zh: 四十七年，卒。
entries.en: In year 47 he died.
entries.literal: In the forty-seventh year he died.

entries.zh: 三十八年，遷左都御史。
entries.en: In year 38 he was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief.
entries.literal: In the thirty-eighth year he was transferred to Left Censor-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 再遷兵部尚書，充經筵講官、議政大臣。
entries.en: He was promoted again to Minister of War, made a lecturer at the Classics Colloquium, and named a Deliberative Minister.
entries.literal: He was again promoted to Minister of War, appointed lecturer at the Classics Colloquium, and enrolled among the Deliberative Ministers.

entries.zh: 四十三年，歲饑，流民就食京師。
entries.en: In year 43 famine struck, and refugees flocked to the capital for relief.
entries.literal: In the forty-third year there was famine and displaced people came to the capital for food.

entries.zh: 命與內大臣佟國維、明珠、阿密達等監賑。
entries.en: He was ordered to supervise famine relief with Grand Ministers Tong Guowei, Mingzhu, Amida, and others.
entries.literal: He was ordered to supervise relief distribution with Grand Ministers of the Imperial Household Tong Guowei, Mingzhu, Amida, and others.

entries.zh: 四十六年，調吏部。
entries.en: In year 46 he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
entries.literal: In the forty-sixth year he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.

entries.zh: 四十八年，以老病乞休。
entries.en: In year 48 he requested retirement on grounds of age and illness.
entries.literal: In the forty-eighth year he begged leave to retire on grounds of age and illness.

entries.zh: 五十七年，卒，年八十五。
entries.en: In year 57 he died at eighty-five.
entries.literal: In the fifty-seventh year he died, aged eighty-five.

entries.zh: 上遣內大臣臨奠，賜祭葬。
entries.en: The emperor sent a grand minister to mourn on his behalf and granted state funeral honors.
entries.literal: The emperor sent a Grand Minister of the Imperial Household to offer mourning and granted funeral rites.

entries.zh: 雍正八年，世宗諭獎瑪爾漢謹慎忠厚，事聖祖宣力多年，完名引退，贈太子太傅。
entries.en: In Yongzheng year 8 the Yongzheng Emperor praised Ma Erhan's prudence and loyalty, his long service to the Kangxi Emperor, and his honorable retirement, and posthumously made him Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
