entries.literal: In the eighth year of Yongzheng the Shizong issued an edict praising Ma Erhan's prudence and loyalty, his many years of service to the Sage Ancestor, and his honorable retirement, and posthumously made him Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 賢良祠成，命入祀。
entries.en: When the Worthy and Good Shrine was completed, he was ordered enshrined there.
entries.literal: When the Worthy and Good Shrine was completed, he was ordered enshrined.

entries.zh: 乾隆元年，高宗命追諡恭勤。
entries.en: In the first year of Qianlong the Qianlong Emperor ordered the posthumous title Gongqin.
entries.literal: In the first year of Qianlong the Gaozong ordered the posthumous title Gongqin.

entries.zh: 十六年，擢工部侍郎。
entries.en: In year 16 he was promoted to Vice Minister of Works.
entries.literal: In the sixteenth year he was promoted to Vice Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 十七年，以夏旱求言，疏言：「今日官至督撫，居莫敢誰何之勢，自非大賢，鮮不縱恣。
entries.en: In year 17, when summer drought prompted a call for advice, he memorialized, "Today officials who reach governor-general stand where none dare challenge them; unless they are great worthies, few refrain from excess.
entries.literal: In the seventeenth year, when drought in summer prompted a call for advice, he memorialized: "Today officials who reach the rank of governor-general occupy a position none dare challenge; unless they are great worthies, few do not indulge themselves.

entries.zh: 道府歲納規禮，加之以搜括，則道府所轄官民，不啻鬻之道府矣。
entries.en: Circuits and prefectures pay annual customary gifts, and with additional squeezing the officials and people under them are virtually sold to those circuits and prefectures.
entries.literal: Circuits and prefectures pay annual customary gifts, and with additional squeezing the officials and people under the circuits and prefectures are no better than sold to them.

entries.zh: 州縣歲納規禮，重之以勒索，則州縣所屬士民，不啻鬻之州縣矣。
entries.en: Departments and counties pay annual customary gifts, and with further extortion the gentry and people under them are virtually sold to those departments and counties.
entries.literal: Departments and counties pay annual customary gifts, and with further extortion the gentry and people belonging to them are no better than sold to the departments and counties.

entries.zh: 世祖朝，山東巡按程衡劾巡撫耿焞，江南巡按秦世禎劾土國寶，皆置重典，天下肅然。
entries.en: In the Shunzhi reign, Shandong regional inspector Cheng Heng impeached Governor Geng Tun, and Jiangnan regional inspector Qin Shizhen impeached Tu Guobao—both received heavy punishment, and the empire was awed.
entries.literal: In the Shizu reign, Shandong Regional Inspector Cheng Heng impeached Governor Geng Tun, and Jiangnan Regional Inspector Qin Shizhen impeached Tu Guobao—both received heavy punishment, and all under Heaven were awed.

entries.zh: 今巡按久停，雖欲議复，恐一時難得多人。
entries.en: Surveillance commissioners have long been suspended; though one might wish to restore them, it will be hard to find enough qualified men at once.
entries.literal: Today surveillance commissioners have long been suspended; though one wishes to deliberate restoring them, I fear it will be hard to find many qualified men at once.

entries.zh: 惟有出自上意，欲清一省，則選一人遣往，不必一時俱發。
entries.en: Only if the emperor himself wishes to cleanse a province should one man be chosen and sent; there is no need to dispatch them all at once.
entries.literal: Only if it comes from the emperor's own intent, wishing to cleanse a province, should one man be chosen and sent—there is no need to dispatch them all at once.

entries.zh: 出其不意，示以不測，使天下奸惡吏不敢恃督撫而肆志，即有不肖之督撫，亦莫敢庇貪而害民。」
entries.en: Striking without warning and showing unpredictable resolve will make corrupt officials everywhere afraid to rely on governors-general for license; even unworthy governors-general will not dare shield the greedy and harm the people."
entries.literal: Taking the enemy unawares and showing unpredictable action will make corrupt officials under Heaven not dare rely on governors-general and governors to indulge their will; even unworthy governors-general will not dare shield the greedy and harm the people."

entries.zh: 疏入，報聞。
entries.en: The memorial was received and acknowledged.
entries.literal: When the memorial entered, acknowledgment was returned.

entries.zh: 列傳五十五
entries.en: Biographies 55
entries.literal: Biographies 55

entries.zh: 索額圖，赫舍里氏，滿洲正黃旗人，索尼第二子。
entries.en: Songgotu of the Heseri clan, a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner, was Sony's second son.
entries.literal: Songgotu, of the Heseri clan, was a bannerman of the Manchu Plain Yellow Banner and the second son of Sony.

entries.zh: 初授侍衛，自三等洊升一等。
entries.en: He began as a guard and rose in steady steps from third to first rank.
entries.literal: At first he was appointed a guard, and was promoted step by step from third to first rank.

entries.zh: 康熙七年，授吏部侍郎。
entries.en: In Kangxi 7 (1668) he became vice president of the Board of Civil Appointments.
entries.literal: In the seventh year of Kangxi he was appointed vice president of the Board of Civil Appointments.

entries.zh: 八年五月，自請解任效力左右，復為一等侍衛。
entries.en: In the fifth month of Kangxi 8 (1669) he resigned his office to serve at court and was restored to first-rank guard.
entries.literal: In the fifth month of the eighth year he asked to resign his post and serve at the emperor's side, and was again made a first-rank guard.

entries.zh: 及鼇拜獲罪，大學士班布爾善坐黨誅，授索額圖國史院大學士，兼佐領。
entries.en: After Oboi's fall, Grand Secretary Banbursan was put to death as his partisan; Songgotu was made grand secretary of the Historiographic Institute and company commander.
entries.literal: When Oboi was condemned, Grand Secretary Banbursan was executed for partisan attachment; Songgotu was appointed grand secretary of the Historiographic Institute and concurrently made a company commander.

entries.zh: 九年，改保和殿大學士。
entries.en: In Kangxi 9 (1670) he became grand secretary of the Hall of Preserving Harmony.
entries.literal: In the ninth year he was transferred to be grand secretary of the Hall of Preserving Harmony.

entries.zh: 十一年，世祖實錄成，加太子太傅。
entries.en: In Kangxi 11 (1672), on completion of the Shunzhi Veritable Records, he received the title Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year, when the Veritable Records of the Shizu Emperor were completed, he was promoted to Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince.

entries.zh: 十五年，大學士熊賜履票本有誤，改寫草簽，既又毀去。
entries.en: In Kangxi 15 (1676) Grand Secretary Xiong Cilü's draft memorial was faulty; he rewrote it on a slip and then destroyed the slip.
entries.literal: In the fifteenth year Grand Secretary Xiong Cilü's draft memorial contained an error; he rewrote it on a slip and then destroyed it.

entries.zh: 索額圖與大學士巴泰、杜立德等疏劾，賜履坐罷歸。
entries.en: Songgotu joined Grand Secretaries Batai and Du Lide in impeaching him, and Cilü was dismissed and sent home.
entries.literal: Songgotu, together with Grand Secretaries Batai, Du Lide, and others, memorialized in impeachment, and Cilü was dismissed and sent home.

entries.zh: 十八年，京察，侍講學士顧八代隨徵稱職，翰林院以「政勤才長」注考，索額圖改注「浮躁」，竟坐降調。
entries.en: At the Kangxi 18 (1679) metropolitan review, Lecturing Reader Gu Badai was rated competent on campaign service; the Hanlin entered 'diligent in government, gifted in talent,' but Songgotu altered it to 'frivolous,' and Badai was demoted.
entries.literal: In the eighteenth year, at the metropolitan evaluation, Lecturing Reader Gu Badai was rated competent on the campaign circuit; the Hanlin Academy entered him as 'diligent in government and gifted in talent,' but Songgotu changed the entry to 'frivolous,' and he was in the end demoted and transferred.

entries.zh: 語詳顧八代傳。
entries.en: The full account appears in Gu Badai's biography.
entries.literal: The account is given in full in the biography of Gu Badai.

entries.zh: 余國柱，字兩石，湖廣大冶人。
entries.en: Yu Guozhu, styled Liangshi, was from Daye in Huguang.
entries.literal: Yu Guozhu, style name Liangshi, was a native of Daye in Huguang.

entries.zh: 順治九年進士，授兗州推官。
entries.en: A Shunzhi 9 jinshi, he became investigating censor of Yanzhou.
entries.literal: A jinshi in the ninth year of Shunzhi, he was appointed investigating censor of Yanzhou.

entries.zh: 遷行人司行人，轉戶部主事。
entries.en: He became a courier in the Courier Office, then a director in the Ministry of Revenue.
entries.literal: He was transferred to be a courier in the Courier Office and then made a director in the Ministry of Revenue.

entries.zh: 康熙十五年，考授戶科給事中。
entries.en: In Kangxi 15 (1676) he became supervising censor of the Revenue Section.
entries.literal: In the fifteenth year of Kangxi he was examined and appointed supervising censor of the Revenue Section.

entries.zh: 時方用兵，國柱屢疏言籌餉事，語多精覈。
entries.en: During the wars he memorialized repeatedly on supplies with sharp, precise analysis.
entries.literal: War was then in progress; Guozhu repeatedly memorialized on raising supplies, his language often precise and penetrating.

entries.zh: 二十年，擢左副都御史。
entries.en: In Kangxi 20 (1681) he became vice censor-in-chief of the left.
entries.literal: In the twentieth year he was promoted to vice censor-in-chief of the left.

entries.zh: 旋授江寧巡撫，請設機制寬大緞疋。
entries.en: He was soon made governor of Jiangning and proposed machine weaving of wide satin.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed governor of Jiangning and asked to establish machine production of wide satin bolts.

entries.zh: 得旨：「非常用之物，何為勞費？」
entries.en: The emperor replied, 'This is not an everyday item—why waste labor and money?'
entries.literal: He received an edict: 'This is not an article of daily use—why expend labor and expense?'

entries.zh: 當明珠用事，國柱務罔利以迎合之，及內轉左都御史，遷戶部尚書，湯斌繼國柱撫江蘇；
entries.en: Under Mingzhu's power Guozhu sought illicit profit to please him; promoted to left censor-in-chief and revenue minister, he was succeeded in Jiangsu by Tang Bin;
entries.literal: When Mingzhu held power, Guozhu strove for illicit profit to please him; when he was transferred within the capital to left censor-in-chief and promoted to minister of revenue, Tang Bin succeeded Guozhu as governor of Jiangsu;

entries.zh: 國柱索斌獻明珠金，斌不能應，由是傾之。
entries.en: Guozhu demanded gold for Mingzhu; when Bin refused, they destroyed him.
entries.literal: Guozhu demanded that Bin present gold to Mingzhu; Bin could not comply, and for this reason they brought him down.

entries.zh: 二十六年，授武英殿大學士，益與明珠結，一時稱為「余秦檜」。
entries.en: In Kangxi 26 (1687) he became grand secretary of the Hall of Military Glory, tightened his bond with Mingzhu, and was nicknamed 'Yu Qin Hui.'
entries.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was appointed grand secretary of the Hall of Military Glory, bound himself still closer to Mingzhu, and for a time was called 'Yu Qin Hui.'

entries.zh: 會上謁陵，中途召于成龍入對，成龍盡發明珠、國柱等貪私。
entries.en: While attending the tombs the emperor summoned Yu Chenglong en route; Chenglong fully exposed the corruption of Mingzhu, Guozhu, and their circle.
entries.literal: When the emperor went to attend the tombs, he summoned Yu Chenglong midway for audience; Chenglong fully exposed the greed and private conduct of Mingzhu, Guozhu, and the rest.

entries.zh: 上歸詢高士奇，士奇亦以狀聞。
entries.en: On his return the emperor questioned Gao Shiqi, who confirmed the report.
entries.literal: On his return the emperor questioned Gao Shiqi, who also reported the facts.

entries.zh: 及郭琇疏論劾，言者蜂起，國柱門人陳世安亦具疏糾之，頗中要害，國柱遂奪官。
entries.en: After Guo Xiu's impeachment, accusers swarmed; even Guozhu's disciple Chen Shi'an memorialized against him with telling force, and Guozhu lost his post.
entries.literal: When Guo Xiu's memorial of impeachment followed, accusers swarmed forth; Guozhu's disciple Chen Shi'an also submitted a memorial of correction that struck vital points, and Guozhu was stripped of office.

entries.zh: 既出都，於江寧治第宅，營生計，復為給事中何金蘭所劾，命逐之回籍。
entries.en: After leaving Beijing he built a mansion at Jiangning; Supervising Censor He Jinlan impeached him again and he was ordered home.
entries.literal: After leaving the capital he built a mansion at Jiangning and managed his livelihood; he was again impeached by Supervising Censor He Jinlan and ordered expelled to his native place.

entries.zh: 卒於家。
entries.en: He died at home.
entries.literal: He died at home.

entries.zh: 索額圖明珠余國柱佛倫
entries.en: Songgotu, Mingzhu, Yu Guozhu, and Folun
entries.literal: Songgotu, Mingzhu, Yu Guozhu, and Folun

entries.zh: 五十四年，復召來京修書，充省方盛典總裁官。
entries.en: In year 54 he was summoned again to Beijing and made chief compiler of the record of the imperial southern tour.
entries.literal: In the fifty-fourth year he was again summoned to the capital to compile books and appointed chief compiler of the Imperial Tour Record.

entries.zh: 雍正元年，卒於京。
entries.en: He died in Beijing in the first year of the Yongzheng reign.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng he died in the capital.

entries.zh: 乾隆四十三年，國史館進鴻緒傳，髙宗命以郭琇劾疎載入，使後世知鴻緒輩罪狀。
entries.en: In Qianlong 43 the Historiographical Institute submitted his biography; the Qianlong Emperor ordered Guo Xiu's impeachment memorial appended so posterity would know Wang Hongxu's offenses.
entries.literal: In the forty-third year of Qianlong the State Historiographical Institute submitted Hongxu's biography; the Gaozong Emperor ordered that Guo Xiu's impeachment memorial be included, so that later generations would know the crimes of Hongxu and his kind.

entries.zh: 列傳五十八
entries.en: Biographies 58
entries.literal: Biographies 58

entries.zh: 世祖定鼎京師，十一月，以湯若望掌欽天監事。
entries.en: After the Shunzhi Emperor made Beijing the capital, in the eleventh month he placed Tang Ruowang in charge of the Astronomical Bureau.
entries.literal: When the Shizu Emperor established the capital at Beijing, in the eleventh month Tang Ruowang was put in charge of Astronomical Bureau affairs.

entries.zh: 湯若望疏辭，上不許。
entries.en: Tang Ruowang asked to be excused; the emperor refused.
entries.literal: Tang Ruowang memorialized to decline; the emperor did not permit it.

entries.zh: 又疏請別給敕印，而以監印繳部，謂治歷之責，學道之志，庶可並行不悖，上亦不許。
entries.en: He also asked for a personal imperial seal and to surrender the Bureau seal to the ministry, arguing that calendar duty and religious vocation could then coexist—the emperor again said no.
entries.literal: He again memorialized requesting a separate imperial seal be granted, while the Bureau seal be returned to the ministry, saying the duty of governing the calendar and the aspiration of studying the Way could thus proceed without conflict; the emperor also did not permit it.

entries.zh: 並諭湯若望遵旨率屬精修曆法，整頓監規，如有怠玩侵紊，即行參奏。
entries.en: Shunzhi further ordered Tang Ruowang to lead his staff in refining the calendar and tightening Bureau rules, and to report any slackness or misconduct at once.
entries.literal: He also instructed Tang Ruowang to obey the order, lead his subordinates in carefully refining the calendar, and put the Bureau regulations in order; if there were negligence, laxity, or irregularities, he should immediately memorialize against them.

entries.zh: 加太僕寺卿，尋改太常寺卿。
entries.en: He was promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, then transferred to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud; soon after changed to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

entries.zh: 十年三月，賜號通玄教師，敕曰：「國家肇造鴻業，以授時定歷為急務。
entries.en: In the third month of Shunzhi 10 he received the title Master of Penetrating Mysteries. The edict read: "A dynasty at its founding treats fixing time and calendar as urgent business.
entries.literal: In the third month of the tenth year he was granted the title Master who Penetrates the Mysteries; the edict said: "The state, at the founding of its great enterprise, regards bestowing time and fixing the calendar as urgent tasks.

entries.zh: 羲和而後，如漢洛下閎、張衡，唐李淳風、僧一行，於曆法代有損益。
entries.en: Since the calendar minister Xihe, Han had Luoxia Hong and Zhang Heng, Tang had Li Chunfeng and the monk Yixing—each age revised the calendar in turn.
entries.literal: Since Xihe, men such as Luoxia Hong and Zhang Heng of Han, Li Chunfeng and the monk Yixing of Tang, in each generation made additions and subtractions to calendrical methods.

entries.zh: 元郭守敬號為精密，然經緯之度，尚不能符合天行，其後晷度遂以積差。
entries.en: Yuan's Guo Shoujing was called exacting, yet even his longitudes and latitudes never fully matched heaven's motion; gnomon readings drifted ever farther off.
entries.literal: Yuan's Guo Shoujing was famed for precision, yet even his degrees of longitude and latitude could not fully accord with celestial motion; afterward gnomon measurements gradually accumulated error.

entries.zh: 爾湯若望來自西洋，精於象緯，閎通曆法。
entries.en: You, Tang Ruowang, came from the West, master astral patterns, and grasp calendrical method through and through.
entries.literal: You, Tang Ruowang, coming from the Western Ocean, are skilled in astral patterns and versed in calendar methods.

entries.zh: 徐光啟特薦於朝，一時專家治歷如魏文魁等，實不及爾。
entries.en: Xu Guangqi singled you out to the court; reigning calendar men like Wei Wenkui could not match you.
entries.literal: Xu Guangqi especially recommended you to the court; calendar specialists of the time such as Wei Wenkui truly did not equal you.

entries.zh: 但以遠人，多忌成功，終不見用。
entries.en: Yet as a foreigner you met envy; despite your gifts, Ming never fully used you.
entries.literal: Yet because you were a foreigner, many envied your success and in the end you were not employed.

entries.zh: 朕承天眷，定鼎之初，爾為朕脩大清時憲歷，迄於有成。
entries.en: Heaven favored me; at the founding you compiled the Great Qing Shixian Calendar for me until it stood complete.
entries.literal: I, receiving Heaven's favor, at the founding of the capital you for me compiled the Great Qing Shixian Calendar, until it was completed.

entries.zh: 又能潔身持行，盡心乃事。
entries.en: You kept your conduct clean and gave your duties your full heart.
entries.literal: You also kept your person pure in conduct and devoted your heart to your duties.

entries.zh: 今特錫爾嘉名，俾知天生賢人，佐佑定歷，補數千年之闕略，非偶然也。」
entries.en: I now grant this honorific title so you may know Heaven sends able men to fix the calendar and fill gaps of millennia—no accident."
entries.literal: Now I specially bestow upon you this honored name, so you may know that Heaven produces wise men to assist in fixing the calendar, filling a lacuna of several thousand years—it is no accident.

entries.zh: 旋復加通政使，進秩正一品。
entries.en: He was soon made Commissioner of the Office of Transmission and raised to rank 1a.
entries.literal: Soon after he was further promoted to Commissioner of the Office of Transmission and advanced to rank 1a.

entries.zh: 順治元年，睿親王多爾袞定京師，是歲六月，湯若望啟言：「臣於明崇禎二年來京，用西洋新法釐正舊曆，制測量日月星晷、定時考驗諸器。
entries.en: In Shunzhi 1, after Prince Regent Dorgon took Beijing, Tang Ruowang wrote in the sixth month: "I reached the capital in Chongzhen 2, corrected the old calendar by Western methods, and built instruments to measure the sun, moon, and stars, mark shadows, and keep time for verification.
entries.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi, Prince Regent Dorgon secured the capital; that year in the sixth month Tang Ruowang memorialized: "Your servant came to the capital in the second year of Chongzhen of Ming, used the new Western methods to rectify the old calendar, and made instruments for measuring the sun, moon, and stars, shadows, timekeeping, and verification.

entries.zh: 近遭賊毀，擬重製進呈。
entries.en: Bandits recently destroyed them; I propose to rebuild and submit them anew.
entries.literal: Recently they were destroyed by rebels; I propose to remanufacture and present them.

entries.zh: 先將本年八月初一日日食，照新法推步。
entries.en: First, I have computed this year's solar eclipse on the first day of the eighth month by the new method.
entries.literal: First, according to the new methods, I have calculated the solar eclipse on the first day of the eighth month of this year.

entries.zh: 京師日食限分秒並起復方位，與各省所見不同諸數，開列呈覽。」
entries.en: I attach the eclipse limits to the second for Beijing, the points of first and last contact, and how each province's view will differ."
entries.literal: The limits in degrees, minutes, and seconds of the eclipse at Beijing and the directions of first contact and totality, along with the various figures differing from what other provinces will see, are listed for submission and inspection.

entries.zh: 王命湯若望修正曆法。
entries.en: Dorgon ordered Tang Ruowang to revise the calendar.
entries.literal: The prince ordered Tang Ruowang to revise the calendar.

entries.zh: 七月，禮部啟請頒歷，王言：「治歷明時，帝王所重。
entries.en: In the seventh month the Ministry of Rites asked permission to issue the calendar. Dorgon replied: "Ordering the calendar and marking the seasons is among an emperor's gravest duties.
entries.literal: In the seventh month, the Ministry of Rites memorialized requesting issuance of the calendar; the prince said: "Regulating the calendar and clarifying the seasons is what emperors esteem.

entries.zh: 今用新法正歷，以敬迓天休，宜名​​時憲歷，用稱朝廷憲天乂民之至意。
entries.en: Since we now correct the calendar by the new method, in reverence for Heaven's favor, it should be called the Shixian Calendar—'Observing Heaven's Norm'—fitting the court's purpose of harmonizing with Heaven and bringing order to the people.
entries.literal: Now using the new method to correct the calendar, to reverently receive Heaven's blessings, it should be named the Shixian Calendar, to express the court's utmost intent in conforming to Heaven and governing the people.

entries.zh: 自順治二年始，即用新歷頒行天下。」
entries.en: From Shunzhi 2 onward, the new calendar shall be promulgated empire-wide."
entries.literal: Beginning from the second year of Shunzhi, the new calendar shall be issued throughout the realm.

entries.zh: 湯若望復啟言：「敬授人時，全以節氣交宮，與太陽出入、晝夜時刻為重。
entries.en: Tang Ruowang added: "To give the people correct time, nothing matters more than the solar terms crossing the lodges, and the sun's times of rising, setting, and the hours of day and night.
entries.literal: Tang Ruowang further memorialized: "In reverently bestowing human time, what matters entirely is the solar terms' passage through the lodges, and the sun's rising and setting and the times of day and night.

entries.zh: 今節氣、日時、刻分與太陽出入、晝夜時刻，俱照道里遠近推算，增加歷首，以協民時，利民用。」
entries.en: Solar terms, clock times, and sun-rise and sun-set tables for day and night should now be computed for each distance from the capital, added to the calendar's front matter, so local time aligns with the people and serves daily life."
entries.literal: Now the solar terms, days and hours, and quarter-hours, along with the sun's rising and setting and the times of day and night, are all calculated according to distance near and far, added to the calendar header, to harmonize with the people's time and benefit the people's use.

entries.zh: 王獎其精確。
entries.en: Dorgon praised the precision of the proposal.
entries.literal: The prince praised its precision.

entries.zh: 八月丙​​辰朔，日有食之。
entries.en: On bingchen, the first day of the eighth month, there was a solar eclipse.
entries.literal: On the first day of the eighth month, day bingchen, there was a solar eclipse.

entries.zh: 王令大學士馮銓與湯若望率欽天監官赴觀像台測驗，惟新法吻合，大統、回回二法時刻俱不協。
entries.en: Dorgon sent Grand Secretary Feng Quan and Tang Ruowang with Bureau officials to the observatory—the new method alone matched observation; Datong and Muslim reckoning both missed the times.
entries.literal: The prince ordered Grand Secretary Feng Quan and Tang Ruowang to lead Astronomical Bureau officials to the observatory platform for testing; only the new method matched, while the Datong and Muslim methods both failed to agree on the times.

entries.zh: 欽天監舊設回回科，湯若望用新法，久之，罷回回科不置。
entries.en: The Bureau had long kept a Muslim astronomy section; once Tang Ruowang's new method took hold, that section was abolished for good.
entries.literal: The Astronomical Bureau had long maintained a Muslim section; Tang Ruowang used the new method, and after a time the Muslim section was abolished and not reestablished.

entries.zh: 十四年四月，革職回回科秋官正吳明炫疏言：「臣祖默沙亦黑等一十八姓，本西域人。
entries.en: In the fourth month of Shunzhi 14, the dismissed Muslim section's Autumn Officer Wu Mingxuan wrote: "My forebear Mashayihei and seventeen other clans were Western Region families.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of the fourteenth year, dismissed Muslim section Autumn Officer Wu Mingxuan memorialized: "My ancestor Mashayihei and eighteen clans were originally people of the Western Regions.

entries.zh: 自隋開皇己未，抱其歷學，重譯來朝，授職歷官，歷一千五十九載，專管星宿行度。
entries.en: Since Sui Kaihuang jiwei they brought their calendar science, came to court by reinterpretation, and served in office for 1,559 years, charged solely with star lodges and their motion.
entries.literal: Since jiwei of Kaihuang in Sui, bearing their calendrical learning, they came to court through retranslation, received office and served through successive appointments, for one thousand five hundred fifty-nine years exclusively managing the positions and movements of star lodges.

entries.zh: 順治三年，掌印湯若望諭臣科，凡日月交食及太陰五星陵犯、天象佔驗，俱不必奏進。
entries.en: In Shunzhi 3 Director Tang Ruowang told our section that eclipses, lunar and planetary encroachments, and omen readings need no longer be reported to court.
entries.literal: In the third year of Shunzhi, Chief Tang Ruowang instructed our section that all solar and lunar eclipses, lunar and five-planet encroachments, and celestial omens need not be memorialized.

entries.zh: 臣察湯若望推水星二八月皆伏不見，今於二月二十九日仍見東方，又八月二十四日夕見，皆關象佔，不敢不據推上聞。
entries.en: Tang Ruowang predicted Mercury hidden in both the second and eighth months—but on the twenty-ninth of the second it still appeared in the east, and on the evening of the twenty-fourth of the eighth as well; such signs bear on divination, and I must report what the math shows.
entries.literal: Your servant observed that Tang Ruowang calculated Mercury invisible in both the second and eighth months, yet on the twenty-ninth of the second month it was still seen in the east, and on the evening of the twenty-fourth of the eighth month it was seen—these all concern omen interpretation; I dare not fail to report according to calculation.

entries.zh: 乞上復存臣科，庶絕學獲傳。」
entries.en: I beg Your Majesty to restore our section, so this nearly lost science may survive."
entries.literal: I beg Your Majesty to restore our section, so that this dying learning may be transmitted.

entries.zh: 並上十四年回回術推算太陰五星陵犯書，日月交食、天象佔驗圖像。
entries.en: He also submitted Muslim calculations of lunar and planetary encroachments for Shunzhi 14, plus eclipse and omen charts.
entries.literal: He also submitted writings on lunar and five-planet encroachments calculated by Muslim methods for the fourteenth year, and charts of solar and lunar eclipses and celestial omen interpretation.

entries.zh: 別疏又舉湯若望舛謬三事：一、遺漏紫炁，一、顛倒觜參，一、顛倒羅計。
entries.en: A separate memorial listed three Tang Ruowang errors: omitting Purple Qi, reversing Turtle Beak and Three Stars, and reversing Rahu and Ketu.
entries.literal: In a separate memorial he also cited three errors of Tang Ruowang: one, omitting Purple Vapor; one, reversing Turtle Beak and Three Stars; one, reversing Rahu and Ketu.

entries.zh: 八月，上命內大臣愛星阿及各部院大臣登觀像台測驗水星不見，議明炫罪，坐奏事詐不以實，律絞，援赦得免。
entries.en: In the eighth month the emperor sent Inner Minister Esen and ministers from every yamen to the observatory to test Mercury's visibility. Wu Mingxuan was judged guilty of false reporting—strangulation by statute—but escaped through amnesty.
entries.literal: In the eighth month the emperor ordered Inner Minister Esen and ministers of all boards and departments to ascend the observatory platform and test whether Mercury was invisible; Mingxuan's offense was deliberated; he was convicted of memorializing fraudulently and not truthfully, punishable by strangulation by law, but obtained exemption through amnesty.

entries.zh: 國初，命湯若望治歷用新法，頒時憲曆書，面題「依西洋新法」五字。
entries.en: Early in the dynasty Tang Ruowang was ordered to govern the calendar by the new method; the Shixian calendar books bore on their cover the five characters "According to the Western new method."
entries.literal: At the founding of the dynasty, Tang Ruowang was ordered to govern the calendar using the new method; the issued Shixian calendar books bore on their face the five characters "According to the Western Ocean New Method."

entries.zh: 光先上書，謂非所宜用。
entries.en: Yang Guangxian wrote that this should not be used.
entries.literal: Guangxian memorialized, saying this was not what should be used.

entries.zh: 既又論湯若望誤以順治十八年閏十月為閏七月，上所為摘謬、辟邪諸論，攻湯若望甚力，斥所奉天主教為妄言惑眾。
entries.en: He then argued that Tang Ruowang had wrongly made Shunzhi 18's intercalary tenth month into an intercalary seventh; in the Refutation of Errors and anti-heterodoxy essays he had composed, he attacked Tang Ruowang fiercely and denounced Catholicism as delusion misleading the people.
entries.literal: He then again argued that Tang Ruowang had mistakenly taken the intercalary tenth month of Shunzhi 18 as the intercalary seventh month; the Refutation of Errors and various treatises repelling heterodoxy that he had previously composed attacked Tang Ruowang with great force and denounced the Catholicism he professed as wild talk deluding the masses.

entries.zh: 聖祖即位，四輔臣執政，頗右光先，下禮、吏二部會鞫。
entries.en: When Kangxi ascended the throne the four regent ministers favored Yang Guangxian and sent the case to the Ministries of Rites and Personnel for joint trial.
entries.literal: When the Sacred Ancestor ascended the throne, the four assisting ministers held power and largely favored Guangxian; the case was sent to the Ministries of Rites and Personnel for joint interrogation.

entries.zh: 康熙四年，議政王等定讞，盡用光先說，譴湯若望，其屬官至坐死。
entries.en: In Kangxi 4 the regents fixed the verdict wholly on Yang Guangxian's side, censured Tang Ruowang, and punished his subordinates up to death.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Kangxi the regent princes fixed the verdict, wholly adopting Guangxian's views, censuring Tang Ruowang, and his subordinate officials punished up to death.

entries.zh: 遂罷新法，復用大統術。
entries.en: The new method was abandoned and the Datong system restored.
entries.literal: The new method was then abolished and the Datong system restored.

entries.zh: 除光先右監副，疏辭，不許；
entries.en: Yang Guangxian was made Right Assistant Director; he asked to decline and was refused;
entries.literal: Guangxian was appointed Right Assistant Director; he memorialized to decline and was not permitted;

entries.zh: 即授監正，疏辭，復不許。
entries.en: He was then made Director; he declined again and was again refused.
entries.literal: He was immediately appointed Director; he memorialized to decline and again was not permitted.

entries.zh: 列傳五十九
entries.en: Biographies 59
entries.literal: Biographies 59

entries.zh: 十六年春，世祖幸南苑，雍建疏言：「昨因聖體違和，傳諭孟春饗太廟，遣官致祭。
entries.en: In the spring of the sixteenth year the Shunzhi Emperor went to the Southern Park, and Yongjian submitted a memorial: 'Recently, because Your Majesty was unwell, the court announced that the spring sacrifice at the Grand Temple would be performed by dispatched officials.
entries.literal: In the spring of the sixteenth year the Shizu Emperor visited the Southern Park; Yongjian memorialized, saying: 'Yesterday, because the Sacred Person was unwell, an edict was issued that at the first month of spring the Grand Temple would be feasted and officials dispatched to perform the sacrifice.

entries.zh: 至期皇躬康豫，仍親廟祀，此敬修祀典之盛心也。
entries.en: When the day arrived Your Majesty had recovered and still went in person to the temple—a splendid devotion to the rites of worship.
entries.literal: When the day came the imperial person was restored to health and still personally worshipped at the temple—this is the great mind that reverently maintains the sacrificial statutes.

entries.zh: 乃回宮未幾，复幸南苑，寒威未釋，陟歷郊原，恐不足以慎起居。
entries.en: Yet scarcely had you returned to the palace when you went again to the Southern Park; the cold has not lifted, and to range the open countryside may not be prudent for Your Majesty's health and regimen.
entries.literal: Yet not long after returning to the palace, again visiting the Southern Park—cold majesty not yet released, climbing and traversing the suburban wilds—I fear this is not enough to be careful of daily living.

entries.zh: 且古者蒐苗狝狩，各有其時。
entries.en: Besides, in antiquity the spring, summer, autumn, and winter hunts each had its proper season.
entries.literal: Moreover, in antiquity the sou, miao, xian, and shou hunts each had their season.

entries.zh: 設使獸起於前，馬逸於後，驚屬車之清塵，豈能無萬一之慮？」
entries.en: If a beast should start up ahead or a horse run away behind and startle the imperial train, could there be no risk at all?'
entries.literal: Suppose a beast sprang up ahead or a horse bolted behind and startled the clear dust of the attendant chariots—how could there be no thought of the slightest mishap?'

entries.zh: 疏入，上甚怒，宣雍建入，諭以閱兵習武之意。
entries.en: When the memorial arrived the emperor was furious and had Yongjian brought in to explain that the visit was for inspecting troops and military drill.
entries.literal: When the memorial entered, the emperor was greatly angry, summoned Yongjian in, and instructed him of the intent to review troops and practice martial arts.

entries.zh: 雍建奏對不失常度，上意亦解。
entries.en: Yongjian answered calmly and without losing his bearing, and the emperor's anger subsided.
entries.literal: Yongjian replied in audience without losing his usual composure, and the emperor's mind was also eased.

entries.zh: 十八年，地震，求言。
entries.en: In the eighteenth year an earthquake struck, and the court called for memorials.
entries.literal: In the eighteenth year there was an earthquake; the court sought memorials.

entries.zh: 締虞上疏曰：「科道乃朝廷耳目之官，原期知無不言，有聞則告。
entries.en: Diyu wrote: 'The censors and supervising secretaries are the eyes and ears of the court; they are meant to speak of whatever they know and report whatever they hear.
entries.literal: Diyu submitted a memorial saying: 'The censorate and supervising secretaries are the court's eyes and ears; originally it was expected that knowing something they would not fail to speak, hearing something they would report.

entries.zh: 自故憲臣艾元徵請禁風聞條奏，自此言路氣靡，中外多所顧忌。
entries.en: Ever since the late censor Ai Yuanzheng asked to ban memorials based on rumor, the voice of remonstrance has withered and officials everywhere have grown cautious.
entries.literal: Since the late censor Ai Yuanzheng asked to forbid memorials on hearsay, from then the avenue of speech wilted in spirit and inner and outer circles were much restrained.

entries.zh: 臣請皇上省覽世祖朝諸臣奏議，如何謇諤；
entries.en: I beg Your Majesty to read the memorials of the Shunzhi reign and see how blunt they were;
entries.literal: Your servant asks Your Majesty to review the memorials and deliberations of officials in the Shizu reign—how outspoken they were;

entries.zh: 今者相率以條陳為事，輭熟成風。
entries.en: today everyone files the same bland itemized reports, and timid conformity has become the norm.
entries.literal: now all follow one another in making routine itemized submissions, and a soft, smooth manner has become the fashion.

entries.zh: 蓋平時無以作其敢言之氣，一旦欲其慷慨直陳，難矣。
entries.en: If nothing in peacetime stirs their courage to speak out, it is hard to expect bold truth-telling when it is needed.
entries.literal: For in ordinary times nothing rouses their spirit of daring to speak; once wanting them to speak forthrightly and directly is difficult.

entries.zh: 乞敕廷臣會議，嗣後有矢志忠誠、指斥奸佞者，即少差謬，亦賜矜全。
entries.en: He asked the court to deliberate: hereafter, if a man is loyal at heart and denounces the corrupt, even when he is slightly wrong, let him be spared.
entries.literal: He begged that court ministers be ordered to confer: hereafter if one is steadfast in loyalty and denounces the wicked, even if slightly mistaken, also grant lenient preservation.

entries.zh: 如或快意恩仇，受人指使，章奏鈔傳，眾目難掩，縱令彈劾得實，亦難免於徇私之罪。
entries.en: But if a man pursues private vendettas, takes orders from others, and his memorials circulate in copies for all to see, then even a true accusation will still be punished as self-serving.
entries.literal: If one indulges private enmity, is directed by others, and memorials are copied and spread—many eyes cannot hide it—even if impeachment is substantiated, it is still hard to escape the crime of partiality.

entries.zh: 如此，則言官有所顧忌，不敢妄言；
entries.en: In that way censors would have reason to be careful and would not speak recklessly;
entries.literal: In this way censorial officials would have something to fear and not dare speak rashly;

entries.zh: 中外諸臣有所顧忌，不敢妄為。」
entries.en: and officials everywhere would think twice before acting recklessly.'
entries.literal: inner and outer officials would have something to fear and not dare act rashly.'

entries.zh: 疏下九卿科道會議。
entries.en: The memorial was referred to the Nine Ministers and the censorate for joint deliberation.
entries.literal: The memorial was sent down to the Nine Ministers and the censorate for joint deliberation.

entries.zh: 越日，召廷臣等集中左門，上問：「締虞疏如何定議？」
entries.en: The next day the ministers were summoned to the Left Gate, and the emperor asked, 'What is your decision on Diyu's memorial?'
entries.literal: The next day the court ministers were summoned to assemble at the Left Gate; the emperor asked: 'How is Diyu's memorial to be decided?'

entries.zh: 吏部尚書郝惟訥等暨給事中李宗孔等俱言風聞之例，不宜復開。
entries.en: Minister of Personnel Hao Weine, supervising secretary Li Zongkong, and the others all said the ban on hearsay memorials should not be lifted.
entries.literal: Minister of Personnel Hao Weine and others together with supervising secretary Li Zongkong and others all said the precedent on hearsay should not be reopened.

entries.zh: 上問：「締虞，爾意如何？」
entries.en: The emperor turned to him: 'Diyu, what do you think?'
entries.literal: The emperor asked: 'Diyu, what is your view?'

entries.zh: 締虞對曰：「皇上明聖，從未譴罪言官。
entries.en: Diyu answered: 'Your Majesty is wise and has never punished a censor.
entries.literal: Diyu replied: 'Your Majesty is enlightened and sage and has never punished censorial officials.

entries.zh: 但有處分條例在，言官皆生畏懼。」
entries.en: But as long as the disciplinary statutes remain on the books, every censor is afraid.'
entries.literal: But because disciplinary regulations exist, censorial officials all grow fearful.'

entries.zh: 上曰：「如汝言，條例便當廢耶？」
entries.en: The emperor said, 'So by your logic the regulations should be scrapped?'
entries.literal: The emperor said: 'As you say, should the regulations then be abolished?'

entries.zh: 締虞對曰：「科條雖設，當辨公私誠偽。」
entries.en: Diyu replied, 'The statutes may stay, but each case should be judged on whether the motive was public or private, sincere or false.'
entries.literal: Diyu replied: 'Though the statutes are set up, public and private, sincerity and falsity should be distinguished.'

entries.zh: 上意稍解。
entries.en: The emperor's mood softened.
entries.literal: The emperor's mind was somewhat eased.

entries.zh: 諭言：「官宜敷陳國家大事，如有大奸大貪，糾劾得實，法在必行，決不姑貸。
entries.en: He instructed them: 'Officials should speak frankly on matters of state. When great traitors or great thieves are impeached and the charge is proved, the law will be enforced without mercy.
entries.literal: An edict stated: 'Officials should set forth great affairs of state; if there are great traitors or great corruption and impeachment is substantiated, the law must be enforced and will in no case be indulgently spared.

entries.zh: 且魏象樞彈奏程汝璞，亦是風聞，已鞫問得實，原未嘗有風聞之禁也。」
entries.en: When Wei Xiangshu impeached Cheng Rupu it was also on hearsay, yet the charge was proved in court—there has never really been a ban on hearsay memorials.'
entries.literal: Moreover, when Wei Xiangshu impeached Cheng Rupu it was also on hearsay; inquiry already established the facts—originally there was never a ban on hearsay.'

entries.zh: 上宣締虞前，指內閣所呈世祖時章奏示之曰：「汝以朕為未閱此乎？」
entries.en: He had Diyu step forward, pointed to Shunzhi-era memorials the Grand Secretariat had submitted, and said, 'Do you think I have not read these?'
entries.literal: The emperor had Diyu come forward, pointed to memorials from the Shizu reign presented by the Grand Secretariat, and showed them, saying: 'Do you think I have not read these?'

entries.zh: 締虞對曰：「惟久經聖覽，臣故不憚盡言。」
entries.en: Diyu answered, 'Precisely because Your Majesty has read them, I did not hesitate to speak my mind.'
entries.literal: Diyu replied: 'Because they have long received the Sacred View, your servant therefore does not fear to speak fully.'

entries.zh: 上命以所言宣付史館。
entries.en: The emperor ordered his words recorded and sent to the Historiography Institute.
entries.literal: The emperor ordered that what was said be proclaimed and sent to the Historiography Institute.

entries.zh: 次日，復命締虞入起居注，授筆札記之。
entries.en: The next day he had Diyu enter the office of the Veritable Records and write the account himself.
entries.literal: The next day he again ordered Diyu to enter the Veritable Records office and gave him brush and paper to record it.

entries.zh: 尋轉工科掌印給事中。
entries.en: He was soon made chief supervising secretary with seal in the Office of Scrutiny for Works.
entries.literal: Soon he was transferred to chief supervising secretary with seal in the Office of Scrutiny for Works.

entries.zh: 上考察科道，黜孫緒極、傅廷俊、和鹽鼎三人，而嘉締虞與王曰溫、李迥稱職。
entries.en: When the emperor reviewed the censorate he dismissed Sun Xuji, Fu Tingjun, and He Yanding, but praised Diyu, Wang Yuewen, and Li Jiong as fit for their posts.
entries.literal: The emperor inspected the censorate; Sun Xuji, Fu Tingjun, and He Yanding were dismissed, while Diyu together with Wang Yuewen and Li Jiong were praised as competent in office.

entries.zh: 二十一年，疏論外吏積習，視事偷惰，公務沉閣，文移遲緩；
entries.en: In the twenty-first year he wrote on the chronic habits of provincial officials: neglecting their duties, letting business pile up, and delaying paperwork;
entries.literal: In the twenty-first year he memorialized on the accumulated habits of outer officials: attending to duties with lazy theft, public business sunk in files, documents and transfers delayed;

entries.zh: 僚屬宴會，遊客酬酢，廢時糜費。
entries.en: feasting with subordinates, entertaining visitors, and wasting time and money.
entries.literal: subordinates feasting, travelers exchanging toasts, wasting time and squandering expense.

entries.zh: 請敕部禁飭。
entries.en: He asked the ministries to forbid such conduct.
entries.literal: He asked that the ministries be ordered to forbid and correct this.

entries.zh: 累擢左僉都御史。
entries.en: He rose to left assistant censor-in-chief.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to left assistant censor-in-chief.

entries.zh: 列傳六十一
entries.en: Biography 61
entries.literal: Biographies 61

entries.zh: 石琳兄子文晟徐潮子杞貝和諾子馬喇陶岱
entries.en: Shi Lin; his nephew Wencheng; Xu Chao; his son Ziqi; Bei Henuo; his son Mala; Tao Dai
entries.literal: Shi Lin; his nephew Wencheng; Xu Chao; his son Ziqi; Bei Henuo; his son Mala; Tao Dai

entries.zh: 徐潮，字青來，浙江錢塘人。
entries.en: Xu Chao (Qinglai), from Qiantang in Zhejiang.
entries.literal: Xu Chao, style name Qinglai, was a native of Qiantang, Zhejiang.

entries.zh: 康熙十二年進士，選庶吉士，授檢討，累擢少詹事。
entries.en: He passed the jinshi examination in 1673, entered the Hanlin Academy, became a reviser, and rose to junior tutor of the heir apparent.
entries.literal: A jinshi in the twelfth year of Kangxi, he was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, appointed reviser, and successively promoted to junior tutor of the heir apparent.

entries.zh: 潮學問淹通，在翰林，應奉文字，多出其手。
entries.en: A scholar of wide learning, he drafted most of the court's ceremonial writings in the Hanlin.
entries.literal: Chao's learning was broad and penetrating; in the Hanlin, most of the compositions for imperial service came from his hand.

entries.zh: 聖祖嘗禦門召講易、論語，敷陳明晰，為之傾聽。
entries.en: Kangxi once had him lecture on the Changes and Analects at the palace gate; the emperor listened closely to his lucid exposition.
entries.literal: The Sacred Ancestor once summoned him at the palace gate to lecture on the Changes and the Analects; his exposition was clear, and the emperor listened with full attention.

entries.zh: 三遷至工部侍郎，督理錢局，清介不苟隨俗。
entries.en: Promoted thrice, he became vice minister of Works, oversaw the mint, and maintained a scrupulous independence.
entries.literal: After three promotions he reached vice minister of Works, supervised the mint, and was upright and incorruptible, not compromising with custom.

entries.zh: 局官冒濫事發，潮獨無所連染。
entries.en: When the mint scandal broke, Chao alone was untouched.
entries.literal: When abuses by mint officials came to light, Chao alone was not implicated.

entries.zh: 三十三年，典會試。
entries.en: In 1694 he served as chief examiner of the metropolitan civil service examination.
entries.literal: In the thirty-third year he presided over the metropolitan examination.

entries.zh: 以母憂歸，服闋，起刑部侍郎。
entries.en: After mourning his mother he returned as vice minister of Justice.
entries.literal: He returned home for mourning his mother; when the mourning period ended, he was recalled as vice minister of Justice.

entries.zh: 三十九年，授河南巡撫，上諭之曰：「河南火耗最重，州縣多虧欠，爾當籌畫禁止。」
entries.en: In 1700 he became Henan governor; the emperor told him, "Henan's melting-loss surcharges are the worst in the empire and counties are deep in debt—you must stop it."
entries.literal: In the thirty-ninth year he was appointed Henan governor; the emperor instructed him: "Henan's melting-loss surcharge is heaviest and prefectures and counties owe much in arrears—you must plan to forbid it."

entries.zh: 潮上官，令火耗無過一分，州縣私派，悉皆禁革。
entries.en: On taking office he capped melting loss at one percent and abolished every unauthorized local levy.
entries.literal: When Chao took up his post, he ordered that melting loss should not exceed one percent and abolished all private levies by prefectures and counties.

entries.zh: 南陽承解黑鉛，衛輝辦兌漕米，向皆假手胥吏，恣為侵漁。
entries.en: Nanyang's lead deliveries and Weihui's grain conversions had long been farmed out to clerks who extorted the populace.
entries.literal: Nanyang's delivery of black lead and Weihui's handling of tribute-grain conversion had always been left to clerks, who preyed on the people at will.

entries.zh: 潮悉心區畫，宿弊悉除。
entries.en: Chao reorganized both operations and cleared away entrenched corruption.
entries.literal: Chao carefully planned each matter and removed all longstanding abuses.

entries.zh: 開封五府飢，疏請漕糧暫徵改折，以平市直。
entries.en: During famine in the five Kaifeng prefectures he asked to collect tribute grain in cash to steady prices.
entries.literal: When the five prefectures around Kaifeng suffered famine, he memorialized requesting temporary conversion of grain tribute collection to cash payment to stabilize market prices.

entries.zh: 歸德屬永城、虞城、夏邑三縣被災地畝至一萬七千餘頃，出糶常平、義、社倉穀，借給貧民牛種，全活甚眾。
entries.en: More than 17,000 qing were hit in Yongcheng, Yucheng, and Xiayi under Guide; he sold grain from government granaries and lent cattle and seed to the poor, saving countless lives.
entries.literal: In Guide, Yongcheng, Yucheng, and Xiayi of the three counties had disaster-affected fields reaching more than seventeen thousand qing; he released grain from Ever-Normal, charity, and community granaries for sale, and lent oxen and seed to poor households—very many were preserved alive.

entries.zh: 四十一年，上巡幸畿甸，問巡撫李光地鄰省督撫賢否，光地舉潮對。
entries.en: On his 1702 tour of the capital region the emperor asked Li Guangdi which neighboring governors were capable; Li named Chao.
entries.literal: In the forty-first year, when the emperor toured the capital region, he asked Governor Li Guangdi whether neighboring governors and governors-general were worthy; Guangdi named Chao in reply.

entries.zh: 上褒美，以潮與光地、張鵬翮、彭鵬、郭琇並​​稱。
entries.en: The emperor commended him, naming Chao alongside Guangdi, Zhang Penghe, Peng Peng, and Guo Xiu as model officials.
entries.literal: The emperor praised him and ranked Chao together with Guangdi, Zhang Penghe, Peng Peng, and Guo Xiu.

entries.zh: 四十二年，上南巡，潮迎​​駕泰安，賜冠服及御書榜額。
entries.en: During the 1703 southern tour Chao met the emperor at Tai'an and received court dress and an imperial plaque.
entries.literal: In the forty-second year, when the emperor toured south, Chao met the imperial procession at Tai'an and was granted court robes and an imperially inscribed plaque.

entries.zh: 其冬，西巡，复迎駕，賞賚有加。
entries.en: That winter, on the western tour, he again met the emperor and received further gifts.
entries.literal: That winter, on the western tour, he again met the imperial procession and received additional rewards.

entries.zh: 上念汾、渭皆入河，議於河南儲穀，遇山、陝歲歉，自水道移粟，便於陸運。
entries.en: Noting that the Fen and Wei flow into the Yellow River, the emperor proposed grain reserves in Henan so Shanxi and Shaanxi could be fed by water rather than costly land transport in lean years.
entries.literal: The emperor reflected that the Fen and Wei both enter the Yellow River and proposed storing grain in Henan so that when Shanxi and Shaanxi had lean years, grain could be moved by waterway, easier than overland transport.

entries.zh: 命潮會陝西、山西督撫勘議。
entries.en: Chao was told to confer with the Shaanxi and Shanxi governors on the plan.
entries.literal: Chao was ordered to meet with the governors-general and governors of Shaanxi and Shanxi to survey and deliberate.

entries.zh: 潮與川陝總督博霽會勘三門砥柱。
entries.en: Chao and Sichuan-Shaanxi Governor-General Bo Ji inspected the Sanmen Gorge rapids together.
entries.literal: Chao together with Sichuan-Shaanxi governor-general Bo Ji jointly surveyed the pillar rocks at Sanmen.

entries.zh: 語見博霽傳。
entries.en: See Bo Ji's biography for details.
entries.literal: The account appears in Bo Ji's biography.

entries.zh: 又別疏言：「汴水通淮，一自中牟東經祥符至宿遷，湮塞已久；
entries.en: In another memorial he wrote: "The Bian once reached the Huai: one channel east from Zhongmou through Xiangfu to Suqian has been blocked for ages;
entries.literal: He also separately memorialized: "The Bian River connects to the Huai—one route from east of Zhongmou through Xiangfu to Suqian has long been silted shut;

entries.zh: 一自中牟東南經尉氏至太和，今名賈魯河，尚可通流：請量加疏濬。
entries.en: another southeast from Zhongmou through Weishi to Taihe—the present Jia-Lu River—still runs and should be dredged.
entries.literal: another from southeast of Zhongmou through Weishi to Taihe, now called the Jia-Lu River, can still flow—please dredge it as appropriate.

entries.zh: 鄭州北別有支河，舊跡尚存，若於此建閘，使汴與洛通，尤為民便。」
entries.en: A branch north of Zhengzhou still shows its old bed; a sluice there linking the Bian and Luo would greatly help the people."
entries.literal: North of Zhengzhou there is another branch river whose old course still exists; if a sluice were built here to connect the Bian and Luo, it would especially benefit the people."

entries.zh: 上從之。
entries.en: The emperor approved.
entries.literal: The emperor followed his advice.

entries.zh: 四十三年，擢戶部尚書，充經筵講官，兼翰林院掌院學士，教習庶吉士。
entries.en: In 1704 he became minister of Revenue, lectured at the classics colloquium, and headed the Hanlin Academy as tutor to new bachelors.
entries.literal: In the forty-third year he was promoted to minister of Revenue, served as lecturer at the classics colloquium, and concurrently as chancellor of the Hanlin Academy instructing Hanlin bachelors.

entries.zh: 四十四年，扈從南巡，命赴河南按事。
entries.en: In 1705 he joined the southern tour and was sent back to Henan on an investigative mission.
entries.literal: In the forty-fourth year he accompanied the southern tour and was ordered to go to Henan to investigate affairs.

entries.zh: 時上以高郵、寶應諸州縣頻年被水患，由洪澤湖無所宣洩，宜於高堰二壩築堤束水入河，又於下河築堤束水入海。
entries.en: Gaoyou and Baoying had flooded repeatedly because Hongze Lake had no outlet; the emperor wanted dikes at Gaoyan's two dams to drive water into the river and lower-river dikes to send it to the sea.
entries.literal: At that time, because Gaoyou, Baoying, and other prefectures and counties had suffered flooding year after year, since Hongze Lake had no outlet for discharge, dikes should be built at the two dams of Gaoyan to channel water into the river, and dikes built on the lower river to channel water into the sea.

entries.zh: 會潮按事還，上詢河壖形勢，因指授方略，命往董其役。
entries.en: When Chao returned, the emperor asked about the levees, outlined his plan, and put Chao in charge of the project.
entries.literal: When Chao returned from his investigation, the emperor inquired about the river-bank situation, personally instructed strategy, and ordered him to go oversee the work.

entries.zh: 四十五年，監修高家堰滾水壩、高郵車邏中壩，並濬文華寺減河。
entries.en: In 1706 he oversaw the Gaojiayan spillway, Gaoyou's Cheluo middle dam, and dredging of the Wenhua Temple relief channel.
entries.literal: In the forty-fifth year he supervised repair of the Gaojiayan spillway dam, the Gaoyou Cheluo central dam, and dredging of the Wenhua Temple diversion canal.

entries.zh: 四十六年，監修武家壩、天然壩、蔣家壩及諸堤閘，先後畢工。
entries.en: In the forty-sixth year he oversaw reconstruction of the Wujia, Tianran, and Jiangjia dams and other dikes and sluice gates, finishing each project in turn.
entries.literal: In the forty-sixth year, he supervised repairs to the Wujia Dam, Tianran Dam, Jiangjia Dam, and various dikes and sluices; the work was completed in succession.

entries.zh: 四十七年，調吏部。
entries.en: In the forty-seventh year he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
entries.literal: In the forty-seventh year, he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.

entries.zh: 四十九年，以病乞休，許以原官致仕。
entries.en: In the forty-ninth year he asked to retire on account of illness and was allowed to leave office at his existing rank.
entries.literal: In the forty-ninth year, on grounds of illness he requested retirement; he was permitted to retire with his original rank.

entries.zh: 五十四年，卒，賜祭葬。
entries.en: He died in the fifty-fourth year, and the court bestowed state funeral rites upon him.
entries.literal: In the fifty-fourth year, he died; the court granted sacrificial rites and funeral honors.

entries.zh: 潮居官平易，不事矯飾，所至民咸稱頌。
entries.en: As an official Xu Chao was plain and unpretentious, and the people everywhere he served spoke well of him.
entries.literal: Chao in office was easygoing and unpretentious, not given to affectation; wherever he went the people all praised him.

entries.zh: 乾隆初，追諡文敬。
entries.en: Early in the Qianlong reign he was posthumously honored with the title Wenjing.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Qianlong reign, he was posthumously given the temple name Wenjing.

entries.zh: 子本，自有傳。
entries.en: His son Ben is the subject of a separate biography.
entries.literal: His son Ben has his own biography.

entries.zh: 論曰：康熙中葉後，天下乂安，封疆大吏多尚廉能，奉職循理。
entries.en: Commentary: After the mid-Kangxi era the empire was at peace, and frontier governors mostly prized integrity and competence, fulfilling their duties conscientiously.
entries.literal: The commentator says: After the middle of Kangxi, under heaven all was tranquil; frontier great officials mostly valued integrity and ability and fulfilled duties according to principle.

entries.zh: 若石琳改賦役，徐潮革火耗，博霽、華​​顯、音泰整飭武備，安不忘危，皆能舉其職者。
entries.en: Shi Lin reformed tax and corvée assessments, Xu Chao abolished meltage surcharges, and Bo Ji, Hua Xian, and Yin Tai strengthened military readiness—secure yet vigilant—all fulfilling their duties well.
entries.literal: Such as Shi Lin reforming taxes and corvée, Xu Chao abolishing meltage fees, Bo Ji, Hua Xian, and Yin Tai rectifying military preparedness—secure yet not forgetting danger—all were able to fulfill their offices.

entries.zh: 劉廕樞志在休民，未知應兵之不容已，蔣陳錫、鄂海又以督餉稽遲蒙譴，衛既齊遭際殊異，而不獲以功名終，其治行皆有可稱，膏澤及於民，無深淺遠近，要為不沫矣。
entries.en: Liu Yinshu sought to give the people rest but failed to see that war could not always be avoided; Jiang Chenxi and E Hai were censured for supply delays; Wei Jiqi's fate was singular and he did not finish his career in glory—yet all had governance worth praise; their benefits reached the people alike, near or far, great or small—in the end their legacy has not faded.
entries.literal: Liu Yinshu aspired to rest the people yet did not know that military response could not be avoided; Jiang Chenxi and E Hai also suffered censure for delay in supervising grain rations; Wei Jiqi encountered singular circumstances and did not obtain to end in fame and achievement—yet their governance all had points worth praise; their bounty reached the people without regard to depth, nearness, or distance—in essence undimmed.

entries.zh: 列傳六十三
entries.en: Biographies 63
entries.literal: Biographies 63

entries.zh: 三十八年，擢廣西巡撫。
entries.en: In the thirty-eighth year he was promoted to governor of Guangxi.
entries.literal: In the thirty-eighth year he was promoted to governor of Guangxi.

entries.zh: 湖廣總督郭琇請除學政積弊，給事中慕琛、滿晉，御史鄭惟孜等亦疏列順天鄉試事。
entries.en: Huguang Governor-General Guo Xiu memorialized to remove longstanding abuses in the education intendantcy; supervising secretaries Mu Chen and Man Jin, and censor Zheng Weizi, also submitted memorials on the Shuntian provincial examination.
entries.literal: Huguang Governor-General Guo Xiu requested removal of abuses in the education intendantcy; supervising secretaries Mu Chen and Man Jin, and censor Zheng Weizi, also memorialized listing matters of the Shuntian provincial examination.

entries.zh: 上以李光地。
entries.en: The emperor turned to Li Guangdi.
entries.literal: The emperor turned to Li Guangdi.

entries.zh: 張鵬翮、郭琇與鵬俱清廉，命各抒所見。
entries.en: Zhang Pengfei, Guo Xiu, and Peng Peng were all known for integrity; the emperor ordered each to set forth his views.
entries.literal: Zhang Pengfei, Guo Xiu, and Peng Peng were all clean and upright; he ordered each to set forth his views.

entries.zh: 鵬疏言：「琇請嚴督撫處分，學政貪贓，提問督撫，需索陋規，視貪贓治罪，久有定例，請敕榜示律條。
entries.en: Peng Peng memorialized, "Guo Xiu asks for strict punishment of governors and governors-general when education intendants are corrupt; demanding customary fees has long been treated as corruption under established statutes—please issue an edict posting the relevant legal articles.
entries.literal: Peng Peng memorialized: "Xiu requests strict punishment of governors and governors-general; when education intendants are greedy, governors should be questioned; demanding customary fees—there are long-standing statutes treating it like corruption; request an edict posting the legal articles.

entries.zh: 維孜請令各省監生回籍鄉試，九卿慮成均空虛，應責成祭酒司業，就坐監讀書者講習考課，各省學政擇諸生有文行者送入成均，何慮空虛？
entries.en: Zheng Weizi asks that provincial supervising students return home for the provincial examinations; the Nine Ministers fear the Imperial College would be emptied—but charge the Chancellor and Vice-Chancellor to lecture and examine those who remain, and let provincial education intendants select promising students to send to the college. Why should it be empty?
entries.literal: Weizi requests that supervising students in the provinces return home for provincial examinations; the Nine Ministers fear the Imperial College would be emptied; they should charge the Chancellor and Vice-Chancellor to lecture and examine those who remain; provincial education intendants should select literati students of literary merit to send to the college—why fear emptiness?

entries.zh: 琛、晉請察封坐號以防換卷，臣謂換卷多在入門暗約出號交卷時，請嚴稽於此。」
entries.en: Mu Chen and Man Jin ask to inspect sealed seat numbers to prevent paper-switching; I believe switching mostly occurs when candidates secretly agree numbers at entry and exchange papers at submission—please enforce strict checks at those moments."
entries.literal: Chen and Jin request inspecting sealed seat numbers to prevent changing papers; I say changing papers mostly happens at the dark moment of agreeing numbers at entry and handing in papers at exit—request strict checking at these points."

entries.zh: 又言：「文官子弟請皇上親試，臣謂當另立考場，去取聽睿裁。」
entries.en: He also said, "Some ask that sons of civil officials be examined by the emperor in person; I believe a separate examination ground should be established, with acceptance and rejection left to imperial judgment."
entries.literal: He also said: "For sons of civil officials the emperor's personal examination is requested; I say a separate examination ground should be set up, acceptance and rejection left to imperial decision."

entries.zh: 與光地等疏皆下九卿詳議。
entries.en: The memorials of Li Guangdi and the others were all sent to the Nine Ministers for detailed deliberation.
entries.literal: Memorials of Guangdi and others were all sent down to the Nine Ministers for detailed deliberation.

entries.zh: 互詳光地等傳。
entries.en: See the biographies of Li Guangdi and the others for further detail.
entries.literal: Cross-reference to the biographies of Li Guangdi and others.

entries.zh: 時河南巡撫徐潮之任，上諭曰：「爾能如李光地、張鵬翮、郭琇、彭鵬，不但為今之名臣，亦足重於後世矣。」
entries.en: When Xu Chao took office as governor of Henan, the emperor told him, "If you can be like Li Guangdi, Zhang Pengfei, Guo Xiu, and Peng Peng, you will be not only a famous minister in your own day but one whose name will carry weight for generations."
entries.literal: When Henan Governor Xu Chao took office, the emperor instructed him: "If you can be like Li Guangdi, Zhang Pengfei, Guo Xiu, and Peng Peng, you will not only be a famous minister today but also weigh heavy in later ages."

entries.zh: 鵬在官省刑布德，減稅輕徭。
entries.en: In office Peng Peng reduced punishments and spread benevolent rule, cut taxes, and lightened corvée labor.
entries.literal: Peng Peng in office reduced punishment and spread virtue, lowered taxes and lightened corvée.

entries.zh: 廣西舊供魚膠、鐵葉，非其土物，赴廣東採運，鵬疏請免之。
entries.en: Guangxi had formerly been required to supply fish glue and iron leaf—products not native to the province—and had to procure them from Guangdong; Peng memorialized to have the obligation lifted.
entries.literal: Guangxi formerly supplied fish glue and iron leaf, not products of that province; they were procured and transported from Guangdong; Peng memorialized to request exemption.

entries.zh: 列傳六十四
entries.en: Biographies 64
entries.literal: Biographies 64

entries.zh: 順治中，俄羅斯東部人犯黑龍江邊境，時稱為羅剎。
entries.en: During the Shunzhi reign, Russians from the east raided the Heilongjiang frontier and were known at court as the Luosha.
entries.literal: During Shunzhi, people from eastern Russia violated the Heilongjiang border and were at the time called Luosha.

entries.zh: 九年，駐防寧古塔章京海塞遣捕牲翼長希福率兵與戰，師敗績。
entries.en: In Shunzhi 9 (1652), Hai Sai, military governor of the Ningguta garrison, sent Xifu, chief of a hunting-detail wing, against them; the Qing force was defeated.
entries.literal: In the ninth year the garrison commander of Ningguta, Hai Sai, sent the chief of the hunting-detail wing Xifu to lead troops into battle, and the army suffered defeat.

entries.zh: 世祖命誅海塞，鞭希福百，仍駐寧古塔。
entries.en: The Shunzhi Emperor ordered Hai Sai put to death, had Xifu flogged one hundred strokes, and left him in post at Ningguta.
entries.literal: The Shizu Emperor ordered Hai Sai executed, had Xifu flogged one hundred strokes, and left him still stationed at Ningguta.

entries.zh: 十一年，固山額真明安達里率師討之，敗敵黑龍江。
entries.en: In Shunzhi 11 (1654), banner general Ming Andali led troops against them and defeated the enemy on the Heilongjiang.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year the banner general Ming Andali led an army to campaign against them and defeated the enemy on the Heilongjiang.

entries.zh: 羅剎未大創，复侵入精奇里江諸處。
entries.en: The Russians were not crippled and soon raided again along the Jingqiri River and neighboring areas.
entries.literal: The Luosha were not severely wounded and again invaded the region of the Jingqiri River and elsewhere.

entries.zh: 上命大理寺卿明愛等諭令撤回，遷延不即去，據雅克薩城，於其旁耕種漁獵；
entries.en: The emperor sent Chief Judge Ming Ai of the Court of Judicial Review and others to order them to withdraw; they lingered, refused to leave, seized the town of Albazin (Yaksa), and farmed, fished, and hunted nearby;
entries.literal: The emperor ordered the chief judge of the Court of Judicial Review Ming Ai and others to instruct them to withdraw; they delayed and did not leave at once, occupied the city of Yaksa, and farmed, fished, and hunted beside it;

entries.zh: 又過牛滿、恆滾，侵擾索倫、赫哲、飛牙喀、奇勒爾諸部。
entries.en: they crossed the Amur tributaries Nioman and Henggun and raided the Solon, Hezhe, Feiyaka, Qileer, and other peoples.
entries.literal: they also crossed the Nioman and Henggun and harassed the Solon, Hezhe, Feiyaka, Qileer, and other tribes.

entries.zh: 列傳六十七
entries.en: Biographies 67
entries.literal: Biographies 67

entries.zh: 託合齊陰圖報復，欲伺隙中傷。
entries.en: Tuoheqi secretly plotted revenge and watched for a chance to strike at him.
entries.literal: Tuoheqi secretly plotted revenge and wished to seize an opening to wound him.

entries.zh: 五十年，上自暢春園還，見內城街道被侵占甚窄，召託合齊詰責之。
entries.en: In the fiftieth year, returning from the Garden of Everlasting Spring, the emperor saw inner-city streets narrowed by encroachment and summoned Tuoheqi to rebuke him.
entries.literal: In the fiftieth year, when the emperor returned from the Garden of Everlasting Spring he saw that inner-city streets had been encroached upon until very narrow and summoned Tuoheqi to rebuke him.

entries.zh: 託合齊奏外城尤窄。
entries.en: Tuoheqi reported that the outer city was even narrower.
entries.literal: Tuoheqi memorialized that the outer city was even narrower.

entries.zh: 命尚書赫碩色等察勘，託合齊故引視僻巷，民居佔官街得三百餘間，謂皆遐昌任內所造，逮下刑部獄。
entries.en: The emperor ordered Minister Hesose and others to inspect; Tuoheqi deliberately led them through secluded alleys, found more than three hundred dwellings encroaching on official streets, claimed all were built during Xiachang's tenure, and had him sent to the Ministry of Punishments prison.
entries.literal: The emperor ordered Minister Hesose and others to inspect; Tuoheqi deliberately led them to view secluded alleys, finding more than three hundred dwellings occupying official streets, claiming all were built during Xiachang's tenure, and had him arrested and sent to the Ministry of Punishments prison.

entries.zh: 尚書齊世武，託合齊黨也，將刑訊，主事蔣晟持不可。
entries.en: Minister Qishiwu, a member of Tuoheqi's faction, was about to torture him in interrogation; director Jiang Sheng objected.
entries.literal: Minister Qishiwu was of Tuoheqi's faction and was about to apply torture in interrogation; director Jiang Sheng objected that this should not be done.

entries.zh: 乃議遐昌以官街邀民譽，應發奉天安置。
entries.en: They then argued that Xiachang had used official streets to win popular praise and ought to be sent to Fengtian for resettlement.
entries.literal: They then debated that Xiachang had used official streets to win popular praise and ought to be sent to Fengtian for resettlement.

entries.zh: 託合齊黨复譁，言遐昌受賂。
entries.en: Tuoheqi's faction clamored again, claiming Xiachang had taken bribes.
entries.literal: Tuoheqi's faction again clamored, saying Xiachang had taken bribes.

entries.zh: 嚴訊家屬，定爰書，謂據供雖未受賂，但風聞街道舊規，鋪戶修房，每間與胥役錢二三百，以此例之，房三百餘間，計錢七百五十千，當枉法贓律處絞。
entries.en: His family was strictly interrogated and the case record fixed: though confession showed no direct bribes, by old street practice shopkeepers paid clerks two or three hundred cash per room when repairing houses; for more than three hundred rooms that totaled seven hundred fifty thousand cash, warranting strangulation under the statute on illicit gain through bending the law.
entries.literal: His family was strictly interrogated and the case record fixed, stating that though confession did not show he had taken bribes, it was heard that by old street regulations shopkeepers repairing houses gave clerks two or three hundred cash per room; by this reckoning, for more than three hundred rooms the total was seven hundred fifty thousand cash, and he ought to be executed by strangulation under the statute on illicit gain through bending the law.

entries.zh: 朝審，具冤狀。
entries.en: At court review he presented a statement of wrongful conviction.
entries.literal: At court review he presented a statement of wrongful conviction.

entries.zh: 尚書王掞、李天馥謂遐昌廉能為上知，宜從寬典，富寧安讚之，獄乃緩。
entries.en: Ministers Wang Yan and Li Tianfu said the emperor knew Xiachang's integrity and ability and he ought to receive lenient treatment; Funing'an agreed, and the case was slowed.
entries.literal: Ministers Wang Yan and Li Tianfu said Xiachang's integrity and ability were known to the emperor and he ought to receive lenient treatment; Funing'an praised this, and the case was slowed.

entries.zh: 會託合齊以病乞假，隆科多攝其職，因言託合齊罔上行私，橫恣貪婪，及誣陷遐昌狀。
entries.en: When Tuoheqi begged sick leave, Longkodo took over his duties and reported that Tuoheqi had deceived the throne, pursued private ends, acted violently and greedily, and had framed Xiachang.
entries.literal: When Tuoheqi begged leave on grounds of illness, Longkodo took over his duties and reported that Tuoheqi had deceived the throne and pursued private ends, acted violently and was greedy, and described how he had framed Xiachang.

entries.zh: 上命釋遐昌，都人爭赴獄舁之出，擁赴闕謝。
entries.en: The emperor ordered Xiachang released; capital residents rushed to the prison to carry him out and escorted him to the palace gate to give thanks.
entries.literal: The emperor ordered Xiachang released; capital residents rushed to the prison to carry him out and escorted him to the palace gate to give thanks.

entries.zh: 及出都，送者填溢，醵金完懸贓。
entries.en: When he left the capital, well-wishers filled the roads and pooled money to pay off the suspended illicit-gain fine.
entries.literal: When he left the capital, senders filled the roads; they pooled money to pay off the suspended illicit-gain fine.

entries.zh: 遐昌歸，未幾卒。
entries.en: Xiachang returned home and died before long.
entries.literal: Xiachang returned home and before long died.

entries.zh: 列傳六十九
entries.en: Biographies 69
entries.literal: Biographies 69

entries.zh: 乾隆四十七年，高宗命侍衛阿彌達詣西寧祭河神，再窮河源。
entries.en: In Qianlong 47 the Gaozong Emperor sent bodyguard Amita to Xining to sacrifice to the river god and once more trace the Yellow River to its source.
entries.literal: In the forty-seventh year of Qianlong, the Gaozong Emperor ordered the bodyguard Amita to go to Xining to sacrifice to the river god and again trace the river source to its end.

entries.zh: 還奏：「星宿海西南有水名阿勒坦郭勒，更西有巨石高數丈，名阿勒坦噶達素齊老。
entries.en: On returning he reported: "Southwest of the Sea of Starry Constellations lies a stream called Altan Gol; farther west stands a boulder several zhang high called Altan Gadasu Qilao.
entries.literal: On his return he memorialized: "Southwest of the Sea of Starry Constellations is a stream called Altan Gol; farther west is a boulder several zhang high called Altan Gadasu Qilao.

entries.zh: 蒙古語'阿勒坦'為黃金，'噶達素'為北極星，'郭勒'為河，'齊老'石也。
entries.en: In Mongol altan means gold, gadasu the North Star, gol a river, and qilao a stone.
entries.literal: In Mongol 'altan' means gold, 'gadasu' the North Star, 'gol' a river, and 'qilao' a stone.

entries.zh: 崖壁黃金色，上有池，池中泉噴湧，釃為百道，皆黃金色。
entries.en: The cliff shone golden; above it a pool fed springs that burst forth in a hundred golden streams.
entries.literal: The cliff face was golden in color; above it was a pool from which springs gushed, dividing into a hundred channels, all golden-hued.

entries.zh: 入阿勒坦郭勒，迴旋三百餘裡，入星宿海，為黃河真源。」
entries.en: The Altan Gol wound over three hundred li before reaching the Sea of Starry Constellations—the Yellow River's true source."
entries.literal: Entering the Altan Gol, it wound more than three hundred li before joining the Sea of Starry Constellations—this was the true source of the Yellow River."

entries.zh: 高宗命四庫館諸臣輯河源紀略識其事。
entries.en: The emperor ordered Siku scholars to compile the He Yuan Ji Lue to document the discovery.
entries.literal: The Gaozong ordered scholars of the Siku Library to compile the He Yuan Ji Lue to record the matter.

entries.zh: 阿彌達更名阿必達。
entries.en: Amita was renamed Abida.
entries.literal: Amita was renamed Abida.

entries.zh: 大學士阿桂子，附見阿桂傳。
entries.en: He was a son of Grand Secretary Agui; see Agui's biography.
entries.literal: He was a son of Grand Secretary Agui; see the biography of Agui.

entries.zh: 圖理琛遷郎中。
entries.en: Tulichen was promoted to director.
entries.literal: Tulichen was transferred to director.

entries.zh: 世宗即位，命赴廣東察籓庫，就擢廣東布政使。
entries.en: When Yongzheng acceded, he was sent to inspect Guangdong's treasury and was promoted provincial administration commissioner on the spot.
entries.literal: When the Shizong Emperor acceded, Tulichen was ordered to Guangdong to inspect the treasury and was there promoted provincial administration commissioner of Guangdong.

entries.zh: 調陝西。
entries.en: He was transferred to Shaanxi.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Shaanxi.

entries.zh: 三年，擢巡撫。
entries.en: In Yongzheng 3 he was made governor.
entries.literal: In the third year he was promoted governor.

entries.zh: 五年，召為兵部侍郎，調吏部。
entries.en: In Yongzheng 5 he was recalled as vice minister of War, then moved to the Board of Civil Office.
entries.literal: In the fifth year he was summoned as vice minister of the Board of War and transferred to the Board of Civil Office.

entries.zh: 偕喀爾喀郡王額駙策淩等往定喀爾喀與鄂羅斯界。
entries.en: With Khalkha Prince and imperial son-in-law Celeng he went to delimit the Khalkha–Russia border.
entries.literal: Together with Khalkha Prince and imperial son-in-law Celeng and others he went to fix the border between Khalkha and Russia.

entries.zh: 仍調兵部。
entries.en: He was transferred back to the Board of War.
entries.literal: He was again transferred to the Board of War.

entries.zh: 六年，追議前定界時，與鄂羅斯使臣薩瓦鳴砲謝天，私立木牌，並擅納鄂羅斯貿易人入界；
entries.en: In Yongzheng 6 a review of the border mission charged that with Russian envoy Sava he had fired cannon to thank Heaven, erected markers without authorization, and admitted Russian traders across the border;
entries.literal: In the sixth year, on review of the earlier border delimitation, it was charged that with the Russian envoy Sava he had fired cannon to thank Heaven, erected wooden markers on his own authority, and improperly admitted Russian traders within the border;

entries.zh: 又前任陝西巡撫時，將天下兵數繕摺私給將軍延信，逮問論斬。
entries.en: and as Shaanxi governor he had privately given General Yanxin a memorial listing empire-wide troop strengths; he was arrested and sentenced to death.
entries.literal: further, while governor of Shaanxi he had privately given General Yanxin a memorial listing troop strengths empire-wide; he was arrested, tried, and sentenced to death.

entries.zh: 詔宥免，遣築扎克拜達里克城。
entries.en: An edict pardoned him and sent him to build Zakbaydarik.
entries.literal: An edict pardoned him and sent him to build Zakbaydarik City.

entries.zh: 高宗即位，授內閣學士，遷工部侍郎。
entries.en: When Qianlong acceded he was made grand secretary and vice minister of the Board of Works.
entries.literal: When the Gaozong acceded he was appointed grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat and transferred to vice minister of the Board of Works.

entries.zh: 乾隆元年，以老解侍郎任，仍為內閣學士。
entries.en: In Qianlong 1, citing age, he left the vice ministership but remained grand secretary.
entries.literal: In the first year of Qianlong, on grounds of age he was relieved of the vice ministership but remained grand secretary.

entries.zh: 二年，引疾去。
entries.en: In Qianlong 2 he retired on grounds of illness.
entries.literal: In the second year he retired citing illness.

entries.zh: 五年，卒。
entries.en: In Qianlong 5 he died.
entries.literal: In the fifth year he died.

entries.zh: 高宗既定準噶爾，乾隆二十一年，命國宗偕侍衛努克三、哈清阿率欽天監西洋人往伊犁，自巴里坤分西北兩路，測天度繪圖。
entries.en: After Qianlong pacified Dzungaria, in Qianlong 21 Guozong was sent with bodyguards Nukesan and Haqing'a to lead Astronomical Bureau Europeans to Ili; from Barkol they split into northwest and southwest routes to measure latitude and survey maps.
entries.literal: After the Gaozong had pacified Dzungaria, in the twenty-first year of Qianlong Guozong was ordered, with bodyguards Nukesan and Haqing'a, to lead Westerners of the Astronomical Bureau to Ili; from Barkol they divided into northwest and southwest routes to measure celestial degrees and survey maps.

entries.zh: 既還報，命署左都御史。
entries.en: On their return he was ordered to serve as acting left censor-in-chief.
entries.literal: On their return he was ordered to act as left censor-in-chief.

entries.zh: 二十二年，授禮部尚書。
entries.en: In Qianlong 22 he was made minister of Rites.
entries.literal: In the twenty-second year he was appointed minister of Rites.

entries.zh: 以京察舉弟國棟，​​坐徇庇，奪官。
entries.en: In the metropolitan evaluation he recommended his brother Guodong; for favoritism he was stripped of office.
entries.literal: In the metropolitan evaluation he recommended his brother Guodong; for favoritism his office was stripped.

entries.zh: 尋授編修，直上書房。
entries.en: He was soon made compiler and assigned to the Upper Study.
entries.literal: Soon he was appointed compiler and served in the Upper Study.

entries.zh: 二十八年，复授內閣學士。
entries.en: In Qianlong 28 he was again made grand secretary.
entries.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was again appointed grand secretary.

entries.zh: 是歲，上以諸回部悉定，復遣尚書明安圖等往測天度繪圖，是為乾隆內府皇輿圖。
entries.en: That year, with the Muslim regions pacified, the emperor again sent Minister Ming Antu and others to measure and map—the Qianlong inner-palace imperial atlas.
entries.literal: That year, with all Muslim regions pacified, the emperor again sent Minister Ming Antu and others to measure celestial degrees and survey maps—this was the Qianlong inner-palace imperial map.

entries.zh: 二十六年，遷禮部侍郎。
entries.en: In Qianlong 26 he was made vice minister of Rites.
entries.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was transferred to vice minister of Rites.

entries.zh: 二十七年，以老休致。
entries.en: In Qianlong 27 he retired on grounds of age.
entries.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he retired on grounds of age.

entries.zh: 三十一年，卒。
entries.en: In Qianlong 31 he died.
entries.literal: In the thirty-first year he died.

entries.zh: 論曰：國家撫有疆宇，謂之版圖，版言乎其有民，圖言乎其有地。
entries.en: The commentator writes: When the state holds territory, it is called ban tu—ban refers to having people, tu to having land.
entries.literal: The commentator says: When the state extends its rule over territory, this is called ban tu—ban speaks of having people, tu of having land.

entries.zh: 聖祖東訪長白山，西探河源，北撫土爾扈特，武默訥、舒蘭、圖理琛奉使稱職。
entries.en: The Sacred Ancestor visited Changbai in the east, traced the river source in the west, and received the Torghuts in the north; Wu Mone, Shu Lan, and Tulichen all served ably as envoys.
entries.literal: The Sacred Ancestor inspected Mount Changbai in the east, explored the river source in the west, and comforted the Torghuts in the north; Wu Mone, Shu Lan, and Tulichen discharged their missions worthily.

entries.zh: 觀所還奏，曲折詳盡，歷歷如繪。
entries.en: Their returned memorials are exhaustive in detail, vivid as paintings.
entries.literal: Reading their returned memorials, the detail is exhaustive, vivid as painting.

entries.zh: 國宗以明算事聖祖，又幸老壽，迨高宗朝，詣新疆測繪。
entries.en: Guozong, expert in calculation, served the Sacred Ancestor and lived to great age; under Qianlong he went to Xinjiang to survey and map.
entries.literal: Guozong, skilled in calculation, served the Sacred Ancestor and was blessed with long life; reaching the Gaozong reign he went to Xinjiang to survey.

entries.zh: 康熙、乾隆兩內府圖皆躬與編摹。
entries.en: He personally helped compile both the Kangxi and Qianlong inner-palace atlases.
entries.literal: He personally took part in compiling both the Kangxi and Qianlong inner-palace maps.

entries.zh: 揆之於古，其裴秀、賈耽之倫歟？
entries.en: Judged against antiquity, is he not the equal of Pei Xiu and Jia Dan?
entries.literal: Measured against antiquity, is he not in the company of Pei Xiu and Jia Dan?

entries.zh: 列傳七十
entries.en: Biographies 70
entries.literal: Biographies 70

entries.zh: 六十一年，授台灣總兵。
entries.en: In 1722 he was appointed regional commander of Taiwan.
entries.literal: In the sixty-first year he was appointed Taiwan Regional Commander.

entries.zh: 雍正元年，擢福建水師提督，加左都督，賜孔雀翎，予三等阿達哈哈番世職。
