entries.en: In 1723 he was promoted to naval commander of Fujian, given the additional rank of Left Commander-in-Chief, bestowed a peacock feather, and granted a hereditary rank of Third Class Adahafan.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng he was promoted to Fujian Naval Commander, given the additional rank of Left Commander-in-Chief, bestowed a peacock feather, and granted a hereditary rank of Third Class Adahafan.

entries.zh: 世宗褒廷珍忠赤，惟屢勉以操守。
entries.en: The Yongzheng Emperor praised Tingzhen's loyal devotion but repeatedly urged him to keep his integrity.
entries.literal: The Yongzheng Emperor praised Tingzhen's loyal devotion but repeatedly exhorted him on integrity.

entries.zh: 二年，入覲，命赴馬蘭峪謁景陵，賞賚稠疊。
entries.en: In 1724 he came to court, was ordered to pay respects at the Jing Mausoleum at Malanyu, and received lavish rewards.
entries.literal: In the second year he came to audience, was ordered to go to Malanyu to pay respects at the Jing Mausoleum, and received rich rewards.

entries.zh: 七年，病聞，遣醫診視。
entries.en: In 1729 word came that he was ill, and the court sent physicians to attend him.
entries.literal: In the seventh year word of illness came; physicians were sent to examine him.

entries.zh: 尋卒，贈太子少保，諡襄毅。
entries.en: He soon died and was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the posthumous title Xiangyi.
entries.literal: Soon he died and was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the posthumous title Xiangyi.

entries.zh: 子日寵，嗣世職，官銅山營參將。
entries.en: His son Richong succeeded to the hereditary rank and served as garrison deputy commander of the Tongshan camp.
entries.literal: His son Richong succeeded to the hereditary rank and served as garrison deputy commander of the Tongshan camp.

entries.zh: 孫元枚，自有傳。
entries.en: His grandson Yuanmei has his own biography.
entries.literal: His grandson Yuanmei has his own biography.

entries.zh: 族弟鼎元，字玉霖，力學負才。
entries.en: His clansman younger brother Dingyuan, whose style was Yulin, was a diligent scholar of real ability.
entries.literal: His clansman younger brother Dingyuan, style name Yulin, studied hard and possessed talent.

entries.zh: 廷珍統師入台灣，鼎元參軍事，著平台紀略。
entries.en: When Tingzhen led the army into Taiwan, Dingyuan served on his staff and wrote A Brief Account of Pacifying Taiwan.
entries.literal: When Tingzhen commanded the army into Taiwan, Dingyuan took part in military affairs and wrote A Brief Account of Pacifying Taiwan.

entries.zh: 雍正元年，詔舉文行兼優之士，貢入太學，有司以鼎元薦，大學士硃軾器之，用薦得召見。
entries.en: In 1723 an edict called for men distinguished in both learning and conduct to enter the Imperial Academy. Local officials recommended Dingyuan; Grand Secretary Zhu Shi valued him, and on that recommendation he was summoned to audience.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng an edict called for men excellent in both learning and conduct to be presented to the Imperial Academy; the local officials recommended Dingyuan; Grand Secretary Zhu Shi valued him and through recommendation he was summoned to audience.

entries.zh: 上書陳時政，上嘉納。
entries.en: He submitted a memorial on current affairs, and the emperor praised and accepted it.
entries.literal: He submitted a memorial on current policy and the emperor praised and accepted it.

entries.zh: 授廣東普寧知縣。
entries.en: He was appointed magistrate of Puning in Guangdong.
entries.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Puning in Guangdong.

entries.zh: 居官有惠政，長於斷獄。
entries.en: In office he governed with kindness and excelled at deciding cases.
entries.literal: In office he had benevolent policies and excelled at deciding cases.

entries.zh: 性伉直，坐事劾罷。
entries.en: He was blunt and upright by nature and was impeached and dismissed over an affair.
entries.literal: His nature was upright and blunt; he was impeached and dismissed for an affair.

entries.zh: 總督鄂彌達白其誣，召詣京師。
entries.en: Governor-General E'erjidari reported that the charge was false, and he was summoned to the capital.
entries.literal: Governor-General E'erjidari reported that he had been falsely charged and he was summoned to the capital.

entries.zh: 旋署廣州知府。
entries.en: He was soon appointed acting prefect of Guangzhou.
entries.literal: Soon he was appointed acting prefect of Guangzhou.

entries.zh: 甫一月，卒。
entries.en: After only one month in office he died.
entries.literal: After only one month he died.

entries.zh: 鼎元嘗論台灣善後策，謂諸羅宜畫地更設一縣，總兵不可移駐澎湖。
entries.en: Dingyuan once proposed policies for governing Taiwan after the rebellion, arguing that Zhuluo should be divided to form a new county and that the regional commander should not be moved to Penghu.
entries.literal: Dingyuan once discussed policies for Taiwan after pacification, saying Zhuluo should be divided to establish another county and the regional commander should not be moved to garrison Penghu.

entries.zh: 後諸羅析縣曰彰化，更設北路三營，總兵官仍駐台灣，皆如鼎元言。
entries.en: Later Zhuluo was split off as Zhanghua county, three northern-route camps were established, and the regional commander remained in Taiwan—all as Dingyuan had urged.
entries.literal: Later Zhuluo was divided into the county of Zhanghua, three northern-route camps were newly established, and the regional commander still garrisoned Taiwan—all as Dingyuan had said.

entries.zh: 列傳七十一
entries.en: Biographies 71
entries.literal: Biographies 71

entries.zh: 王掞子奕清奕鴻勞之辨硃天保陶彝任坪范長發鄒圖雲
entries.en: Wang Shan; his sons Yiqing and Yihong; Lao Zhibian; Zhu Tianbao; Tao Yi; Ren Ping; Fan Changfa; and Zou Tuyun
entries.literal: Wang Shan; his sons Yiqing and Yihong; Lao Zhibian; Zhu Tianbao; Tao Yi; Ren Ping; Fan Changfa; Zou Tuyun

entries.zh: 王掞，字藻儒，江南太倉人，明大學士錫爵孫。
entries.en: Wang Shan, whose style was Zaoru, came from Taicang in Jiangnan. He was the grandson of the Ming Grand Secretary Xijue.
entries.literal: Wang Shan, style Zaoru, was a native of Taicang in Jiangnan; he was the grandson of Xijue, Grand Secretary of the Ming.

entries.zh: 康熙九年進士，選庶吉士，授編修，為掌院學士熊賜履所器。
entries.en: In 1670 he became a metropolitan graduate, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was made a compiler. Chancellor Xiong Cili held him in high regard.
entries.literal: In the ninth year of the Kangxi reign he passed the metropolitan examination, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed compiler; he was esteemed by Xiong Cili, the academy's chancellor.

entries.zh: 遷左贊善，充日講起居注官。
entries.en: He was promoted to Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent and appointed to the Daily Lecture and Imperial Diary.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent and served as an officer of the Daily Lecture and Imperial Diary.

entries.zh: 以病告八年，起右贊善。
entries.en: After eight years' leave for illness, he was recalled as Right Assistant to the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: He resigned on grounds of illness for eight years, then was recalled as Right Assistant to the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 提督浙江學政，嚴剔積弊，所拔多宿學寒畯。
entries.en: As Zhejiang educational commissioner, he rooted out entrenched abuses and chiefly promoted seasoned scholars from poor families.
entries.literal: As educational commissioner of Zhejiang, he rigorously eliminated long-standing abuses; most of those he advanced were veteran scholars of humble birth.

entries.zh: 龍泉知縣茅國璽以印揭薦武童，掞疏劾，國璽坐譴，別疏陳剔除積弊，報聞。
entries.en: When Longquan magistrate Mao Guoxi used his official seal to recommend a military candidate, Shan impeached him and Mao was punished. Shan also submitted a separate memorial on rooting out abuses, which the throne acknowledged.
entries.literal: Mao Guoxi, magistrate of Longquan, used an official seal on a memorial to recommend a military candidate; Shan memorialized in impeachment, and Guoxi was punished. In a separate memorial he set forth the elimination of accumulated abuses; the court was informed.

entries.zh: 累遷侍讀學士。
entries.en: He rose through several posts to Reader-in-Waiting.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Reader-in-Waiting.

entries.zh: 三十年，超擢內閣學士。
entries.en: In 1691 he was specially promoted to Academician of the Grand Secretariat.
entries.literal: In the thirtieth year he was promoted by special selection to Academician of the Grand Secretariat.

entries.zh: 三十三年，遷戶部侍郎，直經筵。
entries.en: In 1694 he became Vice Minister of Revenue and continued to attend the imperial lecture.
entries.literal: In the thirty-third year he was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue and attended the Classics Lecture.

entries.zh: 三十八年，調吏部，禁革臨選駁查、臨掣買簽諸弊，銓政以肅。
entries.en: In 1699 he moved to the Ministry of Personnel, banned abuses such as last-minute rejections, rigged lot-drawing, and purchased appointments, and brought the civil service roster under order.
entries.literal: In the thirty-eighth year he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, forbade and abolished such abuses as last-minute rejection of candidates, last-minute drawing of lots, and buying appointments; personnel administration was thereby rectified.

entries.zh: 偕尚書范承勳、王鴻緒督修高家堰河工。
entries.en: With Ministers Fan Chengxun and Wang Hongxu he oversaw repairs on the Gaojia Embankment.
entries.literal: Together with Ministers Fan Chengxun and Wang Hongxu he supervised repairs on the Gaojia Embankment river works.

entries.zh: 四十三年，擢刑部尚書。
entries.en: In 1704 he was appointed Minister of Justice.
entries.literal: In the forty-third year he was promoted to Minister of Justice.

entries.zh: 刑部奏讞無漢字供狀，掞言：「本朝官制，兼設滿、漢，欲其彼此參詳。
entries.en: When the Ministry reported a verdict with no Chinese deposition, Shan said: "In our dynasty Manchu and Han officials serve side by side so that each may review the other.
entries.literal: The Ministry of Justice reported a verdict without a Chinese-language deposition. Shan said: "Our dynasty's official system sets up both Manchu and Han posts, intending that they consult each other.

entries.zh: 今獄詞不錄漢語，是非曲直，漢司官何由知之？
entries.en: If the record omits Chinese, how can Han officials judge right from wrong?
entries.literal: Now if the case record does not include Chinese, how are Han officials to know right from wrong?

entries.zh: 若隨聲畫諾，幾成虛設。
entries.en: If they only nod along, their offices are reduced to empty names.
entries.literal: If they merely echo assent, their posts are nearly empty titles.

entries.zh: 嗣後定讞，當滿、漢稿並具。」
entries.en: From now on verdicts should be drawn up in both Manchu and Chinese."
entries.literal: Henceforth in fixing verdicts, Manchu and Han drafts should both be prepared."

entries.zh: 詔報可，著為令。
entries.en: The emperor approved and issued it as a permanent rule.
entries.literal: The edict approved and made it a standing regulation.

entries.zh: 累歷工、兵、禮諸部，務總紀綱，持大體。
entries.en: He served in turn at Works, War, and Rites, always keeping the broad framework in view and holding to principle.
entries.literal: He successively served in the Ministries of Works, War, and Rites, always keeping to the overall framework and upholding the larger principles.

entries.zh: 五十一年，授文淵閣大學士，兼禮部尚書，直經筵如故。
entries.en: In 1712 he became Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion and concurrent Minister of Rites, and continued at the imperial lecture as before.
entries.literal: In the fifty-first year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion and concurrently Minister of Rites, attending the Classics Lecture as before.

entries.zh: 五十二年，典會試。
entries.en: In 1713 he presided over the metropolitan examination.
entries.literal: In the fifty-second year he presided over the metropolitan examination.

entries.zh: 其冬，以疾疏辭閣務，溫旨慰留。
entries.en: That winter he asked to leave the Grand Secretariat on grounds of illness, but the emperor warmly urged him to stay.
entries.literal: That winter, citing illness, he memorialized to resign from Grand Secretariat duties; a gracious edict urged him to remain.

entries.zh: 越年春，疾愈，仍入直。
entries.en: The next spring, recovered, he returned to regular duty at court.
entries.literal: The following spring, recovered, he resumed attendance at court.

entries.zh: 孝惠章皇后祔太廟，議者欲祔於孝康章皇后之次，掞曰：「孝康章皇后雖母以子貴，然孝惠章皇后，章皇帝嫡配也，上聖孝格天。
entries.en: When Empress Xiaohui was to be installed in the Ancestral Temple, some proposed placing her after Empress Xiaokang. Shan said: "Empress Xiaokang was honored as mother through her son, yet Empress Xiaohui was the lawful consort of Emperor Zhang, and the emperor's filial devotion reaches Heaven.
entries.literal: When Empress Xiaohui was to be enshrined in the Imperial Ancestral Temple, deliberators wished to place her after Empress Xiaokang. Shan said: "Although Empress Xiaokang was honored as mother through her son, Empress Xiaohui was the lawful consort of Emperor Zhang; His Majesty's filial piety moves Heaven.

entries.zh: 曩者太皇太后祔廟時，不以躋孝端文皇后之上，今肯以孝康章皇后躋孝惠章皇后上乎？」
entries.en: When the Grand Empress Dowager was enshrined, she was not ranked above Empress Xiaoduan. Would the throne now rank Empress Xiaokang above Empress Xiaohui?"
entries.literal: When the Grand Empress Dowager was enshrined, she was not placed above Empress Xiaoduan; would His Majesty now place Empress Xiaokang above Empress Xiaohui?"

entries.zh: 禮部不從，上果以為非，令改正。
entries.en: The Ministry of Rites disagreed, but the emperor found the plan improper and ordered it changed.
entries.literal: The Ministry of Rites did not agree, but the emperor indeed held it wrong and ordered correction.

entries.zh: 六十年春，群臣請賀萬壽，上勿許。
entries.en: In the spring of 1721 the court asked to celebrate his birthday, but the emperor refused.
entries.literal: In the spring of the sixtieth year the officials asked to celebrate his longevity; the emperor did not permit it.

entries.zh: 掞复疏前事，請釋二阿哥，語加激切。
entries.en: Shan memorialized again on the same issue, urging release of the Second Prince in increasingly forceful terms.
entries.literal: Shan again memorialized on the earlier matter, asking that the Second Prince be released; his language grew sharply urgent.

entries.zh: 既而御史陶彝等十二人連名入奏，上疑出掞意，大怒，召諸王大臣，降旨責掞植黨希榮，且謂：「錫爵在明神宗時，力奏建儲，泰昌在位，未及數月，天啟庸懦，天下大亂，至愍帝而不能守。
entries.en: Then Censors Tao Yi and eleven others submitted a joint memorial. Suspecting Shan had orchestrated it, the emperor flew into a rage, summoned the princes and senior ministers, and rebuked Shan for faction-building and ambition. He said: "Under the Ming Shenzong, Xijue pressed hard for an heir. Taichang reigned only months. Tianqi was weak, the realm collapsed, and even Chongzhen could not hold the state.
entries.literal: Soon after, Censors Tao Yi and eleven others jointly memorialized. The emperor suspected this came from Shan's instigation, was greatly angered, summoned the princes and high ministers, and issued an edict rebuking Shan for forming factions and seeking glory, saying: "Xijue in the Ming under Shenzong strongly urged establishing an heir. Taichang reigned less than a few months; Tianqi was weak and timid; the realm fell into great disorder, until Chongzhen could not hold it.

entries.zh: 明之亡，錫爵不能辭其罪。
entries.en: Xijue cannot escape blame for the fall of the Ming.
entries.literal: For the fall of the Ming, Xijue cannot escape blame.

entries.zh: 掞以朕為神宗乎？
entries.en: Does Shan take me for Shenzong?
entries.literal: Does Shan take Me for Shenzong?

entries.zh: 朕初無誅大臣之意，大臣自取其死，朕亦無如何。」
entries.en: I never meant to kill a great minister. If ministers court their own ruin, there is little I can do."
entries.literal: I had no initial intent to execute great ministers; the ministers bring death upon themselves, and I can do nothing about it."

entries.zh: 令王大臣傳旨詰掞，令回奏。
entries.en: He ordered the princes and ministers to question Shan and demand a written reply.
entries.literal: He ordered the princes and ministers to convey the edict interrogating Shan and to require a written reply.

entries.zh: 時舉朝失色，無敢與筆硯者。
entries.en: The whole court was stricken. No one dared give him brush and ink.
entries.literal: At the time the whole court turned pale; none dared supply him brush and ink.

entries.zh: 掞就宮門階石上裂紙，以唾濡墨，奏言：「臣伏見宋仁宗為一代賢君，而晚年立儲猶豫，其時名臣如范鎮、包拯等，皆交章切諫，鬚髮為白。
entries.en: On the palace steps Shan tore paper and wrote with saliva for ink. He said: "I observe that Song Renzong was a sage ruler, yet even he hesitated over the heir in his later years. Ministers such as Fan Zhen and Bao Zheng remonstrated in urgent memorial after memorial until their hair turned white.
entries.literal: Shan tore paper on the palace gate steps, moistened ink with saliva, and memorialized: "Your servant has observed that Emperor Renzong of Song was an exemplary ruler of his age, yet in his later years he hesitated over establishing an heir; eminent ministers such as Fan Zhen and Bao Zheng all submitted urgent joint remonstrances until their hair turned white.

entries.zh: 臣愚，信書太篤，妄思效法古人，實未嘗妄嗾台臣共為此奏。」
entries.en: I am foolish and trusted the histories too much. I rashly hoped to follow the ancients. I did not incite the censors to join in this memorial."
entries.literal: Your servant is foolish and trusted the histories too deeply, rashly thinking to imitate the ancients; I truly did not rashly incite censors to make this memorial together."

entries.zh: 奏上，越五日，詔緩議罪，與諸御史俱赴西陲軍前效力。
entries.en: Five days later the emperor suspended punishment and ordered Shan and the censors to serve at the western frontier.
entries.literal: When the memorial was submitted, five days later an edict suspended deliberation on punishment; he and the censors were all sent to serve at the western frontier army.

entries.zh: 因掞年老，責其子奕清代往，為父贖罪。
entries.en: Because Shan was elderly, his son Yiqing was sent in his stead to atone for him.
entries.literal: Because Shan was old, his son Yiqing was ordered to go in his place to redeem his father's offense.

entries.zh: 先是，掞嘗密奏請減蘇、松浮糧，言至剴切，疏久留中。
entries.en: Earlier he had secretly asked to cut the excess grain levies in Suzhou and Songjiang. His plea was earnest, but the memorial had long been held back.
entries.literal: Earlier, Shan had secretly memorialized to reduce the excess grain levies of Suzhou and Songjiang; his words were most earnest, but the memorial long remained withheld.

entries.zh: 至是忤旨，乃與建儲奏疏一併擲還。
entries.en: Now, having offended the throne, both that memorial and the heir memorial were returned together.
entries.literal: Now, having offended the imperial will, both that and the heir-establishment memorial were thrown back together.

entries.zh: 是年冬，上自熱河還京師。
entries.en: That winter the emperor returned from Rehe to Beijing.
entries.literal: That winter the emperor returned from Rehe to the capital.

entries.zh: 掞迎駕石槽，上望見，遣內侍慰問。
entries.en: Shan met the procession at Shicao. The emperor saw him from afar and sent a eunuch with words of comfort.
entries.literal: Shan met the imperial procession at Shicao; the emperor saw him from afar and sent a eunuch to console him.

entries.zh: 六十一年元旦，諸大臣表賀，未列掞名，上發表命列名以進。
entries.en: On New Year's Day of 1722 the ministers' congratulatory memorial omitted Shan's name. The emperor returned it and ordered his name added.
entries.literal: On New Year's Day of the sixty-first year the ministers presented congratulatory memorials without listing Shan's name; the emperor returned the memorial and ordered his name included before resubmission.

entries.zh: 翌日，賜宴太和殿，再召見西暖閣，賜坐，慰諭有加。
entries.en: The next day he was feasted in the Hall of Supreme Harmony, summoned again to the West Warm Pavilion, given a seat, and warmly reassured.
entries.literal: The next day he was granted a banquet in the Hall of Supreme Harmony, summoned again to the West Warm Pavilion, given a seat, and comforted with added kindness.

entries.zh: 尋起原官，視事如故。
entries.en: He was soon restored to his former post and resumed duty as before.
entries.literal: Soon he was restored to his former office and administered affairs as before.

entries.zh: 雍正元年，以老乞休，世宗降旨褒嘉，以原官致仕，仍留京師備顧問。
entries.en: In 1723 he asked to retire on account of age. The Yongzheng Emperor praised him in an edict, let him retire at his former rank, and kept him in Beijing as an adviser.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng, citing age he requested retirement; the Shizong Emperor issued an edict of praise, allowed him to retire with his former rank, and kept him in the capital for consultation.

entries.zh: 三年，上諭閣臣云：「王掞向人言，曾在聖祖前奏免蘇、松浮糧，未蒙允行。
entries.en: In 1725 the emperor told the Grand Secretariat: "Wang Shan has told others that he once asked the late emperor to cut the excess grain levies in Suzhou and Songjiang, but was not granted his request.
entries.literal: In the third year the emperor told the Grand Secretariat: "Wang Shan has told others that he once memorialized before the late emperor to exempt Suzhou and Songjiang excess grain levies, but it was not granted.

entries.zh: 朕查閱宮中並無此奏。」
entries.en: I have searched the palace archives and found no such memorial."
entries.literal: I have searched the palace archives and there is no such memorial."

entries.zh: 因責掞藉事沽名，並涉其子奕清、奕鴻諂附年羹堯，目為奸巧，乃遣奕鴻與奕清同在軍前效力。
entries.en: He rebuked Shan for using the matter to seek fame and accused his sons Yiqing and Yihong of currying favor with Nian Gengyao, calling them deceitful. He sent both sons to serve at the front.
entries.literal: He therefore rebuked Shan for trading on events to seek reputation, and implicated his sons Yiqing and Yihong in fawning on Nian Gengyao, calling them crafty; he then sent Yihong and Yiqing alike to serve at the army front.

entries.zh: 六年，掞卒，年八十四。
entries.en: In 1728 he died at the age of eighty-four.
entries.literal: In the sixth year Shan died, aged eighty-four.

entries.zh: 乾隆二年，奕清始請䘏於朝，賜祭葬如製。
entries.en: In 1737 Yiqing first petitioned for posthumous honors at court, and state sacrifices and burial were granted by regulation.
entries.literal: In the second year of Qianlong, Yiqing first petitioned the court for posthumous honors; imperial sacrifices and burial were granted according to regulation.

entries.zh: 論曰：理密親王在儲位久，未聞顯有失德，而終遭廢黜，聖祖手詔，若有深痛鉅慝至不可言者。
entries.en: The commentator says: Prince Limi long held the heir's place and no marked misconduct was heard of, yet he was deposed in the end. The Kangxi Emperor's own edict seems to hold a grief at some great evil beyond words.
entries.literal: The commentator says: Prince Limi long held the heir's position and no marked misconduct was heard of, yet in the end he suffered deposition; the sage ancestor's own edict seems to hold deep pain at a great evil beyond words.

entries.zh: 夫以聖祖之仁明，而不克全監撫之重，終父子之恩，讒人罔極，靡所不至，甚矣！
entries.en: That the Kangxi Emperor, so benevolent and clear-sighted, could not fully fulfill the duty of overseeing and instructing the heir, nor bring father and son to reconciliation—slanderers reached everywhere without limit. How extreme it was!
entries.literal: That one so benevolent and clear-sighted as the sage ancestor could not fully fulfill the weight of overseeing and instructing, nor bring father-son affection to its end—slanderers without limit reaching everywhere—is extreme indeed!

entries.zh: 掞力主復故，聖祖雖深罪之，固諒其無他心。
entries.en: Shan strongly urged restoring the former heir. Though the Kangxi Emperor punished him severely, he surely understood Shan had no other intent.
entries.literal: Shan strongly urged restoration of the former heir; though the sage ancestor punished him deeply, he surely understood he had no other intent.

entries.zh: 勞之辨諫於初廢，大臣拜杖，已非故事；
entries.en: Lao Zhibian remonstrated at the first deposition. Beating great ministers with the rod was already not precedent.
entries.literal: Lao Zhibian remonstrated at the first deposition; great ministers beaten with the rod was already not precedent;

entries.zh: 硃天保爭於再黜，遂以誅死，罪及其親。
entries.en: Zhu Tianbao contended at the second dismissal and was executed, guilt reaching his kin.
entries.literal: Zhu Tianbao contended at the second dismissal and was then put to death by execution, guilt reaching his kin.

entries.zh: 一則但責其沽名，一則深疑其受指，故譴有重輕歟？
entries.en: In one case he was only rebuked for seeking reputation; in the other deeply suspected of acting on others' orders. Was that why the punishments differed in severity?
entries.literal: In one case he was only rebuked for seeking reputation; in the other deeply suspected of taking direction—thus were the punishments light and heavy?

entries.zh: 彝等但坐謫戍，已為寬典，拳拳效忠，固人臣之義也。
entries.en: Yi and the others received only banishment to frontier service, already a lenient measure. Earnest loyalty is indeed a subject's duty.
entries.literal: Yi and the others received only banishment to frontier garrison, already a lenient measure; earnest loyalty is indeed the duty of a subject.

entries.zh: 時上春秋高，皇太子允礽既廢，儲位未定。
entries.en: The emperor was then in advanced age. Crown Prince Yunreng had been deposed and the succession remained unsettled.
entries.literal: At that time the emperor was advanced in years; the Crown Prince Yunreng had already been deposed and the succession was unsettled.

entries.zh: 掞年七十馀，自念受恩深，又以其祖錫爵在明神宗朝，以建儲事受惡名，欲幹其蠱。
entries.en: Shan was over seventy. Mindful of the deep favor he had received, and that his grandfather Xijue had been vilified under the Ming Shenzong for pressing the heir question, he hoped to lift that family shadow.
entries.literal: Shan was over seventy; reflecting on the deep favor he had received, and that his grandfather Xijue had borne an ill name in the Ming under Shenzong for urging the establishment of an heir, he wished to dispel that curse.

entries.zh: 五十六年，密奏請建儲，疏入，留中。
entries.en: In 1717 he secretly memorialized to name an heir. The memorial was received but not acted upon.
entries.literal: In the fifty-sixth year he submitted a secret memorial requesting the establishment of an heir; the memorial was received but held back.

entries.zh: 是年冬，御史陳嘉猷等八人復以為言，上不悅，遂並發掞疏，命內閣議處。
entries.en: That winter Censor Chen Jiayou and seven others raised the issue again. Displeased, the emperor released Shan's memorial with theirs and ordered the Grand Secretariat to decide his punishment.
entries.literal: That winter Censor Chen Jiayou and seven others again spoke on the matter; the emperor was displeased, released Shan's memorial together with theirs, and ordered the Grand Secretariat to deliberate punishment.

entries.zh: 忌掞者欲置重典，掞止宮門外不敢入。
entries.en: His enemies sought a heavy sentence. Shan halted outside the palace gate and did not dare enter.
entries.literal: Those who resented Shan wished to impose severe penalties; Shan stopped outside the palace gate and dared not enter.

entries.zh: 上顧左右，問：「王掞何在？」
entries.en: The emperor looked about and asked, "Where is Wang Shan?"
entries.literal: The emperor looked to those beside him and asked: "Where is Wang Shan?"

entries.zh: ​​李光地奏掞待罪宮門。
entries.en: Li Guangdi reported that Shan was waiting outside the gate to accept punishment.
entries.literal: Li Guangdi reported that Shan was awaiting judgment at the palace gate.

entries.zh: 上曰：「王掞言甚是，但不宜令御史同奏，蹈明季惡習。
entries.en: The emperor said, "Wang Shan is quite right, but he should not have had censors join him in memorializing. That revives a vicious late-Ming habit.
entries.literal: The emperor said: "Wang Shan's words are very much to the point, but he should not have had censors submit together with him, reviving the evil custom of late Ming.

entries.zh: 汝等票擬處分太重，可速召其來。」
entries.en: Your proposed penalties are too harsh. Bring him in at once."
entries.literal: Your draft punishments are too severe; summon him at once."

entries.zh: 掞聞命趨入，免冠謝。
entries.en: Hearing this, Shan hurried in, removed his cap, and apologized.
entries.literal: On hearing the order Shan hurried in, removed his cap, and apologized.

entries.zh: 上招掞跪禦榻前，語良久，秘，人不能知。
entries.en: The emperor had him kneel before the couch and spoke with him at length in private. No one else learned what was said.
entries.literal: The emperor summoned Shan to kneel before the imperial couch and spoke with him at length in secret; no one could know what was said.

entries.zh: 六十年三月，彝與同官任坪、范長發、鄒圖雲、陳嘉猷、王允晉、李允符、範允、高玢、高怡、趙成麃、孫紹曾合疏奏曰：「皇上深恩厚德，浹洽人心。
entries.en: In the third month of 1721 Yi and his colleagues Ren Ping, Fan Changfa, Zou Tuyun, Chen Jiayou, Wang Yunjin, Li Yunfu, Fan Yun, Gao Bin, Gao Yi, Zhao Chengbiao, and Sun Shaozeng jointly memorialized: "Your Majesty's deep grace and great virtue fill the hearts of the people.
entries.literal: In the third month of the sixtieth year Yi and his colleagues Ren Ping, Fan Changfa, Zou Tuyun, Chen Jiayou, Wang Yunjin, Li Yunfu, Fan Yun, Gao Bin, Gao Yi, Zhao Chengbiao, and Sun Shaozeng jointly memorialized: "Your Majesty's deep grace and thick virtue saturate the hearts of the people.

entries.zh: 茲逢六十年，景運方新，普天率土，歡欣鼓舞，而建儲一事，尤為鉅典。
entries.en: We mark the sixtieth year, a renewed age of fortune, and all under Heaven rejoices. Yet establishing the heir is the greatest ritual of all.
entries.literal: Now we meet the sixtieth year; the auspicious fortune is newly renewed; all under Heaven within the four seas rejoice and exult; yet establishing the heir is especially a great ritual.

entries.zh: 懇獨斷宸衷，早定儲位。」
entries.en: We earnestly beg Your Majesty to decide in Your own heart and fix the succession soon."
entries.literal: We earnestly beg Your solitary decision from the imperial heart to fix the heir's place early."

entries.zh: 疏入，下內閣。
entries.en: When it was submitted it was sent to the Grand Secretariat.
entries.literal: When the memorial was submitted it was sent down to the Grand Secretariat.

entries.zh: 時大學士王掞正密疏請建儲。
entries.en: At that time Grand Secretary Wang Shan was secretly memorializing to name an heir.
entries.literal: At that time Grand Secretary Wang Shan was secretly memorializing to establish an heir.

entries.zh: 後數日，彝等疏又上，上震怒，斥掞植黨希榮。
entries.en: Several days later Yi's memorial was submitted again. The emperor was enraged and rebuked Shan for faction-building and ambition.
entries.literal: Several days later Yi's memorial was submitted again; the emperor was greatly angered and rebuked Shan for forming factions and seeking glory.

entries.zh: 於是王大臣奏請奪掞及諸御史官，從重治罪。
entries.en: The princes and senior ministers then asked to strip Shan and the censors of office and punish them severely.
entries.literal: Thereupon the princes and high ministers memorialized to strip Shan and the censors of office and punish them severely.

entries.zh: 越日，諭廷臣曰：「王掞及御史陶彝等妄行陳奏，俱稱為國為君。
entries.en: The next day he told the court: "Wang Shan and Censor Tao Yi and others rashly memorialized, all claiming to act for the state and the sovereign.
entries.literal: The next day he instructed the court: "Wang Shan and Censor Tao Yi and others rashly memorialized, all claiming to act for the state and the sovereign.

entries.zh: 今西陲用兵，為人臣者，正宜滅此朝食。
entries.en: War is now on the western frontier. As subjects they ought to swallow the enemy this very morning.
entries.literal: Now war is waged on the western frontier; as subjects they ought rather to swallow the enemy this very morning.

entries.zh: 可暫緩議罰，如八旗滿洲文官例，俱委署額外章京，遣往軍前效力贖罪。」
entries.en: Punishment may wait. Following the precedent for Manchu civil officials of the Eight Banners, appoint them acting extra clerks and send them to the front to serve and redeem their guilt."
entries.literal: Punishment may be suspended for the moment; following the precedent for Manchu civil officials of the Eight Banners, let them all be appointed acting extra clerks and sent to the army front to serve and redeem their guilt."

entries.zh: 雍正四年，世宗以諸御史不諳國體，心本無他，詔釋歸，以原職休致還籍。
entries.en: In 1726 the Yongzheng Emperor, judging that the censors did not understand statecraft but meant no harm, ordered them released to retire at their former ranks and return home.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Yongzheng the Shizong Emperor, considering that the censors did not understand statecraft but had no other intent at heart, ordered them released to retire at their former ranks and return home.

entries.zh: 嘉猷，字讱叔，江南溧陽人。
entries.en: Jiayou, whose style was Renshu, came from Liyang in Jiangnan.
entries.literal: Jiayou, style Renshu, was a native of Liyang in Jiangnan.

entries.zh: 康熙三十九年進士。
entries.en: In 1700 he became a metropolitan graduate.
entries.literal: Metropolitan graduate in the thirty-ninth year of Kangxi.

entries.zh: 自吏部員外郎考選山西道御史。
entries.en: From vice director in the Ministry of Personnel he was selected as censor of the Shanxi Circuit.
entries.literal: From vice director in the Ministry of Personnel he was selected by examination as censor of the Shanxi Circuit.

entries.zh: 五十六年，王掞密請建儲。
entries.en: In 1717 Wang Shan secretly memorialized to name an heir.
entries.literal: In the fifty-sixth year Wang Shan secretly memorialized to establish an heir.

entries.zh: 未幾，嘉猷與同官八人亦合疏陳請，上疑之，掞幾獲罪，事具掞傳。
entries.en: Soon after Jiayou and eight colleagues jointly memorialized as well. The emperor was suspicious and Shan nearly fell. The matter is told fully in Shan's biography.
entries.literal: Before long Jiayou and eight colleagues also jointly memorialized in request; the emperor was suspicious; Shan nearly incurred punishment—the matter is fully set forth in Shan's biography.

entries.zh: 至是，嘉猷復與彝等申請，獲咎。
entries.en: On this occasion Jiayou again joined Yi and others in petitioning and was punished.
entries.literal: On this occasion Jiayou again joined Yi and others in petitioning and incurred blame.

entries.zh: 列傳七十三
entries.en: Biographies 73
entries.literal: Biographies 73

entries.zh: 五十八年，卒，賜祭葬。
entries.en: In year 58 he died; imperial funeral rites were granted.
entries.literal: In the fifty-eighth year he died; funeral sacrifices were granted.

entries.zh: 雍正元年，贈太傅，諡端純。
entries.en: In the first year of Yongzheng he was posthumously made Grand Tutor with the posthumous title Duanchun.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng he was posthumously made Grand Tutor, with the posthumous title Duanchun.

entries.zh: 世宗手書「仁孝勤恪」榜，命表於墓道。
entries.en: Emperor Shizong personally wrote the tablet 'Benevolent, Filial, Diligent, and Earnest' and ordered it set up along the tomb road.
entries.literal: The Shizong Emperor personally wrote the tablet 'Benevolent, filial, diligent, and earnest' and ordered it displayed at the tomb road.

entries.zh: 子隆科多，自有傳。
entries.en: His son Longkedo has a separate biography.
entries.literal: His son Longkedo has his own biography.

entries.zh: 世宗即位，降敕褒諭，予一等阿達哈哈番，尋命襲其祖哈什屯一等阿思哈尼哈番，進二等伯，加太子太保。
entries.en: When Emperor Shizong took the throne, he issued a commendatory edict, granting a first-class ada hafan; Ma Qi was soon ordered to inherit his grandfather Hashutun's first-class ashan i hafan, was raised to second-class baron, and made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: When the Shizong Emperor ascended the throne, he issued an edict of praise and reward, granting a first-class ada hafan; he was soon ordered to inherit his grandfather Hashutun's first-class ashan i hafan, was advanced to a second-class baron, and made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 雍正元年，改保和殿，進太保。
entries.en: In the first year of Yongzheng he was moved to the Hall of Preserving Harmony and promoted Grand Tutor.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng he was moved to the Hall of Preserving Harmony and advanced to Grand Tutor.

entries.zh: 三年，复降詔褒其忠誠，加拜他喇布勒哈番，以其子富良襲。
entries.en: In year 3 another edict praised his loyalty; he was granted an additional tabun niru hafan, which his son Fuliang inherited.
entries.literal: In the third year an edict again praised his loyalty; he was granted an additional tabun niru hafan, which his son Fuliang inherited.

entries.zh: 十三年，引疾乞罷，許致仕。
entries.en: In year 13, pleading illness, he asked to retire and was allowed to leave office.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year, citing illness, he begged to retire and was permitted to leave office.

entries.zh: 乾隆四年，病篤，高宗諭謂馬齊歷相三朝，年逾大耋，舉朝大臣未有及者，命和親王及皇長子視疾。
entries.en: In Qianlong year 4, gravely ill, Emperor Gaozong said Ma Qi had served as chief minister through three reigns, was past great old age, and no court minister matched him; he ordered the Prince of He and the eldest imperial son to visit him.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Qianlong, gravely ill, the Gaozong Emperor instructed that Ma Qi had served as chief minister through three reigns, was past great old age, and no minister in the whole court matched him; he ordered the Prince of He and the eldest imperial son to visit him in his illness.

entries.zh: 尋卒，年八十八，贈太傅，諡文穆。
entries.en: He soon died at eighty-eight; he was posthumously made Grand Tutor with the posthumous title Wenmu.
entries.literal: He soon died at eighty-eight; he was posthumously made Grand Tutor with the posthumous title Wenmu.

entries.zh: 子富興，襲爵，坐事黜，以富良襲，進一等伯。
entries.en: His son Fuxing inherited the title but was dismissed for an offense; Fuliang inherited instead and was raised to first-class baron.
entries.literal: His son Fuxing inherited the title but was dismissed for an offense; Fuliang inherited instead and was advanced to first-class baron.

entries.zh: 十五年，加封號曰敦惠。
entries.en: In year 15 the additional style-name Dunhui was granted.
entries.literal: In the fifteenth year an additional style-name Dunhui was granted.

entries.zh: 子阿爾松阿，降襲二等公，擢領侍衛內大臣、刑部尚書。
entries.en: His son Ersong'a inherited at reduced rank as second-class duke and was promoted Chief Grand Minister of the Imperial Bodyguard and Minister of Punishments.
entries.literal: His son Ersong'a inherited at reduced rank as second-class duke and was promoted Chief Grand Minister of the Imperial Bodyguard and Minister of Punishments.

entries.zh: 雍正二年，世宗召諸大臣諭曰：「本朝大臣中，居心奸險，結黨營私，惟阿靈阿、揆敘為甚。
entries.en: In Yongzheng year 2 Emperor Shizong summoned the great ministers and said: 'Among this dynasty's ministers, none were more treacherous in heart or more given to faction and private gain than Aringa and Kui Xu.
entries.literal: In the second year of Yongzheng the Shizong Emperor summoned the great ministers and instructed: 'Among the great ministers of this dynasty, those most treacherous in heart and most given to faction and private gain are Aringa and Kui Xu.

entries.zh: 當年二阿哥之廢，斷自聖衷。
entries.en: When the Second Prince was deposed, the decision came solely from the Sacred Mind.
entries.literal: When the Second Prince was deposed in those years, the decision came solely from the Sacred Mind.

entries.zh: 豈因臣下蜚語遂行廢立？
entries.en: How could deposition and installation have followed mere slander from subjects?
entries.literal: How could deposition and installation have followed mere slander from subjects?

entries.zh: 乃阿靈阿、揆敘攘為己力，要結允禩等，造作無稽之言，轉相傳播，致皇考憤懣，莫可究詰。
entries.en: Yet Aringa and Kui Xu claimed the deed as their own merit, courted Yinshi and others, fabricated baseless talk, and spread it hand to hand until my late father was filled with anger beyond all inquiry.
entries.literal: Yet Aringa and Kui Xu claimed the deed as their own merit, courted Yinshi and others, fabricated baseless talk, and spread it from hand to hand, until my late father was filled with anger beyond all inquiry.

entries.zh: 阿靈阿子阿爾松阿柔奸狡猾，甚於其父。
entries.en: Aringa's son Ersong'a was soft, treacherous, and cunning — worse than his father.
entries.literal: Aringa's son Ersong'a was soft, treacherous, and cunning — more so than his father.

entries.zh: 令奪官，遣往奉天守其祖墓；
entries.en: He was stripped of office and sent to Fengtian to guard his grandfather's tomb;
entries.literal: He was ordered stripped of office and sent to Fengtian to guard his grandfather's tomb;

entries.zh: 並將阿靈阿墓碑改鐫'不臣不弟暴悍貪庸阿靈阿之墓'，以正其罪。」
entries.en: and Aringa's tombstone was re-cut to read 'Tomb of Aringa — disloyal subject, unfilial brother, violent, greedy, and base,' to rectify his crime.'
entries.literal: and Aringa's tombstone was re-cut to read 'Tomb of Aringa — disloyal subject, unfilial brother, violent, greedy, and base,' to rectify his crime.'

entries.zh: 四年，命誅阿爾松阿，妻子沒入官。
entries.en: In year 4 he ordered Ersong'a executed and his wife and children confiscated.
entries.literal: In the fourth year he ordered Ersong'a executed and his wife and children confiscated to the state.

entries.zh: 乾隆元年，以阿靈阿墓碑立祖塋前，墓已遷而碑尚存，命去之。
entries.en: In the first year of Qianlong, because Aringa's tombstone still stood before the ancestral grave though the tomb had been moved, the emperor ordered it removed.
entries.literal: In the first year of Qianlong, because Aringa's tombstone still stood before the ancestral grave though the tomb had been moved, he ordered it removed.

entries.zh: 妻子釋令歸旗。
entries.en: His wife and children were released and allowed to return to the banner.
entries.literal: The wife and children were released and allowed to return to the banner.

entries.zh: 雍正三年，諭曰：「鄂倫岱與阿靈阿皆黨於允禩。
entries.en: In Yongzheng year 3 he instructed: 'Olondai and Aringa both belonged to Yinshi's faction.
entries.literal: In the third year of Yongzheng he instructed: 'Olondai and Aringa both belonged to Yinshi's faction.

entries.zh: 當日允禩得罪，皇考時方駐蹕遙亭，命執允禩門下宦者刑訊，具言鄂倫岱等黨附狀。
entries.en: When Yinshi offended then, my late father was encamped at Yaoting and ordered Yinshi's household eunuchs tortured for interrogation; they fully reported Olondai and others' factional attachment.
entries.literal: When Yinshi offended in those days, my late father was then encamped at Yaoting and ordered Yinshi's household eunuchs taken and interrogated under torture; they fully reported how Olondai and others had attached themselves to him.

entries.zh: 鄂倫岱等色變，不敢置辯。
entries.en: Olondai and the others turned pale and dared not reply.
entries.literal: Olondai and the others changed color and dared not reply.

entries.zh: 四十九年春，皇考自霸州回鑾，途中責鄂倫岱等結黨，鄂倫岱悍然不顧。
entries.en: In the spring of year 49, as my late father returned from Bazhou, he reproached Olondai and others for faction on the road; Olondai was defiant and heedless.
entries.literal: In the spring of the forty-ninth year, as my late father returned from Bazhou, he reproached Olondai and others for forming a faction on the road; Olondai was defiant and heedless.

entries.zh: 又從幸熱河，皇考不豫，鄂倫岱日率乾清門侍衛較射遊戲。
entries.en: Again at Rehe, when my late father was unwell, Olondai daily led Qianqing Gate bodyguards in archery and games.
entries.literal: Again accompanying him to Rehe, when my late father was unwell, Olondai daily led the Qianqing Gate bodyguards in archery contests and games.

entries.zh: 皇考於行圍時數其罪，命侍衛鞭撻之。
entries.en: During the hunting encampment my late father repeatedly counted his crimes and ordered bodyguards to flog him.
entries.literal: During the hunting encampment my late father repeatedly counted his crimes and ordered bodyguards to flog him.

entries.zh: 鄂倫岱頑悍怨望，雖置極典，不足蔽辜。
entries.en: Olondai was stubborn, fierce, and resentful; even the extreme penalty would not cover his guilt.
entries.literal: Olondai was stubborn, fierce, and resentful; even the extreme penalty would not cover his guilt.

entries.zh: 朕念為皇祖妣、皇妣之戚，父又陣亡，不忍加誅。
entries.en: I reflect that he was kin to my imperial grandmother and mother, and his father died in battle — I could not bear to execute him.
entries.literal: I reflect that he was kin to my imperial grandmother and imperial mother, and his father fell in battle — I could not bear to execute him.

entries.zh: 令往奉天與阿爾松阿同居。」
entries.en: He was ordered to Fengtian to live with Ersong'a.'
entries.literal: He was ordered to go to Fengtian and live with Ersong'a.'

entries.zh: 四年，與阿爾松阿並誅，仍諭不籍其家，不沒其妻子。
entries.en: In year 4 he was executed with Ersong'a, yet an edict still said his household would not be registered and his wife and children would not be confiscated.
entries.literal: In the fourth year he was executed together with Ersong'a, yet an edict still said his household would not be registered and his wife and children would not be confiscated.

entries.zh: 馬武，馬齊弟。
entries.en: Ma Wu was Ma Qi's younger brother.
entries.literal: Ma Wu was Ma Qi's younger brother.

entries.zh: 初授侍衛，兼管佐領。
entries.en: He was first made a bodyguard and concurrently managed a company.
entries.literal: He was first appointed a bodyguard and concurrently managed a company.

entries.zh: 累擢鑲白旗漢軍副都統。
entries.en: He rose to Vice Commandant of the Bordered White Banner Chinese Brigade.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Vice Commandant of the Bordered White Banner Chinese Brigade.

entries.zh: 因馬齊得罪奪官。
entries.en: When Ma Qi fell from favor his office was stripped.
entries.literal: Because of Ma Qi's offense his office was stripped.

entries.zh: 旋起內務府總管，遷鑲白旗蒙古都統。
entries.en: He was soon restored as Superintendent of the Imperial Household and transferred to Commandant of the Bordered White Banner Mongol Brigade.
entries.literal: He was soon reinstated as Superintendent of the Imperial Household and transferred to Commandant of the Bordered White Banner Mongol Brigade.

entries.zh: 世宗即位，授領侍衛內大臣。
entries.en: When Emperor Shizong took the throne, he was appointed Chief Grand Minister of the Imperial Bodyguard.
entries.literal: When the Shizong Emperor ascended the throne, he was appointed Chief Grand Minister of the Imperial Bodyguard.

entries.zh: 雍正四年，卒，命視伯爵賜卹，授三等阿達哈哈番，賜祭葬，諡勤恪。
entries.en: In Yongzheng year 4 he died; he was granted baronial funeral rites, a third-class ada hafan, imperial funeral sacrifices, and the posthumous title Qinke.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Yongzheng he died; he was ordered funeral rites according to a baron's rank, granted a third-class ada hafan, granted funeral sacrifices, with the posthumous title Qinke.

entries.zh: 鄂倫岱，滿洲鑲黃旗人，佟國綱長子。
entries.en: Olondai, of the Manchu Bordered Yellow Banner, was Tong Guogang's eldest son.
entries.literal: Olondai was a man of the Manchu Bordered Yellow Banner and the eldest son of Tong Guogang.

entries.zh: 初任一等侍衛。
entries.en: He first served as first-class bodyguard.
entries.literal: He first served as a first-class bodyguard.

entries.zh: 出為廣州駐防副都統。
entries.en: He went out as Deputy Commandant of the Guangzhou Garrison.
entries.literal: He went out as Deputy Commandant of the Guangzhou Garrison.

entries.zh: 康熙二十九年，擢鑲黃旗漢軍都統，襲一等公。
entries.en: In Kangxi year 29 he was promoted Commandant of the Bordered Yellow Banner Chinese Brigade and inherited a first-class duke.
entries.literal: In the twenty-ninth year of Kangxi he was promoted Commandant of the Bordered Yellow Banner Chinese Brigade and inherited a first-class duke.

entries.zh: 三十五年，上親征噶爾丹，鄂倫岱領漢軍兩旗火器營，出古北口。
entries.en: In year 35, when the emperor campaigned in person against Galdan, Olondai led the firearms battalion of the two Han Brigade Chinese banners and marched out by Gubeikou.
entries.literal: In the thirty-fifth year, when the emperor personally campaigned against Galdan, Olondai led the firearms battalion of the two Chinese banners of the Han Brigade and marched out by Gubeikou.

entries.zh: 扈蹕北巡塞外。
entries.en: He attended the emperor on the northern tour beyond the passes.
entries.literal: He attended the emperor on the northern tour beyond the passes.

entries.zh: 三十六年，擢領侍衛內大臣。
entries.en: In year 36 he was promoted Chief Grand Minister of the Imperial Bodyguard.
entries.literal: In the thirty-sixth year he was promoted Chief Grand Minister of the Imperial Bodyguard.

entries.zh: 坐事降一等侍衛。
entries.en: For an offense he was demoted to first-class bodyguard.
entries.literal: For an offense he was demoted to first-class bodyguard.

entries.zh: 尋授散秩大臣。
entries.en: He was soon appointed Minister without Specific Duty.
entries.literal: He was soon appointed Minister without Specific Duty.

entries.zh: 四十六年，复授領侍衛內大臣。
entries.en: In year 46 he was again appointed Chief Grand Minister of the Imperial Bodyguard.
entries.literal: In the forty-sixth year he was again appointed Chief Grand Minister of the Imperial Bodyguard.

entries.zh: 五十九年，命出邊管蒙古驛站。
entries.en: In year 59 he was ordered beyond the frontier to manage Mongol relay stations.
entries.literal: In the fifty-ninth year he was ordered beyond the frontier to manage Mongol relay stations.

entries.zh: 世宗立，召還，授正藍旗漢軍都統。
entries.en: When Emperor Shizong took the throne he was recalled and appointed Commandant of the Plain Blue Banner Chinese Brigade.
entries.literal: When the Shizong Emperor took the throne he was recalled and appointed Commandant of the Plain Blue Banner Chinese Brigade.

entries.zh: 論曰：理密親王既廢，自諸皇子允禟、允䄉輩及諸大臣多謀擁允禩，聖祖終不許。
entries.en: The commentary says: After Prince Limi was deposed, from Princes Yintang and Yin'e to the great ministers, many plotted to install Yinshi, but the Sacred Ancestor never permitted it.
entries.literal: The commentary says: After Prince Limi was deposed, from the princes Yinqi, Yin'e, and their like to the great ministers, many plotted to install Yinshi, but the Sacred Ancestor never permitted it.

entries.zh: 誠以儲位至重，非可以覬覦攘奪而致也。
entries.en: Truly the heirship weighs beyond measure; it cannot be won by covetous scheming and seizure.
entries.literal: Truly the heirship is weight beyond measure; it cannot be attained by covetous scheming and seizure.

entries.zh: 佟國維陳奏激切，意若不利於故皇太子，語不及允禩，而意有所在，馬齊遂示意諸大臣。
entries.en: Tong Guowei's memorial was fiercely worded, as though unfavorable to the former crown prince; he did not name Yinshi, yet his intent lay elsewhere, and Ma Qi then signaled the ministers.
entries.literal: Tong Guowei's memorial was fiercely worded, as though unfavorable to the former crown prince; his words did not name Yinshi, yet his intent lay elsewhere, and Ma Qi then signaled the great ministers.

entries.zh: 然二人者，皆非出本心，聖祖諒之，世宗亦諒之，故能恩禮勿替，賞延於後嗣。
entries.en: Yet neither acted from his true heart; the Sacred Ancestor understood, and Emperor Shizong understood as well, and so favor and ritual were never withdrawn, and rewards extended to their descendants.
entries.literal: Yet neither man acted from his true heart; the Sacred Ancestor understood this, and the Shizong Emperor understood it as well, and so favor and ritual were never withdrawn, and rewards extended to their descendants.

entries.zh: 若阿靈阿父子、揆敘、鄂倫岱、王鴻緒固擁允禩最力者，世宗既譴允禩，諸臣生者被重誅，死者蒙惡名，將安所逃罪？
entries.en: As for Aringa father and son, Kui Xu, Olondai, and Wang Hongxu — those who most forcefully backed Yinshi — once Emperor Shizong punished Yinshi, living ministers suffered heavy execution and the dead bore foul names; where could guilt escape?
entries.literal: As for Aringa father and son, Kui Xu, Olondai, and Wang Hongxu — those who most forcefully backed Yinshi — once the Shizong Emperor punished Yinshi, the living ministers suffered heavy execution and the dead bore foul names; where could guilt escape?

entries.zh: 鴻緒又坐與徐乾學等比，被論。
entries.en: Hongxu was also punished for being classed with Xu Qianxue and others.
entries.literal: Hongxu was also punished for being classed with Xu Qianxue and others.

entries.zh: 事別見，故不著於此篇。
entries.en: The affair is treated elsewhere and is therefore not given in this chapter.
entries.literal: The affair is treated elsewhere and is therefore not given in this chapter.

entries.zh: 列傳七十四
entries.en: Biography 74
entries.literal: Biographies 74

entries.zh: 徐元夢，字善長，舒穆祿氏，滿洲正白旗人。
entries.en: Xu Yuanmeng, whose style was Shanchang, was a Manchu of the Sumuru clan in the Plain White Banner.
entries.literal: Xu Yuanmeng, style name Shanchang, of the Sumuru clan, was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner.

entries.zh: 康熙十二年進士，改庶吉士，散館授戶部主事。
entries.en: He passed the palace examination in 1673, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and after completing his term there was appointed a principal secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.
entries.literal: A jinshi in the twelfth year of Kangxi, he became a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and upon leaving the academy was appointed a principal secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.

entries.zh: 二十二年，遷中允，充日講起居注官。
entries.en: In 1683 he was promoted to junior compiler and appointed diarist of the Daily Lecture.
entries.literal: In the twenty-second year he was transferred to junior compiler and served as diarist of the Daily Lecture.

entries.zh: 尋复遷侍講。
entries.en: He was soon promoted again to lecturer.
entries.literal: Soon after he was again promoted to lecturer.

entries.zh: 徐元夢以講學負聲譽，大學士明珠欲羅致之，其遷詞曹直講筵，明珠嘗薦於上。
entries.en: Xu Yuanmeng was renowned as a lecturer. Grand Secretary Mingzhu wished to recruit him, and when Xu was transferred to the secretariat and the lecture hall, Mingzhu once recommended him to the emperor.
entries.literal: Xu Yuanmeng had a reputation for lecturing on learning; Grand Secretary Mingzhu wished to recruit him. When he was transferred to the secretariat and attended the lecture hall, Mingzhu once recommended him to the throne.

entries.zh: 徐元夢以明珠方擅政，不一至其門，而掌院學士李光地亦好講學，賢徐元夢及侍講學士德格勒，亟稱於上前，二人者每於上前相推獎；
entries.en: Because Mingzhu then monopolized power, Xu never once called at his door. Chancellor Li Guangdi also loved scholarly lecturing and esteemed Xu Yuanmeng and Lecturer Degeli, repeatedly praising both before the emperor. The two men often commended each other in the emperor's presence;
entries.literal: Xu Yuanmeng, because Mingzhu was then monopolizing power, never once went to his door; but Chancellor Li Guangdi also loved lecturing, esteemed Xu Yuanmeng and Lecturer Degeli, and repeatedly praised them before the throne—the two men often commended each other before the throne;

entries.zh: 明珠黨蜚語謂與光地為黨。
entries.en: and Mingzhu's faction spread rumors that they were in league with Li Guangdi.
entries.literal: Mingzhu's faction spread rumors that they formed a clique with Guangdi.

entries.zh: 二十六年夏，上御乾清宮，召陳廷敬、湯斌、徐乾學、耿介、高士奇、孟亮揆、徐潮、徐嘉炎、熊賜瓚、勵杜訥及二人入試，題為理學真偽論。
entries.en: In the summer of 1687 the emperor held court in the Qianqing Palace and summoned Chen Tingjing, Tang Bin, Xu Qianxue, Geng Jie, Gao Shiqi, Meng Liangkui, Xu Chao, Xu Jiayan, Xiong Cixuan, Li Dunuo, and the two men to an examination on the theme "On the True and False in Neo-Confucian Learning."
entries.literal: In the summer of the twenty-sixth year the emperor held court in the Qianqing Palace, summoned Chen Tingjing, Tang Bin, Xu Qianxue, Geng Jie, Gao Shiqi, Meng Liangkui, Xu Chao, Xu Jiayan, Xiong Cixuan, Li Dunuo, and the two men to take an examination on the theme "On the True and False in Neo-Confucian Learning."

entries.zh: 方屬草，有旨詰二人，德格勒於文後申辯，徐元夢卷未竟。
entries.en: While they were still writing, an edict rebuked the two men. Degeli appended a defense to his essay; Xu Yuanmeng's paper was unfinished.
entries.literal: While they were drafting, an edict rebuked the two men; Degeli appended a defense after his essay, while Xu Yuanmeng's paper was unfinished.

entries.zh: 上閱畢，於德格勒及賜瓚有所譙讓，命同試者互校，斌仍稱徐元夢文為是。
entries.en: After reading the papers, the emperor reproached Degeli and Xiong Cixuan and ordered the candidates to cross-check one another's work. Tang Bin still declared Xu Yuanmeng's essay the best.
entries.literal: When the emperor had finished reading, he reproached Degeli and Cixuan, ordered those who had taken the examination to cross-check one another, and Bin still declared Xu Yuanmeng's essay correct.

entries.zh: 列傳七十六
entries.en: Biographies 76
entries.literal: Biographies 76

entries.zh: 旋授直隸總督。
entries.en: He was soon appointed governor-general of Zhili.
entries.literal: Soon after he was appointed governor-general of Zhili.

entries.zh: 四年，紱入覲。
entries.en: In the fourth year Fu came to court for audience.
entries.literal: In the fourth year Fu came to court for audience.

entries.zh: 初，左都御史蔡珽薦起其故吏知縣黃振國授河南信陽知州，忤巡撫田文鏡。
entries.en: Earlier, Left Censor-in-Chief Cai Ting had recommended his former subordinate Magistrate Huang Zhenguo for appointment as prefect of Xinyang in Henan, which offended Governor Tian Wenjing.
entries.literal: Earlier, Left Censor-in-Chief Cai Ting had recommended his former subordinate, Magistrate Huang Zhenguo, for appointment as prefect of Xinyang in Henan, offending Governor Tian Wenjing.

entries.zh: 文鏡馭吏嚴，尤惡科目，劾振國貪劣。
entries.en: Wenjing ruled his subordinates harshly and especially despised men who had risen through the civil service examinations; he impeached Zhenguo for corruption and misconduct.
entries.literal: Wenjing governed subordinates strictly and especially hated examination-degree holders; he impeached Zhenguo for greed and misconduct.

entries.zh: 紱過河南，詰文鏡胡為有意蹂踐士人。
entries.en: When Fu passed through Henan he confronted Wenjing, asking why he deliberately abused men of learning.
entries.literal: When Fu passed through Henan he questioned Wenjing: why deliberately trample upon scholars?

entries.zh: 入對，因極言文鏡貪虐，且謂文鏡所劾屬吏，如振國及邵言綸、汪諴皆枉，振國已死獄中。
entries.en: At audience he spoke at length of Wenjing's greed and cruelty, and said that subordinates Wenjing had impeached—among them Zhenguo, Shao Yanlun, and Wang Yan—had all been wronged, and that Zhenguo had already died in prison.
entries.literal: At audience he spoke at length of Wenjing's greed and cruelty, and said that subordinates Wenjing had impeached, such as Zhenguo, Shao Yanlun, and Wang Yan, were all wronged, and Zhenguo had already died in prison.

entries.zh: 文鏡因紱語，先密疏聞，謂紱與振國同年袒護。
entries.en: Because of Fu's remarks, Wenjing sent a secret memorial first, claiming that Fu and Zhenguo were examination cohort-mates and that Fu was shielding him.
entries.literal: Because of Fu's words, Wenjing first sent a secret memorial, saying Fu and Zhenguo were examination cohort-mates and Fu was showing favoritism.

entries.zh: 紱疏辨，上不直紱，而振國實未死，逮至京師，上更謂紱妄語。
entries.en: Fu memorialized in his own defense, but the emperor did not take his side. Zhenguo had in fact not died; when he was brought to the capital, the emperor concluded that Fu had lied.
entries.literal: Fu memorialized in defense; the emperor did not side with Fu. Zhenguo had in fact not died; when he was brought to the capital, the emperor further said Fu had spoken falsely.

entries.zh: 良輔奏雲南、廣西所屬土司與貴州接壤者，皆改歸貴州安籠鎮節制，命紱往與雲貴總督高其倬會勘，疏請循舊制，從之。
entries.en: Liangfu had memorialized that native chieftains under Yunnan and Guangxi bordering Guizhou should all be placed under the Anlong garrison of Guizhou. The emperor ordered Fu to go and conduct a joint survey with Yunnan-Guizhou Governor-General Gao Qizhuo. Fu memorialized asking to follow the old arrangements, and his request was approved.
entries.literal: Liangfu memorialized that native chieftains subordinate to Yunnan and Guangxi bordering Guizhou should all be placed under the control of Guizhou's Anlong garrison; the emperor ordered Fu to go and jointly survey with Yunnan-Guizhou Governor-General Gao Qizhuo. Fu memorialized requesting to follow the old system, and it was approved.

entries.zh: 文鏡劾屬吏黃振國、邵言綸、汪諴等，李紱訟言其枉，並謂河南諸吏張球最劣，文鏡縱弗糾。
entries.en: Wenjing had impeached subordinates Huang Zhenguo, Shao Yanlun, Wang Yan, and others. Li Fu argued they had been wronged and also said that among Henan officials Zhang Qiu was the worst, yet Wenjing indulged him and did not impeach him.
entries.literal: Wenjing impeached subordinates Huang Zhenguo, Shao Yanlun, Wang Yan, and others. Li Fu argued they were wronged and also said among Henan officials Zhang Qiu was the worst, yet Wenjing indulged him and did not impeach.

entries.zh: 入對，具為上言之。
entries.en: At audience he fully stated this to the emperor.
entries.literal: At audience he fully stated this to the emperor.

entries.zh: 上先入文鏡言，不直紱，而濟世罪狀文鏡又及枉振國、言綸、諴庇球諸事。
entries.en: The emperor had first accepted Wenjing's account and did not side with Fu, yet Jishi's charges against Wenjing again cited the wrongful cases of Zhenguo, Yanlun, and Yan and Wenjing's shielding of Qiu.
entries.literal: The emperor had first accepted Wenjing's words and did not side with Fu, yet Jishi's charges against Wenjing again cited the wrongful cases of Zhenguo, Yanlun, and Yan and shielding Qiu.

entries.zh: 上召大學士、九卿、科道等入見，舉前事，謂：「濟世言與紱奏一一吻合，今詰濟世劾文鏡諸事，濟世皆茫無憑據，俯首無詞，是其受人指使，情弊顯見。」
entries.en: The emperor summoned the grand secretaries, Nine Chief Ministers, censors, and others for audience, cited the prior matters, and said, "Jishi's words match Fu's memorials point for point. Now when Jishi is questioned on his impeachment of Wenjing, he has no basis for any of it and bows his head without a word—clearly he was directed by others; the circumstances are obvious."
entries.literal: The emperor summoned grand secretaries, Nine Chief Ministers, censors, and others for audience, cited the prior matters, and said: 'Jishi's words match Fu's memorials one by one. Now when Jishi is questioned on his impeachment of Wenjing, he has no basis for any of it and bows his head without words—clearly he was directed by others; the circumstances are obvious.'

entries.zh: 命奪濟世官，往阿爾泰軍前效力贖罪。
entries.en: He ordered Jishi stripped of office and sent to serve before the army in Altai to redeem his crime.
entries.literal: He ordered Jishi stripped of office and sent to serve before the army in Altai to redeem his crime.

entries.zh: 濟世至軍，大將軍平郡王福彭頗敬禮之，濟世講學著書不稍輟。
entries.en: When Jishi reached the army, Generalissimo Fupeng, Prince of Ping, treated him with considerable respect, and Jishi continued lecturing and writing without pause.
entries.literal: When Jishi reached the army, Generalissimo Fupeng, Prince of Ping, treated him with considerable respect; Jishi lectured on learning and wrote books without the slightest pause.

entries.zh: 七年，振武將軍順承郡王錫保以濟世撰古本大學注毀謗程、硃，疏劾，請治罪。
entries.en: In the seventh year, Pacifying Martial General Xibao, Prince of Shuncheng, citing Jishi's commentary on the ancient text of the Great Learning as slandering Cheng Yi and Zhu Xi, memorialized in impeachment and requested punishment.
entries.literal: In the seventh year, Pacifying Martial General Xibao, Prince of Shuncheng, cited Jishi's commentary on the ancient text of the Great Learning as slandering Cheng Yi and Zhu Xi, memorialized in impeachment, and requested punishment.

entries.zh: 上摘「見賢而不能舉」兩節注，有「拒諫飾非，拂人之性」語，責濟世怨望謗訕，下九卿、翰詹、科道議罪。
entries.en: The emperor excerpted the commentary on the two passages "seeing the worthy and not being able to advance him," which contained the words "rejecting remonstrance, covering faults, going against human nature," and charged Jishi with resentment and slander. The case was referred to the Nine Chief Ministers, Hanlin academicians, and censors for deliberation on punishment.
entries.literal: The emperor excerpted the commentary on the two passages 'seeing the worthy and not being able to advance him,' which contained the words 'rejecting remonstrance, covering faults, going against human nature,' and charged Jishi with resentment and slander; the case was referred to Nine Chief Ministers, Hanlin and Hanlin bachelors, and censors for deliberation on punishment.

entries.zh: 有陸生棻者，自舉人選授江南吳縣知縣，引見，上有所詰問，不能對，改授工部主事。
entries.en: There was a man named Lu Shengfen who, selected from among provincial graduates, was appointed magistrate of Wuxian in Jiangnan. At audience the emperor questioned him and he could not answer; he was reassigned as principal clerk in the Ministry of Works.
entries.literal: There was one Lu Shengfen who, selected from provincial graduate, was appointed magistrate of Wuxian in Jiangnan. At audience the emperor questioned him and he could not answer; he was reassigned as principal clerk in the Ministry of Works.

entries.zh: 復引見，上見其傲慢，以其廣西人，疑與濟世為黨，命奪官發軍前，令與濟世同效力。
entries.en: At a second audience the emperor found him arrogant. Because he was from Guangxi, the emperor suspected he was in league with Jishi and ordered him stripped of office and sent to the army to serve together with Jishi.
entries.literal: At a second audience the emperor saw he was arrogant; because he was a Guangxi man, he suspected he was in league with Jishi and ordered him stripped of office and sent to the army, commanded to serve together with Jishi.

entries.zh: 生棻撰通鑑論十七篇，錫保以為非議時政，別疏論劾。
entries.en: Shengfen composed seventeen essays on the Comprehensive Mirror. Xibao deemed them criticism of current policy and separately memorialized in impeachment.
entries.literal: Shengfen composed seventeen essays on the Comprehensive Mirror; Xibao deemed them criticizing current policy and separately memorialized in impeachment.

entries.zh: 上並下九卿、翰詹、科道議罪，尋議濟世詆訕怨望，怙惡不悛，生棻憤懣猖狂，悖逆恣肆，皆於軍前正法。
entries.en: The emperor referred both cases to the Nine Chief Ministers, Hanlin academicians, and censors for deliberation. Soon it was decided that Jishi had slandered and harbored resentment without reform, and that Shengfen was resentful, reckless, rebellious, and unrestrained—all were to be executed before the army according to law.
entries.literal: The emperor referred both to Nine Chief Ministers, Hanlin and Hanlin bachelors, and censors for deliberation on punishment. Soon it was deliberated that Jishi had slandered and harbored resentment without reform, and Shengfen was resentful, reckless, rebellious, and unrestrained—all to be executed before the army according to law.

entries.zh: 上密諭錫保誅生棻，縛濟世使視，生棻既就刑，宣旨釋之。
entries.en: The emperor secretly instructed Xibao to execute Shengfen, bound Jishi and made him watch, and after Shengfen had been executed proclaimed an edict releasing Jishi.
entries.literal: The emperor secretly instructed Xibao to execute Shengfen, bound Jishi and made him watch; after Shengfen had been executed, he proclaimed an edict releasing Jishi.

entries.zh: 謝濟世，字石霖，廣西全州人。
entries.en: Xie Jishi, whose style name was Shilin, came from Quanzhou in Guangxi.
entries.literal: Xie Jishi, styled Shilin, was a native of Quanzhou in Guangxi.

entries.zh: 康熙四十七年，舉鄉試第一。
entries.en: In the forty-seventh year of the Kangxi reign he placed first in the provincial examination.
entries.literal: In the forty-seventh year of Kangxi he placed first in the provincial examination.

entries.zh: 五十一年，成進士，改庶吉士，授檢討。
entries.en: In the fifty-first year he passed the jinshi examination, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and was appointed a reviser.
entries.literal: In the fifty-first year he became a jinshi, was made a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and appointed reviser.

entries.zh: 雍正四年，考選浙江道御史。
entries.en: In the fourth year of the Yongzheng reign he was selected by examination as censor of the Zhejiang circuit.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Yongzheng he was selected by examination as censor of the Zhejiang circuit.

entries.zh: 未浹旬，疏劾河南巡撫田文鏡營私負國，貪虐不法，列舉十罪。
entries.en: Before ten days had passed he memorialized impeaching Henan Governor Tian Wenjing for pursuing private interest against the state, for greed, cruelty, and lawlessness, listing ten crimes.
entries.literal: Before ten days had passed he memorialized in impeachment that Henan Governor Tian Wenjing pursued private interest against the state, was greedy, cruel, and lawless, listing ten crimes.

entries.zh: 上方倚文鏡，意不懌，命還濟世奏，濟世堅持不可。
entries.en: The emperor was then relying on Wenjing and was displeased. He ordered Jishi to withdraw his memorial, but Jishi firmly refused.
entries.literal: The emperor was then relying on Wenjing and was displeased; he ordered Jishi to withdraw his memorial, but Jishi firmly refused.

entries.zh: 上諭曰：「文鏡秉公持正，實心治事，為督撫中所罕見者，貪贓壞法，朕保其必無，而濟世於督撫中獨劾文鏡，朕不知其何心？
entries.en: The emperor said, "Wenjing upholds justice impartially and governs with a sincere heart—rare among governors. As for greed and corruption, I guarantee he has none. Yet among all governors Jishi impeaches Wenjing alone—what can his intent be?
entries.literal: The emperor instructed: 'Wenjing upholds justice impartially and governs affairs with sincere heart—rare among governors. Greed and corruption violating law, I guarantee he certainly has none. Yet Jishi among all governors impeaches Wenjing alone—I do not know his intent?

entries.zh: 朕訓誡科道至再至三，誠以科道無私，方能彈劾人之有私者。
entries.en: I have admonished the censorate again and again, for only when censors are without private interest can they impeach those who act from private interest.
entries.literal: I have admonished the censorate again and again, truly because only when censors are without private interest can they impeach those with private interest.

entries.zh: 若自恃為言官，聽人指使，顛倒是非，擾亂國政，為國法所不容。
entries.en: If one relies on being a remonstrating official, listens to others' direction, inverts right and wrong, and disrupts state affairs, the law will not tolerate it.
entries.literal: If one relies on being a remonstrating official, listens to others' direction, inverts right and wrong, and disrupts state affairs, this is not tolerated by national law.

entries.zh: 朕豈不知誅戮諫官史書所戒？
entries.en: Do I not know that executing remonstrating officials is what histories warn against?
entries.literal: Do I not know that executing remonstrating officials is what histories warn against?

entries.zh: 然誅戮諫官之過小，釀成人心世道之害大。
entries.en: Yet the fault in executing a remonstrating official is small compared with the great harm done to public morale and the moral order of the age.
entries.literal: Yet the fault in executing remonstrating officials is small; the harm brewed to hearts and the age is great.

entries.zh: 禮義不愆，何卹於人言，朕豈卹此區區小節哉？」
entries.en: When ritual and righteousness are not violated, why should I worry about what people say? Would I shrink from this petty concern?"
entries.literal: When ritual and righteousness are not violated, why worry about people's words? Would I worry about this petty small matter?'

entries.zh: 奪濟世官，下大學士、九卿、科道會鞫，濟世辨甚力。
entries.en: Jishi was stripped of office, and the case was referred to the grand secretaries, Nine Chief Ministers, and censors for joint trial. Jishi argued vigorously.
entries.literal: Jishi was stripped of office; the case was referred to grand secretaries, Nine Chief Ministers, and censors for joint trial. Jishi argued vigorously.

entries.zh: 刑部尚書勵杜訥問：「指使何人？」
entries.en: Minister of Punishments Li Dun'e asked, "Who directed you?"
entries.literal: Minister of Punishments Li Dun'e asked: 'Who directed you?'

entries.zh: 對曰：「孔、孟。」
entries.en: He answered, "Confucius and Mencius."
entries.literal: He answered: 'Confucius and Mencius.'

entries.zh: 問：「何故？」
entries.en: Asked, "For what reason?"
entries.literal: Asked: 'For what reason?'

entries.zh: 曰：「讀孔、孟書，當忠諫。
entries.en: He said, "Reading the books of Confucius and Mencius, one ought to remonstrate loyally.
entries.literal: He said: 'Reading the books of Confucius and Mencius, one ought to remonstrate loyally.

entries.zh: 見姦弗擊，非忠也！」
entries.en: Seeing wickedness and not striking at it is not loyalty!"
entries.literal: Seeing wickedness and not striking at it is not loyalty!'

entries.zh: 讞上，以濟世所言風聞無據，顯係聽人指使，要結朋黨，擬斬。
entries.en: When the sentence was submitted, because Jishi's charges were hearsay without basis and he had clearly acted at others' direction and formed factions, execution was proposed.
entries.literal: When the sentence was submitted, because Jishi's words were hearsay without basis, clearly listening to others' direction and forming factions, execution was proposed.

entries.zh: 列傳八十
entries.en: Biographies 80
entries.literal: Biographies 80

entries.zh: 沈起元，字子大，江南太倉人。
entries.en: Shen Qiyuan, whose courtesy name was Zida, came from Taicang in Jiangnan.
entries.literal: Shen Qiyuan, courtesy name Zida, was a man of Taicang in Jiangnan.

entries.zh: 康熙六十年進士，選庶吉士，改吏部主事。
entries.en: He earned his jinshi degree in the sixtieth year of the Kangxi reign, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was then appointed principal clerk in the Ministry of Personnel.
entries.literal: In the sixtieth year of Kangxi he passed the jinshi examination, was chosen as a Hanlin bachelor, and was transferred to be a principal clerk in the Ministry of Personnel.

entries.zh: 擢員外郎，以知府發福建用。
entries.en: Promoted to vice department director, he was sent to Fujian to serve as a prefect.
entries.literal: He was promoted to vice department director and was dispatched to Fujian for appointment as prefect.

entries.zh: 總督高其倬令權福州，調興化。
entries.en: Governor Gao Qisuo placed him in charge of Fuzhou as acting prefect, then moved him to Xinghua.
entries.literal: Governor Gao Qisuo had him act as prefect of Fuzhou and transferred him to Xinghua.

entries.zh: 時世宗聞福建倉穀虧空，遣廣東巡撫楊文乾等往按，被劾者半，受代者爭為煩苛，起元獨持平。
entries.en: When the Yongzheng Emperor learned that Fujian's granary accounts showed large shortfalls, he sent Guangdong governor Yang Wenqian and others to investigate. Half of those investigated were impeached, and their successors competed to be harsh and troublesome—only Qiyuan remained fair and even-handed.
entries.literal: At that time the Yongzheng Emperor, hearing that Fujian's granary grain was in deficit, sent Guangdong Governor Yang Wenqian and others to investigate; half of those impeached [were found guilty], and those who succeeded them vied to be vexatious and harsh, but Qiyuan alone held to the middle course.

entries.zh: 莆田民因訟互鬥，其倬恐釀亂，令捕治。
entries.en: The people of Putian had come to blows over lawsuits, and Qisuo, fearing unrest, ordered them rounded up.
entries.literal: The people of Putian fought one another in the course of litigation, and Qisuo, fearing disorder, ordered arrests.

entries.zh: 起元責兩人而釋其餘，報曰：「罪在主者，餘不足問也。」
entries.en: Qiyuan punished the two ringleaders and released the others, reporting: "The offense rests with the leaders; the rest do not warrant inquiry."
entries.literal: Qiyuan held two responsible and released the rest, reporting: "The guilt lies with the principals; the rest need not be questioned."

entries.zh: 尋攝海關，裁陋規萬餘金。
entries.en: He was soon put in charge of the maritime customs and eliminated irregular levies amounting to more than ten thousand taels.
entries.literal: Soon he was placed in charge of the customs house and cut shabby fees by more than ten thousand taels.

entries.zh: 巡撫常安有奴在關，以索費困商舶。
entries.en: Governor Chang An kept a servant at the customs who extorted merchants and impeded their ships.
entries.literal: Governor Chang An had a slave at the customs who harassed merchant vessels by demanding fees.

entries.zh: 起元聞，立督收稅如額，令商舶行，白常安斥奴。
entries.en: On hearing this, Qiyuan at once enforced full tax collection, allowed the merchant fleet to sail, and reported to Chang An to have the servant expelled.
entries.literal: When Qiyuan heard of it, he immediately supervised tax collection to the full quota, let merchant vessels proceed, and informed Chang An to dismiss the slave.

entries.zh: 自是人皆奉法。
entries.en: After that, all conformed to the regulations.
entries.literal: From then on everyone obeyed the law.

entries.zh: 其倬奏開南洋，報可。
entries.en: Qisuo memorialized to reopen trade with the Southern Seas, and the court approved.
entries.literal: Qisuo memorialized to open the Southern Seas; approval was granted.

entries.zh: 已，復令商出洋者，必戚里具狀，限期返，逾者連坐。
entries.en: Before long, however, a new order required merchants sailing abroad to obtain affidavits from kinsmen, with fixed deadlines for return—those who missed the deadline would bring collective punishment on their families.
entries.literal: Soon afterward it was again ordered that merchants going to sea must have relatives provide bonds, with a fixed time limit for return; those who exceeded it would be punished by association.

entries.zh: 起元曰：「人之生死，貨之利鈍，皆無常，戚里豈能預料？
entries.en: Qiyuan objected: "Whether a man lives or dies, whether goods prosper or fail—all is unforeseeable. How can relatives predict such outcomes?
entries.literal: Qiyuan said: "Life and death of men, profit and loss of goods—all are uncertain; how can kinsmen anticipate them?

entries.zh: 且始不聽出洋則已，今聽之，商造船集貨費不貲，奈何忽撓以結狀？
entries.en: Besides, if going to sea were still forbidden, that would be one thing; but now that it is allowed, merchants have spent fortunes fitting out ships and assembling cargo—why suddenly burden them with bond requirements?
entries.literal: Moreover, if you will not allow going to sea, fine; but now that it is permitted, merchants spend untold sums building ships and gathering cargo—how can you suddenly trouble them with bonds?

entries.zh: 若令商自具狀，過三年不歸，勿聽回籍，不猶愈乎？」
entries.en: If merchants filed their own bonds, and those who failed to return within three years were barred from re-registering in their home districts, would that not serve better?"
entries.literal: If merchants themselves provide bonds, and if they do not return within three years they are not heard for household registration, would that not be better?"

entries.zh: 其倬從之。
entries.en: Qisuo adopted his proposal.
entries.literal: Qisuo followed his advice.

entries.zh: 七年，命往湖南讞獄，並巡察湖南、湖北兩省，裹糧出，有餽觴酒豆肉，皆卻之，令行禁止。
entries.en: In the seventh year he was ordered to Hunan to review criminal cases and to inspect both Hunan and Hubei. He traveled at his own expense; gifts of wine, beans, or meat were all refused, and he forbade such offerings outright.
entries.literal: In the seventh year he was ordered to go to Hunan to adjudicate criminal cases, and also to inspect Hunan and Hubei provinces; he set out carrying his own rations; when gifts of wine, beans, and meat were offered, he refused them all and ordered a ban enforced.

entries.zh: 與巡撫趙申喬同按永順苗變獄，群情帖服，苗疆以安。
entries.en: Together with Grand Coordinator Zhao Shenqiao he investigated the Yongshun Miao uprising; the public submitted, and the Miao frontier was pacified.
entries.literal: Together with Grand Coordinator Zhao Shenqiao he jointly investigated the Yongshun Miao rebellion case; popular sentiment submitted in compliance, and the Miao frontier was thereby pacified.

entries.zh: 湖南捕役多通盜，奏請捕役為盜，加重治罪，報可，入新例。
entries.en: Many Hunan constables colluded with bandits. He memorialized that constables who turned bandit should face heavier penalties; the request was approved and entered the new code.
entries.literal: In Hunan many arrest officers colluded with bandits; he memorialized requesting that arrest officers who acted as bandits receive heavier punishment; approval was granted, and it entered the new statutes.

entries.zh: 八年，擢通政司參議。
entries.en: In the eighth year he was promoted to counselor in the Office of Transmission.
entries.literal: In the eighth year he was promoted to counselor of the Office of Transmission.

entries.zh: 九年，擢鴻臚寺卿。
entries.en: In the ninth year he was promoted to director of the Court of State Ceremonial.
entries.literal: In the ninth year he was promoted to director of the Court of State Ceremonial.

entries.zh: 尋命以本銜署河南按察使，旋授湖北按察使。
entries.en: He was soon ordered to serve as acting judicial commissioner of Henan at his present rank, then appointed judicial commissioner of Hubei.
entries.literal: Soon he was ordered, retaining his current rank, to act as Henan judicial commissioner; shortly after he was appointed Hubei judicial commissioner.

entries.zh: 繼祖在兩湖久，熟知吏民情偽。
entries.en: Having served long in the two Hu provinces, Jizu knew officials and commoners alike—their truths and their lies.
entries.literal: Jizu had long been in the two Hu provinces and thoroughly knew the truth and falsehood of officials' and people's situations.

entries.zh: 楚俗刁健，黠吏與姦豪通，伺官喜怒，訟益難治。
entries.en: Hubei folk were sharp and litigious; cunning clerks colluded with local bullies, watched every shift in an official's mood, and lawsuits grew harder to settle.
entries.literal: Chu custom was crafty and contentious; cunning clerks colluded with powerful scoundrels, watched officials' joys and anger, and lawsuits became ever harder to govern.

entries.zh: 繼祖閉諸胥於一室，不令與外通，訟風衰減。
entries.en: Jizu confined the yamen clerks to a single room, cut off from outsiders, and the litigious mania subsided.
entries.literal: Jizu shut all the minor clerks in one room, not allowing them to communicate with the outside, and the wind of litigation declined.

entries.zh: 雪監利女子冤獄，按鍾祥民變，皆為時所稱。
entries.en: He righted a wrongful conviction in Jianli involving a woman, investigated the popular disturbance at Zhongxiang, and both won contemporary praise.
entries.literal: He cleared the wrongful case of a woman in Jianli, investigated the popular uprising in Zhongxiang, and both were praised by contemporaries.

entries.zh: 世宗馭吏嚴，內外大僚凜凜，救過不暇。
