entries.en: The Yongzheng Emperor ruled his officials with an iron hand; high officers at court and in the provinces lived in awe, scrambling merely to cover their mistakes.
entries.literal: Emperor Shizong governed officials strictly; senior officials within and without were in awe, with no leisure to remedy their faults.

entries.zh: 繼祖一意展舒，所陳奏無不允。
entries.en: Jizu alone acted with confidence and ease; every proposal he submitted won approval.
entries.literal: Jizu in all matters acted freely and at ease; every memorial he submitted was granted.

entries.zh: 上欲大用之，出巡察，賜以摺匣，許奏事，曰：「朕於督撫賢者始賜摺匣，汝宜好為之！」
entries.en: The emperor intended to promote him further. Before he left on his inspection tour, he was granted a memorial case and permission to report directly to the throne. The emperor said, "I grant the memorial case only to governors and governors-general I deem worthy. Conduct yourself accordingly!"
entries.literal: The Emperor wished to employ him on a grand scale; as he went out on inspection tour, he was granted a memorial case and permitted to memorialize; he said: "I grant the memorial case only to worthy governors-general and governors—you should do well!"

entries.zh: 調江西，未之任，以疾乞歸。
entries.en: He was transferred to Jiangxi but never took up the post, pleading illness to return home.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Jiangxi, did not take up the post, and requested leave to return home on account of illness.

entries.zh: 病癒將出，遽卒。
entries.en: His illness had healed and he was preparing to depart when he died suddenly.
entries.literal: When his illness was cured and he was about to set out, he suddenly died.

entries.zh: 王葉滋，字槐青，江南華亭人。
entries.en: Wang Yezi, styled Huaiqing, came from Huating in Jiangnan.
entries.literal: Wang Yezi, courtesy name Huaiqing, was a native of Huating in Jiangnan.

entries.zh: 弱冠，補諸生。
entries.en: In his youth he became a licentiate.
entries.literal: In his youth he became a licentiate.

entries.zh: 浙江巡撫硃軾闢佐幕，器其才。
entries.en: Zhejiang Governor Zhu Shi recruited him to his staff and valued his talent.
entries.literal: Zhejiang Governor Zhu Shi opened a staff and valued his talent.

entries.zh: 雍正元年，重開明史館，軾薦之，引見稱旨，命入館纂修。
entries.en: In the first year of Yongzheng, when the Ming History Office reopened, Zhu Shi recommended him. He pleased the emperor at audience and was ordered to join the compilation staff.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng the Ming History Office was reopened; Shi recommended him; on audience he pleased the emperor and was ordered to enter the office to compile and edit.

entries.zh: 舉順天鄉試。
entries.en: He passed the Shuntian provincial examination.
entries.literal: He passed the Shuntian provincial examination.

entries.zh: 福敏督湖廣，世宗命葉滋往贊其幕。
entries.en: When Fu Min governed Huguang, the Shizong Emperor ordered Yezi to assist his staff.
entries.literal: Fu Min governed Huguang; the Shizong Emperor ordered Yezi to assist his staff.

entries.zh: 五年，應禮部試，甫畢，上召見，問湖廣吏治、民生利弊，奏對甚悉，趣馳傳還湖廣。
entries.en: In the fifth year he took the Ministry of Rites examination. As soon as it ended the emperor summoned him and asked about Huguang governance and the welfare of the people. His replies were thorough, and he was ordered to hurry back to Huguang by relay.
entries.literal: In the fifth year he took the Ministry of Rites examination; as soon as it ended the emperor summoned him and asked about Huguang official governance and the benefits and harms to people's livelihood; his replies were thorough, and he was urged to hurry back by relay to Huguang.

entries.zh: 榜發中式，未與殿試，賜二甲進士，即授常德知府。
entries.en: When the results were posted he had passed. Before the palace examination he was granted second-rank jinshi status and immediately appointed prefect of Changde.
entries.literal: When the results were posted he had passed; before taking the palace examination he was granted second-rank jinshi and immediately appointed prefect of Changde.

entries.zh: 常德例，知府至，行戶更新照，規費四千金，葉滋革其例。
entries.en: By Changde custom, when a new prefect arrived, brokerage houses paid four thousand taels to renew licenses. Yezi abolished this custom.
entries.literal: By Changde custom, when the prefect arrived, brokerage houses renewed licenses at a fee of four thousand taels; Yezi abolished this custom.

entries.zh: 境數被水災，請帑增築花貓新陂堤堰，豁被水荒田額糧，民德之。
entries.en: The district suffered repeated floods. He requested treasury funds to enlarge the Huamao and Xinpo dikes and exempted grain quotas on flooded wasteland. The people were grateful.
entries.literal: The district suffered repeated flood disasters; he requested treasury funds to enlarge the Huamao and Xinpo dikes and exempted grain quota on flooded wasteland; the people were grateful.

entries.zh: 辰州關木稅為利藪，時議移關常德，葉滋恐累民，拒之，請仍舊制。
entries.en: The Chenzhou Pass timber tax was a lucrative source of revenue. Some proposed moving the pass to Changde, but Yezi feared burdening the people, refused, and requested that the old system remain.
entries.literal: The Chenzhou Pass timber tax was a rich profit source; at the time there was discussion of moving the pass to Changde; Yezi feared burdening the people, refused, and requested the old system remain.

entries.zh: 行法不避豪貴，興學造士，薦舉優行諸生陳悌為武平知縣，貴金馬為上蔡知縣，劉樵為清平知縣，並為良吏。
entries.en: Enforcing the law without fear of the powerful, promoting learning and cultivating scholars, he recommended the excellent licentiate Chen Ti as magistrate of Wuping, Gui Jinma as magistrate of Shangcai, and Liu Qiao as magistrate of Qingping—all became capable officials.
entries.literal: Enforcing law without avoiding the powerful and noble, promoting learning and cultivating scholars, he recommended the excellent licentiate Chen Ti as magistrate of Wuping, Gui Jinma as magistrate of Shangcai, and Liu Qiao as magistrate of Qingping—all became good officials.

entries.zh: 何師儉，字桐叔，浙江山陰人。
entries.en: He Shijian, whose courtesy name was Tongshu, came from Shanyin in Zhejiang.
entries.literal: He Shijian, courtesy name Tongshu, was a man of Shanyin in Zhejiang.

entries.zh: 以納貲，於康熙六十年選授兵部員外郎。
entries.en: Having purchased his office, he was appointed vice department director in the Ministry of War in the sixtieth year of Kangxi.
entries.literal: By purchase of office, in the sixtieth year of Kangxi he was selected and appointed vice department director in the Ministry of War.

entries.zh: 奉職勤懇，常數月不出署。
entries.en: He served with tireless diligence, often remaining at his office for months on end.
entries.literal: He served his post diligently and often did not leave the yamen for months.

entries.zh: 雍正元年，遷廣西右江道僉事，部請留任一年，世宗命以升銜留任，賜人葠、貂皮。
entries.en: In Yongzheng 1 he was transferred to surveillance commissioner of the Guangxi Right River Circuit; when the ministry asked to retain him another year, the Yongzheng Emperor ordered him kept on with an elevated title and rewarded him with ginseng and sable fur.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng he was transferred to be surveillance commissioner of the Guangxi Right River Circuit; the ministry requested he remain one year; the Yongzheng Emperor ordered him retained with promoted rank and bestowed ginseng and sable fur.

entries.zh: 師儉以執法卻重賄，忤要人，因誣以避瘴故留部。
entries.en: Shijian had offended powerful figures by enforcing the law and refusing large bribes; they slandered him as having lingered at the capital to escape the southern miasma.
entries.literal: Shijian, in enforcing the law, refused heavy bribes and offended powerful men, who therefore slandered him as having stayed at the ministry to avoid miasma.

entries.zh: 侍郎李紱昌言曰：「今部曹不名一錢，才者尤勞瘁，苟得郡，爭趨之，況監司耶？」
entries.en: Vice Minister Li Fu spoke up plainly: "Ministry clerks today take not a single cash in bribes; the ablest work themselves to exhaustion—given a chance at a prefecture they would all scramble for it, let alone a provincial surveillance post."
entries.literal: Vice Minister Li Fu spoke forthrightly, saying: "Nowadays ministry clerks do not take a single cash; the able are especially worn with labor—if they could obtain a prefecture, they would all rush for it—how much more so for a surveillance or circuit post?"

entries.zh: 期滿，復請留，加按察司副使銜。
entries.en: When his term expired he was again retained, with the added title of vice judicial commissioner.
entries.literal: When his term expired, he was again requested to remain, with the added rank of vice judicial commissioner.

entries.zh: 司疏奏皆出其手，他司事難治者亦時委之。
entries.en: He drafted every memorial and report for his bureau, and difficult cases from other bureaus were often assigned to him as well.
entries.literal: All bureau memorials and reports came from his hand; difficult matters in other bureaus were also sometimes entrusted to him.

entries.zh: 高宗即位，起江西驛鹽道副使。
entries.en: When the Qianlong Emperor took the throne, Qiyuan was recalled as vice commissioner of the Jiangxi courier-and-salt circuit.
entries.literal: When the Gaozong Emperor acceded, [Qiyuan] was recalled as vice commissioner of the Jiangxi courier and salt circuit.

entries.zh: 乾隆二年，擢河南按察使。
entries.en: In Qianlong 2 he was promoted to judicial commissioner of Henan.
entries.literal: In the second year of Qianlong he was promoted to Henan judicial commissioner.

entries.zh: 會久雨，被災者四十餘縣，饑民四走，或議禁之。
entries.en: Prolonged rains had flooded more than forty counties, and starving refugees scattered in every direction—some officials proposed barring their movement.
entries.literal: There had been long rains; more than forty counties suffered disaster, and starving people fled in all directions; some proposed to forbid their movement.

entries.zh: 起元謂：「民飢且死，奈何止其他徙？」
entries.en: Qiyuan protested: "The people are starving to death—how can you block them from seeking refuge elsewhere?"
entries.literal: Qiyuan said: "The people are starving and near death—how can you stop them from fleeing elsewhere?"

entries.zh: 令安置未被水諸縣，給以糧，遂無出河南境者。
entries.en: He had them settled in counties untouched by flood and issued grain rations, so that none left the province.
entries.literal: He ordered them settled in counties not flooded, provided grain, and thus none left Henan.

entries.zh: 巡撫雅爾圖檄府縣修書院，以起元總其事，乃教群士省身克己之學。
entries.en: Governor Yartu directed local governments to restore academies and placed Qiyuan in overall charge; he instructed the scholars in the discipline of inward scrutiny and moral self-restraint.
entries.literal: Governor Yartu ordered prefectures and counties to repair academies and put Qiyuan in charge; he then taught the scholars the learning of self-examination and self-restraint.

entries.zh: 立章善坊，書孝子、悌弟、義夫、貞婦名，採訪事實，為章善錄版行，一時風動。
entries.en: He founded a Zhangshan workshop to inscribe the names of the filial, the fraternal, the righteous, and the chaste, collected verified cases, and published a Zhangshan Record—inspiring moral emulation throughout the region.
entries.literal: He established a Zhangshan workshop, inscribed the names of filial sons, dutiful younger brothers, righteous husbands, and chaste wives, gathered facts, printed the Zhangshan Record, and for a time custom was stirred.

entries.zh: 擢按察使，數平疑獄。
entries.en: Promoted to judicial commissioner, he repeatedly resolved doubtful criminal cases.
entries.literal: He was promoted to judicial commissioner and several times settled doubtful cases.

entries.zh: 吏有故入人罪者，必按如法，雖貴勢賢親不徇縱。
entries.en: When officials had framed innocent defendants, he always prosecuted them to the full extent of the law, showing no favor even to the powerful or well connected.
entries.literal: When officials had intentionally entered false charges against others, he always prosecuted according to law, not yielding even to the powerful, eminent, or kin.

entries.zh: 十三年，以目疾乞休。
entries.en: In the thirteenth year he retired citing eye trouble.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year he requested retirement on grounds of eye disease.

entries.zh: 高宗即位，赦詔至，時目已失明，令吏誦案牘，諦聽，得邀赦典者，立出之而後上陳。
entries.en: When the Qianlong Emperor took the throne, an amnesty arrived; though Shijian was by then completely blind, he had clerks read case files aloud and listened carefully—any prisoner eligible for amnesty he released immediately before reporting upward.
entries.literal: When the Gaozong Emperor acceded, an amnesty edict arrived; by then his eyes were already blind; he had clerks read case documents and listened intently; those who could claim amnesty he released at once and then reported upward.

entries.zh: 留兩月，畢其事始歸。
entries.en: He stayed two months until every case was settled, then returned home.
entries.literal: He remained two months, finished the business, and only then returned home.

entries.zh: 後卒於家，陝西祀名宦。
entries.en: He later died at home and was entered in Shaanxi's shrine of eminent officials.
entries.literal: Later he died at home; Shaanxi enshrined him among notable officials.

entries.zh: 甸歷官盡革陋規，為按察使，愍囚不能自衣食，取鹽商歲饋三之一以資給之。
entries.en: Throughout his career Dian abolished all irregular fees. As provincial judicial commissioner, pitying prisoners who could not feed or clothe themselves, he took one-third of the salt merchants' annual gifts to support them.
entries.literal: Throughout his offices Dian abolished all irregular fees; as provincial judicial commissioner, pitying prisoners unable to feed and clothe themselves, he took one-third of the salt merchants' annual gifts to support them.

entries.zh: 兼完囹圄，修學宮、書院，委有司出入註籍。
entries.en: He also repaired prisons, academies, and colleges, requiring local officials to keep registers of all income and expenditure.
entries.literal: He also repaired prisons, academies, and colleges, entrusting local officials to keep registers of income and expenditure.

entries.zh: 既去官，上命內閣學士繆沅清察山東鹽政諸弊，舉是劾甸，奪官，歸。
entries.en: After leaving office, the emperor ordered Grand Secretariat Academician Miao Yuan to investigate abuses in Shandong salt administration. Citing Dian's use of merchant gifts, Yuan impeached him, stripped his office, and Dian returned home.
entries.literal: After leaving office, the emperor ordered Grand Secretariat Academician Miao Yuan to investigate abuses in Shandong salt administration; citing this, he impeached Dian, stripped his office, and Dian returned home.

entries.zh: 甸用唐人詩語為人書楹帖，其人有怨家，訐於有司，以為怨望。
entries.en: Dian had written couplets for others using lines from Tang poetry. One recipient had an enemy who denounced the couplets to officials as expressions of resentment against the throne.
entries.literal: Dian used Tang-dynasty poetry lines to write couplets for others; one such person had an enemy who denounced him to officials as harboring resentment.

entries.zh: 有司以甸所書也，並下甸於獄。
entries.en: Because Dian had written the couplets, the officials imprisoned him as well.
entries.literal: The officials, because Dian had written them, also imprisoned Dian.

entries.zh: 事白，遽卒。
entries.en: When the matter was cleared, he suddenly died.
entries.literal: When the matter was cleared, he suddenly died.

entries.zh: 列傳八十七
entries.en: Biographies 87
entries.literal: Biographies eighty-seven.

entries.zh: 訥親，鈕祜祿氏，滿洲鑲黃旗人，額亦都曾孫。
entries.en: Neqin, of the Niohuru clan, was a Manchu bannerman of the Bordered Yellow Banner and a great-grandson of Eidu.
entries.literal: Neqin, of the Niohuru clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner, a great-grandson of Eidu.

entries.zh: 父尹德，附見其父遏必隆傳，訥親其次子。
entries.en: His father Yinde is discussed in the biography of Ebilun; Neqin was Yinde's second son.
entries.literal: His father Yinde is treated in the biography of his father Ebilun; Neqin was the second son.

entries.zh: 雍正五年，襲公爵，授散秩大臣。
entries.en: In 1727 he inherited the ducal title and was appointed a minister without portfolio.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Yongzheng he inherited the dukedom and was appointed minister at large.

entries.zh: 十年，授鑾儀使。
entries.en: In 1732 he was made director of the imperial equipage.
entries.literal: In the tenth year he was appointed director of the imperial equipage.

entries.zh: 十一年十二月，命在辦理軍機處行走。
entries.en: In late 1733 he was ordered to serve on the Grand Council.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month of the eleventh year he was ordered to serve in the Grand Council.

entries.zh: 十三年，世宗疾大漸，訥親預顧命。
entries.en: In 1735, as the Yongzheng Emperor lay gravely ill, Neqin was named to the regency council.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year, when the Shizong Emperor fell gravely ill, Neqin was named to the regency council.

entries.zh: 高宗即位，莊親王允祿、果親王允禮、鄂爾泰、張廷玉輔政，號「總理王大臣」。
entries.en: When the Qianlong Emperor took the throne, Prince Zhuang Yunlu, Prince Guo Yunli, Ortai, and Zhang Tingyu formed the regency styled the 'Chief Ministers in General Affairs.'
entries.literal: When the Gaozong ascended the throne, Prince Zhuang Yunlu, Prince Guo Yunli, Ortai, and Zhang Tingyu assisted in government under the title 'Chief Ministers in General Affairs.'

entries.zh: 授訥親鑲白旗滿洲都統、領侍衛內大臣，協辦總理事務。
entries.en: Neqin was made banner general of the Bordered White Banner Manchus and grand minister of the imperial bodyguard, assisting in general affairs.
entries.literal: Neqin was appointed Banner General of the Bordered White Banner Manchus and Grand Minister of the Imperial Bodyguard, and assisted in general affairs.

entries.zh: 十二月，敕獎訥親勤慎，因推孝昭仁皇后外家恩，進一等公。
entries.en: That December an edict praised Neqin's diligence; in recognition of Empress Xiaozhaoren's maternal kin, he was raised to duke of the first rank.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month an edict praised Neqin's diligence and caution; extending favor to the maternal kin of Empress Xiaozhaoren, he was promoted to duke of the first rank.

entries.zh: 乾隆元年，遷鑲黃旗滿洲都統。
entries.en: In 1736 he was transferred to banner general of the Bordered Yellow Banner Manchus.
entries.literal: In the first year of Qianlong he was transferred to Banner General of the Bordered Yellow Banner Manchus.

entries.zh: 二年，遷兵部尚書。
entries.en: In 1737 he was appointed minister of war.
entries.literal: In the second year he was transferred to Minister of War.

entries.zh: 十一月，莊親王等請罷總理事務，訥親授軍機大臣。
entries.en: In the eleventh month, after the Prince of Zhuang and others asked to abolish the general ministerial board, Neqin was made a grand councillor.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month, when the Prince of Zhuang and others requested abolition of the office of general ministerial affairs, Neqin was appointed Grand Councillor.

entries.zh: 敘勞，加拖沙喇哈番世職。
entries.en: For his services he received the hereditary rank of tušan gūsan hafan.
entries.literal: For meritorious service he was granted the hereditary rank of tušan gūsan hafan.

entries.zh: 三年二月，領戶部三庫。
entries.en: In February 1738 he assumed charge of the three treasuries of the Ministry of Revenue.
entries.literal: In the second month of the third year he took charge of the three treasuries of the Ministry of Revenue.

entries.zh: 九月，命協辦戶部。
entries.en: In September he was ordered to assist at the Ministry of Revenue.
entries.literal: In the ninth month he was ordered to assist in the Ministry of Revenue.

entries.zh: 直隸總督李衛劾總河硃藻詐欺貪虐，命訥親與尚書孫嘉淦勘讞，藻坐流。
entries.en: When Zhili governor Li Wei accused river director Zhu Zao of fraud and corruption, Neqin and Minister Sun Jiagan were sent to investigate; Zhu was sentenced to exile.
entries.literal: Zhili Governor Li Wei impeached Director-General of Rivers Zhu Zao for fraud, oppression, and corruption; Neqin was ordered with Minister Sun Jiagan to investigate and try the case; Zhu was sentenced to banishment.

entries.zh: 訥親因與嘉淦條上永定河南北岸建築閘壩諸事。
entries.en: Neqin and Jiagan also submitted a detailed memorial on sluices and dams along both banks of the Yongding River.
entries.literal: Neqin, together with Jiagan, memorialized item by item on building sluices and dams along the north and south banks of the Yongding River.

entries.zh: 十二月，遷吏部尚書。
entries.en: In December he was transferred to minister of personnel.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month he was transferred to Minister of Personnel.

entries.zh: 四年五月，加太子太保。
entries.en: In May 1739 he received the honorary title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year he was given the honorary title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 訥親貴戚勳舊，少侍禁近，受世宗知，以為可大用。
entries.en: A noble by birth and a minister of long standing merit, Neqin had served near the throne from youth and won Yongzheng's trust as a man fit for high office.
entries.literal: Neqin was a noble by birth and a meritorious minister; from youth he attended close to the throne and won the Shizong Emperor's trust, who regarded him as fit for great employment.

entries.zh: 迨高宗，恩眷尤厚。
entries.en: Under Qianlong his favor was especially deep.
entries.literal: Under the Gaozong, favor and grace were especially thick.

entries.zh: 訥親勤敏當上意，尤以廉介自敕，人不敢干以私。
entries.en: Diligent and attentive to the emperor's wishes, he above all held himself to strict integrity, and no one dared solicit him privately.
entries.literal: Neqin was diligent and alert in suiting the emperor's wishes, and above all restrained himself with integrity; no one dared approach him for private favors.

entries.zh: 其居第巨獒縛扉側，絕無車馬跡。
entries.en: At his house a huge mastiff was tied beside the gate, and no carriage or horse ever came to call.
entries.literal: At his residence a huge mastiff was tied beside the gate; there was never a trace of carriage or horse traffic.

entries.zh: 然以早貴，意氣驕溢，治事務刻深。
entries.en: Yet having risen early to high rank, he grew proud and overbearing, and in office he was relentlessly harsh.
entries.literal: Yet having risen to high rank early, his spirit was proud and overbearing, and in handling affairs he was invariably harsh and severe.

entries.zh: 左都御史劉統勳疏論訥親領事過多，任事過銳。
entries.en: Censor-in-chief Liu Tongxun memorialized that Neqin held too many posts and was too sharp in his handling of affairs.
entries.literal: Censor-in-Chief Liu Tongxun memorialized criticizing Neqin for holding too many posts and for being too sharp in discharge of duty.

entries.zh: 上諭曰：「訥親為尚書，模棱推諉，固所不可，但治事未當，亦所不免，朕時時戒毋自滿。
entries.en: The emperor replied: 'As minister, Neqin must not be evasive or shirking—but it is also inevitable that he sometimes mishandles affairs; I constantly warn him against self-satisfaction.
entries.literal: The emperor instructed: 'Neqin as Minister—evasive shirking is certainly not permissible, but it is also unavoidable that his handling of affairs is sometimes not right; I constantly warn him not to be self-satisfied.

entries.zh: 今見此奏，益當自勉。」
entries.en: Now that I see this memorial, he should strive all the more to improve.'
entries.literal: Now that I see this memorial, he should strive all the more to improve.'

entries.zh: 語詳統勳傳。
entries.en: The full exchange is recorded in Liu Tongxun's biography.
entries.literal: The full account is in Liu Tongxun's biography.

entries.zh: 九年正月，命訥親閱河南、江南、山東諸省營伍，並勘海塘、河工。
entries.en: In the first month of 1744 Neqin was ordered to inspect troops in Henan, Jiangnan, and Shandong and to survey sea walls and river works.
entries.literal: In the first month of the ninth year Neqin was ordered to inspect military colonies in Henan, Jiangnan, and Shandong, and also to survey the sea wall and river works.

entries.zh: 時直隸天津、河間二府方以災治賑，令順道先往察覈。
entries.en: Tianjin and Hejian in Zhili were then under famine relief, and he was told to go first by the way to inspect.
entries.literal: At that time the Tianjin and Hejian prefectures of Zhili were providing famine relief; he was ordered to go first by the way to inspect and verify.

entries.zh: 疏請展賑一月，從之。
entries.en: He memorialized to extend relief by one month, and the request was granted.
entries.literal: He memorialized to extend relief by one month; the request was granted.

entries.zh: 訥親使事既蕆，分疏上陳，其勘諸省營伍，言：「遍閱三省督撫、河漕、提鎮為標者十七，優絀互見。
entries.en: When his tour was finished, Neqin submitted separate memorials; on the troops of the three provinces he wrote: 'Having reviewed the standards set by the governors-general, governors, grain commissioners, and regional commanders—seventeen in all—merit and demerit were mixed.
entries.literal: When Neqin's mission was concluded, he submitted separate memorials; on inspecting the military colonies of the several provinces he said: 'Having read through the standards of the governors-general, governors, grain transport commissioners, and provincial commanders of the three provinces, merits and demerits were mixed.

entries.zh: 惟河南南陽、江南蘇松水師二鎮最劣。
entries.en: Only the Nanyang garrison in Henan and the Suzhou-Songjiang naval command in Jiangnan ranked worst.
entries.literal: Only the Nanyang garrison in Henan and the Suzhou-Songjiang naval garrison in Jiangnan were the worst.

entries.zh: 請下部覈賞罰。」
entries.en: He asked that the ministries verify rewards and punishments.'
entries.literal: Request that the ministry verify rewards and punishments.'

entries.zh: 其勘江、浙海塘，言：「舊日浙江潮自蜀山中小亹出入，近海寧為北大亹，近蕭山為南大亹，漲沙寬闊，為杭州、紹興二府保障。
entries.en: On the Jiangsu and Zhejiang sea walls he wrote: 'Formerly the Zhejiang tide passed through the Small Waist at Shushan; near Haining lay the Great Northern Waist and near Xiaoshan the Great Southern Waist, and the broad buildup of sand protected Hangzhou and Shaoxing.
entries.literal: On inspecting the sea walls of Jiangsu and Zhejiang he said: 'Formerly the Zhejiang tide entered and left by the Small Waist at Shushan; near Haining was the Great Northern Waist and near Xiaoshan the Great Southern Waist; the broad accretion of silt served as a safeguard for Hangzhou and Shaoxing prefectures.

entries.zh: 迨中小亹漸湮，潮趨蜀山北，震盪為患。
entries.en: After the Small Waist gradually silted shut, the tide shifted north of Shushan and surged destructively.
entries.literal: After the Small Waist gradually silted up, the tide turned north of Shushan and in its surge became a calamity.

entries.zh: 若濬中小亹故道，減大亹潮力，上下塘工悉可安堵；
entries.en: If the old channel of the Small Waist were dredged to weaken the Great Waists, upper and lower embankments could all be secured;
entries.literal: If the old course of the Small Waist were dredged to reduce the force of the Great Waists, the upper and lower embankment works could all be secured;

entries.zh: 即中小亹未可遽复，則當擇險要多為坦坡，木石戧壩，俾撇水積淤資以御潮。
entries.en: even if the Small Waist could not soon be restored, dangerous points should be faced with earthen slopes and timber-and-stone wing-dams so diverted water might deposit silt against the tide.
entries.literal: even if the Small Waist could not soon be restored, then dangerous points should be chosen and ramparts of earth, timber, and stone wing-dams built so that diverted water might deposit silt to help resist the tide.

entries.zh: 至諸處柴塘，停沙阻水，無煩議改石工。
entries.en: As for wattled embankments elsewhere, they hold sand and obstruct water—there is no need to convert them to stone.
entries.literal: As for the wattled embankments everywhere, they detain sand and obstruct water—there is no need to discuss converting them to stone works.

entries.zh: 入江南境，地平而潮緩，華亭舊塘堅緻，寶山新塘尺度參差，工作又不中程。
entries.en: In Jiangnan, where the land is flat and the tide slow, Huating's old dike was solid, but Baoshan's new dike varied in size and the workmanship fell short.
entries.literal: Entering Jiangnan territory, where the land is level and the tide slack, the old embankment at Huating was solid and tight; the new embankment at Baoshan varied in dimensions and the work also fell short of specification.

entries.zh: 金山、奉賢、南匯、上海皆土塘，距海稍遠，所司守護如法，當無他虞。」
entries.en: Jinshan, Fengxian, Nanhui, and Shanghai all have earthen dikes somewhat inland; if maintained properly, they should give no further trouble.'
entries.literal: Jinshan, Fengxian, Nanhui, and Shanghai are all earthen dikes, somewhat distant from the sea; if those in charge maintain them according to rule, there should be no other worry.'

entries.zh: 其勘洪澤湖，請濬鹽河俾通江，疏串場河俾達海，並停天然二壩、高堰下游二堤。
entries.en: On Hongze Lake he asked to dredge the Salt River to the Yangtze, clear the Chuan-chang Canal to the sea, and halt the two Tianran dams and the two dikes below Gaoyan.
entries.literal: On surveying Hongze Lake, he requested dredging the Salt River to connect with the Yangtze, clearing the Chuan-chang Canal to reach the sea, and halting the two dams at Tianran and the two dikes below Gaoyan.

entries.zh: 其勘南旺湖，請以湖中涸地貸貧民耕稼。
entries.en: On Nanwang Lake he proposed leasing dried lake bed to poor peasants for farming.
entries.literal: On surveying Nanwang Lake, he requested leasing dried land in the lake to poor peasants for cultivation.

entries.zh: 別疏言：「各直省政事，督撫下司道，司道下州縣，州縣官惟以簿書錢穀為事，戶口貧富、土地肥瘠、物產豐嗇、民情向背、風俗美惡、以及山川原隰、橋樑道路，皆漫置不省。
entries.en: In another memorial he said: 'In every province administration runs from governor-general and governor to circuit intendant and then to prefecture and county; magistrates busy themselves only with ledgers, cash, and grain. Household wealth and poverty, soil quality, local products, popular sentiment, customs, terrain, bridges, and roads—all are ignored.
entries.literal: In a separate memorial he said: 'In each province, local government descends from governor-general and governor to circuit intendant, and from intendant to prefecture and county; county magistrates concern themselves only with ledgers, cash, and grain. Household wealth and poverty, soil fertility, abundance of products, popular inclinations, customs good or bad, mountains and plains, bridges and roads—all are casually disregarded.

entries.zh: 官但有條教，民惟責納賦，浮文常多，實意殊少。
entries.en: Officials issue regulations; the people owe only taxes; paperwork abounds while real concern is slight.
entries.literal: Officials have only statutes and orders; the people are held only to paying tax; empty documents are many, real intent very little.

entries.zh: 請敕各直省督撫，令州縣官遍歷境內，何事當興舉，何事當整飭，行之有無治效，以實報長官，長官即是為殿最，以實達朝廷。
entries.en: He asked that governors-general and governors order magistrates to tour their districts, report what should be promoted or rectified and with what effect, so superiors could grade them honestly for the court.
entries.literal: Request an edict to each governor-general and governor to order county magistrates to traverse their jurisdictions, what should be promoted, what rectified, whether execution has yielded results—all reported truthfully to superiors; superiors take this as the basis of evaluation, reported truthfully to court.

entries.zh: 似亦崇實效、去虛文、飭吏治、厚民生之一端也。」
entries.en: This would be one way to prize results over empty forms, tighten administration, and benefit the people.'
entries.literal: This seems also one means of honoring real effect, removing empty documents, rectifying officialdom, and enriching people's livelihood.'

entries.zh: 皆下部議行。
entries.en: All proposals were sent to the ministries for deliberation and action.
entries.literal: All were referred to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.

entries.zh: 傅恆，字春和，富察氏，滿洲鑲黃旗人，孝賢純皇后弟也。
entries.en: Fu Heng, whose style was Chunhe, of the Fuca clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner and younger brother of Empress Xiaoxianchun.
entries.literal: Fu Heng, style Chunhe, of the Fuca clan, Manchu Bordered Yellow Banner, was younger brother of Empress Xiaoxianchun.

entries.zh: 父李榮保，附見其父米思翰傳。
entries.en: His father Li Rongbao is discussed in the biography of Misanhan.
entries.literal: His father Li Rongbao is treated in the biography of Misanhan, Li Rongbao's father.

entries.zh: 傅恆自侍衛洊擢戶部侍郎。
entries.en: Fu Heng rose from the guards to vice-minister of the Ministry of Revenue.
entries.literal: Fu Heng was promoted step by step from guard to vice-minister of Revenue.

entries.zh: 乾隆十年六月，命在軍機處行走。
entries.en: In June 1745 he was ordered to serve on the Grand Council.
entries.literal: In the sixth month of the tenth year of Qianlong he was ordered to serve in the Grand Council.

entries.zh: 十二年，擢戶部尚書。
entries.en: In 1747 he was made minister of revenue.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year he was promoted to Minister of Revenue.

entries.zh: 十三年三月，孝賢純皇后從上南巡，還至德州崩，傅恆扈行，典喪儀。
entries.en: In March 1748 Empress Xiaoxianchun accompanied the emperor on a southern tour and died at Dezhou on the return; Fu Heng had accompanied the journey and directed the mourning rites.
entries.literal: In the third month of the thirteenth year, when Empress Xiaoxianchun accompanied the emperor on a southern tour and died at Dezhou on the return, Fu Heng attended the journey and directed the mourning rites.

entries.zh: 四月，敕獎其勤恪，加太子太保。
entries.en: In April an edict praised his diligence and made him Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: In the fourth month an edict praised his diligence and granted him the honorary title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 時訥親視師金川，解尚書阿克敦協辦大學士以授傅恆，並兼領吏部。
entries.en: While Neqin commanded in Jinchuan, Minister Aikedun was replaced as associate grand secretary by Fu Heng, who also took charge of the Ministry of Personnel.
entries.literal: At that time Neqin was commanding the army in Jinchuan; Minister Aikedun was relieved as associate grand secretary and the post given to Fu Heng, who also concurrently headed the Ministry of Personnel.

entries.zh: 訥親既無功，九月，命傅恆暫管川陝總督，經略軍務。
entries.en: After Neqin's failure, in the ninth month Fu Heng was ordered to act as Sichuan-Shaanxi governor-general and take command of the campaign.
entries.literal: After Neqin's failure, in the ninth month Fu Heng was ordered temporarily to administer the Sichuan-Shaanxi governor-generalship and command military affairs.

entries.zh: 尋授保和殿大學士，發京師及諸行省滿、漢兵三萬五千，以部庫及諸行省銀四百萬供軍儲，又出內帑十萬備犒賞。
entries.en: He was soon made grand secretary of the Hall of Preserving Harmony; 35,000 Manchu and Han troops marched out with four million taels for supplies and 100,000 taels from the privy purse for rewards.
entries.literal: Soon he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hall of Preserving Harmony; thirty-five thousand Manchu and Han troops from the capital and provinces were sent out, four million taels from the ministries and provinces supplied the army, and one hundred thousand taels from the privy purse were issued for rewards.

entries.zh: 十一月，師行，上詣堂子告察，遣皇子及大學士來保等送至良鄉。
entries.en: In November the army marched; the emperor sacrificed at the Tangzi and sent princes and Grand Secretary Lai Bao to escort Fu Heng to Liangxiang.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month the army set out; the emperor went to the Tangzi to offer sacrifice and sent princes and Grand Secretary Lai Bao and others to see Fu Heng off to Liangxiang.

entries.zh: 傅恆既行，上日降手詔褒勉。
entries.en: After Fu Heng left, the emperor sent him personal edicts of praise each day.
entries.literal: After Fu Heng departed, the emperor daily sent personal edicts of praise and encouragement.

entries.zh: 傅恆道陝西，言驛政不修誤軍興，上命協辦大學士尚書尹繼善攝陝西總督，主饋運。
entries.en: Passing through Shaanxi, Fu Heng reported that bad courier service was hindering the army; Yin Jishan was ordered to act as Shaanxi governor-general and handle supply.
entries.literal: Fu Heng, passing through Shaanxi, reported that neglected courier service was delaying the army; the emperor ordered Associate Grand Secretary and Minister Yin Jishan to act as Shaanxi governor-general and manage transport.

entries.zh: 入四川境，馬不給，上又命尹繼善往來川、陝督察。
entries.en: In Sichuan horses were scarce; Yin Jishan was again ordered to supervise between Sichuan and Shaanxi.
entries.literal: Entering Sichuan, horses were lacking; the emperor again ordered Yin Jishan to travel between Sichuan and Shaanxi to supervise.

entries.zh: 旋以傅恆師行甚速，紀律嚴明，命議敘，部議加太子太傅，特命加太保。
entries.en: When Fu Heng's march proved swift and discipline strict, the ministry proposed Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent; the emperor instead made him Grand Preceptor.
entries.literal: Soon, because Fu Heng's march was very rapid and discipline strict, he was recommended for reward; the ministry proposed Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, but the emperor specially ordered Grand Preceptor.

entries.zh: 固辭，不允，發京師及山西、湖北馬七千佐軍。
entries.en: He declined firmly but was overruled; 7,000 horses from the capital, Shanxi, and Hubei were sent to the army.
entries.literal: He firmly declined but was not allowed; seven thousand horses from the capital and Shanxi and Hubei were sent to support the army.

entries.zh: 傅恆發成都，經天赦山，雪後道險，步行七十里至驛。
entries.en: Leaving Chengdu he crossed Tianshe Mountain; after snow the road was treacherous and he walked seventy li to the next station.
entries.literal: Fu Heng set out from Chengdu, passed Tianshe Mountain; after snow the road was perilous and he walked seventy li to the post station.

entries.zh: 上聞，賜雙眼孔雀翎，复固辭。
entries.en: On hearing this the emperor gave him a double-eyed peacock feather, which Fu Heng again declined.
entries.literal: When the emperor heard, he bestowed a double-eyed peacock feather; Fu Heng again firmly declined.

entries.zh: 初，小金川土舍良爾吉間其兄澤旺於莎羅奔，奪其印，即烝於嫂阿扣。
entries.en: Earlier, Lesser Jinchuan chieftain Liang Erji had betrayed his brother Zewang to Slob Dpon, seized his seal, and taken his sister-in-law A Kou.
entries.literal: Earlier, the Lesser Jinchuan chieftain Liang Erji had turned his brother Zewang over to Slob Dpon, seized his seal, and took his sister-in-law A Kou in marriage.

entries.zh: 莎羅奔之犯邊也，良爾吉實從之，後詐降為賊諜。
entries.en: When Slob Dpon invaded, Liang Erji had aided him; later he pretended to surrender and spied for the enemy.
entries.literal: When Slob Dpon raided the border, Liang Erji had in fact followed him; later he feigned surrender and served as the enemy's spy.

entries.zh: 張廣泗入奸民王秋言，使領蠻兵，我師舉動，賊輒知之。
entries.en: Zhang Guangsi trusted the traitor Wang Qiu, who led tribal troops, so the enemy always knew our movements.
entries.literal: Zhang Guangsi trusted the traitor Wang Qiu, who led barbarian troops; our army's every move the enemy learned at once.

entries.zh: 傅恆途中疏請誅良爾吉等，將至軍，使副將馬良柱招良爾吉來迎，至邦噶山，正其罪，並阿扣、王秋悉誅之。
entries.en: En route Fu Heng asked to execute Liang Erji; near the front he had Ma Liangzhu summon Liang Erji to Bangga Mountain, tried him, and executed him with A Kou and Wang Qiu.
entries.literal: Fu Heng memorialized on the road requesting execution of Liang Erji and others; nearing the army he had Deputy Commander Ma Liangzhu summon Liang Erji to welcome him; at Bangga Mountain he tried their crimes and executed Liang Erji, A Kou, and Wang Qiu.

entries.zh: 事聞，上褒傅恆明斷，命拜前賜雙眼孔雀翎，毋更固辭。
entries.en: The emperor praised Fu Heng's decisiveness and told him to accept the peacock feather he had earlier refused.
entries.literal: When the report arrived, the emperor praised Fu Heng's decisiveness and ordered him to accept the earlier gift of the double-eyed peacock feather without further refusal.

entries.zh: 十月，至卡撒，以屯軍地狹隘，與賊相望，且雜處番民巿肆中，乃相度移舊壘前，令總兵冶大雄監營壘。
entries.en: In the tenth month he reached Kasa; the camp was cramped and mixed with tribal markets, so he moved the lines forward under Ye Daxiong's supervision.
entries.literal: In the tenth month he reached Kasa; finding the garrison ground narrow and facing the enemy amid tribal markets, he chose a site before the old camp and had Commander Ye Daxiong supervise building the encampment.

entries.zh: 十四年正月，上疏言：「臣至軍，察用兵始末：當紀山進討之始，馬良柱轉戰而前，逾沃日收小金川直抵丹噶，其鋒甚銳。
entries.en: In the first month of 1749 he wrote: 'At the army I reviewed the campaign: when Ji Shan first attacked, Ma Liangzhu fought through Wo Ri, took Lesser Jinchuan, and reached Danga with great momentum.
entries.literal: In the first month of the fourteenth year he memorialized: 'Having reached the army, I examined the whole course of the campaign: when Ji Shan first advanced, Ma Liangzhu fought forward, crossed Wo Ri, took Lesser Jinchuan, and reached Danga—his momentum was very sharp.

entries.zh: 彼時張廣泗若速進師，賊備未嚴，殄滅尚易；
entries.en: Had Zhang Guangsi advanced quickly then, the enemy was unprepared and could have been destroyed easily;
entries.literal: If Zhang Guangsi had then pressed forward quickly, the enemy's defenses were not yet firm and extermination would still have been easy;

entries.zh: 乃坐失事機，宋宗璋宿留於雜穀，許應虎敗衄於的郊，賊得盡據險要，增碉備禦。
entries.en: instead he lost the moment; Song Zongzhang stalled at Zagu, Xu Yinghu was beaten at Dijiao, and the enemy held the passes and strengthened their diao.
entries.literal: but he lost the moment; Song Zongzhang lingered at Zagu, Xu Yinghu was defeated at Dijiao, and the enemy held all the passes and strengthened their diao defenses.

entries.zh: 訥親初至，督戰甚急，任舉敗沒，銳挫氣索，軍無鬥志，一以軍事委張廣泗。
entries.en: When Neqin arrived he pressed battle hard; Ren Ju fell, morale collapsed, and he handed everything to Zhang Guangsi.
entries.literal: When Neqin first arrived he urged battle fiercely; Ren Ju was defeated and killed, spirits were broken and the army lost will to fight, and he left all military affairs to Zhang Guangsi.

entries.zh: 廣泗又為奸人所愚，專主攻碉。
entries.en: Guangsi was fooled by traitors and attacked only diao.
entries.literal: Guangsi was again deceived by traitors and devoted himself solely to assaulting diao.

entries.zh: 先後殺傷數千人，匿不以聞。
entries.en: Thousands were killed or wounded, which he hid from reports.
entries.literal: Thousands were killed or wounded before and after, and he concealed it without reporting.

entries.zh: 臣惟攻碉最為下策，槍砲不能洞堅壁，於賊無所傷。
entries.en: Assaulting diao is the worst plan: guns cannot breach solid walls or harm the enemy.
entries.literal: I hold that assaulting diao is the worst stratagem; muskets and cannon cannot pierce solid walls and do the enemy no harm.

entries.zh: 賊不過數人，自暗擊明，槍不虛發。
entries.en: A few men in the dark shoot at many in the light, and every shot tells.
entries.literal: The enemy are but a few men; shooting from darkness at those in the light, not a shot is wasted.

entries.zh: 是我惟攻石，而賊實攻人。
entries.en: We strike stone while the enemy strike men.
entries.literal: Thus we attack only stone while the enemy in fact attack men.

entries.zh: 賊於碉外為濠，兵不能越，賊伏其中，自下擊上。
entries.en: They dig moats we cannot cross and fire downward from within.
entries.literal: Outside the diao the enemy dig moats our troops cannot cross; hidden within, they strike from below upward.

entries.zh: 其碉銳立，高於浮屠，建作甚捷，數日可成，旋缺旋補。
entries.en: The diao rise like pagodas, built in days and patched as fast as they crumble.
entries.literal: The diao stand sharp, higher than pagodas; they are built very quickly, finished in days, repaired as fast as they fall.

entries.zh: 且眾心甚固，碉盡碎而不去，砲方過而復起。
entries.en: The people stand firm: when diao are smashed they do not flee, and when cannon pass they rebuild.
entries.literal: The people's hearts are very firm; though diao are shattered they do not leave, and when cannon pass they rise again.

entries.zh: 客主勞佚，形勢迥殊，攻一碉難於克一城。
entries.en: Guest fights host on unequal terms; one diao is harder than a city.
entries.literal: Guest and host, labor and ease—the situations differ utterly; taking one diao is harder than taking a city.

entries.zh: 即臣所駐卡撒，左右山巔三百餘碉，計日以攻，非數年不能盡。
entries.en: At Kasa alone more than three hundred diao crown the hills; to take them day by day would take years.
entries.literal: Even at Kasa where I am stationed, there are more than three hundred diao on the left and right peaks; counting days to attack, years would not suffice to take them all.

entries.zh: 且得一碉輒傷數十百人，得不償失。
entries.en: Each diao costs dozens or hundreds of lives—the gain is not worth the price.
entries.literal: And for each diao taken dozens or hundreds of men are lost—the gain does not repay the cost.

entries.zh: 兵法，攻堅則瑕者堅，攻瑕則堅者瑕。
entries.en: In war, strike the hard point and the soft hardens; strike the soft and the hard weakens.
entries.literal: In warfare, attack what is strong and the weak become strong; attack what is weak and the strong become weak.

entries.zh: 惟使賊失所恃，我兵乃可用其所長。
entries.en: Only by depriving the enemy of what they rely on can our troops use their strengths.
entries.literal: Only if the enemy is made to lose what they rely on can our troops use their strengths.

entries.zh: 擬俟諸軍大集，分道而進。
entries.en: When the armies gather I plan to advance on separate routes.
entries.literal: I plan when the armies are fully gathered to advance by separate routes.

entries.zh: 別選銳師，旁探間道，裹糧直入，逾碉勿攻，繞出其後。
entries.en: Picked troops will find by-paths, carry rations, pass the diao without fighting, and strike from behind.
entries.literal: Choosing picked troops, scouts will seek by-paths, carry rations and penetrate deep, pass the diao without attacking, and circle behind them.

entries.zh: 番眾不多，外備既密，內守必虛。
entries.en: The tribes are few; thick outer defense means thin inner defense.
entries.literal: The tribesmen are not numerous; with outer defenses thick, inner defense must be thin.

entries.zh: 我兵既自捷徑深入，守者各懷內顧，人無固志，均可不攻自潰。
entries.en: Once we penetrate by a swift route, defenders will look homeward and collapse without a fight.
entries.literal: Once our troops penetrate by the swift route, defenders will each look inward, men will lack firm will, and all can collapse without attack.

entries.zh: 卡撒為進噶拉依正道，嶺高溝窄，臣當親任其難。
entries.en: Kasa is the main road to Gala-i; I shall take that hard road myself.
entries.literal: Kasa is the direct road to Gala-i; the ridge is high and the gorge narrow, and I shall personally undertake that hardship.

entries.zh: 黨壩隘險，亦幾同卡撒，酌益新軍。
entries.en: Dangba is almost as narrow as Kasa; I shall reinforce that route too.
entries.literal: Dangba pass is nearly as narrow as Kasa; I shall add fresh troops there as well.

entries.zh: 兩道並進，直搗巢穴，取其渠魁。
entries.en: Both columns will drive at the nest and seize the chiefs.
entries.literal: Advancing on both routes, we shall strike straight at the nest and seize the chiefs.

entries.zh: 期四月間奏捷。」
entries.en: I expect victory by the fourth month.'
entries.literal: I expect to report victory within the fourth month.'

entries.zh: 上以金川非大敵，勞師兩載，誅大臣，失良將，內不懌。
entries.en: The emperor thought Jinchuan no great foe, yet two years of war had cost ministers' lives and good generals, and he was displeased.
entries.literal: The emperor, holding that Jinchuan was no great enemy yet the army had labored two years, ministers were executed, and good generals lost, was inwardly displeased.

entries.zh: 及是聞其地險難下，益不欲竟其事，遂以孝聖憲皇后諭命班師，而傅恆方督總兵哈攀龍、哈尚德等攻下數碉。
entries.en: Learning how hard the country was, he wished to end the war on the empress dowager's order, though Fu Heng was still taking diao under Ha Panlong and Ha Shangde.
entries.literal: Now hearing the ground was hard to subdue, he was even less willing to press the affair to the end; on the empress dowager's order he recalled the army, while Fu Heng was still directing generals Ha Panlong and Ha Shangde to take several diao.

entries.zh: 上以金川水土惡，賜傅恆人蓡三斤，並及諸將有差，屢詔召傅恆還。
entries.en: He sent Fu Heng ginseng and rewards for the generals and repeatedly recalled him, citing Jinchuan's foul climate.
entries.literal: Because Jinchuan's climate and water were malignant, the emperor gave Fu Heng three jin of ginseng and varying amounts to the generals, and repeatedly ordered Fu Heng's return.

entries.zh: 又以孝聖憲皇后諭封一等忠勇公，賜寶石頂、四團龍補服。
entries.en: On the empress dowager's order he was made Duke of Loyal Valor of the first rank, with jeweled finial and four-dragon patch.
entries.literal: Again on the empress dowager's order he enfeoffed him duke of the first rank as Duke of Loyal Valor, with a jeweled finial and four-dragon rank patch.

entries.zh: 傅恆奏言：「金川事一誤，今復輕率蕆事，賊焰愈張。
entries.en: Fu Heng wrote: 'Jinchuan was mishandled once; to end it lightly now will only embolden the rebels.
entries.literal: Fu Heng memorialized: 'The Jinchuan affair was once mishandled; to end it lightly now will only make the rebels fiercer.

entries.zh: 眾土司皆罹其毒，邊宇將無寧日。
entries.en: Every tribal chief suffers them; the frontier will never be quiet.
entries.literal: All the tribal chiefs suffer their poison; the border will know no peace.

entries.zh: 審度形勢，賊碉非盡當道，其巢皆老弱，我兵且戰且前，自昔嶺中峰直抵噶拉依，破竹建瓴，功在垂成，棄之可惜。
entries.en: Not every diao blocks the road; their nests are weak; advancing from Xiling Peak to Gala-i would be irresistible, and to stop now would be wasteful.
entries.literal: Judging the situation, not every enemy diao blocks the road; their nests are mostly old and weak; our troops fighting forward from Xiling Peak straight to Gala-i would be like splitting bamboo—success is near and to abandon it would be a pity.

entries.zh: 且臣受詔出師，若不掃穴擒渠，何顏返命？」
entries.en: Having been ordered to campaign, how can I return without destroying the nest and capturing the leaders?'
entries.literal: Moreover, having received orders to take the field, if I do not root out the nest and capture the leaders, with what face can I return to report?'

entries.zh: 並力辭封賞，上不允，手詔謂：「匈奴未滅，無以家為，乃驃姚武人銳往之概。
entries.en: He also refused honors; the emperor refused to accept and wrote: 'Until the Xiongnu are destroyed there is no home—that was Huo Qubing's spirit.
entries.literal: He also firmly declined enfeoffment and rewards; the emperor would not allow it and personally wrote: 'Until the Xiongnu are destroyed one cannot make a home—such was the bold spirit of Huo Qubing.

entries.zh: 大學士抒誠贊化，豈與兜鍪閫帥爭一日之績？」
entries.en: How should a grand secretary who aids the state vie with field commanders for a day's glory?'
entries.literal: A grand secretary who expounds sincerity and aids transformation—how should he vie for a single day's merit with helmeted commanders?'

entries.zh: 反复累數千言，复賜詩喻指。
entries.en: He wrote thousands of words in personal edicts and sent a poem to make his meaning plain.
entries.literal: Repeatedly he wrote thousands of words and again bestowed a poem to make his meaning plain.

entries.zh: 傅恆直軍機處二十三年，日侍左右，以勤慎得上眷。
entries.en: For twenty-three years Fu Heng served on the Grand Council at the emperor's side and won favor by diligence.
entries.literal: Fu Heng served in the Grand Council twenty-three years, daily attending at the emperor's side, and won imperial favor through diligence and caution.

entries.zh: 故事，軍機處諸臣不同入見，乾隆初，惟訥親承旨。
entries.en: By precedent councillors did not all attend together; early in Qianlong only Neqin took edicts.
entries.literal: By precedent, grand councillors did not all enter audience together; in early Qianlong only Neqin received edicts.

entries.zh: 迨傅恆自陳不能多識，乞諸大臣同入見。
entries.en: Fu Heng said he could not remember enough and asked that all ministers attend together.
entries.literal: When Fu Heng said he could not remember much, he begged that all ministers enter audience together.

entries.zh: 上晚膳後有所諮訪，又召傅恆獨對，時謂之「晚面」。
entries.en: After supper the emperor still summoned Fu Heng alone for consultation—the 'evening audience.'
entries.literal: After the evening meal when the emperor had something to consult, he again summoned Fu Heng alone—this was called the 'evening audience.'

entries.zh: 又軍機處諸大臣既承旨，退自屬草，至傅恆始命章京具稿以進。
entries.en: Formerly councillors drafted their own memorials after audience; Fu Heng had secretaries draft them first.
entries.literal: Also, after grand councillors received edicts they had drafted memorials themselves; from Fu Heng's time secretaries were first ordered to prepare drafts for submission.

entries.zh: 上倚傅恆為重臣，然偶有小節疏失，即加以戒約。
entries.en: The emperor relied on Fu Heng but admonished even small slips.
entries.literal: The emperor relied on Fu Heng as a great minister, yet if he slipped in small matters he was at once admonished.

entries.zh: 傅恆益謙下，治事不敢自擅。
entries.en: Fu Heng grew more humble and would not decide affairs alone.
entries.literal: Fu Heng became all the more humble and in handling affairs did not dare act on his own.

entries.zh: 敬禮士大夫，翼後進使盡其才。
entries.en: He honored scholars and helped younger men use their talents.
entries.literal: He respected scholar-officials and helped juniors use their talents to the full.

entries.zh: 行軍與士卒同甘苦。
entries.en: On campaign he shared the soldiers' hardships.
entries.literal: On campaign he shared hardship with the soldiers.

entries.zh: 卒時未五十，上尤惜之。
entries.en: He was not yet fifty when he died, and the emperor mourned him deeply.
entries.literal: He died before fifty; the emperor especially mourned him.

entries.zh: 傅恆自渡戛鳩江，未嘗與緬甸兵戰，刈禾為糧，行二千里不血刃，而士馬觸暑雨多疾病。
entries.en: After crossing the Jiugu Fu Heng fought no Burmese troops; he lived off the harvest and marched two thousand li unblooded, but heat and rain brought widespread sickness.
entries.literal: From the time Fu Heng crossed the Jiugu he had not fought Burmese troops; reaping grain for provisions, he marched two thousand li without drawing a blade, yet men and horses suffered many illnesses from heat and rain.

entries.zh: 會阿桂將萬餘人自虎踞關出野牛壩，造舟畢成，徵廣東、福建水師亦至，乃合軍並進。
entries.en: Agui brought more than ten thousand men from Huju Pass to Yeniuba; when the boats were ready and Guangdong and Fujian fleets arrived, the armies joined and advanced.
entries.literal: Meanwhile Agui led more than ten thousand men out from Huju Pass to Yeniuba; when boat-building was finished and the Guangdong and Fujian naval forces also arrived, the armies united and advanced together.

entries.zh: 哈國興將水師，阿桂、阿里袞將陸師，阿桂出江東，阿里袞出江西。
entries.en: Ha Guoxing led the fleet; Agui and Aligun the land forces—Agui east of the river, Aligun west.
entries.literal: Ha Guoxing commanded the navy; Agui and Aligun commanded the land forces; Agui went out east of the river and Aligun west of the river.

entries.zh: 緬兵壘金沙江兩岸，又以舟師扼江口。
entries.en: The Burmese fortified both banks of the Jinsha and blocked the mouth with boats.
entries.literal: Burmese troops fortified both banks of the Jinsha and also used a fleet to hold the river mouth.

entries.zh: 阿桂先與緬兵遇，麾步兵發銃矢，又以騎兵陷陣，緬兵潰。
entries.en: Agui met the Burmese first, poured musket and arrow fire into them, sent cavalry to break their line, and routed them.
entries.literal: Agui first met Burmese troops, ordered the infantry to fire muskets and arrows, and also sent cavalry to break the formation; the Burmese routed.

entries.zh: 哈國興督舟師乘風蹴敵，緬兵舟相擊，死者數千。
entries.en: Ha Guoxing drove the fleet downwind into the enemy; thousands died as boats collided.
entries.literal: Ha Guoxing directed the fleet to strike the enemy with the wind; Burmese boats collided and several thousand died.

entries.zh: 阿里袞亦破西岸緬兵，傅恆以所獲纛進。
entries.en: Aligun broke the west-bank Burmese as well, and Fu Heng sent up the captured banners.
entries.literal: Aligun also broke the Burmese on the west bank; Fu Heng presented the captured banners.

entries.zh: 上復為賦詩，阿里袞感瘴而病，改將水師，旋卒。
entries.en: The emperor wrote another poem; Aligun took miasma fever, switched to the fleet, and soon died.
entries.literal: The emperor again composed a poem; Aligun fell ill from miasma, was changed to command the navy, and soon died.

entries.zh: 十一月，傅恆復進攻老官屯，老官屯在金沙江東，東猛密，西猛墅，北猛拱、猛養，南緬都阿瓦，為水陸通衢。
entries.en: In the eleventh month Fu Heng attacked Laoguantun on the Jinsha, the junction of Mengmi, Mengshu, Menggong, Mengyang, and the road to Ava.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month Fu Heng again advanced on Laoguantun; Laoguantun lies east of the Jinsha, with Mengmi to the east and Mengshu to the west, Menggong and Mengyang to the north and the Burmese capital Ava to the south—a thoroughfare for land and water.

entries.zh: 緬兵伐木立寨甚固，哈國興督諸軍力攻，未即克。
entries.en: The Burmese built a timber stockade; Ha Guoxing assaulted it hard but could not take it quickly.
entries.literal: Burmese troops felled timber and built a very solid stockade; Ha Guoxing directed all armies in a fierce assault but did not take it at once.

entries.zh: 師破東南木寨，緬兵夜自水寨出，傅恆令海蘭察御之，又令伊勒圖督舟師掩擊，复獲船纛。
entries.en: Our troops took the southeast timber camp; the Burmese sallied by night from the water camp; Hailancha repelled them and Yiletui's fleet seized more boats and banners.
entries.literal: The army broke the southeastern timber stockade; Burmese troops came out at night from the water stockade; Fu Heng ordered Hailancha to repel them and Yiletui to direct the fleet in a surprise attack, again capturing boats and banners.

entries.zh: 緬兵潛至江岸築壘，又自林箐中出，海蘭察擊之，屢有斬馘。
entries.en: The Burmese built riverside forts and struck from the woods; Hailancha beat them back again and again.
entries.literal: Burmese troops secretly came to the riverbank to build forts and also emerged from the forest thickets; Hailancha struck them and repeatedly took heads.

entries.zh: 師久攻堅，士卒染瘴多物故，水陸軍三萬一千，至是僅存一萬三千。
entries.en: After long assaults, miasma killed many; of 31,000 land and water troops only 13,000 remained.
entries.literal: The army had long assaulted strong positions; soldiers contracted miasma and many died; of thirty-one thousand land and water troops, only thirteen thousand now remained.

entries.zh: 傅恆以入告，上命罷兵，召傅恆還京。
entries.en: Fu Heng reported the losses; the emperor ended the campaign and recalled him.
entries.literal: Fu Heng reported this; the emperor ordered the campaign ended and Fu Heng recalled to the capital.

entries.zh: 傅恆俄亦病，阿桂以聞。
entries.en: Fu Heng soon fell ill; Agui informed the court.
entries.literal: Fu Heng soon fell ill himself; Agui reported it.

entries.zh: 上令即馳驛還，而以軍事付阿桂。
entries.en: The emperor ordered him home by relay post and left the army to Agui.
entries.literal: The emperor ordered him to return post-haste by courier relay and entrusted military affairs to Agui.

entries.zh: 會緬甸酋懵駁遣頭人諾爾塔齎蒲葉書乞罷兵，傅恆奏入，上許其行成。
entries.en: The Burmese chief Meng Bo sent Nuoerta with a palm-leaf plea for peace; Fu Heng reported it and the emperor agreed to truce.
entries.literal: Meanwhile the Burmese chief Meng Bo sent headman Nuoerta with a palm-leaf letter begging to cease hostilities; Fu Heng memorialized it and the emperor permitted a settlement.

entries.zh: 傅恆附疏言：「用兵之始，眾以為難。
entries.en: Fu Heng added: 'When war began everyone called it hard.
entries.literal: Fu Heng appended a memorial saying: 'At the start of the campaign all held it difficult.

entries.zh: 臣執意請行，負委任，請從重治罪。」
entries.en: I insisted on going and failed my charge; punish me severely.'
entries.literal: I insisted on going and have failed my commission; I ask to be punished severely.'

entries.zh: 上手詔謂：「用兵非得已，如以為非是，朕當首任其過。
entries.en: The emperor wrote: 'War is never chosen lightly; if it was wrong, I should bear the blame.
entries.literal: The emperor's personal edict said: 'Using force is never willingly chosen; if you think it wrong, I should bear the blame first.

entries.zh: 皇祖時，吳三桂請撤籓，諮於群臣，議撤者惟米思翰、明珠數人。
entries.en: Under the Kangxi Emperor, when Wu Sangui asked to give up his fief, only Misanhan, Mingzhu, and a few others favored withdrawal.
entries.literal: In our grandfather's time, when Wu Sangui asked to withdraw the fief, the emperor consulted the ministers; only Misanhan, Mingzhu, and a few others favored withdrawal.

entries.zh: 及三桂反，眾請誅議撤諸臣，皇祖深闢其非。
entries.en: When Sangui rebelled, many wanted those ministers killed; the grandfather firmly refused.
entries.literal: When Sangui rebelled, many asked that the ministers who had favored withdrawal be executed; the grandfather deeply rejected that as wrong.

entries.zh: 朕仰紹祖訓，傅恆此事，可援以相比。
entries.en: I follow that teaching; Fu Heng's case is like it.
entries.literal: I follow our grandfather's teaching; Fu Heng's case may be compared to this.

entries.zh: 傅恆收猛拱，當賜三眼孔雀翎，疏辭，俟功成拜賜。
entries.en: For recovering Menggong he should have the three-eyed peacock feather; he declined until victory.
entries.literal: Fu Heng recovered Menggong and should receive the three-eyed peacock feather; he memorialized to decline, asking to receive it only when merit was achieved.

entries.zh: 今既未克賊巢，當繳進賜翎，以稱其請罪之意。」
entries.en: Since the nest was not taken, he should return the feather to match his plea for guilt.'
entries.literal: Now that the enemy nest has not been taken, he should return the gifted feather to match his plea for punishment.'

entries.zh: 懵駁遣頭人詣軍獻方物。
entries.en: Meng Bo sent headmen with tribute to the army.
entries.literal: Meng Bo sent headmen to the army presenting local products.

entries.zh: 十月，傅恆還駐虎踞關，上命傅恆會雲貴總督彰寶議減雲南總兵、知府員缺，釐正州縣舊制。
entries.en: In the tenth month Fu Heng garrisoned Huju Pass and met Governor Zhang Bao to reform Yunnan's military and civil posts.
entries.literal: In the tenth month Fu Heng returned to garrison at Huju Pass; the emperor ordered Fu Heng to meet with Yunnan-Guizhou Governor Zhang Bao to discuss reducing the posts of Yunnan regional commander and prefect, and rectifying the old system of prefectures and counties.

entries.zh: 三十四年二月，班師。
entries.en: In the second month of 1769 the army withdrew.
entries.literal: In the second month of the thirty-fourth year the army withdrew.

entries.zh: 三月，上幸天津，傅恆朝行在。
entries.en: In the third month the emperor went to Tianjin and Fu Heng attended him on the journey.
entries.literal: In the third month the emperor visited Tianjin; Fu Heng attended audience at the traveling palace.

entries.zh: 既而緬甸酋謝罪表久不至，上謂傅恆方病，不忍治其罪。
entries.en: When Burma's apology lagged, the emperor spared Fu Heng because he was ill.
entries.literal: Later the Burmese chief's letter of apology long failed to arrive; the emperor said Fu Heng was ill and could not bear to punish him.

entries.zh: 七月，卒，上親臨其第酹酒，命喪葬視宗室鎮國公，諡文忠。
entries.en: In the seventh month he died; the emperor poured libation at his house, gave him a prince's funeral, and posthumous title Wenzhong.
entries.literal: In the seventh month he died; the emperor personally visited his house to pour libation, ordered funeral rites equal to a clansman prince of the blood of the third degree, and gave the posthumous title Wenzhong.

entries.zh: 又命入祀前所建宗祠。
entries.en: He was also enshrined in the hall built for his family.
entries.literal: He was also ordered enshrined in the ancestral hall built earlier.

entries.zh: 其後上复幸天津，念傅恆於此復命，又經傅恆墓賜奠，皆紀以詩。
entries.en: Later visits to Tianjin and offerings at Fu Heng's tomb were all remembered in the emperor's poems.
entries.literal: Later when the emperor again visited Tianjin, remembering Fu Heng's audience there, and passing Fu Heng's tomb bestowed sacrifice—all were recorded in poems.

entries.zh: 及賦懷舊詩，許為「社稷臣」。
entries.en: In a poem of remembrance he called Fu Heng a 'pillar of the state.'
entries.literal: In his poem recalling old ministers he allowed him to be called a 'pillar of the state.'

entries.zh: 嘉慶元年，以福康安平苗功，贈貝子。
entries.en: In 1796 Fukang'an's pacification of the Miao won Fu Heng a posthumous beizi rank.
entries.literal: In the first year of Jiaqing, because Fukang'an pacified the Miao, Fu Heng was posthumously given the rank of beizi.

entries.zh: 福康安卒，推恩贈郡王銜，旋並命配享太廟。
entries.en: After Fukang'an's death the family was raised to princely rank and granted shared sacrifice in the Ancestral Temple.
entries.literal: When Fukang'an died, favor was extended to grant the posthumous rank of prince; soon he was also ordered to share sacrifice in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

entries.zh: 列傳八十八
entries.en: Biography 88
entries.literal: Biographies 88

entries.zh: 徐本，字立人，浙江錢塘人，尚書潮子。
entries.en: Xu Ben, whose style name was Liren, came from Qiantang in Zhejiang and was the son of Minister Xu Chao.
entries.literal: Xu Ben, style name Liren, was a native of Qiantang in Zhejiang, son of Minister Xu Chao.

entries.zh: 本，康熙五十七年進士，改庶吉士，授編修。
entries.en: Xu Ben earned his jinshi degree in 1718, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and received appointment as a compiler.
entries.literal: Ben passed the civil examinations in the fifty-seventh year of Kangxi, was made a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed compiler.

entries.zh: 雍正五年，提督貴州學政，授贊善，遷侍讀。
entries.en: In 1727 he was appointed educational commissioner of Guizhou, then reader-in-waiting, and soon after promoted to reader.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Yongzheng he was made educational commissioner of Guizhou with concurrent supervision, appointed reader-in-waiting, and promoted to reader.

entries.zh: 七年，擢貴州按察使。
entries.en: In 1729 he was promoted to surveillance commissioner of Guizhou.
entries.literal: In the seventh year he was promoted to surveillance commissioner of Guizhou.

entries.zh: 八年，調江蘇，遷湖北布政使。
entries.en: In 1730 he was transferred to Jiangsu and then promoted to provincial treasurer of Hubei.
entries.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to Jiangsu and promoted to provincial treasurer of Hubei.

entries.zh: 十年，擢安慶巡撫。
entries.en: In 1732 he was promoted to governor of Anqing.
entries.literal: In the tenth year he was promoted to governor of Anqing.

entries.zh: 奏定比緝盜賊章程，竊案責府州，盜案責臬司。
entries.en: He submitted regulations for tracking down bandits, assigning petty theft cases to prefectural authorities and robbery cases to the provincial surveillance commissioner.
entries.literal: He memorialized to fix regulations for comparing and apprehending bandits: petty theft cases were the responsibility of prefectures and departments, robbery cases that of the provincial surveillance commissioner.

entries.zh: 案多而未獲，巡撫親提。
entries.en: When many cases remained unsolved, the governor personally took charge of the investigations.
entries.literal: When cases were numerous and culprits had not been caught, the governor personally conducted the inquiry.

entries.zh: 比立限，定勸懲。
entries.en: He also established deadlines and defined incentives and penalties.
entries.literal: He likewise set time limits and fixed rewards and punishments.

entries.zh: 上嘉之。
entries.en: The emperor praised his work.
entries.literal: The emperor commended this.

entries.zh: 十一年，疏言：「雲、貴、廣西改流土司安置內地，例十人給官房五楹，地五十畝。
entries.en: In 1733 he memorialized: "When native chieftains from Yunnan, Guizhou, and Guangxi were brought under direct administration and resettled inland, the rule allotted five bays of official housing and fifty mu of land for every ten people.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year he memorialized: "For native chieftains in Yunnan, Guizhou, and Guangxi who were transformed and resettled in the interior, the rule is that ten persons receive five bays of official housing and fifty mu of land.

entries.zh: 安慶置二十一人，地遠在來安。
entries.en: Twenty-one such persons were settled at Anqing, but their allotted land lay far away in Lai'an.
entries.literal: At Anqing twenty-one persons were settled, but the land lay far away in Lai'an.

entries.zh: 請變價別購，俾耕以食。」
entries.en: He asked that the distant plots be sold and other land bought nearby so they could farm for their sustenance."
entries.literal: He requested that the property be sold and other land purchased so they could farm for their livelihood."

entries.zh: 又疏言：「州縣徵糧，例由府道封櫃，請改州縣自封。
entries.en: He also proposed: "Grain tax collection, which customarily required sealing by prefectural and circuit offices, should be changed so that counties and districts sealed the funds themselves.
entries.literal: He also memorialized: "When prefectures and districts collected grain taxes, by rule the prefectural and circuit offices sealed the coffers; he requested that districts and counties seal them themselves.

entries.zh: 完糧十截串票改仍用三連由票，零戶銀以下以十錢當一分。」
entries.en: He restored the three-part tax warrant in place of the ten-section receipt for completed payments, and set ten cash equal to one fen for fractional household payments."
entries.literal: The ten-section tax receipt for completed payments was changed back to the three-part tax warrant, and for fractional household payments amounts below one fen were reckoned with ten cash as one fen."

entries.zh: 又疏言：「壽州濱淮，盜聚族而居，假捕魚為業，每出劫掠，已次第捕治，令漁船編甲。
entries.en: He further reported: "Along the Huai at Shouzhou, bandit clans posing as fishermen had been raiding in turn; after successive arrests, fishing boats were now organized into militia units.
entries.literal: He also memorialized: "Shouzhou lies along the Huai River, where bandits live in clan settlements and pretend to fish for a living, going out to plunder whenever they can; they have been captured and punished in turn, and fishing boats are now registered in militia units.

entries.zh: 孫、平、焦、鄧諸姓設族正，有盜不時舉發。」
entries.en: Clan heads were appointed among the Sun, Ping, Jiao, and Deng families to report banditry promptly."
entries.literal: Clan heads were appointed among the Sun, Ping, Jiao, and Deng surnames, who were to report any theft without delay."

entries.zh: 皆下部議行。
entries.en: All these proposals were sent to the ministries for deliberation and enactment.
entries.literal: All were referred to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.

entries.zh: 徐本汪由敦來保劉綸劉統勳
entries.en: Xu Ben, Wang Youdun, Lai Bao, Liu Lun, and Liu Tongxun
entries.literal: Xu Ben, Wang Youdun, Lai Bao, Liu Lun, Liu Tongxun

entries.zh: 十二年，命徵金川，隸總督張廣泗軍。
entries.en: In Qianlong 12 (1747), he was ordered to campaign against Jinchuan under Governor-General Zhang Guangsi.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year he was ordered to campaign against Jinchuan and served under Governor Zhang Guangsi.

entries.zh: 尋授西鳳協副將。
entries.en: He was soon made brigade deputy commander of the Xifeng garrison.
entries.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed brigade deputy commander of the Xifeng garrison.

entries.zh: 舉至軍，與總兵許應虎、副將高宗瑾、參將買國良攻色底賊碉，擊以砲二百餘發，碉一角圮，垣鑿孔發砲，密如鱗比。
entries.en: Ju joined the army and, with Regional Commander Xu Yinghu, Brigade Deputy Gao Zongjin, and Regimental Colonel Mai Guoliang, assaulted the rebel blockhouses at Sedi. After more than two hundred cannon shots, one corner of a blockhouse collapsed; its walls were pierced with gunports as closely packed as fish scales.
entries.literal: Ju arrived at the army and, together with Regional Commander Xu Yinghu, Brigade Deputy Gao Zongjin, and Regimental Colonel Mai Guoliang, attacked the rebel blockhouses at Sedi. After more than two hundred cannon shots, one corner of a blockhouse collapsed; its walls were pierced with gunports, packed together as closely as fish scales.

entries.zh: 舉度我軍砲小不能下，將移軍退守，賊出戰，再設伏敗之。
entries.en: Judging their guns too light to reduce the fort, Ju prepared to pull back to the defensive line; when the rebels sallied out, he laid another ambush and routed them.
entries.literal: Ju judged that their cannon were too small to bring the fort down and was about to withdraw the army to defensive positions; the rebels came out to fight, and he set an ambush and defeated them again.

entries.zh: 十三年，上諭謂：「在軍諸將狃於瞻對之役，庸懦欺矇，已成夙習。
entries.en: In year thirteen the emperor declared: "The commanders in the field, spoiled by the Zhandui campaign, have made timidity and double-dealing a fixed habit.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year, the emperor issued an edict saying: "The generals in the army, habituated to the Zhandui campaign, have grown slothful and cowardly in deceit — this has become a longstanding practice.

entries.zh: 今別用舉等，皆未從征瞻對，無所掣肘，宜鼓勵勇往。」
entries.en: Ju and the others are being used afresh; none served at Zhandui and none are held back by old habits — they should be urged to advance boldly."
entries.literal: Now, employing Ju and the others separately — none of them served in the Zhandui campaign and they have no restraints — they should be encouraged to press forward boldly.

entries.zh: 廣泗亦奏在川鎮將，忠誠勇幹無出舉右者，令率漢、土兵三千取道攻昔嶺。
entries.en: Zhang Guangsi also reported that among Sichuan's regional commanders none matched Ju in loyalty, courage, or capacity, and ordered him to lead three thousand Han and native troops against Xiling by a separate route.
entries.literal: Guangsi also memorialized that among the commanders in Sichuan, none surpassed Ju in loyalty, courage, and ability, and ordered him to lead three thousand Han and native troops by a separate route to attack Xiling.

entries.zh: 尋又奏令署重慶鎮總兵。
entries.en: He soon memorialized again to make Ju acting regional commander of Chongqing.
entries.literal: Soon he memorialized again to appoint Ju acting regional commander of Chongqing.

entries.zh: 時上方命舉真除，經略大學士訥親以舉死事聞，上閱疏為泣下，並諭：「舉忠憤激發，甘死如飴，而朕以小丑跳梁，用良臣於危地，思之深惻！」
entries.en: The emperor had just ordered Ju's formal appointment when Commissioner-General Neqin reported his death in battle; reading the memorial, the emperor wept and declared: "Ju, roused by loyal wrath, met death as gladly as sweetness — yet I, over trifling rebels in revolt, put a good man in mortal danger; the thought wounds me deeply!"
entries.literal: At that time the emperor had just ordered Ju's formal appointment; Commissioner-General and Grand Secretary Neqin reported Ju's death in service; the emperor, reading the memorial, wept and also issued an edict: "Ju, stirred by loyal indignation, welcomed death as though it were sweet; yet I, on account of petty rebels rampaging, sent a worthy minister into peril — the thought cuts deeply!"

entries.zh: 命視提督例賜卹，加都督同知，諡勇烈，祀昭忠祠，官其子承恩都司，承緒千總。
entries.en: He was granted posthumous relief on the scale accorded a provincial commander, raised posthumously to Vice Commissioner-in-chief, given the posthumous name Yonglie (Valiant and Steadfast), enshrined in the Shrine of Manifest Loyalty, and his sons Chengen and Chengxu were appointed battalion commander and company captain.
entries.literal: He was ordered granted posthumous compensation on the model of a provincial commander, conferred Vice Commissioner-in-chief of the Chief Commandant's Office, given the posthumous title Yonglie, enshrined in the Shrine of Manifest Loyalty, and his sons Chengen and Chengxu were given office as battalion commander and company captain respectively.

entries.zh: 承恩喪終入謝，上以尚幼，命傳諭其母善教之。
entries.en: When Chengen came to court after mourning, the emperor, finding him still young, sent word to his mother to raise him with care.
entries.literal: When Chengen completed mourning and came to give thanks, the emperor, seeing he was still young, ordered a message conveyed to his mother to train him well.

entries.zh: 二十四年，授三等侍衛。
entries.en: In year twenty-four he was made a third-class imperial guardsman.
entries.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, he was appointed a third-class imperial guardsman.

entries.zh: 累遷福建陸路提督。
entries.en: He rose in time to provincial commander of Fujian's land forces.
entries.literal: He was promoted in succession to provincial military commander of Fujian's land forces.

entries.zh: 五十二年，台灣林爽文為亂，承恩請往討之，師無功，逮詣京師，罪當死，上寬之。
entries.en: In year fifty-two, when Lin Shuangwen rebelled in Taiwan, Chengen volunteered to suppress him; the campaign failed, he was brought to the capital under arrest, and though his crime warranted death the emperor spared him.
entries.literal: In the fifty-second year, Lin Shuangwen rebelled in Taiwan; Chengen requested to go suppress him; the army achieved nothing, he was arrested and brought to the capital, his offense merited death, but the emperor showed leniency.

entries.zh: 五十三年，赦出獄。
entries.en: In year fifty-three he was pardoned and released from prison.
entries.literal: In the fifty-third year, he was pardoned and released from prison.

entries.zh: 五十五年，复授巡捕營參將，遷副將。
entries.en: In year fifty-five he was again made regimental colonel of the patrol garrison and promoted to brigade deputy.
entries.literal: In the fifty-fifth year, he was again appointed regimental colonel of the patrol garrison and promoted to brigade deputy.

entries.zh: 卒。
entries.en: He died.
entries.literal: He died.

entries.zh: 承緒官巡捕營游擊，市中火，赴救被創，卒。
entries.en: Chengxu held the post of battalion colonel in the patrol garrison; when fire broke out in the city he rushed to help, was wounded, and died.
entries.literal: Chengxu served as battalion colonel of the patrol garrison; during a fire in the city he went to the rescue, was wounded, and died.

entries.zh: 上之赦承恩，謂其未有子，承緒又死勤事，不可使舉無嗣也。
entries.en: In pardoning Chengen, the emperor noted that Chengen had no son and Chengxu had died in the performance of his duty; Ren Ju's line could not be allowed to end.
entries.literal: In pardoning Chengen, the emperor said that Chengen had no son and Chengxu had died in public service; Ju must not be left without an heir.

entries.zh: 準噶爾犯克什圖、峨崙磯諸卡倫。
entries.en: The Dzungars struck the karun outposts at Keshitu, Elunji, and elsewhere.
entries.literal: The Dzungars attacked the karun outposts at Keshitu, Elunji, and others.

entries.zh: 大雄偕總兵樊廷以​​二千人當賊二萬，轉戰七晝夜，拔守卡倫兵以出。
entries.en: With Regional Commander Fan Ting, Daxiong held twenty thousand rebels at bay with two thousand men, fought seven days and nights, and extricated the garrison of the karun.
entries.literal: Daxiong together with Regional Commander Fan Ting with two thousand men held off twenty thousand rebels, fought for seven days and nights, and rescued the soldiers defending the karun.

entries.zh: 與總兵張元佐等師會，力戰殺賊。
entries.en: He joined Regional Commander Zhang Yuanzuo and others, fought hard, and killed many rebels.
entries.literal: He joined forces with Regional Commander Zhang Yuanzuo and others, fought fiercely, and killed rebels.

entries.zh: 賜拜他喇布勒哈番世職，賚白金五千。
entries.en: He was granted the hereditary rank of Baitalabulehafan and rewarded with five thousand taels of silver.
entries.literal: He was granted the hereditary rank of Baitalabulehafan and given five thousand taels of white silver.

entries.zh: 尋授直隸山永協副將。
entries.en: He was soon made brigade deputy commander of Shanyong in Zhili.
entries.literal: Soon he was appointed brigade deputy commander of Shanyong in Zhili.

entries.zh: 命署湖北彝陵鎮總兵。
entries.en: He was ordered to serve as acting regional commander of Yiling in Hubei.
entries.literal: He was ordered to serve as acting regional commander of Yiling in Hubei.

entries.zh: 上言：「彝陵距省千餘裡，兵餉歲以四季支給，請改夏秋、冬春二次匯支。」
entries.en: He memorialized: "Yiling lies more than a thousand li from the provincial capital, and troop pay is issued in four seasonal installments; I ask that it be paid instead in two lump sums, in summer-autumn and winter-spring."
entries.literal: He submitted a memorial: "Yiling is more than a thousand li from the provincial capital; troops' pay is currently disbursed in four seasonal allotments — I request it be changed to two consolidated payments in summer-autumn and winter-spring."

entries.zh: 下督撫議行。
entries.en: The court referred the proposal to the governor-general and governor for review and implementation.
entries.literal: The memorial was referred to the governor-general and governor for deliberation and implementation.

entries.zh: 尋調署山西大同鎮總兵。
entries.en: He was soon transferred to acting regional commander of Datong in Shanxi.
entries.literal: Soon he was transferred to serve as acting regional commander of Datong in Shanxi.

entries.zh: 與前任總兵李如栢互劾，均奪職。
entries.en: He and the former regional commander Li Rubo impeached each other, and both were stripped of office.
entries.literal: He and the former regional commander Li Rubo impeached each other, and both were dismissed from office.

entries.zh: 乾隆元年，以副將發湖廣，尋授衡州協副將。
entries.en: In Qianlong 1 (1736) he was posted to Huguang as a brigade deputy and soon made brigade deputy commander of Hengzhou.
entries.literal: In the first year of Qianlong he was dispatched to Huguang as a brigade deputy and soon appointed brigade deputy commander of Hengzhou.

entries.zh: 城綏苗、瑤為亂，大雄駐長安堡，焚賊寨，戮其渠，餘相率就撫。
entries.en: When the Miao and Yao of Chengsui rose, Daxiong encamped at Chang'an Fort, burned rebel stockades, killed their chiefs, and the remainder came in one after another.
entries.literal: The Miao and Yao of Chengsui rebelled; Daxiong stationed at Chang'an Fort, burned rebel stockades, killed their leaders, and the rest successively submitted.

entries.zh: 擢鎮筸鎮總兵。
entries.en: He was promoted to regional commander of Zhengan.
entries.literal: He was promoted to regional commander of Zhengan.

entries.zh: 總督孫嘉淦劾大雄貪縱，奪職。
entries.en: Governor-General Sun Jiagan impeached him for greed and lax discipline, and he was dismissed.
entries.literal: Governor-General Sun Jiagan impeached Daxiong for greed and indulgence, and he was dismissed.

entries.zh: 湖南巡撫蔣溥言讞無貪縱跡，引見，复授雲南昭通鎮總兵。
entries.en: Hunan Governor Jiang Pu reported that the case showed no proof of greed or indulgence; Daxiong was summoned to audience and restored as regional commander of Zhaotong in Yunnan.
