entries.literal: Hunan Governor Jiang Pu said the verdict found no evidence of greed or indulgence; Daxiong was granted an audience and again appointed regional commander of Zhaotong in Yunnan.

entries.zh: 敘剿苗功，加都督僉事銜。
entries.en: For his service against the Miao he was given the additional rank of Assistant Commissioner-in-chief.
entries.literal: For his merit in suppressing the Miao, he was given the additional title of Assistant Commissioner-in-chief of the Chief Commandant's Office.

entries.zh: 繼鈞至常德迎家，中途假回民金，大雄以聞。
entries.en: Jijun went to Changde to fetch the family; en route he borrowed money from Hui people, and Daxiong reported it.
entries.literal: Jijun reached Changde to meet the family; on the way he borrowed money from Hui people; Daxiong reported this.

entries.zh: 上以大雄知事不可揜乃始奏劾，左授哈密總兵。
entries.en: Because Daxiong had known of the affair yet reported and impeached only when it could no longer be hidden, the emperor demoted him to regional commander of Hami.
entries.literal: The emperor, because Daxiong had known of the matter but only reported and impeached when it could no longer be concealed, demoted him to regional commander of Hami.

entries.zh: 命署安西提督，赴巴里坤驗馬駝，疏報四千餘。
entries.en: He was ordered to serve as acting provincial commander of Anxi, inspect horses and camels at Barkol, and reported more than four thousand on hand.
entries.literal: He was ordered to serve as acting provincial military commander of Anxi, proceed to Barkol to inspect horses and camels, and memorialized reporting more than four thousand.

entries.zh: 會總督方觀承核參將鍾世傑等至巴里坤領馬千九百餘，途中馬多死，論罪。
entries.en: When Governor-General Fang Guancheng verified that Regimental Colonel Zhong Shijie and others had drawn more than nineteen hundred horses at Barkol, with many dying on the road, they were punished.
entries.literal: When Governor-General Fang Guancheng verified that Regimental Colonel Zhong Shijie and others had reached Barkol to receive more than nineteen hundred horses, many horses died en route, and they were punished.

entries.zh: 上以大雄疏不實，下部議；
entries.en: Finding Daxiong's report inaccurate, the emperor referred the case to the ministry for adjudication.
entries.literal: The emperor, because Daxiong's memorial was inaccurate, referred the matter to the ministry for deliberation.

entries.zh: 總督黃廷桂复劾大雄，命奪官，逮京師治罪。
entries.en: Governor-General Huang Tinggui impeached him again; he was stripped of rank, arrested, and sent to the capital for trial.
entries.literal: Governor-General Huang Tinggui again impeached Daxiong; he was ordered stripped of office, arrested, and brought to the capital for punishment.

entries.zh: 二十一年四月，行至西安，卒。
entries.en: In the fourth month of year twenty-one, while being conveyed to the capital, he reached Xi'an and died.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of the twenty-first year, while traveling, he reached Xi'an and died.

entries.zh: 三十二年，上以綠營世職不得世襲罔替，下兵部察諸將有功者，俟襲次畢，賜恩騎尉世襲罔替，大雄與焉。
entries.en: In Qianlong 32 (1767), because Green Standard hereditary offices could not pass in perpetuity, the emperor ordered the Board of War to review meritorious officers and, once their prescribed successions ended, grant their lines the perpetual hereditary rank of Commandant of Grace Cavalry; Daxiong was among them.
entries.literal: In the thirty-second year, because Green Standard Army hereditary offices could not pass down in perpetuity, the emperor ordered the Board of War to examine meritorious generals and, when the prescribed successions were exhausted, grant the hereditary rank of Commandant of Grace Cavalry in perpetuity; Daxiong was among them.

entries.zh: 三十年，從將軍明瑞徵緬甸，進攻蠻結，克木卡十六，殪賊三，傷額，明日，仍裹創出戰。
entries.en: In the thirtieth year of Qianlong (1765) he followed General Ming Rui against Burma, attacked Manjie, took sixteen wooden palisades, killed three rebels, was wounded in the forehead, and fought again the next day still bandaged.
entries.literal: In the thirtieth year he followed General Ming Rui in the Burma campaign, advanced to attack Manjie, captured sixteen wooden palisades, killed three rebels, was wounded in the forehead, and the next day still went out to fight wrapped in bandages.

entries.zh: 事聞，賜孔雀翎，號法式善巴圖魯。
entries.en: When the report reached court he received a peacock feather and the title Fashishan Batulu.
entries.literal: When this was reported he was granted a peacock feather and given the title Fashishan Batulu.

entries.zh: 擢雲南臨元鎮總兵。
entries.en: He was promoted to regional commander of Linyuan in Yunnan.
entries.literal: He was promoted to regional commander of Linyuan in Yunnan.

entries.zh: 明瑞令將五千人屯龍陵關備調遣。
entries.en: Ming Rui stationed him with five thousand men at Longling Pass for deployment as needed.
entries.literal: Ming Rui ordered him to station five thousand men at Longling Pass for deployment as needed.

entries.zh: 召詣熱河行在，入見，命乾清門行走，賜貂皮、銀幣，令還軍。
entries.en: Summoned to the Rehe traveling palace, he was granted audience, assigned to the Gate of Heavenly Purity, rewarded with sable and silver, and sent back to the army.
entries.literal: He was summoned to the emperor's traveling palace at Rehe, granted an audience, ordered to serve at the Gate of Heavenly Purity, and bestowed sable fur and silver coins, then ordered back to the army.

entries.zh: 旋移普洱鎮總兵，擢雲南提督。
entries.en: He was soon moved to Pu'er as regional commander and promoted to provincial commander of Yunnan.
entries.literal: Soon he was transferred to regional commander of Pu'er and promoted to provincial military commander of Yunnan.

entries.zh: 卒，加太子太保，諡勤毅。
entries.en: He died; posthumously he was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the posthumous name Qinyi (Diligent and Resolute).
entries.literal: He died; posthumously he was given Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and the posthumous title Qinyi.

entries.zh: 十三年，從征金川，至卡撒，統雲南、貴州諸軍進攻色底、光多諸寨。
entries.en: In year thirteen he joined the Jinchuan campaign, reached Kasai, and took command of the Yunnan and Guizhou forces against Sedi, Guangduo, and neighboring stockades.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year he joined the Jinchuan campaign, reached Kasai, and commanded the armies of Yunnan and Guizhou in attacking the stockades at Sedi, Guangduo, and elsewhere.

entries.zh: 引兵出昔嶺中峰之西，與署總兵哈攀龍、任舉師會，克大小碉十、石城一，墮碉百三十。
entries.en: He led troops west of Xiling's central peak, united with Acting Regional Commander Ha Panlong and Ren Ju, took ten blockhouses large and small plus one stone fortress, and demolished one hundred thirty blockhouses.
entries.literal: He led troops out to the west of the central peak of Xiling, joined forces with Acting Regional Commander Ha Panlong and Ren Ju, captured ten blockhouses large and small and one stone fortress, and destroyed one hundred thirty blockhouses.

entries.zh: 同攻克昔嶺溝底石城水卡。
entries.en: Together they captured the stone fortress and water palisade at the foot of Xiling Ravine.
entries.literal: Together they captured the stone fortress and water palisade at the bottom of Xiling Ravine.

entries.zh: 經略大學士傅恆奏大雄歷經戰陣，令總理營壘，措置妥協，賜孔雀翎。
entries.en: Grand Secretary and commissioner-general Fu Heng reported that Daxiong, a veteran of many battles, had been put in charge of camps and fortifications with thoroughly sound results, and he was awarded a peacock feather.
entries.literal: Grand Secretary and Commissioner-General Fu Heng memorialized that Daxiong had passed through many battles, ordered him to take charge of encampments and fortifications, his arrangements were thoroughly satisfactory, and he was granted a peacock feather.

entries.zh: 金川頭人莎羅奔等乞降，師還。
entries.en: When the Jinchuan chieftains Suoluoben and others sued for surrender, the army withdrew.
entries.literal: The Jinchuan chieftains Suoluoben and others sued for surrender, and the army returned.

entries.zh: 授雲南提督，加左都督銜。
entries.en: He was appointed provincial commander of Yunnan with the additional rank of Left Chief Commandant.
entries.literal: He was appointed provincial military commander of Yunnan and given the additional rank of Left Chief Commandant.

entries.zh: 入覲，官其子繼鈞藍翎侍衛，命送大雄上官。
entries.en: Daxiong entered court for an audience. His son Jijun was appointed an imperial guardsman with the blue arrow feather and ordered to escort Daxiong to his new command.
entries.literal: Called to court for an audience, his son Jijun was given office as an imperial guardsman with the blue arrow feather, and ordered to escort Daxiong to his post.

entries.zh: 疏言：「西藏喀拉烏蘇諸地與準噶爾連界，盜竊紛擾，是其故習。
entries.en: He memorialized: "In places such as Kalawusu on Tibet's frontier, which adjoin Dzungar lands, brigandage and raids are chronic — an old pattern there.
entries.literal: He memorialized: "Places such as Kalawusu in Tibet border on Dzungar territory; theft and raids are constantly troubling — this is their old habit.

entries.zh: 今藏北鄙即我邊地，防邊自可弭盜。
entries.en: Tibet's northern marches are now our border; solid frontier defense will itself check the robbers.
entries.literal: Now Tibet's northern frontier is our borderland; guarding the frontier can naturally suppress brigandage.

entries.zh: 請駐藏大臣仍設重兵，循大道置台站，以資防守。」
entries.en: I ask that the Resident Ministers in Tibet keep substantial troops in place and set relay stations along the main road for defense."
entries.literal: I request that the Resident Ministers in Tibet continue to maintain strong forces and establish relay stations along the main road to support defense."

entries.zh: 上嘉其留心。
entries.en: The emperor praised his careful attention to the matter.
entries.literal: The emperor praised his attentiveness.

entries.zh: 乾隆十年，師复徵瞻對，破直達、鬆多諸寨，奪碉七十餘。
entries.en: In Qianlong 10 (1745) the army marched again on Zhandui, broke the stockades at Zhida, Songduo, and elsewhere, and took more than seventy blockhouses.
entries.literal: In the tenth year of Qianlong the army again campaigned against Zhandui, broke the stockades at Zhida and Songduo and elsewhere, and seized more than seventy blockhouses.

entries.zh: 進攻下密左山梁，獲頭人噶籠丹坪。
entries.en: Pressing the attack on the left ridge of Xiami, he captured the chieftain Galong Danping.
entries.literal: Advancing to attack the left ridge of Xiami, he captured the chieftain Galong Danping.

entries.zh: 再進克下密等百餘寨，獲頭人塔巴四交。
entries.en: Advancing further he took more than a hundred stockades including Xiami and captured the chieftain Taba Sijiao.
entries.literal: Pressing forward he captured more than a hundred stockades including Xiami and captured the chieftain Taba Sijiao.

entries.zh: 渡丫魯河，遂破瞻對，焚其寨。
entries.en: Crossing the Yalu River, he broke Zhandui and burned its stockades.
entries.literal: Crossing the Yalu River, he then broke Zhandui and burned its stockades.

entries.zh: 其渠姜錯太死於火。
entries.en: Its chief Jiang Cuotai perished in the fire.
entries.literal: Its leader Jiang Cuotai died in the flames.

entries.zh: 十二年，大金川酋莎羅奔攻革布什咱土司，並掠明正土司所屬魯密、章谷諸地。
entries.en: In year twelve the Greater Jinchuan chieftain Suoluoben attacked the Gebushenzha native ruler and raided Lumi, Zhanggu, and other districts under the Mingzheng native official.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year, the Greater Jinchuan chieftain Suoluoben attacked the native official of Gebushenzha and also raided Lumi, Zhanggu, and other territories belonging to the Mingzheng native official.

entries.zh: 巡撫紀山移良柱威茂協副將，督兵防禦。
entries.en: Governor Jishan moved Liangzhu to brigade deputy commander of Weimao and put him in charge of the defensive forces.
entries.literal: Governor Jishan transferred Liangzhu to brigade deputy commander of Weimao and directed troops in defense.

entries.zh: 莎羅奔糾小金川土司澤旺侵沃日各寨，都司馬光祖赴援，賊大至，光祖困於熱籠。
entries.en: Suoluoben joined Lesser Jinchuan's Zewang in an invasion of Wori's stockades; Battalion Commander Ma Guangzu went to relieve them, but the rebels came in strength and trapped Guangzu at Relong.
entries.literal: Suoluoben rallied Lesser Jinchuan native official Zewang to invade the stockades of Wori; Battalion Commander Ma Guangzu went to their aid; the rebels came in force and Guangzu was trapped at Relong.

entries.zh: 良柱率輕騎馳救，敗賊巴納山，進克石卡二百二十三。
entries.en: Liangzhu galloped to the rescue with a light cavalry detachment, routed the rebels at Bana Mountain, and pushed on to take two hundred twenty-three stone palisades.
entries.literal: Liangzhu led a light cavalry force in a rapid rescue, defeated the rebels at Bana Mountain, and advanced to capture two hundred twenty-three stone palisades.

entries.zh: 光祖等出應，賊潰，圍解。
entries.en: Guangzu and the others sallied forth; the rebels broke and the siege was raised.
entries.literal: Guangzu and others came out to meet them; the rebels were routed and the siege was lifted.

entries.zh: 澤旺降，並還所侵沃日三寨。
entries.en: Zewang submitted and restored the three Wori stockades he had taken.
entries.literal: Zewang surrendered and also returned the three stockades of Wori he had seized.

entries.zh: 詔嘉其奮勇，遷重慶鎮總兵。
entries.en: The throne praised his daring and promoted him to regional commander of Chongqing.
entries.literal: An edict praised his valor and promoted him to regional commander of Chongqing.

entries.zh: 再進复孫克宗官寨，攻江卡，戰屢勝，克大小碉寨百餘，降二十餘寨。
entries.en: Pressing on he retook Sunkezong stockade, attacked Jiangka, won battle after battle, took more than a hundred forts and stockades, and received the submission of more than twenty stockades.
entries.literal: Advancing again he recovered the stockade of Sunkezong, attacked Jiangka, won repeated battles, captured more than a hundred blockhouses and stockades large and small, and received the surrender of more than twenty stockades.

entries.zh: 進克丹噶山，分兵焚撒籠等七寨，噶固等寨先後降。
entries.en: He took Danga Mountain, sent detachments to burn seven stockades including Salong, and Gagu and other stockades submitted in turn.
entries.literal: Advancing he captured Danga Mountain, detached troops to burn seven stockades including Salong, and stockades including Gagu surrendered one after another.

entries.zh: 賊守石達大碉，良柱冒雨進，數十戰，賊乘夜來撲營，設伏，殲焉。
entries.en: The rebels held the great blockhouse at Shida; Liangzhu pushed forward through the rain in dozens of fights; when the rebels raided the camp by night he ambushed and destroyed them.
entries.literal: The rebels held the great blockhouse at Shida; Liangzhu advanced in the rain through dozens of battles; the rebels came by night to storm the camp; he set an ambush and annihilated them.

entries.zh: 馬邦頭人思錯已降，總兵許應虎馭之不以道，复叛，圍應虎於的交，良柱馳救。
entries.en: Mabang chieftain Sicuo had submitted, but Regional Commander Xu Yinghu mistreated him until he rebelled again and besieged Yinghu at Dijiao; Liangzhu rode to relieve him.
entries.literal: The Mabang chieftain Sicuo had already surrendered; Regional Commander Xu Yinghu drove him harshly and he rebelled again, surrounding Yinghu at Dijiao; Liangzhu galloped to the rescue.

entries.zh: 賊退入戎布寨，攻之未下。
entries.en: The rebels fell back into Rongbu stockade, which did not fall immediately.
entries.literal: The rebels withdrew into Rongbu stockade; the attack did not succeed at once.

entries.zh: 旋复犯馬邦，副將張興被圍。
entries.en: They soon struck Mabang again and surrounded Brigade Deputy Zhang Xing.
entries.literal: Soon they again raided Mabang, and Brigade Deputy Zhang Xing was surrounded.

entries.zh: 良柱請移戎布師赴援，總督張廣泗不許，興陷於賊。
entries.en: Liangzhu asked to move the Rongbu column to the rescue; Governor-General Zhang Guangsi refused, and Zhang Xing fell into the rebels' hands.
entries.literal: Liangzhu requested that the troops at Rongbu be moved to the rescue; Governor Zhang Guangsi would not permit it, and Xing fell into the rebels' hands.

entries.zh: 侵噶固，守兵叛附賊，奪卡倫七。
entries.en: They invaded Gagu; the garrison mutinied to the rebels' side and seized seven karun outposts.
entries.literal: They invaded Gagu; the garrison rebelled and joined the rebels, seizing seven karun outposts.

entries.zh: 廣泗令良柱往攻，力戰，賊未卻。
entries.en: Guangsi ordered Liangzhu to attack; despite hard fighting the rebels held their ground.
entries.literal: Guangsi ordered Liangzhu to go attack; after fierce fighting the rebels were not driven off.

entries.zh: 值大雪二十餘日，糧匱，煮鎧弩以食。
entries.en: Snow fell for more than twenty days; supplies ran out and they boiled armor and crossbow parts for food.
entries.literal: Heavy snow lasted more than twenty days; grain ran short, and they boiled armor and crossbows to eat.

entries.zh: 力不支，廣泗檄退師。
entries.en: When they could no longer hold, Guangsi ordered a withdrawal.
entries.literal: Unable to hold out, Guangsi by dispatch ordered the army to withdraw.

entries.zh: 倉卒移營，砲械為賊得。
entries.en: In the hurried evacuation the rebels captured their cannon and arms.
entries.literal: In the hasty move of camp, cannon and weapons were taken by the rebels.

entries.zh: 列傳九十八
entries.en: Biography 98
entries.literal: Biographies 98

entries.zh: 十二年，西藏郡王頗羅鼐卒。
entries.en: In the twelfth year Polhané, the Tibetan princely regent, died.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year Polhané, prince of Tibet, died.

entries.zh: 頗羅鼐愛其次子珠爾默特那木札勒，請以為嗣，遂襲爵為郡王。
entries.en: Polhané had favored his second son Gyurmé Namgyal and asked that he succeed; Gyurmé Namgyal then inherited the princely title.
entries.literal: Polhané favored his second son Gyurmé Namgyal and requested that he succeed him; Gyurmé Namgyal thereupon inherited the title of prince.

entries.zh: 上諭傅清曰：「頗羅鼐更事多，黽勉事中國。
entries.en: The emperor wrote to Fu Qing: "Polhané was seasoned in affairs and served the dynasty with steady diligence.
entries.literal: The emperor instructed Fu Qing: "Polhané had wide experience and strove diligently to serve China.

entries.zh: 珠爾默特那木札勒幼，傅清宜留意。
entries.en: Gyurmé Namgyal is still young. Fu Qing should keep a close watch on him.
entries.literal: Gyurmé Namgyal is young; Fu Qing should pay attention.

entries.zh: 如珠爾默特那木札勒思慮所未至，當為指示。」
entries.en: Where his judgment falls short, you should guide him."
entries.literal: If there are matters Gyurmé Namgyal has not yet considered, you should instruct him."

entries.zh: 傅清疏言：「頗羅鼐在時，長子公珠爾默特策布登出駐阿里克夏，當令珠爾默特那木札勒帥師出駐騰格里諾爾、喀喇烏蘇諸處。
entries.en: Fu Qing replied in a memorial: "While Polhané lived, the eldest son Duke Gyurmé Tseten was posted at Ali Khasha, and Gyurmé Namgyal was then ordered to lead troops out to Tengri Nor, Kar Usu, and the other places.
entries.literal: Fu Qing memorialized: "While Polhané lived, his eldest son Gyurmé Tseten was posted at Ali Khasha; Gyurmé Namgyal should have led troops out to garrison Tengri Nor, Kar Usu, and other places.

entries.zh: 今仍遣珠爾默特策布登駐阿里克夏，令別遣宰桑駐騰格里諾爾、喀喇烏蘇諸處。」
entries.en: Gyurmé Tseten should remain at Ali Khasha, while other zasag officers should be sent to hold Tengri Nor, Kar Usu, and the like."
entries.literal: Now Gyurmé Tseten should still be sent to garrison Ali Khasha, and other zasag officials should be dispatched to Tengri Nor, Kar Usu, and the rest."

entries.zh: 又以準噶爾入藏熬茶，請增兵分路防護。
entries.en: He also requested additional troops posted along the routes to guard the Dzungar tea pilgrimage parties.
entries.literal: He also asked, because the Dzungars were entering Tibet for the tea pilgrimage, that troops be increased to guard the routes in separate columns.

entries.zh: 上命與珠爾默特那木札勒商榷，毋涉張皇。
entries.en: The emperor told him to consult Gyurmé Namgyal and to avoid any show of alarm.
entries.literal: The emperor ordered him to consult with Gyurmé Namgyal and not to be alarmist.

entries.zh: 十三年，命以提督拉布敦代，傅清還。
entries.en: In the thirteenth year Labdon was sent as provincial commander to relieve him, and Fu Qing returned home.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year Labdon the provincial commander was ordered to replace him, and Fu Qing returned.

entries.zh: 复授天津鎮總兵，遷古北口、固原提督。
entries.en: He was again made commander of the Tianjin garrison, then promoted to provincial commander at Gubeikou and Guyuan.
entries.literal: He was again appointed commander of the Tianjin garrison and was transferred to be provincial commander at Gubeikou and Guyuan.

entries.zh: 珠爾默特那木札勒請撤留藏兵，上從之。
entries.en: Gyurmé Namgyal asked that the garrison troops in Tibet be withdrawn, and the emperor agreed.
entries.literal: Gyurmé Namgyal requested withdrawal of the troops left in Tibet, and the emperor assented.

entries.zh: 旋以副都統紀山代拉布敦。
entries.en: Soon afterward Jishan replaced Labdon as deputy commander in Tibet.
entries.literal: Soon afterward the deputy commander Jishan replaced Labdon.

entries.zh: 傅清，富察氏，滿洲鑲黃旗人，李榮保次子，傅恆弟也。
entries.en: Fu Qing, of the Fuca clan, came from the Manchu Bordered Yellow Banner. He was Li Rongbao's second son and Fuheng's younger brother.
entries.literal: Fu Qing, of the Fuca clan, a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner, was the second son of Li Rongbao and younger brother of Fuheng.

entries.zh: 雍正間，授侍衛。
entries.en: In the Yongzheng era he received appointment as an imperial bodyguard.
entries.literal: During the Yongzheng reign he was appointed an imperial bodyguard.

entries.zh: 乾隆初，累遷至直隸天津鎮總兵。
entries.en: Early in the Qianlong reign he rose step by step to command the Tianjin garrison in Zhili.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Qianlong reign he was promoted in succession to commander of the Zhili Tianjin garrison.

entries.zh: 康熙中定西藏，留兵鎮撫，以大臣駐藏辦事，為員二，嗣省其一。
entries.en: After Tibet was pacified in the Kangxi era, garrison troops remained to keep order and imperial ministers were posted to Lhasa. The office began as a two-man commission and was later cut to one.
entries.literal: In the Kangxi reign Tibet was pacified; troops were left to guard and pacify it, and ministers were stationed in Tibet to handle affairs—two posts at first, later reduced to one.

entries.zh: 是時駐藏副都統索拜當代，命傅清以副都統往。
entries.en: Suobai's term as the deputy commander in Tibet was ending, and the court ordered Fu Qing to replace him in that post.
entries.literal: At that time the deputy commander stationed in Tibet, Suobai, was due to be relieved; Fu Qing was ordered to go as deputy commander.

entries.zh: 十一年，疏言：「西藏處徼外，西北界準噶爾，北通青海，為四川西南外郛。
entries.en: In the eleventh year he submitted a memorial: "Tibet stands beyond the frontier. It borders the Dzungars to the northwest, links with Qinghai to the north, and serves as Sichuan's outer defense to the southwest.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year he memorialized: "Tibet lies beyond the frontier; on the northwest it borders the Dzungars, on the north it connects with Qinghai, and it forms the outer bulwark southwest of Sichuan.

entries.zh: 自雍正十二年設塘汛，不特傳送官文書，且以聯絡聲氣。
entries.en: Courier stations had been set up since Yongzheng 12 not merely to carry official dispatches but to keep communications open along the route.
entries.literal: Since the twelfth year of Yongzheng courier stations have been established, not only to transmit official documents but also to maintain communication.

entries.zh: 上年索拜以節費議撤汛，使藏人任郵遞，謂之番塘。
entries.en: The year before, Suobai had proposed abolishing the stations to save money and entrusting the mail to Tibetans, a system called the fan tang.
entries.literal: Last year Suobai, to economize, proposed abolishing the stations and having Tibetans handle the mail, calling this the 'Tibetan courier route.'

entries.zh: 未幾輒被盜。
entries.en: Before long the route was repeatedly plundered.
entries.literal: Before long it was repeatedly robbed.

entries.zh: 今準噶爾當入藏熬茶，番塘恐滋誤。
entries.en: With Dzungars soon due to enter Tibet for the tea pilgrimage, relying on the Tibetan courier route risks serious mishaps.
entries.literal: Now the Dzungars are about to enter Tibet for the tea pilgrimage; the Tibetan courier route may cause delays and errors.

entries.zh: 請自打箭爐至藏復置塘汛，酌衝僻遠近，當得兵千人以內。」
entries.en: I ask that stations be re-established from Dartsendo to Lhasa, with troop strength adjusted to each post's importance and distance; the total should come to no more than a thousand men."
entries.literal: I request that courier stations be restored from Dartsendo to Tibet, allotting troops according to whether posts are on main routes or remote, which should require no more than a thousand men."

entries.zh: 議如所請。
entries.en: The memorial was approved as he had asked.
entries.literal: The court approved his request.

entries.zh: 十四年，紀山疏言珠爾默特那木札勒與達賴喇嘛有隙，請移達賴喇嘛置泰宁。
entries.en: In the fourteenth year Jishan reported a rift between Gyurmé Namgyal and the Dalai Lama and asked that the Dalai Lama be moved to Taining.
entries.literal: In the fourteenth year Jishan memorialized that Gyurmé Namgyal was at odds with the Dalai Lama and requested that the Dalai Lama be moved to Taining.

entries.zh: 上知珠爾默特那木札勒乖戾且為亂，命駐藏大臣復舊置二員，予傅清都統銜，自固原復往。
entries.en: Seeing that Gyurmé Namgyal was defiant and heading toward rebellion, the emperor restored the two-man commission in Tibet, gave Fu Qing commander-in-chief rank, and sent him back from Guyuan.
entries.literal: The emperor knew Gyurmé Namgyal was perverse and would rebel; he ordered restoration of the former two resident ministers in Tibet, gave Fu Qing the rank of commander-in-chief, and sent him again from Guyuan.

entries.zh: 紀山复疏謂珠爾默特那木札勒言其兄珠爾默特策布登將舉兵相攻，上命傅清途中诇虛實。
entries.en: Jishan also reported Gyurmé Namgyal's claim that his brother Gyurmé Tseten was about to attack him. The emperor told Fu Qing to verify the story on the road to Lhasa.
entries.literal: Jishan again memorialized that Gyurmé Namgyal claimed his brother Gyurmé Tseten would raise troops to attack him; the emperor ordered Fu Qing to investigate the truth en route.

entries.zh: 傅清疏言：「珠爾默特策布登未嘗構兵，特珠爾默特那木札勒妄言，藉以奪其兄分地。
entries.en: Fu Qing replied: "Gyurmé Tseten has made no move to raise troops. Gyurmé Namgyal invented the story so he could seize his brother's lands.
entries.literal: Fu Qing memorialized: "Gyurmé Tseten has never raised troops; Gyurmé Namgyal spoke falsely only to seize his brother's allotted territory.

entries.zh: 臣至藏，即將珠爾默特那木札勒懲治。」
entries.en: Once I reach Lhasa I will punish Gyurmé Namgyal at once."
entries.literal: When your servant reaches Tibet, he will at once punish Gyurmé Namgyal."

entries.zh: 是時上已遣侍郎拉布敦代紀山，因諭傅清，珠爾默特那木札勒乖戾且為亂，令熟計密奏。
entries.en: The emperor had already dispatched Vice Minister Labdon to replace Jishan. He told Fu Qing that Gyurmé Namgyal was treacherous and likely to rebel, and ordered him to plan carefully and report in confidence.
entries.literal: By then the emperor had already sent Vice Minister Labdon to replace Jishan; he therefore instructed Fu Qing that Gyurmé Namgyal was perverse and would rebel, and ordered him to deliberate carefully and report in secret.

entries.zh: 十五年，傅清與拉布敦先後至藏，珠爾默特那木札勒迫其兄珠爾默特策布登至死，遂逐其子，遣使通準噶爾，叛益有跡。
entries.en: In the fifteenth year Fu Qing and Labdon arrived in Tibet one after another. Gyurmé Namgyal had hounded his brother Gyurmé Tseten to death, driven out the nephew, and opened contact with the Dzungars. Rebellion was now unmistakable.
entries.literal: In the fifteenth year Fu Qing and Labdon reached Tibet in succession; Gyurmé Namgyal drove his brother Gyurmé Tseten to death, then expelled his son, sent envoys to communicate with the Dzungars, and signs of rebellion grew clearer.

entries.zh: 上命副都統班第赴西藏，與傅清、拉布敦密謀取進止，仍詔傅清、拉布敦毋輕發，並密諭四川總督策楞勒兵為備。
entries.en: The emperor sent Deputy Commander Bandi to Tibet to confer secretly with Fu Qing and Labdon on how to proceed, while also warning them not to strike prematurely and privately ordering Sichuan Governor Celeng to ready his forces.
entries.literal: The emperor ordered Deputy Commander Bandi to go to Tibet to consult secretly with Fu Qing and Labdon on what course to take, yet also instructed Fu Qing and Labdon not to act rashly, and secretly told Sichuan Governor Celeng to muster troops in readiness.

entries.zh: 珠爾默特那木札勒謀愈急，絕塘汛，軍書不得達。
entries.en: Gyurmé Namgyal pressed his plot harder, severed the courier route, and blocked all military dispatches.
entries.literal: Gyurmé Namgyal's plotting grew more urgent; he cut off the courier stations so military dispatches could not get through.

entries.zh: 傅清與拉布敦未得上詔，計以為：「珠爾默特那木札勒且叛，徒為所屠。
entries.en: Fu Qing and Labdon never received the edict. They concluded: "Gyurmé Namgyal is on the verge of rebellion. If we wait we will simply be butchered.
entries.literal: Fu Qing and Labdon had not received the imperial edict; they reckoned: "Gyurmé Namgyal is about to rebel; we will only be slaughtered in vain.

entries.zh: 亂既成，吾軍不得即進，是棄兩藏也。
entries.en: Once the revolt breaks out our armies cannot reach Lhasa in time. That would mean abandoning Tibet altogether.
entries.literal: Once rebellion is complete our army cannot advance at once—that is to abandon both Tibets.

entries.zh: 不如先發，雖亦死，亂乃易定。」
entries.en: Better to strike first. We may die as well, but the rebellion will be far easier to crush."
entries.literal: Better to strike first: though we too may die, the rebellion will be easier to settle."

entries.zh: 十月壬午，召珠爾默特那木札勒至通司岡駐藏大臣署，言有詔，使登樓，預去其梯，若將宣詔。
entries.en: On the renwu day of the tenth month they summoned Gyurmé Namgyal to the ministers' compound at Tangsikang, announced an imperial edict, and had him climb to the upper floor after removing the ladder, as though they were about to read the decree.
entries.literal: On the renwu day of the tenth month Gyurmé Namgyal was summoned to the resident ministers' compound at Tangsikang; they said there was an edict, had him ascend the building, removed the ladder beforehand, as if an edict were to be proclaimed.

entries.zh: 珠爾默特那木札勒方拜跪，傅清自後揮刀斷其首。
entries.en: While Gyurmé Namgyal was kowtowing, Fu Qing struck from behind and cut off his head.
entries.literal: As Gyurmé Namgyal was bowing in obeisance, Fu Qing struck from behind with a blade and severed his head.

entries.zh: 於是其黨羅卜藏札什始率眾圍樓數重，發槍砲，縱火，傅清中三創，度不免，自剄死。
entries.en: His follower Lobsang Tashi then led rebels to ring the building, opened fire with muskets and cannon, and set it ablaze. Fu Qing took three wounds, knew he could not escape, and cut his own throat.
entries.literal: Thereupon his follower Lobsang Tashi led the crowd to surround the building in several rings, opened fire with muskets and cannon, and set fires; Fu Qing received three wounds, saw he could not escape, and cut his own throat to die.

entries.zh: 拉布敦死樓下。
entries.en: Labdon died at the foot of the building.
entries.literal: Labdon died below the building.

entries.zh: 主事策塔爾、參將黃元龍皆自殺。
entries.en: The secretary Cetar and Brigadier Huang Yuanlong also took their own lives.
entries.literal: The secretary Cetar and the brigade commander Huang Yuanlong both killed themselves.

entries.zh: 通判常明中矢石死。
entries.en: Subprefect Chang Ming was killed by arrows and stones.
entries.literal: The subprefect Chang Ming was struck by arrows and stones and died.

entries.zh: 從死者千總二、兵四十九、商民七十七。
entries.en: Two thousand-commanders, forty-nine soldiers, and seventy-seven merchants died with them.
entries.literal: Those who died with them were two company commanders, forty-nine soldiers, and seventy-seven merchants.

entries.zh: 事聞，上軫悼，宣示始末，謂其「揆幾審勢，決計定謀，心苦而功大」。
entries.en: When word reached the throne the emperor mourned them and published the full story, praising them for "reading the moment, weighing the odds, settling on a plan, and fixing their resolve—hearts wrung with hardship, yet a great service done."
entries.literal: When the affair was reported, the emperor grieved and proclaimed how it had begun and ended, saying of them: "They gauged the moment and weighed the situation, settled on a plan and fixed their resolve; their hearts suffered yet their achievement was great."

entries.zh: 傅清追封一等伯，諡襄烈，旋命立祠通司岡。
entries.en: Fu Qing was posthumously made a first-class baron with the posthumous name Xianglie, and a shrine was soon ordered at Tangsikang.
entries.literal: Fu Qing was posthumously enfeoffed as a first-class baron with the posthumous title Xianglie, and soon ordered to have a shrine built at Tangsikang.

entries.zh: 喪還，上臨奠。
entries.en: When the coffin returned to the capital the emperor came in person to mourn.
entries.literal: When the coffin returned, the emperor came in person to offer mourning.

entries.zh: 其子孫以一等子世襲，賜白金萬。
entries.en: His descendants received a hereditary first-class viscounty, along with ten thousand taels of silver.
entries.literal: His descendants were granted hereditary succession as first-class viscount, and ten thousand taels of silver were bestowed.

entries.zh: 班第至藏，戮羅卜藏札什等，疏陳珠爾默特那木札勒自立名號，通款準噶爾，稱策旺多爾濟那木札勒為汗，請其發兵至拉達克為聲援。
entries.en: Bandi reached Tibet and executed Lobsang Tashi and his followers. His memorial reported that Gyurmé Namgyal had proclaimed his own title, treated with the Dzungars, hailed Tsewang Dorji Namgyal as khan, and asked for Dzungar troops at Ladakh as backing.
entries.literal: When Bandi reached Tibet he executed Lobsang Tashi and others; he memorialized that Gyurmé Namgyal had set up his own title, opened relations with the Dzungars, called Tsewang Dorji Namgyal khan, and asked him to send troops to Ladakh as a supporting force.

entries.zh: 上复降詔褒傅清、拉布敦，建祠京師，命曰雙忠。
entries.en: The emperor issued another edict honoring Fu Qing and Labdon, built a shrine in the capital, and named it the Shrine of Twin Loyalty.
entries.literal: The emperor again issued an edict praising Fu Qing and Labdon, built a shrine in the capital, and named it Shuangzhong ('Twin Loyalty').

entries.zh: 子明仁，以侍衛襲子爵。
entries.en: His son Mingren inherited the viscountcy while serving as an imperial bodyguard.
entries.literal: His son Mingren inherited the viscountcy as an imperial bodyguard.

entries.zh: 從征金川，卒於軍。
entries.en: He campaigned in Jinchuan and died on active service.
entries.literal: He followed the campaign against Jinchuan and died in the army.

entries.zh: 十三年，駐藏副都統傅清當代，命拉布敦往。
entries.en: In the thirteenth year Fu Qing's term as deputy commander in Tibet was ending, and Labdon was sent to replace him.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year the deputy commander stationed in Tibet, Fu Qing, was due to be relieved, and Labdon was ordered to go.

entries.zh: 十四年，召還，以紀山代，授工部侍郎。
entries.en: In the fourteenth year he was recalled. Jishan took his place, and Labdon was appointed Vice Minister of Works.
entries.literal: In the fourteenth year he was recalled; Jishan replaced him, and Labdon was appointed Vice Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 未終歲，上徵紀山還，復命赴藏。
entries.en: Before the year was out the emperor recalled Jishan and ordered Labdon back to Tibet.
entries.literal: Before the year was out the emperor summoned Jishan back and again ordered Labdon to go to Tibet.

entries.zh: 十五年，授左都御史。
entries.en: In the fifteenth year he was made Censor-in-Chief of the Left.
entries.literal: In the fifteenth year he was appointed Censor-in-Chief of the Left.

entries.zh: 尋與傅清謀誅珠爾默特那木札勒，其黨羅卜藏札什圍樓，拉布敦挾刃躍下樓，擊殺數十人，自剖其腹死。
entries.en: He soon joined Fu Qing in the plot to kill Gyurmé Namgyal. When Lobsang Tashi's men surrounded the building, Labdon leaped down with his blade, cut down dozens of rebels, then opened his own belly and died.
entries.literal: Soon he joined Fu Qing in plotting to execute Gyurmé Namgyal; when Lobsang Tashi and his followers surrounded the building, Labdon leaped downstairs with a blade in hand, killed several dozen men, and disemboweled himself to die.

entries.zh: 上聞，贈爵、賜金、立祠如傅清。
entries.en: On hearing the news the emperor granted posthumous honors, bestowed gold, and ordered a shrine built as he had for Fu Qing.
entries.literal: When the emperor heard, he granted posthumous rank, bestowed gold, and ordered a shrine built as for Fu Qing.

entries.zh: 命以拉布敦之族升隸正黃旗，諡壯果。
entries.en: Labdon's clan was raised to the Plain Yellow Banner and he received the posthumous name Zhuangguo.
entries.literal: He ordered Labdon's clan raised to the Plain Yellow Banner, with the posthumous title Zhuangguo.

entries.zh: 子隆保，以侍衛襲子爵。
entries.en: His son Longbao inherited the viscountcy while serving as an imperial bodyguard.
entries.literal: His son Longbao inherited the viscountcy as an imperial bodyguard.

entries.zh: 誤班奪官，爵除。
entries.en: He lost his post and title for a lapse in court attendance.
entries.literal: For a court-attendance error his office was taken and the title abolished.

entries.zh: 班第，博爾濟吉特氏，蒙古鑲黃旗人。
entries.en: Bandi, of the Borjigit clan, came from the Mongol Bordered Yellow Banner.
entries.literal: Bandi, of the Borjigit clan, was a Mongol of the Bordered Yellow Banner.

entries.zh: 康熙間，自官學生授內閣中書。
entries.en: In the Kangxi era he left the Imperial Academy for appointment as a Grand Secretariat secretary.
entries.literal: In the Kangxi reign, from the Imperial Academy he was appointed a secretary in the Grand Secretariat.

entries.zh: 五遷，雍正初至內閣學士。
entries.en: After five promotions he reached Grand Secretariat academician early in the Yongzheng reign.
entries.literal: After five promotions, at the beginning of Yongzheng he reached Grand Secretariat academician.

entries.zh: 四川、雲南徼外與西藏定界，命偕副都統鄂齊如西藏宣諭。
entries.en: When borders beyond Sichuan and Yunnan were delimited with Tibet, he was sent with Deputy Commander Eqi to Lhasa to proclaim the settlement.
entries.literal: When the borders beyond Sichuan and Yunnan were fixed with Tibet, he was ordered with Deputy Commander Eqi to go to Tibet to proclaim the edict.

entries.zh: 遷理籓院侍郎。
entries.en: He was promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs.
entries.literal: He was transferred to be Vice Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs.

entries.zh: 坐事左遷，在內閣學士上行走。
entries.en: After a demotion for misconduct he served as acting Grand Secretariat academician.
entries.literal: For an offense he was demoted and served as acting Grand Secretariat academician.

entries.zh: 十一年，命在軍機處行走。
entries.en: In the eleventh year he was assigned to the Grand Council.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year he was ordered to serve in the Grand Council.

entries.zh: 乾隆三年，授兵部侍郎。
entries.en: In Qianlong 3 he was appointed Vice Minister of War.
entries.literal: In the third year of Qianlong he was appointed Vice Minister of War.

entries.zh: 外擢湖廣總督。
entries.en: He was then appointed governor-general of Huguang.
entries.literal: He was promoted outside the capital to governor-general of Huguang.

entries.zh: 剿鎮筸、永綏亂苗，兩閱月而畢，上嘉焉。
entries.en: He put down the Miao revolts in Zhenqian and Yongsui within two months, and the emperor commended him.
entries.literal: He suppressed the rebellious Miao of Zhenqian and Yongsui; within two months it was finished, and the emperor praised him.

entries.zh: 五年，以憂還京師。
entries.en: In the fifth year he returned to Beijing to observe mourning.
entries.literal: In the fifth year he returned to the capital on account of mourning.

entries.zh: 六年，命仍在軍機處行走，授兵部尚書。
entries.en: In the sixth year he resumed service in the Grand Council and was appointed Minister of War.
entries.literal: In the sixth year he was ordered to continue in the Grand Council and was appointed Minister of War.

entries.zh: 十三年，師徵金川，授內大臣，出督軍餉，加太子少保。
entries.en: In the thirteenth year, during the campaign against Jinchuan, he was made a Grand Minister of the Household, put in charge of army provisions, and granted the added rank of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year, when the army marched against Jinchuan, he was appointed Grand Minister of the Household, sent out to supervise military supplies, and given the added title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 尋按四川巡撫紀山加徵累民狀，命即署巡撫。
entries.en: Soon afterward he investigated Sichuan Governor Jishan's extra levies that burdened the people and was ordered to serve at once as acting governor.
entries.literal: Soon, upon investigating Acting Sichuan Governor Jishan's memorial on extra levies burdening the people, the emperor ordered him to serve immediately as acting governor.

entries.zh: 時訥親、張廣泗師久無功，上諮班第，但言廣泗罪狀，語不及訥親。
entries.en: Neqin and Zhang Guangsi had campaigned for months without success. When the emperor questioned Bandi, he cited only Zhang Guangsi's faults and said nothing about Neqin.
entries.literal: At the time Neqin and Zhang Guangsi's army had long been without success; the emperor questioned Bandi, who spoke only of Zhang Guangsi's offenses and said nothing about Neqin.

entries.zh: 上諭曰：「班第雖職餉，然為本兵軍機大臣，軍事及將弁功罪，皆職掌所在，不得以督餉，一切置不問。」
entries.en: The emperor replied: "Bandi may supervise provisions, but as Minister of War and Grand Councilor he is responsible for military operations and for the merit or blame of every officer. He cannot ignore those duties simply because he oversees supply lines."
entries.literal: The emperor instructed: "Although Bandi's duty is provisions, as Minister of War and Grand Councilor, military affairs and the merits and faults of officers are all within his charge; he may not, on the ground of supervising supplies, set everything aside and ask no questions."

entries.zh: 左遷兵部侍郎。
entries.en: Bandi was demoted to Vice Minister of War.
entries.literal: He was demoted to Vice Minister of War.

entries.zh: 拉布敦，其第六子也。
entries.en: Labdon was his sixth son.
entries.literal: Labdon was his sixth son.

entries.zh: 生有力，能彎十力弓，左右射。
entries.en: He was born strong enough to draw a ten-strength bow and shoot equally well with either hand.
entries.literal: From birth he was strong, able to draw a ten-strength bow and shoot to left and right.

entries.zh: 工詩文，習外國語言。
entries.en: He wrote poetry and prose well and studied foreign languages.
entries.literal: He was skilled in poetry and prose and studied foreign languages.

entries.zh: 康熙間，襲叔祖勒爾圖三等阿達哈哈番世職。
entries.en: In the Kangxi era he inherited his grand-uncle Le'ertu's hereditary third-rank adaha hafan office.
entries.literal: In the Kangxi reign he inherited his grand-uncle Le'ertu's hereditary third-rank adaha hafan post.

entries.zh: 雍正朝，從傅爾丹討準噶爾，戰於和通呼爾哈諾爾；
entries.en: Under Yongzheng he followed Furdan against the Dzungars and fought at Khoton Nor;
entries.literal: In the Yongzheng reign he followed Furdan against the Dzungars and fought at Khoton Nor;

entries.zh: 又從策淩討準噶爾，戰於額爾德尼昭：皆有所斬馘，授世管佐領。
entries.en: he also campaigned under Celeng at Erdene Zuu. In both battles he took enemy heads and was made a hereditary company commander.
entries.literal: he also followed Celeng against the Dzungars and fought at Erdene Zuu: in both he took heads in battle and was appointed hereditary company commander.

entries.zh: 上命軍中舉驍勇之士，拉布敦與焉，賜孔雀翎。
entries.en: When the emperor called for the bravest men in the army Labdon was chosen and received a peacock feather.
entries.literal: The emperor ordered that valiant men in the army be recommended; Labdon was among them and was granted a peacock feather.

entries.zh: 乾隆初，累遷正紅旗滿洲副都統。
entries.en: Early in the Qianlong reign he rose to deputy commander of the Plain Red Banner Manchus.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Qianlong reign he was promoted in succession to deputy commander of the Plain Red Banner Manchus.

entries.zh: 八年，复討準噶爾，授參贊大臣，出北路。
entries.en: In the eighth year he campaigned again against the Dzungars as coordinating minister on the northern route.
entries.literal: In the eighth year he again campaigned against the Dzungars, was appointed coordinating minister, and marched by the northern route.

entries.zh: 九年，授定邊左副將軍。
entries.en: In the ninth year he was made Left Deputy General for the Pacification of the Frontier.
entries.literal: In the ninth year he was appointed Left Deputy General for the Pacification of the Frontier.

entries.zh: 其冬，疏言：「厄魯特宰桑額勒慎等內牧布爾吉推河，烏梁海得木齊札木禪內牧布延圖河源。
entries.en: That winter he reported: "The Oirat jaisang Elesen and others are grazing inside at the Burjitu River, while the Uriankhai Demchi Zhamchen is grazing inside at the headwaters of the Buyantu.
entries.literal: That winter he memorialized: "The Oirat zasag Elesen and others are grazing inside at the Burjitu River; the Uriankhai Demchi Zhamchen is grazing inside at the headwaters of the Buyantu River.

entries.zh: 布爾吉推河在阿爾台山梁外，布延圖河源在阿爾台山梁內，距卡倫不遠，已闉坐卡侍衛等嚴防。」
entries.en: The Burjitu lies beyond the Altai ridge and the Buyantu headwaters within it, both close to our border posts. Guards at the posts have been ordered to watch them closely."
entries.literal: The Burjitu River lies beyond the Altai ridge; the headwaters of the Buyantu lie within the Altai ridge, not far from the border posts; garrison guards at the posts have already been ordered to guard strictly."

entries.zh: 十年冬，疏言：「烏梁海得木齊烏爾巴齊等避雪，內牧黃加書魯克，距卡倫不遠。
entries.en: The next winter he reported: "The Uriankhai Demchi Urbaqi and others, fleeing snow, were grazing inside at Huangjiashuluke, again close to the border posts.
entries.literal: In the winter of the tenth year he memorialized: "The Uriankhai Demchi Urbaqi and others, fleeing snow, are grazing inside at Huangjiashuluke, not far from the border posts.

entries.zh: 託爾和烏蘭、布延圖、哈瑪爾沙海諸卡倫外，皆有準噶爾人踪跡，仍闉坐卡侍衛等嚴防。」
entries.en: Dzungar tracks had been seen beyond the posts at Torh Ulan, Buyantu, and Khamarshahai, and the guards were again ordered to keep strict watch."
entries.literal: Beyond the posts at Torh Ulan, Buyantu, and Khamarshahai there are traces of Dzungars; garrison guards at the posts have again been ordered to guard strictly."

entries.zh: 尋召還京師，授正白旗滿洲副都統。
entries.en: He was soon recalled to Beijing and made deputy commander of the Plain White Banner Manchus.
entries.literal: Soon he was recalled to the capital and appointed deputy commander of the Plain White Banner Manchus.

entries.zh: 復出署古北口提督。
entries.en: He again served as acting provincial commander at Gubeikou.
entries.literal: He again went out to serve as acting provincial commander at Gubeikou.

entries.zh: 列傳九十九
entries.en: Biography 99
entries.literal: Biographies 99

entries.zh: 高天喜，甘肅西寧人。
entries.en: Gao Tianxi was a native of Xining in Gansu.
entries.literal: Gao Tianxi was a man of Xining in Gansu.

entries.zh: 天喜本準噶爾人，雍正中為我師所俘。
entries.en: Tianxi was originally a Zunghar who had been taken prisoner by the Qing forces during the Yongzheng reign.
entries.literal: Tianxi was originally a Zunghar; in the Yongzheng reign he was captured by our army.

entries.zh: 高氏撫為子，因從其族籍。
entries.en: The Gao family adopted and raised him as their son, and he was entered on their clan register accordingly.
entries.literal: The Gao family raised him as a son, and he therefore followed their clan registration.

entries.zh: 從軍，累擢保寧堡守備。
entries.en: He took up military service and rose through repeated promotions to the post of defender of Baoning Fort.
entries.literal: He entered the army and was repeatedly promoted to Defender of Baoning Fort.

entries.zh: 乾隆二十二年，副將軍兆惠擊伊犁，天喜從參將邁斯漢赴援。
entries.en: In the twenty-second year of the Qianlong reign, when Deputy General-in-Chief Zhaohui marched against Ili, Tianxi went as a subordinate of Colonel Maisihan to reinforce him.
entries.literal: In the twenty-second year of Qianlong, Deputy General-in-Chief Zhaohui attacked Ili; Tianxi followed Colonel Maisihan to go to the relief.

entries.zh: 遇噶勒雜特賊百餘，擊殺之，獲其駝馬。
entries.en: They came upon a band of more than a hundred Galjut rebels, routed them, and seized their camels and horses.
entries.literal: They encountered more than a hundred Galjut bandits, killed them in battle, and captured their camels and horses.

entries.zh: 既，聞兆惠被困濟爾哈朗，議馳救，邁斯漢怯不進。
entries.en: Soon afterward they learned that Zhaohui was trapped at Jierhalang. When a rapid rescue was proposed, Maisihan hung back out of fear and refused to move.
entries.literal: Afterward, hearing that Zhaohui was besieged at Jierhalang, they discussed riding to the rescue, but Maisihan was afraid and would not advance.

entries.zh: 巴里坤辦事大臣雅爾哈善以聞，上即奪邁斯漢官以命天喜。
entries.en: Yarghashi, the minister resident at Barkul, reported the matter to the throne, and the emperor at once removed Maisihan from office and put Tianxi in command.
entries.literal: Yarghashi, the Grand Minister Resident at Barkul, reported this; the emperor immediately stripped Maisihan of his office and appointed Tianxi in his place.

entries.zh: 尋遷金塔協副將。
entries.en: He was soon promoted to assistant deputy commander at Jinta.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward he was transferred to be Assistant Deputy Commander at Jinta.

entries.zh: 再遷西寧鎮總兵，授領隊大臣。
entries.en: He was promoted again to commander of the Xining garrison and appointed a leading-column grand minister.
entries.literal: He was again transferred to be Commander-in-Chief of the Xining garrison and was appointed a leading-column grand minister.

entries.zh: 二十三年十月，師攻葉爾羌，兆惠議出間道襲取賊輜重，渡黑水。
entries.en: In the tenth month of the twenty-third year, as the army advanced on Yarkand, Zhaohui proposed a flanking march along a side route to seize the enemy baggage train and cross the Black River.
entries.literal: In the tenth month of the twenty-third year, the army attacked Yarkand; Zhaohui planned to take a bypath to strike at the rebels' baggage train and cross the Black River.

entries.zh: 天喜督兵修橋渡師，未及半，賊大至。
entries.en: Tianxi directed his men in building a bridge to get the army across, but before even half the force had crossed, a large rebel host appeared.
entries.literal: Tianxi supervised the troops in repairing a bridge to ferry the army across; before half had crossed, the rebels arrived in force.

entries.zh: 天喜聞兆惠陷賊陣，舍橋亟赴之，奮與賊戰，與鄂實、三格、特通額俱沒於陣。
entries.en: Hearing that Zhaohui was caught in the enemy lines, Tianxi left the bridge unfinished and rushed to his relief. He fought the rebels with desperate valor and fell in battle together with E Shi, San Ge, and Tetonge.
entries.literal: Tianxi heard that Zhaohui was trapped in the rebel formation; abandoning the bridge he hurried to his aid, fought fiercely against the rebels, and perished in battle together with E Shi, San Ge, and Tetonge.

entries.zh: 上賦詩惜之。
entries.en: The emperor composed a poem lamenting his death.
entries.literal: The emperor composed a poem to mourn him.

entries.zh: 諡果義，又賜其家白金千。
entries.en: He was posthumously honored with the title Guoyi, and his family was granted a thousand taels of silver besides.
entries.literal: He was given the posthumous title Guoyi, and his family was also granted a thousand taels of silver.

entries.zh: 鄂實，西林覺羅氏，滿洲鑲藍旗人，大學士鄂爾泰第二子。
entries.en: E Shi, of the Xilin Gioro clan, belonged to the Manchu Bordered Blue Banner and was the second son of Grand Secretary Ortai.
entries.literal: E Shi, of the Xilin Gioro clan, was a man of the Manchu Bordered Blue Banner and the second son of Grand Secretary Ortai.

entries.zh: 出為叔父鄂禮後。
entries.en: He was established as heir to his uncle E Li.
entries.literal: He was made the heir of his uncle E Li.

entries.zh: 自廕生授三等侍衛。
entries.en: Through hereditary privilege he received appointment as a third-rank imperial bodyguard.
entries.literal: By hereditary privilege he was appointed a third-rank imperial bodyguard.

entries.zh: 累遷本旗副都統、左翼前鋒統領。
entries.en: He rose through successive promotions to vice commander of his banner and commander of the Left Vanguard.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to vice commander of his banner and commander of the Left Vanguard.

entries.zh: 兄鄂容安死阿睦爾撒納之亂，鄂實請從軍，授參贊大臣，佐定邊將軍成袞扎布，出西路。
entries.en: When his elder brother Erong'an was killed in Amursana's rebellion, E Shi volunteered for active service. He was appointed deputy assisting grand minister to support Pacification General Cheng'enjab on the western campaign route.
entries.literal: His elder brother Erong'an died in the rebellion of Amursana; E Shi requested to join the army, was appointed a deputy assisting grand minister, and aided the Pacification General Cheng'enjab on the western route.

entries.zh: 二十二年夏，成袞扎布令逐捕扎那噶爾布，鄂實以地險馬疲，中道引還。
entries.en: In the summer of the twenty-second year, Cheng'enjab ordered a pursuit of Zanagarbu, but E Shi turned the troops back halfway, pleading dangerous terrain and exhausted horses.
entries.literal: In the summer of the twenty-second year, Cheng'enjab ordered pursuit of Zanagarbu; E Shi, citing dangerous terrain and exhausted horses, turned the army back midway.

entries.zh: 上手詔詰責曰：「若謂地險，賊何以能行？
entries.en: The emperor sent a personal edict of rebuke: "If the ground is too dangerous, how do the rebels manage to cross it?
entries.literal: The emperor personally issued an edict of rebuke, saying: "If you say the terrain is dangerous, how can the rebels travel it?

entries.zh: 若謂馬疲，賊馬何獨能壯健？」
entries.en: If our horses are worn out, why are the enemy's horses alone still fresh and strong?"
entries.literal: If you say the horses are exhausted, why are the rebels' horses alone strong and healthy?"

entries.zh: 左授藍翎侍衛。
entries.en: He was demoted to the rank of blue-plume imperial bodyguard.
entries.literal: He was demoted to a blue-plume imperial bodyguard.

entries.zh: 是冬，鄂實逐扎哈沁賊，斬一百四十餘級，獲牲械。
entries.en: That winter he pursued the Zhahakin rebels, killing more than a hundred and forty of them and capturing livestock and arms.
entries.literal: That winter, E Shi pursued the Zhahakin rebels, beheaded more than a hundred and forty, and captured livestock and weapons.

entries.zh: 上謂：「今當大雪，馬力應疲乏，尚能勦賊。
entries.en: The emperor remarked, "There is heavy snow now, and the horses ought to be exhausted—yet you were still able to rout the rebels.
entries.literal: The emperor said: "Now there is heavy snow; the horses ought to be exhausted, yet you were still able to suppress the rebels.

entries.zh: 彼時鄂實為參贊大臣，有事但諉諸將軍。
entries.en: When you were deputy assisting grand minister, you used to push every difficulty off onto the general.
entries.literal: At that time E Shi was deputy assisting grand minister and, whenever anything arose, simply shifted blame onto the general.

entries.zh: 茲以負罪，乃直前勦賊，朕知其隱矣。」
entries.en: Now that you are under a cloud, you charge straight at the enemy—I see what you are really about."
entries.literal: Now, bearing guilt, you press forward to suppress the rebels—I know your hidden motive."

entries.zh: 量遷三等侍衛。
entries.en: He was nevertheless promoted to third-rank imperial bodyguard.
entries.literal: He was accordingly promoted to third-rank imperial bodyguard.

entries.zh: 死事，上令仍視前鋒統領賜卹，諡果壯。
entries.en: He died in action. The emperor ordered that he receive the condolence grants due a vanguard commander and honored him posthumously with the title Guozhuang.
entries.literal: He died in service; the emperor ordered that condolence grants still be made as for a vanguard commander, and gave him the posthumous title Guozhuang.

entries.zh: 三格，棟鄂氏，滿洲正白旗人。
entries.en: San Ge, of the Donggo clan, belonged to the Manchu Plain White Banner.
entries.literal: San Ge, of the Donggo clan, was a man of the Manchu Plain White Banner.

entries.zh: 自諸生授藍翎侍衛。
entries.en: Having passed the licentiate examination, he was appointed a blue-plume imperial bodyguard.
entries.literal: From the rank of licentiate he was appointed a blue-plume imperial bodyguard.

entries.zh: 累遷黑龍江副都統。
entries.en: He rose through successive promotions to vice commander at Heilongjiang.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to vice commander at Heilongjiang.

entries.zh: 命將索倫、巴爾呼兵三千，佐參贊大臣策楞出西路，為領隊大臣。
entries.en: He was ordered to lead three thousand Solon and Barghu troops in support of Deputy Assisting Grand Minister Celeng on the western route and was appointed a leading-column grand minister.
entries.literal: He was ordered to command three thousand Solon and Barghu troops, to assist Deputy Assisting Grand Minister Celeng on the western route, and was made a leading-column grand minister.

entries.zh: 策楞以怯懦逮，三格亦坐奪官。
entries.en: When Celeng was arrested for cowardice, San Ge was stripped of office as well.
entries.literal: Celeng was arrested for cowardice, and San Ge also had his office taken away on the same charge.

entries.zh: 旋复授正白旗蒙古副都統。
entries.en: He was soon reappointed vice commander of the Mongol Plain White Banner.
entries.literal: Shortly afterward he was again appointed vice commander of the Mongol Plain White Banner.

entries.zh: 攻呼爾璊台吉賽音伯勒克等，再戰，掠其牧地，予三等輕車都尉世職。
entries.en: He attacked the Khurlet taiji Sayinbelik and others, fought them twice, and raided their pastures, for which he was granted the hereditary rank of third-class commandant of light chariots.
entries.literal: He attacked the Khurlet taiji Sayinbelik and others, fought again, raided their pastures, and was granted the hereditary office of third-class commandant of light chariots.

entries.zh: 二十二年春，定邊將軍成袞扎布令逐捕扎那噶爾布，未得。
entries.en: In the spring of the twenty-second year, Pacification General Cheng'enjab ordered a pursuit of Zanagarbu, but failed to take him.
entries.literal: In the spring of the twenty-second year, Pacification General Cheng'enjab ordered pursuit of Zanagarbu, but he was not captured.

entries.zh: 秋，師至博羅和羅，遇叛黨額林沁達瓦等百餘戶，三格與戰。
entries.en: In autumn the army reached Boluheluo, where San Ge engaged more than a hundred rebel households led by Elinjindawa and others.
entries.literal: In autumn the army reached Boluheluo and encountered more than a hundred rebel households under Elinjindawa and others; San Ge fought them.

entries.zh: 會布魯古特台吉琿齊、呼爾璊台吉達瓦斬扎那噶爾布偽請降，並請招額林沁達瓦，三格信之，遽引師還，琿齊等旋遁去。
entries.en: The Burut taiji Hunqi and the Khurlet taiji Dawa had killed Zanagarbu and now offered a false surrender, asking also to bring over Elinjindawa. San Ge believed them, withdrew the army at once, and Hunqi and his party promptly fled.
entries.literal: At that time the Burut taiji Hunqi and the Khurlet taiji Dawa, having killed Zanagarbu, falsely offered surrender and also asked to win over Elinjindawa; San Ge believed them, abruptly led the army back, and Hunqi and the others soon fled.

entries.zh: 坐奪官，並削世職，以兵伍自效。
entries.en: He was dismissed from office, stripped of his hereditary rank as well, and reduced to serving in the ranks to redeem himself.
entries.literal: He was stripped of office and also lost his hereditary rank, serving thereafter as a common soldier to redeem himself.

entries.zh: 死事，上命仍視副都統賜卹，諡剛勇。
entries.en: He died in action. The emperor ordered that he receive the condolence grants due a vice commander and honored him posthumously with the title Gangyong.
entries.literal: He died in service; the emperor ordered that condolence grants still be made as for a vice commander, and gave him the posthumous title Gangyong.

entries.zh: 和起，馬佳氏，滿洲鑲藍旗人。
entries.en: He Qi, of the Magiya clan, belonged to the Manchu Bordered Blue Banner.
entries.literal: He Qi, of the Magiya clan, was a man of the Manchu Bordered Blue Banner.

entries.zh: 其先世阿音布，國初以軍功授拜他喇布勒哈番世職。
entries.en: His ancestor Ayinbu received the hereditary rank of baitalabure hafan at the founding of the dynasty for military service.
entries.literal: His ancestor Ayinbu, at the founding of the dynasty, was granted the hereditary office of baitalabure hafan for military merit.

entries.zh: 和起襲職，授盛京協領。
entries.en: He Qi inherited the rank and was appointed a garrison colonel at Mukden.
entries.literal: He Qi inherited the office and was appointed a garrison colonel at Mukden.
